summary: Viant reported record Q2 2024 advertiser spend, with revenue up 15% YoY and contribution ex-TAC up 23%, while adjusted EBITDA grew 41% to $9.6M. CTV spend grew over 40% and streaming audio nearly doubled YoY, together representing over 50% of platform spend. The company rebranded its AI suite as ViantAI, with new LLM-based planning, and expects Chat with Data in Q4 and autonomous optimization in 2025. Q3 guidance was raised (implied by context), with overhead growth expected in the low teens for 2024.

negative_highlights: Same-station local revenue declined 10% due to a 3% drop in agency business and 4.9% decline in direct.
Auto category revenue fell 18.5% year-over-year, primarily driven by a 60% drop in domestic auto spend.
Pacings for the second half of the year are down to low-to-mid-single digits.
positive_highlights: Digital revenue grew 10.2% year-over-year, now accounting for 21.5% of total revenue.
Political revenue exceeded budget by 72%, generating $586,000 in net revenue.
Operating income turned positive at $5.4 million, a 219% increase from the prior year quarter.
summary: Second quarter same-station revenue declined 2% year-over-year to $60.4 million total net revenue, driven by a 10.9% drop in local spot and divestitures, while digital revenue grew 10.2%. Adjusted EBITDA increased 11.4% to $8.8 million due to expense reductions of $2 million (including $1.3M severance) and debt interest savings, though operating income remains volatile at $5.4 million. Management lowered full-year revenue paces to low-to-mid-single digits and emphasized a strategic focus on deleveraging ahead of the 2026 bond maturity.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.5M from $1.9M in prior year
SG&A expenses increased to $19M from $13.8M
New interest expense on CRG term loan and higher amortization
positive_highlights: 11th consecutive record revenue quarter; revenue up 28% YoY
Soft tissue product sales grew from $13.2M to $17.6M year-over-year
Surgical segment generated positive EBITDA of $1.4M in Q2
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q2 2024 revenue of $20.2 million, up 28% year-over-year, marking the 11th consecutive record quarter, with soft tissue products driving growth from $13.2 million to $17.6 million. The company generated positive adjusted EBITDA of $600,000, though net loss widened to $3.5 million due to higher SG&A and interest expenses. Management guided to additional $4-5 million investment in Tissue Health Plus in H2 2024, with a pilot launch planned for Q1 2025 and commercial launch in H2 2025. The new CRG debt facility provides non-dilutive capital, and the Surgical segment remains EBITDA positive.

negative_highlights: Pediatric revenue declined 10% year-over-year due to soft census
DaVita pilot progress slower than anticipated
Cash balance only $1 million; completed $2 million offering
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 67.2% from 55.3% year-over-year
Operating loss improved by $2.7 million versus prior year
First commercial sale of QUELIMMUNE to Cincinnati Children's Hospital
summary: Nuwellis reported Q2 2024 revenue of $2.2 million, up 6% year-over-year, driven by a 30% increase in heart failure and critical care consumables utilization, though pediatric revenue fell 10% due to lower census. Gross margin improved to 67.2% from 55.3%, and operating loss narrowed to $2.3 million from $5.0 million. The company secured first commercial sale of QUELIMMUNE, but noted slower-than-expected progress with the DaVita pilot and cash balances are low at $1 million, with a recent $2 million offering.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined due to reduced wind tower demand and softer PRS shipments
Q3 guidance implies lower EBITDA margin sequentially
Orders declined year-over-year across all segments
positive_highlights: Maintained 10% EBITDA margin despite lower revenue, with $3.6 million EBITDA
Quoting activity elevated across segments; Gearing quoting up 163% YoY
Cost actions contributing >$4 million annualized savings, with most implemented
summary: Broadwind's Q2 2024 revenue declined year-over-year (Heavy Fab -42%, Gearing -5%, Industrial Solutions +3%), but EBITDA margin held at 10% due to favorable mix and cost cuts. Net income was $0.5 million, down from $1.4 million a year ago. Management introduced Q3 guidance of $36-$38 million revenue and $1.7-$2.5 million EBITDA, implying margin compression. They noted robust quoting in non-wind markets (Gearing quoting up 163% YoY) and expect wind demand to accelerate in 2025-2026.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to $10.7 million from $6.9 million in the prior year period.
R&D expenses rose to $7.6 million driven by costs associated with launching PALISADE-3 and preparing for PALISADE-4.
G&A expenses increased to $4.6 million due to headcount growth and professional service fees.
positive_highlights: Enrollment cadence for PALISADE-3 is on track with expectations and green failure rates are consistent with projections.
The company remains well-funded with $108.4 million in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities as of June 30, 2024.
PALISADE-2 achieved historic success as the first positive Phase 3 trial for acute treatment of SAD, supporting potential NDA submission.
summary: Vistagen Therapeutics reported Q1 FY2025 results with R&D expenses of $7.6 million and G&A expenses of $4.6 million, resulting in a net loss of $10.7 million compared to $6.9 million in the prior year period. The company confirmed that enrollment for its PALISADE-3 Phase 3 trial is on track with projections, while PALISADE-4 is expected to initiate in the second half of the year. Both studies are targeted to read out in 2025.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $5M from $4M YoY.
ASCEND top-line data not yet available; key catalyst remains delayed until Q4 2024.
No revenue; company is pre-revenue clinical-stage.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased 19.7% YoY to $5.5M, with R&D down 17.7% and G&A down 21.3%.
BOLSTER trial achieved complete enrollment in first-line cholangiocarcinoma nearly six months ahead of plan, accelerating data to mid-2025.
Cash runway extends into early 2026, covering anticipated data milestones.
summary: Lisata reported Q2 2024 operating expenses down 19.7% YoY to $5.5M, with R&D down 17.7% to $2.6M and G&A down 21.3% to $2.9M. Net loss widened to $5M from $4M YoY. Cash stood at $38.3M, expected to fund operations into early 2026. Management highlighted complete enrollment in BOLSTER nearly six months ahead of plan, with top-line ASCEND data expected in Q4 2024. No revenue reported; clinical-stage biotech.

negative_highlights: Net investment income per share decreased sequentially from $0.63 to $0.59
Weighted average yield on income-producing securities declined to 12.2%
Debt-to-equity ratio increased to 1.18x from 1.11x
positive_highlights: NII of $0.59 per share exceeded the recently increased regular dividend
NAV per share increased to $20.30, highest since June 2022
Portfolio credit stable with 89% of risk-rated 1 and 2 investments
summary: CCAP reported Q2 2024 NII of $0.59 per share, translating to an annualized NII ROE of 11.7%, exceeding its increased regular dividend of $0.42 plus a supplemental dividend of $0.09. NAV per share rose to $20.30, the highest since June 2022. Gross deployment was $119 million, with 92% in first-lien, while net deployment was $46 million. The portfolio remained stable with 1.6% of debt on nonaccrual at cost, and management maintained a confident outlook on LBO volume acceleration in the second half.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance implies a deceleration in second-half growth due to tougher comps
Operating expenses still elevated with $80-84 million full-year range
DIXI distribution carries lower gross margin, creating mix drag
positive_highlights: Revenue up 17% YoY to $19.3 million, beating the high end of guidance
Gross margin expanded 90 basis points to 73.4%
RNS sales growth ex-NAUTILUS was 21% YoY
summary: Q2 2024 revenue of $19.3 million grew 17% YoY, with RNS system sales up 21% excluding prior-year NAUTILUS study contributions. Gross margin expanded to 73.4% from 72.5%, operating expenses grew only 3%, and net loss improved to $7.5 million from $9.1 million. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $76-78 million (16-19% growth) while maintaining gross margin and operating expense guidance. New sales reps completed training, and the NAUTILUS trial remains on track for primary endpoint readout in Q1 2025.

negative_highlights: Sequential decline in revenue driven by compounding issues and reimbursement challenges in pediatric centers
G&A expenses increased to $6.9 million due to pre-commercialization efforts for the EU launch and Norgine transaction costs
note and marketing expenses rose significantly to $4.6 million, largely attributable to payroll increases and AYA initiatives
positive_highlights: PEDMARK net sales increased approximately 120% compared to the same quarter in 2023
NCCN guidelines updated to include patients up to age 39, expanding the AYA population opportunity
$43.2 million upfront consideration received from Norgine partnership for European commercialization
summary: Fennec reported Q2 FY2024 PEDMARK net sales of $7.3 million, representing a 120% increase year-over-year but down sequentially from the prior quarter due to compounding issues and reimbursement delays in pediatric centers. Management highlighted recent milestones including FDA safety communication updates for substitutions, CMS J-Code resolution, and NCCN guideline expansions allowing access up to age 39 (AYA), which they believe will drive growth starting Q3. The company sold EU rights to Norgine for an upfront payment of $43.2 million with a potential €10 million milestone upon German pricing approval in late Q4.

negative_highlights: Total Q2 revenue came in slightly below the outlook provided last quarter due to a slowdown at Wayfair.
Management noted that inflation is taking a toll on consumer budgets, dampening demand for home furnishings.
The company reiterated full-year guidance but explicitly stated it does not include material impact from prime creditors tightening above them.
positive_highlights: Non-Wayfair gross originations grew nearly 20% in the second quarter as Wayfair declined.
Gross margin expanded to 16.9%, with operating expenses decreasing by 7% year-over-year.
Katapult Pay delivered $15.7 million in gross originations, representing incremental growth from direct and waterfall channels.
summary: Katapult reported Q2 revenue of $58.9 million (up 8.7% YoY) and gross originations of $55.3 million (up 1.1%), missing the prior outlook due to a slowdown at Wayfair which accounted for roughly half of business. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by $1.2 million year-over-year, but management reiterated full-year guidance while noting macro headwinds and uncertainty regarding interest rate cuts.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from $9.9M in Q2 FY2023 to $16.9M in Q2 FY2024.
SG&A expenses increased by $3.6 million YoY due to the cost of being a publicly traded company, partially offsetting revenue growth.
A significant $2.8 million non-cash charge related to Forward Purchase Agreement valuation impacted reported earnings.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 16% year-over-year to $15.1 million driven by a 28% increase in aircraft usage revenue.
Blended yield improved 6% YoY to $5,330 as non-owner demand mix increased to 56%. Total flight hours grew 5% YoY.
Vaunt subscription product reached an ARR of $1 million for the first time during the quarter.
summary: Q2 revenue was $15.1 million (up 16% YoY) while net loss widened to $16.9 million due to a $2.8 million non-cash charge on Forward Purchase Agreements and increased SG&A of $9.7 million driven by public company costs. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations based on aircraft deliveries, projecting total 2024 revenue between $72M-$90M from HondaJets and $50M from G280s, with EBITDA positivity expected in Q4.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 26% year-over-year to $1.3 million due to the RV market downturn
Gross margin contracted from 26.3% in Q2 FY2023 to 25.5% as lower sales volume drove higher fixed overhead costs per unit
Net loss widened significantly to negative $0.30 EPS (or $2.2 million) compared to negative $0.21 EPS last year
positive_highlights: Revenue achieved 32% sequential growth compared to Q1 2024
Substantial pre-orders placed for next-generation Group 27 and GC2 batteries with VHC technology, all of which have been shipped
Strategic partnership announced with K-Z Recreational Vehicles (Thor Industries) integrating Expion360's Edge Battery into premium off-grid offerings
summary: Expion360 reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of $1.3 million, a 26% year-over-year decrease driven by the lingering downturn in the RV market and customers limiting orders ahead of new product launches. Gross profit declined to $300,000 (25.5% margin) from $500,000 last year due to lower sales volume increasing fixed overhead costs per unit, resulting in a net loss of $2.2 million or negative $0.30 EPS compared to a prior period loss of $1.5 million. Management noted sequential revenue growth of 32% versus Q1 but emphasized that the recent public offering proceeds will be used for home energy storage commercialization and future initiatives.

negative_highlights: Zero revenue reported for the quarter due to offsetting deferred revenues and refunds.
Orders were stopped in mid-February due to capital market conditions, resulting in no sales activity.
FDA review process encountered additional requests for information regarding wellness aspects of the Evie Med Ring.
positive_highlights: Operating loss narrowed to $6.4 million from $7.4 million in the prior year period.
Company raised $24.1 million in gross proceeds via a strategic seed investment in April.
Secured three new B2B commercial opportunities with global pharmaceutical companies and a large payer.
summary: Movano Health reported zero revenue for Q2 FY2024 as previously deferred revenues were offset by refunds following the cessation of orders in mid-February. The company recorded an operating loss of $6.4 million, a sequential improvement from the prior period's $7.4 million loss, with cash and cash equivalents standing at $16.9 million. Management confirmed that order intake will resume on September 17 after operational improvements and inventory buildup.

negative_highlights: Gross margin collapsed to 6% from 26% on C$1.9M inventory write-offs
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened 357% YoY to C$2.3M
Cash and equivalents fell to C$0.7M from C$1.8M end-2023
positive_highlights: Revenue up 11.7% YoY to C$14.8M, Germany sales up 129% YoY
German monthly sales grew from C$307k in March to C$1.63M in June, 200% QoQ
OpEx down 29% YoY and note price per gram up 21% to $6.09
summary: Q2 2024 revenue rose 11.7% YoY to C$14.8M, driven by 129% growth in Germany, with German monthly sales accelerating from C$307k in March to C$1.63M in June (200% QoQ increase). Gross margin fell to 6% (down from 26%) due to C$1.9M in inventory clearance and slow-moving stock accruals, while adjusted EBITDA loss widened to C$2.3M from C$0.5M. Management highlighted strong demand and supply constraints in Germany, and cancelled the Kadimastem reverse merger to focus on German growth, though cash position thinned to C$0.7M.

negative_highlights: VIP enrollment revenue decreased 28% sequentially to $1.2 million due to lower estimated customer lives and new entry levels at lower price points.
Cash burn from operations for the six months ended June 30 was $5.6 million, though down from the prior year period.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $4.1 million driven by a 28% increase in product revenue.
Gross margin expanded to 65% from 62% in the prior year period.
Operating expenses decreased by 31% year-over-year, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of YoY expense reduction.
summary: Vivos reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of $4.1 million, representing a 19% year-over-year increase and a sequential increase from Q1 2024. Gross margin expanded to 65%, while operating expenses decreased by 31% year-over-year due to cost-cutting initiatives. Management highlighted the launch of a new strategic alliance with a Colorado sleep clinic in July, which is expected to materially broaden patient access and reduce reliance on VIP enrollments.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they cannot provide meaningful guidance on revenue trends due to 'lumpy' distribution cycles and recent launches.
General & Administrative (G&A) expense reductions are lagging behind R&D cuts, with CEO noting G&A will take longer to tackle than natural project roll-offs in R&D.
The company remains dependent on external financing for milestones rather than being self-funding across all pillars yet.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew ~83% YoY to approx $396k driven by Nu.Q Vet Cancer test sales exceeding full-year 2023 totals.
Operating expenses contracted significantly (approx. 24% lower than prior year) as part of a broader cost reduction plan.
Raised approximately $7 million upfront plus up to $14.5 million in milestone-linked warrants from a healthcare-focused investment fund.
summary: VolitionRx reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of approximately $396,000 (up ~83% YoY) and H1 revenue of $567,000 (up 55%), driven by the Nu.Q Vet Cancer test launch. Operating expenses decreased significantly to roughly 24% lower than Q2 last year due to cost-cutting measures targeting a total reduction of US$10 million annually. The company raised approximately $21.5 million in gross proceeds via a registered direct offering and warrants, aiming for cash flow positivity by 2025.

negative_highlights: Top line revenues were flat sequentially due to approximately $1.8 million in deferred revenue from delayed launches
Management noted prolonged inflation causing softening of consumer spend and ad sales
Company is currently operating with approximately 15% less headcount than last year
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased 25% year-over-year to pro forma levels
Operating losses decreased 23% year-over-year
Pipeline features 68 new brand entrants and strong repeat opportunities with major clients like Visa, Google, and Kraft
summary: Super League reported flat sequential revenue in Q2 FY2024 due to approximately $1.8 million of deferred revenues from delayed advertiser launch dates, though the company noted it continues to win large signature programs with recurring potential. Management highlighted a significant reduction in operating expenses and losses (down 25% and 23% respectively) driven by headcount reductions and cost control measures as they aim for profitability in Q4. While management expressed confidence in their productization strategy and pipeline, the flat top line amidst macroeconomic overhangs resulted in a cautious outlook.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue of $1.1 million fell sharply from $1.9 million year-ago
Revenue impacted by ~$450,000 EMEA software license delays and lower services
Market cap of ~$2.5 million deemed inadequate versus $6 million in ARR
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 77% from 69% in Q2 2023
Net loss narrowed to $1.7 million from $2.6 million year-over-year
Launched Passkey:YOU with favorable initial customer reaction and AWS marketplace listing
summary: Q2 FY2024 revenue fell to $1.1 million from $1.9 million a year ago, mainly due to delayed EMEA software license contracts (~$450k) and lower services revenue. Gross margin improved to 77% from 69%, and net loss narrowed to $1.7 million from $2.6 million. Management expects Q3 and full-year revenue growth, citing new product Passkey:YOU and AWS marketplace launch, but acknowledges continued quarterly variability.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined from 21.2% in Q1 due to write-offs and inventory reserve adjustments.
Non-GAAP operating loss widened slightly to $9.7M compared to prior quarter, with free cash flow deteriorating to negative $26.1M driven by working capital increases.
Accounts receivable balance spiked to $29.7M due to government incentive collection terms.
positive_highlights: Achieved fourth consecutive quarter of positive GAAP gross margin at 13.1% despite lower ASPs due to mix.
Hub production capacity ramping up, expected to reach two per week by end of Q2.
summary: Xos reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of $15.5 million (up 18% sequentially) and delivered 90 units, achieving a fourth consecutive quarter of positive GAAP gross margin at 13.1%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue between $66.7M-$100.4M and non-GAAP operating loss between $43.7M-$48.7M, noting that Q2 results were impacted by inventory reserves and product mix rather than a fundamental demand issue.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.5 million compared to a net income of $0.31 (excluding one-time benefits) last year.
Gross profit margins declined from 52% to 45.9% due to the absence of high-margin digital revenue.
positive_highlights: Paid off over $5 million in debt and other liabilities during the first half of the year, significantly cleaning up the balance sheet.
summary: Net revenues declined to $3.4 million from $4.5 million a year ago due to reduced digital advertising spend and the sale of Sundry units in the prior period comparison. Gross margins contracted to 45.9% as low-margin wholesale sales replaced high-margin digital revenue, while G&A expenses decreased by $1.1 million following debt paydowns totaling over $5 million. Management indicated a strategic pivot from growth spending to balance sheet cleanup for H1 and plans to ramp marketing spend in H2 once the consumer environment stabilizes.

negative_highlights: Americas segment revenue declined 4% year-over-year as customers pushed out orders, indicating lingering destocking caution in the largest region.
Management expects Q1 FY2025 (July-Sept) to be slower than expected before an uptick in October due to seasonal patterns and customer inventory levels below pre-COVID norms.
Brazil margins face pressure as raw material input costs normalize after a period of lower freight and container rates.
positive_highlights: Brazil segment delivered strong sequential growth of approximately 9% driven by pricing power, full utilization, and market share gains following a competitor exit.
Asia segment achieved robust recovery with net sales up 21% sequentially due to higher volumes and improved conditions.
Gross profit saw an improvement exceeding 100% on a sequential basis for the third consecutive quarter.
summary: UFI reported Q4 FY2024 consolidated net sales of $157.5 million, representing a 4% year-over-year increase and a 6% sequential gain driven by strong performance in Brazil (up ~9% sequentially) and Asia (up 21% sequentially), while the Americas segment was flat sequentially but down 4% YoY due to customer destocking delays. Gross profit improved significantly with three consecutive quarters of growth, aided by cost reductions that are now fully realized, though management noted raw material input costs in Brazil will normalize later this year. Management provided Q1 FY2025 guidance for net sales between $147 million and $153 million (midpoint ~$150M) and adjusted EBITDA of $1-3 million.

positive_highlights: Revenue grew 32% year-over-year to $22.2M driven by organic unit adoption and ASP acceleration without adding sales headcount.
summary: MDxHealth reported Q2 FY2024 revenue of $22.2 million, a robust 32% year-over-year increase driven by organic growth in both tissue-based and liquid-based test segments without sales headcount expansion. Gross margins expanded to 60%, while the company reduced its operating loss from $7.7M to $7.4M. Management raised full-year 2024 revenue guidance to a range of $85 million-$87 million, up from an initial expectation of $79 million-$81 million.

negative_highlights: Comparable restaurant revenue declined 0.8% excluding loyalty benefits due to a broad-based consumer slowdown.
Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered by approximately $20 million, primarily driven by a 6% reduction in traffic expectations for the remainder of the year.
Restaurant level operating profit margins contracted 80 basis points to 11.8%, impacted by elevated commodity inflation and higher labor costs.
positive_highlights: Guest satisfaction scores reached parity with the casual dining industry for the first time in nearly nine years.
The relaunched Red Robin Royalty Program significantly outperformed expectations, driving a 1.4% lift to comparable restaurant revenue and increasing new member sign-ups by 156% year-over-year.
Operational improvements reduced false waits from 10% in Q2 2022 to just 1% in Q2 2023.
summary: Red Robin reported Q2 FY2024 total revenue of $300.2 million, a slight increase from the prior year but with comparable restaurant revenue declining 0.8% excluding loyalty program benefits due to a broad consumer slowdown. Management lowered full-year guidance for traffic and Adjusted EBITDA, citing a shift in consumer trends mid-quarter and higher-than-expected commodity inflation and labor costs. While operational metrics like guest satisfaction improved significantly, the company expects Q3 and Q4 traffic to decline before a potential rebound in 2025.

negative_highlights: Fleet operational utilization fell to 87.7% from 89.6% YoY.
Unrealized loss on warrants of $14.5 million in Q2 2024 (noncash).
Crude tanker spot rates weakened in Q2, with earnings down 13% on average.
positive_highlights: Net revenues increased 403% YoY and TCE up 185% in Q2 2024.
Adjusted EBITDA up 555% in H1 2024; adjusted net income up 1,790%.
Paid off $38.7 million balance on Aframax tanker without bank debt in July 2024.
summary: C3is reported Q2 2024 net revenues of $10.8 million, up 403% YoY, with adjusted net income of $2.9 million versus a loss of $0.4 million in Q2 2023. Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $4.9 million versus $0.3 million a year ago. First-half adjusted EBITDA was $11.3 million (up 555% YoY) and adjusted net income was $7.3 million (up 1,790%). The Aframax tanker contributed about 80% of revenues. Management raised no formal guidance but expressed confidence in favorable earnings momentum and affirmed fleet growth strategy.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue collapsed 93% YoY to RMB45.1 million from RMB675.4 million.
Q3 revenue guidance of RMB20-25 million implies a further sequential decline of over 50% from Q2 and a drastic YoY contraction.
The company is strategically winding down its legacy auto-financing business, with outstanding loan balance down to RMB6.2 billion and credit-risk-bearing loans reduced.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP adjusted net income per ADS was RMB0.87, with net income of RMB86 million and a net recovery on credit provisions of RMB33 million.
AutoCango.com attracted over 180,000 visits and 20,000+ registered users across 207 countries since March 2024 launch.
Cango U-car holds over 260,000 vehicle listings and facilitated 266 vehicle transactions and 124 auctions in Q2.
summary: Q2 2024 total revenue fell sharply to RMB45.1 million from RMB675.4 million a year ago, while net income improved to RMB86 million from a loss, aided by a net recovery on credit provisions of RMB33 million. The company issued Q3 revenue guidance of RMB20-25 million, implying a sequential decline and halving year-over-year levels. Management is pivoting to used-car platforms (Cango U-car and AutoCango.com), with modest early traffic and transaction volumes, but the legacy auto-financing business continues to shrink.

negative_highlights: No revenue generated in Q4 FY2024 as commercial sales have not yet commenced
Production limited to one note weakness in ton per day due to maintenance issues and enclosure work required for bagging section
Ongoing teething pains including heat exchanger leaks, screw conveyor design revisions, and plant downtime
positive_highlights: Raised $10 million in capital ($4M equity, $6M convertible notes) providing runway through early 2025
Achieved head grades of 5.5% to 6% boric acid at the small-scale facility with zero safety incidents
Advanced customer qualification program with positive feedback from two specialty glass customers
summary: Management reported zero revenue for Q4 FY2024 as the company is in a pre-commercial production phase focused on engineering and customer qualification rather than sales. The company raised $10 million via equity and convertible notes to fund operations through early 2025, targeting completion of Phase 1 commercial engineering by December/January 2025. While small-scale facility testing achieved head grades of 5.5% to 6%, production is currently limited to one short ton per day due to ongoing teething pains and modifications.

negative_highlights: Chaveroo wells cost more than expected due to unusually high fluid losses during drilling and completion.
Delhi production was negatively impacted by a field-wide power outage for 7 days and CO2 recycle compressor downtime in May.
Natural gas revenue declined significantly due to historically low pricing environments.
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 17% year-over-year to $21.2 million driven by higher oil and NGL revenue.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 12% sequentially to $8 million due to reduced operating costs from lower CO2 purchases.
Cash flow from operations turned positive at $8 million compared to cash used of $400,000 in the prior year period.
summary: Fiscal Q4 FY2024 revenue was $21.2 million (up 17% YoY) with net income of $1.2 million and adjusted EBITDA increasing to $8 million despite low natural gas prices. The company generated record liquids production driven by acquisitions in SCOOP/STACK and Chaveroo, which added significant reserves but also incurred higher-than-expected drilling costs at Chaveroo due to fluid losses. Management maintained a strong tone regarding future growth potential while acknowledging temporary operational headwinds like CO2 pipeline downtime.

negative_highlights: FY24 revenue declined 2.8% YoY due to migration from lower-margin onshore regions and macro headwinds in telecom/fintech
DSO increased to 72 days, up from 63 days prior year
positive_highlights: Record FY24 adjusted EPS of $2.10, up from $1.96 last year
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 12.8% in FY24 (up ~310 bps over four years) and is expected to reach low teens in FY25
Won 18 new client relationships, nearly double the prior year's count of 10
summary: FY24 revenue decreased slightly by 2.8% to $509 million while adjusted EPS beat expectations at $2.10 (up from $1.96). The company raised FY25 guidance for revenue ($510M-$525M) and Adjusted EBITDA ($67M-$69M), citing an inflection point in top-line growth driven by higher-margin offshore/nearshore regions and new AI services.

negative_highlights: Gross profit declined 32.2% to $2.71 million as management reduced premiums to compete in a disrupted market.
Net loss of $1.62 million marks a shift from a prior period gain, driven by margin compression and higher operating costs.
Operating expenses rose 64% to $4.12 million due to strategic investments in network expansion and new biofuel supply chains.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 44.4% YoY to $277.2 million driven by a 39.4% increase in sales volume.
Biofuel revenue surged 95.8% YoY with volumes up 84.6%, reflecting strong demand for sustainable fuels.
Company maintains a debt-free balance sheet with cash increasing 30.9% to $9.7 million.
summary: CBL International reported H1 FY2024 revenue of $277.2 million, a 44.4% year-over-year increase driven by a 39.4% surge in sales volume and network expansion to over 60 ports. However, gross profit declined 32.2% to $2.71 million due to reduced premiums offered to capture market share amidst Red Sea crisis-induced competition, resulting in a net loss of $1.62 million compared to a prior period gain. Management maintains a cautiously optimistic outlook for the remainder of 2024, citing continued demand from rerouted vessels and strong growth in biofuels, while acknowledging that operating expenses rose 64% due to strategic investments in new geographic areas and sustainable fuel operations.

negative_highlights: Revenues decreased by approximately $1.4 million (91%) year-over-year due to the absence of equity-based contract revenues
Operating loss increased significantly from roughly $750k in Q1 FY2024 to approximately $2.5 million in Q1 FY2025
Management admitted holding off on a broader launch of the secondary trading platform due to usability issues and regulatory factors
positive_highlights: Regained compliance with NASDAQ Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) bid price rule, allowing continued trading on the exchange
Launched a beta version of the secondary trading platform through Templum ATS approved in over 50 U.S. states and territories
Filed application for broker-dealer registration with FINRA to offer Reg A+ and Reg D deals
summary: Netcapital reported a significant miss in Q1 FY2025 with revenues declining approximately 91% to $142k and an operating loss widening to roughly $2.5 million from the prior year's $749k. Management attributed the revenue drop primarily to a cessation of equity-based contracts, which generated over $1.1M in Q1 FY2024 but yielded zero this quarter due to strategic shifts away from that model. The company disclosed an ATM agreement and maintained its NASDAQ listing compliance while delaying the broader launch of its secondary trading platform.

negative_highlights: Q1 FY2025 guide of $93-99 million revenue reflects muted U.S. Tier 1 and Africa CapEx; down sequentially.
Material weakness in internal controls caused delayed 10-K filing; management apologizes.
Full-year FY2025 guidance delayed; backlog only slightly up year-over-year to $292 million.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 28% year-over-year to $116.7 million; international revenue up 67%.
Pasolink acquisition accretive to adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP net income; Pasolink revenue grew to $25 million in Q4.
Private networks achieved highest quarterly revenue in 11 quarters; FY2024 gross margins expanded to 38% from 36.1%.
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $116.7 million, up 28.1% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.72 and adjusted EBITDA of $11.9 million. The Pasolink acquisition was accretive to adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP net income, and Pasolink revenue grew to $25 million. However, management guided Q1 FY2025 revenue to only $93-99 million due to muted U.S. Tier 1 CapEx and Africa spending, with a recovery expected in later quarters. The company also disclosed a material weakness in internal controls related to accounting personnel turnover, leading to a delayed 10-K filing, and will not provide full-year guidance until later.

negative_highlights: Management expects loan growth to moderate in Q4 after recent strong quarters
Noninterest expense from oil and gas assets is expected to peak in Q3 with $1M impact continuing into Q4
Deposit mix shifts have largely slowed across the client base
positive_highlights: Record earnings and EPS achieved through normal operations without share buybacks
Strong liquidity position with two meaningful sources of additional liquidity (FHLB and new Fed facility)
Net interest income grew over 20% YoY, allowing for a large increase to the cash dividend
summary: Bank7 Corp reported record earnings and EPS for Q3 FY2024 driven by strong loan growth in a moderate to high single-digit annualized range. Management expressed cautious optimism regarding the upcoming election but noted choppy waters ahead due to storm devastation on the Eastern seaboard, though they remain comfortable with their liquidity position including two backstops (FHLB and new Fed facility). Net interest income grew 20%+ YoY despite rate cuts, while noninterest expense is expected to peak in Q4 before normalizing.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined year-over-year, dropping by approximately $200k from the prior period's $6.6 million.
Cash balance decreased to $1 million at quarter end compared to $2.1 million in the same period last year.
Inventory levels rose substantially to $6.1 million (from $4.4 million) as a strategic buildup for the holiday season.
positive_highlights: Gross profit improved significantly from $0.4 million to $0.6 million due to price increases and operating efficiency gains.
Net loss decreased by approximately $0.3 million year-over-year, improving EPS from a loss of $0.16 to a loss of $0.11 per share.
Company secured a new $6 million credit facility to retire previous debt and fund growth initiatives.
summary: Total revenue for Q2 FY2025 was $6.4 million, a decrease from $6.6 million in the prior year period. Net loss narrowed to $0.7 million ($0.11 per share) compared to $1.0 million last year, driven by gross margin expansion to 11.5% and reduced costs of $7.3 million versus $7.6 million previously.

negative_highlights: Total operating expenses of $4.5M were higher than the baseline cash expense guidance due to non-recurring legal fees ($800k) and project costs.
Run-rate cost guidance for next fiscal year is lowered toward $12 million, with management now targeting a range closer to $11 million.
Liquidity runway relies on closing Reed deal in November; without it, the company has only ~$4.4M cash plus board loan until mid-February.
positive_highlights: Reed Financing transaction is on track to close in November with Societe Generale acquiring a 75% stake for $250M initial commitment (potential up to $350M).
India project site selection finalized in Gujarat province, utilizing 100% biomass energy and secured feedstock from local polyester hubs.
Management identified an additional ~$1 million in annual savings opportunities via productivity initiatives and government incentives.
summary: Loop Industries reported Q2 FY2025 total operating expenses of $4.5 million, which exceeded the guided baseline cash expenses due to non-recurring items including $800k in legal fees and project costs; excluding these reconciliatory items ($3M), run-rate guidance for next fiscal year is lowered toward $11 million from a prior expectation closer to $12 million. The company confirmed it has sufficient liquidity, bolstered by a potential $2M board loan and an imminent Reed Financing closing in November, to cover working capital needs through February 2025 before the India facility construction accelerates.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined 2% year-over-year
Revenue slightly below expectations
U.S. revenue down against expectations due to advertiser timing
positive_highlights: Operating income increased 30% year-over-year
Jack's Flight Club revenue up 11% and premium subscribers up 14%
Europe margin expanded to 17%, approaching North America
summary: Travelzoo's Q3 2024 revenue was $20.1 million, down 2% year-over-year, slightly below expectations, but operating income rose 30% to $4 million with non-GAAP operating profit up to $4.9 million. Membership fee revenue remains small but is expected to drive substantial growth in 2025 as legacy members become paying members. Jack's Flight Club grew revenue 11% and premium subscribers 14% year-over-year, with plans for further expansion. Management expects Q4 revenue growth and higher profitability, and maintains a disciplined approach to costs and investments.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined by 4% in China due to decreased average spend per customer
Management anticipates a continued challenging operating environment through the remainder of fiscal year 2024
EPS was higher than anticipated but margins are expected to be lower in Q4 due to increased promotional spending
positive_highlights: Active customer counts increased by 7% year-over-year in China despite sales decline
Successful American-Europe Convention generated positive feedback on rebuilding trust with associate leaders
New products including Celavive Resurfacing Serum and Whey Protein Isolate launched successfully
summary: Third quarter net sales fell modestly short of internal expectations due to a challenging operating environment in key markets like China, where active customer counts rose by 7% but average spend declined causing a 4% drop in net sales. Management lowered fiscal 2024 guidance citing continued headwinds and plans for increased promotional activity in Q4 which will impact margins. While the company remains confident in its long-term strategy and new product pipeline, immediate financial results were weak.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net income down 8.4% YoY due to higher tax provisions
Betterware Mexico gross margin fell to 54.8% from 56.2% on peso and freight costs
Temporary Shopify adoption disruption affected Jafra U.S. activity in September
positive_highlights: Net revenues up 6.6% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 11.7%
Jafra U.S. revenue up 11.7% in peso, second consecutive quarter of growth
19th consecutive dividend payment announced
summary: BeFra reported Q3 2024 net revenues up 6.6% YoY and adjusted EBITDA up 11.7% to MXN 592 million, with EBITDA margin expanding 81 bps to 17.8%. Growth was driven by all units, with Jafra Mexico up 9.2% and Betterware Mexico up 3.2%, but adjusted net income fell 8.4% due to tax provisions. Gross margin was pressured by peso depreciation and higher freight costs, though management expects 58-59% gross margin in Q4 and reaffirms full-year guidance. The company also paid its 19th consecutive dividend and is expanding internationally.

negative_highlights: Weather-related losses totaled $24.4 million, including $6 million from Hurricane Helene, impacting the loss ratio.
Policies-in-force declined 7.3% due to intentional new business reductions and a run-off of legacy personal lines in Maryland.
Workers' compensation frequency trends are steepening, with ongoing pressure from wage inflation.
positive_highlights: Net income reached $16.8 million, the highest level since 2020, despite weather-related headwinds.
Core loss ratio declined 6.6 percentage points to improve underwriting profitability across all lines of business.
Expense ratio decreased by approximately half a point excluding incentives, reflecting successful cost reduction initiatives.
summary: Donegal Group reported Q3 FY2024 net premiums earned of $238 million (up 6% YoY) and net income of $16.8 million ($0.51 EPS), marking the highest quarterly earnings since 2020 despite $6 million in pre-tax catastrophe losses from Hurricane Helene. The combined ratio improved to 96.4% driven by a core loss ratio decline of 6.6 percentage points and favorable reserve development, while expense ratios remained stable at 34.5%. Management expressed confidence in executing strategies for profitable growth in 2025, including small business expansion and systems modernization.

negative_highlights: Loan demand is not strong; loan outstandings were relatively flat compared to Q2 despite vertical construction growth
Net income for the first nine months of 2024 ($17M) was lower than the same period in 2023 ($19.6M)
Anticipated payoffs from large C&I customer sales and commercial advances will reduce loan balances
positive_highlights: Net interest margin expanded 5 basis points this quarter compared to the second quarter of 2024
Core deposit balances increased approximately 7% year-to-date, driven by public funds, commercial, and retail activity
Credit quality remains very strong with zero past dues in the commercial real estate portfolio
summary: West Bancorporation reported Q3 FY2024 net income of $6 million (up from $5.2M in the prior quarter) and a Net Interest Margin expansion of 5 basis points to 18% year-to-date, though total loan outstandings remained relatively flat at over $3 billion compared to the second quarter. Management noted that while deposit gathering is successful with core deposits up ~7%, loan demand remains weak due to limited new projects in commercial real estate and anticipated payoffs from construction advances closing down assets.

negative_highlights: Global retail sales down 13% in Q3; consolidated revenue down 26%
Wholesale shipments down 39% to 27,500 units, driving operating margin down to 9.2%
Full-year guidance revised lower due to weaker-than-expected retail demand
positive_highlights: Touring segment up almost 10% in U.S. with 4+ points of market share gain
HDFS operating income up 29% to $77 million in Q3
Productivity program delivered $84 million through Q3, on track to $400 million goal
summary: Q3 2024 was challenging for Harley-Davidson due to macroeconomic headwinds, with global retail down 13% and consolidated revenue down 26%. The company revised its full-year outlook and is focusing on inventory reduction and cost productivity. Despite the downturn, touring segment gained market share and HDFS performed well, while LiveWire adjusted guidance to 600-1,000 units and announced plans for a new product segment.

negative_highlights: Sequential revenue decline of 24% due to weak bookings in July
Industrial projects moving more slowly than originally anticipated, delaying deployment until late 2025/early 2026
EBITDA turned negative at $-500k compared to positive $870k in the preceding quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue increased by 21% YoY to $3.9 million
Gross margin expanded to 49%, up from 44% prior year and 51% sequentially
Operating loss narrowed to $1M compared to a $1.4M loss in Q3 2023
summary: Q3 revenue grew 21% YoY to $3.9 million but fell 24% sequentially due to weak July bookings and uneven distribution across the quarter. The company reported an operating loss of $1 million (improving from $1.4M prior year) with gross margins expanding to 49%. Management raised $1 million in convertible notes for working capital, noting that industrial projects are moving slower than anticipated.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin declined 6 basis points (FTE) due to excess liquidity, estimated 6 bps drag from cash
Nonperforming loans increased during the quarter, though metrics remain favorable
Loan early payoffs negatively impacted NIM by another 6 basis points
positive_highlights: Net income up 21% sequentially, EPS up over 19% — fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
Total revenue up over 4% sequentially and 36% year-over-year, with record SBA gain-on-sale revenue
Deposit costs stabilized; CD pricing inflection point reached, new CD rates down 28 bps vs maturing CDs
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q3 2024 net income of $7 million, up 21% sequentially, and diluted EPS of $0.80, up over 19%, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings growth. Revenue grew over 4% sequentially and 36% year-over-year, driven by record SBA gain-on-sale revenue and a 25% year-over-year increase in net interest income. Net interest margin declined 6 basis points to 1.70% on a fully taxable equivalent basis due to excess liquidity, but management expects margin rebound in Q4 as deposit costs decline following Fed cuts. Loan growth was 7.5% annualized, deposits surged 12%, and tangible book value per share rose 3.6% sequentially and nearly 11% year-over-year. Guidance implies continued earnings growth in Q4 and 2025, with management confident in lower deposit costs and improved loan mix.

negative_highlights: Core pretax pre-provision earnings fell to $9.3M from $10.6M on an adjusted basis
Accounting error and delayed SEC filings create ongoing uncertainty
Cost of funds peaked in August; only modest rate cuts implemented so far
positive_highlights: Core bank cost of deposits improved to 2.21% from 1.97% a year ago
Mortgage locked loans up 67% YoY in Q3, reaching $1 billion annual run rate
New commercial relationship pipeline is 3x year-ago level
summary: Primis Financial reported Q3 2024 core pretax pre-provision earnings of $10 million, up from $9.4 million in Q2, but adjusting for accounting changes core PPNR fell to $9.3 million from $10.6 million. The company is correcting a consumer loan accounting error, with SEC consultation open; it targets being fully current on filings by mid-November. Margins improved to 2.97% from 2.72% on interest catch-up, while core expenses declined slightly. Management is replacing the Life Premium Finance portfolio with higher-yielding mortgage warehouse loans, expects margin lift, and projects reaching a 1% ROA by late 2025.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 4% YoY in Q3, and full-year trend is toward the higher end of decline (~9%)
Free cash flow negative $92M first nine months vs negative $18M prior year
Loss of a large grocery client and softer CPG demand noted
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin up 54 bps to 8.7% in Q3
Adjusted diluted EPS more than doubled to $0.26 vs $0.11
Debt leverage expected to improve to ~1.5x by year-end, below target range
summary: Quad reported Q3 2024 net sales of $675 million, down 4% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up to $59 million from $57 million and adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 54 bps to 8.7%. Adjusted diluted EPS rose to $0.26 from $0.11. Full-year net sales are trending to a ~9% decline, at the higher end of the guidance range, but management maintains midpoints for adjusted EBITDA ($225M) and free cash flow ($60M). They announced a definitive agreement to watch majority of European operations for ~$45M enterprise value, expected to close by year-end, and now expect net debt leverage of ~1.5x versus prior 1.8x. Free cash flow was negative $92M in the first nine months, down from negative $18M, due to nonrecurring 2023 inventory benefits.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed by approximately $1 million despite the strong Q3 beat.
SG&A expenses surged 38% YoY to $21.6 million, primarily driven by increased headcount and compensation costs.
Net loss per share widened significantly from $0.43 in prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 28% in the US Heart Failure business driven by expansion into new sales territories and accounts.
Secured two significant reimbursement wins: DRG reassignment increasing inpatient payments from ~$23k to ~$43k, and approval of Category 1 CPT codes effective Jan 1, 2026.
Active implanting centers increased to 208 at quarter end compared to 159 a year ago.
summary: CVRX reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $13.4 million (up 27% YoY) and a net loss widening to $13.1 million ($0.57/share). Management raised full-year guidance slightly, narrowing the range from prior expectations to $50.5-$51.5 million due to Q4 outlook adjustments despite strong operational momentum.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS for first nine months down to $4.50 from $5.66 in 2023.
Early POS data shows soft note-through across the industry.
About 1% of year-over-year sales decline attributable to retailer credit deterioration.
positive_highlights: All three toy consumer products divisions delivered year-over-year sales increases in Q3.
Gross margin above 33% in the quarter, with full-year guidance of at least 30%.
Remained debt-free with no credit line drawdown at quarter end.
summary: Q3 2024 was a seasonally strong quarter with net sales slightly above the prior year, as all three toy/consumer product divisions grew. Adjusted EPS was $4.79 for the quarter, down from $4.75 last year, with gross margin above 33%, and trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA of $58.5 million (8.5% margin). Management reiterated full-year gross margin guidance of at least 30% and highlighted continued debt-free status, but flagged soft industry watch-through and concerns about retailer creditworthiness, with about 1% of sales decline from credit issues. Capital allocation plans remain undecided.

negative_highlights: Full-year sales guidance lowered to low end of $450-$460 million range
Q3 sales down 2.4% (excluding non-recurring) and adjusted EPS down to $0.77
XTRATUF inventory shortages left several million dollars in sales on the table
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin up 110 basis points to 38.1%
Durango and XTRATUF US growth double-digit; Lehigh sales up double-digits with 200 new accounts
Spring bookings robust for Durango and XTRATUF; strong Q4 start for Muck
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q3 sales of $114.5 million, down 2.4% excluding non-recurring items, and adjusted EPS of $0.77, below prior-year's $1.09. Management lowered full-year sales guidance to the low end of the $450-$460 million range, citing warm weather, less promotional activity, and XTRATUF inventory shortages. Durango, XTRATUF, and Lehigh saw double-digit growth, but Muck and Georgia were weak. Gross margin improved 110 bps to 38.1%, and interest expense fell to $3.3 million from $5.8 million.

negative_highlights: Americas segment sales declined sequentially due to Hurricane Helene impacts, which pushed approximately $1.5 million in revenue into Q2.
Asia segment net sales fell 2% year-over-year driven by struggling economic conditions in China and pricing pressure.
Adjusted EBITDA for the upcoming quarter is expected to be negative ($4M-$2M) due to holiday seasonality.
positive_highlights: Consolidated net sales grew 6% year-over-year to $147.4 million, driven by strong performance in the Brazil segment (up 15% YoY).
Beyond Apparel initiatives are gaining traction with significantly better margins than traditional apparel products.
New REPREVE innovations like ThermaLoop received overwhelmingly positive customer and media response.
summary: Consolidated net sales were $147.4 million, up 6% year-over-year but down 6% sequentially due to seasonality and a ~2% impact from Hurricane Helene in the Americas segment. Management reiterated fiscal 2025 guidance for top-line growth of approximately 10%, citing cost reductions and new product traction as drivers despite softness in Asia.

negative_highlights: O&M expenses increased by $58 million YoY due to wildfire mitigation and storm damage.
Full-year O&M forecast revised upward to a 3%-4% increase relative to 2023 levels.
Interest charges decreased earnings by $0.08/share driven by rising rates.
positive_highlights: Ongoing earnings beat at $1.25/share driven by rate case outcomes (+$0.25) and AFUDC (+$0.04).
Reaffirmed 2024 guidance of $3.50-$3.60 EPS despite higher O&M costs.
Initiated strong 2025 earnings guidance range of $3.75 to $3.85, implying ~7% growth from the prior year's midpoint.
summary: Xcel Energy reported Q3 ongoing earnings of $1.25 per share, beating the prior quarter's $1.23 and reaffirming its full-year 2024 guidance range of $3.50 to $3.60 while initiating a new 2025 guidance range of $3.75 to $3.85 representing approximately 7% growth from the prior year's midpoint. Management updated their five-year capital investment plan to $45 billion, reflecting annual rate base growth of 9.4%, and raised long-term EPS growth objectives to a range of 6% to 8%. The company noted that O&M expenses increased by $0.09 per share due to wildfire mitigation and storm costs, leading to a revision in the full-year O&M forecast.

negative_highlights: Oilsands revenue declined year-over-year, with scope changes and deferred work limiting visibility; 2025 oilsands guidance is withheld pending contract finalization.
Canadian utilization target of 75% was pushed off by a year to end-2025.
Free cash flow was only $11 million due to a $32 million working capital draw and $12 million spent on capital work in progress.
positive_highlights: Record Q3 EBITDA of $106 million, up 75% from the prior Q3 record, with a 29% margin.
Backlog increased ~$300 million sequentially to $3.1 billion, with bid pipeline exceeding $10 billion.
Australia fleet utilization hit 84% in Q3, peaking at 88% in July, and 25 trucks moved to Australia are expected to contribute $10-20 million incremental EBITDA in 2025.
summary: Q3 2024 delivered record EBITDA of $106 million (29% margin) and adjusted EPS of $1.17, driven by Australia (MacKellar) achieving 84% utilization and operating at above 20% gross margins. Canadian utilization recovered to 51% from 42% in Q2, but oilsands revenue remained down year-over-year. Backlog rose about $300 million quarter-over-quarter to $3.1 billion, with management expecting year-end backlog to stay above $3 billion. Guidance for 2024 is unchanged, and management expects 2025 EBITDA to increase meaningfully on Australia growth and stable oilsands, while Canadian utilization is targeted to reach 75% by end-2025.

negative_highlights: Q3 U.S. seasonality was more pronounced than the prior year's 'anomaly'.
Management not guiding to 2025 yet, suggesting growth catalysts are later.
LungTraX platform not yet generating direct revenue; adoption will take time.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% year-over-year, with U.S. up 17% and international up 12%.
Added 15 new U.S. accounts, ending Q3 with 280 active accounts.
Year-to-date patient engagement up 150% to over 34,000 potential patients.
summary: Pulmonx reported Q3 2024 worldwide revenue of $20.4 million, up 15% year-over-year (15% constant currency), with U.S. revenue of $13.8 million (up 17%) and international revenue of $6.6 million (up 12%). Gross margin was 74%, flat year-over-year. Total operating expenses increased 3% to $29.2 million. The company reaffirmed full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $81-84 million, implying ~20% growth at the midpoint, and noted the launch of LungTraX Connect and Detect pilots into select centers. Management expressed confidence in commercial execution but highlighted early innings for strategic initiatives and expects material contributions from Japan only in 2026.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 70 bps to 37.5% due to mix shift from cushioning to void-fill
Europe/APAC environment remains uneven and sluggish, especially in Germany and Poland industrial sectors
Input cost environment expected to rise in coming quarters as paper indices increased mid-single-digits
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 10.5% constant currency; volumes up 14.7% YoY
North America revenue up 15.5% on strong strategic account activity and plastic-to-paper switch
Automation bookings year-to-date up 60%; Q4 expected to set record; 2025 visibility highest ever
summary: Ranpak reported Q3 FY2024 with strong double-digit top-line and adjusted EBITDA growth, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of volume growth. North American net revenue surged 15.5% (constant currency) driven by strategic accounts and e-commerce plastic-to-paper switching, while Europe/APAC grew 7.1% with volumes up 9%. Gross margin came in at 37.5% (down 70 bps YoY) due to mix shift toward void-fill and pricing pressure, but adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 21.6%. The company reiterated full-year guidance, highlighted record automation bookings expected in Q4, and noted strong progress on deleveraging (net leverage down to 4.0x). Management expressed optimism about 2025, citing robust backlog and visibility.

negative_highlights: Operating profit decreased significantly due to one-time pension termination expense of $7.6 million and stock-based comp increase
Net income dropped from $10.3M YoY to $1.9M primarily driven by the non-cash charges mentioned above
Global commercial revenue declined due to soft international markets, specifically in China
positive_highlights: Gross profit margin expanded by 190 bps to 28% driven by favorable mix and lower product costs
Revenue growth achieved despite expected average price decreases, indicating volume strength
HealthBeacon integration progressing with revenue increasing quarterly
summary: Hamilton Beach reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $156.7 million (up 2% YoY) and gross profit margin expansion to 28%, but operating income fell to $10.6 million due to non-cash pension termination charges ($7.6M) and higher equity incentive compensation ($2.9M). Management reaffirmed full-year revenue growth expectations while noting that comparisons are now normalizing, which will likely moderate reported results in the back half of 2024.

negative_highlights: Offshore segment margin fell to $72 million in Q3 from $97 million in Q1 due to rare technical issues.
Soda ash production challenges and higher maintenance spending at Westvaco; export prices expected lower in Q4.
Fourth quarter results negatively impacted by delays in offshore repairs.
positive_highlights: Offshore expansion project on schedule, with Shenandoah and Salamanca expected online in Q2 2025.
Management reiterates confidence in 2025 adjusted EBITDA growth and turning cash flow positive.
No growth capital projects identified; committed to debt reduction and preferred redemption.
summary: Genesis Energy reported Q3 2024 results that were well below original expectations due to multiple operational and technical issues in offshore and soda ash segments. Offshore segment margin dropped to $72 million from $97 million in Q1, driven by rare mechanical failures at producer fields, with repairs delayed to year-end, impacting Q4. Soda ash faced production challenges at Westvaco and softer export prices. Management reiterates confidence in 2025 growth from offshore startups (Shenandoah and Salamanca) and expects to turn cash flow positive next year, though soda ash headwinds persist.

negative_highlights: R&D revenue declined to $1.7 million from $3.9 million due to discontinued program
Total revenue growth partially driven by timing of customer orders
Forward-looking growth still dependent on ongoing customer adoption and milestones
positive_highlights: Product revenue increased to $11.2 million from $5.4 million in Q3 2023
Product gross margin improved to 61% up from 58%
Net loss reduced to $20.6 million from $34.9 million
summary: Codexis reported Q3 2024 revenue of $12.8 million, up from $9.3 million in Q3 2023, with product revenue increasing to $11.2 million from $5.4 million. Product gross margin improved to 61% from 58%. The company reiterated full-year guidance, ended the quarter with $90 million in cash, and continues to target profitability by end of 2026. Management emphasized progress in ECO Synthesis platform, including upcoming TIDES presentations and a planned GMP scale-up partnership for 2025.

negative_highlights: Consolidated sales down 20.2% YoY driven by hurricanes and high interest rates.
Labor Day event sales were down in the mid-teens compared to last year.
Closing rates remain below last year's levels due to a more deliberate consumer.
positive_highlights: Traffic improvement observed over the last month following election conclusion.
Design business grew 19% for the quarter as a percentage of total business.
Company remains debt-free with $121.2 million in cash and equivalents.
summary: Consolidated sales fell 20.2% to $175.9 million and EPS dropped to $0.29 from $1.02 year-over-year due to a cautious consumer, high interest rates, and hurricane disruptions. Gross margin decreased 60 bps to 60.2%, while SG&A expenses rose as a percentage of sales to 57.4%. Management noted traffic is improving but remains below prior levels, with closures in Florida and North Carolina impacting the quarter.

negative_highlights: Guidance for Q4 implies a sequential decline in revenue ($132-142M) and EBITDA due to seasonality and budget exhaustion.
Natural gas prices remain challenging (averaging ~$2 year-to-date), pressuring activity in Haynesville and Northeast.
International tool sales increased in Q3 but are expected to decrease in Q4, and full-year international sales are tracking lower year-over-year.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $138.2M exceeded guidance ($127-137M) and grew ~4% QoQ.
Adjusted EBITDA increased ~47% QoQ to $14.3M with incremental margins of ~79%.
Cementing market share grew ~23% QoQ in operating areas, with revenue up 12% despite lower rig count.
summary: Q3 revenue was $138.2M, beating guidance of $127-137M, with adjusted EBITDA up ~47% QoQ to $14.3M despite a 3% decline in US rig count. Cementing drove growth, increasing jobs ~9% and revenue ~12% on market share gains, while total revenue grew ~4% QoQ. Management expects Q4 revenue of $132-142M, down sequentially due to seasonality and budget exhaustion, but views Q3 results as repeatable and anticipates a moderate activity pickup in 2025 if gas prices support it. Adjusted EBITDA margins improved significantly, with incremental margins of ~79%.

negative_highlights: Biopharma services revenue fell 17% due to project completion shifting from late Q3 into early October.
Hurricanes in Florida and the Southeast disrupted testing volumes for approximately two weeks at the end of the quarter, causing a slight miss on expectations.
Sales team expansion was slightly slower than planned with an average of 63 contributing reps versus guidance to catch up by year-end.
positive_highlights: Lung diagnostic testing revenue grew 40% year-over-year driven by test volume expansion and new payer coverage additions.
Gross margins remained robust at 77.0%, consistent with the upper-70s target despite biopharma timing shifts.
Net loss narrowed to $10.3 million, representing a 6% improvement versus the prior year quarter.
summary: Biodesix reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $18.2 million (up 35% YoY), driven by a 40% increase in lung diagnostic testing revenue to $17.2 million, while biopharma services revenue declined 17%. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 guidance of $70-72M and expects adjusted EBITDA breakeven in H2 2025, noting that Q3 growth was slightly below expectations due to hurricanes affecting the Southeast sales territory. The company anticipates a sequential recovery in lung volumes for Q4 as hurricane impacts subside.

negative_highlights: B2B sales declined due to Watsons channel weakness in Hong Kong
Cash flow from operations decreased year-over-year ($3.5M vs $6.5M) driven by working capital changes
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with $25.6M reported, up 31% YoY
Gross margins expanded to 63.5%, a significant improvement over the prior year's 60.8%
Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance from a range of 10-15% to approximately 15%
summary: ChromaDex reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $25.6 million, a 31% year-over-year increase driven by record ingredient sales ($14.8M) and e-commerce growth. The company achieved profitability with net income of $1.9 million and positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.9 million, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of operational cash flow generation. Management raised its full-year 2024 top-line guidance to approximately 15% year-over-year growth from a prior range of 10-15%, citing strong momentum in Niagen Plus and e-commerce.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined YoY to $38.8M; OA Pain Management decreased 2% due to lower U.S. JNJ sales.
OEM channel (including JNJ) guided down 8-10% for 2024 and 12-18% for 2025 due to competitive pricing and reduced market access.
Recorded a $27M non-cash impairment on Arthrosurface assets; $3-$5M restructuring costs expected.
positive_highlights: Commercial channel revenue expected to grow 14-19% in 2024 and 12-18% in 2025, driven by Integrity and international OA pain sales.
Integrity surgeries grew >40% sequentially to nearly 200, with over 20% of surgeons new to Anika.
First module of Hyalofast PMA filed; company remains on track for U.S. launch by 2026.
summary: Anika's Q3 2024 total revenue was $38.8M, down $2.7M YoY, with adjusted gross margin of 65% (down 1 point) and an adjusted EBITDA of $5.4M. The quarter included a $27M impairment on Arthrosurface, recorded in Q3, as the company executed a strategic pivot: watching Arthrosurface (~$10M) and planning to divest Parcus Medical. Management lowered 2024 guidance for the OEM channel (down 8-10%) due to JNJ U.S. pricing and market access pressures, but guided commercial channel growth of 14-19% in 2024 and 12-18% in 2025. The company also announced planned headcount reduction from ~325 to ~225.

negative_highlights: Gas Cylinders sales down 4.7% year-over-year due to timing of SCBA projects
Graphic Arts divestiture delayed to H1 2025 as original buyer did not meet valuation
Pull-forward from customers (hurricane/port strike) may create demand timing uncertainty
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 22.7% year-over-year to $13.5 million, with margin up 260 bps to 14.8%
Adjusted EPS up 35% to $0.27
Raised full-year 2024 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $45M-$47M (excluding legal recoveries)
summary: Luxfer reported Q3 2024 sales of $91.4 million, up 1.2% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA up 22.7% to $13.5 million and a margin of 14.8%, the third consecutive quarter of margin growth. Adjusted EPS rose 35% to $0.27. The company raised full-year 2024 guidance, now expecting adjusted EBITDA between $45M-$47M (excluding legal recoveries) and $52M-$54M including recoveries, with adjusted EPS of $0.88-$0.94 excluding and $1.09-$1.14 including recoveries. Management remains optimistic about operational efficiency and strategic investments, while the Graphic Arts divestiture is expected to close in H1 2025 after the original buyer failed to meet valuation expectations.

negative_highlights: Southwest region adjusted EBITDA decreased significantly by 16%, attributed to a note weakness in-term shift in product service line mix driven by customer scheduling issues.
Q4 outlook anticipates a sequential revenue decline of approximately 10% to 14% due to winter holidays and budget exhaustion.
Rockies segment incremental revenue was predominantly from lower margin coiled tubing and wireline services.
positive_highlights: Q3 consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin remained stable at 15%, consistent with Q2 despite a sequential decline in average U.S. land rigs of 7%.
Northeast Mid-Con segment revenue increased by 7% sequentially, driven largely by pressure pumping and frac rentals activity.
Rockies segment revenue grew 10.6% sequentially due to incremental activity.
summary: KLX reported Q3 revenue of $189 million (up 5% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA of $27.8 million with a margin of 15%. Management noted that while the quarter was strong, they expect a sequential decline in Q4 revenue of approximately 10-14% due to seasonality and budget exhaustion. For 2025, management expressed optimism but declined to provide specific guidance numbers until after the Q4 results.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 7% YoY to $178.5M due to government program expirations and construction slowdowns.
US Telecom segment recorded a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $35 million reflecting market multiple compression.
Operating income turned negative at -$38.4 million, down from $6.8 million in the prior year.
positive_highlights: International segment achieved double-digit Adjusted EBITDA growth of 17.3% to $32.2 million despite flat revenue.
Strong free cash flow generation from operations totaling $97.4 million for the first nine months, up year-over-year.
High-speed data subscribers in international markets increased by 4% compared with last year.
summary: ATN International reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $178.5 million (down 7% YoY) and a net loss of $32.7 million ($2.26/share), driven by the conclusion of government programs, construction revenue declines, and a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $35.3 million in the US Telecom segment. Management updated its full-year guidance downward to revenues of $720-$730M (from $730-$750M) and Adjusted EBITDA of $182-$188M (from $190-$200M). While the International segment showed double-digit adjusted EBITDA growth, overall performance was weighed down by US headwinds.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 40.6% year-over-year driven by a 36.3% drop in active earning OPTAVIA Coaches.
Income from operations fell sharply to $2.1 million (1.5% of revenue) compared to $25.5 million in the prior year period.
Q4 guidance indicates continued decline with an expected loss per share ranging from $0.10 to $0.65.
positive_highlights: EPS of $0.10 per diluted share beat the high end of the guidance range of $0.10 to $0.65 loss.
Revenue met the upper end of the provided guidance range.
Gross profit margin improved 20 basis points to 75.4% despite lower volumes.
summary: Third quarter revenue was $140.2 million, a decrease of 40.6% year-over-year, while EPS beat the high end of guidance at $0.10 per diluted share. Management provided Q4 revenue guidance of $100 million to $120 million and expects a loss per share between $0.10 and $0.65 due to continued pressure on customer acquisition from GLP-1 competition. The company canceled its credit facility to save fees, citing a strong cash position of $170 million.

negative_highlights: Hurricane-related infrastructure damage caused delays in deliveries and procedural volumes for customers, impacting Q3 results.
Patient eligibility backlog within Patient Direct continues to shrink slowly but remains a headwind compared to prior year levels.
Adjusted EPS was flat with the prior year despite revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew across both segments with Patient Direct up 6% YoY driven by strong demand in diabetes and sleep supplies.
Gross margins expanded approximately 20 basis points sequentially, though they remain lower than the prior year due to a LIFO credit last quarter.
The company reduced total debt by nearly $200 million during the quarter.
summary: Owens & Minor reported Q3 FY24 revenue of $2.7 billion (up 5% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.42 (flat vs prior year). Management provided full-year guidance for revenue between $10.6B-$10.8B, adjusted EBITDA between $540M-$550M, and adjusted EPS between $1.45-$1.55. The company acknowledged that hurricane-related supply chain disruptions and patient eligibility backlogs negatively impacted Q3 performance relative to prior expectations.

negative_highlights: Oil sales down 9% QoQ due to lower prices and wider discounts
Operating netback down 12% to $34.18 per barrel
Cash balance expected to drop by ~$170 million due to i3 funding
positive_highlights: Funds flow from operations up 31% from prior quarter to $60 million
Completed i3 Energy acquisition, increasing 2P reserves by 119%
Sixth consecutive discovery in Ecuador with Charapa-B7 initial 30-day rate of 2,043 bopd
summary: Gran Tierra reported Q3 2024 with $60 million funds flow from operations (up 31% QoQ), $93 million adjusted EBITDA, and net income of $1 million. Production was flat at 32,764 bopd, while oil sales fell 9% due to lower Brent prices and wider differentials. The company completed the i3 Energy acquisition on October 31, significantly boosting reserves and adding Canadian assets, with management reaffirming 2024 guidance and expecting to issue 2025 guidance in early January.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $36 million due to high development expenses and R&D activities.
Certification timeline pushed to 2027, with flight test campaigns starting in 2026.
Production facility investment peak expected in 2026, implying increased cash burn next year.
positive_highlights: Raised $236 million in new capital since July, resulting in record pro forma liquidity of $445 million.
Completed assembly and testing of full-scale engineering prototype; flight campaign expected to start early next year.
ANAC published the basis of certification for eVTOLs in Brazil, a key regulatory milestone.
summary: Eve Air Mobility reported a net loss of $36 million for Q3 FY2024, driven by $32 million in R&D and $9 million in SG&A, partially offset by interest revenues and mark-to-market gains. The company raised $236 million in new capital since July, bringing pro forma liquidity to $445 million, which covers approximately three years of current cash consumption. Management reaffirmed its 2024 cash guidance of $130 million to $170 million, noting that higher Brazilian currency helped stay at the low end of this range.

negative_highlights: Arcadia sales down 19% YoY and adjusted EBITDA margin down 13pts to 5.8%
DynaEnergetics roughly breakeven due to $5M bad debt and inventory charges
Adjusted EPS attributable to DMC was -$0.49; guided Q4 sales and EBITDA below Q3
positive_highlights: NobelClad adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 23.2% on favorable project mix
Leverage ratio remains low at 1.18, below covenant threshold of 3.0
Automation of DynaStage assembly phase one complete; phase two early next year
summary: DMC Global's Q3 FY2024 sales fell 11% sequentially and year-over-year to $152.4 million, with adjusted EBITDA at $5.7 million (4% of sales) and an adjusted net loss of $9.6 million (EPS -$0.49). Weakness was driven by lower construction and energy activity, with Arcadia sales down 19% YoY and EBITDA margin collapsing to 5.8% from 18.8%, and DynaEnergetics roughly breakeven due to $5 million in bad debt/inventory charges. The company halted its strategic review, wrote off $142 million of goodwill, and provided Q4 guidance of $138-148 million sales and $5-8 million adjusted EBITDA, reflecting continued market challenges.

negative_highlights: Local core advertising revenue declined approximately 9% YoY due to displacement in over one-third of the footprint.
Scripps Networks division revenue fell 6% YoY, with Q4 guidance expecting a mid-single-digit decline continuing into next year.
No pay-TV contract renewals occurred in the quarter or prior two quarters, contributing to distribution revenue declines.
positive_highlights: Local Media revenue beat guidance with a 26% YoY increase driven by record political ad spending ($125M).
Company significantly exceeded EBITDA expectations due to tight expense management and strong political cash flow.
Leverage ratio improved rapidly from 6x in Q2 to 5.1x at quarter-end, with a plan to reach high-4s by year end.
summary: Scripps reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $1.7 billion (implied from segment data) with Local Media up 26% YoY driven by record political advertising ($125M), while Scripps Networks revenue declined 6% and core local ad revenue fell 9%. Management raised full-year political revenue guidance to over $340 million but maintained Q4 guidance for a decline in network revenues. The company significantly exceeded EBITDA expectations, paid down $115M of debt, reduced leverage from 6x to 5.1x, and expects further deleveraging to the high-4s by year-end.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 4%, with connected machines down 11% due to Q4 promotional planning
90-day engaged users decreased 3% as pandemic cohorts aged without sufficient new user acquisition offsetting attrition
Gross margin contracted slightly to 46.1% from 46.8% in the prior year
positive_highlights: Paid subscriber count grew 5% year-over-year to over 2.8 million
New user onboarding success improved by nearly 50% compared to a year ago in machine connection time
Cash flow from operations increased significantly to $70 million, up from $36 million the prior year
summary: Cricut reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $167.9 million, a 4% year-over-year decline driven by an 11% drop in connected machines and lower accessories/materials sales on favorable comps. Operating income fell 55% to $10.6 million as higher marketing spend and increased hosting fees pressured margins despite paid subscribers growing 5%. Management maintained full-year guidance, reiterating expectations for continued revenue declines but anticipating slight platform growth and incremental operating margin improvement.

negative_highlights: Total net revenue declined 4.6% year-over-year driven by the divestiture of WJBR and closure of Guarantee Digital.
National advertising revenue dropped 15.3% ex-political due to advertiser hesitation post-election.
Auto category revenue fell 11% year-over-year reflecting industry-wide profit squeezes from high inventory levels.
