positive_highlights: Debt reduced from $300 million to $220 million pro forma following a successful exchange offer and tender.
Digital revenue grew 11.7% on a same-station basis for the quarter as the company shifts mix away from agency business.
Political revenue exceeded budget with $8.2 million booked in Q4 year-to-date, up 23% relative to last year.
summary: Q3 same-station revenue grew 0.5% sequentially but declined 1.6% year-over-year on a same-station basis and 4.6% for total net revenue due to divestitures and the closure of Guarantee Digital. Operating income swung from negative $85.5 million in Q3 last year to positive $1.2 million this year, driven by an impairment reversal and debt reduction, though Adjusted EBITDA declined 6.9% to $5.6 million. Management noted that national advertising remains constrained with advertisers hesitant to book inventory until after the election.

negative_highlights: Operating profit declined 40% due to lower production volumes and higher costs
Global bookings down 36% year-over-year to $370 million
Full-year tax rate increased to 32% from 31%, and Nuvera revenue fell to $0.3 million
positive_highlights: Revenue grew year-over-year with average sales prices up 25%
Bolzoni operating profit improved more than 100% year-over-year
Debt-to-capital ratio improved 500 basis points to 46%
summary: Hyster-Yale reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $1 billion, up year-over-year, but operating profit fell to $33 million and net income to $17 million from $36 million a year ago, missing expectations due to supply chain constraints and product introduction issues that reduced production volumes. Bookings dropped 36% year-over-year to $370 million, and the company guided to a global market decline in Q4 and a modest decrease in 2025. Management maintained its full-year outlook for significant improvement and expects 2025 shipments roughly in line with 2024, supported by a $2.3 billion backlog, but warned production may moderate without share gains.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 13% year-over-year driven by a 13% reduction in volume mix, with nearly half of that decline attributed to customers trading down to more affordable products.
Full-year revenue guidance was cut significantly as the anticipated core revenue decline worsened from 5%-9% to 13%-14%.
The company lost a Midwest retailer business worth approximately $20 million to $25 million in sales impact for 2024 due to the customer sourcing windows from China.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin remained resilient at 8.7% despite significant volume and mix headwinds.
The company is exceeding its targeted annual cost savings, now expecting approximately $115 million versus a prior target of $100 million.
Significant progress was made in improving quality for door skin production compared to the previous quarter.
summary: Third quarter revenue was $935 million, down 13% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $82 million and a margin of 8.7%. Management revised full-year 2024 guidance downward to net revenue of $3.7 billion to $3.75 billion (from $3.9B-$4.1B) and adjusted EBITDA of $265 million to $280 million (from $340M-$380M), citing softer demand, mix shifts toward lower-priced products, quality issues, and the loss of a Midwest retailer.

negative_highlights: Q3 production and LOE impacted by a 100-year flood, causing ~800 BOE/d shut-ins and higher LOE
LOE slightly above midpoint due to storm remediation, but offset by reaffirming LOE guidance
Infrastructure projects mostly complete; Q4 capital is primarily D&C, but CapEx guidance reaffirmed at $540-580 million
positive_highlights: raised full-year production guidance by over 5% versus August and 10% above initial 2024 guidance
fifth consecutive quarter of positive free cash flow with debt paydown and share buybacks
Kallus Middle Spraberry well IP of ~1,500 BOE/d, outperforming Wolfcamp A type curve; identified ~300 Middle Spraberry locations
summary: HighPeak Energy reported Q3 2024 production averaging over 51,000 BOE/d, beating expectations and raising full-year production guidance by over 5% versus the prior August guide, to 48,000-51,000 BOE/d. The company generated positive free cash flow for the fifth consecutive quarter, paid down debt, and repurchased shares. Costs were elevated due to a 100-year flood, but LOE guidance is reaffirmed. Strong well results include a 1,500 BOE/d IP from the first Middle Spraberry well, and the company highlighted sub-$50 breakeven inventory of over 1,150 locations.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2.5% year-over-year to $15.9 million.
Biopharma revenue dropped over $2 million due to budget constraints and elongated sales cycles.
Latin America churned a large account acquired earlier in the year, partially offsetting growth elsewhere.
positive_highlights: Cash burn reduced by 39% year-over-year to $9.6 million due to strong cost management.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 73.1% despite soft revenue.
MSK-ACCESS adoption accelerated with 18 customers signed globally, including recent implementations in Q4.
summary: SOPHiA reported Q3 revenue of $15.9 million, a year-over-year decline of approximately 2.5% driven by material weakness in the biopharma segment which fell over $2 million. Despite this miss, clinical volume reaccelerated with 16% growth (17% excluding COVID), gross margin expanded to 73.1%, and cash burn improved significantly by 39% year-over-year. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $65M-$67M and adjusted operating loss guidance despite the quarterly miss.

negative_highlights: B2B co-issue channel decreased quarter-over-quarter due to unanticipated price changes by GSEs Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
Lock volumes are trending lower in the fourth quarter as mortgage rates sit in the high 6s/low 7s compared to Q3 levels.
Ongoing negotiations with Rithm regarding renewal terms for a portion of their subservicing contract.
positive_highlights: Adjusted pre-tax income of $35 million with a 31% adjusted ROE, up from negative returns in prior years.
MSR hedge delivered a net favorable benefit of $10 million this quarter and offset all but $12 million of MSR value changes over the last 12 months.
Total servicing additions reached $60 billion year-to-date with consumer direct recapture volume up 52% versus Q2.
summary: Onity Group reported Q3 FY2024 net income of $21 million and adjusted pre-tax income (PTI) of $35 million with a 31% adjusted ROE, representing sequential improvements in both metrics. The company executed significant debt restructuring transactions reducing corporate and MSR debt by over $180 million year-to-date to close the quarter at a pro forma leverage ratio of roughly 2.9:1 (down from nearly 4x). Management provided forward guidance anticipating slightly improved originations markets but noted potential servicing PTI declines due to lower float, while maintaining an early estimate for full-year adjusted ROE around 15%.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 23.2% from 36.2% year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA of -$7.7 million and non-GAAP EPS loss of -$0.87
Full-year revenue guidance midpoint lowered by $20 million and adjusted EBITDA by $14 million
positive_highlights: Q2 orders shaping up to be even stronger; record bookings possible
Trailing 12-month book-to-bill above 1
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $88.4 million, up 1.7% year-over-year, but with non-GAAP gross margin of 23.2% (down from 36.2%) and adjusted EBITDA of -$7.7 million. The company lowered its full-year FY2025 guidance to $430-$470 million revenue and $30-$40 million adjusted EBITDA, citing US Tier 1 CapEx weakness, project timing issues, and execution distractions. Management noted a book-to-bill over 1 for the trailing twelve months and expects a V-shaped recovery with Q2 orders tracking strong, potentially record bookings. They remain optimistic about private network growth, including ProVision Plus software opportunity and Aprisa 5G wins.

negative_highlights: Total advertising revenue decreased 10% year-over-year driven by an unusual high mix of harder-to-monetize G and PG rated movies in July
National attendance declined 8% year-over-year, contributing to lower national revenue per attendee (down 3%)
Q4 guidance reflects a challenging comparable due to the absence of Taylor Swift's Eras Tour demand pull from last October
positive_highlights: Revenue of $62.4 million beat guidance range of $56-58 million; adjusted OIBDA of $8.8M beat guidance of $6-8M
Scatter market revenue per attendee increased year-over-year as advertisers shifted spend closer to campaign dates
New programmatic self-serve offering saw sales up 96% quarter-over-quarter with its biggest quarter since launch
summary: NCM reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $62.4 million and adjusted OIBDA of $8.8 million, both exceeding guidance ranges but representing a year-over-year decline in total advertising revenue (down 10%) due to lower attendance and an unfavorable mix of G/PG-rated films. Management raised Q4 FY2024 guidance for revenue ($82-86M) and adjusted OIBDA ($28-30M), citing challenges from the Taylor Swift event in October last year and a soft December film slate, while expressing optimism about 2025.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell to RMB27.0 million from RMB353.6 million year-over-year, a 92% decline.
Q4 revenue guidance of RMB15-17.5 million is a further sequential decline from Q3's RMB27.0 million.
General and administrative expenses rose to RMB45.2 million from RMB34.7 million, outpacing revenue.
positive_highlights: Net income swung to RMB67.9 million from a loss a year ago, with operating profit of RMB35.2 million.
Overseas platform AutoCango.com accumulated over 370,000 page views and nearly 60,000 registered users since launch.
Net recovery on credit provisions was RMB74.4 million, helping profitability and balance-sheet improvement.
summary: Cango's Q3 2024 revenue was RMB27.0 million, down sharply from RMB353.6 million a year ago, but the company swung to operating profit of RMB35.2 million from a loss of RMB87.8 million, and net income was RMB67.9 million. Non-GAAP adjusted net income was RMB71.3 million, with basic non-GAAP EPS of RMB0.69 per ADS. The company guided Q4 2024 revenue to RMB15-17.5 million, implying continued sequential decline, but highlighted growth in its international used-car platform AutoCango.com and continued diligence on credit risk, with M1+ at 3.17% and M3+ at 1.76%.

negative_highlights: Net interest income decreased from the prior quarter due to projecting increased prepayment speeds on the residential loan portfolio given recent rate moves.
EAD per share declined from $0.19 in Q2 (implied) or previous levels to $0.17, with Arc Home contributing a specific loss of $0.02 for the quarter.
Management indicated they will likely commit less capital to agency-eligible investor loans over the next few quarters due to increased competition and stretching MBS execution channels.
positive_highlights: Book value increased by approximately 2% to $10.58 per share driven by hedge-adjusted mark-to-market gains on securitized loan and non-Agency RMBS portfolios.
Successfully retired the $86 million WMC convertible note maturity after issuing $100 million in investment grade unsecured bonds earlier in the year.
Initiated a new home equity lending segment with acquisitions of approximately $150 million and commitments for another $200 million, targeting an attractive market size.
summary: MITT reported GAAP EPS of $0.40 and EAD per share of $0.17 for Q3 FY2024, driven by mark-to-market gains but offset by a projected increase in prepayment speeds due to rate rallies which reduced net interest income compared to the prior quarter. The company deleveraged its balance sheet from 2.5 turns to 1.5 turns following the maturity of WMC convertible notes and sold Agency RMBS, ending with $120 million in liquidity. Management expressed caution regarding near-term volatility around elections but maintained confidence in their credit book resilience.

negative_highlights: Net income declined 66% YoY primarily due to $8.8 million of pretax debt refinancing costs associated with retiring Senior Notes.
Free cash flow generation was lower than the prior year period, impacted by increased working capital usage for contactless chip inventory and CEO transition-related costs.
positive_highlights: Net sales increased 18% YoY with product sales growing 25%, driven by eco-focused contactless cards and Card@Once instant issuance solutions.
Gross margins expanded 170 basis points from the prior year quarter to 35.8% due to operating leverage.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 18% YoY, with income from operations in the Debit and Credit segment rising 30%.
summary: CPI Card Group reported Q3 FY2024 net sales growth of 18% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 18%, driven by a 25% increase in product sales led by eco-focused contactless cards. Management raised its full-year outlook for both net sales (to mid-to-high single-digit) and adjusted EBITDA, citing strength across the portfolio despite ongoing channel inventory normalization. The company also updated free cash flow expectations to be slightly below 2023 levels due to working capital improvements.

negative_highlights: Fourth quarter guidance implies lower servicing revenue and absence of one-time insurance benefit
Management notes expected ongoing market challenges and inflationary vendor costs
Mortgage market volumes remain historically low, though forecast to recover in 2025
positive_highlights: First profitable quarter since Q1 2022, with adjusted net income of $7 million
Pull-through weighted rate lock volume up 19% YoY, near high end of guidance
Gain on sale margin of 329 bps, above guidance of 280-300 bps
summary: In Q3 2024, loanDepot returned to profitability with adjusted net income of $7 million, versus a $29 million adjusted net loss in the prior year, driven by higher volume and improved margins. Pull-through weighted rate lock volume was $6.7 billion (up 19% YoY), at the high end of guidance, and gain on sale margin of 329 bps exceeded guidance of 280-300 bps. The company completed its Vision 2025 cost program (reducing annualized non-volume expenses by over $730 million) and launched a new multi-year strategic plan, Project North Star. For Q4, management guides to rate lock volume of $5.5-7.5 billion and gain on sale margin of 285-305 bps.

negative_highlights: Home furnishings category, specifically Wayfair applications, fell note weakness in of expectations due to meaningful declines in application flow.
Full-year gross originations guidance was cut significantly from prior levels to a range of 2-4% growth following the Q3 miss in furniture demand.
Total operating expenses grew by 38% YoY primarily driven by a $1.5 million litigation settlement payment made in Q4.
positive_highlights: Gross originations excluding Wayfair grew 37% YoY as the company diversified its merchant base with new direct integrations like BB Wheels, Tire Agent, and PayTomorrow partnerships.
Katapult Pay (KPay) gross originations reached $16 million in Q3, representing 31% of the total base, up from a negligible presence last year.
The company achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $600k for the quarter and expects full-year 2024 adjusted EBITDA to be approximately $5.5 million.
summary: Katapult reported Q3 gross originations of $51.2 million (up 3.3% YoY) and revenue of $60.3 million (up 10%), driven by strong growth excluding Wayfair but weighed down by a soft home furnishings category that missed expectations. Management adjusted its full-year guidance, expecting only 2-4% gross originations growth for the year compared to prior higher targets, while reiterating at least 10% revenue growth and breakeven Q4 EBITDA due to ongoing macro headwinds in furniture demand.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue down 5.8% due to LED project delays
Full-year revenue growth outlook lowered to ~10%
LED lighting segment impacted by customer delays and soft new construction
positive_highlights: EV charging segment revenue grew 40% to $4.7M
Maintenance gross margin improved 2,300 bps
Strong October orders, strongest month of the year
summary: Q2 FY2025 revenue fell to $19.4M from $20.6M YoY, with strong EV charging growth (+40% to $4.7M) and maintenance rebound, but LED lighting was hit by customer project delays. Management revised FY2025 revenue growth outlook to ~10% from 10-15%, citing delays shifting revenue to the second half. They expect positive adjusted EBITDA in the second half and neutral for the full year. New contracts announced include a $25M LED supply deal and a $10M+ multi-year project.

negative_highlights: Content licensing revenue declined sequentially to $2.8 million compared to $7M in the prior quarter due to timing differences and non-cash barter deals.
Q4 guidance for adjusted free cash flow ($2-3M) is lower than Q3 actuals, reflecting management's caution regarding acceptance periods on large licensing agreements.
positive_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow hit a record $2.6 million, representing an improvement of nearly $6 million versus the prior year period.
Direct subscription revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $9.8 million driven by price increases and new partnerships with Samsung TV Plus, Amazon Prime Video Channels, Tubi, Pluto, and Roku.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 54%, up from 46% a year ago, due to reduced content amortization and lower cash costs of revenue.
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $12.6 million (up from $12.4M in the prior quarter) and adjusted free cash flow of $2.6 million, which is at the high end of guidance ($2-3M). The company raised its top-line growth outlook for direct subscriptions to 13% year-over-year while maintaining Q4 revenue guidance between $12M-$14M.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 25% year-over-year primarily due to reduced demand from SMBs in a prolonged labor market downturn.
Net loss widened significantly to $2.6 million compared to net income of $7M in Q2 and $24.1M in the prior year.
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted sequentially as operating expenses rose relative to revenue declines.
positive_highlights: Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA both came in above the high end of guidance despite significant revenue decline.
Job seeker web traffic grew by 21% year-over-year with organic growth at 23%, outperforming competitors by over 13 percentage points.
New product ZipIntro saw exceptional adoption, generating three times more quality applications per job and receiving high user satisfaction.
summary: ZipRecruiter reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $117.1 million, a 25% year-over-year decline driven by reduced SMB demand and labor market volatility. Net loss was $2.6 million while adjusted EBITDA came in at $15 million (13% margin), both figures exceeding the high end of prior guidance despite the revenue miss. Management provided Q4 FY2024 guidance for revenue between $97M-$118M ($107M midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $9M, reflecting expectations of a seasonally softer quarter continuing a prolonged downturn.

negative_highlights: Gross margins contracted to 61.2%, down from 64.9% in Q3 last year, attributed to timing differences in Medicare backlog recognition.
Operating loss increased slightly to $6.1 million compared to $4.6 million due to specific one-time expenses like clinical studies and GPS lab transition.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew organically by 21% YoY without expanding sales organization, demonstrating leverage and market penetration.
Tissue-based test volumes surged 36% YoY to over 10,000 tests in Q3, while liquid-based tests increased 24%.
Raised full-year guidance for the third consecutive quarter with a new range of $87M-$89M.
summary: MDX Health reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $23.3 million, a 21% year-over-year increase driven by organic unit volume growth across its tissue-based and liquid-based test menus without sales headcount expansion. Gross margins declined to 61.2% from the prior year due to timing differences in Medicare backlog recognition, while operating loss widened slightly to $6.1 million primarily due to clinical study expenses and GPS laboratory transition costs. Management raised full-year 2024 revenue guidance by approximately $3-5 million (from a midpoint of ~$87M) based on the strong beat.

negative_highlights: Gross written premiums were down 8% in Q3 across all segments.
Aviation line has experienced three consecutive years of market rating decline.
positive_highlights: Reinsurance segment remains the brightest spot with positive rate movement of around 5% overall.
U.S. note weakness in-tail business grew to over $100 million in gross premium and remained extremely profitable.
summary: IGIC reported Q3 FY2024 gross written premiums down 8% and a combined ratio of 86%, driven by currency impacts and reserve strengthening in the long-tail segment. Net income was $34.5 million for the quarter, while nine-month net income reached $105.1 million with a combined ratio of 80.5%. Management noted that Q3 premium declines are typical timing issues rather than a trend, but highlighted ongoing pressure in long-tail lines and competitive pricing in short-tail markets.

negative_highlights: Consumer cannabis revenue declined to $10.4 million from $12 million YoY due to prioritization of medical supply
Plant propagation adjusted gross margin fell to 19% from 22% due to seasonal timing and Orchid ramp-up
Cash used in operating activities was still negative at $24.9 million, though improved YoY
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA of $10.1 million, up 210% YoY and eighth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA
Net revenue up 29% to $81.1 million, with record medical cannabis revenue up 41% YoY
International medical cannabis revenue up 93%, now 57% of global medical revenue
summary: Aurora Cannabis reported strong Q2 FY2025 results with net revenue up 29% to $81.1 million, record medical cannabis revenue of $61.3 million (up 41% YoY), and record adjusted EBITDA of $10.1 million (up 210% YoY). International medical revenue surged 93%, now 57% of global medical revenue, and the company guided to positive free cash flow in Q3. Management expressed confidence in continued profitable growth driven by international expansion, particularly in Germany and Australia.

negative_highlights: Drug discovery revenue declined 14% year-over-year to $1.6 million due to cautious capital equipment spending.
Gross margin contracted significantly from 90% in Q3 FY2023 to 76% in Q3 FY2024 primarily due to a one-time inventory write-off related to discontinued product redesign initiatives.
positive_highlights: Core revenue exceeded internal expectations with cell therapy segment growing 39% year-over-year to $6.5 million.
PA processing assembly revenue grew 54% sequentially and was very strong at $3.4 million driven by clinical program progression.
Company signed six new Strategic Platform Licenses (SPLs) in FY2024, including a record number for the year.
summary: MaxCyte reported Q3 FY2024 total revenue of $8.2 million (up 2% YoY), driven by a strong 39% increase in cell therapy core revenue ($6.5M) and robust PA processing assembly growth, though drug discovery revenue declined 14%. Management raised full-year 2024 guidance for core revenue to at least 5% growth following the quarter's outperformance. Gross margin was impacted by a one-time inventory write-off but adjusted non-GAAP margins remain in the mid-80s.

negative_highlights: UDENYCA revenue declined sequentially by approximately 3% quarter-over-quarter due to a temporary supply interruption
Management stated they do not have a Q4 sales estimate today and will provide one in early January
Cash equivalents decreased from $117.7 million at year-end last year to $97.7 million as of September 30, 2024
positive_highlights: UDENYCA achieved 100% year-over-year revenue growth to $66 million despite the supply disruption
LOQTORZI net revenue grew 54% quarter-over-quarter following its commercial launch in nasopharyngeal cancer
Management raised full-year combined R&D and SG&A guidance range upper end to $250-$260 million due to divestitures
summary: Q3 FY2024 revenue was $68 million (implied by YoY flatness and QoQ growth), with UDENYCA net revenue of $66 million up 100% year-over-year but down sequentially due to a supply interruption, while LOQTORZI added $5.8 million in new product revenue. Management raised the upper end of full-year combined R&D and SG&A guidance from prior expectations to $250-$260 million following divestitures and cost savings. The company reiterated that UDENYCA sales will resume late November/early December after a temporary supply interruption, with no Q4 estimate provided yet.

negative_highlights: Full-year 2024 revenue guidance remains flat at $57.2M-$57.5M despite the strong Q3 beat.
GAAP gross margin contracted to 56.4% from 61.4% in Q2, attributed to product mix shifts and lower fixed cost absorption.
Operating expenses increased significantly due to a $2.2 million charge related to a batch production incident.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $16 million exceeded the top end of Q3 guidance range ($14.7M - $15.4M).
Acroname acquisition contributed $1.6 million to revenue, surpassing its specific guidance of $1.2M-$1.4M.
Secured three new automotive design wins with leading European OEMs expected to integrate chipsets starting in 2026.
summary: Valens Semiconductor reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $16 million, exceeding the top end of guidance ($14.7M-$15.4M), driven by a strong contribution from Acroname acquisitions and solid automotive design wins. GAAP gross margin was 56.4% while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.1 million, beating the guided range; however, full-year 2024 guidance remains unchanged with revenue expected between $57.2M-$57.5M. Management expressed confidence in emerging from the inventory cycle bottom and expanding market share in industrial machine vision and automotive sectors.

negative_highlights: Casino & Resorts segment adjusted EBITDA declined 15% year-over-year due to headwinds in Rhode Island and Atlantic City
C&R segment margins contracted from 33% a year ago to 28%
North America Interactive reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $11 million
positive_highlights: North America Interactive revenue grew 55% year-over-year driven by iGaming operations in Rhode Island contributing $9.7 million gross gaming revenue
UK business generated a 12% increase in revenues and achieved all-time high active customer levels
$940 million funding commitment secured from Gaming & Leisure Properties to construct the flagship permanent casino in Downtown Chicago
summary: Third quarter revenues declined less than 1% year-over-year to $630 million as Casino & Resorts revenue fell 2%, partially offset by a 55% surge in North America Interactive and growth in the UK. Adjusted EBITDA for the C&R segment decreased 15% due to headwinds in Rhode Island, Atlantic City, and Chicago ramp-up costs, while International Interactive margins expanded despite lower revenues.

negative_highlights: Core revenue declined 1% YoY, primarily driven by the exit of the risk assessment testing business which contributed only $1.9M to Q3.
Sample Management Solutions revenue decreased 16% YoY due to a soft consumer genomics market and evolving regulatory environment for diagnostic labs.
Q4 gross margin guidance is slightly lower than prior outlooks, with management citing elevated exit costs from the risk assessment business as a factor.
positive_highlights: International Diagnostics revenue increased sequentially driven by strong order trends in the HIV portfolio following WHO prequalification of OraQuick HCV Self-Test.
Sample Management Solutions revenue increased for a second consecutive quarter as key end markets show signs of gradual recovery post-COVID.
Company generated $12.7 million of operating cash flow and maintains a strong balance sheet with zero debt and $279 million in cash.
summary: Q3 total revenue was $39.9 million with core revenue of $37.8 million (excluding exited businesses) which decreased 1% YoY due to the wind-down of the risk assessment testing business; excluding that impact, core growth would have been flat at 0%. The company is exiting its unprofitable risk assessment and molecular sequencing services by end-2024 while guiding Q4 total revenue between $36 million and $38 million. Management expects a return to YoY growth in the fourth quarter for core business as international HIV demand strengthens, though gross margins are expected to remain flat at ~43% due to lower-margin international mix and exit costs.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined year-over-year due to the closure of nine restaurants and a 4.5% decline in casual dining guest traffic through Q3.
Restaurant-level operating profit margin decreased 210 basis points to 9%, driven by increased discount levels of approximately 190 basis points and lower guest counts.
Q4 guidance anticipates a 4% traffic decline and an $11 million reduction in note and G&A expenses compared to the prior year.
positive_highlights: Comparable restaurant revenue increased 0.6%, exceeding industry averages as measured by Black Box Intelligence.
Loyalty 2.0 exceeded expectations with over 150,000 new sign-ups per four-week period and the re-engagement of over 400,000 previously lapsed members.
Overall OSAT scores are up over 13 points since the North Star plan launch, reaching the highest levels since at least 2016.
summary: Red Robin reported Q3 FY2024 total revenue of $274.6 million, a decline from the prior year primarily due to the closure of nine restaurants, though comparable restaurant revenue grew 0.6% driven by higher average check offsetting traffic declines. Management updated guidance for full-year 2024 revenue to approximately $1.25 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $35-$37.5 million, citing near-term costs from promotional discounts and a fiscal calendar change that reduces Q4 sales expectations. While guest satisfaction scores improved significantly and the Loyalty 2.0 program drove strong re-engagement, management noted that traffic is expected to decline approximately 4% in Q4.

negative_highlights: Customer acquisition costs up significantly year-over-year, pressuring marketing spend
Over 50% of current members considering compounded GLP-1 due to insurance denials
Ongoing drug shortages and elevated CAC impacting clinical business
positive_highlights: Clinic member retention improved to 7.5 months in Q3 from 6.5 months in Q2
Added compounded semaglutide, driving the single highest day for clinic sign-ups in 2024
B2B channel sees positive Q4 note season with newly contracted partnerships
summary: WW International reported Q3 2024 results that were broadly on track with expectations, but acknowledged significant work ahead to revert to growth. Clinic member retention improved to 7.5 months from 6.5 months, and adding compounded semaglutide drove a record day for clinic sign-ups, though overall impact on 2024 is expected to be immaterial. Management announced a $100 million cost action plan with full run-rate savings by end of 2025, while noting elevated customer acquisition costs and ongoing medication shortages. They are not guiding 2025 yet, but expressed optimism about long-term opportunities in clinical and B2B segments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue growth still modest at 2% YoY
Media and Telecom segment revenue declined 4% YoY
Net dollar retention only 101% after 98% in prior three quarters
positive_highlights: Revenue and subscription revenue exceeded high end of guidance
Adjusted EBITDA highest since Q2 2020, fifth consecutive profitable quarter
Record cash flow from operations of $10.7M, up from $1.7M year-ago
summary: Kaltura's Q3 2024 revenue of $44.3M (+2% YoY) and subscription revenue of $42.1M (+3% YoY) both exceeded guidance. Adjusted EBITDA of $2.4M marked a fifth consecutive profitable quarter, and operating cash flow hit a record $10.7M. Full-year guidance was raised again, with expectations of positive annual cash flow from operations for the first time since 2020.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue missed expectations with a sharp 35.5% decline, primarily due to the infrastructure segment dropping 37%.
Full-year guidance remains unchanged at 'slightly lower' versus last year despite strong H1 performance and margin expansion in Q3.
Cash position weakened significantly from $80.8 million at end of FY2023 to $51 million as of September 30, 2024.
positive_highlights: Life Sciences segment (R2) revenue surged 400% YoY to $3 million, driven by Glacial fx system sales and international expansion.
Spectrum adjusted EBITDA improved significantly from a loss of $300k in the prior year quarter to a profit of $1.7 million due to new network launches.
DBM Global gross margin expanded 360 basis points YoY to 18.8%, and total adjusted backlog increased to $1.1 billion.
summary: INNOVATE reported Q3 FY2024 consolidated revenue of $242.2 million, a decrease of 35.5% year-over-year to $375.3 million in the prior period, driven by lower infrastructure segment sales partially offset by growth at Life Sciences and Spectrum segments. Adjusted EBITDA decreased to $16.8 million from $22.1 million previously due to revenue declines outweighing margin improvements. Management reiterated that full-year results are expected to be slightly lower than last year's as the second half of 2024 is projected to be lighter compared to Q3 2023.

negative_highlights: Rental income decreased year-over-year primarily due to the disposition of two properties in Q1 and sale of 14 properties
Interest expense increased by $3.2 million compared to the prior period driven by unrealized non-cash net losses on swap valuations totaling $2.4 million
Acquisition pipeline activity slowed with management citing high pricing (high-7s, low-8s) and lack of buyers limiting deal flow
positive_highlights: AFFO per share of $3.7 million is comparable year-over-year despite lower rental income
Weighted average lease term extended to 13.8 years following new extensions with WSP USA and LabCorp
Board declared a cash dividend increase for Q1 2025, raising the annualized rate from $1.15 to $1.17 per share
summary: Modiv Industrial reported Q3 FY2024 rental income of $11.6 million, a decrease from the prior year's $12.5 million due to property dispositions and sales partially offset by new acquisitions; AFFO was $3.7 million per share compared to $3.8 million in the adjusted pro forma calculation that excludes swap losses but beats the reported GAAP-equivalent of $0.34/share which is comparable year-over-year. Management highlighted a dividend increase for Q1 2025 and noted significant unrealized non-cash interest expense due to expired swaps, while expressing caution about capital markets conditions limiting acquisition activity.

negative_highlights: Total prescriptions (TRX) declined approximately 8% year-over-year, indicating underlying demand weakness despite the QoQ recovery.
Inventory at specialty pharmacies increased by ~$600k and bottles in distributor channels rose significantly, contributing to revenue inflation rather than pure sales growth.
China royalty revenues were a one-time bolus of $24.4M (up from $2.7M prior quarter) which distorts the QoQ comparison for future quarters.
positive_highlights: Net product revenue increased to $56.1M from Q2's $44.4M due to higher US ex-factory sales and a lower gross-to-net adjustment of 17.1% versus 20.4% in the prior quarter.
Cash burn turned positive at approximately -$0.1 million compared to a cash burn of $10.3 million in Q2, aided by an Ethereum loan principal payment reducing debt balance to ~$78M.
New patient starts increased 3% quarter-over-quarter and enrollments were up 10% year-over-year.
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $80.5 million ($56.1M product net), driven by a significant one-time royalty spike from China sales and inventory build-up at distributors rather than pure demand growth, which was flat quarter-over-quarter for total prescriptions but down 8% year-over-year. Management provided full-year guidance expecting positive net income of $15-17 million despite the Inflation Reduction Act impacting gross-to-net adjustments, while noting that future China sales will remain 'lumpy' and quarterly.

negative_highlights: Q3 same-store sales impacted by competitive discounting and delivery decline
Full-year comp guidance remains negative -3% to -1.5%
Announced closures of 12-14 company-owned restaurants in 2024
positive_highlights: Traffic improved to -0.8% Q4-to-date after new menu launch
New dish Crispy Chicken Bacon Alfredo is second best-note item with 2x sales of predecessor
Guest satisfaction improved 10 percentage points in six months
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q3 2024 results impacted by a difficult consumer environment, elevated competitive discounting, and a sudden drop in third-party delivery sales. They guided full-year revenue to $487-495 million with negative comps of 3% to -1.5%, and restaurant contribution margin between 12.7% and 13.3%. The company rolled out three new menu items in October, which improved traffic from roughly -6% to -0.8% quarter-to-date in Q4, and they reduced capex to under $15M for 2025 expecting free cash flow positive. They are testing new menu markups in delivery to regain traffic and announced a credit facility amendment for flexibility.

negative_highlights: Net attrition in enterprise account count offset pipeline growth, resulting in a decline in total enterprise account numbers for three consecutive quarters.
Non-enterprise ARR declined 1% YoY due to lapping prior small business plan price adjustments.
Full-year FY2025 planning targets mid-single-digit growth (approx. 4-6%) rather than the higher rates previously anticipated.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating margin expanded significantly from negative 2% in Q3 FY2023 to positive 5% in Q3 FY2024.
Enterprise ARR grew 7% YoY with ARPA up 8%, driven by prioritizing dollarized retention of largest accounts.
EMEA region revenue increased 12% YoY, emerging as the best-performing market.
summary: BigCommerce reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of approximately $84 million (up 7% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of just over $4 million, marking a turnaround from the prior year's loss. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 guidance at the midpoint ($331.7M-$333.7M) but issued early planning for mid-single-digit growth in FY2025 due to weaker-than-expected pipeline and attrition in lower-tier enterprise accounts. The company announced a restructuring charge of $9.9 million related to headcount reductions, leadership changes, and cost consolidation.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth was modest as the company replaces nearly $12 million in annualized revenue from the ended New York City COVID incentive program
Output Solutions revenues were up only 2% due to a large one-time deal in Q3 masking underlying performance, with sequential gross margin decline attributed to product mix and lack of NY benefit
positive_highlights: Total payment dollar processing volume growth accelerated to 46% from 24% last quarter
GAAP earnings significantly better than expected due to an income tax benefit reflecting higher taxable income projections
Record backlog of pending implementations and strongest pipeline in company history
summary: Usio reported Q3 FY2024 results generally in line with expectations, though GAAP earnings were significantly better than expected due to an income tax benefit from increased deferred tax assets. Total payment dollar processing volume growth accelerated to 46% YoY and transactions processed rose 31%, driven by strong performance across all electronic transaction businesses including ACH (up 22%) and Card Issuing (dollars loaded up 21%). Management highlighted a record backlog of pending implementations, the strongest pipeline in company history, and positive GAAP net income for two consecutive quarters.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $5.9 million primarily due to a $5.8 million realized loss on REO conversion.
CECL reserve increased by $21 million, bringing total reserves to approximately $146 million.
Office market remains challenged with business plans taking longer to achieve and some assets downgraded.
positive_highlights: Reduced risk-rated 4 and 5 loans by approximately 33% or $157 million compared to last quarter.
Available capital increased 11% to $134 million due to deleveraging and financing sources.
Received over $4 million in cash interest payments from nonaccrual loans during the quarter.
summary: ACRE reported a GAAP net loss of $5.9 million ($0.11/share) for Q3 FY2024, driven by a $5.8 million realized loss on taking title to a North Carolina office property as REO. Distributable earnings excluding this one-time loss were $9.5 million ($0.17/share), while the company declared a regular cash dividend of $0.25 per share for Q4. Management highlighted progress in reducing risk-rated 4 and 5 loans by approximately 33% ($157 million) and increasing available liquidity to $134 million, though they noted the office market remains challenged.

negative_highlights: Production declined by approximately 1,300 BOE/day sequentially before a one-time adjustment brought it to flat.
Net income was artificially boosted by non-cash unrealized gains on commodity derivatives rather than operational performance improvements.
Borrowing base was reduced by $5 million during the quarter's redetermination.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $25.5M met expectations, demonstrating stable cash generation from the diversified asset base.
summary: Amplify Energy reported Q3 FY2024 adjusted EBITDA of $25.5 million and free cash flow of $3.6 million, both in-line with expectations but missing the implied beat from a prior quarter's net income driven by non-cash derivative gains rather than operational volume growth. Production averaged 19,000 BOE/day, which was flat sequentially after adjusting for one-time benefits, while lease operating expenses decreased to $33.3 million due to optimization and reclassifications. Management maintained its annual capital guidance of $60-65M despite Q4 acceleration in non-operated costs.

negative_highlights: Hurricane Milton resulted in an estimated gross loss between $150 million and $200 million, exceeding the company's retention
Operating expenses increased by $9.5 million year-over-year primarily due to reduced ceding commission income
Company expects a net after-tax loss of approximately $16.2 million from Hurricane Milton in Q4
positive_highlights: Net income of $28.1 million with core income increasing by $11.4 million year-over-year
Combined ratio improved to 57.7%, significantly below the 65% target
Cash and investments grew 83.1% to $571.1 million reflecting strong liquidity
summary: American Coastal reported Q3 FY2024 net income of $28.1 million and gross premiums earned of $160.2 million, driven by a quota share step-down from 40% to 20%. The company incurred approximately $9.5 million in operating expenses due to lower ceding commissions but maintained an underlying combined ratio below its target despite hurricane activity.

negative_highlights: Canadian cannabis consolidated gross margins were impacted by non-branded spec sales, resulting in a reported margin of 26% versus an estimated 31% excluding those lower-margin items.
U.S. Cannabis business posted negative adjusted EBITDA of CAD 159,000 and net loss of CAD 192,000 due to headwinds from unregulated hemp-derived products in several states.
Sales velocity was negatively impacted by out-of-stock inventory on popular SKUs during the quarter, estimated at approximately $2.5 million in lower sales.
positive_highlights: Canadian cannabis total net sales grew 29% year-over-year to roughly CAD 15 million, driven by retail branded growth (20%) and international medicinal doubling.
Fresh Produce business achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.3M with gross margin improving 400 basis points year-over-year to 8%.
Village Farms secured #1 market share in both Ontario and Quebec, holding the top position across Canada's two most populous provinces.
summary: Village Farms reported Q3 FY2024 consolidated sales growth of 20% to $83.4 million and a net loss narrowing to CAD 800,000 (CAD 0.01/share) from the prior year's larger loss. The company delivered positive adjusted EBITDA across its Canadian cannabis segment ($6.5M), Fresh Produce business ($2.3M), and Clean Energy project, while U.S. operations remained in a small net loss but showed stabilization. Management highlighted strong market share gains in Canada (#1 in Ontario and Quebec) and the commencement of cultivation at their new Netherlands facility.

negative_highlights: Q3 product revenue only $9 million, a modest quarter despite strong order book
PALM 007 mpox trial did not meet primary endpoint
Resistance to TPOXX reported in a small number of patients, though low overall
positive_highlights: Secured $122 million in procurement orders in Q3, with $146 million outstanding at quarter-end
Nine-month product revenues outpaced prior year at $53 million
First oral TPOXX sale in Africa, expanding international reach
summary: SIGA reported Q3 2024 product revenue of $9 million, with nine-month product revenue of $53 million, outpacing the prior year. The company secured $122 million in procurement orders during the quarter, ending with $146 million in outstanding orders, positioning for strong Q4 and 2025 revenue. Net income for Q3 was $1 million ($0.02 per diluted share), and cash stood at $99 million with no debt. Management expects a new Strategic National Stockpile (SNS) contract in 2025, targeting a 5-10 year agreement with initial order, and highlighted ongoing mpox studies and a new monoclonal antibody license from Vanderbilt University.

negative_highlights: Book value per share worsened to negative $39.19 from negative $32.56
National statutory capital declined to $1 billion from $1.117 billion
Unencumbered cash at holding company decreased to $326 million from $411 million
positive_highlights: Net loss improved to $56 million from $185 million year-over-year
Adjusted net loss essentially breakeven for the quarter
National statutory net income of $19 million versus a loss of $133 million prior year
summary: MBIA reported a net loss of $56 million for Q3 2024, improved from a $185 million loss in Q3 2023, with adjusted net loss nearly breakeven. The improvement was driven by lower loss and loss adjustment expenses at National related to PREPA, though uncertainty around the PREPA bankruptcy persists with mediation extended to January 2025. National's insured portfolio declined to $26 billion, and the company holds $326 million unencumbered cash at the holding company. The company remains cautious on watching the company due to PREPA uncertainty but is open to considering seller structures with back-end payments.

negative_highlights: Affiliate and subscription revenue declined 1%, primarily due to non-recurring Showtime pay-per-view events absent this quarter compared to last year's Q3.
Licensing and other revenue fell 9% driven by lower secondary market volume, home entertainment declines, and lingering strike impacts on output levels.
positive_highlights: Paramount+ added 3.5 million subscribers, reaching a total of 72 million overall.
DTC segment achieved its second consecutive quarter of adjusted OIBDA profitability with improvement exceeding $1 billion over the past four quarters.
Digital advertising growth accelerated to 18% year-over-year in DTC.
summary: Paramount Global reported a strong Q3 FY2024 with Paramount+ adding 3.5 million subscribers and DTC achieving its second consecutive quarter of profitability via adjusted OIBDA improvement exceeding $1 billion over the prior four quarters. Total company advertising grew 2% year-over-year, driven by an acceleration in direct-to-consumer growth to 18%, while affiliate revenue declined slightly due to non-recurring Showtime pay-per-view events absent this period. Management raised expectations for full-year free cash flow and reiterated on-track progress toward domestic streaming profitability in 2025.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports revenue remains flat due to decline of largest customer and integration delays with major US operators like DraftKings and FanDuel
Management declined to provide explicit forward guidance or raise targets, preferring to wait for clarity in early next year
positive_highlights: Interactive revenue increased 40% YoY driven by strong UK and North America performance
EBITDA margins reached 38.6%, up 3 percentage points from the prior year period
Cash balance improved to $36.5 million as accounting restatement costs are resolved
summary: Inspired Entertainment reported Q3 FY2024 with Interactive revenue up 40% YoY and EBITDA rising 13%, while overall EBITDA margins expanded to 38.6%. Management expressed confidence in the consensus for full-year results but declined to provide specific forward guidance, citing a preference to wait until early next year before being more explicit on targets.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined $13 million year-over-year to $24 million due to Helene losses
Q3 net income flat at $19 million despite stronger underlying margins
Fully loaded loss ratio of 60% reflects $25 million of Hurricane Helene claims
positive_highlights: Third quarter total revenue grew 17% to $323 million
Year-to-date operating cash flow up 43% to $190 million
Full year revenue guidance raised to $1.18 billion
summary: Hagerty reported Q3 2024 total revenue of $323 million, up 17% year-over-year, with written premiums up 13% and retention improving to 89%. The quarter included $25 million of catastrophe losses from Hurricane Helene, which pressured operating income to $10 million and adjusted EBITDA to $24 million, down from prior year. For the full year, management raised revenue guidance to $1.18 billion (18-19% growth) and maintained underlying profit outlook, while adjusting net income to $65-74 million and adjusted EBITDA to $110-120 million to reflect $30 million of combined Helene and Milton losses. Management highlighted strong cost discipline, record new member additions, and growth initiatives like State Farm rollout and Enthusiast Plus launch in 2025.

negative_highlights: Combined RBC ratio estimated at 365%-385%, down from the target range; new business strain has consumed ~35 points of RBC year-to-date.
The runoff segment posted an adjusted loss of $107M ex-notables, with lower net investment income and underwriting margin.
positive_highlights: Shield annuity sales reached a record $5.8B year-to-date, up 15% YoY, and October sales were strong.
Corporate expenses down 5% YoY on a year-to-date basis, with full-year 2024 expected to be below 2023.
A pending reinsurance deal, expected to close before year-end, would bring the pro forma RBC ratio to the low end of the 400%-450% target range.
summary: Q3 2024 adjusted earnings excluding notable items were $243M, down from $346M in Q2 2024 and $275M in Q3 2023, driven by lower alternative investment returns. A $524M after-tax favorable impact from the annual assumption review lifted GAAP results. The statutory combined RBC ratio was estimated between 365% and 385% at September 30, below the 400%-450% target, with new business strain cited as a significant drag; management expects a pending reinsurance deal to close before year-end, which would bring the pro forma RBC to the low end of the target range. Annuity sales were $7.8B year-to-date (flat YoY) with record Shield sales of $5.8B (+15% YoY); corporate expenses fell 5% YoY. Management guided to lower new business strain in Q4 and beyond from hedging changes but would not provide RBC projections.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 9.1% YoY and Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted by over 8 percentage points to 11%.
Cost of service increased to 41.8% due to new center ramp-up costs, with a specific 130 bps impact from de novo openings.
Customer acquisition cost rose sequentially and YoY to $2,900 per case as marketing spend shifted back toward search channels.
positive_highlights: Revenue guidance raised with the midpoint increased from an implied ~$185M to a range of $183M-$189M despite lower quarterly results.
Same-store case decline improved significantly from -14% in Q2 to -8.1% in Q3, indicating stabilization after de novo costs normalized.
New 2023 cohort centers are performing ahead of the year-one revenue objective of $4.5 million.
summary: AirSculpt reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $42.5 million, down 9.1% year-over-year due to lower case volume and new center openings, while Adjusted EBITDA fell to $4.7 million (11% margin) from $9.1 million in the prior year quarter. Management raised full-year 2024 revenue guidance midpoint to a range of $183-$189 million but maintained adjusted EBITDA guidance at $23-$28 million, citing continued macro headwinds and seasonal Q3 weakness.

negative_highlights: Recorded $116.1M non-cash impairment charge in the quarter
International Real Estate revenues fell from $4.1M to $1.5M YoY
Strategic review of real estate businesses underway and may result in exit
positive_highlights: Revenues grew 11% YoY to $53.3M, with 97% from recurring fees
Core segment adjusted EBITDA up 62% YoY, margin from 19% to 26%
Closed $250M Allianz investment and launched private debt JV with Allianz
summary: AlTi reported Q3 2024 revenues of $53.3 million, up 11% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $9.6 million, a $12.6 million improvement versus the prior year. Core Wealth & Capital Solutions segment revenue increased 17% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA grew 62% with margin expanding from 19% to 26%. The company took a $116.1 million non-cash impairment charge, largely due to goodwill write-downs in real estate and event-driven strategy intangibles, and is reviewing strategic options for its real estate businesses with a decision expected by year-end. Management is confident, highlighting strong organic growth, the Allianz partnership, and continued cost discipline.

negative_highlights: Life Sciences Data & Solutions gross profit decreased by 13.1%
Non-school revenue fell from $7.6 million to $6.4 million due to deliberate service reduction
DSOs spiked, resulting in receivables approximately $10 million higher than expected
positive_highlights: Healthcare gross profit grew by 11.1% driven by school revenue up 16.3%
Engineering business on pace to exceed budgeted EBITDA with new substation and ethanol projects
Aerospace & Defense headcount doubled in two clients, leading to a multiyear contract award
summary: Consolidated gross profit grew by $0.5 million (3.2%) to $17.8 million in Q3 FY24, while Adjusted EBITDA increased 9.5% year-over-year to $5.6 million. Healthcare revenue rose 16.3%, driven largely by school contracts which are ramping up new business, though non-school revenue declined due to a deliberate reduction of services with one large client. Management expressed optimism for the remainder of the fiscal year and noted that cash flow is expected to improve in Q4.

negative_highlights: Net sales decreased 14.4% to $134 million
Adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 16.5%
Free cash flow was negative $2.1 million, down $23.8 million year-over-year
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margins expanded 170 basis points to 39%
Direct-to-consumer sales up 16% year-over-year
New product revenue increased 25% with 133% revenue per launch improvement
summary: Holley reported Q3 FY2024 net sales of $134 million, down 14.4% year-over-year, with adjusted gross margin up 170 basis points to 39%, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 16.5% and free cash flow was negative $2.1 million. The company cited distributor inventory normalization and improved lead times as temporary revenue drags, and noted distributor inventories have normalized. Management reaffirmed long-term targets of 40% gross margin and 20%+ EBITDA margin, while highlighting strong D2C growth, new product revenue up 25%, and a 133% improvement in revenue per new product launch.

negative_highlights: FinTech vertical declined by 13% YoY due to changing client payment support models.
Free cash flow decreased to $4.1 million compared to $6.6 million last year, driven by higher capital expenditures and longer DSOs of 75 days.
positive_highlights: Record Q1 revenue of $129.7M representing a 4.1% YoY increase, ending a period of flat-to-down performance.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 12%, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of year-over-year improvement in this metric.
Raised full-year FY2025 revenue guidance lower bound from $510M to $515M, signaling confidence in momentum.
summary: IBEX reported record Q1 FY2025 revenue of $129.7 million (up 4.1% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.52 (up 30% YoY). Management raised the full-year fiscal 2025 revenue guidance range to $515-$525 million from a prior lower bound of $510 million, while maintaining an adjusted EBITDA outlook of $67-$69 million. The quarter featured margin expansion driven by offshore growth and new AI wins.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined sequentially by 6% to $88.8 million, driven by a significant drop in marketing-driven business lines.
RPS for the Partner Network decreased 68% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter due to Google Search Partner Network volatility.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $10.3 million exceeded the high end of guidance by approximately $600k-$700k combined across key metrics.
summary: System1 reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $88.8 million (up 1% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $10.3 million, exceeding the high end of guidance by approximately $600k-$700k combined across metrics despite a sequential decline in total revenue driven by marketing-driven business volatility. Management highlighted strong performance from owned-and-operated products like MapQuest (record usage) and CouponFollow, which offset declines in Google Search Partner Network-dependent segments where RPS fell 68% YoY due to watch-side policy changes. Due to ongoing market uncertainty regarding the SPN rebound timing and holiday season dynamics, management decided not to provide Q4 guidance.

negative_highlights: Revenue down 16.8% YoY and gross margin fell to 12.5% due to $3.4M inventory charge
Sluggish growth in Germany, Italy, Netherlands; continued macro headwinds
Q4 guidance includes potential additional inventory charges and EBITDA loss remains
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue growth of 12.1% and continued momentum over three quarters
Market share gains: DC optimizer share up from 9% in 2022 to 13% in 2023
New contracts and ARR growth in EI software; strong growth in newer markets
summary: In Q3 FY2024, Tigo Energy reported revenue of $14.2 million, down 16.8% YoY but up 12.1% sequentially. Gross margin fell to 12.5% due to a $3.4 million battery inventory charge; adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $8.3 million. Management raised market share gains and strong growth in newer regions like Czech Republic and Australia, but noted sluggishness in Germany, Italy, and Netherlands. Q4 guidance is $14-17 million revenue and $6.5-8.5 million adjusted EBITDA loss, with potential additional inventory charges. EBITDA breakeven is expected in 2025, likely H2.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin contracted sharply to 0.9% due to a one-time inventory write-down of $2.8 million.
A large Clinical Solutions order was canceled for Q4 delivery, expected to lower fourth-quarter revenue.
Lab Essentials revenue decreased 2% YoY despite sequential customer growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 17% YoY driven by a 229% increase in Clinical Solutions revenue ($0.6M -> $2.0M).
Free cash outflow improved significantly to $2.4 million, the lowest level since Q2 2021.
Operating expenses declined sequentially and reached their lowest level since IPO.
summary: Teknova reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $9.6 million (up 17% YoY), driven by a surge in Clinical Solutions sales ($2.0M) and stable Lab Essentials growth despite specific customer headwinds. However, GAAP gross margin collapsed to 0.9% due to a one-time $2.8 million non-cash inventory write-down; excluding this charge, margins would have been 29.8%. The company reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $35M-$38M and lowered its free cash flow outflow forecast for the year from an implied higher level to less than $16 million.

negative_highlights: Spreads continued to compress in Q3, albeit at a slower pace
Watch list increased slightly to 5.6% of fair value
Repurchase activity remains modest relative to program size ($14M of $100M)
positive_highlights: NII of $0.58 per share fully covers regular and special distributions
Net asset value increased to $18.15 per share from $18.03
No new non-accruals during the quarter; non-accruals stable at 1.5% of fair value
summary: NCDL reported Q3 2024 net investment income of $0.58 per share, fully covering its regular and special dividends of $0.45 and $0.10 per share, with total GAAP net income of $0.67 per share including $0.09 of net realized and unrealized gains. Net asset value rose to $18.15 per share from $18.03, and the company originated $226 million of new investments, with no new non-accruals and non-accruals at roughly 1.5% of fair value. Management expressed optimism for 2025, citing moderate spread compression, expected M&A pickup, and a large repurchase program with $14 million used of a $100 million authorization.

negative_highlights: SUNRISE-3 trial did not have desired outcome
COVID-19 variants trended milder, limiting drug impact
Market research shows 94% of prescribers not satisfied with current treatments
positive_highlights: Cash runway projected into 2027
Phase II HCV lead-in cohort showed 97% SVR12
Phase III HCV program expected to start early next year
summary: Atea reported Q3 2024 results with cash of $482.8 million, down from $492.8 million at the start of Q4, and expects cash runway into 2027. The key event was the failure of the SUNRISE-3 COVID-19 trial, which did not meet expectations due to milder disease and no hospitalizations. The company is pivoting to its HCV program, with Phase II top-line results expected in early December and Phase III planned for early 2025. R&D expenses decreased mainly due to lower COVID-19 spending.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 3% year-over-year reflecting lingering macroeconomic headwinds and reduced customer expansion in the prior period.
Average paid members were flat quarter-over-quarter but decreased 5% compared to last year, indicating continued pressure on subscription growth.
positive_highlights: Total revenue beat street consensus with a $35.4M quarter-over-quarter increase driven by strong performance in adjusted EBITDA ($9.7M).
Interchange revenue from the Expensify Card surged 48% year-over-year to $4.6 million as migration to the new program accelerated.
Full-year free cash flow guidance was raised sequentially for a third time, now set at $19-$20 million.
summary: Expensify reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $35.4 million (6.3% QoQ increase) and adjusted EBITDA of $9.7 million, beating consensus forecasts despite a 3% YoY decline in revenue due to lingering macro challenges. Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance from the previous range up to $19-$20 million, citing strong performance driven by higher interchange take rates on the new card program and operational efficiencies. The company highlighted that 94% of existing card spend has migrated to the new Expensify Card program, which generates 20% more interchange revenue.

negative_highlights: SaaS ARPU declined sequentially to $307 from $333 due to introductory pricing for migrated customers.
Marketing Services billings fell 35% year-over-year as customers convert to the SaaS platform.
Recorded a noncash impairment charge of $83.1 million related to the structural decline of the marketing services business.
positive_highlights: SaaS revenue beat guidance at $87.1M, representing a 29% year-over-year increase.
Net dollar retention expanded significantly to 101%, up 900 bps year-over-year.
Raised full-year EBITDA guidance range to $33.5-$34.5 million following the Keap acquisition.
summary: Thryv reported Q3 FY2024 SaaS revenue of $87.1 million (up 29% YoY) and Marketing Services revenue of $92.8 million, beating guidance on both fronts. The company raised its full-year consolidated EBITDA guidance to $33.5-$34.5 million following the acquisition of Keap, which added over 15,000 customers and $80+ million in annualized revenue. Consolidated adjusted gross margin expanded 480 bps YoY to 65%, driven by SaaS mix and the transition of marketing services clients to higher-margin SaaS products.

negative_highlights: General and administrative expenses surged year-over-year from $3.8M to $6.1M due to non-cash stock comp for the new CEO, severance payments ($0.7M), and IP litigation costs.
Operating cash flow decreased by approximately $2 million (excluding one-time items) despite revenue growth.
Management declined to provide specific Q4 guidance or financial targets, citing ongoing uncertainty regarding business development priorities.
positive_highlights: Net product sales of $7.0M beat Q3 FY2023 ($6.5M) and H1 2024 total sales (~$22M) exceeded full-year 2023 revenue.
Achieved >90% reimbursement rates in the AYA population, validating commercial viability for a new growth segment.
Secured partnerships with major health plans (via Orsini) and academic centers to drive adoption over compounded alternatives.
summary: Fennec reported Q3 FY2024 net product sales of $7.0 million compared to $6.5 million in the prior year quarter and total H1 2024 sales of approximately $22 million, exceeding full-year 2023 revenue but missing analyst expectations for a profitable or cash-positive quarter due to significant G&A increases driven by CEO severance ($0.7M) and IP litigation expenses. Management highlighted positive momentum in the Adolescent/Young Adult (AYA) segment with >90% reimbursement achieved and new customer adoption, while noting that operating cash decreased by approximately $2 million for the period excluding one-time items.

negative_highlights: Consolidated adjusted gross profit margins decreased by 40 basis points YoY due to the partial quarter impact of acquiring Plastiq in Q3.
SMB segment margins contracted as higher credit losses and a mix shift with top resellers offset revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased by more than 20% YoY driven by organic growth in SMB, B2B, and enterprise segments.
Adjusted EBITDA reached a new quarterly record of $54.6 million with an increase of over 18% from the prior year quarter.
Plastiq acquisition is now profitable after integration, contributing to sequential margin expansion when excluding timing impacts.
summary: Priority Technology Holdings reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $227 million (up >20% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $54.6 million (a record). Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $200-$204 million, citing strong organic growth in B2B and enterprise segments which now contribute nearly 60% of gross profit. The company affirmed revenue and gross profit guidance while noting that the reported consolidated margin decline was primarily due to the partial quarter impact from the Plastiq acquisition.

negative_highlights: Capital expenditures were elevated at $2.9 million due to equipment purchases for oncology and wound care growth.
Negative pressure wound therapy equipment sales were lower due to a difficult comparison with a surge in leases from the prior year.
Chemo Mouthpiece revenue is not expected to contribute meaningfully until next year (2025).
positive_highlights: Revenue exceeded $35 million for the first time ever with strong sequential growth of nearly 5%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 22.3%, exceeding the prior year's 19.8%.
Operating cash flow surged to $9.8 million, more than double the prior year quarter.
summary: InfuSystem reported Q3 FY2024 net revenue of $35.2 million, representing an 11% year-over-year increase and nearly 5% sequential growth. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 22.3%, driven by higher-margin oncology and rental mix, while operating cash flow reached a record $9.8 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 guidance for high single-digit revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA margins in the high teens.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 18.8% year-over-year due to a 13.7% decrease in volume mix and 4.9% pricing decline.
Free cash flow was negative $5.3 million, impacted by investments in new partner brands and working capital delays.
Industry headwinds persist with oversupply in cannabis and closures of large retailers.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross profit margin expanded 130 bps to 24.3% due to higher-margin proprietary brand mix and productivity gains.
Six consecutive quarters of adjusted gross profit margins at or above 23%.
Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled compared to 2023, demonstrating profitability at lower sales levels.
summary: Hydrofarm reported Q3 FY2024 net sales of $44 million, a decline of 18.8% year-over-year driven by volume mix and pricing pressures. Adjusted gross profit margin expanded to 24.3%, marking the sixth consecutive quarter above 23%, while adjusted EBITDA turned slightly positive at $2.1 million. Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 guidance for net sales (low to high teens decline), adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened slightly to $1.2 million ($0.10/share) from a prior year loss of $1.4 million due to nonrecurring litigation and business combination expenses related to the ADA Site Compliance acquisition.
Operating expenses on a GAAP basis increased 9% YoY, though this was partially driven by one-time items rather than core spend increases.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew sequentially from $8.47 million to $8.93 million, representing a 21% annualized growth rate and exceeding high-end guidance.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly from 17% in Q2 to 23% in Q3 as non-GAAP operating expenses were reduced by 10%.
The company achieved its first-ever Rule of 40 status, with both Enterprise and Partner/Marketplace channels growing organically around 5% sequentially.
summary: AudioEye reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $8.9 million (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of a record $2 million, beating both prior guidance and consensus estimates. Management raised full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $35.2M-$35.3M and increased Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $675k (to $2.2M-$2.3M) while maintaining the Rule of 40 milestone for the first time.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted from 50% in Q3 2023 to 46% due to a higher mix of system sales.
Net loss widened slightly to $1.5M ($0.13/share) compared to net income of $2.6M last year, though this is attributed to the absence of favorable warrant valuation swings seen previously.
Q4 OUS system placements are expected to be 'one or two systems shy' of Q3 levels as backlog clears.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with a 38% year-over-year increase to $13.5 million, fueled by international expansion.
Adjusted EBITDA swung positive at $429k compared to a negative $1.4M in the prior year quarter.
Trailing twelve-month recurring revenue grew 22% to $38 million as new systems ramp up.
summary: LENSAR reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $13.5 million (up 38% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $429k (a turnaround from -$1.4M prior year), driven by the sale of 24 ALLY systems globally, including 11 outside the U.S. following regulatory clearances in Europe and Taiwan. Management expects Q4 OUS system sales to approximate the strong Q3 volume but notes difficulty beating that specific number due to backlog depletion; procedure volumes are expected to remain robust despite seasonal holidays and hurricane disruptions.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance lowered from $760M-$800M range to approximately $750M.
Non-political advertising spending slowed leading up to election day, impacting Q4 outlook and full year expectations.
Multiplatform Group revenues declined 1.1% YoY (2.9% ex-political) with adjusted EBITDA down significantly due to Olympic timing.
positive_highlights: Digital Audio Group revenue grew 12.7% YoY with podcasting EBITDA margins remaining accretive at 33.2%.
Audio & Media Services Group revenues surged 45.3% YoY, driven by digital growth and political advertising tailwinds.
Successfully entered a Transaction Support Agreement extending ~$4.1B of debt maturities to 2029-2031 while keeping annual cash interest expense flat.
summary: iHeartMedia reported Q3 FY2024 consolidated revenues of $1 billion (up 5.8% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $205 million, which was in-line with guidance but missed the top end due to a slowdown in non-political advertising near election day. Management lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance from a range of $760M-$800M to approximately $750M and expects Q4 revenues to be up high single digits, excluding political which is expected to rise slightly but not match the prior cycle peak.

negative_highlights: Surgical glaucoma revenue missed expectations with a sequential decline of 8% and lower-than-anticipated recovery from LCDs.
Dry eye pricing increase effective October 1 is expected to have a significant negative impact on cash pay procedure volumes in Q4, capping dry eye revenue below $0.5M for the quarter.
Final Medicare rule denied device-intensive status for CPT code 66174 as reported costs fell just under the 30% threshold.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating expense guidance lowered to $104M-$106M from prior range, reflecting improved leverage and lower legal costs.
Dry eye revenue ($1.5M) was ahead of expectations despite a sequential decline due to fewer new accounts and the upcoming price increase.
Cash flow turned positive at $0.4 million in Q3 compared to cash burn of $10 million in the same period last year.
summary: Sight Sciences reported Q3 FY2024 revenue of $20.2 million (1% YoY growth), missing internal expectations due to slower-than-expected recovery in surgical glaucoma utilization following LCD finalization and a sequential decline driven by seasonality, partially offset by dry eye demand ahead of an October 1 price increase. Management maintained full-year 2024 revenue guidance but lowered adjusted operating expense guidance from $107M-$109M to $104M-$106M due to lower legal expenses and improved working capital management, while reiterating the expectation for double-digit surgical glaucoma growth in Q4. The company ended with $118.6 million in cash and generated positive operating cash flow of $0.4 million.

negative_highlights: Wavelo revenue down 9% YoY and EBITDA down 18.5% YoY
Ting workforce cut by over 40% and no common equity partner found
Cash flow from operations was negative $4.6M in Q3
positive_highlights: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA up 94% to $8.7M in Q3
Ting adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.1M from $12.2M YoY
Domains gross margin up 8% YoY, value-added services margin up 26%
summary: Consolidated Q3 revenue grew 6.1% YoY to $92.3M, gross profit up 32.4% to $22.2M, and adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $8.7M from $4.5M, driven by Domains and Ting improvements. Domains revenue rose 5.9% to $64.7M with EBITDA up 5.6% to $11.5M, while Wavelo revenue declined 9% to $10.1M and EBITDA fell 18.5% to $3.4M. Ting revenue grew 19% to $15.3M, EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.1M from $12.2M, and net additions were 1,400. Management reduced Ting workforce by 40% to cut ~$22M in cash costs, stopped expansion, and expects Ting to be near adjusted EBITDA breakeven in 2025. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA year-to-date exceeded $22M, on track to approximately double from 2023's $15.5M.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $13 million from $6.6 million year-over-year due to increased clinical and development expenses.
R&D expenses surged to $10.2 million, primarily driven by the PALISADE Phase 3 program costs.
G&A expenses increased to $4.2 million due to headcount growth and professional services fees.
positive_highlights: PALISADE-3 and PALISADE-4 Phase 3 trials initiated on time with no site overlap, addressing previous variability concerns.
Significant excitement and engagement from Principal Investigators (PIs) across the research community for the new intranasal therapies.
