Management guided to 50 EH hash rate by end of Q1 2025 (from 32 EH now) and forecasts ~6,000 Bitcoins annually from the current base, while used car exports remain a secondary focus.

First quarter FY2025 adjusted OIBDA is expected to be negative ($7.5M to -$9.5M) driven by softer box office slate

summary: NCMI reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $86.3 million and adjusted OIBDA of $35 million, both exceeding their respective guidance ranges ($82-86M and $28-30M). Full-year 2024 results were slightly below prior year levels with revenue at $240.8 million versus $259.8 million in 2023. Management noted Q1 FY2025 guidance of negative adjusted OIBDA ($7.5M to -$9.5M) due to a weaker film slate and government spending delays, while expressing optimism for the second half.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue was impacted by transient supply interruptions for both UDENYCA (inventory write-downs) and LOQTORZI, limiting growth potential in a rare disease space.
Management explicitly stated they are not satisfied with the current stock price despite strong execution on balance sheet deleveraging and asset sales.
LOQTORZI revenue ramp is constrained by the rarity of nasopharyngeal cancer (1-2 new patients per physician annually) and ongoing efforts to displace off-label Keytruda use.
positive_highlights: UDENYCA net sales increased 62% year-over-year in FY2024 to $206 million, driven by supply resumption after Q3 interruptions and strong demand upon re-entry into the market.
LOQTORZI achieved NCCN preferred status for metastatic nasopharyngeal cancer following guideline updates, with new account growth of 37% in Q4 despite headwinds from divestiture uncertainty.
Strategic transformation milestones reached: SEC/CFIUS reviews completed and shareholder vote scheduled to approve the UDENYCA sale.
summary: Coherus BioSciences reported Q4 FY2024 net sales of $13 million ($46.3M for UDENYCA and $7.5M for LOQTORZI), representing a sequential decline due to supply interruptions, though full-year revenue grew significantly driven by the biosimilar franchise before divestiture. Management confirmed substantial progress on the strategic transformation, including closing conditions for the UDENYCA divestiture which is expected late Q1/early Q2 2025, leaving the company with approximately $250 million in cash post-transaction to fund oncology development. The CEO expressed dissatisfaction with current stock valuation and emphasized a focus on maximizing LOQTORZI revenue as standard of care while advancing the proprietary pipeline.

negative_highlights: Total installed cost estimate increased from a prior $950 million preliminary figure to an indicative range of $1.7 billion - $2 billion.
Project timeline delayed with best-case groundbreaking pushed to mid-2026 (if capital secured) and in-service date shifted to 2028 or later depending on FID timing.
positive_highlights: Completed FEED for Project Permian (SN1) identifying no fatal technical flaws or design issues.
summary: Net Power reported a liquidity position of $533 million at year-end Q4 FY2024, down from $580 million in Q3 due to operating cash outflows and capital expenditures for La Porte upgrades. The company completed the FEED for Project Permian (SN1) but revised its total installed cost estimate upward significantly to between $1.7 billion and $2 billion, driven by inflationary pressures and site-specific challenges like inland transportation costs in West Texas. Consequently, management pushed the project timeline with a best-case groundbreaking date of 2027 and an in-service target of 2029.

PEDMARK gaining traction at major academic centers including UCLA, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, and Mount Sinai
summary: Fennec reported Q4 FY2024 net product sales of $7.9 million (13% sequential growth) and full-year revenue of $29.6 million versus $21.3 million in the prior year, driven by strong momentum in both pediatric and adolescent/young adult segments. The company reduced cash burn to approximately $0.6 million for Q4 after repaying $13 million of debt, while SG&A expenses decreased quarter-over-quarter due to non-cash equity compensation and a one-time severance payment. Management expressed confidence in 2H FY25 growth driven by European commercialization milestones (Norgine deal) and expanded adoption at major academic centers.

Advertising spend decreased by 26% sequentially as the company adjusted payments following lower monetization from Google's Search Partner Network changes.
Google announced plans to automatically opt advertisers out of AdSense for Domains (AFD), creating note weakness in-term disruption and expected material decline in that specific line of business.

Organic sessions for owned products rose over 20% sequentially from Q3 as users seek privacy-focused alternatives.

Management provided specific guidance for Q1 2025 with estimated revenue between $69-71 million and adjusted gross profit growth of approximately 25%, while explicitly declining to provide full-year guidance due to ongoing Google Search Partner Network changes. The quarter highlighted strong performance in owned-and-operated products like Startpage, MapQuest, and CouponFollow, which grew significantly year-over-year.

The company ended the year with $12.6 million cash, no bank debt, and increased fleet capacity by 234% since inception. Management is cautious but confident in 2025, citing potential positive impacts from US tariffs on Chinese-built vessels (none in fleet) and 'drill baby drill' policies.

2025 turn-in-line count slightly lower than last year

Heart failure and pediatric categories down 36% and 20% respectively
Q4 console sales only 3 units vs 11 in Q3

Management expressed optimism about outpatient market entry and ongoing account wins, but noted limited near-term visibility on trial timelines.

Management provided conservative guidance for FY2025 expecting Core revenue growth of 8-15%, explicitly stating they are not baking in any macroeconomic recovery.

Rockies segment liquids volumes declined due to natural production declines, partially offset only by new connections

Station operating income (SOI) increased 46% YoY to $14.1 million in Q4, excluding severance costs.
Digital revenue increased sequentially from Q3 to Q4 despite a slight decline in percentage mix due to political surge.
summary: Q4 FY2024 total net revenue was $67.3 million (up 2.3% YoY), driven by $8.3 million in political advertising which offset weakness in national and local ad spend; however, same-station revenue for the quarter grew only 4.4% while full-year revenue declined 2.8%. Management provided a specific Q1 2025 guidance step-down, pacing same-station revenue down roughly 10% starting in February due to advertiser caution and sports betting pullback.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 91% in Q4 compared to 93% last year, primarily due to higher R&D costs during the Azure-to-AWS cloud migration.
Retail transaction volumes declined approximately 2.5% year-over-year as consumers shifted to needs-based spending and credit usage slowed.
Q1 FY2025 outlook faces headwinds with expected retail volume retractions, though management expects Q4-like strength in the back half of the year.
positive_highlights: Achieved adjusted EBITDA positive results for the full year ($520,000), a strategic milestone not met previously.
SaaS revenue grew 17% quarter-over-quarter to $5.9 million in Q4, driven by new verticals like automotive and title insurance.
Secured significant wins including a mid-seven figure annual contract with a leading bank (up ~15%) and guaranteed volume commitments from an off-price retailer.
summary: Intellicheck reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $5.936 million, a 15% year-over-year increase driven by growth in new verticals like automotive and title insurance which offset declines in retail volumes down ~2.5%. Full-year 2024 adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $520,000 after achieving the strategic goal of profitability for the first time. Management provided a Q1 FY2025 revenue guidance estimate of approximately $4.78 million (in-line with consensus) and expects continued gross margins near 90% in 2025.

negative_highlights: No revenue or financial performance reported in the earnings call.
Cash runway only into Q3 2025, requiring future capital raises.
US enrollment expected to start later than non-EU and Middle Eastern countries.
positive_highlights: Phase 2 MB106 achieved 50% complete remission rate, double the historic control.
Median overall survival at 11 months and progression-free survival at 9 months, still climbing.
Expected first patient treated in MIRACLE Phase 3 trial in Q1 2025 and interim data readout by year-end.
summary: Moleculin Biotech provided a business update on its Phase 3 MIRACLE trial for Annamycin in relapsed/refractory AML. The company highlighted strong Phase 2 results (50% CR, 11-month OS) and expects first patient treatment in Q1 2025, with interim data unblinding by end of 2025. Cash balance of ~$13 million (including $9 million raised in February 2025) funds operations into Q3 2025. No financial results were reported; focus was on clinical milestones.

negative_highlights: Tissue Health Plus segment EBITDA loss widened to $3.1 million in Q4
OsStic U.S. launch not expected until Q1 2027
THP investment expected to be $7.5-$10 million in H1 2025
positive_highlights: Q4 net revenue up 49% YoY to $26.3 million, above prior 33% growth
Full-year adjusted EBITDA positive at $2.7 million, up $2.6 million
Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA up 73% to $9.1 million
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q4 FY2024 net revenue of $26.3 million, up 49% year-over-year, with soft tissue repair sales up 56% and bone fusion up 8%, though $1.8 million was attributed to hurricane-related demand. Full-year net revenue was $86.7 million, up 33%, with positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.7 million. The company expanded its distributor network to over 350 partners and facilities to over 1,300, and announced a partnership for OsStic with FDA breakthrough designation, targeting U.S. launch in Q1 2027. For 2025, they expect continued investment in Tissue Health Plus ($7.5-$10 million in H1) and pilot launches in Q2, while seeking financial partners to offset investment.

negative_highlights: Missed organic revenue guidance range of 14-16% for FY2024.
$1.5 million one-time ERC benefit included in GAAP net income, obscuring underlying operating performance.
No specific numerical forward guidance provided beyond qualitative 'great growth' language.
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 3% sequentially with sequential margin expansion driven by efficiency gains in Card and Output Solutions.
Record total dollars processed of $1.9 billion in Q4, a 36% increase year-over-year.
PayFac card processing volume accelerated to +28% for the full year, now accounting for ~54% of total card activity.
summary: Total revenue grew 3% sequentially and margins expanded due to productivity enhancements in Card and Output Solutions segments. The company reported GAAP net income of $600,000 ($0.02/share) including a one-time ERC benefit, marking the third consecutive quarter of positive earnings despite missing on organic growth guidance for FY24 (which was 14-16%). Management raised visibility to 'great' but did not provide specific numerical guidance updates.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted by 460 basis points from 29.2% in the prior year quarter primarily due to customer marketing support costs.
Operating income swung from positive $1.2M in Q4 FY23 to negative $1.3M in Q4 FY24 as higher operating expenses ($10M vs $7.8M) and lower gross profit offset revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% year-over-year to $35.6M driven by a 40.2% increase in Bath Furniture revenue and strong growth across US (14.7%), Canada, and Europe markets.
Bath Furniture segment outpaced sales expectations due to new business wins and market-aligned program pricing.
summary: FGI reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $35.6 million (up 15% YoY) but GAAP operating income turned negative at -$1.3 million due to a gross margin decline from 29.2% to 24.6%. Management provided initial full-year 2025 guidance for adjusted net income between negative $1.9 million and positive $1 million, explicitly noting that the outlook is conservative given tariff pressures.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated current cash balance is insufficient to complete the Phase 3 trial, necessitating future capital raises.
Funding environment described as 'difficult and challenging', requiring a stepwise approach to raising necessary funds including equity or debt.
No specific financial guidance provided for upcoming quarters; focus remains on clinical milestones rather than revenue generation.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed year-over-year from $42.9M to $37.6M due to a decrease in total operating expenses of $6.7 million (R&D down $5.2M, G&A down $1.5M).
VERSATILE-003 Phase 3 trial initiated with FDA approval for the Versamune HPV + pembrolizumab combination.
Phase 2 data showed improved median overall survival of 30 months and objective response rate increased to 36% compared to prior benchmarks.
summary: PDS Biotech reported a net loss of $37.6 million for the full year ended December 31, 2024, compared to a prior-year loss of $42.9 million, driven by decreased operating expenses partially offset by increased interest expense on debt and lower cash balances. The company initiated its VERSATILE-003 Phase 3 clinical trial with an FDA-approved design for approximately 350 patients targeting HPV16-positive head and neck cancer, reducing the sample size from over 400 based on improved durability data observed in the Phase 2 study. Management indicated that current cash reserves of $41.7 million are insufficient to complete the Phase 3 trial without further capital raises via equity or non-dilutive sources.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased to approximately $25 million from $26 million due to higher manufacturing and R&D costs.
Cash balance decreased to $5.5 million at year-end, reflecting significant cash usage in operating activities.
Management stated they have 'no idea' regarding potential pauses or changes to BARDA funding following political shifts.
positive_highlights: BARDA Project Next-Gen Award valued at almost $400 million announced in June for the GEO-CM04S1 COVID-19 vaccine program.
summary: GeoVax reported a net loss of approximately $25 million for FY2024 compared to $26 million in the prior year, driven by increased R&D expenses and manufacturing costs associated with its BARDA contract. While revenues from the BARDA project reached roughly $4 million (up from zero), management provided no specific financial guidance or earnings estimates for 2025 due to ongoing uncertainties regarding government funding levels and potential trial delays. The company highlighted progress on clinical programs, including a new manufacturing process and discussions with international partners like WHO.

negative_highlights: Full-year medical margin decreased by approximately 37% year-over-year, driven primarily by elevated medical expenses including Part D costs.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA included unfavorable out-of-period true-ups of roughly $17 million related to accounting process cleanup and a single-payer partner.
Part D expense reduction is ongoing but has not yet fully offset the impact of increased facility unit costs and surgical procedure utilization.
positive_highlights: Management reaffirmed all revenue and profitability guidance metrics except slightly raising total membership expectations.
Operational efficiencies of $20 million were executed in Q4, alongside contract rationalization yielding an additional $35 million EBITDA improvement.
Early indicators for 2025 show positive trends with utilization improving following benefit design changes and a reduction in Part D risk exposure.
summary: P3 Health Partners reported Q4 FY2024 revenue of $371 million (up 7% YoY) and full-year adjusted EBITDA loss widening to $68 million in the quarter due to unfavorable out-of-period true-ups. Management reaffirmed its 2025 guidance for revenues between $1.35 billion and $1.5 billion, while slightly raising total membership expectations to a range of 109,000-119,000 members. The company reiterated an adjusted EBITDA outlook ranging from negative $35 million to positive $5 million for the full year.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 11% due to exit from Swivel Secure
Hardware revenue declined 88% in Q4
Net loss per share still $15.02 for 2024
positive_highlights: License fee revenue up 20% to $5.2 million in 2024
Gross margin improved to 78% adjusted from 64%
Cash burn reduced 23% to $2.9 million
summary: BIO-key's Q4 FY2024 revenue declined 11% to $6.9 million, with license fee revenue up 20% to $5.2 million, partially offset by lower-margin services and hardware declines after exiting a Swivel Secure agreement. Gross margin improved to 78% adjusted, and net loss narrowed to $4.3 million from $8.5 million. Management is confident about 2025 growth, citing a $910,000 contract, a tripling defense deployment, and a strengthened balance sheet with $3.8 million warrant proceeds.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA missed the outlook with a loss of $1.1 million, primarily driven by front-loaded lease depreciation costs associated with rapid gross originations growth.
Write-offs as a percent of revenue increased to 9.6% in Q4 from 8.7% in Q4 FY2023 and remained elevated compared to the prior year's low single digits.
Management expressed caution regarding Wayfair, which represented 27% of total gross originations but saw application flow decline; they remain conservative on home furnishings and mattresses.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue beat expectations with $63 million reported, representing 9.4% YoY growth and the seventh consecutive quarter of positive growth.

Gross originations grew 11.3% to $75.2 million in Q4, exceeding the internal guidance range of 6%-8%, driven by a strong holiday season with December up 24%. Excluding home furnishings/mattress, direct and waterfall gross originations grew over 50%.
The company achieved its first full-year of positive adjusted EBITDA ($4.8 million) in FY2024 after reporting losses previously.
summary: Katapult reported Q4 revenue of $63 million (up 9.4% YoY) and gross originations growth of 11.3%, both beating the company's guidance range. However, adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $1.1 million in Q4 due to front-loaded lease depreciation from strong prior-quarter growth, missing its positive outlook for the quarter but delivering full-year profitability of $4.8 million. Management raised 2025 gross originations and revenue growth guidance to at least 20% while maintaining a gross margin target range of 18%-20%, noting that Q1 margins will be impacted by continued high depreciation costs.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue fell 27.3% sequentially due to seasonal parcel delivery delays
Guided deliveries fell note weakness in for the year
Potential tariffs could add $5,000 to $20,000 per vehicle in costs
positive_highlights: Full-year 2024 GAAP gross margin turned positive at 7.1% vs -2.9% in 2023
Secured several major orders after quarter-end, including ~200 strip chassis for UPS and 20 hubs for Caltrans
Implemented over $10 million in cost reductions in the last 12 months
summary: XOS reported Q4 2024 revenue of $11.5 million (down 27.3% from Q3) and 51 unit deliveries, missing guided deliveries due to seasonal parcel delays. Full-year 2024 revenue grew to $56 million from $44.5 million, with positive GAAP gross margin of 7.1% and non-GAAP gross margin of 18%. Management guided for continued gross margin growth in 2025, citing cost reductions and higher-margin hub mix, while flagging tariff risks and charging infrastructure as key uncertainties. The company secured major orders post-quarter, including nearly 200 strip chassis for UPS and 20 hubs for Caltrans.

negative_highlights: Financial results for the back half of FY24 did not live up to expected levels.
The Infinite Reality acquisition deal has not completed and its exclusivity period expired, forcing exploration of alternative strategic options.
Management explicitly stated that financial performance in H2 2024 was a 'speed bump' on the path to profitability.
positive_highlights: Revenue from mobile gaming expanded to roughly 16% of total revenue in Q4 with a trajectory toward 20% in Q1.
summary: Management disclosed that financial results for the back half of FY24 did not meet expectations due to micro-cap headwinds and structural shifts in the Roblox ad ecosystem. The company is executing a strategic realignment including leadership changes (CEO transition) and cost restructuring, with an aim to achieve EBITDA positivity by Q4 2025. While revenue diversification into mobile games shows promise at approximately 16% of total revenue in Q4, the immediate focus remains on reducing burn rather than reporting specific beat/miss figures.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased significantly due to a noncash ground lease accrual exceeding $1.4 million and hiring costs for new campuses.
Debt service coverage ratio for the Obligated Group in 2025 is projected at 1.36x, lower than the previously stated expectation of over 3x three years ago due to current revenue ramp-up status.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenues increased 13% sequentially over Q3 driven by new leases and optimized operations at existing campuses.
Assets under construction and completed construction accelerated to reach over $250 million as of year-end.
Management confirmed they have crossed into positive cash flow from operations at the project level for Sky Harbour Capital.
summary: Consolidated revenues increased 13% sequentially in Q4 to over $250 million in assets under construction/completed construction driven by new leases and the Camarillo acquisition, while full-year consolidated revenues doubled versus 2023. Operating expenses rose due to hiring for new campuses and a noncash ground lease accrual of over $1.4 million at three airport locations. Management reaffirmed guidance to reach cash flow breakeven in Q4 but noted that the Obligated Group's debt service coverage ratio is currently lower than prior 3-year projections until later campus ramps.

negative_highlights: Ovaprene Phase III study recruitment paused at CCTN sites due to uncertainty surrounding federal contracts and funding following executive orders in Q1 2025.
Company reported a comprehensive loss of $4.5 million for the full year ended December 31, 2024.
Enrollment rate prediction impossible for Ovaprene Phase III study due to recruitment pauses at designated sites.
positive_highlights: Royalty monetization transaction with XOMA closed in Q4 2024 generating $22 million in gross proceeds to fund development activities.
Non-dilutive funding awards totaling up to $20.7 million secured from a Federal Agency and the Gates Foundation during 2024.
Significant cost reductions achieved with G&A expenses down 24% year-over-year driven by reduced headcount.
summary: Daré Bioscience reported a comprehensive loss of $4.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, with G&A expenses decreasing by 24% to approximately $9.2 million and R&D expenses falling by 34% to roughly $14.2 million due to reduced headcount and commercial readiness costs. The company closed a royalty monetization transaction receiving $22 million in gross proceeds from XOMA for its product candidate XACIATO, alongside up to $20.7 million in non-dilutive funding awards received during the year. Management announced a strategic pivot to utilize Section 503B compounding pathways to make their proprietary Sildenafil Cream formulation available via prescription by Q4 2025 as an interim revenue source while continuing FDA approval efforts, though they noted that recent executive orders and federal contract uncertainties have paused recruitment at key clinical trial sites for the Ovaprene Phase III study.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 16% in 2024 from 20%, hit by $3.9 million inventory write-offs
Cash dropped to $0.9 million from $1.8 million year-over-year
Germany Q4 growth slower than Q2/Q3 due to supply chain delays
positive_highlights: Q4 adjusted EBITDA positive at $0.5 million, a ~$5 million improvement
German Q4 revenue up 280% YoY; Germany now 40% of H2 revenue
Operating expenses down 42% in Q4; full-year OpEx down 17%
summary: IM Cannabis reported Q4 2024 revenue of $13.3 million, up 25% year-over-year, driven by German revenue growth of 280%, and achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.5 million versus a loss of $4.3 million in Q4 2023. Full-year revenue grew 11% to $54 million, but gross margin fell to 16% from 20% due to $3.9 million inventory write-offs. Management expects Q1 2025 to be the best quarter in Germany to date and sees margin improvement ahead, though it anticipates price compression and no significant Israel growth.

negative_highlights: Infrastructure segment revenue decreased 36.2% due to project timing and completion of large commercial construction projects
Consolidated net loss increased from $9.6 million to $16.9 million on a lower revenue base
Total cash and cash equivalents declined significantly to $48.8 million compared to $80.8 million at the end of 2023
positive_highlights: MediBeacon received FDA approval for its transdermal GFR systems
Life Sciences segment R2 delivered record top line revenues of almost $10 million, a 197% increase over 2023
Spectrum adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $2.3 million in the fourth quarter compared to last year
summary: INNOVATE reported Q4 FY2024 consolidated revenue of $236.6 million, a decrease of 34.5% year-over-year driven by the Infrastructure segment which fell to $225.7 million from $353.8 million in the prior period. Adjusted EBITDA declined to $15 million for the quarter and net loss widened to $16.9 million compared to a narrower loss of $9.6 million last year, primarily due to project timing delays at DBM Global offset by growth in Life Sciences (R2 revenue up 173%) and Spectrum segments.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue decreased 6% to $5.6 million due to a slowdown in the consumer market driving decreases in OEM sales.

Gross margin percentage declined from 23.9% in Q4 FY2023 to 22.1% in Q4 FY2024, with full-year margins at 20.5%, attributed to lower volumes and liquidation of non-core products increasing cost of sales.
Cash position weakened significantly with cash on hand dropping from $3.9 million at year-end 2023 to $0.5 million at December 31, 2024.
positive_highlights: Q4 Revenue surged 131% year-over-year to $2 million, primarily driven by expanding OEM relationships with major retailers like Camping World and K-Z Recreational Vehicles.
New Home Energy Storage Solutions (HESS) shipments began in January 2025 targeting a market expected to surpass $123 billion globally by 2029.
Substantial pre-orders were announced for next-generation Group 27, GC2, and Edge batteries featuring vertical heat conduction technology.
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue reached $2 million (up 131% YoY) driven by OEM sales, while full-year revenue declined 6% to $5.6 million due to a slowdown in the consumer/RV market. Gross margins contracted slightly to 22.1% in Q4 from 23.9% prior year and averaged 20.5% for the full year as lower volumes reduced economies of scale, resulting in an annual net loss of $13.5 million ($21.03/share). Management raised incremental revenue guidance to approximately $5 million for FY2025 based on new OEM partnerships.

negative_highlights: Service revenue declined by $400,000 due to fewer VIP enrollments as part of the strategic shift.
The company remains a net cash user with operating cash flow used at $12.7 million, requiring additional financing in the near term.
New alliance revenues (e.g., Rebis) are not yet reflected in 2024 results and will accelerate starting in Q2 2025.
positive_highlights: Product revenue increased 26% year-over-year to $7.9 million due to higher appliance sales and reduced discounts.
Operating loss decreased by 35% to $11.2 million as the company successfully lowered its cost structure.
Cash position strengthened with total cash and equivalents rising to $6.3 million from $1.6 million.
summary: Vivos Therapeutics reported full year 2024 revenue of $15 million, a 9% increase from $13.8 million in 2023, driven by a 26% rise in product revenue to $7.9 million despite a decrease in service revenue. Operating loss narrowed significantly to $11.2 million from $17.3 million due to cost-cutting measures and higher gross profit, while the company raised approximately $17.9 million through equity transactions. Management highlighted a strategic pivot toward sleep center alliances and acquisitions, noting that 2025 is expected to be materially better than 2024 as new revenue streams from these partnerships begin to materialize.

negative_highlights: Cash at year-end only $3.3 million, with continued cash burn
No revenue guidance for 2025 due to lumpy revenues
Centralized lab automation still needed for scale; current ELISA platform manual and limited
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue up 59% to $1.2 million
Vet test volumes more than doubled to ~120,000 tests, revenue up 75%
Operating expenses down 23% full-year and 31% in H2
summary: VolitionRx reported Q4 FY2024 full-year revenue of $1.2 million, up 59% year-over-year, with vet revenue up 75% to $0.8 million and Discover revenue up 40% to $0.4 million. Operating expenses were reduced 23% year-over-year and 31% in H2, while net cash used in operations was $25.9 million. Cash at year-end was $3.3 million, with subsequent non-dilutive funding and equity sales. Management reiterated its 2025 cash-neutral goal and emphasized progress toward licensing deals in human space, but did not provide revenue guidance.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined slightly on a year-over-year basis for the fourth quarter.
The company explicitly stated it is not providing financial guidance or forward-looking numbers at this time.
Operating loss remained significant at $3.18 million in Q4, though flat versus last year.
positive_highlights: Subscription revenue grew 10% year-over-year, now accounting for over $6.2 million in full-year total.
Gross margin expanded to 82% from 78%, driven by a reduction in cost of revenues and the shift away from professional services.
Net retention rate improved significantly to 100% from 73% last year, supported by six major logo renewals in Q4.
summary: Q4 FY2024 revenue declined slightly to $1.66 million compared to the prior year quarter, while full-year subscription revenue grew only 10% YoY despite a shift in business model toward SaaS (87% of total). The company reported an operating loss of $3.18 million for Q4 and significantly reduced OpEx by 20%, but explicitly stated it is not providing financial guidance due to the transition period.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly paused share buyback strategy, citing a 'scary time' and caution over the next few months.
Significant macro headwinds including tariffs, trade wars, government spending disruptions (DOGE), and nervous capital markets causing equity outflows.
positive_highlights: Exceptional level of earnings producing top-tier returns on equity despite capital levels being at record highs.
summary: Bank7 Corp reported a 'great quarter' with strong earnings and exceptional returns on equity despite macro uncertainty regarding tariffs and government spending disruptions. Management highlighted clean credit migration, low past dues, and successful cost management that lowered the average cost of funds to 2.58%. However, due to volatile market conditions and geopolitical risks (specifically China debt concerns), leadership decided to pause share buybacks until near-term normalcy returns.

negative_highlights: Net income fell from a profit of USD 1.13 million in 2023 to a loss of USD 3.87 million in 2024.
Gross profit declined by 25.5% due to reduced premium pricing and increased competition following the Red Sea crisis.
Operating expenses rose significantly by 56.8% to USD 8.7 million, primarily due to business expansion and enhanced ESG initiatives.
positive_highlights: Total sales volume surged by 38.1% year-over-year driven by network expansion to over 60 ports across 4 continents.
Biofuel sales volume increased over 600% year-over-year, supported by the launch of B24 biofuel and ISCC certifications.
Revenue growth in emerging markets was robust, with South Korea up 187%, Singapore up 102%, and Europe/Asia others up 291%.
summary: CBL International reported Q4 FY2024 results for the full year ended December 31, 2024, with total revenue rising 35.9% to USD 592.5 million driven by a 38.1% surge in sales volume and network expansion. However, gross profit declined 25.5% to USD 5.37 million due to strategic pricing adjustments and increased operating expenses of 56.8%, resulting in a net loss of USD 3.87 million compared to a prior year profit. Management attributes the loss to a volume-driven strategy aimed at market share gain and biofuel adoption, with guidance for FY2025 focused on margin recovery through economies of scale and sustainable fuel development.

negative_highlights: Q2 production faced a slowdown in processing tonnes due to mining harder rock before grade improvements take full effect.
The PEA utilizes a conservative 5% discount rate for valuation rather than the analyst-standard ~10%, which may impact comparable valuations.
positive_highlights: PEA study projects $1.2 billion pretax NPV at $3,000/oz gold price with just under 18 years of mine life.
Processing costs reduced significantly from $22/t to approximately $13-14/t as the plant scaled up.
Management confirmed metallurgical recoveries are improving and sulfide ore is not refractory, addressing a key investor concern.
summary: TRX Gold reported Q2 FY2025 results driven by a robust PEA study released the prior day, projecting an average annual production of over 60,000 ounces with peak output exceeding 90,000 ounces and low cash costs around $1,000/oz. Management highlighted that processing costs have decreased from $22 to roughly $13-14 per tonne due to scale expansion at the plant's current 2,000 tonnes/day capacity. The company is transitioning into higher-grade ore in H2 FY25 following a strip campaign and plans an incremental plant upgrade to increase throughput.

negative_highlights: Consumer sentiment in key markets remains cautious
No tariff impact included in guidance due to uncertainty
India still slow roll with high hopes but no growth acceleration yet
positive_highlights: Consolidated net sales grew 12% YoY in constant currency, including Hiya contribution
Mainland China net sales and active customers grew 6% and 4% sequentially
Hiya delivering robust results with strong growth in net sales and active subscribers
summary: USANA reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated net sales up 12% year-over-year in constant currency, including the first full quarter of Hiya contribution, and results were in line with internal expectations. Direct watching net sales and active customers grew modestly sequentially for the second consecutive quarter, with Mainland China up 6% in net sales and 4% in active customers sequentially. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, excluding any tariff impact, and highlighted strong Hiya growth and planned product launches in the second half.

negative_highlights: Paid members were slightly down less than 0.5% in April, breaking previous lockstep growth with revenue.
Management raised FCF guidance but described it as 'conservative' due to a 'tumultuous nature of the economy' and tariff uncertainty.
Customers are currently in a 'wait-and-see holding pattern,' delaying hiring and expenditures until macro impacts clarify.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8% year-over-year despite flat paid member count due to diversified revenue streams including interchange fees which rose 43% YoY.
Expensify travel saw a massive 166% quarter-over-quarter increase in Q1, indicating strong cross-note adoption from the traditional expense product.
New simplified pricing for the 'collect' plan ($5 per member) is designed to improve conversion at the lower end of the market.
summary: Expensify reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $36.1 million (up 8% YoY) and adjusted net income of $4.8 million, while paid members were flat at approximately 657k in April following a slight decline from the quarter end. Management raised annual free cash flow guidance to $17-$21M but explicitly adopted a conservative tone regarding macroeconomic headwinds and potential tariff impacts on customer behavior.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net revenues decreased 2.9% year over year
Consolidated EBITDA decreased 29.1%
Free cash flow was negative for the quarter
positive_highlights: Maintained full-year guidance of 6-9% net revenue and EBITDA growth
Board proposed a 200 million peso dividend
Business remains strongly profitable with EBITDA margin of 15.3%
summary: In Q1 2025, Betterware de México reported a 2.9% decrease in consolidated net revenues, gross margin contraction of 303 basis points, and a 29.1% decline in EBITDA, with EPS down 48.7%. The quarter was affected by softened consumer demand in Mexico and the US, a weakened peso, and China tariffs. Management maintained full-year guidance of 6-9% net revenue and EBITDA growth, despite acknowledging near-term challenges and pausing growth investments in Betterware US. The board proposed a 200 million peso dividend, reflecting prudent cash management.

negative_highlights: Q1 EPS missed expectations due to higher O&M expenses ($81M increase) and increased depreciation reflecting capital investment programs.
Updated estimated liability for Smokehouse Creek wildfires to $290 million, incorporating previously excluded categories like railroad claims and tree damage settlements.
Management noted a change in sentiment meter regarding tariffs over the last 45 days due to recent executive orders and trade actions.
positive_highlights: Electric sales increased 2% quarter-over-quarter driven by growth across most operating companies, with C&I sales up 9% year-over-year in SPS.
Management reaffirmed the ability to deliver earnings for the 21st consecutive year and remains confident in navigating tariff impacts estimated at 2-3% of capital expenditures.
Reached a constructive unanimous settlement on the Colorado wildfire mitigation plan, securing cost recovery mechanisms including insurance deferral extensions.
summary: Xcel Energy reported Q1 FY2025 earnings of $0.84 per share, missing the prior quarter's EPS by a few cents due to higher O&M and depreciation expenses. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance for EPS between $3.75 and $3.85 despite tariff uncertainties and elevated wildfire liabilities which were updated to an estimated low-end liability of $290 million.

negative_highlights: Deposit growth was flat and total deposits decreased slightly in the quarter
Commercial real estate office property sector is deteriorating with significant vacancy concerns
Management noted loan opportunities are less available than in previous years, limiting portfolio expansion
positive_highlights: Net income increased $700k quarter-over-quarter and $2 million year-over-year
No credit loss expense recorded due to excellent credit quality with no nonaccruals or OREO
Loan yields improved slightly to 5.52% as fixed-rate portfolio cash flows rolled over
summary: Net income was $7.8 million for Q1 FY2025 compared to $7.1 million in the prior quarter and $5.8 million year-over-year, driven by a net interest margin expansion of 30 basis points as deposit costs fell 38 bps. Loan portfolio growth remained modest with approximately $100 million in payoffs from asset sales and refinances replaced at better rates, while deposits decreased slightly due to ordinary cash flow fluctuations rather than relationship loss. Management noted that loan opportunities are currently less available than in previous years despite a good pipeline.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports EBITDA declined sequentially due to Brazil tax implementation and customer onboarding friction in early quarter.
Leisure business performance was negatively impacted by the slippage of the U.K. Easter holiday from Q1 FY24 to Q2 FY25.
U.K. retail high street market showed softness with key customers Betfred and Paddy Power, though William Hill provided an offset.
positive_highlights: Interactive segment revenue grew 49% YoY while EBITDA surged 75%, expanding margins from 54% to 64%.
U.S. Interactive business grew by 90% against a market growth of only 20%, driven by new states like Delaware and strong content performance.
Debt refinancing secured with flexible terms, extending maturity to June 2026 and reducing call protection.
summary: First quarter adjusted EBITDA of $18.5 million beat the prior year by nearly 20%, driven primarily by a 49% revenue increase and 79% EBITDA growth in the Interactive segment which expanded margins from 54% to 64%. Management successfully refinanced debt with flexible terms, though they noted sequential declines in Virtual Sports due to Brazil regulatory changes. The company reiterated its deleveraging strategy via a holiday park sale and pub business restructuring.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 20% year-over-year to $4 million due to weakness in domestic and international businesses
Operating loss widened from $500,000 in Q1 2024 to $900,000 in the current quarter
Retail business expected to remain at current levels until tariff uncertainty resolves
positive_highlights: First green shoots observed in the industrial portion of the business
Launched Xtreme iXG and iXS Series handheld computers powered by iOS
summary: Socket Mobile reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $4 million, a decrease of 20% year-over-year and 18% sequentially from Q4 2024. Gross margins declined slightly to 50.4%, while the company recorded an operating loss of $900,000 compared to a prior quarter's loss of $400,000. Management expressed caution regarding near-term retail demand due to tariff uncertainty but highlighted initial progress in industrial segments and new product launches.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs totaled $9.7 million, equivalent to 92 basis points of loans
Nonperforming loans increased to 80 basis points
Net income down to $0.9 million due to elevated provision
positive_highlights: Net interest income up 6.6% linked quarter and 20% year-over-year
Total operating revenue up 22% year-over-year
Fintech revenue forecast for 2025 expected to exceed $4 million
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q1 2025 net income of $0.9 million and diluted EPS of $0.11, heavily impacted by $9.7 million in net charge-offs, mostly in franchise finance and small business lending. Net interest income grew 6.6% linked quarter and 20% year-over-year, with net interest margin up 16 basis points; total operating revenue rose 22% year-over-year. The company raised its 2025 fintech revenue forecast from $4 million to 'blow through' that level, and expects continued NII/NIM growth for the year. Credit quality deteriorated with nonperforming loans at 80 basis points, but management cited borrower-specific issues and no systemic stress.

negative_highlights: Net premiums written decreased by 1.7% due to lower new business volume and planned attrition in personal lines.
Workers' compensation experienced $1.8 million of unfavorable development, though the line remains rate adequate.
Personal lines net premiums written fell 9.9% as part of a strategic initiative to prune less profitable classes.
positive_highlights: Combined ratio improved substantially to 91.6% from 102.4% in the prior year quarter.
After-tax net income surged to $25.2 million, a significant increase compared to $6 million in Q1 2024.
Weather-related losses decreased by 2.2 million dollars and large fire losses dropped by 50%.
summary: Donegal Group reported Q1 FY2025 net premiums earned of $232.7 million (up 2.2% YoY) and a combined ratio of 91.6%, driven by a core loss ratio improvement of 4.5 percentage points to 89.1%. The company achieved record quarterly earnings, exceeding the prior year's record level, with after-tax net income rising significantly from $6 million in Q1 2024 to $25.2 million. Management raised the quarterly cash dividend and highlighted successful systems modernization milestones.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 33.8% year-over-year due to significantly lower sales volumes and fewer active coaches.
Loss from operations widened to $1.3 million, down $9.2 million versus the prior year period.
SG&A as a percentage of revenue increased 560 basis points primarily due to loss of leverage on fixed costs.
positive_highlights: New coach cohorts are exhibiting new customer growth ahead of last year's levels.
Year-over-year decline in revenue per active earning coach moderated to only 1.4% compared to a 22.8% decline in the prior year.
ASCEND product line orders remained right in line with expectations, reaching mid-teens as a percentage of total orders.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $115.7 million, a 33.8% year-over-year decrease driven by a 32.8% drop in active earning coaches to approximately 25,400. EPS was $0.07, resulting in a net loss of $0.8 million compared to prior year income. Management provided Q2 guidance for revenue between $85 million and $105 million and a loss per share ranging from zero cents to $0.55.

negative_highlights: Credit card volume growth intentionally paused in Q2 for app improvements
SBA premium levels remain soft; no near-term improvement expected
Nonperforming loans up $6.2 million due to SBA loan repurchase
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 31% year-over-year to $17.4 million
Noninterest income up 127% year-over-year to $5.5 million
Book value per share up 28% to $10.27
summary: GBank Financial Holdings reported Q1 FY2025 net income of $4.5 million or $0.31 per diluted share, including nearly $1 million in one-time expenses. Net revenue was $17.4 million, up 31% year-over-year, with noninterest income up 127% driven by credit card interchange. The company completed its NASDAQ listing, downstreamed $15 million to the bank, and maintains a strong SBA/commercial pipeline of over $300 million. Management expects a temporary slowdown in credit card growth in Q2 as they enhance the app, with major marketing and product launches planned for the second half.

negative_highlights: adjusted EPS still -$0.03; Q1 smallest quarter
tariff uncertainty, holding goods, cautious view
SG&A up 1%, minimal cost growth
positive_highlights: sales up 26%, led by Sonic 3, Moana 2, Dog Man
adjusted EBITDA positive at $0.4M vs -$17.2M last year
gross margin 34.4%, product margin up, SG&A flat
summary: Q1 FY2025 sales grew 26% YoY, with dolls and role play/dress-up up 37% and action play/collectibles up 30%; adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.4 million, a $17.6 million improvement. Gross margin hit 34.4%, driven by product mix and favorable timing. The company remains debt-free with $59.2 million cash, but management is cautious on tariffs, holding some goods and adjusting sourcing; 2025 guidance not explicitly reaffirmed.

negative_highlights: Gross margin expected to decrease approximately 3-4 percentage points in Q2 due to customer migration costs on upgraded platform
Net loss widened to $1.5 million from $800,000 prior year primarily driven by litigation expenses and debt extinguishment
positive_highlights: 37th consecutive quarter of record revenue
Q1 adjusted EBITDA improved by approximately $1 million year-over-year to $1.9 million
Strong pipeline building in both U.S. and EU ahead of the European Accessibility Act deadline
summary: AudioEye reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $9.7 million (up ~34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $1.9 million, marking the 37th consecutive quarter of record revenue. Management raised guidance for Q2 revenue to between $9.85M-$10M and reiterated full-year FY2025 revenue guidance at $41M-$42M despite a one-time gross margin impact in Q2 from platform migration costs.

negative_highlights: Wholesale sales down 6.3%
Gross margin guidance pressured by tariffs
Inflationary price increases may pressure demand
positive_highlights: Record Q1 gross margin of 41.2%, 210 bps expansion
Adjusted EPS up to $0.73 vs $0.41
Retail segment sales rose 20.5%
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $114.1 million, up 1.1% year-over-year, slightly ahead of expectations, with record first-quarter gross margins of 41.2%. Adjusted EPS rose to $0.73 from $0.41 a year ago. Retail segment grew 20.5%, but wholesale declined 6.3% due to planned military reductions. Management reiterated full-year guidance despite tariff uncertainties and plans price increases in June, expecting EPS just below last year's $2.54.

negative_highlights: Operating income down 34% YoY due to member growth investments
Europe revenue up only 1%, operating margin flat at 3%
GAAP operating margin fell to 16% from 26% a year ago
positive_highlights: Revenue of $23.1 million, highest since pandemic, up 5% YoY; constant currency up 6%
Jack's Flight Club revenue up 20% YoY, premium subscribers up 13%
Expect Q2 revenue growth to double YoY, accelerating trend expected
summary: Travelzoo reported Q1 2025 revenue of $23.1 million, up 5% year-over-year, the highest quarterly revenue since the pandemic, with constant currency revenue up 6%. Operating income fell 34% to $3.7 million due to increased member acquisition investments, and non-GAAP operating profit was $4.3 million versus $6.0 million last year. Management expects Q2 revenue growth to double year-over-year and accelerate through the year as subscription fees are recognized ratably. While North America and Jack's Flight Club led growth, Europe was flat, and management acknowledged near-term EPS pressure from marketing investments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 3% YoY due to lower fuel surcharge and tonnage
LTL tonnage per day down 7.5% YoY, though outperforming the industry
Adjusted EBITDA down 3% YoY with lower fuel surcharge, tonnage, and pension income
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.73 exceeded expectations
LTL adjusted OR improved 30 bps sequentially, better than seasonality
Yield ex-fuel accelerated to 6.9% YoY and purchase transportation costs down 53%
summary: XPO reported Q1 2025 total revenue of $2 billion, down 3% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $278 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.73, exceeding expectations despite a challenging freight market. LTL margins improved sequentially by 30 basis points to an adjusted operating ratio of 85.9%, with yield ex-fuel up 6.9% year-over-year and purchase transportation costs down 53%. The company lowered outsourced linehaul miles to 8.8% of total miles, a record low, and highlighted ongoing technology and AI investments aimed at further productivity gains. Management expressed confidence in continued above-market yield growth and margin expansion, while noting the uncertain macro environment and expected moderation in CapEx.

negative_highlights: Organic net sales declined 2% due to lower paper, logistics, and agency sales
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 7.2%
Free cash flow was negative $100 million, worse than prior year
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS doubled to $0.20 per share
Net debt decreased by $81 million year-over-year
Growing In-Store Connect network and new client wins
summary: Quad's Q1 2025 net sales were $629 million, down 2% organically, with adjusted EBITDA down from $51 million to $46 million and margin down to 7.2%. Adjusted diluted EPS doubled to $0.20, and free cash flow was negative $100 million due to working capital timing. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance despite tariff and postal headwinds, noting limited direct tariff exposure and USPS promotional discounts for catalogers.

negative_highlights: First quarter ROA was 66 bps, below the 1% goal
Consumer portfolio charge-offs remain high, with provision additional credit expense
Panacea consolidation reduced operating ROA by 10 bps
positive_highlights: Net interest margin up to 3.15% from 290 bps last quarter
Core community bank loan pipeline about 3 times last year; April loans up $25 million
Expect 24 bps ROA from earning assets, 15 bps from mortgage, 15 bps from tech savings
summary: Q1 FY2025 pre-tax net income was $4.5 million excluding Panacea, or $7.5 million adjusted for one-time items, equating to a 66 basis point ROA. Net interest margin improved to 3.15% from 290 basis points last quarter. Management expects to grow earning assets back to $3.75 billion, add 15 bps to ROA from mortgage growth, and reduce technology spend by 15 bps to exceed a 1% ROA goal. Panacea deconsolidation is possible with a potentially substantial gain, but not guaranteed.

negative_highlights: Sub-servicing additions of roughly flat year-over-year due to lower subservicing additions related to the timing of bulk boardings.
Reverse servicing was up from the prior quarter but remained lower versus the prior year, primarily driven by strong asset gains in Q1 '24 and valuation adjustments on buyout loans.
positive_highlights: Adjusted pre-tax income of $25 million exceeded the full-year guidance range of 16%-18% adjusted ROE (actual annualized ROE was 22%).
Originations volume grew 53% year-over-year, significantly outpacing the industry's 8% increase.
Total servicing additions were up $17 billion versus Q1 '24, with owned MSR editions more than doubling.
summary: Onity Group reported Q1 FY2025 adjusted pre-tax income of $25 million and GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders of $21 million ($2.50 per share), exceeding full-year guidance for both metrics. The company confirmed its full year 2025 financial objectives remain unchanged, citing strong execution in originations volume (up 53% YoY) and servicing UPB growth despite a decline in subservicing additions due to timing of bulk boardings.

negative_highlights: Gas Cylinders sales down 9%, margin down to 6.3% from 9%
Alternative fuel softness drove transportation sales down 23%
FX volatility noted as key sensitivity (~$1M EPS impact per $0.05 move)
positive_highlights: Sales up 8.9% to $90.5M, adjusted EPS up to $0.23
Elektron sales up 31% with 120 bps margin expansion
UGR-E demand expected to more than double in 2025; first European bulk gas module order secured
summary: Luxfer's Q1 2025 sales rose 8.9% to $90.5M, with adjusted EPS of $0.23 up from $0.20, adjusted EBITDA up 9.7% to $11.3M (12.5% margin), and operating cash flow of $5.1M. Elektron grew 31% with margin expansion, while Gas Cylinders fell 9% with margin down. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed: EPS $0.95-$1.05, EBITDA $48-$52M, and free cash flow $20-$25M. Management highlighted tariff mitigation, strong defense demand, UGR-E record backlog, and a first bulk gas transportation order, while noting FX and rare earth risks.

negative_highlights: Management suspended full-year guidance citing unpredictability from new reciprocal tariffs imposed in April, reducing visibility into near-term trends.
Gross margin expansion was driven by product mix rather than volume or pricing power as average price decreases offset some gains.
Inventory pull-forward of approximately $32 million occurred due to tariff uncertainty, impacting cash flow and working capital.
positive_highlights: Operating profit improved $3.2 million year-over-year, turning a loss from Q1 FY24 into an operating loss of only $943k for Q1 FY25.
North American consumer markets delivered solid growth led by the U.S., partially offsetting slight international declines.
HealthBeacon contributed $1.5 million in revenue and marked its third consecutive quarter of increasing patient subscriptions.
summary: First quarter revenue was $133.4 million (up 4% YoY) with operating profit improving by $3.2 million to reach a loss of only $943k compared to a prior year loss of $1.2m, driven by HealthBeacon and mix shifts. Management suspended full-year guidance due to new retaliatory tariffs in April reducing visibility into the remainder of 2025. The company is implementing price increases and accelerating sourcing diversification outside China with benefits expected to flow through starting in 2026.

negative_highlights: U.S. growth moderated over past four quarters and came in below expectations
Gross margins lower due to geographic mix
R&D expenses expected to increase with trial enrollment
positive_highlights: Worldwide sales $22.5M, up 20% YoY and 21% constant currency
International revenue grew 39% YoY, driven by China
Added 10 new U.S. accounts, ending quarter with 285 active accounts
summary: Pulmonx reported Q1 2025 worldwide sales of $22.5 million, up 20% YoY (21% constant currency), with strong international growth of 39%, but U.S. growth moderated. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $96-98 million, noting that Q1 likely represents a low point for U.S. growth and expects acceleration in the back half from new initiatives. Gross margin was pressured by geographic mix, and China distributor stocking contributed to international strength.

negative_highlights: BARDA Project NextGen contract terminated via Stop Work Order in April, halting incremental spending on that specific award
Net loss increased to $5.4 million driven by R&D expenses of $5.4 million and G&A increase of $200,000
No new funding awards received from BARDA despite proposal being deemed appropriate
positive_highlights: BARDA proposal for advanced MVA manufacturing process deemed worthy and placed into a two-year funding basket
Encouraging interim results from CLL trial showing Pfizer arm did not meet endpoint while GeoVax study continues
cGMP production of GEO-MVA clinical batch completed with sufficient product available for upcoming evaluation
summary: GeoVax reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $1.6 million from BARDA (up from zero in the prior year) and a net loss of approximately $5.4 million or $0.45 per share, compared to a loss of $5.9 million ($2.47 EPS) in 2024. The company disclosed that it received an unexpected Stop Work Order terminating its BARDA Project NextGen contract for convenience with less than $750,000 annual financial impact and no significant operational changes anticipated. Management remains focused on advancing GEO-CM04S1 trials in immunocompromised populations and completing cGMP production of the GEO-MVA vaccine candidate.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $15.5 million due to higher maintenance expenses related to Spanish Scooper return-to-service work.
2025 guidance explicitly excludes any impact from the Spanish Super Scoopers, indicating uncertainty regarding their deployment timeline.
Cash balance declined to $22.3 million from $39.3 million at the end of 2024 due to winter maintenance and training activities.
positive_highlights: Record first quarter revenue of $15.6 million driven by early wildfire activity and new exclusive use contracts.
Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly to negative $5.1 million compared to negative $6.9 million in the prior year.
Secured a 5-year IDIQ contract with the Bureau of Land Management for Alaska Fire Service and an exclusive use agreement with Montana.
summary: Bridger Aerospace reported record Q1 FY2025 revenue of $15.6 million, an 184% increase year-over-year driven by early wildfire deployments and the inclusion of acquired subsidiary FMS. The company posted a net loss of $15.5 million ($0.41 diluted EPS) but improved Adjusted EBITDA to negative $5.1 million from negative $6.9 million in the prior year. Management raised 2025 guidance, projecting adjusted EBITDA growth of approximately 20% with a midpoint range of $42 million to $48 million on revenue between $105 million and $111 million.

negative_highlights: SaaS customer additions declined by 3,000 quarter-over-quarter due to holiday seasonality and a strategic shift toward expansion over new acquisition.
First quarter Marketing Services billings fell 42% YoY as the company continues converting legacy clients to SaaS.
Full-year guidance was taken with a 'cautious view' in light of recession headlines, though not materially cut.
positive_highlights: SaaS revenue beat guidance at $111.1 million with 50% YoY growth.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 10% from the prior period.
Seasoned net revenue retention reached a record high of 103%.
summary: Thryv reported Q1 FY2025 SaaS revenue of $111.1 million, beating guidance with 50% year-over-year growth and a sequential increase of 7%. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 10%, driven by a 490 bps YoY gross margin improvement and strong subscriber growth of 37% to 111,000 total subscribers. Management raised full-year SaaS revenue guidance to $460.5M-$471M and confirmed Marketing Services EBITDA guidance, citing a conservative outlook due to macro uncertainty despite delivering a top-line beat.

negative_highlights: Same-store sales declined 2% for the quarter, driven by softer new boat sales on the West Coast.
Gross profit declined from $120 million in Q2 FY24 to $110 million due to lower margins and model mix shifts.
SG&A expenses increased 50 basis points as a percentage of revenue (to 18%) because cost savings were offset by inflationary pressures on boat shows.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net loss narrowed significantly from a prior year loss of $5 million ($0.27/share) to just $375,000 ($0.02/share).
Pre-owned boat sales increased 14% to $90 million driven by higher volumes and trade-ins.
Inventory reduction is tracking ahead of schedule with a target to end the year down 10% to 15%, exceeding initial full-year goals.
summary: Fiscal second quarter revenue decreased 1% to $484 million and adjusted EPS fell from $0.67 to $0.13 due to lower gross margins on exited brands and a challenging pricing environment. Management updated its fiscal 2025 guidance downward, forecasting total sales between $1.7 billion and $1.8 billion (downside risk) and adjusting EBITDA expectations to the range of $65 million to $95 million amidst tariff concerns and macroeconomic uncertainty.

negative_highlights: DynaEnergetics sales down 16% year-over-year
NobelClad backlog down to $41 million from $49 million
Guidance implies lower Q2 EBITDA and sales, citing tariffs and demand disruption
positive_highlights: Consolidated sales up 5% sequentially to $159.3 million
Adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC up 39% sequentially to $14.4 million
Arcadia adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 14.2% from 9.5% in prior year
summary: DMC Global reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated sales of $159.3 million, up 5% sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC of $14.4 million, up 39% sequentially. Arcadia sales grew 9% sequentially and 6% year-over-year to $65.6 million, while DynaEnergetics sales were flat sequentially but down 16% year-over-year due to pricing adjustments. NobelClad sales were flat sequentially but up 5% year-over-year, with backlog down to $41 million from $49 million. The company guided Q2 sales to $149-157 million and adjusted EBITDA to $10-13 million, citing tariff uncertainty, lower residential demand, and softer energy markets. Management expressed cautious optimism around operational improvements but noted significant external headwinds.

negative_highlights: Comparable store sales declined 4.8% due to winter storms, inflation concerns, and high interest rates.
President's Day sales were disappointing, down roughly 10% over the two-week period.
Management reduced CapEx guidance by approximately $3 million due to tariff uncertainty affecting expansion plans.
positive_highlights: Gross margins expanded 90 bps to 61.2% driven by product selection and merchandise mix.
Operating margin improved significantly to 2.9% from 1.7% in the prior year quarter.
New store openings and inventory buildup strategies are proceeding as planned despite macro headwinds.
summary: Havertys reported Q1 FY2025 net sales of $181.6 million, a 1.3% decrease year-over-year, with comparable store sales down 4.8%. Gross margins expanded 90 basis points to 61.2%, driven by merchandise mix, while operating margin improved to 2.9% from 1.7%. Management provided full-year guidance assuming current tariffs are in effect, projecting gross margins between 60% and 60.5% and reducing CapEx expectations due to tariff uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 17.3% YoY driven by a 17.9% drop in cases.
Same-store revenue fell approximately 24%, with management expecting continued pressure through the year before returning to growth at year-end.
Customer acquisition cost increased to $3,130 per case due to lower volume and reduced marketing spend.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA improved by $1.9 million sequentially versus Q4 2024 due to cost discipline and workforce reductions.
Lead volume growth over Q1 last year driven by reallocated marketing spend, expanding the pipeline without increasing total ad spend.
Average revenue per case remained stable between $12,000 and $13,000 despite a challenging macro environment.
summary: AirSculpt reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $39.4 million (down 17.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.8 million (margin 9.5%), missing the prior year's performance due to lower case volume despite a slight increase in average revenue per case ($12,799). Management provided fiscal 2025 guidance for revenue between $160M-$170M and adjusted EBITDA of $16M-$18M, maintaining the prior outlook without raising it. While management noted sequential improvement in lead generation and same-store sales trends since February, they explicitly stated that Q4-like softness is expected to persist through most of 2025.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net sales declined 2% year-over-year primarily due to lower volumes in Asia and foreign currency impacts.
Gross margin in Americas Segment contracted by 350 basis points driven by inflationary pressures and transition costs.
Asia Segment saw a 12% decline in net sales and 150 bps gross margin contraction amid macroeconomic pressure.
positive_highlights: Americas Segment net sales increased by 3% year-over-year driven by Beyond Apparel initiatives and Central America recovery.
Reached agreement to note Madison facility for $53.2 million, expected to close May 15th to reduce debt and retire obligations.
REPREVE represented 31% of total sales with strong brand visibility from partners like Nike, Target, and Walmart.
summary: Consolidated net sales were $146.6 million, down 2% year-over-year due to lower volumes and unfavorable mix in Asia offset by Americas growth. Gross margins contracted significantly across the board: -350 bps in Americas (transition costs) and -150 bps in Asia (macro/pricing). Management reiterated that Q4 results will improve sequentially but warned of potential 10-15% revenue downturns in Asia due to tariffs.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $19 million in Q1 2025
Adjusted EBITDA down from $95 million in Q1 2024
positive_highlights: Production up 45% YoY and 14% QoQ to 46,619 BOE/d
Ecuador wells Iguana B1/B2 averaged 1,684 bbl/d over 30 days
Simonette wells exceed budget type curves by 80%
summary: Gran Tierra reported Q1 2025 production of 46,619 BOE/d, up 45% YoY and 14% QoQ, with a net loss of $19 million (improved from $34 million loss in Q4) and adjusted EBITDA of $85 million. Capex was $95 million, funded by a heavy capital program, and the company reduced gross debt by $27 million, repurchased shares, and added a new $75 million Colombia facility. Management highlighted record drilling times, strong Ecuador discoveries, and improved Canadian well performance, while maintaining full-year production guidance of 47-53 MBoe/d.

negative_highlights: U.S. Domestic revenue declined 9.5% due to the conclusion of Emergency Connectivity Fund and Affordable Care Program subsidies.
Operating income decreased to $2.7 million, impacted by transaction-related expenses and restructuring costs.
Net loss widened slightly to $8.9 million compared to a prior year net loss of $6.3 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 2% to $44.3 million despite lower top-line revenue.
Cash from operations increased significantly by 55% year-over-year to $35.9 million.
International segment adjusted EBITDA rose 10.6% YoY as the business stabilizes.
summary: ATN International reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $179.3 million, down 4% year-over-year due to the wind-down of government subsidy programs in the U.S., while adjusted EBITDA grew by 2% to $44.3 million driven by international segment performance and cash from operations increasing 55%. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2025 guidance, expecting revenue flat with last year (excluding construction) and essentially flat adjusted EBITDA, citing ongoing U.S. transition costs but steady progress in international markets.

negative_highlights: Global retail sales down 21%, North America down 24%, citing low consumer confidence
Withdrew 2025 guidance due to tariff and macro uncertainty; tariff impact estimated at $130M-$175M
HDMC operating income declined 51% on lower volume and higher fixed costs per unit
positive_highlights: HDFS operating income increased 19% to $64 million, driven by lower credit provision and lower opex
Q1 bottom line better than expected, with operating margin at 12.1% despite environmental pressures
Tariff impact limited to $9 million in Q1, below initial expectations
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenues down 23%, with HDMC down 27% and wholesale shipments down 33%. Operating income fell 51% at HDMC, but HDFS grew 19% to $64M. EPS was $1.07. Retail sales down 21% globally and 24% in North America. Management withdrew full-year 2025 guidance due to tariff and macro uncertainty, citing a potential $130M-$175M tariff impact. They remain committed to reducing dealer inventory by ~10% year-end and expect productivity savings of $100M in 2025. LiveWire reduced its full-year operating loss guidance to ~$59M from $70-80M.

negative_highlights: Continued market challenges and cautious retail environment
Diving business still very challenged
Tariffs will impact business despite U.S. manufacturing
positive_highlights: New Humminbird products (MEGA Live 2, Xplore) demand exceeding expectations
Jetboil new orders outpacing expectations
Inventory down $69 million year-over-year
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported Q2 FY2025 results reflecting continued market challenges and a cautious retail environment. Gross margin improved slightly to 35% due to cost savings, despite marketplace discounting. Operating expenses decreased $7.7 million year-over-year. Inventory was down $69 million to $180 million. New products in fishing and camping are exceeding expectations, but overall demand remains soft and tariffs are expected to impact the business.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted slightly to 58.9% from 59.6% due to transitory headwinds including partial quarter new marker recognition and upfront lab investments.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $2.5 million from $2.0 million in the prior year period.
New markers were reflected for only a partial quarter, limiting the full ASP impact of the $90 per test incremental boost.
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $15.5M representing a nearly 8% increase compared to Q1 2024.
Successful debt refinancing with Perceptive Advisors extending maturity to April 2030 and providing up to $50M in additional capacity.
Secured positive medical policy with TRICARE after a two-year review process, validating clinical evidence for active duty service members.
summary: Exagen reported record Q1 FY2025 revenue of $15.5 million, an 8% year-over-year increase driven by new biomarker launches and volume growth of 6% sequentially. The company achieved a gross margin of 58.9%, slightly down from the prior year due to transitory headwinds including partial quarter recognition of new markers and upfront lab investments, but expects steady expansion into the low 60s in H2. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance of at least $65 million and raised expectations for adjusted EBITDA positivity by Q4.

negative_highlights: Tariff exposure estimated at up to 2-2.5% of COGS in near term, pressuring gross margins
Q4 gross margin not expected to accelerate due to tariff and software mix
International revenue down 5% year-over-year on tough APAC comp
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA of $14.9 million, second consecutive quarterly record
Non-GAAP EPS up 13% year-over-year to $0.88
Initial sales of ProVision Plus software to Pasolink customers
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $112.6 million, up 1.6% year-over-year, with record adjusted EBITDA of $14.9 million (up 17% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.88 (up 13% YoY). Gross margins improved to 35.8% non-GAAP, driven by software and regional mix, but management expects Q4 margins to be pressured by tariffs and a softer software quarter. The company reiterated full-year guidance within the $430-$470 million range and expects to approximate consensus revenue and EBITDA, citing tariff uncertainty and a cautious Q4 outlook.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss of $25 million, though improved from $38 million YoY
Servicing fee income fell from $124 million to $104 million due to 2024 bulk sales
Total expenses increased 4% YoY
positive_highlights: Pull-through weighted lock volume up 15% YoY to $5.4 billion
Gain on sale margin of 355 bps exceeded guidance of 320-340 bps
Unit share market gain expanded from 145 to 187 basis points
summary: In Q1 FY2025, loanDepot reported pull-through weighted rate lock volume of $5.4 billion, up 15% year-over-year and within guidance, while adjusted revenue rose to $278 million from $231 million. Gain on sale margin came in above guidance at 355 basis points, and adjusted net loss narrowed to $25 million from $38 million. For Q2, the company guided lock volume of $5.5-8.0 billion and gain on sale margin of 300-350 basis points, noting seasonal strength offset by market volatility. CEO transition to founder Anthony Hsieh is underway.

negative_highlights: Book value estimated down approximately 3% through April due to market volatility in early spring
Securitization spreads widened significantly, requiring a wider spread on retained securities (estimated 50-75 bps)
Existing home sales remain historically low and supply of newly constructed homes is narrowing
positive_highlights: Book value remained stable at $10.65 per share despite macro volatility
Quarterly dividend increased to $0.20, representing a 5.3% increase from the prior quarter
Arc Home achieved breakeven earnings with lock volumes increasing 50% year-over-year
summary: MITT reported Q1 FY2025 GAAP EPS of $0.21 per share and increased its quarterly dividend by 5.3% to $0.20 per share. Book value remained stable at $10.65, rising slightly despite an estimated 3% decline through April due to market volatility in early spring. Management noted that securitization spreads widened significantly (estimated 50-75 bps) and markets closed briefly before reopening by late April.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss applicable to common stockholders was $9.3 million ($0.29 per share).
Book value per common share decreased by approximately 6% from the prior quarter end.
Earnings available for distribution (EAD) are expected to trend lower moving forward due to the maturation of a large interest rate hedge.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses declined quarter-over-quarter following the elimination of the management fee upon internalization.
The company ended Q1 with $47 million of unrestricted cash on its balance sheet, maintaining a solid liquidity profile.
Prepayment speeds for both MSR and RMBS portfolios remained relatively steady despite interest rate volatility.
summary: Cherry Hill reported a GAAP net loss of $9.3 million ($0.29 per share) for Q1 FY2025, with book value declining to $3.58 from $3.82 at year-end due to mark-to-market losses on RMBS and the maturation of interest rate hedges reducing EAD. Management maintained a neutral stance on rates amidst tariff uncertainty and noted that while they have been reinvesting amortization into MBS, MSR acquisitions remain paused until potential portfolio rebalancing occurs later in 2025.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue missed expectations with a year-over-year decline of 13% to $274.2 million.
Adjusted EBITDA decreased significantly from $12.8 million in the prior period to $7.2 million.
Cash and cash equivalents declined by approximately $15.5 million quarter-over-quarter, dropping from $48.8 million at year-end 2024.
positive_highlights: Life Sciences revenue tripled (up 210%) driven by increased demand for Glacial fx and Rx systems in North America.
Infrastructure backlog grew to $1.4 billion, adding over $500 million of new awards during the quarter.
R2 social media engagement growth outperformed industry competitors by 774%.
summary: Consolidated revenue decreased by 13% to $274.2 million and adjusted EBITDA fell to $7.2 million compared to the prior year period. The decline was driven primarily by a 14% drop in Infrastructure segment revenue due to project timing, partially offset by a strong 210% surge in Life Sciences revenue led by R2's unit sales growth.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly withheld Q2 financial guidance due to uncertainty surrounding Google's AFD policy changes.
Total owned and operated revenue fell 16% YoY driven by a non-core marketing business segment decline (-35%).
Network active partners decreased 14% sequentially as the company pushes partners toward Google's new RSOC product.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA surged to $12.1 million, up significantly from just $400k in the prior year quarter.
Owned and operated product revenue grew 53% YoY with sessions up 6%, driven by CouponFollow (+160%) and MapQuest (+30%).
OpEx declined for the seventh consecutive quarter, demonstrating ongoing cost reduction efforts.
summary: System1 reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $74.5 million (down 1% sequentially and down 12% YoY) with adjusted gross profit of $41.5 million ($33M O&O, $15M Network). While the company beat its high-end guidance on key metrics due to a one-time reversal of invalid traffic revenue in Q1, management explicitly declined to provide financial guidance for Q2 2025 or the full year citing volatility from Google's product transition (shift away from AFD) and macro uncertainty. Management highlighted strong YoY growth in owned-and-operated products (+38% share mix) but noted a sequential decline driven by seasonality.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 19% year-over-year, with volume drops of 16% and a divestiture impact.
Free cash flow was a use of $125 million, compared to a contribution of $46 million in the prior year.
Net debt leverage ratio increased to 4.6x, exceeding the targeted range of 2.0x to 2.5x.
positive_highlights: Management expects to pass through approximately $30 million in tariff costs to customers with minimal timing impact.
New business acquisition with production builders is ahead of internal plans despite muted seasonal uptake.
Transformation initiatives are on track to deliver approximately $150 million in total benefits, with 40% realized in the first half.
summary: JELD-WEN reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $776 million, a 19% year-over-year decline driven by volume reductions and the divestiture of Towanda operations.
