Adjusted EBITDA fell to $22 million (margin of 2.8%), with free cash flow turning into a use of $125 million due to lower earnings and unfavorable working capital dynamics. Management withdrew full-year guidance citing significant short-term volatility from tariffs and softer-than-expected demand, though they expect Q2 adjusted EBITDA to be slightly above Q1 levels.

negative_highlights: SMB adjusted gross margin contracted by 30 bps YoY due to reseller mix shifts and attrition in the historical residual portfolio.
Salaries, benefits, and SG&A expenses increased significantly (SG&A up $4.1M), partially offsetting top-line growth with lower operating leverage in SMB.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 9% YoY to $224.6 million, driven by strong performance across all three business segments.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 170 bps sequentially and adjusted EBITDA improved 11% YoY to $51.3 million.
B2B revenue surged 12.1% while Enterprise revenue grew 22.2%, with recurring revenues now comprising over 62% of total gross profit.
summary: Priority Technology Holdings reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue of $224.6 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.22 (up from $0.18 in the prior year quarter). The company maintained its full-year 2025 guidance for revenue ($965M-$1B) and adjusted EBITDA ($220M-$230M), citing strong growth in higher-margin B2B (+12%) and Enterprise (+22%) segments. Management expressed confidence in achieving sequential profit growth throughout the year despite macroeconomic uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Europe and APAC combined revenue down 6% on constant currency basis, with weaker March
Adjusted EBITDA declined 7.8% (3.6% ex-warrants) on constant currency basis
Input cost pressures and production inefficiencies hurt margins; gross margin declined
positive_highlights: North America net revenue up 33.5% with PPS volume growth of 45% in Q1
7th consecutive quarter of volume growth
Management confident in 50% automation growth for 2025, with projects continuing despite tariffs
summary: Ranpak reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated net revenue up 8.8% on a constant currency basis, driven by 12% volume growth and North America PPS volume up 45% (net revenue +33.5%). However, Europe and APAC revenue fell 6% on a constant currency basis due to March weakness, and adjusted EBITDA declined 7.8% (or 3.6% excluding Amazon warrants). Management announced structural cost reductions of $8 million, expects gross margin to improve sequentially in Q2 and further in Q3/Q4, and remains confident in 50% automation growth for the year despite tariff uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 3% year-over-year
Accessories and materials declined 15%, including 5 points of one-time benefit
90-day engaged users declined 4% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Paid subscribers up 6% year-over-year to 2.97 million
Connected machines revenue up 4%, with both note-in and note-out units up
International revenue up 8% year-over-year
summary: Cricut reported Q1 2025 revenue of $162.6 million, down 3% year-over-year, with net income of $23.9 million (14.7% margin). Paid subscribers rose 6% to 2.97 million, but accessories and materials declined 15% and 90-day engaged users fell 4%. Management noted tariff uncertainty but cited strong machine watch-in and watch-out, and highlighted capital allocation including a special dividend and share repurchase. The company guided to an inflection point later in 2025 but acknowledged risk from tariffs.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings reported for Q1 FY2023 as company is pre-revenue and cash-funded
Celly Nutrition's IPO plans are ongoing subject to market conditions; listing timeline uncertain
LUCID MS Phase 2 submission targeted for latter part of year with trial start hoped for early 2026
positive_highlights: Net cash available provides an 18-24 month forecast for future burn without financing
LUCID MS Phase 1 concluded with the drug well tolerated in healthy participants; toxicity studies underway
unbuzzd sales have started in Puerto Rico following partnership with FUSION
summary: This was a shareholder update call rather than an earnings report; the company reported no revenue or EPS for Q1 FY2023 as it remains pre-revenue and cash-funded through at least late 2027. Management highlighted progress on LUCID MS (Phase 1 concluded, moving to toxicity studies) and commercial launch of unbuzzd in Puerto Rico with sales now started. The company removed the going concern uncertainty from its financials but noted that Celly Nutrition's IPO plans are ongoing subject to market conditions.

negative_highlights: Direct subscription revenue declined slightly year-over-year due to marketing spend optimization and seasonality, though management notes this is manageable.
positive_highlights: Achieved first-ever positive net income ($0.3M) and adjusted EBITDA ($1.1M), marking a landmark turnaround from losses.
Revenue grew 26% year-over-year to $15.1 million, driven by licensing revenue growth of approximately $4 million which offset slight declines in direct subscriptions.
Adjusted free cash flow reached $2 million at the high end of guidance for Q2.
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $15.1 million (up 26% YoY) and achieved its first-ever positive net income ($0.3M) and adjusted EBITDA ($1.1M). Management raised the quarterly dividend from $0.04 to $0.08 per share, citing strong cash flow generation of $2 million in free cash flow which was at the high end of guidance for Q2 (expected revenue $16-17M and FCF $2-3M).

negative_highlights: A small number of advertisers have adjusted plans, redirecting spend from Q2 to later in the year
Some concern about macro uncertainty from tariffs, though minimal impact expected
Amazon competition was addressed, but perceived as a threat by some investors
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 32% YoY, exceeding guidance
Adjusted EBITDA up 76% YoY, ninth consecutive quarter of >30% growth
AI Bidding automates 85% of ad spend, with contribution ex-TAC up 75% YoY
summary: Viant reported record Q1 2025 results with revenue up 32% YoY and contribution ex-TAC up 25% YoY, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of >20% growth in contribution ex-TAC. Adjusted EBITDA grew 76% YoY to $5.4 million, the ninth straight quarter of >30% growth. The company highlighted strong performance despite tariffs, with March being the strongest month and April continuing double-digit growth. They raised Q2 guidance and are positioned for continued strength, citing CTV, addressability, and AI as key drivers.

negative_highlights: Rental income decreased by approximately 2% year-over-year to $11.7 million due to dispositions and acquisitions timing.
Management stated they are not finding compelling acquisition opportunities, with cap rates in the low-to-mid 7s deemed insufficient for current cost of capital (~14%).
Trading volume was elevated (32k shares) but stock price declined $0.25 to close at $14.58.
positive_highlights: AFFO increased 18% year-over-year to $3.9 million driven by lower interest expense ($200k decrease) and property expenses ($140k decrease).
Preferred shares were retired, reducing leverage and saving over $400,000 annually in preferred dividends.
Weighted average lease term remains strong at 14.2 years across the portfolio.
summary: Modiv Industrial reported Q1 FY2025 rental income of $11.7 million, a decrease from the prior year period due to property dispositions and acquisitions partially offsetting each other. Adjusted Funds From Operations (AFFO) was $3.9 million per share on an annualized basis ($0.03 diluted), reflecting lower cash interest expense but no revenue beat against implied expectations given the decline in rental income. Management maintained a cautious stance, citing market volatility and lack of compelling acquisition opportunities at current pricing.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $9.1 million from $6.1 million in prior year
Restaurant-level contribution margin down to 10.3% from 13.1%
COGS up 160 basis points to 26.6% due to new menu and one-time rollout costs
positive_highlights: Same-store sales up 4.4% system-wide in Q1, accelerating from Q4 growth of 0.5%
Post-menu launch same-store sales up approximately 5% through April despite difficult comparison
Double-digit increases in brand awareness, brand search traffic, and app sessions since relaunch
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $123.8 million, up 2% year-over-year, with system-wide same-store sales increasing 4.4% (company-owned 4.7%, franchise 2.9%). Traffic rose 1.8% and check increased 2.9% (1.3% pricing). Net loss widened to $9.1 million from $6.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.4 million from $5.5 million, pressured by one-time menu rollout costs and higher marketing. Management reiterated full-year guidance, widening the lower end of restaurant contribution margin by 50 basis points to account for tariffs, and noted same-store sales up ~5% through April post-menu launch. They expect free cash flow positive in Q3 and Q4.

negative_highlights: Q1 revenue missed consensus expectations due to a weaker-than-anticipated box office slate and tariff-related advertiser uncertainty.
Government advertising spend reduced significantly following policy shifts, impacting national on-screen revenue mix.
Adjusted OIBDA remained negative at $9M compared to the prior year's loss of only $5.7M.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue guidance raised to $56M-$61M, reflecting optimism about a strong upcoming box office slate including 'A Minecraft Movie' and 'Mission: Impossible'.
Secured a five-year extension with AMC Theaters through 2042 featuring improved payment structures aligned with performance metrics.
Launched new AI-driven products Bullseye and Blueprint to enhance targeting capabilities in the NCMx suite.
summary: NCMI reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $34.9 million, a 7% year-over-year decline driven by lower box office attendance and government ad spend reductions, which fell within the company's guidance range of $34M-$36M. Adjusted OIBDA was negative $9 million, aligning with prior guidance but reflecting reduced top-line performance. Management noted that while Q1 results were seasonally soft and impacted by specific film underperformance (e.g., Snow White), they do not view this as indicative of full-year performance.

negative_highlights: Net income and core operating income declined significantly due to higher loss activity and reinstatement premiums.
Currency revaluation negatively impacted non-U.S. dollar reserves by approximately 10 points.
positive_highlights: Combined ratio of 94.4% demonstrates resilience despite significantly elevated loss environment and macroeconomic uncertainty.
Reinsurance treaty segment showed strong top-line growth of almost 44% driven by new business in specialty lines.
Prior year development was favorable by $25.8 million, partially offsetting current accident year losses.
summary: IGIC reported Q1 FY2025 net income of $27.3 million ($0.59/share) and core operating income of $19.5 million ($0.42/share), both down significantly from the prior year due to elevated loss activity, reinstatement premiums, and currency impacts. The combined ratio was 94.4%, reflecting a 6-7 point quarter-over-quarter deterioration on a like-for-like basis after adjusting for approximately 10 points of currency revaluation impact. Management noted that while the short-tail and reinsurance segments showed growth, the long-tail segment recorded an underwriting loss of $7.5 million amidst declining rates and FX headwinds.

negative_highlights: Core revenue decreased 2% year-over-year primarily due to a complete loss of volume from one large consumer genomics customer in the SMS segment.
Revenue from the Together Take Me Home public health program is expected to drop significantly, falling from $8 million in 2024 to approximately $4 million for fiscal 2025.
U.S. diagnostics business faces elevated uncertainty due to potential budget cuts and staffing reductions at federal agencies like HHS and CDC.
positive_highlights: International diagnostics revenue grew 8% year-over-year driven by initial orders for the WHO PQ listed hepatitis C self-test and expansion in emergency room settings.
Sample Management Solutions (SMS) revenue excluding the single large customer disruption showed organic growth, demonstrating successful diversification of the customer base.
Board authorized a new $40 million share repurchase program over two years to fund capital deployment strategy.
summary: Q1 total revenue was $29.9 million and core revenue of $29.5 million decreased 2% year-over-year due to a significant disruption from a large consumer genomics customer in the Sample Management Solutions segment. While international diagnostics grew 8%, overall results were weighed down by headwinds including an expected end to the Together Take Me Home program later this year and continued uncertainty regarding U.S. public health funding. The company raised its Q2 guidance range slightly compared to prior expectations, citing a more stable outlook for PEPFAR programs than previously feared.

negative_highlights: CEO noted that near-term earnings may vary quarter-to-quarter as the company executes strategy in an uncertain economic environment.
Management indicated they are being patient and selective with new lending opportunities, waiting for market volatility related to tariffs to settle before regrowing the portfolio.
The Life Science Boston project continues to struggle with negative supply growth and potential conversion back to traditional office use.
positive_highlights: Collected $307 million in repayments, double the prior quarter's amount, representing the highest percentage of outstanding principal balance in company history.
Reduced net debt to equity ratio (excluding CECL) to 1.2x from 1.9x at end of Q1 2024 by reducing borrowings $228 million.
Book value per share remained stable at $9.88, supported by a reduction in the total CECL reserve to $140 million.
summary: ACRE reported Q1 FY2025 GAAP net income of $9.3 million ($0.17 per share) and distributable earnings of $7.2 million ($0.13 per share), with no realized losses incurred. The company significantly improved its liquidity position, reducing outstanding borrowings to $946 million and increasing available capital to $147 million through loan repayments of $307 million and refinancing actions. Management declared a regular cash dividend of $0.15 per common share for the second quarter.

negative_highlights: Lift Truck revenues declined 14% year-over-year, driving significant operating profit drop
Full-year 2025 revenues, production, and profits expected below 2024's strong results
April saw customer order hesitation due to tariff effects
positive_highlights: Q1 bookings of $590 million, up nearly 50% sequentially, with book-to-bill at 100%
Nuvera realignment expected to deliver $15-20 million annualized cost savings from second half 2025
Inventory down nearly $70 million year-over-year, supporting cash flow
summary: In Q1 2025, Hyster-Yale reported a 14% year-over-year decline in Lift Truck revenues due to lower volumes, with adjusted operating profit down significantly on reduced manufacturing absorption. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance below 2024's record results, noting Q2 operating profit is expected to decline moderately due to tariff cost timing. The company announced a strategic realignment of Nuvera away from fuel cells toward energy solutions, expecting $15-20 million annualized savings. Long-term targets include a 7% operating margin through the cycle.

negative_highlights: Royalty revenue was explicitly stated as lower in Q1 FY2025 compared to the same period last year.
Service revenue decreased due to the completion of certain small molecule ion channel programs, indicating a natural attrition cycle.
The newly launched exploration partner access program is excluded from 2025 financial guidance.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased year-over-year driven by a Phase I milestone from Genmab's 1078 clinical program.
Operating expenses declined to $23.0M due to lower stock-based compensation and reduced external costs on small molecule programs.
Net loss narrowed sequentially compared to the prior period.
summary: OmniAb reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $4.2 million (up from $3.8M in prior year) and a net loss narrowing to $18.2 million ($0.17/share). Management provided full-year 2025 guidance for revenue between $20-25 million, which excludes the new exploration partner access program launch announced today.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined by 30 basis points to 13.8% due to increased SG&A expenses related to investments in India and technology expansion.
Fintech vertical revenue decreased by 12%, though management notes this impact is expected to largely lap going forward.
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $140.7M representing an 11% YoY increase and the highest quarterly revenue ever for the company.
Adjusted EPS reached a record high of 82 cents, driven by higher margins from offshore regions (up 19%) and digital/omnichannel services growth.
Management raised full-year guidance on both revenue and EBITDA while initiating a new $15 million share repurchase program.
summary: IBEX reported record Q3 FY2025 revenue of $140.7 million (up 11% YoY) and adjusted EPS of 82 cents (up 18% YoY). Management raised full-year guidance for both revenue ($540-$545M vs prior $525-$535M) and EBITDA ($68-70M vs prior $68-69M), citing structural growth, market share gains in Q3 against seasonal trends, and the launch of a new $15 million share repurchase program. The quarter featured record profitability with adjusted EBITDA margins at 13.8% despite investments in India.

negative_highlights: Clinical solutions revenue declined more than 30% compared to Q1 2024 due to a large one-time order in the prior period not recurring.
Growth from biopharma custom products was lower than expected, though management maintains at least 15% growth guidance for the year.
Free cash flow remained negative ($4.3M) with an expectation of less than $12M outflow for the full year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew low double digits for catalog products (approx 60% of total) driven by increased customer count and general demand increase.
Gross margin expanded to 30.7%, exceeding previously communicated expectations, aided by higher revenue mix and lower overhead costs.
Operating expenses decreased $900k YoY excluding the prior year's non-recurring workforce reduction charge.
summary: Alpha Teknova reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $9.8 million (up 5% YoY), driven by low double-digit growth in catalog products but offset by a decline in clinical solutions due to the absence of one large year-ago order. Gross margin expanded significantly to 30.7%, while operating expenses decreased excluding non-recurring charges from the prior period. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $39M-$42M, maintaining expectations despite macro headwinds and lower-than-guided growth in biopharma custom products.

negative_highlights: Crude oil prices have significantly reduced since early March guidance, creating potential downside exposure for the crude-oriented Rockies segment.
Natural gas volumes averaged a decrease of 2 million cubic feet per day relative to the fourth quarter in the Rockies segment due to production declines.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased by $1.6 million in the Rockies segment and $9.6 million in the Mid-Con segment compared to Q4.
summary: Summit Midstream reported Q1 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $57.5 million and capital expenditures of $20.6 million against a full-year guidance range of $245-$280 million in adjusted EBITDA and $65-$75 million in capex, which management reiterated despite recent crude price softening. The company raised an additional $250 million in senior secured notes to repay revolver borrowings and maintain over $350 million liquidity while closing the accretive acquisition of Moonrise Midstream. Management noted that if all remaining second-half wells are deferred due to lower prices, they would trend toward the low end of existing guidance.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined year-over-year by approximately 24% to $35.7 million due to reduced store count and demand softness.
Management withdrew full-year guidance entirely, citing tariff uncertainty and potential fluctuations in consumer demand.
Store traffic dropped significantly in areas without vibrant caregiver laws as consumers walk away from retail.
positive_highlights: Proprietary product sales accounted for 32% of total revenue, up from 22.6% in the prior year period.
Gross margins expanded to 27.2%, reflecting a stronger product mix and disciplined execution on procurement.
The company ended the quarter with $52.6 million in liquidity and no debt.
summary: GrowGeneration reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue of $35.7 million, a decline from the prior year's $47.9 million due to reduced store count and softness in durables demand driven by tariff concerns. Gross margins improved sequentially to 27.2% as proprietary brand sales reached 32% of total revenue, but management withdrew full-year guidance citing macroeconomic uncertainty while providing a Q2 expectation of over $40 million.

negative_highlights: Q1 product revenues of $6 million low versus prior quarter
Pretax operating loss of $2 million and net loss of $1 million
PEP submission delayed to H1 2026 with sample analysis not expected until Q4 2025
positive_highlights: April deliveries of $62 million to SNS expected to be recognized in Q2
U.S. government exercised $26 million IV option and added $14 million manufacturing funding
Special cash dividend of $0.60 per share declared, fourth consecutive year
summary: SIGA reported Q1 2025 product revenues of $6 million from an international sale, with pretax operating loss of $2 million and net loss of $1 million. The company highlighted April deliveries of $62 million to the SNS, a $26 million IV order for 2026 delivery, and a $14 million contract modification for manufacturing. Management expressed confidence in the U.S. government partnership and expects substantial sales ahead, but provided no formal revenue guidance.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 9% YoY to $17.5 million, driven primarily by a 10% decrease in account utilization.
Dry eye segment revenue fell significantly from $1M to $400k due to fewer SmartLids sales following the price increase enacted in October 2024.
Surgical glaucoma revenue decreased 6% YoY as Medicare coverage for multiple MIGS procedures was restricted.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating expenses decreased 7% YoY to $24.7 million due to lower legal fees and expense controls offsetting tariffs.
Ordering accounts increased 3% sequentially despite the new Medicare LCD restrictions on stacked MIGS procedures.
Gross margin remained flat at 86%, as tariff impacts were deferred by using pre-tariff inventory.
summary: Sight Sciences reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $17.5 million (down 9% YoY) and adjusted operating expenses of $24.7 million (down 7% YoY). Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance at approximately $70-75M but lowered the adjusted expense guidance to $101-105M from a prior range of $105-107M, citing tariff impacts and fiscal discipline. The quarter was impacted by new Medicare LCD restrictions on stacked MIGS procedures in five states.

negative_highlights: Total revenues decreased by approximately 1.4% YoY to $34.6 million due to portfolio changes.
FFO ($0.20/share) and AFFO ($0.22/share) both declined sequentially from the prior year quarter.
Q1 lease renewal rate was lower than typical at roughly 62%, with Q2 expected volatility including a non-renewing 50,000 sq ft lease.
positive_highlights: Net income attributable to common shareholders increased significantly YoY from $800k in Q1 2024 to $2.1 million in Q1 2025 ($0.03/share vs $0.01/share).
Successfully closed a strategic five-property acquisition for $69.6 million at an attractive 9% cap rate, substantially below replacement cost.
Completed the sale of two medical properties generating aggregate gross proceeds of $8.2 million and a gain of $1.4 million.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue decreased by approximately 1.4% to $34.6 million due to acquisitions and dispositions, while expenses fell slightly to $32.2 million driven by non-cash compensation adjustments related to the CEO transition. Net income attributable to common shareholders was $2.1 million ($0.03/share), representing a significant YoY increase from $800k in Q1 2024 primarily due to lower prior-year comparables rather than operational expansion, as FFO and AFFO per share declined sequentially by roughly $0.01 each. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 AFFO guidance of $0.89-$0.93 despite the CEO succession plan impacting Q2-G&A expenses.

negative_highlights: Gross margin improvement was partially offset by lower negative pressure wound therapy equipment sales ($200k decrease) and lower margin new business in Patient Services.
Chemo Mouthpiece revenue is delayed due to formulary adoption and billing logistics, with meaningful revenue expected later in 2025.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8.5% YoY to $34.7 million, with Patient Services up 11.7% and Device Solutions up 4%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 18.2%, the highest since 2021, driven by improved collections and revenue mix.
Operating cash flow improved nearly fourfold to $1.8 million compared to the prior year quarter.
summary: InfuSystem reported Q1 FY2025 net revenue of $34.7 million, an 8.5% increase year-over-year, driven by strong growth in Patient Services and Device Solutions segments. Adjusted EBITDA reached $6.3 million (18.2% margin), representing a 64% year-over-year improvement and the highest first-quarter result since 2021. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance of 8% to 10% growth and expects adjusted EBITDA margins to exceed the prior year's 18.8%, noting that Q1 results put the company on track despite ongoing IT upgrade costs.

negative_highlights: D2C advertising revenue declined 9%, including an 800-basis point headwind from last year's Super Bowl comparison.
TV Media affiliate revenue declined 8.6% due to subscriber declines and recent deal renewals.
Digital advertising monetization is softer than expected due to increased supply, with no immediate firming observed.
positive_highlights: D2C OIBDA improved by $177 million to a loss of $109 million driven by subscriber growth and churn reduction (improved 130 bps YoY).
Paramount+ ended the quarter with 79 million global subscribers, up 11% year-over-year.
Film segment revenue grew 4% to $627m primarily due to Sonic the Hedgehog 3 box office success of nearly $500 million.
summary: Paramount Global reported Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $7.2 billion (up 2% YoY excluding the Super Bowl) and adjusted OIBDA of $688 million. D2C subscription revenue grew 16%, while TV Media advertising was flat ex-Super Bowl, with affiliate revenue down 8.6%. Management reiterated full-year guidance for Paramount+ domestic profitability but noted macro uncertainty could impact later-quarter results.

negative_highlights: Second-line Bolster cohort enrollment capped at ~20 patients, half of original target
FORTIFIDE study initiation remains on hold pending a potentially cheaper alternative
Cash runway only into Q3 2026, constraining ability to initiate new trials
positive_highlights: ASCEND Cohort A showed positive overall survival trend and 4 complete responses vs 0 in placebo
Bolster first-line enrollment completed ~6 months ahead of plan, accelerating top-line data to mid-2025
Qilu completed enrollment in 96-subject study; $10 million milestone due upon first Phase 3 patient dosing
summary: Lisata reported Q1 2025 operating expenses of $5.8 million, down 11.4% year-over-year, with R&D spend down 19.7% to $2.6 million. Net loss narrowed to $4.7 million from $5.4 million in Q1 2024. Cash and marketable securities stood at $25.8 million, expected to fund operations into Q3 2026. Management highlighted upcoming data readouts across ASCEND, Bolster, and CENDIFOX trials, with no guidance change.

negative_highlights: note and administrative expenses increased due to approximately $500k in professional fees for a multiyear financial restatement
Cash balance decreased from $600,000 at June 30, 2024 to $500,000 as of March 31, 2025 due to working capital changes
Management acknowledged tariff pressures forcing price list updates and the need for rapid supplier diversification
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 16% YoY driven by unit growth of 25% in GSE markets and 10% in material handling
Gross margin expanded to 32%, a 4.7 percentage point increase from the prior year quarter, aided by lower warranty costs
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed significantly to $1.1 million compared to $1.7 million last year
summary: Flux Power Holdings reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $16.7 million (up 16% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 32%, driven by unit growth in material handling (+10%) and GSE markets (+25%). The company posted an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.1M, narrowing from a prior year loss of $1.7M due to higher gross profit partially offset by restatement-related S&A expenses. Management noted tariff headwinds requiring price adjustments but expressed confidence in maintaining momentum through supply chain diversification and domestic assembly expansion.

negative_highlights: Revenue performance fell note weakness in of expectations due to a sales force realignment that was 'more significant than initially anticipated'.
Full-year revenue guidance for 2025 was lowered, with management stating Q1 results set the new baseline.
Approximately half (50%) of current territory managers were hired in the last 15 months and are still ramping up productivity.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% YoY despite significant headwinds, driven by expansion into new territories and accounts in the US heart failure business ($11.1M revenue).
Gross margin remained stable at 84%, consistent with full-year guidance of 83-84%.
New clinical evidence presented showed an 85% reduction in heart failure hospital visits post-Barostim implantation.
summary: CVRX reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $12.3 million (up 15% YoY) and a net loss narrowing to $13.8 million ($0.53/share). Management explicitly stated the quarter fell short of expectations due primarily to significant sales force realignment, with 25% of territory managers hired between December and March causing disruption in 'dabbler' accounts. Full-year 2025 guidance was lowered to $55-$58 million revenue (down from prior implied higher levels) while maintaining gross margin guidance at 83-84%. Q2 guidance is set at $13-$14 million.

negative_highlights: Three major offshore fields impacted by mechanical issues, volumes below normalized levels
Incremental segment margin from new projects dependent on producers hitting their numbers
No significant market impact yet from new leasing program—opportunities years away
positive_highlights: Shenandoah FPU moored, SYNC pipeline commissioning by end of May, first oil expected in June
Marine Transportation on pace to post record earnings in 2025
Cash costs reduced to $425-450 million per year from soda ash sale
summary: Genesis Energy exited its soda ash business, using proceeds to reduce debt and lower annual cash costs to $425-450 million. Offshore pipeline volumes declined due to producer mechanical issues but are expected to normalize by Q3, with Shenandoah and Salamanca startups on track and new tiebacks adding volumes. Marine Transportation is on pace for record earnings in 2025, and the company plans to allocate excess cash to redeeming preferred units, debt reduction, and potential unitholder returns.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income guidance was cut significantly from the prior high of $38.8M down to a new range top of $34M.
Adjusted EBITDA turned negative at -$12.5M compared to +$2.6M in Q1 2024, driven by a $6.6 million write-down on assets held for sale and product expiration.
Advanced Wound Care revenue declined 23% due to the delayed LCD implementation causing customer confusion and inventory expiry.
positive_highlights: Revenue delivered in line with the previously issued guidance range despite significant market uncertainty.
Surgical and Sports Medicine segment revenue grew 11% year-over-year, providing a partial offset to Advanced Wound Care declines.
Management reaffirmed confidence in executing strategy post-LCD delay due to portfolio optionality.
summary: First quarter net revenue was $86.7 million, down 21% year-over-year due to customer demand disruption and product expiration from LCD delays, though results were in line with prior guidance range of $85-95M. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance but lowered profitability expectations significantly, narrowing GAAP net income guidance by approximately half (from a high of ~$38.8M to a new high of $34M) and reducing EBITDA guidance similarly due to Q1 write-downs and margin pressure from excess inventory.

negative_highlights: Marketplace revenue declined due to intentional reduction in marketing spend
BNPL originations dipped due to seasonal shift and tightened underwriting
Fintech revenue ramp expected later in year, not immediate
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 95% YoY to $6.75 million
Operating expenses decreased 10% YoY while revenue nearly doubled
Received largest-ever $2 million bulk order from Pregnancy Resource Center coalition
summary: PSQ Holdings reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $6.75 million, up 95% year over year, with fintech contributing $3.05 million, marketplace adding $0.4 million, and brands (EveryLife) $3.27 million. Operating expenses decreased 10% year over year to $14 million, and total margin expanded to 58% from 43%. The company highlights strong fintech onboarding, a $2 million recurring bulk order for EveryLife, and expects revenue ramp in Q3 and Q4, while noting a deliberate reduction in marketplace marketing led to lower marketplace revenue. Fintech underwriting was tightened due to a soft consumer credit environment.

negative_highlights: Q1 revenue was impacted by delayed carrier mobile broadband promotions, lower FWA purchases from a key customer transitioning inventory, and the end of a special national program.
Mobile hotspot promotion started later than anticipated in Q1.
Gross margin expected to moderate to high-30s in Q2 due to higher product revenue mix.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $3.7 million exceeded expectations for a fourth consecutive quarter.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to a record 47.5% driven by favorable revenue mix and sequential expansion.
Services revenue grew nearly 50% year-over-year on the strength of SaaS platforms.
summary: Inseego delivered Q1 FY2025 revenue within guidance and adjusted EBITDA of $3.7 million (up from the prior year quarter), driven by a record non-GAAP gross margin of 47.5% despite lower FWA purchases during a transition period. Management provided Q2 2025 guidance for total revenue between $37M-$40M and adjusted EBITDA between $2.5M-$3.5M, noting that sequential growth is expected to begin in Q2 as the company transitions from record prior-year levels.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross margin contracted by approximately 50 basis points due to commodity input costs (nitrile) and adverse foreign currency rates.
Products & Healthcare Services revenue declined 0.8% YoY, with tariffs expected to impact annual exposure between $100M-$150M requiring price increases in June.
Q1 cash flow was the weakest of the year due to working capital consumption for inventory and costs related to Rotech acquisition discussions.
positive_highlights: Patient Direct revenue grew by 6% YoY, with sleep supplies showing high single-digit growth and oxygen therapy seeing continued recovery.
Adjusted operating income for Patient Direct expanded significantly by 31%, driven by improved collection rates and category expansion in wound/ostomy/urology.
Management reaffirmed full-year guidance despite the tariff headwinds and potential distraction from the P&HS segment sale process.
summary: Owens & Minor reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $2.6 billion (up ~1% YoY) and adjusted net income of $18 million ($0.23/share), beating expectations with a solid beat in the Patient Direct segment which grew 6%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance despite acknowledging significant tariff exposure estimated between $100M-$150M, primarily impacting the Products & Healthcare Services (P&HS) segment where price increases are scheduled for early June. The company noted that Q1 cash flow was weaker than usual due to inventory build and acquisition costs but expects marked improvement in subsequent quarters.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was widened to reflect downside risks from tariffs and macroeconomic uncertainty.
Management explicitly stated that the first half of 2025 is expected to be challenging due to transformation costs and external headwinds.
Potential tariff impacts on customer supply chains remain a 'wait-and-see' risk with no material impact seen yet but acknowledged as a downside factor.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin strengthened significantly to 80.3%, up 240 basis points year-over-year.
Pipeline growth is particularly strong in the B2B segment following sales organization realignment.
ARR reached $351 million, a 3% increase year-over-year.
summary: BigCommerce reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $82.4 million (3% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $7.6 million with a margin expansion to 9.2%. Management delivered results within the previously issued guidance range but widened full-year 2025 revenue guidance from $315M-$335M to $335.1M-$351.1M and non-GAAP operating income guidance due to macroeconomic uncertainty, tariffs, and potential consumer spending shifts.

negative_highlights: Net investment income declined quarter-over-quarter due to one-time expenses and lower base rates
NAV per share declined to $17.96 from $18.18
One portfolio company was placed on non-accrual status during the quarter
positive_highlights: Net investment income excluding non-recurring items was $0.56 per share, in line with Q4 2024
Portfolio remains highly diversified with non-accruals at 0.4% of fair value
Platform investment activity up 60% year over year in Q1
summary: Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp reported Q1 2025 net investment income of $0.53 per share, or $0.56 excluding one-time expenses, in line with Q4 2024. Total investment income declined to $53.6 million due to lower base rates. NAV fell to $17.96 from $18.18, driven by valuation declines in watch list names. Management expressed confidence in navigating tariff-related volatility, citing portfolio insulation and a strong pipeline.

negative_highlights: Loss ratio includes $10 million in Southern California wildfire losses
Q1 operating margins only 8% due to seasonality and tech investments
Guidance reaffirmed but not raised despite strong quarter
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 18% to $320 million
Net income up 233% and adjusted EBITDA up 45%
Membership, Marketplace and Other revenue grew 60%
summary: In Q1 2025, Hagerty reported total revenue of $320 million, up 18%, with net income of $27 million, a 233% increase, and adjusted EBITDA of $40 million, up 45%. Written premium grew 12% and commission revenue grew 13%, while membership, marketplace and other revenue jumped 60% due to strong auction results. Operating margins expanded 360 basis points to 8% despite $10 million in wildfire losses. Management reaffirmed 2025 guidance of 12-13% revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA of $150-160 million, noting technology transformation spending is on track.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $10.7 million from $6.6 million

Revenue pipeline expected to be back-end loaded with limited near-term deal visibility

CAPTAIN trial demonstrates TULSA has no blood loss and no overnight stay versus robotic prostatectomy

Net loss widened to $10.7 million from $6.6 million, with operating expenses up to $13 million from $8.7 million. Management highlighted the CAPTAIN trial data at AUA showing TULSA advantages over robotic prostatectomy, new TULSA AI BPH module release plans, and reimbursement catalyst, but reiterated a back-end loaded revenue pipeline for the year.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year by 10% with paid employers down 11%.
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted sharply from 17% in Q1 '24 to just 5%.
Net loss widened materially from $6.5 million in Q1 '24 to $12.8 million.

summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $110 million, representing a 1% sequential decline and a 10% year-over-year decrease compared to Q4 '24 ($111M) and Q1 '24 respectively. Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted significantly from 17% in the prior year quarter to 5%, while net loss widened to $12.8 million. Management provided Q2 guidance of $111 million at the midpoint, maintaining a cautious outlook due to macroeconomic uncertainty despite sequential growth.

negative_highlights: OEM channel revenue down 23% due to lower J&J pricing and contractually obligated rebates

Manufacturing yield issues for Monovisc and Cingal led to higher scrap and lower gross margin, with full-year gross margin expected to be lower

summary: Anika's Q1 2025 revenue was $26.2M, down 10% YoY, with commercial channel up 18% to $11.3M and OEM channel down 23% to $14.9M due to J&J pricing pressure. Adjusted EBITDA was essentially breakeven at $100K, down from $2.7M, and gross margin fell to 56%. The company lowered full-year OEM guidance to $62M-$65M and adjusted EBITDA guidance to -3% to +3%, citing lower pricing, manufacturing yield issues, tariffs, and Cingal study costs. Management expects gross margin improvement in H2 2025 to 58%-59% and continues to see strong Integrity growth.

negative_highlights: Total prescriptions declined approximately 9% quarter-over-quarter and 8% year-over-year.

Cash burn increased from approximately $4.3 million earned in Q4 2024 to approximately $7.8 million burned in Q1 2025.

Phase I trial data for neratinib + Enhertu showed tumor regression in advanced pancreatic cancer patients, with Dose Level 3 selected as Recommended Phase II dose.
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q1 FY2025 net product revenue of $43.1 million, a decline from the prior quarter's $54.4 million and an increase year-over-year to $40.3 million. The quarterly miss was driven by approximately $4.7 million in inventory drawdown at specialty pharmacies and distributors rather than demand weakness alone. Management provided full-year 2025 guidance for net NERLYNX revenue between $192M-$198M, which is lower than the prior year due to expected reduced shipments from China.

negative_highlights: Book value per share fell to negative $42.22 from negative $40.99
PREPA exposure remains large and timing of resolution uncertain
Foreign exchange losses and investment fair value losses partially offset improvements

summary: MBIA reported a Q1 2025 GAAP net loss of $62 million (negative $1.28 per share), improved from an $86 million loss ($1.84 per share) in Q1 2024, with adjusted net loss narrowing to $8 million from $24 million. Losses improved due to lower PREPA-related losses and reduced operating expenses, but were partially offset by foreign exchange losses and higher RMBS losses. Book value per share deteriorated to negative $42.22 from negative $40.99. PREPA resolution remains uncertain, though the company notes litigation stays have been lifted and expresses cautious optimism about progress.

negative_highlights: Cash, cash equivalents, and note weakness in-term deposits declined from $131 million at end of Q4 to $112.5 million by March 31.

summary: Valens Semiconductor reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $16.8 million, exceeding the top end of guidance ($16.3M-$16.6M), with GAAP gross margin expanding to 62.9% and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to $4.3 million within expectations. Management highlighted significant automotive design wins including a partnership with Mobileye for EyeQ6 programs, while noting that Q2 revenue guidance remains unchanged at $16.5M-$16.8M despite ongoing tariff monitoring.

negative_highlights: Total annuity sales declined 21% year-over-year, driven by lower fixed annuity sales

summary: Q1 2025 adjusted earnings were $235M including a $10M notable item; excluding that, $245M versus $268M a year ago and $352M in Q4 2024, about $15M/0.26 below run-rate. Annuity sales were $2.3B, down 21% YoY on lower fixed annuity sales, while Shield sales grew 5% YoY and life sales rose 24% YoY. Management confirmed the mid-year target for updated statutory free cash flow projections is no longer realistic and declined to give a new date.

Management provided Q2 guidance for low to mid-single digit revenue growth, citing continued Southwest strength but maintaining caution due to macro volatility and potential second-half rig count reductions.

negative_highlights: Cost of goods sold surged by $5.6 million (215%) year-over-year to $8.2 million, significantly compressing gross margins.
Management explicitly stated that future revenues from license/R&D services will be minimal following the linear amortization of prior development costs.
No financial guidance was provided for Q2 or full year 2025.

Phase one clinical trial for PRX-115 completed all cohorts with encouraging results showing dose-dependent reduction in plasma uric acid levels.
Commercial partner Chiesi reported strong sales efforts and patient recruitment pace exceeding expectations.

The company recorded a net loss of approximately $3.6 million for the quarter compared to $4.6 million in Q1 FY2024. Management provided no updated financial guidance and noted that future revenues will be minimal from license/R&D services, with potential regulatory milestones capped at an estimated $75 million.

Operating income declined to a loss of $2 million from a loss of $1.1 million last year, though adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.1 million due to cost reductions and digital margin expansion. Management maintains Q2 revenue pacing at down 10% citing macroeconomic pressure but notes bright spots in Philadelphia and New Jersey.

negative_highlights: Core advertising revenue fell 3%, with automotive (low double-digits) and retail (mid-single digits) being the worst performers.
Local distribution revenue decreased 5% year-over-year, consistent with mid-single-digit subchurn trends expected to continue in Q2.
The company reported a $4 million restructuring charge that increased the loss per share by an additional $0.04.
positive_highlights: Scripps Networks achieved a record margin improvement of 870 basis points for Q1, significantly exceeding guidance of 400-600 bps.
Connected TV revenue grew strongly by 42% driven by effective sales strategies and the NWSL/WNBA partnerships.
The company successfully completed refinancing transactions to retire or extend up to $1.5 billion in debt.
summary: First quarter revenue declined approximately 1% year-over-year due to a 3% drop in core advertising and a 5% decline in local distribution revenue driven by economic uncertainty. While Scripps Networks delivered its highest margins since Q4 2022 at 32%, the company reported an EPS loss of $0.22, which was slightly better than consensus but still negative due to preferred dividends and restructuring charges.

NOPARK study results may take a year or more to be public after June completion
Concerns about marketplace competitors note ineffective NAD products
positive_highlights: Revenue up 38% year-over-year to $30.5 million, record quarter

Full-year revenue growth guidance raised to 20-25% from approximately 18%

Gross margin improved to 63.4% from 60.7%. Full-year revenue growth guidance was raised from approximately 18% to 20-25% year-over-year. The company also noted strong growth in e-commerce (up 31%) and ingredient sales (up 95%).

negative_highlights: IT, Life Sciences, and Data Solutions gross profit declined 5.3% YoY to $3.6 million
Health Care consolidated gross margin compressed slightly from 29.0% to 28.2%
Engineering normalized gross margins were lower than expected due to pass-through construction revenue
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 14.4% YoY to $7.8 million

summary: RCM Technologies reported Q1 FY2025 consolidated gross profit of $22.0 million (up 7.9% YoY) and Adjusted EPS of $0.63 (up 18.9% YoY). Management highlighted strong growth in Health Care (+10.2%) and Engineering (+12.4%), though IT/Life Sciences declined slightly (-5.3%). The company reduced net debt by $12.0 million to $18.2 million while retiring over 300,000 shares year-to-date.

negative_highlights: Q1 EPS of $0.19 below adjusted Q4 2024 EPS of $0.31

Higher SG&A and R&D expenses in the quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue up 45% to $3.1M, with hardware up 78%

Operating income increased by $526,000, with operating expenses declining to 56% of revenue from 71% a year ago. EPS rose to $0.19 from $0.03, though adjusted for tax and audit expenses it would be $0.27. The company is launching new Omni and OmniPro monitors in June and has filed to uplist to Nasdaq, expecting completion by Q3 2025.

negative_highlights: Still reporting GAAP net loss of $7 million for the quarter
Approximately 20% of Q1 revenue exposed to reciprocal tariffs (5% at 145%, 15% at 10%)
Cash remains low at $20.3 million and converting $50 million due early 2026
positive_highlights: Revenue up 92.2% YoY and 9.1% sequentially to $18.8 million
Gross margin expanded to 38.1% from 28.2% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 67.4% to $2 million; targeting positive EBITDA in Q2
summary: Tigo Energy reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $18.8 million, up 92.2% YoY and 9.1% sequentially, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Gross margin improved to 38.1% from 28.2% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 67.4% to $2 million. For Q2 2025, the company guides revenue between $21 million and $23 million and adjusted EBITDA between negative $1.5 million and positive $500,000, reiterating full-year revenue guidance of $85-$100 million. Management cited broad geographic growth, tariff exposure limited to about 20% of Q1 revenue, and confidence in continued top-line growth.

negative_highlights: Reported revenue growth was dampened by approximately $400,000 in foreign exchange headwinds.
Latin America volume declined slightly due to the acquisition of a top customer by another lab.
Liquid biopsy applications (MSK-ACCESS) are still in early stages with modest initial volumes expected to ramp in H2.

Adjusted gross margin expanded 273 bps year-over-year to a record 68.7% (IFRS) / 75.7% (non-IFRS).
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved 24% year-over-year to $9.8 million, demonstrating operational leverage.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $17.8 million on a reported basis (15% constant currency), driven by strong new business and U.S. market expansion. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $72-76 million and adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $35-39 million, noting that the quarter was slightly ahead of expectations but maintaining a back-half-weighted outlook.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 8% YoY due to a significant drop in instrument sales ($1.4M vs $1.9M).
SPL program-related revenue fell from $3.2 million in Q1 FY2024 to $2.1 million.
Customers are exhibiting hesitation and caution regarding capital equipment purchasing decisions.

Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, indicating confidence in the pipeline despite current headwinds.

Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for core revenue growth (excluding SeQure Dx) of 8% to 15% and SPL program-related revenue of approximately $5 million, citing cautious customer capital spending but confidence in executing against the pipeline.

summary: Q1 2025 revenue was $150.5M, near the upper end of guidance ($146-152M) and up about 6% QoQ. Adjusted EBITDA was $16.5M, up about 17% QoQ. Segment growth was led by coiled tubing (+16% QoQ) and cementing (+4% QoQ, jobs +11%). Management guided Q2 revenue to $138-148M, expecting declines due to oil price weakness and tariff-related cost pressure, while citing strong April and a supportive natural gas outlook.

negative_highlights: Professional services revenue down 42% YoY
RPO declined 9% sequentially

positive_highlights: Record total revenue of $47M, up 5% YoY, above the high end of guidance

Net dollar retention improved to 107%, the highest since Q1 2022, but the company maintained its full-year revenue guidance, citing seasonal slow bookings and macro uncertainty, while slightly raising adjusted EBITDA guidance.

negative_highlights: Core income decreased by $3.7 million year-over-year primarily due to increased policy acquisition costs resulting from lower seeding commission income.
Operating expenses increased significantly by $12.1 million, driven largely by a 144.8% increase in policy acquisition costs.
positive_highlights: Gross premiums written grew by over 7% compared to the same period last year, reaching a total of $68.3 million in net premium earned.

Management noted that while new business growth and retention remain strong at approximately 88%, they are proceeding cautiously with their apartment building initiative as the market is more competitive than expected.

Free cash flow negative $10.8 million, down $28.6 million YoY

positive_highlights: Core business grew 3.3% across all divisions, first growth in five quarters
D2C channel grew over 10% and third-party platforms grew over 50%
Gross margin up 200 bps from operational efficiencies and lower warranty costs
summary: Holley reported Q1 2025 net sales of $153 million with 3.3% core business growth, the first growth in five quarters, driven by D2C (up >10%) and B2B (up >2.5%), with third-party platforms like Amazon growing over 50%. negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 8% to $21.2 million due to negative sales mix, higher production costs, and transition expenses for the new Indiana facility.

positive_highlights: Net sales increased 10% YoY led by strong performance from debit and credit cards and prepaid solutions.
summary: CPI Card Group reported Q1 FY2025 net sales growth of 10% driven by debit/credit and prepaid segments, but adjusted EBITDA declined 8% to $21.2 million due to negative sales mix and increased production costs including a new Indiana facility transition. negative_highlights: R&D expenses were higher than expected at $45 million, with management indicating this pace will likely continue.
Cash consumption was elevated due to a working capital timing gain that slipped from Q1 to Q2, masking underlying burn rates.

positive_highlights: Backlog remains unchanged at approximately 2,800 aircraft with a total value close to $14 billion based on list price.
Full-scale prototype testing is progressing toward initial flights in 2025, including successful pusher motor and lifter motor tests.
Conforming prototype assembly site at Embraer's facility in Sao Jose dos Campos is ready to receive tooling for the certification campaign.
summary: EVEX reported a net loss of $49 million in Q1 FY2025, driven by $45 million in program development costs and $8 million in SG&A. negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin was flat sequentially at 33%, dragged down by lower-margin Motif operations compared to the core business.

Adjusted EBITDA swung to positive $4.9 million from a loss in the prior year, driven by higher margins and Motif integration synergies. Management reiterated guidance that results will continue improving through Q3 and Q4 seasonality.

negative_highlights: Revenue was flat at $7.3 million primarily due to a seasonal inventory drawdown masking the underlying 15% demand growth.
Q1 results were transitional following the divestiture of UDENYCA and significant sales force restructuring which impacted momentum.
positive_highlights: Patient demand grew 15% in Q1 driven by new patient starts and increased duration of treatment despite revenue flatness due to inventory drawdown.

Management provided guidance for full-year 2025 SG&A between $90-100 million following the divestiture.

negative_highlights: Multiplatform Group revenue declined 4.2% YoY ($473M), with political advertising drag reducing the decline.

Management reiterated full-year 2025 revenue guidance of down low single digits but noted that current macro volatility requires positive movement in the back half of the year to avoid negative impacts.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $3 million for the quarter

International real estate exit not yet finalized; definitive plan deferred to next quarter
positive_highlights: Revenue up 14% and core segment up 23% year-over-year

summary: AlTi's Q1 FY2025 revenue was $58 million, up 14% year-over-year, with core Wealth Management and Capital Solutions revenue up 23% and segment adjusted EBITDA of $19 million at a 34% margin. Management is executing a zero-based budgeting program expected to yield substantial savings fully reflected in 2026, with further cost and real estate exit details to come in August.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance lowered significantly with an expected decline of 5-13%, down from prior expectations.

negative_highlights: Gross margin decreased from 62.0% to 60.9%, primarily due to product and channel partner mix shifts.

positive_highlights: Revenue grew 11% YoY to $21.9 million, beating consensus estimates.

Committed contracted revenue exceeded $70 million, representing a greater than 25% year-over-year increase.

negative_highlights: Critical care revenue fell 25% YoY due to customer inventory timing

positive_highlights: Pediatrics and heart failure revenue up 38% and 28% YoY

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered from prior expectations due to a one-quarter delay in hiring primary care and associate sales reps.

positive_highlights: Revenue grew 21% year-over-year driven by lung diagnostics (up 16%) and development services (up 61%).

summary: Biodesix reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $18 million (up 21% YoY) and gross margins expanding to 79.4%, but adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $6.2 million due to sales force reconfiguration delays. negative_highlights: Dropping one rig for May–August and pausing completions due to macro uncertainty and weak oil prices.

EBITDA nearly $200 million, up ~10% QoQ on similar oil price.

summary: HighPeak Energy reported Q1 2025 production of over 53,000 Boe/d, beating guidance and consensus, up ~6% sequentially, with EBITDA near $200 million, up ~10% QoQ. The company is taking proactive steps to manage activity in a volatile market by dropping one rig for four months and pausing completions, while still expecting to complete the same number of wells as originally guided. Guidance was narrowed with the floor raised to 48,000 Boe/d, and management highlighted significant drilling efficiencies (spud-to-spud down to 11 days) and expects further cost savings from simul-frac operations. Capital spend was 38% of the full-year budget in Q1, but the company still generated positive free cash flow.

Management announced termination of SEEG distribution to focus on higher-margin RNS business, with minimal 2025 revenue impact.

Management highlighted strong international medical export growth of 285% year-over-year in Canada but noted that retail branded sales were lower due to a strategic shift away from low-margin value offerings.

summary: SoundThinking reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $28.3 million (up 12% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $4.5 million (up 50% YoY), driven by catch-up revenue from delayed NYPD contracts. positive_highlights: Q1 revenues of $17.4 million, up ~3x sequentially and ~2.5x YoY, a record

summary: Q1 2025 revenues were a record $17.4 million, up ~3x sequentially and ~2.5x year-over-year, with record gross margin of ~40%, driven by NRE payments and LiDAR sales. The company expanded its NRE payment plan from ~$80 million to ~$95 million, ended Q1 with $85.4 million in cash, and maintained full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $50-60 million (more than twofold YoY growth). Management highlighted a new manufacturing partnership with Fabrinet, accelerated LiDAR shipments to Volkswagen for robotaxi deployments, and expanding collaboration with NVIDIA. They expect first Fabrinet product unit shipments within a month and continue to target 1-3 new programs in 2025.

negative_highlights: Israel Innovation Authority grant declined to $25,000 from $209,000 year-over-year
Gross margin may vary with mix; expected range 72%-76%
positive_highlights: Record Q1 revenue of $16.6 million, up 17.5% year-over-year
Raising full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance to 15%-18%
Highest-ever non-GAAP operating income of $3.1 million and $4.4 million positive cash flow
summary: RADCOM reported record Q1 2025 revenue of $16.6 million, up 17.5% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating income of $3.1 million (19% of revenue) and cash flow of $4.4 million, ending the quarter with $99.1 million in cash and no debt. The company raised its full-year 2025 revenue growth guidance from 12%-15% to 15%-18% year-over-year, citing strong momentum and strategic partnerships with ServiceNow and Nvidia. Management highlighted expanding agentic AI capabilities and a renewed tier-one North American contract.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $3.5 million from $1.8 million
Tissue Health Plus segment adjusted EBITDA loss deepened to $2.0 million
SG&A expenses increased 32% year-over-year
positive_highlights: Net revenue up 26% year-over-year to $23.4 million
Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 92%
Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA up $1.5 million to $2.7 million
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q1 2025 net revenue of $23.4 million, up 26% year-over-year, with soft tissue repair products up 28% and bone fusion up 18%. Gross margin improved 240 basis points to 92%, and Sanara Surgical segment adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.7 million from $1.2 million. The company reaffirmed its growth expectations, narrowed THP cash investment guidance, and remains on track to launch the THP pilot in Q2. Net loss widened to $3.5 million due to higher SG&A and interest expense.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased moderately due to a reporting change including fuel gross at Camarillo and startup costs, obscuring underlying operational efficiency.
Management explicitly identified new competition as its 'biggest concern today' in response to analyst questions about replicators of the model.
positive_highlights: Revenues surged 133% year-over-year driven by full quarter operations at the newly acquired Camarillo campus and ramp-up in Phoenix, Dallas, and Denver.
Management reaffirmed prior guidance to achieve consolidated cash flow breakeven before year-end as leasing accelerates on new campuses over summer/fall.
Nashville occupancy remains strong at 92% (above 100% utilized space), demonstrating demand for the home basing model.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenues increased significantly by 133% YoY and 20% sequentially primarily due to the incorporation of operations from the Camarillo campus acquisition in December 2024. Operating expenses rose moderately, driven largely by a reporting change that now includes fuel gross at Camarillo rather than net, alongside startup costs for new headcount at Phoenix, Dallas, Denver, and APA locations. Management reaffirmed guidance to reach consolidated cash flow breakeven by the end of FY25 as leasing ramps up on three new campuses.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell sharply to $7.5M from $17.1M YoY, partly due to a one-time 2024 Roche license
Net loss widened to $20.7M from $11.5M in Q1 2024
A $2.5M pharma biocatalysis order slipped into April, missing the top of Q1 guidance
positive_highlights: Product gross margin expanded to 55% from 49% YoY
First ligase order delivered to a large pharma customer in Q1, with additional orders expected
Three CDMOs validated ligase performance in-house, supporting scalability
summary: Codexis reported Q1 FY2025 total revenue of $7.5 million, down from $17.1 million in Q1 2024, with product gross margin up to 55% from 49%. Net loss widened to $20.7 million from $11.5 million, and cash stood at $59.8 million. The company reiterated its 2025 revenue guidance of $64–68 million, noting revenue timing was affected by a $2.5 million payment shifting to April. Management highlighted early commercial progress in its ECO platform, including first orders for its ligase products and upcoming presentations at TIDES USA.

negative_highlights: Cash only $8 million, sufficient into Q3; need $15 million more
EMA approval contingent on additional GLP studies that may impact EU timeline
Phase 2 MB-106 first patient relapsed after over 600 days of complete remission
positive_highlights: First patient treated in Phase 3 MIRACLE trial with 38 sites selected
EMA approved trial in all nine EU countries
FDA feedback reduced Part B enrollment to 222 patients
summary: Moleculin Biotech reported Q1 2025 progress with its Phase 3 MIRACLE trial for Annamycin (naxtarubicin) in relapsed/refractory AML, including first patient treated, 38 sites selected, EMA approval for nine EU countries, and WHO recognition of the generic name. The company has roughly $8 million cash, enough into Q3, and needs about $15 million to reach Q1 2026 funding. FDA feedback reduced Part B enrollment to 222 patients. Final data from the MB-107 soft tissue sarcoma trial is expected soon. The company remains confident in achieving the 45-patient interim readout by end of 2025.

negative_highlights: Gross margins were softer than a year ago due to revenue mix changes, specifically the inclusion of $1 million in NYC COVID-related spoilage revenue which had no margin.
Card issuing revenues were slightly down compared to the prior year quarter primarily because the New York City COVID program provided over $1 million in revenue that is not recurring.
positive_highlights: Record numbers in first quarter revenues driven by significant increases in processing volume across all segments.
Adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially, rising from $500,000 in Q4 2024 to $700,000 in Q1 FY2025.
PayFac business continues strong growth trajectory with revenues up 25% and now accounting for approximately 59% of total card revenues.
summary: Usio reported record Q1 FY2025 revenues with a 5% increase year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA rising to $700,000 from the prior quarter's $500,000. Processing volume surged significantly across segments: total processing up 34%, ACH volumes up 36%, card transactions up 65%, and PayFac revenues up 25%. Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance of 14% to 16% growth.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly stated it does not currently provide financial guidance for future quarters.
Cash balance declined to $40 million from $41.7 million at year-end despite recent capital raise.
No specific revenue figures were reported as the company is pre-revenue in its clinical stage.
positive_highlights: Net loss decreased to $8.5 million from $10.6 million in Q1 FY2024 due to lower operating expenses of $9.1 million versus $10.1 million previously.
Successfully initiated the VERSATILE 003 Phase 3 registrational trial with FDA approval and added Mayo Clinic sites, targeting approximately 350 patients.
summary: PDS Biotech reported a net loss of $8.5 million ($0.21 per share) for Q1 FY2025, representing an improvement from the prior year quarter due to lower operating expenses and increased tax benefits. The company raised approximately $11 million in new capital earlier this month but did not provide financial guidance or raise its operational outlook. Management highlighted the initiation of the VERSATILE 003 Phase 3 trial for Versamune HPV plus pembrolizumab, noting that enrollment is ongoing and specific timelines are pending.

negative_highlights: Total production declined 7.5% year-over-year to 6,667 BOE/day due to planned maintenance at Delhi and weather-related downtime in Barnett.
Oil revenue fell 19%, resulting in a net loss for the quarter compared to prior year income.
Development of third Chaveroo block delayed into FY2026 to optimize timing amid low oil prices.
positive_highlights: Tex-Mex acquisition completed at an attractive valuation of approximately 3.4x forward adjusted EBITDA, adding stable low-decline production.
Natural gas revenue rose 33% year-over-year to $7.8 million and NGL revenue up 14%, partially offsetting oil weakness.
New Chaveroo wells drilled under budget with initial rates approximately 50% above expectations.
summary: Evolution Petroleum reported Q3 FY2025 revenue of $22.6 million (down 2% YoY) and a net loss of $2.2 million ($0.07/share), driven by an 8% volume decline despite higher commodity prices, though adjusted metrics showed improvement over the prior quarter. Management maintained its dividend at $0.12 per share for the 47th consecutive quarter while deferring oil-weighted development in Chaveroo to focus on gas opportunities and preserve cash flow amidst volatility. The company closed a Tex-Mex acquisition adding ~850 net BOE/day (combined with new wells) funded by cash and a modest credit facility draw.

positive_highlights: Revenue growth accelerated to 22% YoY with organic expansion and no new sales hires.
summary: MDxHealth reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $24.3 million, representing a 22% year-over-year increase and organic growth without sales force expansion. Gross margins expanded to 63.8%, driven by the high-margin tissue-based segment which grew volume by 41%. Management confirmed full-year 2025 guidance of $108-$110 million, citing continued execution toward positive adjusted EBITDA in Q2.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined due to a shift in Roblox business resulting from changes in how the platform determines advertising revenue growth
Company remains EBITDA negative and requires further capital raises, with no specific date for breakeven other than targeting Q4 FY2025
positive_highlights: Gross margin increased from 38% (FY2024) to 44% in Q1 FY2025
Operating expense decreased approximately 25% compared to the prior year, with total cost reduction of ~30%
Net loss narrowed by 20% versus Q1 2024 despite revenue headwinds
summary: Super League reported Q1 FY2025 results where revenue met internal goals but declined due to a shift in the Roblox business following platform changes; however, net loss decreased by 20% compared to Q1 2024. Gross margin improved significantly from 38% in fiscal year 2024 to 44% in Q1 FY2025 driven by higher-margin programs and a ~25% reduction in operating expenses via cost-cutting measures including staff reductions.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 12% to $3.0 million due to VIP enrollment elimination
Gross margin contracted 700 bps to 50%
Cash used in operations increased to $3.8 million from $2.5 million, cash down to $2.3 million
positive_highlights: Total arches shipped grew 87% YoY from 1,996 to 3,736
Product revenue increased 8% to $1.8 million despite lower pediatric price points
Rebis alliance data shows 71% of patients chose Vivos over CPAP at $4,500 average revenue per case
summary: Vivos reported Q1 2025 total revenue of $3.0 million, down 12% YoY from $3.4 million, with a net loss of $3.9 million versus $3.8 million in the prior year. Product revenue grew 8% to $1.8 million on 87% higher arch volumes (3,736 arches), but service revenue fell due to the elimination of VIP enrollment. Gross margin declined to 50% from 57%, and cash dropped to $2.3 million from $6.3 million at year-end. Management is pivoting to a sleep-provider acquisition model, expecting to close the Sleep Center of Nevada acquisition within months, funded by a $7.5 million senior loan and equity infusion, and forecasts a Q3 accretive impact.

negative_highlights: Operating loss of RMB 155.5 million and net loss of RMB 207.3 million due to fair value decline of Bitcoin holdings.
April mining output fell 11.3% sequentially to 470 coins due to record global hash rate increase and 8% rise in mining difficulty.
Revenue concentration risk: Bitcoin mining accounts for 99% of total revenue, and power costs are relatively high under hosted model.
positive_highlights: Bitcoin mining revenue of RMB 1 billion contributed to total revenue of RMB 1.1 billion, a significant increase from RMB 64.4 million in Q1 2024.
Mined 1,541 Bitcoin in Q1 with an average effective hash rate of 30 EH/s and efficiency of 93.8%, ranking among top 3 publicly listed mining firms.
Cash and cash equivalents increased to RMB 2.5 billion from RMB 1.3 billion at year-end 2024, and credit risk exposure fell 30% to RMB 760 million.
summary: Cango's Q1 2025 revenue surged to RMB 1.1 billion (USD 145 million) from RMB 64.4 million a year earlier, driven by the new Bitcoin mining business which contributed RMB 1 billion. The company mined 1,541 Bitcoin at an average cost of USD 70,602 per coin, but recorded an operating loss of RMB 155.5 million and a net loss of RMB 207.3 million, largely due to a decline in Bitcoin prices in March. Management maintained its Mine and Hold strategy, targeting deployment of 18 EH/s of additional hash rate by end of July, bringing total capacity to 50 EH/s.

negative_highlights: Israeli revenue declined 56% YoY, partly due to supply delays and the Oranim deal cancellation.
Cash balance remains low at $1.4 million, with reliance on credit facilities and future financing.
Revenue growth was modest at 4% YoY, as German gains were mostly offset by Israeli declines.
positive_highlights: Achieved net profit of $0.2 million and positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.6 million, a ~$3M improvement YoY.
German revenue grew 569% YoY, now 62% of total revenue; 12 new strains launched in Q1 alone.
Gross profit up 94% YoY, aided by a 56% reduction in operating expenses.
summary: IM Cannabis reported Q1 2025 revenues of $12.5 million, up 4% YoY, with a net profit of $0.2 million versus a $6.0 million loss a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.6 million, improving from a $2.2 million loss in Q1 2024. German revenue surged 569% YoY to offset a 56% decline in Israel, while gross margin improved 87 percentage points. Operating expenses fell 56% YoY, driving the profitability turnaround.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year due to shipment deferrals in the Aero and Architecture divisions caused by customer hesitation regarding tariff impacts.
Adjusted EBITDA deteriorated quarter-over-quarter from negative $4.8 million to negative $5.5 million, widening the loss despite margin expansion.
Management explicitly stated that 2025 will not be a positive free cash flow year; FCF is expected to turn positive only in 2026.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 50 bps to 25.6% driven by operational efficiencies in Safety Tech (margin up from 12.8%) and Architecture segments.
Total purchase order backlog increased significantly to $36 million, indicating strong underlying demand despite timing delays.
Secured first tranche of a new debt facility with Mizrahi Bank at favorable terms ($370 bps interest rate reduction), enhancing liquidity.
summary: Gauzy reported Q1 FY2025 revenue of $22.4 million (down from $24.7M prior year) and adjusted EBITDA of negative $5.5 million (worse than the prior quarter's -$4.8M). Gross margin expanded 50 bps to 25.6%, driven by Safety Tech, while Aero revenue grew but margins contracted due to shipment timing shifts related to tariff uncertainty in March/April. Management reaffirmed full-year 2025 guidance of $130-$140 million revenue and positive adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: China tariffs expected to impact gross margin by approximately $1 million in the back two quarters
Physical Playboy Club development is projected as a one-to-two-year project, not immediate revenue
Licensing business excluding Byborg still grew but at a slower pace of over 50% YoY
positive_highlights: Licensing business revenue surged 175% year-over-year
Honey Birdette is ahead of plan for Q2 with an easy comparable base
Byborg deal includes a $20 million annual minimum guarantee plus additional payments
summary: PLBY Group reported Q1 FY2025 results where the licensing business grew significantly by 175% year-over-year to positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.4 million (excluding one-time personnel costs). Management highlighted strong performance in Honey Birdette with an easy comparable base and noted that Byborg contributed a significant portion of growth, though excluding it still showed over 50% YoY improvement. The company expects continued benefits from new deals in gaming and hospitality starting in the back half of the year.

negative_highlights: Company reported a net loss of $1.2 million, though improved from the prior period.
Cash used in operating activities was $1.2 million due to prepaid inventory purchases for tariff mitigation.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 111% year-over-year driven by RV market recovery and new HESS shipments.
summary: Revenue for Q1 FY2025 was $2.0 million, representing an increase of 111% year-over-year to the prior period's $1 million, driven by a rebound in RV sales and initial shipments from new Home Energy Storage Solutions (HESS). Gross profit margin expanded slightly to 24.5%, while SG&A expenses decreased significantly due to lower headcount and stock-based compensation. The company reported a net loss of $1.2 million but raised cash reserves to $1.1 million following a recent public offering.

negative_highlights: Weather reduced gross margins by 5-7% in Q1, with Australian gross margin falling to 16-17% vs normal ~25%.
Adjusted EPS of $0.52 was significantly hurt by $11 million higher depreciation, equivalent to $0.30 per share, partly due to idle equipment.
Backlog decreased by ~$300 million sequentially to $3.2 billion, though expected to recover to $4 billion by mid-year.
positive_highlights: Record trailing 12-month combined revenue of $1.5 billion, with Canadian Q1 revenue of $178 million up 45% from Q2 2024.
Canadian equipment utilization hit 68% in Q1 (best since winter 2022-23), approaching 75% year-end target.
Australian fleet capacity expanded 25% year-over-year, and bid pipeline grew to $15 billion, including $4 billion in new infrastructure opportunities.
summary: Q1 FY2025 revenue was $392 million, up 18% from Q2 2024, but adjusted EBITDA of $100 million (25.5% margin) was flat year-over-year, hit by severe weather in Australia and Canada. Adjusted EPS was $0.52, impacted by $11 million of higher depreciation ($0.30 per share). Management kept full-year 2025 guidance unchanged, expecting weather impacts to be made up in H2, with backlog expected to reach a record $4 billion by mid-year, up from $3.2 billion pro forma.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $22 million was driven by a single underperforming contract with prior year claim impacts.
Total revenue declined 4% YoY due to the intentional reduction in membership base from exiting unprofitable plans.
One specific payer partner remains an outlier requiring collaborative resolution for performance issues.
positive_highlights: Three of four markets achieved breakeven or better performance, with the outlier being a single payer partner.
PMPM funding increased by 8% to $1,063 due to improved disease burden capture and favorable contract terms.
Utilization metrics trended positively including a 21% decrease in ED visits per 1,000 and an 11% drop in high-cost claims >$20k.
