Quality customer growth (spending $400+ monthly) accelerated to 18% YoY, now representing over 20% of the client base.
SaaS adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 70 bps YoY to 16.8%, reflecting improved unit economics in the higher-value segment.
summary: Thryv reported Q4 FY2025 SaaS revenue of $119 million (up 14.1% QoQ) and full-year SaaS revenue of $461 million (up 34.2% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 16.8%. Management provided conservative guidance for 2026, expecting SaaS revenue between $461-$471 million, citing a transition period where growth rates will moderate due to the conclusion of legacy upgrade migrations and some product cannibalization. Marketing services revenue declined 34% YoY as the company continues its strategic shift away from legacy billings toward a pure-play software business.

negative_highlights: GNA increased 24% in Q4 due to software and professional fees
Transition to new fronting arrangement carries non-cash transitional costs
State Farm business has lower premiums per policy, a mix headwind
positive_highlights: Net income up 238% in Q4 and 91% for the full year
Written premium growth accelerated to 19% in Q4, with 2026 guidance raised to 15%-16%
New Markel fronting arrangement retains 100% of premium starting 2026
summary: Hagerty reported strong Q4 2025 results with total revenue up 19% to $357 million and net income up 238% to $29 million, while full-year revenue grew 17% and net income surged 91% to $149 million. The company achieved record new member count of 371,000, written premium growth of 14% accelerating through the year, and a 46% increase in adjusted EBITDA to $237 million. Management raised 2026 guidance with written premium growth expected to accelerate to 15%-16%, driven by a new fronting arrangement with Markel that allows retention of 100% of premium and expansion of State Farm Classic+ and Enthusiast Plus products.

negative_highlights: New prescriptions declined approximately 11.4% quarter-over-quarter and total prescriptions were up only marginally (1.4%) despite a QoQ demand increase.
Inventory increased by $5.7 million in the channel, masking underlying sales trends as noted by management's explanation of end-of-year note patterns.
R&D expenses are projected to rise 30-35% year-over-year due to clinical trial progress.
positive_highlights: Royalty revenue jumped to $15.6 million from Q3's $2.6 million, driven by a major shipment to partners in China.
ALISCA-Breast1 trial reached full enrollment of 150 patients ahead of the original December 2026 timeline with interim data expected in Q2 2026.
Company achieved positive net income for the third consecutive year, maintaining fiscal discipline.
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q4 FY2025 net product revenue of $59.9 million and GAAP EPS of $0.27 per share (diluted), driven by a significant inventory build rather than pure demand growth, while royalty revenue surged to $15.6 million due to China shipments. Management provided full-year 2026 guidance for net NERLYNX product revenue between $194M-$198M and expects positive net income despite anticipating higher R&D expenses of 30-35% in the coming year.

negative_highlights: Local Media division revenue dropped 30% year-over-year due to the absence of political advertising compared to Q4 FY2024.
Scripps Networks segment profit declined significantly from $199 million in Q4 last year's political cycle to $64 million this quarter.
Q1 guidance for Scripps Networks revenue is a high single-digit decline, impacted by Core TV reverse comp and weaker upfronts.
positive_highlights: Scripps Networks segment profit was $64 million with a 32% margin, exceeding full-year 2025 guidance of nearly 700 bps expansion.
Local Media Core advertising grew 12% in Q4 and is guided to mid-single-digit growth for Q1 driven by sports partnerships (NHL) and Winter Olympics/Super Bowl events.
Scripps Networks revenue was $199 million, down less than 8%, but well ahead of guidance.
summary: The E.W. Scripps Company reported Q4 FY2025 results where Local Media revenue fell 30% due to the absence of political advertising compared to last year's cycle, while Core advertising grew 12%. The Scripps Networks division delivered nearly 700 bps of margin expansion and exceeded full-year guidance. Management provided first-quarter guidance for Low-to-Mid Single Digit growth in Local Media revenue (excluding politics) and High Single-Digit decline in Network revenue.

negative_highlights: OEM channel revenue declined 12% in Q4 and 17% for the full year, due to lower U.S. pricing for Monovisc and Orthovisc.
2026 total revenue growth guidance of 1-9% is modest, with OEM expected to remain flat to down 5%.
FDA deficiency letter received for Hyalofast in Q1 2026; approval uncertain, and Cingal NDA filing timeline remains open-ended.
positive_highlights: Commercial channel revenue grew 22% in Q4 and 15% for full year, driven by international OA pain (up 28% Q4) and Integrity (doubled to ~$6M in 2025).
Q4 GAAP gross margin expanded to 63% from 56% YoY, reflecting operational improvements and higher volumes.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA of $5.3M outperformed revised guidance of -3% to +3% of revenue; operating cash flow improved to $11.2M.
summary: Anika's Q4 2025 total revenue was $30.6M, flat YoY, with commercial channel revenue up 22% to $13.3M, offset by OEM channel down 12% to $17.3M. Full-year revenue was $112.8M, down 6% YoY, while adjusted EBITDA of $5.3M exceeded prior guidance. For 2026, the company guides total revenue of $114-122.5M (1-9% growth) and adjusted EBITDA of 5-10% of revenue, but faces continued OEM pricing headwinds and FDA regulatory uncertainty for Hyalofast.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted OIBDA fell $6.6 million year-over-year, primarily driven by trade-related advertiser pullbacks in the first half.
Q1 FY2026 guidance explicitly excludes a holiday week included last year and anticipates reduced beverage revenue due to contractual adjustments.
Total attendance normalized for Q4 was down 9% YoY (excluding the extra fiscal week), reflecting softer box office performance.
positive_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA of $37 million exceeded guidance range despite lower-than-expected box office attendance.
Programmatic revenue surged 100% YoY, driven by a 2.4x increase in the number of programmatic advertisers.
National impressions sold per attendee increased 27% YoY due to strong demand for premium Platinum and post-show inventory.
summary: NCMI reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $93 million (up 8% YoY) and Adjusted OIBDA of $37 million (exceeding guidance), though full-year adjusted OIBDA declined to $39.1 million due to H1 headwinds. Management provided a cautious Q1 FY2026 revenue outlook between $32.5M-$36.5M, explicitly excluding the holiday week included in last year's quarter and noting potential beverage revenue reductions.

negative_highlights: Q4 EBITDA margin declined due to temporary gross margin impacts
Full-year revenue growth was only 1.2% amid soft consumption
Jafra sales force declined due to aggressive productivity-focused promotions
positive_highlights: Free cash flow more than doubled in Q4 versus prior year
Jafra U.S. delivered first back-to-growth quarter in Q4
Full-year cash conversion at 83% of EBITDA and debt reduced by MXN 700 million
summary: In Q4 FY2025, revenue grew 1.2% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 19%, below last year due to temporary gross margin impacts. Free cash flow more than doubled, with full-year EBITDA conversion at 83% and debt reduced by MXN 700 million, lowering leverage to 1.56x. Management guided to 2026 revenue growth of 4% to 8% and EBITDA margin of 19% or above, citing improved consumption trends and strategic initiatives. They also announced the pending acquisition of Tupperware's Latin American business for $250 million, expected to close in Q2 2026.

negative_highlights: Average revenue per customer decreased 14% in FY2025 due to the addition of new, lower-volume clinical customers.
Management explicitly stated that recent biotech funding upticks are not yet built into the $42-44 million guidance for 2026.
Adjusted EBITDA remains negative at -$1.8 million in Q4 and -$6.7 million full year, with a target of becoming positive by end of 2027.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew sequentially and YoY in Q4, marking the sixth straight quarter of top-line expansion.
Free cash outflow improved significantly from $13.5 million in FY2024 to $9.8 million in FY2025, beating guidance.
Gross margin expanded 950 bps YoY to 32.5% driven by higher Clinical Solutions revenue and manufacturing efficiency.
summary: Teknova reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $10.0 million (up 8% YoY) and full-year revenue of $40.5 million (up 7%), beating the prior free cash outflow guidance of less than $12 million with an actual outflow of only $9.8 million. Gross margin expanded to 32.5% in Q4 driven by higher Clinical Solutions mix, while operating expenses decreased due to reduced headcount and spending despite a slight increase in sales investments for the future. Management provided FY2026 revenue guidance of $42-44 million (approximate 6% growth) but explicitly stated that current biotech funding upticks are not yet built into this plan, with expectations for double-digit growth to materialize by late 2027.

negative_highlights: Q4 time charter revenues decreased to $52.1 million from $57.1 million due to the sale of two vessels reducing ownership days.
Time charter equivalent rate averaged USD 15,397 per day in Q4, a decrease compared to last year's average of USD 15,589.
Vessel operating expenses increased by 6% on a total basis and daily OPEX rose 11%, driven by higher crew costs.
positive_highlights: Fleet utilization reached an impressive 99.7% for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Q4 Capesize earnings averaged USD 28,892 per day with a brief peak of USD 45,000 in December.
The company declared a quarterly cash dividend and repurchased $23 million worth of common shares.
summary: Diana Shipping reported Q4 FY2025 time charter revenues of $52.1 million and adjusted EBITDA of $19.3 million, both lower than the prior year quarter due to a smaller fleet size (average 36 vessels vs 38) and timing of renewals under its medium-term strategy. The company declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.01 per share totaling approximately USD 1.16 million while maintaining strong liquidity with $122.3 million in cash reserves as of quarter-end.

negative_highlights: Reported revenue was $1 million lower than the pre-release approximation due to complex closing processes following acquisition integration.
Operating loss increased by 43% year-over-year (from $4.6M) primarily driven by headcount increases and ExoDx-related expenses.
Tissue-based ASPs declined quarter-over-quarter, attributed to a mix shift between GPS ($3,850) and Confirm ($2,000).
positive_highlights: Liquid-based test volumes surged 128% year-over-year driven by the newly acquired ExoDx business and SelectMDx conversions.
Gross margins expanded slightly to 63.2%, reflecting economies of scale despite mix shifts.
Management successfully transitioned all SelectMDx customers to ExoDx ahead of schedule, accelerating operating efficiencies.
summary: MDxHealth reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $107.9 million (down from a prior pre-release estimate) and full-year growth driven by liquid-based tests (+128% unit volume), though tissue volumes declined (-5%). The company amended its Exact Sciences earnout to lower upcoming payments, providing flexibility despite an operating loss widening to $5.3 million due to ExoDx integration costs.

negative_highlights: Wavelo adjusted EBITDA margin expected down year-over-year in 2026
Conservatively forecasting possible reduction in Wavelo fees from Ting process
Capital allocation conservative, no commitment to buybacks
positive_highlights: Ting process ongoing and not delayed despite external volatility
Liquidity remains sound with $20.9 million unrestricted cash excluding Ting
Syndicated debt paydown ongoing, increasing borrowing capacity
summary: Tucows reported Q4 2025 results and addressed investor questions. Management provided no update on the Ting asset sale timeline, stating it is ongoing and not delayed despite market volatility. They conservatively guided 2026 Wavelo adjusted EBITDA margin down year-over-year, citing potential loss of Ting customers and fully annualized investments. The company noted liquidity of $20.9 million excluding Ting and emphasized deleveraging and conservative capital allocation, with a stock buyback program providing flexibility but no commitment to repurchase.

negative_highlights: Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue outlook to a decline of 25% to 38% year-over-year due to clinician confusion and market freeze following CMS comments on December 30.
First quarter 2026 is expected to see approximately 50% year-over-year revenue declines driven by the aforementioned utilization issues.
Surgical & Sports Medicine segment sales declined 2% year-over-year, though this was within guidance assumptions.
positive_highlights: Advanced Wound Care revenue surged 83% year-over-year to $217.2 million, driven by strong execution and favorable product mix rather than inventory pull-forward.
Total Q4 net income jumped from $5.1 million in the prior year period to $31.5 million for common shareholders (GAAP) or $52.9 million adjusted.
The company delivered record sales results that exceeded the high end of its previously issued guidance range.
summary: Organogenesis reported Q4 FY2025 net product revenue of $225.1 million (up 78% YoY), significantly beating the high end of guidance and exceeding expectations by approximately $50 million due to an 83% surge in Advanced Wound Care sales, while Surgical & Sports Medicine declined 2%. Despite strong Q4 execution, management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a decline range of 25%-38% YoY citing clinician confusion from recent CMS comments and the $127 price reduction. Management expects first-half declines followed by substantial market share gains in the second half as competitive dynamics improve.

negative_highlights: Q4 comparable sales declined 3.3% excluding deferred loyalty revenue due to a 3.6% drop in traffic.
Restaurant-level operating margin contracted by 10 basis points to 11.4% compared to the prior year quarter.
Beef inflation is expected to remain high in 2026, with commodity costs projected to be up roughly 4%.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $11.8 million in Q4 was ahead of expectations discussed on the last earnings call.
Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA grew 53% year-over-year to $69.7 million, driven by labor efficiency and cost savings.
December traffic outpaced the Black Box casual dining index for the first time since Q3 2024.
summary: Red Robin reported Q4 FY2025 revenues of $269 million, a decrease of $16.2 million year-over-year driven by a 3.6% decline in traffic and restaurant closures. While adjusted EBITDA of $11.8 million beat expectations, the company provided full-year 2026 guidance for comparable sales growth of 0.5% to 1.5%, reflecting a cautious outlook due to weather impacts and commodity inflation.

negative_highlights: NAV per share declined to $19.10 from $19.28
Weighted average yield on income-producing securities fell 40 bps to 10%
Nonaccruals increased with two new additions in Q4
positive_highlights: NII covered the base dividend by 107% in Q4
Spillover income of $1.16 per share, nearly 3x the dividend
Pro forma nonaccruals improved after January restructurings
summary: CCAP's Q4 2025 NII was $0.45 per share, down from $0.46 sequentially, and over-earned the $0.42 dividend by 107%. NAV per share fell to $19.10 from $19.28, driven by unrealized losses and higher nonaccruals (two new nonaccruals, with pro forma nonaccruals improving after January restructurings and a sale). Gross deployment was $71 million, but net realizations were about $7 million negative due to $78 million in exits. Management flagged earnings headwinds from lower base rates and is reviewing dividend policy and capital options, with an update expected in May. The supplemental dividend is not paid for Q4 due to the NAV-based measurement test, but the policy remains in place.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue includes $1.0 million in collections from claims older than one year, excluding which core organic growth was lower
First quarter is expected to show a step-down in volume and ASP consistent with historic seasonality
Recent weather events caused disruptions that were considered in the guidance range
positive_highlights: Achieved adjusted EBITDA positivity of $530k in Q4 FY2025
Gross margins expanded to 83% driven by volume growth and improved reimbursement collections
Primary care channel volumes grew 67% YoY, accounting for 12% of total Nodify tests
summary: Biodesix reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $28.8 million (up 41% YoY) and achieved adjusted EBITDA positivity of $530k for the first time in company history, driven by a core organic lung diagnostic growth of 40%. Gross margins expanded to 83%, while management provided FY2026 revenue guidance of $106M-$112M (midpoint representing ~23% annual growth). The quarter was impacted by Q1 seasonality and weather events, which were explicitly factored into the forward outlook.

negative_highlights: Management initiated a lower free cash flow guidance for FY2026 ($6M-$9M) citing conservative outlooks and planned increases in sales/marketing/AI investment.
Q1 paid members decreased to 626,000 from the Q4 level of 650,000 due to expected seasonality.
positive_highlights: New Expensify achieved full feature parity with Classic for customers representing 90% of revenue.
Expensify travel bookings in Q4 were up 434% compared to the prior year period.
Interchange fees increased 24% year-over-year, totaling $5.5 million in Q4.
summary: Expensify reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $35.2 million and full-year revenue of $142.1 million with an average paid member count of 650,000 for both periods. The company generated $19.9 million in free cash flow for the year but initiated a lower fiscal year '2026 guidance range of $6 million to $9 million due to conservative investment plans and increased spending on sales, marketing, and AI.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined 3% quarter-over-quarter due to seasonal hiring slowdowns.
Job openings dropped 10% year-over-year, with job seeker traffic from LLMs still a small portion of the overall mix.
SMB demand remained soft in Q4 despite enterprise strength.
positive_highlights: Achieved first year-over-year revenue growth since Q3 2022 with $111.7M reported.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded sequentially and YoY, reaching 15% from a lower base of paid employers (up 2%).
Enterprise performance marketing revenue grew 9% year-over-year in Q4.
summary: ZipRecruiter reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $111.7 million (up 1% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 15%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, projecting flat revenue growth against a lower base due to soft holiday seasonality in SMB demand.

negative_highlights: Total investment income declined to $50 million from $51.1 million due to lower base rates
NAV per share decreased to $17.72 from $17.85
Q1 2026 dividend reduced to $0.40 per share from $0.45
positive_highlights: NII per share increased sequentially to $0.44 from $0.43
Non-accruals remain low at 0.5% of fair value
Refinanced secured credit facility, reducing borrowing costs by 17 bps
summary: NCDL reported Q4 FY2025 NII of $0.44 per share, slightly above Q3's $0.43, with total investment income declining slightly to $50 million from $51.1 million due to lower base rates. Non-accruals remained low at 0.5% of fair value, and NAV per share dipped to $17.72 from $17.85. Management declared a Q1 2026 dividend of $0.40 per share (regular $0.36 plus $0.04 supplemental), down from the prior quarter's $0.45, and authorized a $50 million share repurchase program. They enter 2026 with a strong pipeline and stabilized spreads, but acknowledge earnings pressure from rate cuts and competitive spreads.

negative_highlights: Guidance explicitly excludes speculative acquisition or disposition activity due to current cost of capital constraints.
Ongoing negative NOI impact from the East Orange asset affected by Steward bankruptcy proceedings.
Management noted potential earnings dilution during the transition period as they delever and note legacy assets.
positive_highlights: Same-store cash NOI increased 5.4% on a year-over-year basis with sequential performance at 2.9%.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA REIT decreased to 6.2x, driven by preferred equity issuance and asset sales.
Company successfully sold an early vintage medical office for $10 million proceeds used for stock repurchase.
summary: Chiron Real Estate reported Q4 FY2025 with Core FFO of $1.16 per share and unit (transitioning from AFFO) and NAREIT-defined FFO of $0.97. Management provided initial 2026 core FFO guidance ranging between $4.30 to $4.45, explicitly excluding speculative acquisition or disposition activity but including anticipated headwinds related to balance sheet fortification efforts in the back half of last year.

negative_highlights: Consolidated GAAP net loss of $177 million for 2025, with book value per share declining to negative $44.27
No substantive progress on PREPA due to unresolved Oversight Board legal issues
MBIA Insurance Corp. statutory capital declined to $79 million from $88 million
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted net income of $23 million vs. adjusted net loss of $184 million in 2024
PREPA-related loss and LAE benefit in 2025 from sale of custodial receipts at favorable prices
National's statutory capital increased to $937 million, up $25 million from year-end 2024
summary: MBIA reported a consolidated GAAP net loss of $177 million for full year 2025, improved from a $447 million loss in 2024, driven by lower PREPA losses and VIE-related expenses. Adjusted net income was $23 million for 2025 versus a $184 million loss in 2024. Book value per share fell to negative $44.27. National's statutory capital rose to $937 million, but PREPA resolution remains stalled due to Oversight Board legal issues, though management expressed optimism for progress this year.

negative_highlights: Company remains in a cash-burn phase with no revenue reported.
Phase 2 ASPEN-9 primary endpoint changed to response rate by high CD47 expression, requiring larger sample size and pushing top-line data readout to mid-2027.
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss decreased YoY from $29.2M to $22.8M due to lower stock compensation and personnel costs.
Completed financing raised net proceeds of ~$140.4M, extending cash runway through 2028.
Phase 2 ASPEN-9 breast cancer trial upsized from 80 to 120 patients to ensure robust biomarker data for CD47 overexpressors.
summary: ALX Oncology Holdings Inc. reported a GAAP net loss of $22.8M for Q4 FY2025 (or $0.42/share), representing an improvement from the prior quarter's $29.2M loss ($0.55/share) driven by lower stock compensation and personnel costs following pipeline prioritization. The company successfully closed a financing round raising net proceeds of approximately $140.4M, strengthening its balance sheet to fund operations through 2028. Management confirmed that clinical timelines for both lead programs remain on track with the goal of advancing them to pivotal studies by year-end next.

negative_highlights: Multiplatform Group GAAP adjusted EBITDA fell 14.2% YoY due to the absence of ~$80M political revenue compared to prior year.
Digital Audio Group Q4 margins contracted slightly from 35.1% in the prior year quarter to 34.1%, driven by variable content costs.
Q1 EBITDA expected to decline despite cost savings, attributed to prepaid marketing expenses deployed early and small base effects.
positive_highlights: Digital Audio Group revenue surged 14.1% YoY driven by podcasting (up 24.5%) exceeding mid-teens guidance.
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA hit $220 million, landing at the midpoint of the provided range despite a non-political year.
Full-year and Q1 revenue guidance raised to high single digits following an in-line quarter.
summary: iHeartMedia reported Q4 FY2025 consolidated revenue of $1.1 billion (up 0.8% YoY), beating guidance for low single-digit decline and hitting adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint of its range ($220M vs $200-240M). The Digital Audio Group significantly outperformed with revenue up 14.1%, while the Multiplatform Group missed on a GAAP basis due to political advertising comparisons, though excluding politics it grew 2.3%. Management raised full-year EBITDA guidance to approximately $800 million and provided specific Q1 expectations of high single-digit revenue growth.

negative_highlights: Reported Q4 gross margin contracted slightly to 67.7% from 68.2%.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $9.9M in Q4 compared to $9.1M prior year, impacted by $1.8M Guardant litigation costs and FX headwinds.
Cash burn increased to $12.3M in Q4 due to foreign exchange impacts from the strengthening Swiss franc.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 22% YoY to $21.7M, with clinical revenue excluding biopharma up 31%.
Signed a record 124 new customers in 2025, including two of the largest US health systems serving ~60,000 patients annually.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 bps to 74.2% due to compute optimizations and scrap cost reductions.
summary: SOPHiA GENETICS reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $21.7 million, representing a 22% year-over-year increase driven by strong clinical growth and new customer signings. Full year 2025 revenue reached $77.3 million (up 19%), with adjusted gross margin expanding to 74.2%. Management provided full year 2026 guidance for reported revenue between $92 million and $94 million, implying approximately 20-22% growth.

negative_highlights: MX908 product and service revenue was relatively flat in Q4.
International revenue mix was 27% in 2025, a modest increase from 25% in 2024.
Management noted possible timing delays from Middle East conflict but no material impact expected.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 21% YoY to $17.4M with positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.7M.
Explorer device grew over 40% YoY, with 150+ units shipped in its first full year.
Viper shipped >40 units in Q4, generating over $3M in revenue (initial demand).
summary: 908 Devices (MASS) reported Q4 2025 revenue of $17.4M, up 21% YoY, with positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.7M versus a loss of $4.0M a year ago. Full-year revenue from continuing operations reached $56.2M, up 18% YoY, and recurring revenue grew 22%, representing 35% of total revenue. The company cited strong Explorer demand (up 40% YoY), early Viper traction (>40 units, $3M revenue in Q4), and 600 bps gross margin improvement. Guidance for 2026 was not explicitly stated in the transcript, but management expressed confidence in sustaining growth and improving profitability with targeted investments.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue down 3% YoY to $203.6 million
Accessories and materials sales down 13% in Q4 and 9% for the year
Management disappointed in lack of total company sales growth for Q4 and 2025
positive_highlights: Paid subscribers up over 4% YoY to 3.09 million in Q4
Full-year net income increased 22% to $76.7 million
International sales up 9% in Q4 and 8% for the year
summary: In Q4 2025, Cricut reported revenue of $203.6 million, down 3% YoY, and full-year revenue of $708.8 million, down less than 1%. Net income for the quarter was $7.8 million and $76.7 million for the year, up 22% from 2024. Paid subscribers grew over 4% YoY to 3.09 million, but accessories and materials sales fell 13% in Q4. Management expressed disappointment in flat revenue and guided for flat to slightly down revenue in 2026, while launching two new next-generation machines bundled with materials and a new DTF service.

negative_highlights: SMB business declined 3% in the quarter and grew only modestly at +1% for the full year due to a mix shift toward lower-margin ISO channels
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted by 130 basis points, with gross margins pressured by interest revenue declines of $13 million annually
Net leverage ratio increased to 5.5x from 4.7x primarily due to FX fluctuations and the business disposal
positive_highlights: Digital Wallet segment revenue grew organically by 13% to $220.2 million, driven by a >200% increase in Latin America
E-commerce processing volumes reached record levels during the U.S. football season with +24% Q4 growth
New product vitality index hit $270 million (16% of total revenue), up from 2% three years ago
summary: Paysafe reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $438.4 million (organic growth +6%) and full-year organic revenue growth of 5%, though adjusted EBITDA declined 1% to $102.1 million in the quarter due to higher marketing investment, OpEx timing items, and a business disposal headwind. Management reiterated FY2026 guidance for revenue between $1.79 billion and $1.83 billion (5-8% growth) with adjusted EBITDA of $449-$464 million, maintaining the full-year margin outlook despite Q4 mix-driven compression. The company highlighted strong e-commerce volumes (+24%) and digital wallet growth in Latin America while noting softer SMB performance.

negative_highlights: Organic revenue declined 22% year-over-year as the terminated diagnostics agreement was dilutive.
Academic revenue is expected to decline approximately 24% on a pro forma basis for full year 2026 due to lower large accelerator projects versus prior years.
Pharma revenue declined 21% year-over-year primarily driven by fewer large accelerator projects compared to the prior period.
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased 25% year-over-year due to pent-up demand from an academic customer base and a terminated diagnostics agreement yielding $5.6M for the full year of 2025.
CMS approved reimbursement rate of $897 for LucentAD complete test in Q4, providing a nationally recognized reference price.
Adjusted cash usage improved sequentially to $3 million from $16.1 million in Q3 due to synergies and working capital improvements.
summary: Q4 revenue was $43.9 million (up 25% YoY), but organic revenue declined 22%, driven by a terminated diagnostics agreement and declines in academic/pharma segments. Management provided full-year 2026 guidance of $169M-$174M, explicitly assuming no underlying improvement in the weak academic or pharmaceutical end markets. The company expects to achieve cash flow breakeven in H2 2026.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA decreased to $1.3M in Q4 due specifically to the delayed execution of two anticipated large contracts.
Full-year revenue guidance was cut by approximately $5 million, dropping from an implied range above $116M down to $109-111M.
Gross margin contracted slightly to 54% in FY2025 compared to 57% the prior year.
positive_highlights: Full-year FY2025 revenue hit a record of $104.1M, representing a 2% increase over the prior year despite headwinds.
ARR grew to $95.4M at quarter end with strong momentum in SafePointe ($800k bookings) and PlateRanger gaining traction.
NYPD contract renewal remains intact for FY2027, signaling continued support from a highly scrutinized jurisdiction.
summary: SoundThinking reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $24.8 million (up 6% YoY) and full-year revenue of $104.1 million (up 2%), but adjusted EBITDA fell to $1.3M in the quarter from $1.7M due to delayed contract executions. Management reduced its FY2026 guidance range for both revenue ($109-111M) and adjusted EBITDA margin (16%-18%) citing delays with a new state CrimeTracer deployment and a Puerto Rico ShotSpotter renewal totaling over $5 million in expected bookings.

negative_highlights: DIXI Medical revenue declined 4% YoY
2026 guidance excludes IGE and other potential contributions
No specific timeline provided for pediatric submission
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24% YoY to $26.6 million in Q4
RNS System revenue up 26% YoY; gross margin 77.4%
Second consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA and positive cash flow
summary: NeuroPace reported Q4 2025 revenue of $26.6 million, up 24% year-over-year, with RNS System revenue up 26% to $22.4 million. Gross margin improved to 77.4% (up 200 bps YoY), and the company delivered its second consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA and positive cash generation. Full year 2026 revenue guidance of $98-$100 million was reiterated, assuming 20%-22% core RNS growth and excluding any IGE contribution. The company submitted its PMA supplement for IGE in December, with FDA review on track, and expects Seizure ID approval in H1 2026.

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted operating loss of $16 million due to tariffs and low volumes
Full-year adjusted operating profit of only $16 million against $100 million tariff costs
Near-term margin pressure from mix shift to lighter-duty, low-priced models and aggressive competition
positive_highlights: Q4 bookings up 42% sequentially and 35% YoY, with early 2026 momentum continuing
Q4 operating cash flow of $57 million driven by improved inventory efficiency
Full-year restructuring savings of $40-45 million and $85-100 million annualized by 2028
summary: Q4 2025 revenue declined to $923 million and adjusted operating loss was $16 million including $40 million gross tariff costs. Full year revenue fell to $3.8 billion with adjusted operating profit of $16 million and ~$100 million tariff costs. Bookings surged 42% sequentially and 35% YoY, and early 2026 bookings remain strong. Management expects Q1 2026 to be the trough, with moderate full-year operating profit, small first-half loss, and stronger H2 volumes.

negative_highlights: Q4 U.S. revenue declined 11% year-over-year
Q4 worldwide revenue fell 5% year-over-year
Management expects U.S. sales to remain down in early 2026, with growth only in back half
positive_highlights: Q4 gross margin expanded to 77.6% from 74% year-over-year
Cost restructuring reduced ongoing operating expenses by over 10%
New $60 million credit facility extends debt maturity to 2031
summary: Q4 2025 worldwide revenue fell 5% YoY to $22.6 million, with U.S. revenue down 11% to $14.1 million, while international revenue rose 8%. Full-year revenue increased 8% to $90.5 million, but U.S. growth was only 1%. Management attributes the U.S. weakness to internal execution issues, sales force turnover, and suboptimal incentives, and has restructured costs, cut operating expenses by over 10%, and refinanced debt to extend maturity to 2031. Guidance for 2026 implies U.S. sales improving from mid-to-high single-digit declines in Q1 to high single-digit growth by Q4, with cash burn reduced to $23 million.

negative_highlights: Early Q1 2026 performance impacted by weather-related store closures and reduced promotional activity.
Inventory levels somewhat heavier due to slow weather-affected weeks.
Negative macro impact on consumer demand noted in the Q&A.
positive_highlights: Fourth quarter core net sales increased 13.5%, the strongest growth of 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 56 basis points to 21.4% in Q4.
Full year adjusted EBITDA margin above 20% for the first time since 2021.
summary: Holley delivered double-digit Q4 core growth of 13.5%, with reported net sales up 10.9% to $155.4M and gross margin expanding 120bps to 46.8%. Full-year sales grew 6.6% on a core basis, with adjusted EBITDA margin above 20% for the first time since 2021, and free cash flow of $34.2M. The company ended 2025 below 3.8x leverage and issued 2026 guidance of over 4% revenue growth and more than $15M in cost synergies, while noting early Q1 softness from weather-related store closures and reduced promotions.

negative_highlights: Q4 Interventional Dry Eye revenue ($0.7M) is significantly below the $5-7M full-year guide, indicating a steep ramp-up required for the new reimbursed model.
Interventional Glaucoma Q1 outlook set at low single-digit growth against an easy prior year comparison due to January/February storms and LCD restrictions on combo procedures.
Cash balance declined from $120.4M in 2024 to $92M, reflecting cash usage of $0.4M despite operational discipline.
positive_highlights: Interventional Dry Eye achieved first reimbursed milestone in Q4, generating $0.7M revenue from ~30 new accounts and strong traction in Novitas/First Coast regions.
Total operating expenses decreased 25% YoY to $21.5M following the August reduction-in-force, with adjusted OpEx down 23%.
Interventional Glaucoma grew sequentially flat but beat top-end of prior guidance range despite LCD headwinds and storm-related disruptions in Q1.
summary: Sight Sciences reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $20.4 million (up 7% YoY), driven by Interventional Glaucoma growth of 5% to $19.7M and the launch of reimbursed Interventional Dry Eye at $0.7M. The company initiated full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue between $82-88 million (representing a beat on prior expectations) with adjusted operating expenses guided up modestly by 6%-9% to fund commercial expansion.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $193 million due to $136 million impairment charges
Adjusted EBITDA down 23% to $284 million on lower Brent prices
Operating expenses up 23% to $249 million, though per BOE down 6%
positive_highlights: Successfully executed bond exchange with ~88% participation, enhancing liquidity
2025 production up 32% to 45,709 boe/d, driven by Ecuador and Canada
Rahoo-2 well producing ~790 bbl/d at <1% water cut, ahead of expectations
summary: Gran Tierra reported a net loss of $193 million in 2025, including $136 million in impairment charges, versus net income of $3.2 million in 2024; adjusted EBITDA fell 23% to $284 million and funds flow from operations declined to $178 million. Production rose 32% to 45,709 boe/d. Management highlighted a successful bond exchange with 88% participation, enhanced liquidity, entry into Azerbaijan, and improved 2026 hedging with an average floor around $60. Despite lower profits, the company is positioned for debt reduction and growth, with shares trading at a meaningful discount to NAV.

negative_highlights: Increased competition in the NAD space, particularly from NMN products.
NOPARK Parkinson's study did not achieve primary endpoint.
Guidance for 2026 is conservative, with back-half-loaded revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue up 30% YoY, exceeding initial 18% growth guidance.
Q4 revenue up 16% YoY; net income positive for the quarter and full year.
Company ended year with $64.8 million cash and no debt.
summary: Q4 revenue was $33.8 million, up 16% YoY, with net income of $4.1 million; full-year revenue reached $129.4 million, up 30% YoY with net income of $17.4 million. Management highlighted strong full-year growth exceeding initial guidance and the launch of Niagen Plus at-home injection kits in H1 2026. They noted increased competition but also cited recent positive scientific studies and ongoing litigation against the FDA regarding NMN. They provided conservative guidance for 2026, with back-half loaded growth expected, while noting potential upside from new products and marketing campaigns.

negative_highlights: C-BEYOND enrollment number inconsistent (press release says 880+; call says 180+).
Phase III data not yet reported; key readouts remain later in 2026.
Commercial launch assumes stable pricing and payer access; no contracts secured yet.
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment for C-BEYOND with over 880 patients; top-line results expected midyear.
Cash position of $301.8 million with runway through 2027 supports both programs.
Market research: physicians would prescribe BEM-RZR to ~50% of patients regardless of cirrhosis status.
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported Q4 2025 cash and investments of $301.8 million, extending runway through 2027. Enrollment completed for the C-BEYOND Phase III HCV trial (over 880 patients) with top-line results expected midyear, and C-FORWARD enrollment expected midyear with results by year-end. The company initiated IND-enabling studies for AT-587, a first-in-class HEV candidate, and aims for a first-in-human study midyear. Commercial preparation included market research showing physician willingness to prescribe the HCV regimen to ~50% of patients and payer formulary interest.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 10.3% in Q4 and 8.5% for the year on a constant currency basis
Europe/APAC revenue fell 1.4% in Q4 and 2.7% for the year, with continued competitive and rebate pressures
Guidance lowered due to uncertainty from recent Middle East events, particularly potential European demand impact
positive_highlights: North America volume growth of 5.5% in Q4 and 14.3% for the year
Automation revenue grew nearly 40% on a constant currency basis in Q4 and ~35% for the year, exceeding $40 million
Strong liquidity: cash of $63 million and no revolver draws
summary: Ranpak's Q4 2025 revenue grew 2.2% on a constant currency basis, or 4.4% excluding warrants, driven by strong North America e-commerce and automation growth. Adjusted EBITDA declined 10.3% on a constant currency basis, or 1.2% excluding warrants, and full-year EBITDA fell 8.5% (down 2.4% excluding warrants). The company hit the low end of its revised EBITDA guidance but missed the top line slightly due to Europe challenges and automation project delays. Management issued a cautious 2026 outlook, citing Middle East events and potential European demand softness, while expecting automation to turn Adjusted EBITDA positive.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin contracted slightly to 84% from 85% due to final migration work and increased AI compute costs
FY2026 revenue guidance implies lower nonrecurring revenue as the company focuses on recurring ARR growth
positive_highlights: Achieved record full-year revenue of $40.3 million with a 15% increase over the prior year
Adjusted EBITDA grew by approximately 35% to a record $9.1 million, implying an accelerating rate of cash flow growth into 2027
Enterprise channel grew 21% for the full year driven by expansion in the EU
summary: AudioEye reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $10.5 million (up 8% YoY) and full-year revenue growth of 15%, driven by strong enterprise channel expansion in the EU. Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $9.1 million for the year with margins expanding to 27%. Management provided conservative guidance for FY2026, projecting revenue between $43M-$44.5M and adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 30%.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue declined 8% due to contract timing and deferred amortization.
Residential generator market slowed due to high interest rates and fewer outages.
AIO partnership not expected to contribute revenue until second half of 2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue rose 4.5% to $11.478 million, a record year.
Monitoring revenue grew 22% with 95% gross margin.
Cash flow from operations more than doubled to $2.09 million, up 131%.
summary: Acorn Energy reported record 2025 revenue of $11.478 million, up 4.5% YoY, with monitoring revenue growing 22% and gross margin improving to 76.8% from 72.8%. Operating cash flow more than doubled to $2.09 million, and the company remains debt-free with $4.45 million in cash. Management reaffirmed a 20% average annual revenue growth target over 3-5 years, though hardware revenue declined due to a large customer contract timing and a decrease in deferred revenue amortization. The new AIO partnership is expected to contribute revenue in the second half of 2026, but no numbers were given.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS declined to -$0.32 in Q4 compared to $0.14, driven by higher other expenses including a minority equity investment mark-to-market charge.
Domestic segment revenue contracted slightly (-2%) for the full year as management pivots away from legacy subsidized consumer offerings in Southwest markets.
FY2026 outlook incorporates headwinds of approximately $5M related to high-cost funding support ending in U.S. Virgin Islands and potential additional reductions upon tower sale closing.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 2% YoY to $184.2M driven by International segment growth (+3%) and Domestic carrier services expansion.
Adjusted EBITDA expanded 8% sequentially or 8% YoY to $50.0M, reflecting successful cost management efforts in the U.S. market.
Full-year net loss narrowed significantly from a prior year loss of $26.4M to $14.9M due to improved operating performance and absence of specific tax benefits seen previously.
summary: ATN International reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $184.2 million (up 2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $50.0 million (up 8%), while full-year revenues remained essentially flat at $728 million against a prior loss narrowing to a net loss of $14.9 million for the year. Management provided a modestly raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range of $190-200 million (excluding tower sale impacts) and confirmed maintenance of the quarterly dividend at $0.275 per share with no buybacks in Q4.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue declined year-over-year by $2.4 million ($8.4M vs $10.8M) due to lower license and milestone payments.
Full-year FY2025 revenue of $18.7M is significantly below the prior year's $26.4M, indicating a material contraction in core business performance.
Company recorded a noncash impairment charge of $3.9 million related to legacy small molecule ion channel assets.
positive_highlights: OmniUltra launch received strong initial reception with early programs already progressing; interest is high among existing partners for new discovery work.
xPloration platform generated approximately $800,000 in Q4 revenue from instrument sales and services, adding a scalable service stream to the business model.
Pipeline advancement remains robust with 25 total program progression events in FY2025, including one OmnidAb-derived program entering human clinical trials.
summary: OmniAb reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $8.4 million (down from $10.8M in the prior year) and a net loss of $14.2 million ($0.11/share), driven by declines in license and milestone revenue partially offset by new xPloration service revenue. For full-year 2025, total revenue was $18.7 million versus guidance expectations (implied miss relative to prior year levels) with operating expenses decreasing to $87.6M due to workforce reductions but including a noncash impairment charge of $3.9M. Management provided FY2026 revenue guidance in the range of $25-30 million, which represents a significant contraction from 2024 full-year levels and reflects current partner pipeline visibility.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly lowered FY2026 revenue guidance to $109-114M, citing a one-time ~$9M managed service contribution in H1 2025 that is not expected to repeat.
Year-to-date contracted revenue numbers are running roughly 15% to 20% below last year's levels due to shorter contract durations and client conservatism regarding MFN pricing negotiations.

Q4 net income of $5M was partially driven by a one-time favorable mix; management does not anticipate gross margins remaining at the record Q4 level in FY26, expecting them to settle in the mid-60% range.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $32.2M beat consensus estimates; full year FY25 adjusted EBITDA margins exceeded 20% with nearly $19M in free cash flow generated.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 74.8% in Q4, driven by a favorable solution and channel partner mix including high-margin specialty messaging.
summary: OptimizeRx reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $32.2 million and adjusted EBITDA of $12 million, beating consensus estimates but noting softness in year-to-date contracted revenue due to a market shift away from managed services (which contributed ~$9M in H1 2025) and conservative client spending on MFN pricing adjustments. Management updated its FY2026 guidance downward for revenue ($109-114 million range, down from prior expectations of higher growth driven by the one-time managed service spike) while maintaining or slightly raising adjusted EBITDA guidance ($21-25 million). The company highlighted a gross margin expansion to 74.8% in Q4 (driven by favorable mix), net income turning positive at $0.26/share, and authorized a new $10 million share repurchase program.

negative_highlights: Prepaid revenue declined 27% year-over-year due to an exceptionally high prior period and accounting changes
Full-year net income decreased 23% primarily driven by $6M in acquisition integration costs and a higher tax rate of ~31%
Tariff expenses totaled approximately $4.0 million impacting profitability
positive_highlights: Fourth quarter revenue hit a record of $153M representing a 22% year-over-year increase
Adjusted EBITDA surged 34% to $29.4 million with gross margin expansion of 170 bps
Integrated PayTech segment grew nearly 20%, now contributing over 20% of total profitability
summary: CPI Card Group reported record fourth quarter revenue of $153 million, a 22% increase driven by the ArrowEye acquisition and organic growth in debit/credit segments. Adjusted EBITDA grew 34% to $29.4 million with margins expanding 170 bps despite tariff expenses and integration costs. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations citing strong execution, though they noted a slow start for prepaid business.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.2 million in Q4 2025 from $4.9 million a year ago
Gross margin declined to 67% from 71% due to product mix and introductory international pricing
Operating expenses remained elevated at $11.4 million vs $11.3 million prior year
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 43% YoY to $6 million
Commercial inflection point with pipeline of 110 new systems in final sales stages
TULSA reimbursement confirmed for 2026 with Category 1 CPT codes and private payer coverage expected in H2 2026
summary: Profound Medical reported Q4 2025 revenue of $6 million, up 43% year-over-year, with gross margin at 67% versus 71% in Q4 2024 due to product mix and introductory international pricing. The net loss widened to $8.2 million from $4.9 million, with cash at $59.7 million. Management highlighted a growing sales pipeline (110 systems in final sales stages), continued reimbursement momentum with CPT Category 1 codes confirmed for 2026, and early international distribution success in Saudi Arabia and Australia. They reiterated a path to profitable growth, targeting ~$85 million annual revenue with 200 sites and 50 procedures per site, and expect high double-digit to low triple-digit revenue growth in 2026. Upcoming CAPTAIN trial data presentations are key catalysts.

negative_highlights: Q4 2025 revenue declined YoY to $8.5 million, though management attributed this to timing differences in Super Scooper deployments.
Q4 2025 reported a net loss of $15.1 million and negative adjusted EBITDA of $9.5 million due to one-time debt extinguishment losses and warrant fair value adjustments.
positive_highlights: Full year 2025 revenue increased 25% YoY to $122.8 million.
Adjusted EBITDA grew to $45.3 million for the full year 2025.
Management raised 2026 revenue guidance range to $135-$145 million and adjusted EBITDA to $55-$60 million.
summary: Full year 2025 revenue grew 25% to $122.8 million, driven by a 23% increase in core operations excluding Spanish Super Scooper return-to-service work. The company reported positive net income of $4.1 million and adjusted EBITDA of $45.3 million for the year. For 2026, management raised guidance to $135-$145 million in revenue and $55-$60 million in adjusted EBITDA, citing fleet expansion and improved utilization.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue delta versus demand growth was negatively impacted by wholesaler inventory declines
R&D expenses increased quarter-over-quarter in Q4 as the company invested heavily in pipeline development
No specific guidance provided for full-year 2026, with management stating it will be released on August earnings call
positive_highlights: LOQTORZI full-year sales doubled in 2025, reaching $40.8M versus $19.1M prior year
Q4 net revenue grew sequentially by 11% to $12.4M with strong demand growth of 15.5%
Debt principal reduced from peak of $480 million down to just $38.8 million at year-end
summary: Coherus Oncology reported Q4 FY2025 net revenue of $12.4 million (up 11% sequentially) and full-year 2025 LOQTORZI sales doubling to $40.8M from $19.1M in 2024, driven by new patient starts and guideline adoption. The company successfully reduced debt by over 90% to $38.8 million and cut headcount while maintaining a strategic focus on advancing its oncology pipeline with data readouts expected mid-2026.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports revenue growth missed expectations due to seasonality and lag pre-World Cup, though margins expanded significantly.
Softening observed in the Brazil market during Q1 following strong Q4 performance.
UK tax changes will reduce customer GGR; while management claims margin impact is neutral on a per-revenue basis, total revenue from UK customers may decline.
positive_highlights: Interactive segment revenue grew 53% YoY with EBITDA growing 60%, marking the single highest day and weekend GGR in recent history.
Full-year company-wide EBITDA margin reached a record 42% for Q4, validating the transformation thesis to move into mid-40s margins by 2026.
Successful launch of NFL licensed Virtual Sports with BetMGM in New Jersey and Ontario serves as a proof point for North American expansion.
summary: Inspired Entertainment reported Q4 FY2025 results with revenue and EBITDA up significantly in the interactive segment (up 53% and 60%, respectively), driving a record full-year company-wide EBITDA margin of 37%. Management raised its 2026 EBITDA guidance to $112 million-$118 million, citing strong momentum from digital mix shifts and successful North American launches. The company is de-levering toward a target net leverage of 2.5-3x by year-end 2026.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss widened to $21M from $3M in prior quarter.
Gain on sale margin declined to 324 bps from 339 bps, with Q1 guidance of 270-300 bps.
Cash decreased by $122M from prior quarter to $337M.
positive_highlights: Origination volume of $8.0B was highest since 2022, up 23% from prior quarter.
Recapture rate reached 71% from in-house servicing platform.
Adjusted revenue up 10% YoY with expense growth under 1% for full year.
summary: loanDepot reported Q4 2025 adjusted net loss of $21 million, worse than the $3 million loss in Q3, due to lower gain on sale margin, higher MSR amortization, and higher expenses. Pull-through weighted lock volume rose 4% to $7.3 billion, and origination volume hit $8.0 billion, the highest since 2022 and up 23% sequentially. Gain on sale margin was 324 basis points at the high end of guidance but down from 339 bps. Q1 2026 guidance calls for lock volume of $7.75-8.75 billion and margin of 270-300 bps. Management emphasized market share gains, a 71% recapture rate, and investments in AI and technology to drive operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue declined 5% to $8.3 million
Ended the year with only $1.2 million in cash despite $7 million raised
Critical care revenue declined 19% for the full year and 24% in the fourth quarter
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded to 68.2% in Q4, up 9.9 percentage points year-over-year
U.S. console sales increased 208% with eight units sold versus three in prior-year
Heart failure and pediatrics grew 814% year-over-year
summary: Nuwellis reported Q4 2025 revenue of $2.4 million, up 4% year-over-year and 9% sequentially, with gross margin expanding to 68.2% from 58.4%. Full-year revenue declined 5% to $8.3 million, with heart failure and pediatrics growing 814% each, offset by a 19% decline in critical care. The company ended the year with $1.2 million cash and no debt, but raised $7 million and reduced guidance on cash burn. Management is focused on operational restructuring, exiting EU markets, terminating a clinical trial, and integrating a new acquisition to drive future growth.

negative_highlights: No specific revenue or earnings figures were reported; management focused entirely on forward-looking project milestones rather than current financial performance.
The company explicitly stated that oxy-combustion work streams have been suspended pending a viability evaluation, representing a significant strategic pivot away from prior technology focus.
positive_highlights: Net Power increased Project Permian Phase I net electrical output capacity from approximately 60 MW to roughly 80 MW via design restructuring.
The company secured two modular gas turbine packages with delivery targeted for early 2028, de-risking the power island supply chain.
Management confirmed site control is in place with an executed ground lease and progressing grid interconnection discussions.
summary: Net Power Inc reported Q4 FY2025 results with no specific revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript; management highlighted a strategic pivot from oxy-combustion to a combined cycle gas turbine plus post-combustion carbon capture (GT+PCC) solution for Project Permian. The company raised its net electrical output target for Phase I from 60 MW to approximately 80 MW and confirmed an FID target in the second half of 2026 with commercial operations targeted for early 2029, though no specific financial guidance was updated or issued during this call.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $7.8 million for Q4 due to increased operating expenses, legal costs related to litigation, and IPO transition fees.
SG&A expenses surged from $9.1M in the prior year quarter to $16.3M, driven by headcount expansion and public company overhead.
Gross margin contracted slightly sequentially (76.5% full-year vs 77.0% prior year) as ASPs faced slight pressure.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 65% year-over-year driven by accelerated adoption among new surgeons (134 core/contender surgeons, up 61%).
Gross margin held steady at 76.7%, demonstrating pricing power and cost discipline despite rapid growth.
New product launches including the InSet I-135RFX Humeral Stem and N-22 Humeral Head are in limited market release with positive early feedback.
summary: Shoulder Innovations reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $14.4 million (up 65% YoY) and full-year revenue of $47.3 million (up 50%). Gross margins remained strong at 76.7% for the quarter, though SG&A expenses increased significantly due to IPO-related costs and headcount expansion in the commercial organization. Management initiated FY2026 guidance of $62-$65 million revenue.

negative_highlights: Full-year gross margin contracted to just over 58% from 60% in 2024 due to ASP pressure and incremental costs from seven new biomarkers.
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened slightly to $9.8 million as the company increased operating expenses by 13% to fund commercial expansion and R&D.
ASP for new biomarkers (T-cell and RA33) faced headwinds, requiring revenue cycle management efforts to recover from an accrual of mid-$70s toward a target of roughly $80.
positive_highlights: Record top-line performance with full-year revenue reaching $66.6 million, up nearly 20% year-over-year.
Volume growth accelerated significantly in the second half of the year, bucking typical seasonality to reach Q4's highest volume ever at 137,000 tests.
Pharma Services business scaled rapidly from roughly $100,000 in 2024 to $1.7 million in revenue in 2025 with over $4 million in backlog.
summary: Exagen reported full-year 2025 revenue of $66.6 million, a near 20% increase driven by over 11% volume growth and a 7% rise in trailing twelve-month ASP to approximately $441. The company provided full-year 2026 guidance of $70-$73 million, maintaining the prior revenue range while adjusting the breakeven Adjusted EBITDA threshold upward to roughly $80 million due to strategic investments in commercial expansion and R&D.

negative_highlights: Commission income declined year-over-year from $14.1 million to $12.4 million due to portfolio realignment.
Adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of $1.6 million, up from a loss of $0.3 million in the prior year.
Salaries and wages increased significantly to $10.3 million, driven largely by non-cash share-based compensation.
positive_highlights: Unrestricted cash increased $0.9 million (250%) to $1.3 million at year-end.
Stockholders' equity increased $3.4 million (114%) to $6.4 million.
Commission income generated more than $12 million from the remaining insurance and insurtech platform.
summary: Reliance Global Group reported a net loss of $9.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to a loss of $9.1 million in 2024 (text states 'Net loss improved by $2 million-$7 million' but cites $9.1M for both years, implying stability or slight improvement masked by divestitures). Commission income decreased to $12.4 million from $14.1 million due to the strategic sale of subsidiaries including Fortman Insurance Services, Employee Benefits Solutions, and U.S. Benefits Alliance. The company strengthened its balance sheet with unrestricted cash increasing 250% to $1.3 million and stockholders' equity rising 114% to $6.4 million.

negative_highlights: Management lowered Payables organic growth expectations for FY2026 to an 8%-10% range citing headwinds from lower interest rates and card network changes.
Merchant Solutions core portfolio slowed in Q4 due to weakness in restaurants, construction, and retail trade verticals like home furnishings.
Treasury Solutions gross margins contracted approximately 170 basis points YoY as high-margin CFTPay growth was offset by the addition of lower-margin Passport and Priority Tech Ventures revenue.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS increased $0.52 or 102% year-over-year to $1.03 driven by significant operating leverage in Payables (EBITDA up 61%) and Treasury Solutions.
Q4 revenue grew 9% YoY with adjusted gross profit margins expanding 360 basis points to 40.6%, reflecting the accretive impact of acquisitions.
The company successfully remediated a material weakness in internal controls over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025.
summary: Priority Technology Holdings reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $247.1 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.03 (up 102% YoY). Management provided full-year 2026 guidance for top-line growth in the range of 6%-9%, with a specific note that Payables organic growth expectations were lowered to an 8%-10% range due to market headwinds including lower interest rates. While Q4 results showed strong margin expansion and EBITDA beats, management explicitly moderated forward outlooks for key segments.

negative_highlights: Q4 results are quiet and should be viewed in full-year context, indicating lumpy revenue
Expects CHMP to recommend withdrawal of the mpox indication
No new U.S. procurement contract announced; timing uncertain
positive_highlights: Secured $27 million in U.S. government development funding during 2025
Received a $13 million international order from a repeat Asia-Pacific customer
Ended 2025 with $155 million cash and no debt
summary: SIGA reported full-year 2025 product revenues of approximately $88 million, with $53 million from oral TPOXX and $26 million from IV TPOXX under the BARDA 19C contract, plus $6 million international sales. Pretax operating income was about $24 million, net income about $23 million, and diluted EPS $0.32. The company ended 2025 with $155 million cash and no debt, and has $26 million of outstanding U.S. government orders expected to deliver in 2026. Management remains engaged with the U.S. government but gave no timing on a new procurement contract, while the EMA CHMP is expected to issue a context in March, with management expecting the smallpox indication maintained and the mpox indication withdrawn.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $1.9M from $2.1M despite higher revenue, due to supply disruption and underutilization
Gearing segment reported adjusted EBITDA loss of $0.3M, revenue down 8% YoY
Supply disruption in Heavy Fab reduced throughput and operating efficiency; Gearing capacity utilization lower
positive_highlights: Industrial Solutions revenue up 60% YoY, highest ever recorded; segment EBITDA margin expanded to 16% (vs 10% prior year)
Backlog in Industrial Solutions hit new record of $38M, fifth consecutive record quarter; Gearing backlog at highest since 2023 ($26M)
Received $6.0M follow-on order for natural gas turbine gearing in March, adding to Q1 orders of ~$11M
summary: Broadwind reported Q4 2025 revenue of $37.7 million, up 12% year-over-year, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $1.9 million from $2.1 million due to a raw material supply disruption and lower Gearing utilization. Industrial Solutions revenue jumped 60% to a record $9.4 million, and backlog hit a new record of $38 million. Gearing orders rose 38% to $9.7 million, with total backlog reaching $26 million, and the company reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $140-150 million revenue and $8-10 million adjusted EBITDA.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $6.4M in FY25 compared to $12.9M, primarily driven by noncash stock-based compensation of $14.4M and one-time charges.
GA&A expenses increased 24% YoY due to the aforementioned nonrecurring items; excluding these would have resulted in a decline over $1M.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 40% YoY in FY25 with Q4 up 36%, driven by licensing ($9.8M) and subscriptions ($9.1M).
Adjusted free cash flow increased 46% to $13.9M for the full year, marking eight consecutive quarters of positive operating cash.
Gross margins expanded significantly from 52% a year ago to 60%, aided by reduced nondiscretionary G&A expenses.
summary: CuriosityStream reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $19.2M (up 36% YoY) and full-year revenue of $71.7M (up 40%), with adjusted free cash flow reaching $4.3M in the quarter ($13.9M for the year). Gross margins expanded to 60%, driven by cost discipline, though net loss widened due to noncash stock-based compensation and one-time charges. Management raised share repurchase authorization to $6M and reiterated a commitment to pay dividends from operations.

negative_highlights: Ex-political growth of 28% in Q4 but guide implies slowdown to high teens in Q1
Full-year performance absorbed tariff pressure and client migration
Q1 guidance slowed due to seasonality and advertiser mix
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 22% YoY, above the high end of quarterly guidance
CTV contribution ex-TAC grew over 40% for the second consecutive year
New flagship customers Molson Coors and WHOOP live and ramping
summary: Viant Technology reported Q4 FY2025 revenue up 22% YoY and contribution ex-TAC up 19%, both above the high end of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $24.7 million, also exceeding guidance. Full-year 2025 revenue increased 19% to $344 million, with contribution ex-TAC up 18%. Management highlighted accelerating CTV growth (46% of spend), strong new customer wins (Molson Coors, WHOOP), and the launch of their AI-driven Outcomes product, while acknowledging Q1 2026 growth is expected to moderate to high teens due to seasonality and advertiser mix.

negative_highlights: Q4 2025 included a one-time restructuring charge.
ECO business currently services-based with limited gross margin contribution.
Guidance includes a speculative portion per CFO comments.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue up 19% YoY to $70.4 million; gross margin expanded to 64%.
Signed three CDMO agreements and first commercial contract for ECOsynthesis siRNA.
Raised 2026 revenue guidance to $72-76 million.
summary: Codexis reported full-year 2025 revenue of $70.4 million, up from $59.3 million in 2024, with product gross margin expanding to 64% from 56%. The company signed three CDMO agreements with Bachem, Nitto Avecia, and Axolabs, and announced its first contract for fully enzymatic siRNA supply (low 7-figure) with an emerging biotech. Management provided 2026 revenue guidance of $72-76 million and expects current cash to fund operations through 2027. A one-time restructuring charge was taken in Q4, and the company expects to sign another licensing-type deal in 2026.

negative_highlights: Vessel operating expenses surged 94% year-over-year due to the integration of the SSI fleet and transfer costs.
Charter-in cost per day increased 39% YoY to $19,100 as market rates rose for new vessels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 22% year-over-year to $28.7 million, supported by a 26% increase in shipping days.
TCE rates averaged 19% above prevailing market indices for Panamax, Supramax, and Handysize vessels.
Management expects approximately $3 million of incremental EBITDA from new terminal operations (Lake Charles, Tampa) coming online throughout 2026.
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported Q4 FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA of $28.7 million (up 22% YoY) and GAAP net income of $11.9 million ($0.19/share), driven by a 26% increase in shipping days to 3,000+ total days despite higher charter-in costs due to market rate increases. Management raised full-year EBITDA guidance expectations for the integrated logistics platform (anticipating ~$3M incremental from new terminals) and reaffirmed priorities of fleet renewal and shareholder returns via dividends ($16.3M paid in 2025) and buybacks (~600k shares).

negative_highlights: Q4 adjusted EPS was a loss of CAD 0.14 due to a $13 million life-to-date cost adjustment on Fargo and wet weather in Australia.
Fargo project required a third retroactive cost adjustment, increasing total costs by ~$50 million gross; only ~85% complete.
EBITDA margin was 23%, down approximately 7% from the run-rate of around 30% due to the same factors.
positive_highlights: Australia Q4 revenue was a record AUD 176 million despite wet weather; full-year Australian revenue up 17%.
Free cash flow of CAD 57 million in Q4, and CAD 103 million in H2 2025, supports 2026 guidance.
Backlog is approximately CAD 3.9 billion, with CAD 1.2 billion secured for 2026; bid pipeline of CAD 12.6 billion, including CAD 4.6 billion in active tenders.
summary: Q4 2025 revenue was CAD 344 million, with adjusted EPS a loss of CAD 0.14, impacted by a $13 million life-to-date cost adjustment on the Fargo project and wet weather in Australia. Excluding these items, gross margin was ~15%, with Q4 EBITDA of CAD 78 million. Full-year 2025 combined revenue was CAD 1.5 billion, up 10% year-over-year. Guidance for 2026 is unchanged: combined revenue of CAD 1.6 billion, adjusted EBITDA of CAD 400 million, and free cash flow of CAD 120 million, excluding any material new wins. The IMC acquisition is delayed to Q2 2026 due to regulatory review but is expected to close with retroactive earnings to January 1.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue was negatively impacted by a labor strike in British Columbia, estimated to reduce sales by approximately $2.5 million.
International export shipments from Germany were delayed into Q1 due to regulatory uncertainty and inventory adjustments at customer sites.
Legacy produce operations saw a 21% decline in sales compared to the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Consolidated net sales increased 9% YoY to $49.6 million, driven by a 384% increase in international medicinal exports from Canada.
Canadian cannabis gross margin expanded significantly to 43%, up from the prior year's negative impact of impairment charges.
Company achieved record levels for profitability ($21M net income full-year), cash flow ($58M), and adjusted EBITDA ($50M) in FY2025.
summary: Village Farms reported Q4 FY2025 consolidated net sales of $49.6 million (up 9% YoY) and record profitability with net income from continuing operations of $2.3 million ($0.02/share). The quarter was impacted by a labor strike in British Columbia reducing revenue by approximately $2.5 million, but gross margins expanded to 43%, driven by higher-margin international exports which grew nearly fourfold year-over-year. Management raised full-year guidance expectations for the cannabis business following record performance and confirmed capacity expansion projects remain on track.

negative_highlights: Suspended dividend to save $20-25 million annually, reflecting market not crediting the payout
Northeast Flat Top area has six wells with anomalous water inflows; no new drilling there in 2026
High cost of capital (10%+ interest) on term loan, with debt reduction as a priority
positive_highlights: Quarter-to-date 2026 production averaging over 46,000 BOE/d, roughly 10% above the midpoint of guidance
Capital budget ~50% lower than 2025, with estimated 65% increase in production per dollar invested
More than 2,600 total drilling locations across stacked formations, with over 100 rig-years of inventory
summary: HighPeak Energy's Q4 2025 earnings release focuses on a conservative 2026 plan prioritizing balance sheet strength and free cash flow over production growth. The company has suspended its dividend (saving $20-25 million annually) and reduced its 2026 capital budget by nearly 50% year-over-year, with early 2026 production of over 46,000 BOE/d running about 10% above the midpoint of guidance. Management has expanded hedging and plans to pay down debt aggressively, especially with stronger oil prices, but also highlights six wells with anomalous water inflows in the Northeast Flat Top area, leading to no new drilling there in 2026.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses rose 31% YoY to $12.6M driven by external development costs for the LX1 product that did not begin shipping until early 2026
Management explicitly stated it is 'impossible' to predict exact FY2026 revenue ranges or specific order volumes due to a bumpy business environment
Significant portion of R&D spend allocated to new products (LX1) and waveguide optimization that are not yet generating commercial sales
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue increased 76% YoY to $2.2 million driven by M400 unit sales and engineering services
Full-year gross loss improved significantly from a $5.6M loss in 2024 to a $1.1M loss, primarily due to lower inventory obsolescence reserves
Net cash position strengthened to $21.2 million at year-end with no debt outstanding
summary: Vuzix reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $2.2 million (up from $1.3M in prior year) and full-year revenue of $6.3 million (up 9% YoY), driven by higher unit sales of the M400 platform and engineering services, though gross loss narrowed to a net loss attributable to common shareholders of $8.7 million for Q4 ($0.12/share). Management provided no specific numerical guidance or earnings estimates for FY2026, instead offering qualitative 'spitball' commentary on OEM growth surpassing branded enterprise revenue later in the year and citing new contracts with Amazon and Collins Aerospace without quantified production timelines.

negative_highlights: Rockies and Southwest segments saw revenues decline roughly 9-10% sequentially due to severe weather, seasonality, and customer budget exhaustion.
Q4 revenue per rig was approximately $297,000 but Q1 guidance forecasts a decrease of about 3% despite the company maintaining its asset base.
Corporate adjusted EBITDA loss remains elevated at approximately $6.3 million in Q4 compared to historical levels.
positive_highlights: Northeast/Mid-Con segment delivered adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 25.3% driven by robust gas-directed work and rig count increases of approximately 6%.
Adjusted EBITDA reached a quarterly high of $23 million, representing the strongest profitability for the year.
Dry gas revenue in Northeast/Mid-Con increased 5.3% quarter over quarter as the portfolio continues to align with higher-margin opportunities.
summary: Fourth quarter revenue of approximately $157 million was in line with guidance but decreased due to seasonality and budget exhaustion. Adjusted EBITDA reached a quarterly high of roughly $23 million (margin ~14%), driven by strong performance in the Northeast/Mid-Con segment where dry gas revenue grew 5.3% sequentially, while Rockies and Southwest segments declined on weather and activity softness. Management provided Q1 guidance for revenues between $145M-$150M (down ~3%) but expects a gradual market recovery starting in H2 2026.

negative_highlights: Revenue base remains small at $0.9 million for the quarter; profitability path not quantified.
InstaMortgage closing remains subject to state-by-state regulatory approvals, with timing uncertain.
Company still early stage with no explicit guidance for 2026 beyond 'predictable growth'.
positive_highlights: Full-year revenue grew 376% to $4.5 million; Q4 revenue grew 70% YoY to $0.9 million.
Cash and cash equivalents ended at $7.8 million, up 149% YoY, and parent-level debt was eliminated.
Prevu acquisition added 13 states and D.C., expanding realty footprint; InstaMortgage deal expected to add lending capabilities.
summary: Q4 FY2025 revenue was $0.9 million, up 70% YoY; full-year revenue rose 376% to $4.5 million. Full-year gross profit was $2.5 million, and cash ended at $7.8 million, up 149% YoY. Management highlighted the Prevu acquisition and the planned InstaMortgage deal (closing expected late Q1 or early Q2) as key drivers for continued platform integration. No formal guidance was provided; tone was upbeat but qualitative.

negative_highlights: Q4 cash cost to mine Bitcoin reached $84,552 per coin, exceeding the average Bitcoin price during the period, causing operational losses.
Net loss from continuing operations for Q4 was $285 million, driven by $171.4 million fair value loss on Bitcoin collateral receivables and $81.4 million impairment on mining machines.
Hash rate will contract in the near term as inefficient machines are phased out, and no specific 2026 hash rate targets were provided.
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA was positive at $24.5 million, despite the net loss.
Revenue grew strongly to $688.1 million for 2025, up from the prior year's small base.
Company raised $75.5 million in new equity financing ($10.5 million injection and $65 million agreements) to strengthen the balance sheet.
summary: Cango's Q4 2025 revenue was $179.5 million with a net loss from continuing operations of $285 million, reflecting heavy impairment and fair value losses. Full-year 2025 revenue reached $688.1 million with a net loss of $622 million, including $96.5 million fair value loss on Bitcoin holdings and $81 million impairment on mining machines. The company sold 4,451 Bitcoin in February 2026 to repay debt and is shifting focus to an AI compute subsidiary, EcoHash, with a pilot in Georgia expected to generate revenue this year. Management guided that hash rate will temporarily decline as they phase out inefficient machines, while emphasizing balance sheet strength and capital discipline.

negative_highlights: 2026 guidance tempered by M&T's double-digit revenue decline due to prior bookings lag
PathFactory acquisition adds investment costs and integration uncertainty for 2026
FX headwinds from Israeli shekel continue to pressure expectations
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDA of $6.3M, tenth consecutive quarter of profitability
Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA grew 150% YoY, above original guidance
PathFactory acquisition adds AI-driven content journey orchestration, with run rate in teens of millions
summary: Kaltura reported Q4 2025 total revenue of $45.5 million and subscription revenue of $42.7 million, with record adjusted EBITDA of $6.3 million, marking the tenth consecutive quarter of profitability. Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $18.6 million, up 150% year-over-year and above original guidance.
