The company announced the planned acquisition of PathFactory for about $22 million, expanding its agentic digital experience platform, and guided 2026 with caution, citing headwinds from M&T revenue decline and PathFactory's contribution timing. New product launches include agentic avatars and an Avatar SDK, with revenue expected in the second half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses decreased but were burdened by ~$3.3 million in transaction and brand marketing costs
Website relaunch is expected later this year rather than immediately monetizing the new digital hub
Honey Birdette growth relies on a recent price increase of 10% which may face macro headwinds
positive_highlights: Honey Birdette sales grew 9% year over year, driven by full-price note up 21% and retail growth of 17% like-for-like
Licensing revenue reached $46 million in FY2025 with a 90% gross margin and nearly half guaranteed via contract
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive for the fourth consecutive quarter at $7.1M, excluding litigation expenses it would have been $8.0M
summary: Playboy reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $34.9 million (up from $33.5M in prior year) and net income of $3.6 million ($0.03/share), marking a significant turnaround from the previous year's loss. The company achieved its fourth consecutive quarter of positive Adjusted EBITDA at $7.1 million, driven by strong performance across licensing (over 90% guaranteed revenue) and Honey Birdette retail growth. Management highlighted successful deleveraging with debt reduced to ~$160M following a UTG China deal expected to close soon.

negative_highlights: Fintech non-GAAP gross margin fell from 96% to 69% due to mix shift
Operating loss of $32 million for 2025, though improved by $9.7 million
Cash and restricted cash only $16.1 million with $6.2 million drawn on credit line
positive_highlights: 2025 net revenue of $18.2 million exceeded guidance of $16.5 million, up 81% YoY
Q4 fintech revenue up 109% YoY and 100%+ QoQ
G&A expenses reduced by $9.9 million (26%) YoY
summary: PSQH reported 2025 net revenue from continuing operations of $18.2 million, an 81% increase year-over-year and above guidance of $16.5 million. Q4 fintech revenue grew 109% to $7.3 million, with credit revenue up 47% to $4.8 million. The company reduced operating loss by $9.7 million versus prior year, cut headcount by over 40%, and expects annualized cash savings of about $8 million. Management is focused on fintech-only strategy, with divestitures of brand and marketplace underway.

negative_highlights: Rockies segment adjusted EBITDA decreased by $1.2M due to natural production declines and no new well connections in Q4
Piceance segment expected decline in volume throughputs with MVC shortfall payments rolling off from $17M in 2025 to ~$13M in 2026
positive_highlights: Full-year FY2025 adjusted EBITDA beat of approximately $46M driven by Permian segment growth
Double E Pipeline mainline capacity now generally fully subscribed with over 1.6 Bcf/day in firm take-or-pay contracts
New term loan refinancing enabled an $85 million distribution to repay preferred dividends and reduce debt
summary: Summit Midstream Corp reported Q4 FY2025 adjusted EBITDA of $58.6 million and full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $243 million against a prior year total of approximately $197 million, representing a significant beat driven by Permian volume growth. Management raised the 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range to $225-$265 million and increased capital expenditure guidance to $85-$105 million following the execution of new long-term take-or-pay agreements on Double E Pipeline that fully subscribed existing capacity. The company also refinanced its Permian joint venture, enabling an $85 million distribution back to Summit Midstream Corp., which will be used to repay accrued preferred dividends and reduce ABL borrowings.

negative_highlights: Cash consumption is expected to increase significantly in 2026, rising from ~$200 million last year to between $225-$275 million.
Backlog contraction occurred as some customers withdrew non-binding letters of intent (LOIs) due to changing strategies or bankruptcy.
Certification timeline faces delays and rework regarding means of compliance with new FAA regulations, impacting the path to type certificate issuance.
positive_highlights: Completed first flight of engineering prototype on December 19, validating integration of fifth-generation fly-by-wire and fixed pitch lifter rotors.
Secured firm orders with AirX for two aircraft plus an option for 48 more, alongside a backlog of ~2,700 aircraft valued at $13.5 billion.
Total liquidity reached $641 million after securing a new syndicated loan and refinancing existing debt.
summary: Eve Holding reported a net loss of $64 million for Q4 2025 and $224 million for the full year, driven by $59 million in R&D expenses and $8 million in SG&A. The company ended the quarter with $393 million in cash and total liquidity of $541 million, which is sufficient to cover expected capital needs well into 2028. Management raised guidance for 2026 cash consumption to a range of $225-$275 million from the prior year's low end of $200 million due to intensified development activities and supplier payments.

negative_highlights: Card Issuing revenues declined in Q4 due to an indirect acquisition of a reseller's amusement park card program
SG&A expenses increased 10% for the year, though management expects headcount savings and flat SG&A in 2026
positive_highlights: Record quarterly and annual revenues with total dollars processed up 19% year-over-year
ACH segment led growth with over 30% revenue increase driven by pinless debit volume surging more than 80%
Output Solutions achieved strong momentum with pieces mailed up 11% in the fourth quarter
summary: USIO reported a solid Q4 FY2025 with record revenue growth accelerating to 8% sequentially and year-over-year for the full year. The company delivered positive adjusted EBITDA for three consecutive years while executing on its strategy of increasing wallet share across ACH, Card, and Output Solutions segments. Management reaffirmed guidance for 10%-12% revenue growth in fiscal 2026.

negative_highlights: Full year 2025 revenues decreased compared to the prior period
Net loss of $6.6 million reflecting increased investment in clinical pipeline and R&D expenses rising 51% YoY
R&D spending on PRX-115 is expected to continue increasing
positive_highlights: $25 million regulatory milestone payment earned from Chiesi
Projected full year 2026 revenue growth of more than 50% driven by high-margin Chiesi sales ($33M-$35M)
PRX-115 Phase II RELEASE study has enrolled first patients with top-line results expected in H2 2027
summary: For full year 2025, Protalix reported revenues of $51.8 million (a modest decrease from the prior year) and a net loss of $6.6 million compared to income in 2024, driven by increased R&D spending on PRX-115. The company received a $25 million regulatory milestone payment for an EU dosing regimen approval, projecting total cash balances near $50 million by early April 2026.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they do not provide formal revenue or earnings guidance for the upcoming period.
Retail channel revenue declined 13% in Q4 compared to the prior year quarter despite seasonal lift from some partners still on transactional models.
GAAP R&D expenses increased due to non-cash amortization of capitalized software costs, though cash spend remains controlled.
positive_highlights: Achieved annual GAAP profitability with net income of $1.3 million and Adjusted EBITDA positive for three consecutive quarters, ending the year at a record $2.6M.
Gross margin expanded to 91.4% in Q4 driven by AWS migration efficiencies and lower Azure spend which declined over 55% from peak levels.
Operating expenses decreased 7% YoY ($357k reduction) while revenue grew, demonstrating strong operating leverage.
summary: Intellicheck reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $6.6 million (up 12% YoY) and full-year revenue of $22.7 million (up 13%), achieving annual GAAP profitability with net income of $1.3 million ($0.06 EPS). The company reached a milestone in adjusted EBITDA positivity, recording Q4 Adjusted EBITDA of $1.9M versus prior year guidance targets without providing new forward revenue or earnings guidance due to policy. Gross margins expanded slightly to 91.4% while operating expenses decreased by 7% YoY.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased significantly to almost $28 million, driven by the accrual basis expense for a larger number of ground leases.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at approximately -$1 million in Q4 despite operational improvements.
Denver campus lease-up is proceeding slower than expected due to seasonal winter effects.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue reached a record $27.5 million, representing an 87% year-over-year increase.
Adjusted EBITDA improved for three consecutive quarters and turned to negative breakeven in Q4 due to higher occupancy and rental rates.
Management successfully met its site acquisition guidance of securing leases at 23 airports.
summary: Sky Harbour Group reported record consolidated revenue of $27.5 million for FY2025 (up 87% YoY), driven by the acquisition of Camarillo and new campus openings in Phoenix, Dallas, and Denver. However, adjusted EBITDA remained negative at approximately -$1 million in Q4 despite improved occupancy rates, as operating expenses rose to nearly $28 million due to increased ground lease accruals for a larger portfolio. Management met its guidance of 23 airports under ground lease but noted that the first obligated group projects are still stabilizing with higher-than-expected initial costs.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined year-over-year for the full year ($161.7M vs $188.9M) due to store consolidations and lower retail volume.
The company continues to close underperforming locations, with plans to reduce the footprint from 23 stores in Q4 down to approximately 15-19 by end of FY2026.
note, general, and administrative expenses increased slightly year-over-year due to one-time severance and legal costs of $1.5 million.
positive_highlights: Q4 net sales grew slightly to $37.8 million despite a smaller footprint of only 23 stores, indicating stabilization in core operations.
Gross margin expanded 370 basis points year-over-year to 26.8% for the full year due to higher proprietary brand mix and cost reductions.
GAAP net loss improved by $15.9 million to a negative $7.4M, with adjusted EBITDA improving by $6.1M to a loss of only $2M.
summary: GrowGeneration reported Q4 FY2025 net sales of $37.8 million, a slight year-over-year increase despite operating with eight fewer retail locations following store closures that reduced the footprint to 23 stores as of December 31. Gross margin expanded significantly to 26.8% for the full year (up from 23.1%), driven by proprietary brand penetration reaching 35.8%, while GAAP net loss narrowed substantially to $7.4 million ($0.12/share) compared to a prior-year loss of $23.3 million. Management provided guidance for FY2026 revenue between $162M and $168M, anticipating breakeven adjusted EBITDA by year-end as the company continues shedding retail locations toward an estimated 15-19 store count.

negative_highlights: Net loss increased significantly year-over-year due to non-cash fair value adjustments on convertible notes and higher stock-based compensation.
Input cost inflation persists with copper prices up ~18% and steel prices up ~8% since October, though management claims the capital plan remains disciplined.
Coosa Graphite Deposit production is not expected until late 2028-2029 due to a permitting timeline of 12-24 months.
positive_highlights: Kellyton construction advanced with commissioning of one micronization mill and one spheroidization mill as part of a qualification line producing customer samples.
Company received a U.S. patent for its graphite purification process that avoids hydrofluoric acid, differentiating it from traditional methods.
Capital plan optimized to reduce estimated Phase I costs by approximately $25 million from the original estimate while maintaining core design capabilities.
summary: Westwater Resources reported a net loss of approximately $27 million for the full year ended December 31, 2025, compared to a prior-year loss of $12.7 million, driven by non-cash convertible note adjustments and increased stock-based compensation. The company maintains cash on hand of roughly $50 million but estimates an additional ~$50 million is needed to complete Kellyton Phase I, excluding contingency. Management reiterated the target for commercial production in 2027 following recent permitting progress at Coosa.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly from Q4 FY2024 due to high commercial launch costs ($8.2M in Q4 vs $4.4M prior year)
Reimbursement delays causing 'natural dampening' where more than half of scripts are not filled immediately
No contracted payer coverage is currently in place, limiting full market penetration
positive_highlights: FDA approval of CARDAMYST achieved late January with retail availability within six weeks
Initial launch data shows over 150 prescriptions filled by more than 100 unique prescribers in the first month
Pro forma cash position strengthened to approximately $200 million, providing runway into late 2027
summary: Milestone Pharmaceuticals reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $1.5 million and a net loss of $17.4 million ($0.16/share), driven by the commercial launch expenses for its newly FDA-approved product CARDAMYST, which had no prior year comparables due to recent approval. Management described the quarter as 'early days' with too little data to extrapolate trends yet, noting that while initial prescription fills are occurring, reimbursement delays and paperwork remain significant headwinds before contracted coverage is secured in 2026-2027.

negative_highlights: Revenues decreased year-over-year due to a decrease in funding portal fees.
Operating loss widened significantly from $1.7 million to $2.2 million compared to Q3 FY2025.
Management explicitly stated the company is still in a transition period and has not yet realized underlying economics at sufficient scale.
positive_highlights: Signed four new broker-dealer clients during the third quarter.
summary: Netcapital reported Q3 FY2026 revenues of approximately $94,000, a decrease from the prior year period primarily due to lower funding portal fees, and an operating loss of approximately $2.2 million compared to $1.7 million in the same quarter last year. Management noted that while revenue increased sequentially from Q2 FY2026, the company remains in a transition period where attractive economics depend on achieving sufficient scale before realizing benefits from its fixed cost structure.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they will not provide specific revenue or EBITDA guidance for 2026 at this time.
Cash flow in Q4 was impacted by receivable collection timing, though early collections are expected to benefit Q1 2026.
positive_highlights: Net product sales reached record levels with Q4 growth driven by AYA patient expansion and new account acquisition.
Fennec HEARS program achieved all-time highs in enrollments, prescribed vials, active patients, and conversion rates (up 70% sequentially).
Patent litigation settlement secured market exclusivity until September 2033 with no other outstanding litigations.
summary: Fennec reported record net product sales of $44.6 million for FY2025 (up ~50% YoY) and Q4 sales of $13.8 million (up ~75% YoY). The company settled patent litigation with Cipla, eliminating debt obligations to reach a cash position of $36.8 million. Management indicated that while momentum is strong into 2026, they will evaluate issuing specific revenue and EBITDA guidance in the coming months rather than providing immediate numbers.

negative_highlights: Q4 total revenue growth of 5% was softer than prior-year's hurricane-boosted quarter
THP wind-down required $5.3M cash use in H2 2025
OsStic U.S. launch not until Q1 2027, no near-term revenue contribution
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue at high end of guidance, up 13% ex hurricane BIASURGE
Gross margin up ~200 bps to 93%, adjusted EBITDA up 86% to $17M
Vizient Innovative Technology contract for BIASURGE expands access to ~1,800 facilities
summary: Sanara MedTech reported Q4 FY2025 net revenue of $27.5 million, up 5% YoY, or 13% excluding $1.8 million of hurricane-related BIASURGE sales, at the high end of guidance. Full-year revenue reached $103.1 million, up 19%, with gross margin expansion to 93% (up 200 bps) and adjusted EBITDA up 86% to $17 million. The company reaffirmed 2026 net revenue growth guidance of 13%–17% and highlighted a new Vizient Innovative Technology contract for BIASURGE, effective January 1, 2026, providing access to ~1,800 facilities.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue declined 15% YoY to $33M, driven by program consolidation and rationalization across SPL customers
Largest SPL customer reorganized supply chain causing inventory drawdowns of PAs and a reduction in midyear leases
Lost six active clinical programs during FY2025 with annualized revenue that will not recur
positive_highlights: Reduced annual cash burn by over $16M due to restructuring and cost-efficiency actions
Launched ExPERT DTX with early traction from beta users and initial sales in Q1
Received a seven-figure milestone payment from an SPL customer dosing patients in a pivotal study
summary: MaxCyte reported full-year FY2025 revenue of $33 million (down 15% YoY) and Q4 revenue of $7.3 million (down 16% YoY), driven by a largest customer's inventory drawdown, program rationalization across SPL partners including six discontinued programs, and reduced leases from manufacturing site reorganization. Management provided FY2026 guidance for total revenue between $30M-$32M ($25M-$27M core + ~$5M SPL), explicitly incorporating a near-term headwind of approximately $4 million in core revenue relative to 2025 levels before expecting stabilization and growth. The company highlighted the launch of ExPERT DTX, integration progress with SecurDx, reduced annual cash burn by over $16 million via restructuring, and receipt of seven-figure milestone payments.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $6.8 million in Q4, though improved from $9.7 million last year
Fourth quarter total revenue only up 0.8% due to store closures
Company closed 33 restaurants in 2025 and expects 30-35 more in 2026
positive_highlights: System-wide comp sales up 6.6% in Q4, accelerating to over 9% in Q1 2026
Adjusted EBITDA up over 88% in Q4, with 2026 guidance more than doubling prior year
Restaurant contribution margin expanded 290 basis points to 14.1% in 2025
summary: Noodles & Company reported Q4 2025 total revenue of $122.8 million, up 0.8% YoY, with system-wide comp sales up 6.6%. Restaurant contribution margin expanded to 14.1% from 11.2%, and adjusted EBITDA rose over 88% to $7.6 million. The company guided 2026 to comp sales of 6-9% and adjusted EBITDA of $30-35 million, more than double prior year, with early Q1 2026 comp trends over 9%. Management attributes momentum to portfolio optimization, menu innovation, and operational improvements.

negative_highlights: Rental income decreased to $11 million from $11.7 million due to lease expirations with Costco and Solar Turbines
AFFO per share declined from $0.37 to $0.32 driven by a $554,000 decrease in cash rents
Interest expense increased $1.1 million compared to the prior year period due to amortization of off-market interest rate swaps
positive_highlights: Interest received on noncore assets including a Kia dealership property at or below appraised cap rate
100% of indebtedness now fixed-rate following January 2026 interest rate swap agreements
$4 million AFFO maintained despite lower rental income
summary: Modiv Industrial reported Q4 FY2025 rental income of $11 million, a decrease from the prior year due to lease expirations with Costco and Solar Turbines. Adjusted Funds From Operations (AFFO) declined to $4 million ($0.32 per share), driven by lower cash rents partially offset by reduced interest expense and dividends. Management indicated that asset recycling activity will pick up in earnest during 2026, though the current M&A environment remains volatile with rates gyrating.

negative_highlights: Company remains pre-revenue with no commercial production of battery-grade lithium carbonate yet started.
Management explicitly declined to provide forward-looking guidance or estimates for the period.
Cash burn continues with net cash used in operating activities totaling $8.3 million.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $15.7 million from $23.8 million in the prior year due to lower financing charges and reduced general and administrative expenses.
Secured an air quality construction permit from ODEQ, allowing the project to proceed with construction and commissioning.
Completed FEL-3 engineering study and independent review by Black & Veatch validating low technical and design risk.
summary: Stardust Power reported a net loss of $15.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, an improvement from the prior year's $23.8 million loss driven by lower financing charges and reduced G&A expenses. The company remains pre-revenue with no commercial production yet started, holding $3.5 million in cash as of year-end. Management explicitly stated that no forward-looking guidance or estimates would be provided during the call.

negative_highlights: Treasury losses widened significantly to $36.8 million in Q4 compared to gains of $11.9M in Q3 due to HYPE price decline.
Adjusted EBITDA turned negative at -$38.9 million, down from +$8.0 million in the prior quarter.
Net cash used in operating activities increased to approximately $4 million as legacy items were streamlined.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross profit surged 87% QoQ from $439k in Q3 to $821k in Q4 as DeFi flywheel strategies matured.
Core operating expenses (ex-SBC) declined 30% quarter-over-quarter, dropping from $4.3M to $3.0M.
Announced a non-binding letter of intent to monetize the Optejet user-filled device in Q1 2026.
summary: Hyperion DeFi reported Q4 FY2025 adjusted gross profit of $821,000, an 87% quarter-over-quarter increase driven by ramping DeFi strategies like staking and validator commissions. However, the company recorded a GAAP net loss of $39.8 million due to significant treasury losses of $36.8 million as HYPE prices declined from ~$45 in Q3 to ~$25 at quarter-end. Management highlighted strong operational execution with core costs declining 30% and announced an LOI to monetize the Optejet life sciences asset, but provided no specific financial guidance for future quarters.

negative_highlights: Life Sciences Q4 revenues fell 24.4% to $3.1 million due to decreased unit sales at R2 in North America
Infrastructure gross margins compressed by approximately 350 basis points year-over-year to 14.7%
Spectrum segment revenue declined and faces a soft advertising environment extending through Q4
positive_highlights: Infrastructure revenue surged 65.7% YoY driven by increased activity on large commercial construction projects
Adjusted EBITDA for Q4 improved to $28 million from $17.4 million due to higher gross profit at DBMG and Banker Steel businesses
R2 segment achieved record full-year revenue of $12.5 million with a 123% surge in international demand
summary: INNOVATE reported Q4 FY2025 consolidated revenues of $382.7 million (up 61.7% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $24.5 million, driven primarily by a massive increase in the Infrastructure segment which grew revenue to $373.9 million. However, this growth was partially offset by significant declines in Life Sciences (-24.4%) and Spectrum segments due to inventory constraints at R2 and soft advertising environments respectively. Management noted gross margin compression of 350 bps year-over-year in the Infrastructure segment despite backlog expansion.

negative_highlights: Q4 Adjusted EBITDA loss widened slightly to -$76.1 million compared to -$67.6 million in the prior year quarter.
Full-year Medical Margin contracted significantly from $85.4 million (FY2024) to a loss of -$23.5 million, with Q4 medical margin at -$28.7 million versus +$7.3 million previously.
Total revenue for the full year declined 2.6% to $1.46 billion from $1.50 billion in FY2024.
positive_highlights: Normalized full-year Adjusted EBITDA improved by $44 million year-over-year to -$149.1 million driven by stronger contracting economics and structural cost actions.
Q4 Capitated Revenue PMPM increased 9% to $1,060 from $971 in the prior year quarter reflecting burden of illness documentation improvements.
Full-year operating expense decreased 9% on a comparable basis (excluding reclassification) due to structural cost actions and tighter discretionary spending controls.
summary: For Q4 FY2025 and the full year ended Dec 31, PIII reported total revenue of $384.8 million (Q4) and $1.46 billion (FY), representing a decline from prior periods due to membership mix changes despite higher per-member-per-month rates ($1,060 in Q4). Adjusted EBITDA losses narrowed year-over-year on a normalized basis (-$149.1M vs -$193.0M) but remained negative at -$76.1 million for the quarter and -$161.3 million for the full year. Management provided 2026 guidance of Adjusted EBITDA between -$20 million and $40 million (midpoint $10 million), citing structural improvements, contract renegotiations, and a new partnership adding 29,000 lives under management.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue of $5.2 million was seasonally light and down sharply from Q2's $18.4 million
Large fleet agreements may compress near-term margins
No formal 2026 revenue or EPS guidance provided
positive_highlights: Full-year 2025 revenue reached $46 million on 328 units, the highest ever
Generated $5.4 million positive free cash flow versus negative $49.1 million in 2024
Accounts receivable reduced to $6 million from $26.9 million, including $9.9 million UPS collection
summary: Xos reported Q4 2025 revenue of $5.2 million on 34 units delivered, with the balance of a 200+ unit UPS program recognized in future periods. Full-year 2025 revenue was $46 million on 328 units, up from prior years, with GAAP gross margin of 5.9%, operating loss narrowed 28% to $33.1 million, and positive free cash flow of $5.4 million versus negative $49.1 million in 2024. The company ended the year with $14 million in cash, down $26.9 million to $6 million in accounts receivable, and renegotiated its convertible note with Aldermay to quarterly installments through 2028. Management guided to expanding operations in 2026 with an upgraded hub product in three configurations, a growing powertrain business with Blue Bird, and continued focus on working capital and inventory turns, while being selective on ATM usage.

negative_highlights: No product revenue was recognized during FY2025 as dispensing had not yet commenced
Reported R&D expenses were $5.5 million but actual investment including grant offsets is higher, indicating heavy reliance on external funding for operations
DARE to PLAY prescriptions are currently in a pre-dispensing phase where orders exist but revenue recognition will only occur once the 503B outsourcing facility completes state licensing
positive_highlights: DARE to PLAY pre-fulfillment prescribing went live across all 50 states as of February 11, 2026 with telehealth access launched simultaneously
Received approximately $19.5 million in non-dilutive capital during FY2025 including grants from the Gates Foundation and ARPA-H to advance multiple programs without shareholder dilution
Ovaprene Phase III pivotal trial enrollment is expected to complete in 2026, positioning for a potential data readout in 2027
summary: Daré Bioscience reported full-year FY2025 revenue of $1.3 million and GAAP net loss of $(48) million with no EPS data provided due to lack of income statement details in the transcript text. The company disclosed a cash balance of approximately $24.7 million at year-end, supported by non-dilutive grants totaling roughly $19.5 million received during 2025. Management indicated that product revenue from DARE to PLAY and Flora Sync LF5 is expected to begin in Q2 2026 following the completion of state licensing for dispensing.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss for FY2025 was $8.5 million due to one-time non-cash debt fair value mark-to-market and extinguishment charges.
Management warned that full financial impact of cost reductions is not yet reflected in reported results, with meaningful progress expected only from Q2 2026 onward.
Q1 2026 revenue outlook remains lagged due to the demands of restructuring work completed in late 2025.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 32% sequentially and returned close to prior year levels despite operating with a significantly reduced team.
Gross margins expanded to 40% for FY2025 from 38%, driven by disciplined program structuring.
Pro forma cash basis EBITDA improved 31% YoY, including a 56% improvement in Q4 alone.
summary: Super League reported Q4 FY2025 revenue up 32% sequentially but noted that full-year results were impacted by significant one-time non-cash charges totaling $8.5 million related to debt restructuring and capitalization table changes, resulting in a GAAP net loss for the year. Management highlighted improved gross margins of 40% for FY2025 (up from 38%) and reduced pro forma cash basis OpEx by 29%, but explicitly stated that full financial benefits are not yet reflected due to ongoing restructuring lag effects expected through Q1-Q2 2026. The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire the Misfits Ads Division, which is pending stockholder approval.

negative_highlights: Company explicitly declined to provide financial guidance for R&D expenses in 2026, citing difficulty forecasting costs until trial reinitiation
No specific sample size or enrollment targets were disclosed for the amended VERSATILE-003 phase III trial
Net interest expense increased from $2.2 million to $4.1 million due to non-cash debt extinguishment and lower cash income
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed from $37.6 million in 2024 to $34.5 million in 2025
R&D expenses decreased by $3.6 million year-over-year, with manufacturing costs down $2.5 million and personnel costs down $1.8 million
VERSATILE-003 protocol amendment approved allowing PFS as an interim primary endpoint to potentially accelerate regulatory submission
summary: PDS Biotechnology reported a net loss of $34.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to a loss of $37.6 million in 2024, driven by R&D expenses of $19 million and G&A of $12.5 million against cash reserves of $26.7 million. Management highlighted clinical progress with the VERSATILE-003 protocol amendment approved by the FDA to use PFS as an interim primary endpoint, potentially shortening time to submission, but explicitly declined to provide financial guidance for 2026 or specific sample sizes due to trial complexity.

negative_highlights: GPMP-related-party gallons contracted significantly to 204 million in Q4 compared to 246.3 million last year due to winter storms and ongoing conversion of retail sites to dealers.
Full-year fuel contribution for GPMP declined from $51.2M to $43.2M as the volume contraction outweighed margin improvements on converted dealer locations.
positive_highlights: Wholesale fuel contribution grew 8% to $24.0M driven by a volume increase of ~4% and margin expansion from dealerization conversions totaling over 650 sites year-to-date.
Fleet fueling margins remained strong at 45.6 cents per gallon in Q4, benefiting from high diesel prices on cost-plus contracts where the company captures prompt pay discounts.
summary: ARKO Petroleum reported Q4 FY2025 net income of $8.1 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $36.9 million, representing a decline in full-year fuel contribution for the GPMP segment due to lower gallons sold at its related-party retail sites despite margin stability from dealerization conversions. Management provided 2026 guidance expecting approximately $156 million in Adjusted EBITDA and noted that recent Middle East volatility has increased costs by roughly $1/gallon, though they expect prompt pay discounts will offset some of this impact.

negative_highlights: Market cap at discount to treasury valuation
Crypto sector out of favor, impacting digital treasury companies
Earlier stage biotech funding scarce
positive_highlights: Net income of $1.23 billion and EPS of $25.48 for 2025
FDA clearance for Phase IIb knee osteoarthritis trial
Extended RAIN token option to Dec 31, 2027 at same price
summary: For full-year 2025, Enlivex reported net income of $1.23 billion and diluted EPS of $25.48, driven by appreciation in treasury assets tied to the Rain Protocol prediction markets token. The company entered a $21 million convertible debt financing, extended its Rain token option to 2027, and approved a $20 million buyback. Clinically, FDA cleared a Phase IIb trial in knee osteoarthritis, with top-line data expected in 2027.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell sharply by 36% from the prior year's $7.2 million due to deliberate exit of lower-quality contracts and customer churn.
Operating expenses increased despite a significant cut in sales and marketing, driven largely by a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $2.1 million.
Management explicitly stated they are not providing specific financial guidance for the upcoming fiscal year.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded five points year-over-year to 87% due to reduced cost of revenues and platform efficiency gains.
Subscription revenue quality improved significantly, now representing 98% of total revenue compared to 87% a year ago.
Cash balance strengthened to $11.1 million as of December 31, providing sufficient runway for six quarters.
summary: Total revenue declined 36% year-over-year to $4.6 million due to the exit of non-core contracts and churn during a strategic platform transition from SaaS to AI-native agentic solutions. Gross margin expanded structurally by five points to 87%, driven by disciplined cloud cost management, while operating expenses increased primarily due to a one-time goodwill impairment charge of $2.1 million. Management provided no specific financial guidance for FY2026 but expressed confidence in achieving double-digit growth once the transition is complete.

negative_highlights: Same-store sales dropped by 11.6% in Q4 due to customer retreat caused by immigration enforcement and reduced discretionary spending.
Cost of goods sold increased significantly, rising 285 basis points to 36.9% in the quarter.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA declined from $13.3 million in FY2024 to just $0.7 million in FY2025.
positive_highlights: CPG business expanded rapidly to over 800 locations in early 2026, projected to reach $100M annual run rate within three years.
Costco gift card sales reached approximately $29 million in FY2025, a 150% increase year-over-year.
CPG business achieved an initial 100% note-in rate from supermarket buyers with no turndowns reported.
summary: Q4 FY2025 revenue decreased to $49.7 million (down from $54.6M in Q4 2024) driven by an 11.6% same-store sales decline due to immigration enforcement and fuel price pressures, resulting in a net loss of $12.5 million ($0.36 diluted EPS). Management lowered full-year guidance for FY2026 to a range of $215-$225 million (down from prior expectations) while initiating a joint venture with Chubby Cattle International and accelerating its consumer packaged goods division.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $155 million for the year.
CEO transition and ongoing strategic review add uncertainty.
Operating leverage not yet visible due to onetime costs.
positive_highlights: Total revenues up 29% year-over-year to $255 million.
Management fees grew 9% to nearly $200 million; Q4 management fees up 14% YoY.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $35 million for the year.
summary: AlTi reported full-year 2025 total revenues of $255 million, up 29% year-over-year, with management fees near $200 million, up 9%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $35 million, but the company posted a GAAP net loss of $155 million, including a $35 million impairment in Q3. AUM reached $50 billion, up 10% year-over-year, aided by the Kontora acquisition. CEO Michael Tiedemann is stepping down, with Nancy Curtin as Interim CEO; a special committee continues evaluating strategic alternatives, and Allianz has filed a 13D. Management expects 2026 to show clearer operating leverage from zero-based budgeting and simplified operations.

negative_highlights: Full-year Adjusted EBITDA of ~$220M (pro forma) missed management's specific guidance range by approximately $20 million.
Q1 production is expected to decline to the low-23,000 BOE/d range due to planned shut-ins for reoccupying pads and offset frac activities.
Recent well performance showed declining initial rates in newer locations (Simpson ~500 BOE/d) compared to earlier performers like Opal Coal Bank (~725 BOE/d).
positive_highlights: Production of ~18,500 BOE/d (excluding Bayswater) met original full-year guidance range when adjusted to pro forma levels (~24,000 BOE/d).
Capital expenditures totaled $183.4 million, coming in significantly below the prior stated CapEx guidance.
Company achieved a 0.0 safety record for FY2025 with no incidents.
summary: Prairie Operating Company reported full-year FY2025 revenue of $242 million (excluding Bayswater) and Adjusted EBITDA of $156 million, both modestly missing pro forma guidance due to the exclusion of Q1 Bayswater volumes. While production exited at 28,000 BOE/d in line with original targets, management lowered full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance by approximately $90 million below the prior midpoint and provided a conservative free cash flow outlook for FY2026.

negative_highlights: Q4 system sales outside the U.S. dropped significantly, with only one sale compared to ten in Q4 FY2024
Gross margin contracted from 48% in FY2024 to 46% in FY2025 due to inflation and tariffs
International business expansion halted for nine months due to acquisition uncertainty
positive_highlights: Full-year procedure volume grew 22%, surpassing 206,000 globally
Recurring revenue increased 15% in FY2025 to $46.3 million annualized run rate
Company retained a $10 million transaction deposit and secured payment deferrals on remaining liabilities
summary: Q4 FY2025 revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $16 million due to lower system sales outside the U.S., while full-year recurring revenue grew 15%. The company terminated its acquisition by Alcon, retaining a $10 million escrow deposit and writing off approximately $9.3 million in unpaid merger-related costs. Management expects operating expenses for FY2026 to be roughly flat or up only ~10% from the normalized base after removing M&A transaction impacts.

negative_highlights: FY2025 revenue fell 12% to $6.1M
Gross margin declined to 77.5% from 81.4%
Net loss widened to $4.6M from $4.3M
positive_highlights: Q1 2026 revenue guided to $2.2M, up 37% YoY with better bottom-line improvement
Foreign bank renewed at over $1M for 2026, a ~30% increase
Cash up $2M+ to $2.7M and book value doubled to $7.6M
summary: BIO-key reported FY2025 revenue of $6.1 million, down 12% YoY, with hardware revenue more than doubling to $1.3 million and services up 6%. Net loss widened to $4.6 million but per-share improved to $0.69. Management guides Q1 2026 revenue to about $2.2 million, up 37% YoY, and expects to approach breakeven in early 2026. Key drivers include an expanded $1M+ renewal from a foreign bank, EMEA transition to branded solutions, and new product launches like EcoID III and PortalGuard 7.0.

negative_highlights: Cash and cash equivalents only $1.1 million at year-end
Revenue remains lumpy and company does not provide 2026 guidance
Operating expenses reduction driven partly by severance and fundamental shift away from R&D
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue up 133% YoY; full-year revenue up 40% to $1.7 million
First order for Nu.Q Cancer clinical certification; Nu.Q NETs inclusion in French government-backed $7.3 million DETECSEPS sepsis program
Two licensing agreements signed (Werfen and Hologic); $5 million feline milestone expected this year
summary: For full fiscal year 2025, VolitionRX reported $1.7 million in revenue, up 40% year-over-year, with Q4 revenue growing 133% year-over-year. Operating expenses decreased 17% to $4.8 million lower than 2024, and net cash used in operating activities fell 24% to $19.7 million. Cash at year-end was $1.1 million, but subsequent to year-end the company raised $5.4 million via ATM and $1.9 million via convertible note, plus received $2.3 million in non-dilutive funding. Management expects to collect a $5 million milestone payment from the feline cancer study and plans to cut cash operating expenses by another 25-30% during 2026. First commercial orders for Nu.Q Cancer and Nu.Q NETs were received, and licensing discussions with about 10 companies are ongoing.

negative_highlights: Q4 net revenue fell 41% year-over-year due to a $2.9 million reversal of terminated international license agreement
Weight loss business (Flat Tummy) continues to decline as the industry shifts toward GLP-1 products
Full-year income from operations dropped significantly, with normalized results still impacted by increased professional fees for corporate development
positive_highlights: Normalized gross margin excluding one-time charges expanded to 68.8% in Q4 compared to prior year
Beverage division generated over $2.5 million run-rate revenue for 2026 following successful Mexico subsidiary launch and Costco shipments
Cash position strengthened significantly with cash and equivalents rising from $687k at end of 2024 to $2.6M in Q4 2025
summary: Synergy CHC Corp reported a Q4 FY2025 net revenue of $6.07 million and a full-year revenue of $30.38 million, both representing significant year-over-year declines driven by the termination of an international license agreement ($2.9M reversal) and GLP-1 headwinds in weight loss products. Management highlighted that excluding one-time charges (bad debt write-offs, inventory obsolescence), normalized gross margins would have expanded to 68.8% for Q4 and $3 million income from operations was expected for the full year without these items. The company maintains a cautious outlook citing macro volatility in international markets while focusing on executing beverage growth initiatives in Mexico and restoring TV advertising.

negative_highlights: Q4 revenue missed significantly due to a challenging consumer spending environment causing lower case volume.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin contracted from 12% in FY2024 to 10%, reflecting the impact of prior year growth and current headwinds.
Cash flow from operations declined sharply to $3.1 million compared to $11.4 million in fiscal 2024.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales turned positive in February after being down 22% at the start of FY2025, indicating stabilization.
Gross margin expanded by roughly 2 percentage points to approximately 59%, driven by an $18.3 million decline in cost of services and a reduction in SG&A expenses of ~$5 million.
Company strengthened its balance sheet with cash at $8.4 million, gross debt reduced to $56 million via ATM proceeds and term loan paydowns.
summary: AirSculpt reported Q4 FY2025 revenue of $33.4 million, a decline of approximately 15% year-over-year driven by lower case volume and same-store sales down 16%. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.5 million with an expansion to roughly 7.4%, while full-year adjusted EBITDA margin contracted from 12% in FY2024 to 10% due to the revenue miss. Management provided a cautious outlook for fiscal 2026, guiding revenue between $151 million and $157 million (midpoint implying ~3% comparable growth) with adjusted EBITDA expected between $15 million and $17 million.

negative_highlights: Full year net revenue declined 14% to $206 million due to Agency weakness and lack of Political spend.
National revenue declined approximately 34% for the full year, with a 50% drop in Q4.
New business declined 14% for the full year and 18% in Q4.
positive_highlights: Digital revenue increased 21% on a same-station basis to approximately $49.5 million.
Digital operating margins expanded significantly to over 29% in Q4 2025 from 17.4% in Q4 2024.
Total debt is expected to be reduced from approximately $220 million to $110 million upon completion of the debt exchange by end of April.
summary: Full year net revenue declined to approximately $206 million from $240 million in 2024, driven by a $13.6 million absence of Political advertising and structural declines in Agency channels. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $10.5 million from $25.8 million, though Digital revenue grew 21% on a same-station basis to $49.5 million. Management raised Q1 2026 guidance expectations for stabilization, projecting same-station revenue down only in the mid-single digits compared to prior year.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined by 14.4% YoY as customers accelerated purchases ahead of anticipated trade policy shifts in Q4 2024

Net loss attributable to shareholders widened to $2.6 million from a net loss of $0.4 million, driven primarily by valuation allowance on deferred tax assets and non-recurring IPO-related compensation
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded by 210 basis points to 26.7% driven by better relative performance of higher-margin businesses
Operating loss improved significantly from $1.3 million in the prior year period to a GAAP operating loss of only $0.7 million due to optimized warehouse operations and lower R&D costs
summary: Fourth quarter revenue decreased by 14.4% to $30.5 million compared to the prior year due to order pull-forward effects and tariff headwinds impacting volumes in sanitaryware and shower systems businesses. Gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 26.7%, while GAAP operating loss narrowed from a loss of $1.3 million to $0.7 million, though net loss widened to $2.6 million due to non-recurring items including valuation allowances on deferred tax assets and IPO-related compensation.

negative_highlights: Loan growth expectations have slightly slowed down from robust levels seen previously due to sizable early payoffs.
Energy portfolio is at a 10-year low (over 8% of the portfolio) with limited dynamic change expected despite energy price spikes.
positive_highlights: Management stated goals for the year remain intact despite a slight slowdown in loan growth compared to Q3/Q4 of last year.
summary: Bank7 Corp reported Q1 FY2026 results where management expressed satisfaction with performance despite market expectations of rate cuts being replaced by potential increases due to Middle Eastern conflict and commodity prices. The company maintained its goal for moderate single-digit loan growth, noting a slight slowdown from the robust pace seen in late last year but expecting similar bookings this year. Net Interest Margin (NIM) is modeled between 440-445 basis points excluding fees, with fee income expected to revert to normalized levels of 28-35 bps.

negative_highlights: Dividends will not be paid this year to fund expansion CapEx plans.
Open pit life reduced by 100-130 meters, deferring underground mining of the Main Zone by at least five years.
Full-year CapEx is expected towards the upper end of guidance ($20 million).
positive_highlights: Gold production hit a quarterly record of just under 7,500 ounces.
Revenue exceeded $34 million with gross profit margins at 62%.
Adjusted EBITDA reached over $20 million in the quarter.
summary: TRX Gold reported a record quarter with gold production of just under 7,500 ounces and revenue exceeding $34 million driven by an average realized price of $4,655/oz. Adjusted EBITDA reached over $20 million for the quarter, while full-year guidance remains on track to produce between 25,000 and 30,000 ounces with cash costs guided at $1,400-$1,600/oz. Management confirmed that dividends will not be paid this year due to capital expenditure plans for plant expansion.

negative_highlights: Legacy VIP appliance revenue fell 18% to $6.5 million due to strategic pivot and increased discounts.
Net loss widened to $21.2 million, reflecting high upfront costs of the new business model.
Q4 revenue declined from Q3 levels due to unexpected provider attrition and lost doctor days.
positive_highlights: Full year revenue grew 16% despite the strategic pivot away from legacy VIP dentists.
Gross margin held steady at 60% despite significant cost increases from integration.
SCN operations are fully booked through April 2026 with in-network status secured for major payers.
summary: Full year 2025 revenue increased by $2.4 million (16%) driven by a $4.8 million rise in sleep testing services and $2.2 million in treatment revenue from the Sleep Center of Nevada acquisition, partially offset by a $1.4 million decline in legacy VIP appliance sales. Gross margin remained constant at 60%, while operating expenses surged to $30.4 million due to integration costs, resulting in a net loss of $21.2 million. Management noted Q4 revenue was lower than Q3 due to unexpected provider attrition and staffing challenges, though they expect significant improvement in Q1 and Q2 as new providers ramp up.

negative_highlights: Loan portfolio remained flat at $3 billion as customers refinance into secondary markets rather than growing the bank's book
Deposit balances declined slightly from year-end levels due to normal cash flow fluctuations and seasonality
New loan activity is described as 'mild' with new construction projects still ramping up slowly
positive_highlights: Net income increased $2.8 million (35%) YoY to $10.6 million
Net interest margin expanded 12 bps QoQ, with deposit costs declining 40 bps YoY
Credit quality remains pristine with no loans past due >30 days and watch list down 20% year-over-year
summary: West Bancorporation reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $10.6 million, a 35% increase from the prior year quarter driven by a 17% rise in net interest income and margin expansion of 12 basis points to previous quarters. Loan balances remained flat at $3 billion due to secondary market refinancing payoffs, while deposits saw normal seasonal fluctuations with about 75% remaining on a specific municipal bond deposit tranche from the prior year. Management maintained guidance for continued earnings improvement assuming steady Fed rates and expressed confidence in future loan growth as construction projects ramp up.

negative_highlights: Total revenue up only 0.3% YoY, below 4-8% guidance pace
Jafra Mexico revenue moderated due to productivity focus, associate base declined
Q1 had one fewer week, impacting reported growth; Betterware comparable growth 3.3%
positive_highlights: EBITDA grew 14% YoY, margin expanded 211 bps to 17.4%
Jafra US net revenue up 8.6% in USD, associate base up 3.4%
Tupperware transaction expected Q2 approval, immediately accretive ~40% to EPS
summary: BeFra reported flat revenue growth of 0.3% YoY, below the high end of its 4-8% full-year guidance, but delivered a 14% EBITDA increase with margin expanding 211 bps to 17.4% (18.4% ex-Tupperware expenses). Management highlighted improving associate trends at Betterware, strong Jafra US growth of 8.6% in USD, and the expected Q2 approval of the accretive Tupperware acquisition, which will add ~40% to EPS. They maintained full-year revenue growth guidance of 4-8%, with an expected inflection in Jafra Mexico starting in Q2.

negative_highlights: Operating profit declined to $3.4 million from $3.8 million
Advertising revenue slowed late Q1 due to geopolitical issues
EPS reduced by $0.13 due to member acquisition costs
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 5% year-over-year, with growth across all segments
Club member growth up 112% year-over-year
Expect membership fees to account for over 20% of revenue this year
summary: Q1 2026 revenue rose 5% YoY to $24.3 million, but operating profit fell to $3.4 million (14% of revenue) from $3.8 million, partly due to higher marketing spend on club member acquisition. The company guided for continued revenue growth and expects margins to recover as renewals grow, but noted a slowdown in advertising revenue late in Q1 due to the war and geopolitical uncertainty. Membership fees are expected to exceed 20% of revenue this year.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS declined to $0.30 from $0.92 YoY due to prior-year gain on deconsolidation
Mortgage revenue impacted by market volatility late in Q1, masking an otherwise blowout quarter
positive_highlights: Operating EPS up 126% YoY to $0.33, ROA doubled to 84 bps
Net interest margin expanded to 3.43% from 3.15% YoY, with expectations for further expansion
Revenue up ~34% YoY with only 4% OpEx growth, showing strong operating leverage
summary: Primis Financial reported Q1 FY2026 operating EPS of $0.33, up 126% from $0.14 in the year-ago quarter, with ROA improving to 84 bps from 40 bps. NIM expanded to 3.43% from 3.15%, and loans grew 11.7% YoY to $3.4B, with mortgage warehouse near $460M. Management highlighted strong operating leverage (revenue up 34%, OpEx up only 4%) and raised its mortgage production outlook to ~$1.8B for 2026, while guiding to further margin expansion and an aspirational 1% ROA by year-end.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined YoY due to higher operating expenses from executive team expansion, one-time corporate costs, and annual merit increases.
Q2 2026 EBITDA margin expected to be flat sequentially due to Phase I implementation costs for the landmark deal.
A $9.4 million charge will be recorded in Q2 related to accelerated vesting of executive restricted equity, including $2.8 million in cash bonus payments.
positive_highlights: TRCV increased 13% YoY to $152.1 million, an all-time high and the largest single-quarter increase in at least seven years.
Booking a landmark multi-year customer win (largest in company history) across multiple products, with phased implementation expected to be accretive to margins after Phase II go-live.
Gross retention rate reached its highest level in over seven years, and pipeline is up 41% YoY.
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $34.8 million, up 4% YoY, the first positive revenue growth since 2023. Total Recurring Contract Value (TRCV) rose 13% YoY to $152.1 million, and new sales bookings grew over 200% YoY, driven by the largest deal in company history. Adjusted EBITDA was $9.4 million (27% margin), up 230 bps sequentially, and adjusted EPS was $0.21, up $0.05 sequentially. Management expects Q2 EBITDA margin to remain flat sequentially due to implementation costs for the landmark deal, with margin expansion resuming in Q3, and reiterated a path to low-30s EBITDA margin in the midterm.

negative_highlights: Gross margin down 470 basis points to 36.5% due to higher tariffs
Adjusted EPS fell to $0.24 from $0.73 in the prior year
Georgia Boot saw slight single-digit decline, though timing-driven
positive_highlights: Q1 sales up 9.1% year-over-year to $124.4 million, in line with expectations
Retail sales increased 16.5% to $42.7 million
Best booking season ever noted across new spring and fall 2026 products
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q1 FY2026 sales of $124.4 million, up 9.1% year-over-year, in line with expectations. Gross margin fell 470 basis points to 36.5% due to over $7 million in higher tariffs, and adjusted EPS dropped to $0.24 from $0.73. The company reiterated full-year guidance of ~6% revenue growth, with tariffs expected to be a ~$10 million headwind split roughly 70/30 between Q1 and Q2. Management cited strong full-price watching, D2C growth, and improving wholesale trends, but noted tariff uncertainty ahead.

negative_highlights: Book value per share decreased to $9.97 from a prior level of $10.48, reflecting significant unrealized losses.
The company reported a GAAP net loss of approximately $8.7 million or $0.27 per share entirely driven by the investment portfolio's performance in March.
Commercial loan resolution is taking longer than anticipated, with some hotel assets expected to wrap up as late as 2027.
positive_highlights: EAD of $0.26 exceeded the newly increased dividend of $0.24 per share, demonstrating earnings resilience despite market volatility.
Arc Home delivered a meaningful contribution to EAD of approximately $0.04 per share driven by strong non-agency originations and improved gain on sale margins.
Serious delinquencies in the non-agency portfolio remain low at 1.3%, with home equity portfolios even lower at 0.4%.
summary: Book value per share declined 4.9% to $9.97 due to net unrealized losses of approximately $8.7 million driven by March macroeconomic volatility and widening spreads. Despite the GAAP miss on book value, Earnings Available for Distribution (EAD) increased to $0.26 per share, fully covering the raised quarterly dividend of $0.24. Management noted that at least 50% of the unrealized decline had already recovered by April.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 4.3% ex-divestiture, driven by lower print and agency volumes
Agency solution sales pulled back and project work shifting to AOR engagements
USPS rate increase expected up to 10% for Co-mail clients; European divestiture note payment past due
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted EPS up 25% year-over-year
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from 7.2% to 7.7%
Returned $7 million to shareholders including dividend increase of 33%
summary: Quad reported Q1 2026 net sales of $581 million, down 4.3% excluding the European divestiture, with adjusted EBITDA of $45 million versus $46 million a year ago and adjusted diluted EPS up 25% to $0.25. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 7.7% from 7.2% due to cost actions and productivity. Management maintained full-year guidance despite postage increases and a temporary ink surcharge, while noting free cash flow was negative $107 million in the quarter, and a $6 million payment from the European divestiture was past due.

negative_highlights: Fraud charge-off of $0.22 per share hit earnings
Net interest margin compressed due to rate cuts and high deposit costs
At-risk non-performing loans increased to $13.2M
positive_highlights: Loan originations up 56% YoY, 65% QoQ
SBA gain on sale margin 4.79% exceeded budget of 4%
April SBA sales already at $39.5M with $2M gain
summary: GBank reported Q1 FY2026 results impacted by a $0.22 per share charge-off related to third-party credit card fraud, which management attributes to bot attacks on a canceled retail card program. Despite this, loan originations surged 56% YoY to $208 million, surpassing $1 billion in on-balance-sheet loans, and SBA gain on sale margins reached 4.79% versus a 4% budget. Net interest margin compressed due to rate cuts and high deposit costs, but management expects improvement in Q2. The company continues to develop its gaming fintech platforms, including Bold Bets V2 and a new Bankroll joint venture.

negative_highlights: Cost of sales for tangible products rose significantly due to high upfront machine purchase costs in FY2025
Expansion into Southeast Asia faces challenges regarding language and culture barriers requiring local dealer partnerships
positive_highlights: Record high revenue of $19.1 million marking a 49% year-over-year increase
Gross profit increased by 45% to $4.3 million driven by SaaS channel fixed costs and kiosk demand
EBITDA margin expanded to 17.8% from the prior period
summary: Sagtec reported record revenue of $19.1 million in FY2025, representing a 49% year-over-year increase driven by service and product sales growth. Gross profit rose to $4.3 million (a 45% YoY increase) with EBITDA reaching $3.4 million on an expanded margin of 17.8%. Management discontinued the rental business model in favor of machine sales and SaaS, positioning for continued expansion into Southeast Asia markets like Indonesia.

negative_highlights: OEM revenue benefited from order timing that may affect Q2 reported revenue
R&D expenses increased 11% YoY due to pipeline investment
ORTHOVISC demand was lower than expected, offset by MONOVISC strength
positive_highlights: Commercial channel revenue grew 12% YoY, with Integrity U.S. procedures up 35% and over 3,000 cases
GAAP gross margin expanded 800 bps to 64% from 56%
Adjusted EBITDA increased by more than $4 million YoY to $4.3 million
summary: In Q1 FY2026, Anika reported total revenue of $29.6 million, up 13% year-over-year, with commercial channel revenue up 12% to $12.6 million and OEM revenue up 14% to $17 million. GAAP gross margin expanded to 64% from 56%, and adjusted EBITDA was $4.3 million, up more than $4 million year-over-year. The company maintained its full-year 2026 guidance for revenue of $114 million to $122.5 million and adjusted EBITDA margin of 5% to 10% of revenue, while completing its $15 million 10b5-1 share repurchase program.

negative_highlights: New lease change was lighter than expected at -1.1% for the quarter, offsetting strong retention.
Boston started the year challenging due to weather impacts in Cambridge around life science funding.
Seattle is trending below expectations as it works to absorb new deliveries from 2025.
positive_highlights: San Francisco and New York exceeded high expectations with strength from AI-driven demand and limited new supply.
summary: Equity Residential reported Q1 FY26 results that met expectations with same-store revenue in line and blended rate growth of 1.5%, though new lease change was lighter than anticipated at -1.1%. Management maintained full-year guidance for blends despite a slower start in Boston, Seattle, D.C., and L.A., while highlighting strong performance in San Francisco and New York driven by low supply deliveries.

negative_highlights: Adjusted sales down 7.3% YoY to $83.9 million
Elektron sales declined 14.8% due to lower volumes and timing
Cash from operations was an outflow of $4.1 million in the quarter
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 17% YoY to $0.27, ahead of expectations
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 220 bps to 14.7% despite lower sales
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to a midpoint of $1.17
summary: Luxfer reported Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.27, up 17% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 8.8% to $12.3 million and EBITDA margin up 220 basis points to 14.7%, despite sales down 7.3% to $83.9 million. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to a midpoint of $1.17, from a range of $1.12-$1.22, citing improved visibility and a strong start to the year. Management also outlined a credible path to robust double-digit earnings growth in 2027, driven by SCBA replacement, aerospace and defense strength, and operational initiatives.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 9% year-over-year, with U.S. down 7% and international down 12% (down 21% constant currency).
International revenue decline fully attributed to the absence of China distributor sales; Chinese registration renewal expected only in second half 2026.
Revenue guidance implies no meaningful China contribution in the back half, and return to growth is back-half loaded.
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 78% from 73% year-over-year, driven by lower distributor mix.
Excluding China, international revenue grew 22% year-over-year, up 9% constant currency.
Adjusted EBITDA loss (excluding restructuring) improved 18% year-over-year to $7 million.
summary: Pulmonx reported Q1 2026 revenue of $20.6 million, down 9% year-over-year and down 12% in constant currency, with U.S. revenue down 7% and international down 12% (or down 21% constant currency) due to the absence of China sales. The company reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $90-$92 million and expects a return to growth in the back half of the year. Gross margin improved to 78% from 73% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $7 million excluding restructuring charges, with a reduced cash burn outlook of about $23 million for the year. Management highlighted progress in restocking the U.S. sales team and advancing AeriSeal CONVERT II enrollment, while still navigating the Chinese registration renewal and ongoing execution challenges.

negative_highlights: Weather-related losses of $17.2 million were double the prior year quarter
Commercial lines segment posted an underwriting loss with a statutory combined ratio of 104.6%
Personal lines net premiums written declined 13.1% due to rate and exposure slowdowns
positive_highlights: Core loss ratio improved to 53.4% excluding specific loss components
Net investment income increased 19% year-over-year to $14.3 million
Personal lines real retention rate was healthy at 88.7%
summary: Net premiums earned decreased 4.9% to $221.4 million and net income fell to $11.5 million from $25.2 million in the prior year quarter, driven by weather-related losses of $17.2 million and large fire losses. Management explicitly stated that first quarter results did not meet expectations due to these unusual loss events, though core underlying performance remained solid.

negative_highlights: North American sales down 16% to $78M
Adjusted EBITDA swung to a loss of $371K from a gain of $354K
U.S. accounts remain cautious and tentative about the year
positive_highlights: International sales up 38% to $29M in Q1
Gross margin held at 33.4%
Board approved $0.25 per share dividend, cash up to $64M
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $170M, down 6% YoY, with North America down 16% and international up 38%. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $371K vs. a gain of $354K a year ago, reflecting margin pressure and tariffs. Management notes cautious U.S. retailers and expects to stay on track for full-year goals, while investing in new anime platform and 2027 launches.

negative_highlights: Q1 consolidated sales down 15% YoY; adjusted EBITDA down to $3.9 million from $14.4 million
Aluminum costs up 64% YoY, pressuring Arcadia margins
DynaEnergetics sales down 9% YoY; Middle East shipments delayed
positive_highlights: NobelClad backlog up 12% sequentially to $70.3 million, highest in more than 15 years
Q2 guidance implies sequential revenue and EBITDA growth across all three businesses
Architectural Billings Index for Western U.S. rose above 50 for first time since December 2024
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue fell 15% YoY to $135.6 million, with adjusted EBITDA down to $3.9 million from $14.4 million, reflecting macro challenges, aluminum cost inflation, and Middle East conflict disruptions. Q2 guidance of $148-$158 million sales and $6-$8 million EBITDA implies sequential improvement, but management cautions on persistent headwinds and uncertain macro environment. Order backlog at NobelClad rose 12% sequentially to $70.3 million, a 15-year high, and management cites early positive indicators in end markets, though improvement is expected only in the longer term.

negative_highlights: CEO noted that attritional loss ratios have been increasing year-over-year, primarily driven by mix shifts rather than underlying liability changes.
Management acknowledged competitive pressure intensifying in parts of the E&S market and admitted to walking away from large non-CAT accounts where rates were not right.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income surged to $25.6M from $8.5M YoY, driven by top-line growth and improved margins.
Combined ratio tightened significantly to 87.4% (from 90.9%) due to a loss ratio drop of 1 point to 58.8% and expense ratio improvement of 2.5 points.
Gross written premiums grew broadly with casualty up 27%, property up 13%, and net earned premiums rising 34%.
summary: Ategrity reported record Q1 FY26 results with gross written premiums growing 23% YoY to $478M and adjusted net income surging from $8.5M to $25.6M, driven by a combined ratio improvement to 87.4%. Management raised the full-year guidance range for direct premium growth (now expecting ~19-20%) while maintaining its Q2 outlook of approximately 20% above market and an underwriting margin in the high 80s.

negative_highlights: SaaS Adjusted EBITDA came in below guidance due to gross margin compression from strategic customer upgrades.
Marketing Services billings declined 33% YoY as legacy digital products are migrated to SaaS.
Full-year SaaS revenue growth is expected to be flat to slightly down before returning to top-line growth in 2027.
positive_highlights: SaaS revenue of $117M beat expectations with a 5% YoY increase.
Marketing Center grew approximately 30% year-over-year, validating the Market, note, and Grow strategy.
Quality customers now represent 70% of SaaS revenue, up from 62% a year ago.
summary: Thryv reported Q1 FY2026 SaaS revenue of $117 million (up 5% YoY) and Marketing Services revenue of $50.9 million, both beating guidance. Adjusted EBITDA beat for the quarter despite a deliberate near-term gross margin compression from upgrading legacy customers to the higher-margin SaaS platform. Management raised full-year SaaS revenue guidance to $463-471 million while maintaining other full-year targets.

negative_highlights: PPS volumes only grew 0.8% due to challenging distribution channel comparison
Adjusted EBITDA flat in constant currency for the quarter
Net leverage high at 4.7 times, with goal of 2.5-3 turns in 24 months
positive_highlights: Automation revenue increased 111% year-over-year, excluding FX
Gross margin improved 210 bps to 43.1% ex-warrants and depreciation
Revenue growth of 4.5% constant currency, with currency tailwinds adding 6.5 points
summary: Ranpak's Q1 2026 revenue grew 4.5% constant currency (5.4% ex-warrants), with automation up 111% and PPS volumes up 0.8%. Adjusted EBITDA was flat constant currency, up 5% ex-warrants, and up 9.2% reported. Management expects 200 bps gross margin improvement for the year and automation revenue near $60 million, with a path to $100 million. They are implementing a temporary surcharge in Europe to offset paper price increases while remaining confident in the growth strategy.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 9% due to event timing shifts (approx. half the decline) and lower new boat unit volumes.
Net loss widened significantly from a prior year net loss of $375,000 to $13 million.
Industry retail demand remains pressured with SSI data indicating double-digit declines in competitive categories.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 110 basis points to 23.9% driven by portfolio optimization and favorable mix.
Pre-owned revenue increased 5% supported by improved availability in a disciplined pricing environment.
Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improved sequentially and year-over-year to 4.1x following $57M of debt repayment.
summary: Revenue declined 9% year-over-year to $442 million driven by a timing shift from the Palm Beach International Boat Show and lower new boat volumes, while pre-owned revenue increased 5%. Gross margin expanded 110 basis points to 23.9%, but SG&A expenses rose as a percentage of sales due to the revenue drop. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($60M-$80M) and EPS ($0.20-$0.70), citing industry headwinds, potential macro noise (e.g., fuel prices), and uncertainty about consumer confidence.

negative_highlights: SBA loan production seasonally light with lower gain on sale revenue
Net charge-offs in franchise finance remained elevated
Management expects higher hold on SBA loans, reducing gain on sale fee income
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 21% YoY to $43.1 million
Net interest margin expanded 54 bps YoY to 2.45% FTE
SBA delinquencies improved 118 bps QoQ
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q1 2026 net income of $2.5 million ($0.29 per share), with total revenue of $43.1 million, up 21% YoY. Net interest income rose 26% YoY, and fully taxable equivalent net interest margin expanded 54 basis points YoY to 2.45%. Pre-provision net revenue grew 51% YoY to $18.1 million. Credit trends improved, with SBA delinquencies down 118 bps QoQ. Management reaffirmed full-year fee income guidance of $33-35 million and expects profitability to improve, targeting a return to 1% ROA by end of 2027.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 34.3% year-over-year due to a decline in active earning coaches down 44.9%.
Gross profit margin contracted to 68.1% from 72.8% due to lower sales volumes and loss of leverage on fixed costs.
Loss from operations increased to $3.3 million, with losses per share widening to $0.19.
positive_highlights: First sequential quarterly revenue growth in three years.
Second consecutive quarter of year-over-year coach productivity gains, up 19% YoY and 16% sequentially.
Record high percentage of new clients coming from referrals in March.
summary: First quarter 2026 revenue was $76.0 million, a decrease of 34.3% year-over-year, while EPS loss narrowed to $0.19 per share from $0.07 in the prior year period. Management reported its first sequential quarterly revenue growth in three years and a second consecutive quarter of year-over-year coach productivity gains (up 19% YoY). The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $270-$300 million revenue and expects to return to profitability starting in the fourth quarter of 2026.

negative_highlights: Development services revenue showed significant pull-forward activity, suggesting the remainder of the year may be slower
Net loss widened to $7.8 million due to planned commercial organization expansion and R&D investment for clinical studies
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 42% year-over-year to $25.6 million
Gross margin expanded 300 basis points year-over-year to 84%
Full-year guidance raised with a new midpoint of $109 million representing 25% growth over 2025
summary: Biodesix reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $25.6 million, a 42% year-over-year increase driven by 37% growth in diagnostic testing and near-doubling development services revenue. Gross margin expanded to 84%, excluding one-time tax recoveries which were 82%. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance range from the prior $105M-$111M (implied) to a new midpoint of $109 million, citing strong Q1 performance and continued commercial expansion.

negative_highlights: Total revenues fell 11% YoY to $100.0 million
Non-GAAP gross margin dropped to 29.4% from 35.8% a year ago
FY2026 guidance lowered for both revenue and adjusted EBITDA
positive_highlights: Maintained trailing 12-month book-to-bill ratio greater than 1.0
Lowered inventories by $4.0 million sequentially and unbilled receivables for second consecutive quarter
Potential release of foreign valuation allowance within next four quarters could create one-time GAAP income benefit
summary: Aviat Networks reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $100.0 million, down from $112.6 million a year ago, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.06 and adjusted EBITDA of $4.4 million. Results were hurt by roughly $9 million in Middle East conflict-related project pushouts and demand shifts. The company lowered full-year revenue guidance to $428-$440 million and adjusted EBITDA to $35-$40 million, but expects Q4 revenue normalization and flagged growth drivers like MDU, utilities, and BEAD for potential FY2027 contribution.

negative_highlights: Total company sales declined less than 2% year-over-year
Paid subscribers dropped 13,000 sequentially from Q4 2025
Gross margin pressured by tariffs, end-of-life impairments, and lower excess inventory monetization
positive_highlights: Platform revenue increased nearly 6% to almost $84.8 million
Paid subscribers up over 3% year-over-year to almost 3.08 million
Global machine note-out units grew year-over-year
summary: Cricut's Q1 FY2026 revenue declined less than 2% year-over-year, with platform revenue up nearly 6% to almost $84.8 million and paid subscribers up over 3% to almost 3.08 million, though sequentially down 13,000. The company launched new machines (Joy 2, Explore 5) and its first service (DTF), with encouraging early adoption and active users up 1%. Gross margin faced headwinds from end-of-life inventory impairments, tariff costs (now ~10% average impact), and lower monetization of excess inventory, while international revenue grew 16% (10 points from FX). Management expects a challenging environment but remains focused on innovation, bundle strategy, and cost discipline.

negative_highlights: Net income declined sharply by 57% YoY due to one-time integration costs of $3M.
Prepaid Solutions segment revenue fell 17%, dragging overall gross margins down from 33.2% to 30.0%.
Q2 Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be slightly lower than the prior year period due to timing of investment spending.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 20% YoY to $147M, led by a 35% surge in secure card solutions including Arroweye.
Free cash flow jumped significantly from $0.3 million last year to $10.1 million this quarter.
Contactless metal and closed-loop prepaid segments showed strong growth.
summary: CPI Card Group reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $147 million, a 20% increase year-over-year driven by secure card solutions and Arroweye, while the prepaid segment declined 17%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 9%, but net income fell 57% due to $3 million in pre-tax integration costs. Management affirmed full-year guidance for high single-digit revenue growth despite Q2 expectations being slightly lower than prior year.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue down 12% and EPS down to $0.22 from $1.07
HDMC gross margin down 380 basis points to 25.3% due to tariffs and pricing
HDMC operating income down to $19M from $116M year-over-year
positive_highlights: North America retail sales up 14% with U.S. up 16% and market share up 2 points to 38%
Global dealer inventory down 22% year-over-year, with current model-year mix improved
Full-year tariff guidance improved to $75M-$90M from prior quarter
summary: Q1 2026 revenue down 12% and EPS down to $0.22 from $1.07, driven by HDFS transition and HDMC tariff costs of $45M. Global retail sales up 8% with North America up 14%, but international down 4%. Management lowered full-year tariff guidance to $75M-$90M, raised 2027 cost savings target to $150M+, and expects improved shipment cadence in Q2 and Q4.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 7% year-over-year primarily due to lower volume mix, with North American sales dropping significantly
Price-cost dynamics remained a negative factor of roughly $21 million as inflation in freight and energy prices was not fully offset by pricing increases
Operating cash flow showed a use of cash for the quarter driven by working capital needs typical of Q1 seasonality
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined only to 0.9% despite a significant volume drop due to strong year-over-year productivity improvements of $22 million
On-Time In-Full (OTIF) delivery rates improved significantly, moving above 90%, indicating better execution and customer service recovery
North America core revenue decline narrowed from the prior quarter's expectation as share loss headwinds reduced by approximately $30 million
summary: First quarter net revenue was $722 million, down 7% year-over-year driven by lower volume mix and a negative price-cost dynamic of approximately $21 million headwind. Adjusted EBITDA declined to $6 million from $22 million in the prior year period as inflationary pressures on freight and materials outweighed productivity gains. Management raised full-year revenue guidance slightly while holding Adjusted EBITDA expectations unchanged, citing improved service levels but acknowledging persistent macro softness.
