negative_highlights: Net premium earned decreased year-over-year due to average account rate decreases in a softening market
Other income declined by $900,000 driven by non-recurring items present in the prior year
Management cautioned that using Q1 results alone is premature for revising full-year guidance given H2 volatility
positive_highlights: Net income of $19.3 million with a combined ratio of 66% in line with targets
Account retention remained within the target low-to-mid-80s range after bouncing back from January walkaways
Core catastrophe reinsurance program renewal secured risk-adjusted cost decreases and increased exhaustion point to over $1.6 billion
summary: American Coastal Insurance Corporation reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $19.3 million and a combined ratio of 66%, which was an increase from the prior year but in line with management's target range. Revenue guidance for the full year remains unchanged, though management noted that H2 results will be critical to meeting these estimates given softening market conditions on the front end. The company highlighted strong retention within its targeted range and successful reinsurance renewals despite losing some premium rates.

negative_highlights: Adjusted pre-tax loss of $6 million, down from prior year income levels due to higher MSR runoff and servicing impacts.
Servicing income declined by $54 million versus the prior year driven by record prepayments and FHA delinquency issues.
Refinancing response exceeded predictions, preventing realization of an estimated $8-14 million in adjusted pre-tax income due to staffing capacity limits.
positive_highlights: Adjusted revenue grew double-digit year-over-year at +26% driven by strong origination volume growth of nearly 4x in consumer direct.
Subservicing additions surged up 94% versus the prior year, with total servicing UPB growing 11% YoY to $338 billion.
Management identified specific incremental adjusted pre-tax income improvement opportunities totaling approximately $27 million for future quarters.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 2% year-over-year and 4% quarter-over-quarter due to a subdued hiring environment with quits rates at lowest levels since 2015.
Revenue per paid employer fell 2% YoY ($1,698) as the number of quarterly paid employers remained flat despite seasonal sequential growth.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA came in at $9.7 million, exceeding the high end of guidance and expanding margin from 5% YoY to 9% sequentially driven by efficient marketing spend.
New AI search engine drove a 37% increase in application volume for exposed job seekers within Q1.
Enterprise segment revenue grew 5% year-over-year, doubling its share of total revenue compared to pre-COVID levels.
summary: ZipRecruiter reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $107.5 million (a decline) and Adjusted EBITDA of $9.7 million, beating the high end of guidance despite a soft hiring backdrop with job openings down 3% YoY. Management raised full-year outlook expectations to flat top-line growth in 2026 compared to declines previously expected, citing operational efficiency gains that pushed Q1 margins above the upper range of their forecast.

negative_highlights: Consolidated commission income decreased year-over-year due to the divestiture of certain non-core operations in 2025
EBITDA turned negative at -$0.4 million compared with positive EBITDA of $0.1 million in the prior period
positive_highlights: Retained insurance businesses achieved 11% organic revenue growth despite portfolio realignment
Balance sheet strengthened with unrestricted cash increasing to $2.3 million and stockholders' equity rising to $7.4 million
summary: Commission income declined to $3.8 million from $4.2 million in the prior year period due to a divestiture of non-core operations, though retained businesses showed 11% organic growth. Net loss narrowed slightly to $1.4 million compared with $1.7 million previously, driven by lower operating expenses and reduced interest costs. Management highlighted balance sheet improvements but provided no specific financial guidance for the next quarter.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined sequentially from $59.9 million in Q4 2025 due to a $7.9 million inventory drawdown and lower demand.
Royalty revenue fell significantly to $2.8 million compared to $15.6 million in the prior quarter, driven by lack of large China shipments.
Demand decreased approximately 6% quarter-over-quarter despite year-over-year growth.
positive_highlights: Full-year guidance raised for both net NERLYNX product revenue (to $202-$206 million) and net income (to $16-$19 million).
New prescriptions increased approximately 25% quarter-over-quarter, indicating underlying demand growth.
Company is now debt-free after making its final payment to Athyrium.
summary: Puma Biotechnology reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $44.8 million ($42M product net), which declined from the prior quarter due to a $7.9 million inventory drawdown and lower demand, though new prescriptions rose 25% year-over-year. Management raised full-year guidance for net NERLYNX product revenue (now $202-206M vs previous $194-198M) and net income ($16-19M), but the quarter itself was a miss on sequential growth driven by inventory normalization.

negative_highlights: One new mobile hotspot model launch delayed into late June due to engineering issues persisting into Q2, impacting quarterly outlook.
FWA revenue declined sequentially as a specific large customer overhauled its executive team and changed go-to-market approach.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA expected to be lower sequentially due to increased investment in sales, marketing, and R&D before second-half profitability improves.
positive_highlights: Q1 results delivered within the guided range with healthy gross margins at 48.9%.
Announced a transformational acquisition of Nokia's FWA business valued at $20 million, which more than doubles revenue size and provides immediate global scale.
Secured commitments for next-generation FWA platforms from existing large customers despite near-term disruption.
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $34.3 million with adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 million at the higher end of guidance. Management noted a sequential decline in FWA revenue due to customer executive changes and persistent delays on one mobile hotspot model impacting Q2 outlook, though they remain positive on full-year targets including an acquisition that will double company scale.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 6% year-over-year
Paid active member count decreased 4% year-over-year
New Expensify performance is not yet fast enough for larger customers seeking migration
positive_highlights: Interchange revenue increased 10% year-over-year to $5.5 million
Free cash flow generated was $2.5 million (excluding a one-time legal payment)
April paid active members rose to 641,000 from the Q1 average of 632,000
summary: Expensify reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $34 million, down 6% year-over-year, with paid active members declining to an average of 632,000 (down 4%). Management reiterated full-year free cash flow guidance at $6-$9 million and noted a one-time legal payment reduced the quarter's reported FCF from roughly $5 million. While April saw member count improvement to 641,000 and interchange revenue grew 10% YoY, management emphasized performance issues in New Expensify are delaying migration of larger customers.

negative_highlights: Virtual Sports growth remains flat as headwinds in Brazil offset gains from other regions
U.K. Interactive revenue faced a tax rate increase from 21% to 40%, though still grew >10%
BetMGM integration results in New Jersey described as 'mixed bag' and below initial hopes
positive_highlights: Continuing revenue grew 15% YoY to $57 million driven by a 38% surge in Interactive segment
Adjusted EBITDA expanded 29% with margin improvement of 1,100 bps after restructuring adjustments
Generated approximately $60 million in free cash flow used for debt paydown and share buybacks
summary: Continuing revenue grew by 15% year-over-year to $57 million in Q1 FY26, driven primarily by a 38% increase in the Interactive segment and strong retail performance despite U.K. tax rate hikes offsetting growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose 29%, expanding margins by 1,100 basis points after adjusting for one-time restructuring impacts from divesting holiday parks and restructing pubs. Management raised adjusted EBITDA margin guidance while maintaining revenue expectations, citing steady sequential trends post-seasonality removal.

negative_highlights: Management withdrew full-year earnings guidance citing a focus on portfolio transition rather than performance issues
Monthly distribution reduced to $0.16 per share starting July, lowering annual run rate to $1.92
positive_highlights: Same-store cash NOI increased 3.2% year-over-year
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA decreased by 0.4 times from the prior quarter
Secured $100 million strategic investment and board seat with Maewyn Capital Partners
summary: Chiron Real Estate reported Q1 FY2026 with Net redefined FFO of $0.97 per share and Core FFO of $1.11 per share, while Same-store cash NOI increased 3.2% year-over-year. Management withdrew its full-year earnings guidance to better focus on the strategic transition toward senior housing rather than due to negative performance events. The company reduced its monthly distribution run rate to $0.16 per share starting in July to retain capital for growth investments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 10% YoY
Behavioral subscribers declined 25% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.8 million in Q1
positive_highlights: Clinical subscription revenue grew 32% YoY and clinical subscribers grew 46% YoY
Core+ subscribers grew 6% YoY, first growth in years
Adjusted gross margin near record at 73.6%
summary: In Q1 2026, WeightWatchers reported revenue of $168 million, down 10% year-over-year, with clinical subscription revenue up 32% and behavioral subscription revenue down 17%. End-of-period clinical subscribers grew 46% year-over-year and 51% sequentially to 197,000, while total behavioral subscribers fell 25% to 2.5 million, though Core+ grew 6% to 537,000. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $1.8 million, but the company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $620-$635 million revenue and $105-$115 million adjusted EBITDA, and expects cash generation. Management highlighted the strategic investment in Med+ marketing during the Wegovy pill launch, which drove a 10-point increase in GLP-1 awareness, and expects clinical subscriber growth to continue but at a slower sequential pace.

negative_highlights: New program starts in the quarter were softer than expected, though management characterized this as standard fluctuations rather than a trend.
A one-time non-cash write-off of $2.9M related to legacy small molecule ion channel and tangible assets impacted GAAP operating expenses.
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased significantly year-over-year from $4.2M to $14.4M driven by higher milestones.
Operating expenses decreased slightly to $22.3M, excluding a one-time non-cash write-off of $2.9M related to legacy assets.
Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance from prior expectations due to strong Q1 performance and an unanticipated milestone.
summary: OmniAb reported Q1 FY26 revenue of $14.4 million (up from $4.2M in Q1 FY25) driven by milestone payments and service revenue growth, while operating expenses decreased to $22.3 million excluding a one-time non-cash write-off of $2.9 million. Management raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to a range of $28-$33 million due to the strong Q1 performance and an unexpected milestone achievement by a partner, while keeping cash operating expense guidance unchanged at $50-$55 million.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue dropped sharply by $10.1 million year-over-year due to a largest material handling customer implementing a capital freeze.
Gross margin contracted significantly from 32% in the prior year period to 27.3% driven by lower volumes and higher unabsorbed labor/overhead.
Net loss widened to $3.2 million ($0.15/share) compared to a net loss of $1.9 million ($0.12/share) in Q3 FY2025.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses declined significantly to $4.8 million from $6.9 million prior year due to efficiency actions and headcount reduction.
Flux Power won the Innovation in Sustainability Award at MODEX for its holistic energy lifecycle management solution.
Management expects sequential revenue growth of approximately 20% in Q4 following a return to normal order activity.
summary: Third quarter revenue fell to $6.6 million from $16.7 million a year ago due to a major customer's capital freeze and geopolitical headwinds. Gross margin contracted to 27.3% from 32%, while operating expenses decreased by 30% YoY following cost-cutting measures including headcount reductions. Management provided no specific financial guidance but indicated an expectation of approximately 20% sequential revenue growth in the fourth quarter.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed prior guidance expectations, which had called for a total revenue decline of approximately 50% YoY.
Gross margin contracted significantly from 73% last year to 29%, impacted by inventory write-downs and regulatory changes.
Operating loss widened substantially to $68.9 million compared to an operating loss of $26.7 million in the prior period.
positive_highlights: Company enhanced market share position as unit volume outperformed industry declines despite significant headwinds.
Completed BLA submission for ReNu program, advancing the pipeline with a new regenerative therapy for knee osteoarthritis.
PuraPly AM trial achieved primary endpoint demonstrating statistically significant wound closure at 12 weeks (p < 0.0477).
summary: Net revenue declined 58% year-over-year to $36.3 million in Q1 FY2026, driven by a 63% drop in advanced wound care sales due to market disruption and CMS commentary on product wastage. Management updated its full-year 2026 guidance downward from a prior decline range of 25%-38% YoY to an expected revenue decline of 45%-52%, citing a more prolonged recovery timeline than previously anticipated.

negative_highlights: Gas netbacks remain weak due to Waha-Henry Hub dislocation
Wrote off 18 wells in the red box area, will not drill there
Back half production likely flat, relying on base optimization
positive_highlights: Production averaged ~46,000 BOE/d, ~7.5% above guidance midpoint
LOE per BOE came in 17%+ below guide and ~22% below Q4
Generated $21M+ FCF excluding working capital, up from -$42M last quarter
summary: HighPeak Energy reported strong Q1 FY2026 results, with production averaging 46,000 BOE/d, about 7.5% above guidance midpoint, and oil production up 10% quarter-over-quarter. LOE per BOE came in more than 17% below guidance and roughly 22% below Q4 levels, while capital spending was about 29% of the full-year budget. The company generated over $21 million of free cash flow excluding working capital changes, and it maintains its maintenance-mode strategy with 2026 capital at roughly $270 million midpoint, expecting flat production for the year. Management expressed confidence in continued efficiency gains and upside to spot pricing given 40% exposure to spot oil.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $0.05 per share with comprehensive loss reaching $0.12 per share due to mark-to-market adjustments
Book value declined 6.1% quarter-over-quarter driven by March volatility and widening spreads
Economic return was negative at -3.2%, offsetting January gains from spread tightening
positive_highlights: Strategic partnership investment with Real Genius continues to progress in line with expectations
MSR portfolio valuation improved, demonstrating resilience despite the challenging environment
RMBS net interest spread expanded to 2.9% driven by reduced repo costs and dollar roll income
summary: Cherry Hill reported a GAAP net loss of $0.05 per diluted share and an economic return of -3.2% for Q1 FY26 due to geopolitical volatility widening mortgage spreads in March. Book value declined by 6.1% (down $7.9M) from year-end, though it recovered nearly 2% post-quarter end as April spread softening began. Management maintains a solid liquidity profile with $47 million cash and expects continued market turbulence until Middle East stability is achieved.

negative_highlights: Cash decreased to $65.1 million from $78.2 million at end of 2025
Revenue guidance unchanged at $72-$76 million with second-half weighting
No new major partnership or licensing deal closed in the quarter
positive_highlights: Total revenues of $15.2 million in Q1 2026, up from $7.5 million in Q1 2025
Product gross margin expanded to 71% from 55%
Net loss reduced to $8.7 million from $20.7 million
summary: Codexis reported Q1 2026 total revenues of $15.2 million, up from $7.5 million in Q1 2025, driven primarily by the fully recognized Merck Technology Transfer Agreement. Product gross margin improved to 71% from 55%, and net loss narrowed to $8.7 million from $20.7 million. The company reiterated its 2026 revenue guidance of $72-$76 million, with revenue expected to be weighted to the second half. Management highlighted progress in its ECO Synthesis platform, including new stereochemistry control, over 50 opportunities in the sales pipeline, and ongoing CDMO partnerships, with a goal to sign a licensing deal with a major pharma company in the back half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance remains unchanged despite strong quarter, implying the tower sale proceeds will not be used for growth investments this year.
Net cash from operating activities decreased by approximately $6 million compared to the prior year due to higher working capital requirements related to government program payments timing.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew nearly 2% year-over-year to $182 million driven by business and carrier services growth.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly, improving 200 basis points to 26.7% from the prior year period.
Net loss narrowed substantially to a $3 million loss ($0.29/share) compared to a $9 million loss in Q1 last year.
summary: ATN reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $182 million (up ~2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $49 million (up 10%), with a net loss narrowing to $3 million. Management reiterated the full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance range of $190-$200 million, noting that this excludes approximately $6-8 million in expected reductions following an anticipated tower sale closing in Q2.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA down 15% to $11.7 million
Net loss widened to $18.1 million from $15.1 million
Wavelo gross profit and EBITDA declined due to sales and marketing investment
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue up 2% to $96.7 million, gross profit up 2.5%
Ting revenue up 19%, adjusted EBITDA loss improved 50% year-over-year
Return to positive operating cash flow of $3.5 million
summary: Tucows reported Q1 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $96.7 million, up 2% year-over-year, with gross profit up 2.5%. Adjusted EBITDA fell 15% to $11.7 million, and GAAP net loss widened to $18.1 million. Domains revenue declined 2% but gross profit and adjusted EBITDA grew; Ting revenue surged 19% with adjusted EBITDA loss cut by 50%; Wavelo revenue was flat but EBITDA declined due to go-to-market investments. The company returned to positive operating cash flow of $3.5 million and remains in covenant compliance. Guidance was not provided, but the Radix migration is expected to benefit Q2, and legacy mobile headwinds persist.

negative_highlights: Q1 results came in below internal expectations, driven by longer producer turnaround and lower Shenandoah rates
Shenandoah 2026 segment margin revised down by $12-15 million versus original guidance
Increasing noneconomic Chinese flake NaHS competition in South American markets
positive_highlights: Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA reaffirmed at or near midpoint, growth of 15-20% over ~$500-510M baseline
Financing cost reduced by ~$12 million annually with balance sheet actions completed during the quarter
Multiple new wells and tiebacks (Monument, Shenandoah South, Tiberius) expected to flow through Genesis infrastructure with no capital
summary: Q1 2026 results came in slightly below internal expectations due to longer-than-expected producer turnarounds and lower-than-anticipated Shenandoah volumes, but other segments met expectations. Management revised Shenandoah 2026 segment margin down by $12-15 million but reaffirmed full-year Adjusted EBITDA at or near the midpoint of prior guidance (~$500-510M baseline, 15-20% growth). Balance sheet actions—new 6.75% notes, redemption of 7.75% notes, upsized revolver, $135M preferred buyback—reduce annual financing costs by ~$12 million. Long-term outlook remains positive with multiple development projects and no required capital.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 1.6% YoY and Adjusted EBITDA dropped significantly due to a $10 million unplanned cost headwind from March.
Underlying market demand is down, tracking with SAAR which fell approximately 5% versus Q1 FY25.
Supply constraints are driven by financial pressure on smaller carriers exiting the market and driver attrition.
positive_highlights: Company delivered a market share gain despite being down less than the industry average in terms of units delivered.
Spot participation increased by a couple percentage points with rate premiums better than recent quarters during March volume recovery.
Management expects Q2 revenue to reflect meaningful sequential increases as fuel surcharge index adjustments normalize.
summary: Total operating revenue for Q1 FY26 was $937 million (decreased 1.6% YoY), while Adjusted EBITDA fell to $45 million from $78 million in the prior year quarter due to a material unplanned cost headwind of approximately $10 million caused by higher fuel costs and timing lags on surcharge recoveries. Management expressed clear disappointment with the results, citing extended plant shutdowns, weak SAAR (down ~5%), severe winter weather, and supply constraints as primary drivers that muted underlying efficiency improvements.

negative_highlights: Reported net loss widened to $6.9 million due to a $2.1 million litigation settlement and associated legal fees
New MGA investments reduced EBITDA by approximately $1.1 million in the quarter compared to $0.6 million prior year
Property lines are softening with rate declines observed, particularly in large/middle market accounts
positive_highlights: Insurance distribution segment revenue grew 92% YoY driven by organic growth of 42% and ArmadaCare acquisition
Adjusted EBITDA increased nearly four-fold to $25.3 million with margins expanding to record highs of 32.3%
Corporate nominal expenses declined significantly from $15 million last year to just over $12 million
summary: Octave Specialty Group reported Q1 FY2026 results with total revenue growing 92% to $78.5 million for the insurance distribution segment, driven by a 42% organic increase and the October 2025 acquisition of ArmadaCare. Adjusted EBITDA surged nearly four-fold to $25.3 million as margins expanded to record highs of 32.3%, though reported net loss was $6.9 million due to litigation settlements at Everspan. Management noted Q1 execution exceeded initial expectations but stated guidance for the full year remains unchanged.

negative_highlights: GAAP revenue declined by approximately $1 million due to a restructuring of the GE HealthCare contract that reduced quarterly rental revenues.
Device Solutions segment net revenue decreased by $2.3M (down 17%), with nearly 70% attributable to the GE HealthCare transition and lower equipment sales/rentals from customer buyouts.
Operating cash flow dropped significantly year-over-year, generating only $970k compared to prior year levels due to higher working capital increases.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded modestly from 18.2% to 18.9% despite lower net revenue due to favorable trade-offs between GE HealthCare restructuring and field service projects.
Wound care segment grew nearly 112% year-over-year, driven by a new compression device supplier adding adjustable wraps for patients with limited mobility.
Successfully cleared the go-live hurdle for the new enterprise resource planning (ERP) system on March 1st, integrating data and workflows across business lines.
summary: InfuSystem reported Q1 FY26 revenue of $33.7 million, a GAAP decline of ~$1M driven by the restructuring of its GE HealthCare biomedical services contract which reduced revenue by $1.6M; however, pro forma revenue grew 1.7% and adjusted EBITDA was approximately $6.4M (GAAP) or $6.3M per CFO figures), in line with prior year despite lower top-line growth. Management raised full-year guidance to a range of 6%-8% annualized pro forma revenue growth, citing the successful go-live of their new ERP system and expansion in wound care compression devices as key drivers for future performance.

negative_highlights: No financial guidance provided; revenue and EPS figures were not disclosed in this clinical update call, limiting quantitative performance assessment to program progress only.
Regulatory path remains uncertain with management stating a Phase III trial is the base case assumption rather than accelerated approval based on single-arm data.
positive_highlights: New clinical data showed all patients who were centrally confirmed HER2-positive and CD47 high achieved a response (100% ORR) including one complete response, compared to lower rates in low expression cohorts.
Median duration of response was observed at 20 months for responders with high CD47 expression versus shorter durations in the overall population or low expressers.
Strong financing from February anchored by very strong investors further strengthens the balance sheet enabling execution through data milestones.
summary: ALX Oncology reported Q1 FY2026 results driven by positive clinical data readouts for evorpacept in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer presented at ESMO Breast Cancer 2026 and progress on the ALX2004 EGFR-targeted ADC program. The company highlighted a strong balance sheet following February financing, new leadership hires including Jeff Knight as CDO/COO, and continued execution with both programs remaining on track for key milestones in late 2027.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net loss unchanged at $8 million with book value declining to -$44.82 per share
No substantive progress on PREPA resolution; legal litigation remains unresolved
Management reported no update on strategic process
positive_highlights: GAAP net loss improved to $40 million from $62 million in Q1 2025
National's leverage ratio improved to 23-to-1 from 24-to-1 at year-end
National statutory net income rose to $11 million from $4 million year-over-year
summary: In Q1 FY2026, MBIA reported a consolidated GAAP net loss of $40 million (-$0.80 per share), an improvement from the $62 million loss (-$1.28 per share) in Q1 2025. Adjusted net loss was $8 million (-$0.16 per share), unchanged year-over-year. National's insured portfolio declined to $21.5 billion, with gross par to statutory capital improving from 24 to 23 to 1. Book value per share fell to -$44.82. No substantive progress on PREPA resolution, with litigation over the Oversight Board stalling negotiations. Management noted no updates on strategic alternatives and limited near-term debt buyback opportunities.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $119 million driven by non-cash charges and non-recurring items
Production down 2% YoY due to waterflood timing and Simonette disposition
Hedging losses forecast of $70-72 million partially offset higher oil prices
positive_highlights: CapEx came in under plan at $45 million
Completed bond exchange and asset disposition, strengthening balance sheet
New strategic partnerships including Azerbaijan and Ecopetrol Tisquirama block
summary: Gran Tierra reported Q1 2026 results with net loss of $119 million, primarily due to non-cash charges and non-recurring items, while adjusted EBITDA was $74 million and funds from operations were $43 million. Production averaged 45,500 BOE/d, down 2% YoY. CapEx was $45 million, below plan, and the company exited with $125 million cash and net debt of $481 million. Management revised 2026 guidance: production 40,000-45,000 BOE/d, EBITDA $345-395 million, free cash flow $95-115 million, capex $130-170 million, reflecting new partnerships and hedging losses.

negative_highlights: System capital sales declined significantly by roughly $1.8 million due to lower placement activity following the merger termination.
Adjusted EBITDA turned negative at -$311,000 compared to positive cash flow in Q1 FY2025.
Gross margin contracted from 50% to approximately 48%, reflecting higher production costs and tariffs that management chose not to pass on.
positive_highlights: Recurring revenue grew by $1.1 million (9%) driven by continued growth in global procedure volumes despite lower placements.
The ALLY installed base reached approximately 205 systems with another 11 on backlog, demonstrating strong adoption of the next-generation platform.
Procedure volume increased to approximately 54,000 procedures from about 52 last year and 39,000 in Q1 2024.
summary: Total revenue was $13.4 million in Q1 FY2026, down approximately 5% year-over-year to $14.2 million due primarily to lower system capital sales of roughly $1.8 million compared to the prior period. Recurring revenue remained a bright spot at $12.6 million (94% of total), up 9%, while adjusted EBITDA was negative $311,000 versus positive $165,000 last year due to lower placements and lack of OUS activity during the quarter. Management provided no forward guidance for revenue or earnings as they focus on rebuilding momentum post-merger termination.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to roughly 8.4% from the prior year's 9.5% due to deliberate increases in marketing spend.
Customer acquisition costs rose significantly to $3,400 per case compared to $3,130 in the prior quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue stabilized with positive same-store sales growth of 1% excluding London, marking a key turning point after two years of decline.
Gross margin expanded to roughly 60%, driven by higher case volume and cost discipline despite increased SG&A investments.
Balance sheet strengthened significantly with cash at $16.7 million and leverage reduced below 2.5x.
summary: AirSculpt reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $39.4 million, which was flat year-over-year but up 1% on a same-store basis excluding London. Adjusted EBITDA decreased to roughly 8.4% of revenue from 9.5% in the prior year due to increased marketing investments and higher customer acquisition costs ($3,400 vs $3,130). Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for revenue between $151 million-$157 million but explicitly stated no new center openings (de novos) are contemplated in the current year.

negative_highlights: Scripps Networks revenue down 10% in Q2 guidance citing macroeconomic pressure on direct response
Nielsen methodology change negatively impacted audience delivery for over-the-air networks, reducing impressions
GAAP EPS loss of $0.20 includes a $30 million gain from asset sales and preferred dividend impact
positive_highlights: Local media core advertising grew industry-leading 7% YoY driven by NHL partnerships and political spending
Scripps Sports Network launched successfully on major streaming platforms (Roku, LG, Samsung)
Net leverage improved to 3.9x ahead of schedule due to asset sales and transformation cost recognition
summary: Local media revenue grew 5.8% YoY to $331 million driven by sports and political advertising, while Scripps Networks revenue declined 9.5% YoY to $174 million due to macro softness and Nielsen methodology impacts. The company reported a GAAP loss of $0.20 per share but raised its EBITDA improvement plan run rate to $75 million annually by Q3/Q4, with full-year net distribution revenue guidance revised slightly upward despite the Comcast impasse.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses rose $11.2 million due to volume and variable comp
Management notes dynamic component costs as a potential headwind
Consumer confidence is down and consumer remains cautious
positive_highlights: Second-quarter revenue grew 15.5% with all segments contributing
Gross margin improved 3.8 points to 38.8% on cost savings and absorption
Fishing demand strong with XPLORE, MEGA Live 2, and Minn Kota line
summary: Johnson Outdoors reported 15.5% revenue growth in the fiscal Q2, with all segments contributing and operating income much improved. Gross margin expanded 3.8 points to 38.8%, driven by volume absorption and cost savings. Year-to-date sales are up 21.5%, and management remains optimistic but cautious about the upcoming season. No formal guidance was provided.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $93 million missed previously provided guidance of ~$100 million due to higher-than-anticipated non-cash marketing expenses and lower March advertising revenues.
Multiplatform Group revenue grew only +4.3% YoY, falling slightly below the midpoint of management's mid-single digit guidance range.
Free cash flow was negative $114 million in Q1 compared to -$81 million last year, driven by a ~$40 million increase in interest expense following debt refinancing.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue grew 9.6% YoY and Digital Audio Group outperformed guidance with +18% growth driven by a 26.9% increase in podcasting revenues to $147 million.
Management announced a new cost reduction initiative targeting an additional $50 million of annualized savings beginning in H2 FY2026, on top of previously announced measures.
Tax code changes are expected to effectively eliminate cash taxes for the next few years, preserving approximately $150-$200 million in free cash flow over 2026-2028.
summary: Consolidated revenue of $884 million beat consensus expectations and came in line with guidance at +9.6% YoY, while Adjusted EBITDA of $93 million missed the prior guidance range by approximately $7 million due to timing differences in non-cash marketing expenses and March softness linked to macro uncertainty. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance at $800 million despite Q1 misses, citing a new cost reduction initiative expected to generate an additional $50 million of annualized savings starting in the second half of the year.

negative_highlights: Cash flow from operations was negative $16.8 million due to a one-time payment of CAD 16.4M ($12.1M) for Canadian corporate income taxes.
Netherlands phase II facility in Groningen faces a delay, with full operations expected only after regulatory approval anticipated by May rather than late March.
positive_highlights: International export sales increased 171% year-over-year and 60% sequentially, reaching a record $15 million net of slipped orders.
Consolidated adjusted EBITDA grew 118%, significantly outpacing revenue growth to achieve an expanded margin profile.
Company achieved its first harvest from the Delta 2 expansion in Canada with initial sales expected by late Q2.
summary: Village Farms reported Q1 FY26 net sales of $50.2 million, a 27% year-over-year increase driven by international exports up 171%. Adjusted EBITDA surged to $9.9 million (up 118%), resulting in positive net income for the fourth consecutive quarter despite negative cash flow from operations due to Canadian tax payments of CAD 16.4 million ($12.1M). Management raised no specific full-year guidance but reiterated a clear line of sight to profitable growth as new capacity ramps up.

negative_highlights: Merchant Solutions gross margins contracted due to higher-than-normal credit losses and a mix shift from acquisitions.
Payables segment margin declined 210 bps YoY primarily due to revenue mix shifts toward lower-margin buyer-funded revenues.
Operating expenses increased 27.4% in Merchant Solutions driven by cloud/software costs, non-recurring legal fees, and acquisition-related headcount.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 11% YoY to $249.6M driven by 35.6% growth in the high-margin Payables segment.
Adjusted gross profit margin expanded 70 bps to 39.6%, with recurring revenue margins reaching over 63%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 13% YoY to $58.1M.
Total customer accounts increased by 50,000 to reach 1.8 million on the commerce platform.
summary: Priority Technology Holdings reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $249.6 million (up 11% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 27%. Management maintained its full-year guidance for revenue between $1.01 billion-$1.04 billion and adjusted EBITDA between $230 million-$245 million, citing strong organic momentum in Payables (+35.6%) and Treasury Solutions segments.

negative_highlights: Q1 net sales declined quarter-over-quarter from $12.4M due to severe weather causing patients to miss treatment cycles
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance is deferred until the August earnings call rather than being provided today
Existing patient growth was negatively impacted by winter storms affecting roughly two-thirds of the country
positive_highlights: LOQTORZI new patient starts reached an all-time high driven by broader prescribing and deeper use
R&D expenses decreased year-over-year from $24.4M to $21.5M due to headcount savings
Tagmokitug clinical programs are tracking to plan with accrual progressing well in HCC, Head & Neck, and GI cohorts
summary: Coherus Oncology reported Q1 FY2026 net sales of $11.8 million for LOQTORZI, a decline from the prior quarter due to severe weather impacting existing patient cycles and seasonal trends, though new starts reached an all-time high. Management reiterated revenue guidance targets but noted that full-year 2026 guidance will be provided in August rather than today. The company raised $54 million via a follow-on equity offering to fund clinical trials.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 5% YoY and subscription revenue down 4% YoY
Media & Telecom segment revenue down 17% YoY
GAAP net loss widened to $3.8M from $1.1M YoY
positive_highlights: Revenue and adjusted EBITDA exceeded high end of guidance
Adjusted EBITDA up 37% YoY and positive first-quarter operating cash flow achieved
Gross retention improved to highest level in last 5 quarters
summary: Kaltura reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $44.6M, down 5% YoY but above the high end of guidance ($42.6M-$43.4M), with subscription revenue of $43.2M, down 4% YoY, also beating guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.7M, up 37% YoY and well above guidance, while the company achieved its first positive operating cash flow in a first quarter. Management raised full-year guidance and noted improving gross retention, but revenue declines persist due to legacy Media & Telecom churn and a large EE&T customer's shift in event timing. They expect new product contributions to begin in H2 2026 and more meaningful impact in 2027.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 6.8% due to the exit from a large commercial payer, though organic growth would have been ~1%
Home respiratory category fell about 4% excluding payer impact
Diabetes revenue was flat as insulin pump growth did not offset drops in CGMs
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $58 million met management expectations
Sleep Journey program delivering anticipated results with strong YoY growth in sleep supplies excluding payer impact
Completed balance sheet optimization transaction to extend debt maturities and reduce near-term pressure
summary: Accendra Health reported Q1 FY2026 revenue decline of 6.8% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of $58 million in line with expectations, driven by the exit from a large commercial payer which reduced growth to approximately -7%. Management affirmed its full-year outlook for both revenue and adjusted EBITDA despite higher interest expenses expected post-financing restructuring.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses up $18 million YoY to $84 million
Costs remain too high, CFO acknowledges
Strategic review costs may continue into Q3
positive_highlights: Revenue up 28% YoY to $73 million
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 20% from 13% sequentially
Incentive distributions up 75% YoY to $21 million
summary: Q1 2026 revenue rose 28% YoY to $73 million, with recurring fees up 16% to $52 million and incentive distributions up 75% to $21 million. Adjusted EBITDA increased 21% to $15 million and margin expanded to 20% from 13% sequentially, but operating expenses rose to $84 million due to restructuring, acquisition earn-outs, and strategic review costs. Management emphasizes cost discipline and organic growth, with expected cost benefits in H2 2026, while strategic review costs may persist into Q3.

negative_highlights: Q1 volume was negatively impacted by winter storms, losing approximately a third of testing during two weeks in late January/early February
R&D expenses grew over 20% YoY due to preparations for the myositis product launch targeted for early 2027
positive_highlights: Record first quarter revenue of $17.3 million, up 12% year-over-year
Trailing twelve-month ASP expanded to $444 (up 6%), the 12th consecutive quarter of increase
Adjusted EBITDA loss reduced by 14% compared to last year
summary: Exagen reported record Q1 FY26 revenue of $17.3 million (up 12% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to $2.2 million (-14%). Gross margin was 59%, up 360 bps sequentially, driven by a trailing twelve-month ASP expansion of 6% to $444. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $70-$73M despite Q1 volume being impacted by winter storms.

negative_highlights: Licensing revenue decreased year-over-year as management proactively terminated or did not renew off-brand legacy licensees.
Net loss of $4 million ($0.03/share) included approximately $3.5 million in transaction expenses related to the UTG deal closure.
positive_highlights: Honey Birdette delivered double-digit comparable store sales growth for six consecutive quarters with full-price sales up 23% year-over-year.
Adjusted EBITDA margins improved to approximately $5 million, representing five straight quarters of positive adjusted earnings despite a net loss driven by transaction costs.
Paid voting contests are on track to exceed 30,000 contestants in the new model search collaboration with Honey Birdette.
summary: Consolidated revenue grew to $30.2 million in Q1 FY26, up 4% year-over-year from $28.9 million, driven by a 15.4% increase at Honey Birdette which delivered double-digit comparable store growth for six consecutive quarters. Adjusted EBITDA reached approximately $5 million (up 111%), marking the fifth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted earnings and an improvement over the prior year's net loss of $9 million due to a one-time transaction expense reduction. Management closed the UTG China deal, paid down $15M in debt, and announced plans for five new Honey Birdette stores while launching major media initiatives like the Karol G magazine cover.

negative_highlights: Fleet fueling gallons declined 3.2% YoY, though margins expanded significantly to offset volume loss.
GPMP segment gallons decreased as retail sites converted to wholesale dealer locations reduced related-party sales volume.
New fleet cardlock locations are expected to contribute primarily in 2027 rather than the current year.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 18% YoY to $36.4 million driven by margin expansion in wholesale and fleet segments.
Wholesale fuel contribution increased 14.2% due to dealerization conversions (totaling 450 sites since mid-2024) and prompt pay discounts.
Net leverage reduced to 2.1x with liquidity of $731 million following the IPO capital raise.
summary: ARKO Petroleum reported Q1 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $36.4 million (up 18% YoY) and discretionary cash flow of approximately $25 million. The company maintained its full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA at ~$156M, citing strong execution despite fuel cost volatility. Management highlighted a net leverage ratio of 2.1x following an IPO debt reduction.

negative_highlights: March Medicare Advantage prior authorization rates softened due to new payer automation processes under federal regulations.
Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated unchanged rather than raised despite the strong Q1 beat.
BENEFIT-HF trial ramp is expected to take multiple quarters, with full enrollment potentially taking 4-6 years.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 20% YoY to $14.8M, exceeding the high end of prior guidance range.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 87%, driven by ASP increases and manufacturing efficiencies.
Transition to Category I CPT codes is underway with a Q1 approval rate of 46% vs 31% in 2024.
summary: CVRX reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $14.8 million (up 20% YoY) and gross margin expansion to 87%, driven by US growth exceeding the high end of prior guidance. Management reiterated full-year 2026 total revenue guidance between $63M-$67M without raising it, citing a desire not to get ahead of themselves early in the year despite Q1 re-acceleration. The company noted March softness in Medicare Advantage approval rates due to new regulatory automation but expects normalization and maintained that current trends support hitting existing targets.

negative_highlights: Outcomes adoption is still early and off a small base
Political advertising contribution in Q2 is expected to be light
Potential for digital ad volatility is acknowledged, though not currently observed
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 25% YoY, well above the high end of quarterly guidance
Adjusted EBITDA increased 81% YoY to $9.8 million, exceeding guidance
CTV contribution ex-TAC increased over 40% YoY, third consecutive year of such growth
summary: Viant delivered a strong Q1 2026 with revenue up 25% YoY, well above the high end of guidance, and contribution ex-TAC up 18% YoY, above the midpoint. Adjusted EBITDA rose 81% YoY to $9.8 million, exceeding guidance. CTV spend grew over 40% YoY for the third consecutive year, now over 50% of total ad spend. Management expects accelerating top-line performance through the year, citing strong demand, new flagship customers, the 2026 World Cup, political advertising in H2, and the recent acquisition of TVision for attention-based measurement.

negative_highlights: Retail scanning volumes declined due to consumer belt-tightening
Title insurance activity slowed by rising mortgage rates and geopolitical uncertainty
CEO explicitly stated no formal guidance will be provided for the full year or Q2
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA swung from a loss of $17,000 one year ago to positive $935,000
Gross margin expanded by 160 basis points on an adjusted basis to 93.4%
Banking and lending vertical grew strongly with over 50% of quarterly revenue
summary: Intellicheck reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $5.5 million (up 13% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $935,000 against a prior year loss of $17k, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA. Gross margin expanded to 91% GAAP and 93.4% adjusted, driven by operating leverage despite macro headwinds in retail and title insurance verticals due to geopolitical conflict and high interest rates. Management declined to provide formal guidance but noted potential acceleration in the back half of the year.

negative_highlights: No revenue or earnings reported as operations are suspended pending the commercial offtake agreement for Project Permian Phase I.
Management explicitly stated that committing substantial capital is contingent on securing committed customer demand and alignment with potential offtakers regarding EOR technology.
positive_highlights: Company ended Q1 with approximately $319 million in cash and no debt, providing sufficient dry powder to fund development milestones.
summary: NET Power reported Q1 FY2026 results with no revenue or EPS disclosed as the company remains in a development stage prior to FID and commercial operation of Project Permian Phase I (targeted for early 2029). Management highlighted $319 million in cash on hand, low G&A burn ($8-9M/quarter), and progress on securing long-lead equipment while emphasizing that capital release is contingent on the outcome of the active strategic advisor-led offtake process. The company reiterated a target Total Investment Cost (TIC) range of $475-$575 million for the first project.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 10% YoY driven by a major client account reduction and lower-margin managed services
Contracted revenue base remains soft, approximately 15-20% below prior year levels due to shorter contract durations
Operating cash flow was negative $0.5 million primarily due to the payout of Q4 bonuses
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA beat consensus estimates at $3.3M despite lower revenue
AI-enabled DAAP solution grew 60% in the quarter with subscription revenue up 45%
Gross margin optimization initiatives expected to normalize margins into the high 60s for FY26
summary: OptimizeRx reported Q1 FY26 revenue of $19.8 million (down 10% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.3 million (up from $1.5M). Management updated full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a conservative range of $95-$100 million while maintaining the prior adjusted EBITDA guidance of $21-$25 million, citing short-term macro headwinds and contract duration issues.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $109 million driven by $92.3 million unrealized loss on digital assets as Solana fell 33% to $83 per token.
Direct treasury expenses of $8.6 million for nine months exceeded staking revenue of $14.7 million for the same period.
Total debt stands at $238 million versus NAV of $227 million, with EV/NAV of 1.5x on a non-converted basis.
positive_highlights: Increased Solana token holdings by 9% sequentially to 2.5 million tokens, with 1.4 million liquid.
Reduced note weakness in-term debt by approximately $7.6 million during the quarter.
Executed buybacks of 2.5 million shares at $0.80 per share and issued $36 million in-kind convertible note to reduce credit risk.
summary: Upexi reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $4.6 million, up from $3.2 million in the prior year quarter, but posted a net loss of approximately $109 million ($1.67 per share), driven largely by a $92.3 million unrealized loss on digital assets as Solana fell 33% during the quarter. The company increased its Solana token holdings by 189,000 tokens (9% sequentially) and reduced short-term debt by $7.6 million. Management expects ongoing cash expenses to fall below staking revenue by July 1, 2026, and reiterated confidence in Solana's long-term fundamentals despite near-term price weakness.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted slightly to approximately 78% from 80% in the prior year
Net loss widened to $2.1 million driven by higher litigation expenses and increased S&M investments
Operating expenses rose YoY due to additional sales/marketing spend
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8% YoY for the 41st consecutive quarter of record revenue
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from 20% in prior year to 22%
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance raised with a target run rate of $15M by end-2026
summary: AudioEye reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $10.6 million (up 8% YoY) and ARR growth to $41.2M, marking the 41st consecutive quarter of record revenue. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to at least $12 million with a target run rate of $15 million by year-end. Management highlighted strong enterprise channel performance and noted that litigation expenses are expected to decline substantially after the Q4 trial date.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance unchanged despite strong Q1, implying slower H2
Cash used in operations improved but still negative at $2.5 million
Other expense increased due to higher interest and equity method losses
positive_highlights: 19% revenue growth, above expectations, despite weather shutdown
First GAAP net income from continuing operations of $0.4 million
Gross margin up ~100 bps to 93%, adjusted EBITDA up 58%
summary: Sanara MedTech reported strong Q1 FY2026 results with 19% revenue growth, gross margin expansion to 93%, and a GAAP net profit of $0.4 million, versus a loss in the prior year. Q2 revenue guidance of $28.5-29.5 million implies 10-14% growth, while full-year guidance of $116-121 million was maintained. The company highlighted the new Vizient contract and expanding sales team as growth drivers, and expects OsStic launch in Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Infused pre-rolls lost 1.6 percentage points in market share due to quality inconsistencies and lower repurchase rates following internalization.
Vape segments fell below competitive benchmarks on pricing and potency, contributing significantly to the overall year-over-year decline in recreational revenue.
Net loss of CAD 0.9 million included a one-time impairment charge of $5.8 million related to hemp-derived products due to changes in the U.S. regulatory environment.
positive_highlights: Organigram maintained its leading position with a 38.9% market share in the milled flower segment despite modest declines year-over-year.
International revenue grew sequentially from Q1 to Q2 (CAD 6.1M vs CAD 5M) as on-spec pass rates improved following post-harvest process adjustments.
The company achieved a record quarterly harvest of over 32,000 kg with average THC at the Moncton facility reaching an all-time high of 29.8%.
summary: Net revenue declined approximately 9% year-over-year to CAD 59.8 million due to share erosion in vapes and infused pre-rolls alongside a Canadian market growth slowdown from an expected 5% to 2.2%. Adjusted gross margin contracted by 16% (rate down 200 bps) driven by mix shifts toward lower-value products, higher returns on specific SKUs, and international out-of-spec volumes missing roughly CAD 4-5 million in sales opportunity.

negative_highlights: No revenue or EPS figures reported for the quarter, indicating pre-revenue status
Management emphasized ongoing diligence and work ahead rather than delivered financial results
Ferroboron program is still in initial crucible testing with samples pending
positive_highlights: Successfully developed metaboric acid achieving approximately 80% B2O3 equivalent content
$36 million public equity offering was four times oversubscribed
summary: The company reported Q3 FY2026 results with no specific revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript; instead, management highlighted a major milestone of signing its first long-term off-take agreement for 7,500 tons/year of boric acid and successfully developing metaboric acid. Guidance was not explicitly raised or lowered as the company remains pre-revenue focused on project de-risking, financing diligence with EXIM/Make More in America, and advancing commercial contracts rather than reporting standard quarterly financial performance.

negative_highlights: Total charter hire expenses increased by 122% due to higher volume and rates on chartered-in vessels.
GAAP net income was impacted by a significant unrealized gain on bunker fuel hedges, masking underlying operational performance compared to adjusted figures of $7 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew by more than $10 million year-over-year to $25.2 million driven by a 34% increase in TCE earnings.
TCE rates averaged 20% above prevailing market indices for Panamax, Supramax, and Handysize vessels.
Terminal operations delivered record EBITDA contribution with incremental income of approximately $200k-$300k from new port activities.
summary: Pangaea Logistics Solutions reported Q1 FY2026 results with revenue growth driven by a 34% year-over-year increase in TCE earnings to $18,808 per day and Adjusted EBITDA rising over $10 million YoY to $25.2 million. Management highlighted strong market fundamentals allowing for significant chartered-in capacity (up 54%) while maintaining a premium operating model. The company ended the quarter with $90 million in unrestricted cash, paid dividends of $3.9 million, and is proceeding with fleet renewal including the sale of Bulk Jamaica.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted YoY to 25.4% due to a 1.5 percentage point impact from four store closures and inventory liquidation.
GAAP net loss widened slightly in dollar terms (from $9.4M) despite lower EPS, driven by the aforementioned one-time charges and tariff impacts on Char Coir.
First quarter gross margin was below management's expectation of a return to positive EBITDA for Q2, requiring less closure activity later in the year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 7.5% YoY to $38.4 million despite operating with a smaller footprint of only 19 facilities compared to 65 previously.
Storage Solutions segment revenue surged 35.5% YoY, contributing meaningfully to overall growth and profitability.
Proprietary brand sales reached 37% of cultivation/gardening revenue, up from 32%, indicating successful mix shift toward higher-value consumables.
summary: GrowGeneration reported Q1 FY2026 net sales of $38.4 million (up 7.5% YoY) and GAAP EPS of -$0.08, driven by commercial business momentum but weighed down by store closures and tariff impacts on gross margins which declined to 25.4%. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $162M-$168M with a target for break-even adjusted EBITDA, while projecting Q2 revenue between $42M-$44M as the business ramps up following first-quarter inventory and closure headwinds.

negative_highlights: Core revenue fell 25% YoY due to inventory management issues at the largest customer and discontinued SPL programs
Management explicitly stated no additional milestone revenue is forecast for the remainder of 2026, down from prior expectations
Gross margin declined to 84% in Q1 compared to 86% last year
positive_highlights: $9.7 million of SPL program-related revenue included a significant $3 million regulatory milestone from a registrational study customer
SeQure revenue grew sequentially by approximately 11% year-over-year, reaching $0.6 million in Q1
Board authorized a new $10 million share repurchase program to support shareholder value
summary: MaxCyte reported Q1 FY2026 total revenue of $9.7 million, a decrease from the prior year quarter driven by core revenue declines and discontinued SPL programs; gross margin compressed to 84% due to inventory provisions at a major customer. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue between $30M-$32M but explicitly removed expectations for additional milestone revenue in H1, citing contract structures tied to dosing timing rather than trial initiation.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue down 8% YoY due to heavy fabrication wind-down
Heavy fabrication revenue decreased 35% YoY
Company withdrew full-year 2026 financial guidance
positive_highlights: Gearing revenue up 42% YoY, Industrial Solutions revenue up 64% YoY
Industrial Solutions set record backlog of $43.3 million, sixth straight quarter of record backlog
Gearing orders up 66% YoY; April orders already exceeded $6 million
summary: In Q1 FY2026, Broadwind's consolidated revenue fell 8% YoY to $34.1 million, but core Gearing and Industrial Solutions segments grew over 40% and 60% respectively. Gearing orders rose 66% to $13.2 million and Industrial Solutions orders rose 44% to a record $14.6 million, with record backlog of $43.3 million. Adjusted EBITDA declined to $2.2 million from $2.4 million but rose 16% sequentially. The company is exiting wind tower production, completed the sale of its Abilene facility, and withdrew FY2026 guidance due to the divestiture.

negative_highlights: Phase III data readouts still pending; no efficacy results disclosed yet
AT-587 is still in preclinical phase with first-in-human study not yet initiated
Commercial launch dependent on regulatory approval and Phase III success
positive_highlights: Cash position of $256 million extends runway through 2027
C-BEYOND fully enrolled and C-FORWARD 95% enrolled ahead of mid-year completion
Payer research shows favorable outlook for formulary inclusion across segments
summary: Atea Pharmaceuticals reported Q1 FY2026 with cash and marketable securities of $256 million, sufficient to fund operations through 2027. The company is advancing its global Phase III hepatitis C program, with C-BEYOND fully enrolled and top-line data expected mid-year, and C-FORWARD 95% enrolled with completion and top-line data expected around year-end. Additional progress includes preparation for first-in-human studies of AT-587 for hepatitis E and commercial launch readiness activities.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased to $6M from $4.1M
Cash and restricted cash only $2.2M
Net loss of approximately $4.3M
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 26% year-over-year
Gross margin improved to 70.1%, up 14%
Pediatrics now represents approximately 50% of total U.S. revenue
summary: Q1 FY2026 revenue was $2.4M, up 26% YoY, with gross margin improving to 70.1% from 56.1% (14% increase). Operating expenses rose to ~$6M from $4.1M due to higher sales headcount, and net loss was ~$4.3M. Cash and restricted cash stood at $2.2M with no debt. The company completed the acquisition of Rendiatech, plans a cash burn reduction of ~50% by Q4 2026, and will launch a new product in 2027.

negative_highlights: Adjusted revenue fell 18% YoY due to a 29% decline in marketplace trading volume
Net loss of JPY 1.2 billion ($7.6 million) caused by severance expenses, professional fees, and software impairment costs
Customer assets decreased primarily due to the decline in market prices for crypto holdings
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 4% YoY to JPY 119.7 billion driven by institutional demand
Verified accounts increased 10% to 2.5 million despite market headwinds
Strategic partnerships announced with KDDI (telecom giant) and Scotiabank subsidiary Dynamic Funds
summary: Total revenue increased 4% to JPY 119.7 billion ($752 million) in Q4 FY2026, driven by institutional and counterparty transactions, while adjusted revenue decreased 18% due to lower marketplace trading volume. The company reported a net loss of JPY 1.2 billion ($7.6 million), down from the prior year's profit but better than fiscal 2025 losses, with significant SG&A increases including severance and impairment costs offsetting some revenue gains.

negative_highlights: MidCon segment underperformed due to lower volumes from two Arkoma pads drilled on the outer edges of dedicated acreage.
Permian segment Adjusted EBITDA was flat relative to Q4, driven by a 7.3% decline in volume throughput including temporary shut-ins.
positive_highlights: Rockies segment generated $26.4 million in Adjusted EBITDA driven by higher crude oil pricing and improved NGL prices starting in March.
summary: Summit Midstream reported Q1 FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $54.2 million and Distributable Cash Flow of $26.9 million, which management described as generally in line with expectations despite lower volumes and realized residue gas prices in the Arkoma segment. The company reiterated its full-year 2026 guidance range of $225-$265 million Adjusted EBITDA but noted that current activity levels suggest results will trend toward the midpoint rather than exceeding it, reflecting a cautious outlook on near-term growth acceleration.

negative_highlights: Total advertising revenue was $31.9 million, approximately in line with the prior year rather than showing growth.
National advertising revenue declined by approximately 2% on a pro forma comparable basis due to deal concentration and Winter Olympics impact.
Q2 adjusted OIBDA guidance range lowered significantly from last quarter's expectation of $4-9M to $1-5M.
positive_highlights: Domestic box office attendance reached 83 million, up 15% versus the prior year period.
Platinum inventory demand remained strong with revenue per attendee up over 54% on a calendar-adjusted basis.
Second quarter booked local revenue is already ahead of last year's second quarter.
summary: NCMI reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $34 million and adjusted OIBDA of negative $10.5 million, both within the previously provided guidance ranges but missing on a comparable basis due to Winter Olympics competition and a fiscal calendar shift. Management noted that while domestic box office attendance grew 15% year-over-year (83 million), national advertising revenue was flat versus the prior year despite strong Platinum inventory performance. The company raised its Q2 FY2026 guidance for adjusted OIBDA from $4-9 million to a range of $1-5 million, citing expected lower attendance levels compared to last year's robust September.

negative_highlights: FDA paused 180-day review clock for follow-up questions on NAUTILUS PMA supplement
GAAP net loss increased to $6.7 million from $6.6 million year-over-year
First-half growth moderation as expected, and IGE still not in guidance
positive_highlights: Revenue growth 20% year-over-year excluding DIXI, above prior commentary
Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $99-$101 million from $98-$100 million
All-time highs in active prescribers, accounts, and patient pipeline during the quarter
summary: NeuroPace reported Q1 2026 revenue of $22.1 million, excluding DIXI Medical $22.0 million, up 20.1% year-over-year with RNS System revenue of $21.7 million. Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed to $3.3 million from $4.1 million, and adjusted EBITDA loss improved similarly. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $99-$101 million from $98-$100 million, citing improved visibility into service and core RNS revenue; guidance still excludes any IGE contribution. FDA mid-cycle review for NAUTILUS PMA supplement completed with a pause for follow-up questions, but management expects a mid-year determination and is confident in the data.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.4 million (from $4.7M prior year) and adjusted EBITDA loss increased to $7.0 million due to higher SG&A ($18.2M vs $10.5M).
Cash burn occurred in Q1 as the company proactively increased inventory and asset purchases for accelerated growth.
Q3 2026 is expected to be lighter sequentially than Q4, introducing typical seasonal volatility.
positive_highlights: Net revenue surged 65% year-over-year driven by rapid adoption among roughly 1,800 high-volume shoulder specialists.
Gross margin expanded 80 basis points sequentially to 77.7%, supported by improved ASPs and cost reduction programs.
The i135RFX product transitioned from limited user release to full commercial launch following FDA clearance for complex fractures.
summary: Shoulder Innovations reported Q1 FY2026 net revenue of $16.7 million, a 65% year-over-year increase and 16% sequential gain, with gross margin expanding to 77.7%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $65-$68 million (37%-44% growth) from the prior range of $62-$65 million due to strong commercial execution and new product launches.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially by roughly 7.8% compared to Q4 FY2025 ($1.02M).
Gross margin contracted from 87% in the prior quarter to 83% due to incremental infrastructure investments.
Management explicitly stated they do not provide guidance for revenue or bookings.
positive_highlights: Bookings reached $1.4M, representing a 12.5% year-over-year increase compared to Q1 FY2025.
Subscription revenue mix improved to 98%, up from 96% in the prior quarter.
Closed three strategic multi-year enterprise deals with approximately $5 million total contract value.
summary: CXAI reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $950K, a slight decline from the prior quarter's $1.02M due to timing differences in enterprise contract recognition and new deal closures. While GAAP EPS improved slightly to negative $0.08 (from -$0.13), gross margin compressed to 83% as management invested in infrastructure for agentic AI rollout and Google Cloud partnerships. Management explicitly declined to provide forward guidance on revenue or bookings, citing a focus on execution over specific targets.

negative_highlights: Gross margins were lower than the prior-year quarter due to decreased interest income and revenue mix shifts.
Overhead expenses increased slightly compared to the prior year despite sequential declines.
RTP growth is partially cannibalizing PINless Debit volume, though RTP offers superior margin profiles.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenues across all business units with Card hitting an all-time high at $9.7 million (+23%).
Output Solutions revenue accelerated sequentially to +19%, driven by a new printer installation and digital mix shift.
Real-Time Payments (RTP) volume surged from 2,000 transactions in January to over 200,000 in April.
summary: Usio reported a record Q1 FY2026 with revenue up 16% YoY to $34 million (implied from growth rates and prior context) driven by strong performance across Card (+23%), ACH/Complementary Services (+25%), and Output Solutions (+19%). The company achieved positive GAAP net income, adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance of 10%-12% revenue growth.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $4.7 million from $2.7 million due to higher stock-based comp and development costs
SK On terminated its procurement agreement, requiring new contracts with other customers
Capital raise of only $1.2M via ATM against a ~$50M liquidity need highlights financing pressure
positive_highlights: Received FAST-41 federal permitting designation for Coosa, improving coordination across agencies
Qualification line at Kellyton produced over 1 metric ton of CSPG samples with positive customer feedback
Company maintains a multi-year first-mover advantage as the most advanced domestic developer
summary: Westwater Resources reported a net loss of $4.7 million ($0.04/share) in Q1 FY26 compared to a $2.7 million loss last year, driven by increased permitting and development costs at Coosa and Kellyton. The company advanced FAST-41 designation for the Coosa permit but lost an agreement with SK On due to evolving market conditions. Management maintains Phase 1 capital guidance of approximately $245 million and expects initial production within roughly 12 months once financing is secured.

negative_highlights: Realized prices were negatively impacted by winter differentials at Jonah and Barnett which were the worst since ownership began.
Unrealized hedge losses totaled $7.6 million due to a spike in crude oil prices, contributing significantly to the reported net loss of $8.9 million.
Production was heavily impacted by January ice storms causing power outages and equipment damage across assets like Tex Mex and Delhi.
positive_highlights: Production held flat year-over-year at 6,700 BOE per day despite significant weather-related downtime and operational disruptions across the portfolio.
Lease operating expenses improved to $13 million ($21.49/BOE) from $22.32/BOE in the prior quarter driven by reduced ad valorem taxes at Barnett Shale and cessation of CO₂ purchases at Delhi.
The board declared its 51st consecutive quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share, reinforcing confidence in underlying cash generation durability.
summary: Fiscal Q3 FY26 revenue declined 11% year-over-year to $20.2 million due to regional natural gas pricing dislocations and a one-time prior period transportation adjustment of $1.2 million at Delhi, resulting in an Adjusted Net Loss of $2.9 million versus adjusted income the prior year. Management attributes reported weakness largely to temporary headwinds including weather-related production disruptions exceeding 300 net BOE per day across multiple fields and unrealized hedge losses of $7.6 million driven by elevated crude prices, rather than structural issues with assets or costs.

negative_highlights: Product revenue from note goods declined YoY to $7.4 million due to lower purchases by Pfizer and Fiocruz driven by timing and inventory dynamics

positive_highlights: $25 million milestone received from Chiesi following EC approval of every-four-week regimen

The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance range of approximately $78-$83 million total revenue (inclusive of the milestone) with Elfabrio non-milestone sales expected at $33-$35 million and Elelyso revenues at $20-$23 million, while cash on hand stands at $51 million.

negative_highlights: Gas transportation auction results were less than requested (received ~400k m3 vs asked for 1.6 million), creating winter supply constraints.
Spot market dispatch prices are volatile, currently around $40/MWh depending on fuel efficiency and equipment type.
Vaca Muerta acquisition requires a de-risking phase with no fixed timeline for drilling pilots or specific CapEx estimates yet.

summary: Central Puerto reported Q1 FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $120 million (up 41.6% qoq) and revenues of $248.6 million (up 43.8% qoq), driven by the full contribution of new assets like Brigadier Lopez combined cycle, solar farms, and Piedra del Aguila following a concession renewal to 2056. Management highlighted strong commercial execution with number one market share in MAT-P contracted capacity segments under Resolution 400/2025. The quarter was capital intensive due to the $301 million CapEx including the transfer of Piedra del Aguila shares and the acquisition of Patagonia Energy S.A.

Management raised guidance for Q2 FY2026 revenue decline expectations from mid-single digits to 'mid to high single digits' on a same-station basis due to macro pressure and internal timing dynamics. The company executed significant balance sheet actions including an asset sale, second lien restructuring reducing debt by $86M net, first lien repurchases, and new ABL facility establishment.

negative_highlights: Net loss before tax hit $13.3 million, primarily driven by non-cash fair value adjustments on derivative instruments unrelated to operations.
Graphite-related expenditures totaled approximately $2.3 million in Q1 as the company transitions from development to commercial execution.
Germanium recovery initiative with Teck Metals is still a cooperation agreement requiring feedstock threshold work, with no cash payments or offtake revenue expected within 12 months.

Zinc production of 14.2M payable pounds was delivered in line with the mine plan and cost guidance.
Commenced first end-to-end domestic natural flake graphite concentrate shipments from the U.S. demonstration facility.

The company delivered zinc production in line with guidance, maintained cost discipline within the $0.98/lb C1 cash cost range, but incurred approximately $2.3 million in graphite-related expenditures and a net loss that masks underlying robust operating capacity.

negative_highlights: Net income dropped significantly due to elevated Citizens takeout activity in Q1 FY25 moderating, resulting in a lower comparable quarter.
Expense ratio increased structurally from 12% to 37.6% YoY as the company retained more premium and associated expenses while reducing quota share ceding commissions.

positive_highlights: Voluntary customer growth of approximately 9 million homes driven by double-digit policy increases across nearly every channel (agents +9%, alliances +40%).
New business production in Tri-County HO-3 policies surged to a quarter of voluntary Florida new gross written premium, up from low single digits last year.
Reinsurance market conditions improved with strong engagement and anticipated meaningful reduction in risk-adjusted pricing at the June 1 renewal.
summary: American Integrity Insurance Group reported Q1 FY2026 net income of $19.9 million ($1.02 diluted EPS) and gross premiums written of $220 million (up 3.7% YoY), though these results are structurally lower than the prior year due to a lack of Citizens takeout activity which benefited Q1 FY25. Management highlighted strong voluntary growth in Tri-County and middle-aged homes, with policies in force growing 14% YoY, but noted that expense ratios increased significantly as they retained more premium via reduced quota share ceding.

negative_highlights: Company remains pre-revenue with no commercial sales reported.

positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $7.3M from $8.5M due to lower clinical and manufacturing costs ($3.5M R&D vs $5.8M prior year).
VERSATILE-003 trial amendment reduces patient count by ~100 (from 350 to 250) and shortens duration, lowering external costs.
PDS01ADC stage I data published in JCO Oncology Advances showing encouraging results for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
summary: PDS Biotechnology reported a net loss of $7.3 million ($0.13 per share) for Q1 FY26, an improvement from the prior year's $8.5 million loss driven by lower R&D and G&A expenses totaling $6.5 million versus $9.1 million previously. Management highlighted significant clinical progress including a trial amendment to reduce patient count from 350 to 250 and costs for PDS0101, alongside positive data publication for PDS01ADC in colorectal cancer; however, the company has no commercial revenue as it remains pre-revenue with cash of $21.7 million.

Rockies segment posted an operating loss of about $3.8 million and Southwest region reported an operating loss of $3.4 million driven by reduced oil-directed activity.

Dry gas revenue in the Northeast region was up approximately 45% year-over-year driven by sustained activity in Haynesville and Marcellus Utica basins.

Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to about 8%, reflecting typical seasonality and weather-related white space in the Rockies segment which saw a revenue decline of roughly 19%. Management maintains full-year CapEx at approximately $40 million but notes it is tracking below that framework, while forecasting sequential Q2 revenue improvement driven by seasonal rebounds.

negative_highlights: Cross-Industry Business (CIB) revenue declined sequentially as demand was pulled into Q4

GAAP gross margin expanded to 62.2%, significantly above the guided range of 57%-59%
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.5M, better than anticipated
summary: Valens reported Q1 FY26 revenues of $16.9 million, exceeding the top end of guidance ($16.3M-$16.7M), with GAAP gross margin expanding to 62.2% versus a guided range of 57%-59%. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $5.5 million compared to an anticipated loss between $4.4M and $7.9M, though the company noted Q1 revenue was lower than Q4 due to seasonality and demand digestion in its Cross-Industry Business (CIB). Management provided unchanged full-year guidance of $75M-$77M but issued a specific warning that CIB growth will accelerate only starting in H2 2026, implying the first half remains soft.

negative_highlights: Net income decreased 2.3% YoY due to a one-time equity tax impact and higher funding costs

Gross loans grew 6% YoY while deposits increased 11.7%, but NIM compressed as liability repricing outpaced asset growth in this quarter. negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined by 130 basis points due to increased marketing and IT investments ($6M) and higher credit loss expense.

The company generated $67 million in unlevered free cash flow (up 17% YoY) while reducing net leverage to 5.2x.
