summary: Milestone Pharma reported its first partial quarter of commercial sales for CARDEMYST in Q1 FY2026 with $0.2 million in product revenue and a net loss of approximately $26.1 million ($0.20 per share). The company successfully launched the drug within two months of FDA approval, capturing roughly 300 prescriptions by late April after securing an early formulary win with Express Scripts covering about one-quarter of commercially insured patients. Management noted that while launch execution is on track and prescriber reception is positive, financial results reflect a pre-revenue phase driven largely by commercial expenses.

The company guided Q2 revenue to $136 million-$146 million and adjusted EBITDA to $10 million-$15 million, reflecting normalization and less weather impact. Management remains confident in the better run rate, with new product launches and international growth expected to support the back half of the year.

Non-SEO marketing revenue exceeded SEO revenue for the second consecutive quarter, indicating successful diversification strategy.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 12% year-over-year due to lower M400 sales volume.

positive_highlights: Engineering services revenues increased 36% year-over-year to $0.35 million.

The company reduced its at-risk membership base by exiting non-economic arrangements while maintaining flat medical cost trends.

Cash position decreased slightly during the quarter, with Q2 cash expected to be lower than Q1 before recovering in H2 2026.
positive_highlights: Net product sales surged 73% year-over-year to $15.1M driven by record new patient enrollments in March and April.
Fennec HEARS full-service hub accounted for over 50% of total Q1 demand, with conversion rates hitting the 80% benchmark for the first time.
Commercial footprint expanded significantly via Project Ignite to reach a target base increasing from ~1,300 to over 5,000 healthcare professionals.
summary: Fennec Pharmaceuticals reported Q1 FY2026 net product sales of $15.1 million, a 73% year-over-year increase from $8.8 million in the prior period and representing six consecutive quarters of growth since new leadership took over. Management highlighted record patient enrollments in March and April as their highest demand month ever, with Fennec HEARS driving approximately 50% of total Q1 demand by itself. While OpEx increased to roughly $14 million due to expanded marketing and headcount for Project Ignite, the company maintains a predominantly fixed cost base and expects meaningful operating income growth in subsequent quarters.

positive_highlights: Secured first FDA precedent gastrointestinal study protocol from NIAID to fully fund BLA enabling programs

positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue increased 33% YoY to $364.8 million

negative_highlights: Revenue growth impacted by lower average note price from powertrain mix

Management highlighted strong demand for the Hub, including a new deployment with MacAllister Caterpillar for a hyperscaler data center project, and expects full-year 2026 margins to be meaningfully better than 2025. They also noted continued cost discipline and a pipeline expansion into public sector and defense applications.

negative_highlights: Subscription revenue was flat sequentially, equivalent only to the prior quarter

Q1 sequential decline in total revenue is attributed to strategic trade-offs prioritizing durable licensing relationships over maximizing upfront recognition

Management provided forward guidance for H1 2026 revenue between $35M-$41M (up from implied Q1 levels) and full-year FY2026 revenue between $75M-$80M, alongside adjusted EBITDA of $16M-$20M. positive_highlights: Secured a minor source air quality construction permit, enabling the start of construction once financing is complete.

The company ended the quarter with $18.5 million in cash but explicitly stated it does not have 12 months of capital runway without anticipated revenue inflows.

The company also highlighted a record Q1 net income of $8.8 million compared to a loss in the prior quarter, with cash flow breakeven anticipated by year-end.

Management guided for full-year revenues between $215-$225 million, a significant slowdown from prior growth plans, and restaurant-level adjusted EBITDA margins targeting 15%-15.5% in the second half of the year following initiatives including menu streamlining and new retail partnerships.

positive_highlights: Fee reductions: base management fee cut from 1.25% to 1% and incentive fee from 17.5% to 15%.

Management reduced base and incentive fees, reset the regular dividend to $0.34 per share, and approved special dividends to manage spillover. Deployment remained modest at $115 million with net deployment of $22 million.

Gross margin at 32.3% was slightly lower than 32.8% a year ago.
No new toy introductions in the second half to support holiday theatrical releases.
positive_highlights: Net sales up 17% YoY to $139.2 million in Q2.
Adjusted EBITDA up to $5.4 million, with 12-month trailing Adjusted EBITDA at $37.8 million.
Tariff refunds of $6.8 million recognized as non-operating income.
summary: Q2 net sales were $139.2 million, up 17% YoY, with Adjusted EBITDA up to $5.4 million from $2.3 million. Adjusted EPS was $0.25 versus $0.03 last year. Management noted an operating loss of $142,000, improved from a $2.8 million loss, and reiterated a front-loaded year with no new toy introductions in the second half. Tariff refunds of $6.8 million were recognized as non-operating income, but excluded from non-GAAP metrics.

negative_highlights: Specific reserve build of $5.3 million on largest office CRE credit
Core net charge-offs rose to 53 bps from 6 bps last quarter
Core OpEx burden expected to remain elevated in Q3 before normalizing
positive_highlights: Core revenue exceeded $50 million for the first time, up 40% YoY
Net interest margin expanded to 3.45% from 2.86% a year ago
Non-performers declined 36% quarter-over-quarter
summary: FRST reported Q2 FY2026 net earnings of $9.4 million or $0.38 per share, up from $2.4 million a year ago, with revenue exceeding $50 million for the first time. Net interest margin expanded to 3.45%, up from 2.86% a year ago, and non-performers declined 36%. Management highlighted $6.1 million in expected earnings improvements from core consolidation and expressed confidence in continued operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Franchise same-store sales spread to company comps grew to ~600 bps; management cites variability
Portfolio optimization includes 30-35 company-owned restaurant closures in 2026
Debt reduction target of only ~$10 million for 2026, though progress noted
positive_highlights: Restaurant-level margin expanded by >400 bps YoY to over 17%, highest in 5 years
Adjusted EBITDA up ~80% in Q2, more than doubled in H1
Full-year 2026 guidance raised for revenue, margins, and adjusted EBITDA
summary: Noodles & Company reported its strongest second quarter as a public company, with restaurant-level margins expanding by over 400 basis points to over 17%, the highest in five years. Adjusted EBITDA grew about 80% in Q2 and more than doubled in the first half. Comparable sales have been positive and increasingly positive for 18 months, with Q2 company-owned comps far exceeding the Black Box index and Q3 quarter-to-date company-owned comps up approximately 10%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, margins, and adjusted EBITDA, and expects year-end debt at or below 3x EBITDA.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income decreased by $0.3 million quarter-over-quarter due to lower mortgage gains.
Non-interest expense guided higher to $20-$21 million per quarter going forward.
Management noted price competition on loans and disciplined pricing may temper loan growth.
positive_highlights: Net income grew 119% year-over-year to $6.7 million, with EPS of $0.57 up 129% from prior year.
Net interest margin expanded 9 bps to 2.9% and gross revenue increased 16% YoY.
No loan charge-offs for the second consecutive quarter; classified and criticized loans slightly down.
summary: First Western Financial reported Q2 2026 net income of $6.7 million and diluted EPS of $0.57, up 119% year-over-year. Net interest margin expanded 9 bps to 2.9%, and loans grew for the fifth consecutive quarter with total deposits up 12.6% YoY. Management raised guidance for quarterly non-interest expense to $20-$21 million and expects improved balance sheet growth and NIM expansion in the second half.

negative_highlights: NPLs increased due to KRW 130 billion in exposures related to the Chung Hong group workout.
SG&A expenses rose QoQ by KRW 42.8B (up 15%) primarily due to one-off voluntary retirement costs, though recurring SG&A declined.
positive_highlights: Net income surged 66% QoQ to KRW 1 trillion, regaining the quarterly level of over KRW 1T.
Non-interest income hit a record high of KRW 628.9 billion in Q2, up 20% YoY driven by capital market performance and fee businesses exceeding KRW 700B quarterly for the first time.
CET1 ratio strengthened to 13.71%, providing ample buffer above the 13% threshold required for aggressive buybacks.
summary: Woori Financial Group reported Q2 FY26 net income of KRW 1 trillion and 4.6 billion (up 66% QoQ), driven by record non-interest income of KRW 628.9 billion which increased 20% YoY. The group maintained a stable NIM at 1.51% despite rising market rates, supported by ALM optimization and core deposit expansion. Management raised the full-year share buyback target to KRW 350 billion (the largest in history) and approved an additional KRW 221 per share dividend.

negative_highlights: Broadscale application delayed, no 2027 GA at target specs
R&D resources shifted from Broadscale, slowing its development
Nine out of ten sales conversations hit sample-type limitation (tau brain-only)
positive_highlights: First revenue recognized from Baylor College and Michael J. Fox Foundation
AKT1, EGFR, and p53 oncology assays met reproducibility criteria, repeatable methodology
Proteoform assay development now capacity-limited, with expected scale to ~20 assays by mid-2028
summary: Nautilus reported its first revenue in Q2 FY2026 from Baylor College and Michael J. Fox Foundation, driven by proteoform assays. However, Broadscale application GA is delayed beyond 2027 due to insufficient assay improvements, and R&D resources are being reallocated to proteoform applications. The company expects tau and AKT1 general availability in mid-2027, with further oncology assays and ~20 proteoform assays by mid-2028.

negative_highlights: Reported operating loss of $2.8 million versus prior year profit
Revenue declined 3% year-over-year due to international conflicts
Cash balance fell to $7.6 million, partly from share repurchases and lower merchant payables
positive_highlights: Management expects 2027 EPS incremental benefit of $1.20 from membership investments
Membership fee revenue grew to $5 million and is expected to exceed 20% of revenue
Advertising revenue improved in June and July, indicating demand recovery
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 3% year-over-year to $23.2 million, with a reported operating loss of $2.8 million versus a $2.1 million profit a year earlier. Management accelerated membership spending, driving marketing costs to $4.6 million, which they expect to produce higher revenue and margins in future periods. They estimate 2027 EPS of $1.20, but clarify this is incremental benefit, not a projection. Q3 revenue growth is expected as demand improves, though international conflicts remain a temporary drag.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 27%, three points lower YoY, driven by higher operating expenses.
Accounting change created a two-point revenue headwind, affecting reported growth.
Average deal size in the pipeline is down, reflecting current market uncertainty.
positive_highlights: TRCV grew 11% YoY to $151.9 million, with Experience TRCV up mid-teens.
The Governance Institute achieved its strongest bookings in seven years and TRCV growth of nearly 10%.
Pipeline up 60% year-over-year, with sales meetings up 35%.
summary: NRC Health reported Q2 FY2026 revenue up approximately 4% YoY and 2% sequentially, with a two-point headwind from an accounting change in reputation management SKUs. TRCV grew 11% YoY to $151.9 million, with Experience TRCV up mid-teens and Governance Institute TRCV up nearly 10%. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 27%, flat with Q1, and adjusted EPS was $0.31. Management expects Q3 revenue to increase sequentially with EBITDA margin similar to H1, and Q4 margin upside.

negative_highlights: Gross margin excluding tariff refund down 430 bps in wholesale due to sourcing and freight headwinds
Inventory down 7.1% but with $3 million expected headwind from expedited sourcing
Customer bankruptcy drove $1.1 million accounts receivable write-off
positive_highlights: Sales up 12% to $118.4M, highest since 2022
XTRATUF became the largest brand, expected to surpass $100M for the year
B2B Lehigh continued strong growth with substantial new account additions
summary: Rocky Brands reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $118.4 million, up 12% year-over-year, with wholesale up 7.9%, retail up 21.8%, and contract manufacturing up 17.2%. GAAP EPS was $1.83, up from $0.48, partly due to a $15 million net IEEPA tariff refund benefit. Full-year guidance was raised modestly, reflecting strong demand and pre-book orders, but management remains cautious on tariff and consumer uncertainty. XTRATUF is expected to exceed $100 million in sales for the year, up 30% over last year.

negative_highlights: OEM revenue guidance implies sequential step-down in H2 due to $1-2 million order timing favorability and tough Q4 2025 comparison
Excluding Hyalofast from 2027 guidance reduces expected revenue by $3 million, reflecting continued regulatory uncertainty
Free cash flow conversion lagged in H1 due to higher AR and inventory investment, expected to improve in H2
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 1,400 bps in first half to 65%, driven by manufacturing productivity and mix
International revenue reached a record $12.6 million, up 22% YoY, with Cingal up 32% and Monovisc up 24%
Raised full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 13%-17% from 5%-10%, reflecting strong operating leverage
summary: Anika reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $32.6 million, up 16% YoY, with commercial channel revenue up 17% to $13.9 million and OEM up 14%. Gross margin expanded to 65% from 51%, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.1 million (22% margin), the strongest quarterly profitability since 2020. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance: total revenue growth to 5%-10% (from 1%-9%), OEM growth to 0%-5% (from down 5% to flat), and adjusted EBITDA margin to 13%-17% (from 5%-10%). The company also adopted a new revenue guidance practice for 2027 excluding unapproved Hyalofast sales, implying a reduction of $3 million in U.S. revenue expectations.

negative_highlights: Loans decreased by $117 million linked-quarter due to residential paydowns and integration focus.
Net interest margin declined quarter-over-quarter, though management attributes this primarily to a one-time Q1 loan income anomaly rather than structural weakness.
Management expressed caution regarding aggressive competitor pricing on large loans (e.g., 5.5% fixed rates) which may limit organic growth opportunities.
positive_highlights: Net income increased 20% YoY to $162 million driven by Stellar integration and margin expansion.
Stellar Bancorp delivered strong adjusted pre-tax core income of $42.1 million in the quarter.
Non-interest expense normalized significantly with an efficiency ratio improving to 46% from Q1's 59.2%.
summary: Prosperity Bancshares reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $162 million and diluted EPS of $1.62, excluding one-time merger gains from Stellar Bancorp which contributed approximately $33 million in adjusted net income. Net interest margin expanded to 3.47% YoY but declined slightly quarter-over-quarter due to a prior period anomaly; management maintains guidance for NIMs between 3.70%-3.85%. Loan growth was flat linked-quarter as paydowns offset new originations, while deposit costs remained stable.

negative_highlights: Negative commentary on macro: ABI down 41 months, 'longest downturn'
DynaEnergetics margin down from 13.4% to 8.4% on pricing/mix, only benefiting from tariff refund
NobelClad sales decreased 17% YoY on weak oil and gas
positive_highlights: Consolidated sales at high end of guidance and adjusted EBITDA above high end
Arcadia sales up 9% YoY and 19% sequentially, EBITDA best in over a year
Q3 guidance implies sequential improvement across all segments
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue of $157 million hit the high end of guidance, and adjusted EBITDA of $10.7 million beat the high end, driven by Arcadia's 9% YoY and 19% sequential sales growth and margin expansion to 13.6%. DynaEnergetics was flat YoY but improved sequentially with a $1.5 million tariff refund; NobelClad sales fell 17% YoY but rose 15% sequentially. Q3 guidance is $158-168 million sales and $10-13 million EBITDA, with no tariff refunds assumed. Management emphasized continued end-market headwinds and discussed the upcoming put/call option on the remaining 40% Arcadia stake.

negative_highlights: Distilling Solutions sales down 42% with brown goods down 59%
Ingredient Solutions gross margin only 10.1% due to waste starch costs
RNDC bankruptcy created financial impact and ongoing distributor transitions
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA and EPS ahead of expectations
Branded Spirits ex other products up 3%, premium plus up 5% vs industry declines
Penelope up 13%, Yellowstone up 54%, Everclear up 13%
summary: Q2 FY2026 sales fell to $124.4M with adjusted EBITDA of $27.6M and adjusted EPS of $0.72, both above expectations though down YoY. Branded Spirits sales ex other products rose 3% with premium plus up 5%; Ingredient Solutions grew 2%, while Distilling Solutions sales dropped 42% due to oversupply. Management guided to higher putaway in H2, raised digital A&P to 15%, and rationalized 52 brands representing 47% of SKUs.

negative_highlights: Cost pressures persist, notably in ink due to Middle East supply chain issues
USPS postage increase up to 10% for mailing clients effective July 12
Global shipping and logistics costs elevated due to Strait of Hormuz security concerns
positive_highlights: Net sales increased compared to the second quarter of 2025
Strong free cash flow generated in the second quarter
Packaging business expected to grow in 2026; new Salt Lake City facility to open in Q4
summary: Quad's Q2 FY2026 results were in line with expectations and full-year guidance is reaffirmed. Net sales increased versus prior year, and strong free cash flow supported returning $13 million to shareholders. The company is expanding its packaging business with a new Salt Lake City facility and growing its in-store retail media network with new retailer wins and expansions. Management continues to manage cost pressures from ink and postage, while pursuing long-term growth initiatives.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down 5% YoY, with U.S. down 4%
International revenue down 6% due to China suspension
Second consecutive quarter of revenue decline; expects typical Q3 seasonality
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss improved nearly 40% to $5.1 million from $8.4 million
Gross margin expanded to 78% from 72% YoY
China registration renewed, shipments expected to resume by early 2027
summary: Pulmonx reported Q2 2026 revenue of $22.8 million, down 5% YoY and 6% constant currency, in line with expectations. U.S. revenue declined 4% YoY but rose 7% sequentially, with 12 new treating centers; international ex-China grew 9% constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA loss improved nearly 40% to $5.1 million, and net loss narrowed to $10.1 million. Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated at $90-$92 million, while operating expense guidance was reduced to $109-$111 million.

negative_highlights: Net interest margin declined to 3.78% due to funding costs and loan yield compression
Provision expense increased by $2.8 million sequentially, driven by higher non-performing assets
Credit card transactions declined to $84.2 million following operator restrictions on card usage
positive_highlights: SBA originations reached $131.4 million with retained yields of 8.01%
Gain on sale income rose to $9.3 million from $5.1 million in the prior-year period
New BVNKROLL partnership with AXES expected to drive scalability
summary: In Q2 FY2026, GBank reported strong SBA loan production of $131.4 million, with $61.3 million retained at an average yield of 8.01%, and gain on sale income rose from $5.1 million to $9.3 million for the first six months. However, net interest margin fell to 3.78%, and provision expense increased $2.8 million due to elevated non-performing assets, including SBA hotel loans and retail credit card delinquencies. Management provided no formal guidance but noted near-term allowance levels may remain elevated while fundamental credit quality is better than reported due to SBA guarantees. The company also highlighted new gaming fintech initiatives, including a BVNKROLL partnership with AXES and a Visa Prepaid Card planned for Q4 launch.

negative_highlights: GMV lines down modestly sequentially in Q2 vs Q1
Cash flow positivity not expected until mid-2027
Revenue growth expected to soften from triple-digit rates
positive_highlights: Revenue up 108% YoY and 136% for the first half
Non-GAAP operating income turned positive to +$400,000 from -$2.7M loss
Operating cash burn cut 52% YoY
summary: PSQH reported Q2 FY2026 revenue up 108% YoY, with non-GAAP operating income turning positive at +$400,000 versus a -$2.7M loss a year ago. The company divested EveryLife for $5.5M in cash and is affirming full-year 2026 revenue of about $32M with positive non-GAAP operating income, targeting operating cash flow positivity in 2027. Payments volume grew 153% YoY, while credit GMV grew 32% YoY. Management emphasized disciplined cost cuts and a focus on core fintech operations.

negative_highlights: Loss ratio increased 0.5 percentage point due to mix shift toward higher loss-ratio brokerage channel
Net written premiums growth (30.8%) lagged gross premium growth, reflecting lower retention in the quarter
positive_highlights: Gross written premiums grew 23.4% YoY to record levels
Combined ratio improved 3 points YoY to 85.9%
Operating expense ratio declined 2.9 points YoY to 9.5%
summary: Ategrity reported record Q2 FY26 results with gross written premiums growing 23.4% YoY and underwriting income rising 66.9%. The combined ratio improved to 85.9%, driven by an operating expense ratio decline to 9.5% despite a slight loss ratio increase of 0.5 pp due to mix shifts toward the brokerage channel. Management raised Q3 guidance for gross written premium growth (expecting >20 pts above market) and combined ratio improvement, citing strong momentum in property and casualty.

negative_highlights: Commission income fell significantly due to the divestiture of non-core operations and portfolio realignment.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased approximately 28% year-over-year to improve cost structure.
summary: Commission income declined to $2.1 million from $3.1 million in the prior year quarter due to portfolio realignment and divestitures of non-core operations. Net loss improved to $2 million compared with a net loss of $2.7 million, driven by reduced operating expenses (down 28% YoY) and lower share-based compensation. Management provided no specific financial guidance for future quarters.

negative_highlights: Net premiums earned decreased 4% to $222.6 million driven by lower rate increases and retention levels
Expense ratio increased to 35.8%, breaking the recent trajectory of decreasing expenses due to legacy system costs and incentives
Commercial lines growth slowed with a real exposure increase excluding workers' comp dropping to 7.8%
positive_highlights: Net premiums written decreased only 3.2% compared to prior year
Commercial lines new business premium growth goals were achieved for H1 2026 despite competitive pressures
Personal auto loss ratio deterioration was offset by favorable weather impacts and reserve development
summary: Net premiums earned decreased 4% to $222.6 million and net income was up 32% year-over-year due to investment gains despite a higher expense ratio of 35.8%. Management noted that the combined ratio improved primarily from lower weather losses, but acknowledged softening market conditions impacting rate achievement and retention.

negative_highlights: Net charge-offs in franchise finance remained elevated at $11.6 million
Linked quarter revenue declined due to lower gain on sale revenue
Average loan balances down 1% sequentially due to paydowns
positive_highlights: Non-performing loans declined sequentially to 1.58% from 1.63%
Total delinquencies fell 26% from Q1 to $29.1 million
Fintech fee revenue up 222% trailing twelve months
summary: First Internet Bancorp reported Q2 2026 net income of $2.4 million or $0.27 per diluted share, with total revenue up 23% year-over-year to $41.1 million and pre-provision net revenue up 28% to $15 million. Provision for credit losses declined sequentially to $13.4 million from $16.3 million, while total delinquencies fell 26% from Q1 to $29.1 million (78 bps of performing loans). Management highlighted a credit inflection point, with SBA charge-offs down nearly 50% sequentially and expectations for continued credit improvement and stronger H2 origination volumes.

negative_highlights: Daily operating expenses increased to $6,396 from $5,944 due to higher crew-related costs and maintenance
Fleet size decreased slightly to an average of 36 vessels compared to 37 in the prior year quarter following a vessel sale
positive_highlights: Time charter revenue increased to $57.3M from $54.7M in Q2 2025
Fleet time charter equivalent rate rose 7% year-over-year to $16,581 per day
Secured $94.7 million of contracted revenues for the remainder of 2026 at an average daily rate of approximately $18,337
summary: Diana Shipping reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with time charter revenues increasing to $57.3 million from $54.7 million in the prior year period and net income rising to $19.3 million compared to $3.1 million previously, driven by higher rates of $18,350 for a new Ultramax charter and an overall fleet time charter equivalent rate increase of 7% to $16,581 per day. The company maintained near-full utilization at 99.6%, secured approximately $94.7 million in contracted revenues for the remainder of 2026 representing 88% of ownership days, and declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.01 per share.

negative_highlights: Customer caution and conservative spending due to elevated oil and gas prices
EMEA margin pressure due to timing lag between surcharge implementation and input cost increases
North America PPS volume was a slight detractor due to tough comparison
positive_highlights: Automation revenue increased 139% year-over-year on a constant currency basis
Consolidated net revenue up 12.2% constant currency, with North America up 8.5% and Europe/APAC up 15.4%
Gross margin improved 150 basis points versus prior year
summary: Ranpak reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net revenue up 12.2% constant currency (14% reported), with automation revenue surging 139% year-over-year constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 13.9% constant currency to $19.1 million, with gross margin up 150 bps year-over-year. Management reiterated full-year automation revenue target of ~$60 million and automation adjusted EBITDA breakeven by year-end, while noting macro uncertainty and a temporary European surcharge to offset input costs.

negative_highlights: July completion factor of 91% below winter storm lows
Weather disruption impacting Q3 start
Integration costs and duplicative overheads persist until early 2028
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.89 and revenue up 8% sequentially on 7% higher block hours
Full-year guidance raised on block hours, revenue, and adjusted EBITDAR
Integration ahead of schedule with FAA approval on first revision cycle
summary: Republic Airways reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income of $41 million ($0.89 per diluted share) on revenue of approximately $571 million, up 8% sequentially as block hour production rose 7%. The company raised full-year guidance: block hours to ~880,000 (from at least 865,000), revenue to >$2.1 billion (from >$2 billion), and adjusted EBITDAR to $395-$405 million (from >$380 million). July weather has hurt completion factor to 91%, but management remains confident, citing strong partner demand and ahead-of-schedule Mesa integration. Integration benefits are expected to materialize in late 2027 into 2028.

negative_highlights: Revenue fell note weakness in of expectations at $3.0 million versus prior year's $3.9 million
Gross margin declined significantly from 49.9% to 46.4%
Operating loss widened to $1.2 million compared to $687,000 in the same quarter last year
positive_highlights: Still a preferred supplier to Shopify despite overall retail decline
No going concern issue raised by auditors
Industrial scanning business grew to ~10% of Q2 revenue with direct enterprise sales gaining traction
summary: Socket Mobile reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.0 million, a decline from the prior year's $3.9 million and missing expectations due to challenges in its retail scanning business. Gross margin contracted to 46.4% from 49.9%, driven by underutilized manufacturing capacity, resulting in an operating loss of $1.2 million compared to a smaller loss previously. Management confirmed continued cost-cutting measures including headcount reductions and highlighted the growing industrial segment which contributed approximately 10% of revenue.

negative_highlights: Revenue decreased 4% due to lower unit volumes and a difficult prior-year comparison for pre-owned revenue which was up 18%
Service parts and other revenue declined 13%, primarily reflecting the impact of the Ocean Bio-Chem sale
Full-year guidance narrowed with expectations that same-store sales will be down low to mid-single digits
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded 70 basis points to 24% driven by favorable product mix and exiting brands with lower margins in prior year
Adjusted net leverage improved significantly from 5.8x trailing EBITDA at the end of last year to 3.7x, achieving the target under four times ahead of schedule
Same-store sales declined only 2%, outperforming an industry that is down high single digits
summary: Revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $531 million while gross margin expanded 70 basis points to 24%. Management updated and narrowed full-year guidance for revenue ($1.75B-$1.8B) and adjusted EBITDA, citing a challenging retail environment where the industry is expected to be down high single digits.

negative_highlights: Credit and occupancy loss guidance assumes 25 basis points, though year-to-date actuals at 10 basis points
Rising interest rates and macro uncertainty noted as risks
positive_highlights: Record quarterly investment volume of over $500 million
AFFO per share up 7.4% year-over-year and guidance raised
Occupancy at record 99.8%, recapture rate 105%
summary: Agree Realty reported record Q2 2026 investment volume of over $500 million across its three platforms, with acquisitions of $451 million at a 7% cap rate and 73% investment-grade tenants. Core FFO per share rose 7.5% to $1.13 and AFFO per share rose 7.4% to $1.14. Full-year AFFO guidance was raised to $4.57-$4.59 and investment volume guidance to $1.6-$1.8 billion. Occupancy set a record at 99.8%, and the company executed 1.6 million square feet of leases in the first half at a 105% recapture rate.

negative_highlights: Temporary loss of ~10% of upstream production due to Middle East conflict
Global diesel and chemical supply constrained; Strait closure removing ~3M bpd refining capacity
Cash opex held flat year-over-year only by offsetting inflation with cost savings
positive_highlights: Earnings of $14.5B and cash flow from operations of $23.6B despite 10% upstream production loss
Guyana production ~900k bpd and Errea Wittu FPSO on schedule; capital recovery accelerated two years
Chemical margins up ~180% QoQ; specialty products record earnings; cumulative cost savings $16.3B
summary: ExxonMobil reported exceptional Q2 results despite losing ~10% of upstream production due to Middle East conflict, with industry-leading earnings of $14.5B and cash flow from operations of $23.6B. Upstream production outside the Middle East hit a two-decade high, chemicals margins surged ~180% QoQ, and specialty products posted record earnings. Guyana's Errea Wittu FPSO on track, and the company achieved $16.3B cumulative structural cost savings since 2019. Guidance implies continued momentum with free cash flow expected to double by 2030 versus 2025.

negative_highlights: Management declined to comment on individual shareholder note, which has pressured the stock
Utility corridor developments are capital-intensive, though planned in advance
No significant impact from AI-related cost increases, but noted only slight revenue reduction from non-strategic asset sales
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 23% and net income up 37% YoY, both second-quarter records
Gross margins expanded across all segments (residential 45% to 48%, hospitality 39% to 42%, commercial 57% to 65%)
Repurchased $32.7 million of stock, reducing share count to lowest in ~30 years
summary: The St. Joe Company reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $158.9 million, up 23% YoY, and net income of $40.5 million, up 37% YoY, both record highs for the quarter. Gross margins expanded across all segments: residential to 48%, hospitality to 42%, and commercial to 65%. The company allocated $32.7 million to buybacks, $24 million to capex, and repaid $10.9 million in debt, with share count at a 30-year low. Management emphasized long-term capital allocation, continued demand from in-migration, and no near-term constraints from power development.

negative_highlights: Non-performing assets up nominally to ~$1.07 billion due to rate delays
Realized losses expected to rise to $20-30 million per quarter
Distributable earnings guided at $0.15-0.17 per share for next few quarters
positive_highlights: Year-to-date agency volume up 30% year over year
$135 million additional liquidity from CLO unwind with reduced pricing and enhanced leverage
Cost-cutting measures expected to save ~$10 million annually
summary: Arbor Realty Trust reported Q2 2026 distributable earnings of $0.15 per share, in line with guidance, but noted $0.02 per share of one-time financing drag and higher specific reserves. Non-performing assets remained around $1.07 billion, with $90 million resolved in July and $105 million contracted for August. The company closed a $375 million convertible offering, used $114 million to watch back stock at 50% of book value, and cut annual expenses by ~$10 million. Agency origination volume was $1.1 billion in Q2, up 30% year-to-date, but management expects a slower resolution timeline for legacy assets due to elevated rates.

negative_highlights: Slower M&A environment tempered deployment but improved sequentially
Gross-to-net trends remain pressured due to high incumbent deployment (75%)
Non-traded BDC redemptions from non-U.S. investors remain elevated
positive_highlights: Record quarterly fundraising of $36B, highest in history
FRE and realized income up 20% and 30%+ respectively
Dividend increased over 20% year-over-year
summary: Ares delivered a record fundraising quarter with $36B raised, driving AUM and fee-paying AUM up 17% YoY to $671B and $410B respectively. FRE grew 20% and realized income grew over 30%, both at or above long-term growth targets. The company raised its dividend by over 20%, and management remains on track for another record fundraising year with a record pipeline and strong deployment outlook for H2.

negative_highlights: Ending loans declined due to one-time billing cycle change
NIM is expected to compress as mix shifts to fintech lending
Cash App contribution appears pushed to late Q4/early 2027
positive_highlights: EPS growth of 14.2% year-over-year and raising full-year guidance
Fintech GDV growth of 22.5% year-over-year, above trend
REBL criticized loans down another 22% to lowest level since mid-2023
summary: The Bancorp reported Q2 2026 EPS of $1.45, up 14.2% year-over-year, with ROE at 34.7%. Fintech GDV grew 22.5% YoY and fintech revenue grew 21%. The company raised its full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $5.95-$6.05 and reiterated 2027 guidance of $8.10-$8.30. Management expects Cash App to contribute more materially in late Q4/early 2027 and announced two new sponsored lending programs expected within six months.

negative_highlights: International comparable sales down approximately 9%
Technology peripherals industry demand weak
Inflationary costs expected to pressure second-half margins
positive_highlights: Second quarter sales and adjusted EPS exceeded our outlook
Americas margin improved 380 basis points to 21.2%

Normalized EPS was $0.42, well above prior guidance of $0.16-$0.19, though this included a one-time ~$100 million IEEPA tariff recovery receivable; excluding this, EPS still beat guidance. Management raised the full-year outlook across all key metrics, citing stronger innovation, distribution gains, and improved execution, while noting input cost inflation headwinds and a cautious view on second-half category trends.

Specialty products faced PDI production issues at a supplier's plant, which the company is addressing with a receiver and plans to reduce reliance.

New large load tariff approved, raising data center prices ~30% and lowering rates for others; 2027 general rate case filing expected next week, proposing 4.8% overall increase. Organic detection sales were flat due to a low single-digit decline in fixed monitoring tied to the Middle East, while industrial PPE grew 16% organically; fire service declined 2% on slower AFG grant orders, but management cited accelerating order momentum and a book-to-bill of approximately 1x, above seasonal trends.

Management continues to push for margins and highlighted growth in Advanced Materials (8%) and Polyurethanes (4%) above underlying markets.

Positive developments included Alberta data center regulations and progress on Centralia coal-to-gas conversion, while S&P shifted TransAlta's outlook to negative, citing soft market pricing and Centralia's outage.

Revenues rose 5% quarter-over-quarter, but operating expenses also increased 5%, partly due to FCP acquisition costs. Management expects seasonality in money markets and remains positive on fixed income flows.

summary: Stoke Therapeutics reported significant progress in its phase III EMPEROR study for zorevunersen in Dravet syndrome, with enrollment completed at 162 patients in just 10 months and no treatment discontinuations. The company is on track for a phase III readout in Q3 2027 and plans a rolling NDA submission starting Q1 2027. Long-term OLE data show durable seizure control and statistically significant improvements in cognition and behavior through four years, with a strong safety profile. The company has a pro forma cash position of approximately $420 million, providing runway to a potential U.S. launch by early 2028. Additionally, STK-002 for ADOA has completed dosing of the first cohort and is advancing to higher doses, with early results expected in the first half of 2027.

Cash and investments declined $101 million quarter-over-quarter, dropping from $783M at end of Q1 to $682M at end of Q2.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 18% YoY, outperforming the broader housing market which was flat or declining.
For Sale mortgages revenue accelerated significantly with 75% growth driven by Zillow Home Loans volume up 95%.
Rentals revenue surged 31% YoY, primarily fueled by multifamily property count growing to an all-time high of 79,000.
summary: Zillow Group reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $772 million (up 18% YoY) and adjusted net income of $118 million ($0.52 diluted EPS), both beating the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year goals, citing strong execution in For Sale (+14%) and Rentals (+31%), though noted a shift from residential to mortgage revenue due to accelerating Preferred monetization.

negative_highlights: Gross margin rate decreased 50 basis points year-over-year to 40% due to higher finished lubricant costs and new store depreciation.
Finished lubricant costs are forecasted to be approximately 60% above March levels, adding $5-$7 per oil change relative to the prior period.
Supply constraints from the Strait of Hormuz closure persist for an estimated four to six months post-reopening.
positive_highlights: System-wide store sales crossed the $1 billion mark for the first time in a quarter with an 8% same-store increase.
EBITDA margin expanded 30 basis points to 29.8%, driven by SG&A leverage improvement of 90 bps and disciplined execution.
The Breeze business conversion performance is slightly ahead of expectations with minimal employee attrition during the transition.
summary: Valvoline reported Q3 FY26 net sales of $545 million (up 24% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.57 (up 21%), beating expectations with EBITDA growing 25%. Management raised full-year same-store sales guidance to a range of 7.5%-8% while narrowing the adjusted EBITDA range to $550-$560 million, citing proactive pricing actions that offset rising lubricant costs.

negative_highlights: Total revenue missed expectations at $211 million, down significantly from the prior year's $248 million
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 35% YoY as management reduced marketing spend during transformation and prepares for a planned increase in Q3/Q4
Product roadmap delayed by several months due to complexity of data migration onto modern cloud infrastructure
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded the high end of guidance at $73 million despite revenue miss
Gross margin expanded roughly 380 basis points YoY driven by alternative billing adoption and lower aggregator fees
Strong cash generation with Q4 operating cash flow of $54M and free cash flow of $51M
summary: Second quarter revenue was $211 million (down from $248M YoY) and adjusted EBITDA was $73 million with a margin of 35% versus the high end of guidance; Q3 guidance for total revenue ($205-213M) and adjusted EBITDA margins (~28%) remains unchanged. Management cited delays in migrating to new cloud infrastructure, which pushed product rollouts into early 2027, while also announcing plans to reinvest heavily in brand marketing starting Q3.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance excludes pending acquisitions (14 Eduro facilities) and future deals, limiting upside visibility from M&A.
Supplemental WQIP payments for Ohio and California are not accrued or included in current full-year guidance due to uncertainty on timing/amounts.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 9.1% YoY to $1.43 billion driven by organic growth and margin expansion as facilities matured.
Same-store skilled nursing revenue increased 5.8%, with occupancy rising 150 bps to 90.6% and skilled mix improving to 29.7%.
Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by $35 million on both ends of the range, reflecting confidence in back-half execution.
summary: PACs Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.43 billion (up 9.1% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $166.8 million (up 25% YoY). Management raised full-year guidance for both revenue ($5.75B-$5.85B range, up from prior midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA ($640M-$660M range), citing strong momentum in the existing portfolio including a 150 bps same-store occupancy improvement. The company also highlighted successful remediation of internal control weaknesses by year-end.

negative_highlights: Management lowered full-year revenue guidance due to planned consolidation and line one downtime at Thorn Hill
Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $71.4 million driven by non-cash warrant revaluations and field deployment costs
Gross margin remains negative (-62%) as fixed cost absorption is weighed down by low utilization of the new manufacturing line
positive_highlights: Record backlog achieved with $24.6 billion pipeline up 31% year-over-year
Fleet performance improved to an average round-trip efficiency of 78%, narrowing the variation range
Adjusted gross margin expanded significantly, marking seven consecutive quarters of improvement
summary: Q2 revenue reached $68.8 million (up 351% YoY) with record backlog and cube shipments, but management tightened the full-year guidance range to $300-$350 million due to a strategic decision to consolidate manufacturing operations into Thorn Hill for long-term margin expansion. Adjusted gross loss was $42.9 million (-62%), reflecting near-term cost pressures from field investments (DawnOS upgrades) and underutilization of the new line, though operating cash flow conversion remained strong at nearly 100%. Management emphasized that while Q3/Q4 will see higher volumes as Thorn Hill ramps to 24/7 operations, this consolidation initiative trades short-term revenue for a lower cost base in 2026.

negative_highlights: Adjusted SG&A expenses increased 7%, partially offsetting earnings growth, driven by higher account receivable reserves and investments in franchisee tools.
Operating cash flow decreased to $67 million from $116 million year-over-year due to elevated acquisition costs for new openings and reimbursable marketing expenses.
U.S. RevPAR of 0%-1.25% guidance reflects a modest outlook compared to the prior period, with management noting Q4 comparisons will be easier than Q3.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 6% to $175 million, primarily reflecting higher U.S. royalties from RevPAR gains and royalty rate expansion.
U.S. net rooms growth improved sequentially for the second consecutive quarter, reaching nearly flat year-over-year performance.
Franchise agreements awarded in the U.S. surged 30% year-over-year with a conversion pipeline expanding 6% sequentially.
summary: Choice Hotels reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $175 million (up 6% YoY) and Adjusted EPS of $2.02 (up 5%), driven by a 7% increase in revenues excluding reimbursables to $277 million. Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($635-$655M), U.S. RevPAR, global net rooms growth (~1.5%), and the lower end of global RevPAR outlook following strong sequential performance and a 6% YoY increase in franchise agreements. The company highlighted improved U.S. operating fundamentals with nearly flat year-over-year room growth for two consecutive quarters and an expansion in loyalty contribution.

negative_highlights: Reported net sales declined 19% in the pet segment due to the exit of the lower-margin distribution business.
Dog and Cat revenues were down, partially attributed to supply issues from a plant fire in South America that required triaging sources.
Non-GAAP gross profit was $318 million (down 4%), with SG&A rising as a percentage of sales due to the portfolio mix shift.
positive_highlights: Organic net sales rose 2% in Q3 despite the pet distribution exit and challenging weather conditions.
Garden segment delivered record performance with operating income up 7%, driven by strong demand for fertilizer, Wild Bird, and grass seed.
Management raised full-year non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance from $2.70 to $2.85 following a solid first nine months.
summary: Central Garden & Pet reported Q3 FY26 net sales of $882 million (down 8% due to the pet distribution exit) and organic net sales growth of 2%. Operating margins expanded 90 bps to 15.4%, driven by garden segment gains, while management raised full-year non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance from $2.70 to $2.85.

negative_highlights: Portfolio receipts growth was slightly ahead of expectations but impacted by lower milestones and other contractual receipts due to a one-time payment in the prior year.
Operating costs are expected to be higher in H2 compared to Q1, reflecting seasonality rather than structural increases.
positive_highlights: Portfolio receipts grew by 14% to $773 million, driven by Tremfya, Voranigo, IMDELLTRA, and Evrysdi.
Raised full-year 2026 guidance for portfolio receipts from a range of $3.325 billion-$3.45 billion to $3.4 billion-$3.5 billion based on strong momentum.
Acquired royalty interest in AstraZeneca's cliramitug, a first-in-class TTR fibril-depleting antibody for ATTR-CM.
summary: Royalty Pharma reported Q2 FY26 portfolio receipts of $773 million (up 6% YoY) and royalty receipts growth of 14%, slightly beating expectations despite headwinds from Promacta and Imbruvica. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for total portfolio receipts to a range of $3.4 billion-$3.5 billion, up from the prior $3.325 billion-$3.45 billion expectation. The company highlighted strong execution on its capital allocation strategy with significant acquisitions including AstraZeneca's cliramitug and continued shareholder returns.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance lowered due to slower new customer acquisition in EverPro.
Organic traffic trends softened in the first half of the year impacting search-based product lines.
Net revenue retention slightly reduced by declining third-party partner revenue and horizontal add-ons.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded top-end guidance at $44.5 million (29.3% margin).
Cross-note motion expanded with ~140,000 customers utilizing multiple solutions (+26% YoY).
Legacy payments business returned to year-over-year growth after prior declines.
summary: EverCommerce reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $152 million (midpoint guidance) and Adjusted EBITDA of $44.5 million (top end of guidance). Management lowered full-year outlook to trend toward the lower end due to slower new customer acquisition in EverPro, though they expect growth acceleration from Q3 to Q4 driven by pricing actions and search optimization improvements.

negative_highlights: GAAP EPS impacted by $0.03 increase in depreciation and lower AFUDC alongside higher interest costs
Operating expenses increased approximately $5.9 million due to merit increases, medical claims, and production costs
Gas segment volumes were lower this quarter compared to the prior period
positive_highlights: Approved a 5.25% increase in the quarterly cash dividend payable September 1, 2026
Merger regulatory approvals received from Kentucky, Ohio, and Virginia with closing expected Q1 FY27
summary: Essential reported Q2 FY26 GAAP EPS of $0.37 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.38, which includes approximately $0.01 in merger-related costs but misses the implied beat from prior period adjusted earnings due to higher operating expenses ($5.9M increase) and lower gas volumes. Management reaffirmed its 2026 guidance for 5%-7% normalized non-GAAP EPS growth anchored to a 2024 baseline of $1.97, while noting that the full-year tax rate is expected to remain in low single digits (less than 5%). The company highlighted record infrastructure investment plans totaling approximately $1.7 billion and approved a 5.25% quarterly dividend increase.

negative_highlights: Non-interest income slowed due to lower transactionality, customer demand impacted by oil prices, and reduced results from financial transactions.
Payment fees in the Getnet business declined as competition intensified following the PagoNxt JV announcement.
Macro outlook remains challenging with unemployment rising to 9.3% and GDP growth forecast revised down to close to 1% for 2026.
positive_highlights: Net income attributable to shareholders reached CLP 382.6 billion, a 40% increase quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year.
Auto loans continued strong growth of 1.8% in the quarter and 4.9% year-to-date.
Total deposits increased 7.1% year-to-date driven by time deposit growth of 11.8%.
summary: Banco Santander-Chile reported Q2 FY26 net income of CLP 382.6 billion (up 40% YoY and QoQ), driven by high inflation supporting readjustment income despite a drop in NIM to 4.7%. Management maintained full-year guidance for mid-single digit loan growth, an efficiency ratio improving into the low-30s%, and cost of risk around 1.35%, while noting that actual H2 performance may be muted by macro headwinds like oil prices.

negative_highlights: Did not repurchase shares in Q2 due to M&A-related blackout period
positive_highlights: Generated record adjusted free cash flow of approximately $232 million
Increased full-year standalone production guidance despite the impact of a non-core divestment
Refinanced debt successfully, extending maturity profile and reducing coupon from 9% to 8%
summary: Talos Energy reported record adjusted free cash flow of approximately $232 million and increased its full-year 2026 standalone production guidance to a range of 64,000-68,000 barrels per day for oil. The company achieved this despite the impact of a non-core shelf divestment that closed early in Q3, driven by strong operational execution exceeding prior expectations and higher crude realizations relative to WTI.

negative_highlights: PC business expectations for the fiscal year have come down due to constrained supply of a key industry platform and OEM delays in new model introductions
Sequential gross margin decrease reflects previously anticipated pricing reductions partially offset by higher freight costs
Days of inventory increased sequentially to approximately 110 days
positive_highlights: Record first quarter revenue of $460 million driven by higher smartphone component sales
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded sequentially to 52.7% due to favorable product mix and a one-time benefit from wafers purchased under prior agreements with GlobalFoundries
Strong pipeline in high-performance mixed-signal (HPMS) described as 'as strong as any we can remember' across camera, battery, and power applications
summary: Cirrus Logic reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $460 million (up 13% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.84, which came in at the midpoint of guidance despite a sequential decline in gross margin due to anticipated pricing reductions. Management raised full-year fiscal 2027 operating expense expectations citing increased R&D investment for new markets like smart meters and AI-enabled PCs. The company reaffirmed its long-term strategy while noting that PC business growth timing has been delayed by supply constraints, though the pipeline remains strong.

negative_highlights: Consumer revenue declined 32% quarter-over-quarter to $556 million as the market adjusts.
Q1 guidance is slightly lower than Q4 results due to prudent assumptions on component costs and inventory levels for NBMs, though still a strong beat.
positive_highlights: Record Q4 revenue of $8,965 million with data center segment growing 103% sequentially to $2.977 billion.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded significantly to 84.6%, exceeding the high end of guidance at 81%.
New Business Models (NBMs) now represent over 50% of supply for FY27 with a weighted average duration of over four years.
summary: Sandisk reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $8,965 million (up 372% YoY) and Non-GAAP EPS of $39.25, both significantly beating the prior guidance range. The company repurchased $4.5 billion in stock during the quarter while raising its full-year buyback authorization to a total remaining balance of $15.5 billion. Management provided Q1 FY27 revenue guidance between $10.3B-$10.8B and Non-GAAP EPS between $44-$46, maintaining high confidence driven by New Business Models (NBMs) which now cover over 50% of supply for the next fiscal year.

negative_highlights: Pay TV core business declined 11%, expected to continue until IPTV growth balances it by mid-2027/28
Consumer electronics revenue fell 35% YoY due to minimum guarantee accounting adjustments from prior year
Capital expenditure outlook raised to $25M citing persistent memory market constraints and cost increases
positive_highlights: Advertising-related revenue accelerated by 54% year-over-year to $18M
Connected Car footprint grew 42% YoY with BYD joining as the 14th automotive brand partner
Non-GAAP EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 21% of revenue
summary: Xperi reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $114 million (up 8% YoY) and Non-GAAP EPS of $0.28, driven by a 54% surge in advertising-related revenue within the Media Platform segment ($18M). Management maintained its full-year outlook but adjusted capital expenditure guidance upward to ~$25M due to memory market issues affecting TiVo OS efficiency. The company highlighted strong execution with over 6 million TiVo ONE MAUs and significant growth in Connected Car, though Pay TV revenue declined 11%.

negative_highlights: Total Q2 revenue decreased $7 million year-over-year due to playing six fewer regular-season home games (34 vs 40)
Baseball event revenue declined by approximately $19 million compared to the prior year period
Operating loss of $19 million in Q2 contrasts with operating income of $42 million in Q2 2025
positive_highlights: Underlying fan demand remained strong with increased average attendance per home game through six months despite fewer games played
BravesVision early success is expected to replicate or exceed revenue from the prior third-party local rights partner on an annualized basis
Mixed-use portfolio occupancy remains above 93% and tenant sales hit a new record high in May
summary: In the second quarter of FY2026, Atlanta Braves Holdings reported total revenue of $305 million, a decrease from $312 million in Q2 2025 primarily due to playing six fewer regular-season home games. Baseball event revenue fell by approximately $19 million year-over-year despite underlying demand metrics like average attendance and season ticket sales remaining strong. The company reported an operating loss of $19 million compared to income of $42 million in the prior period, driven by higher player salaries and new BravesVision expenses.

negative_highlights: Direct delivery volume remains below pre-merger levels, with growth currently driven primarily by price and mix rather than pure unit volume.
Higher transportation costs related to a tighter freight market partially offset EBITDA growth at the enterprise level.
The new warehouse management system is still in pilot mode too early to quantify its impact on supply chain execution.
positive_highlights: Direct delivery returned to growth in Q2, up 0.4%, marking a second consecutive quarter of year-over-year top-line expansion for the company.
Premium brands delivered strong double-digit sales growth of 30.5% driven by expanded distribution and brand equity.
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved sequentially by 260 basis points to reflect enhanced operating efficiency in a seasonally stronger quarter.
summary: Second quarter comparable net sales increased 4.2% to $1.8 billion, driven by a broad-based recovery in direct delivery (up 0.4%) and strong retail growth across all channels including premium brands up 30.5%. Management raised the full-year 2026 comparable net sales guidance range from 1%-3% to 2%-4%, while reaffirming adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1.465 billion-$1.515 billion.

negative_highlights: $30.5 million (or $1 per share) of pre-tax refinancing costs were incurred in Q2, impacting net income and EPS for the quarter.
Cabot Credit Management collections remained flat YoY due to subdued consumer lending conditions and low delinquencies in European markets.
positive_highlights: Global portfolio purchases reached a record level with Q2 at $444 million (up from prior quarters) driven by strong U.S. spot market activity.
Cash efficiency margin expanded to 60.2%, up 290 bps YoY, demonstrating significant operating leverage as expenses grew only 5% while collections rose 13%.
Refinancing of $750 million in high-yield debt and €325 million floating rate notes secured significantly lower coupons with an expected annualized savings of approximately $50.15 million.
summary: Encore Capital Group reported Q2 FY2026 GAAP net income of $64 million ($2.81 EPS) and global collections of a record $737 million (up 13% YoY). Management raised its full-year guidance, now expecting global collections between $2.8 billion-$2.85 billion and EPS between $13-$14 per share despite including the impact of refinancing costs.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net sales declined 6.2% YoY with over half attributed to anticipated bakery reductions.
Foodservice segment operating income was modestly above prior year only because higher distribution costs mostly offset continued improvements in gross profit, masking underlying volume weakness.
Adjusted EBITDA decreased 6.4% from the prior year quarter primarily due to freight and fuel cost pressures increasing $4.7 million net of surcharges.
positive_highlights: Gross profit improved by $1 million-$151 million despite significant fuel and freight pressures.
Retail segment net sales grew 1.7% YoY driven by higher promotions supporting volume, with underlying growth estimated in the mid-single-digit range excluding slotting fees.
Project Apollo plant consolidation savings are ahead of target, allowing management to raise the annualized run rate component from $20 million to at least $25 million.
summary: J&J Snack Foods reported Q3 FY26 net sales of $426 million, down 6.2% YoY primarily due to anticipated bakery reductions and softness in cookies/handhelds. Adjusted EPS was $1.96 versus a prior year adjusted EPS of $2.00, while gross margin expanded 240 bps to 35.5%. Management noted that the peak impact from bakery headwinds occurred in Q3 and will diminish in Q4, with organic growth expected to return in fiscal 2027.

negative_highlights: Development services revenue declined 30% to $1.5 million due to project timing and recognition shifts rather than demand weakness.
The company reiterated that gross margins are unlikely to expand significantly further as they approach an '80%' ceiling.
positive_highlights: Diagnostic testing revenue grew 42% year-over-year to $25.4 million driven by a 133% increase in pulmonology volume and strong adoption from primary care (up 133%).
Gross margin expanded 200 basis points to 82%, the fifth consecutive quarter above this threshold, supported by improved average revenue per test.
Operating expenses grew only 7% year-over-year despite commercial team expansion, demonstrating strong operating leverage.
summary: Biodesix reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $26.9 million, a 34% year-over-year increase driven by a 42% surge in diagnostic testing revenue and an 82% gross margin (up 200 bps). The company reiterated its full-year revenue guidance range of $108-$114 million while maintaining expectations for progress toward adjusted EBITDA profitability. Management highlighted strong adoption from primary care physicians following recent clinical publications, with test volumes growing 38% year-over-year.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income was $7 million compared to $9 million a year ago due to $37 million in non-cash mark-to-market charges on warrant and earn-out liabilities.
Dave Flex Card is not embedded in full-year guidance as it does not expect meaningful revenue contribution from the product in 2026.
positive_highlights: Added 951,000 new members in the quarter, up 32% year-over-year and representing fastest growth in nearly four years at flat CAC of $19.
Originations reached $2.3 billion with average ExtraCash size hitting a new high of $215 following fee cap removals for new and grandfathered members.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 44%, up nearly 600 basis points year-over-year, driven by non-GAAP gross profit growth of 34%.
summary: Q2 revenue grew 30% year-over-year to $171 million with adjusted EBITDA rising 48% to $76 million at a 44% margin. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue ($725M-$735M), adjusted EBITDA ($315M-$325M), and EPS ($17-$17.50) citing strong member acquisition, fee cap removals enhancing monetization, and the rollout of CashAI v6. The company highlighted a record 951,000 new members acquired at flat CAC while credit quality improved with an 28-day past due rate of 2.12%.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to $245 million due to a $108 million non-cash unfavorable change in fair value of warrants.
Capital expenditures remain elevated at approximately $365 million for H1, though declining sequentially after the Ohio facility purchase.
positive_highlights: Blade delivered its best-performing quarter on record with seat sales up over 50% year-over-year and highest new flyers from NYC since 2023.
Full-year revenue guidance raised to $115-$125 million following Blade's H1 growth of 32%.
Manufacturing progress accelerated, reducing non-conformance rates by nearly 40% in the first six months.
summary: Joby Aviation reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $39 million (up from the prior quarter) and raised its full-year guidance to a range of $115-$125 million from the previous $105-$115 million, driven by Blade's record seat sales. Management highlighted that aircraft availability is now the core constraint rather than demand for Blade, with Q2 seats up over 50% year-over-year and revenue growing 32% in H1. The company confirmed plans to complete first eIPP flights in Texas next month while maintaining a disciplined capital approach.

negative_highlights: Transaction revenue declined 1% due to a ~5% drop in business formations caused by reduced Google search traffic.
Management lowered full-year guidance assumptions for the remainder of the year citing persistent pressure from AI-enabled search changes.
Q3 transaction revenue is expected to decline high single-digit to low double-digits.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA beat high-end guidance at $46 million driven by a gross margin expansion of ~250 bps to 71%.
Human-in-the-loop subscription revenue grew ~20% YoY and now represents over 40% of total company revenue.
Partnership channel order volumes increased significantly, rising from 4% to 11% of total orders.
summary: LegalZoom reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $205 million (up 7% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $46 million (up 18%), with the latter beating high-end guidance. Management raised concerns about a structural decline in Google search traffic due to AI-generated answers, leading to lower formation volumes but offset by growth in partnerships and new AI channels. The company announced an additional workforce reduction of approximately 13% effective immediately.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered from previous expectations due to wind-down of the domvanalimab program under Gilead.
Cash balance decreased quarter-over-quarter from $876 million at Q1 end to $775 million as of June 30, 2026.
R&D spend is expected to remain elevated in H1 before meaningful decreases are realized later in the year.
positive_highlights: Secured three major collaborations (BMS, Summit Therapeutics, AVEO Oncology) to evaluate casdatifan combinations without placing demands on internal resources.
Phase III trial PEAK-1 for CAS plus cabozantinib is expected to complete enrollment by the end of 2026.
Late-line monotherapy data shows no inverse correlation between prior TKI exposure and efficacy, contrasting with competitor belzutifan.
summary: Arcus reported Q2 FY26 GAAP revenue of $41 million and R&D expenses of $113 million net of reimbursements. Management lowered its full-year 2026 GAAP revenue guidance to a range of $65-$75 million, citing reduced activity under the Gilead collaboration as it winds down. While clinical progress on casdatifan is highlighted with new partnerships and upcoming data readouts in October, financial results were impacted by the transition period.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin declined to 78.2% from 82.7%, reflecting lower realized prices and a negative currency impact.
U.S. Operations sales growth is expected to decline in the second half of 2026 due to intensifying competition, Medicaid coverage reductions, and MFN price pressures.
ZEUS trial results showed no reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) with ziltivekimab compared to placebo.
positive_highlights: Adjusted sales grew 7% at constant exchange rates driven by GLP-1 volume expansion globally.
Wegovy pill captured around 90% of the oral obesity medication market in the U.S. six months post-launch.
U.K. Wegovy pill launch saw an estimated 300,000 patients start treatment within three weeks.
summary: In Q2 FY2026, Novo Nordisk reported adjusted sales growth of 7% at constant exchange rates (CER), driven by volume but partially offset by lower realized prices and a negative currency impact. Adjusted gross margin contracted to 78.2%, down from 82.7% in the prior year quarter due to price pressures, one-time manufacturing costs, and FX effects. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for adjusted sales growth to 0% to -6% CER following a better-than-expected first half.

negative_highlights: Services revenue declined 11% YoY due to the ongoing migration of customers from on-premise deployments to cloud.
Cloud NRR ticked down slightly to 106%, attributed to anticipated strategic renewals and compression in certain CX components.
Monetization timing for large enterprise AI deals is lagging behind bookings as customers prepare data governance before scaling production.
positive_highlights: Total revenue beat the high end of guidance at $782 million with non-GAAP EPS hitting the top of expectations ($2.70).
Full-year 2026 EPS guidance was raised to a range of $11.06-$11.26, reflecting expected operating margins in the higher end of the 25%-26% range.
Cloud backlog grew 19% YoY and AI bookings reached record levels with HMRC included as an eight-digit ACV win.
summary: NICE reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of $782 million (up 8% YoY), beating the high end of guidance with non-GAAP EPS of $2.70 at the top of expectations. Management raised full-year 2026 EPS guidance to a range of $11.06-$11.26 while reiterating total revenue guidance, citing record AI bookings and backlog growth as key drivers despite some timing lags in monetization for large enterprise deals.

negative_highlights: Management noted that limited service restaurants, movie theaters, and some convenience store segments are currently seeing fewer opportunities or growth compared to auto services.
positive_highlights: AFFO beat internal projections with upside driven primarily by lower bad debt totaling about two basis points of quarterly ABR.
Acquisition activity remained robust, investing just north of $290 million in Q2 alone for a total H1 investment of over $430 million across 130 properties.
Occupancy increased to 99.1%, up 50 basis points sequentially and 110 bps year-over-year.
summary: NNN reported Q2 FY2026 AFFO of $0.90 per share and Core FFO of $0.89 per share, beating internal projections driven by lower-than-expected bad debt (approx two basis points) and strong acquisitions totaling over $430 million in H1 at an average cap rate of 7.4%. Management raised both AFFO and Core FFO guidance for the full year by a penny to midpoints of $3.56-$3.58, while also increasing acquisition volume guidance from $600M to $750M midpoint and disposition guidance.

negative_highlights: Core net sales declined 3.1% due to category softness in cough/cold/allergy and retailer destocking of ~1.8%
All-in adjusted gross margin contracted by 250 basis points to 35.6%, primarily from lower volumes and unfavorable mix
Management maintained full-year outlook rather than raising it, citing continued consumer weakness and macroeconomic pressures
positive_highlights: Market share gains of 50 basis points in both U.S. store brand OTC and Europe branded categories despite volume declines
Infant formula segment grew 23% year-over-year, partially offsetting divestiture impacts
Service levels improved significantly to 91% in the U.S. and 95% internationally
summary: Core net sales declined 3.1% year-over-year to $468 million (implied from context of decline) and all-in net sales fell 3.2%, driven by category softness in cough/cold/allergy, retailer destocking impacting ~1.8% of results, and the sale of Dermacosmetics for $359 million which offset strong infant formula growth of 23%. Adjusted EPS came in at $0.46 (core) and $0.50 (all-in), beating expectations due to one-time cost benefits from operational enhancements and a CEO transition bonus, but management maintained full-year guidance rather than raising it given the dynamic environment.

negative_highlights: RMS segment revenue declined organically by 1.4% year-over-year due to lower volumes in North America and research model services.
Unallocated corporate costs increased to 7.2% of revenue ($72M) compared to the prior outlook, driven largely by deferred compensation plan performance.
RMS segment guidance remains unchanged with expectations for a low-to-mid single-digit organic decline due to flat NIH budgets and slower grants processing.
positive_highlights: DSA segment returned to organic growth of 0.2% with net book-to-bill reaching nearly 1.2x, the highest level in four years.
Operating margin improved sequentially by 420 bps to 20.5%, driven by divestiture benefits and reduced NHP sourcing costs from Cambodia acquisition.
Management raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance range to $11.15-$11.45, representing an increase of $0.25 at the midpoint.
summary: Charles River Laboratories reported Q2 FY26 revenue essentially flat organically (0.1%), exceeding the prior outlook of a low single-digit decline and raising full-year guidance for both organic revenue growth and non-GAAP EPS to $11.15-$11.45. Operating margin expanded 420 bps sequentially to 20.5% driven by divestiture benefits, while DSA net book-to-bill rose to nearly 1.2x in the third consecutive quarter above one time. Management raised full-year organic revenue guidance for DSA and Manufacturing segments but kept RMS unchanged due to constrained academic/government spending.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened due to a $6.25 million legal settlement charge unrelated to current operations.
Gross margin contracted by 220 basis points year-over-year (from 41.3% to 39.1%) driven by higher mix of customer-funded development and early prototype activity.
Operating expenses increased significantly on a GAAP basis due to the settlement charge, though excluding this they rose only 2.9%.
positive_highlights: Revenue accelerated 62.3% year-over-year, exceeding initial expectations for the first half of FY2026.
Record quarterly bookings of $15.1 million and YTD bookings over $30 million demonstrate strong pipeline conversion to production orders.
Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance from 20%-25% to a new range of 25%-30%.
summary: OSS reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $9.3 million, a 62.3% year-over-year increase driven by defense and commercial programs including liquid-cooled servers for medical imaging OEMs. The company achieved record bookings of $15.1 million in the quarter (over $30M YTD) but reported GAAP net losses due to a one-time legal settlement charge, resulting in non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing from $1.8M to $0.3M year-over-year. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to a range of 25%-30% and expects gross margins near 40%, citing strong pipeline conversion despite some quarter-to-quarter margin variability.

negative_highlights: Performance Chemicals gross margins contracted -20 bps to 17.3%, with volume down 2% due to ongoing plant repairs
Fuel Specialties faced sequential margin compression of -150 bps in Q2, expected to worsen further into Q3 due to pricing lags
Supply constraints at the North Carolina facility prevented capturing additional volume opportunities despite strong demand
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 12% YoY to $491.4 million driven by double-digit sales across all businesses
Performance Chemicals operating income increased 15% YoY despite volume reductions, aided by an 8% positive price mix
Oilfield Services delivered strong sequential margin expansion of +270 bps and a 40% increase in operating income
summary: Innospec reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $491.4 million (up 12% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.27 (vs $1.26 prior year), driven by double-digit growth in all segments despite supply constraints at the North Carolina Performance Chemicals plant which limited volume potential. Management noted sequential margin pressure ahead due to pricing lags in Fuel Specialties, with guidance for steady performance there and further operating income growth expected only from Q4 2026 onwards as repairs complete.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance lowered to $3.3-$3.4 billion due to retail channel softness, quality remediation efforts, and costs related to the Tracy warehouse fire.
Unplanned softness in the retail business (less than 2% of total sales) impacted Frontline Care margins disproportionately as it is almost entirely Medline Brand.
Additional $50-$100 million expected from Tracy fire cleanup and operational inefficiencies, with roughly half becoming permanent cost base impacts.
positive_highlights: Second quarter net sales increased 12% year-over-year to $7.7 billion driven by broad-based momentum across the business.
Supply Chain Solutions exceeded expectations with growth of 16%, supported by over $650 million in new customer signings representing more than 65% of the annual goal.
Medline Brand grew 7% including a net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds, while Surgical Solutions kitting division showed continued strength.
summary: Medline reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $7.7 billion (up 12% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 billion (up 13%), driven by strong organic growth in Supply Chain Solutions (+16%) and Medline Brand (+7%). Management raised full-year organic sales guidance to 9%-10%, but lowered the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to $3.3-$3.4 billion from a prior range of $3.5-$3.6 billion due to headwinds including retail softness, quality remediation costs, and operational investments related to new customer signings.

negative_highlights: Q2 benefited from a calendar shift of major promotional events (Prime Day, Walmart Deals) moving into Q3, which management notes will cause revenue and EBITDA to moderate in the back half.
R&D expenses increased significantly by 89% year-over-year due to investments in data infrastructure and AI capabilities ahead of current revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 47% year-over-year to a new quarterly record of $877 million, with Adjusted EBITDA growing at an even faster pace of 54%.
Net Revenue Retention (NRR) reached a record high of 129%, driven by technology-driven optimization and expansion into international marketplaces.
International revenue surpassed the $100 million threshold for the first time, reaching $110 million with growth accelerating at 87% year-over-year.
summary: Pattern reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $877 million (up 47% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $54 million (up 54% YoY), marking the fourth consecutive quarter where earnings growth outpaced top-line growth. Management raised its full-year outlook, projecting revenue between $3.4 billion-$3.5 billion and Adjusted EBITDA between $211 million-$213 million. The company highlighted record Net Revenue Retention (NRR) of 129% and international revenue exceeding $100 million for the first time.

negative_highlights: Total revenue decreased $7 million year-over-year to $305 million due to playing six fewer regular-season home games (34 vs 40)
Adjusted OIBDA dropped sharply from $66 million to approximately $12 million
