Operating loss widened significantly to a $19 million deficit compared to operating income of $42 million in the prior year
positive_highlights: BravesVision revenue line launched successfully with management confident it will replicate or exceed prior third-party local rights partner revenue annually
Direct-to-consumer business is outpacing early projections and insulating the company from broader sports industry pressures
Mixed-use portfolio occupancy remains above 93% with monthly tenant sales hitting a new record high in May
summary: In the second quarter of FY2026, total revenue was $305 million compared to $312 million in Q2 2025, driven by a decrease in baseball event revenue due to six fewer home games. Adjusted OIBDA fell significantly from $66 million to approximately $12 million primarily reflecting lower revenues and increased operating costs including higher player salaries for BravesVision production. Management noted that while the new direct-to-consumer platform is outpacing early projections, legacy cable declines continue to put pressure on the business.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened significantly to -$1.9 billion due to non-cash warrant mark-to-market valuation impacts, obscuring operating fundamentals.
Full-year combined company guidance is not yet available as integration of SkyWater operations remains incomplete for less than a week.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 287% year-over-year to $80.1M, marking the strongest quarter in company history.
Adjusted EPS beat internal expectations by approximately 20%, driven by momentum from fifth-generation system deployments.
Raised full-year revenue guidance for IonQ specifically to a range of $280-$290 million.
summary: IonQ reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $80.1 million (up 287% YoY) and adjusted EPS beat expectations by approximately 20%. Following the recent acquisition of SkyWater, management raised full-year IonQ revenue guidance to a range of $280-$290 million from prior levels. The company highlighted record-breaking performance across its quantum platform, including the first fully featured QPU prototypes returned from SkyWater and breakeven quantum error correction milestones.

negative_highlights: Adjusted earnings were impacted by approximately $0.90 per share from alternative investment performance below expectations due to macro market conditions.
Investment Management net inflows in the quarter included a legacy relationship wind-down that will modestly offset momentum in actively distributed products in H2 2026.
Voluntary loss ratios were elevated in part due to non-recurring items, though management expects normalization toward the mid-50s range for the second half.
positive_highlights: Retirement business delivered over $8 billion in defined contribution net inflows supported by high client retention and large plan implementations.
Investment Management adjusted operating earnings increased 12% year-over-year driven by higher advisory fees across institutional and retail channels.
Employee Benefits saw a five-point improvement in aggregate loss ratios over the last 12 months with early 2026 claims experience emerging favorably.
summary: Voya Financial reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted operating earnings of $140 million ($1.51 per share), which included a non-GAAP impact from lower alternative investment performance and severance costs. Management highlighted strong underlying commercial momentum in Retirement (over $8 billion net inflows) and Investment Management, alongside margin stabilization in Employee Benefits. The company generated approximately $150 million of excess capital and returned roughly $200 million to shareholders via repurchases and dividends.

negative_highlights: Management lowered full-year revenue guidance to reflect lower-than-anticipated retention/utilization trends among Type 2 customers
Type 2 customer attrition was more pronounced than anticipated specifically within the first 90 days of therapy
U.S. Omnipod growth outlook reduced to a range of 17% to 19%, down from prior expectations
positive_highlights: Total company revenue grew 23% YoY with adjusted operating margin expanding 140 bps to 19.3%
Global new customer starts reached a second-highest quarter ever with Type 2 representing over 40% of new starts
Strong cash flow generation and liquidity position, ending the quarter with $535 million in cash
summary: Insulet reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $802 million (up 23% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.66 (up ~42%), driven by strong global demand but offset by emerging retention challenges in the Type 2 customer base during the first 90 days. Management took accountability for underestimating these early-stage dynamics, leading to a downward revision of full-year revenue guidance from prior expectations to 20-22% growth and an update on international outlooks. While acknowledging execution hurdles specifically related to Type 2 onboarding rather than structural market issues or competition, the company remains confident in its long-term opportunity.

negative_highlights: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance lowered from $170-$190M to $160-$175M
Infrastructure Solutions segment margin compressed by 130 bps due to mix shift between asphalt and mobile paving equipment
positive_highlights: Record revenues with net sales up 23.6% YoY
Adjusted EBITDA increased 26% to $42.6 million driven by Materials Solutions growth of 54.5%
Parts and service revenue surged 34.8% to $135.5 million
summary: Net sales increased 23.6% to $408.1 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 26% to $42.6 million with margins expanding 20 bps to 10.4%. Management revised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance downward from a range of $170-$190 million to $160-$175 million due to delivery timing shifts for asphalt plants caused by macro uncertainty and Federal Highway Bill renewal delays.

negative_highlights: Management expects TCE rates to normalize in Q3 following the exceptionally strong second quarter.
Terminal throughput volumes decreased slightly due to falling naphtha prices, global inventory destocking, and European cracker restarts.
Geopolitical uncertainty regarding the Strait of Hormuz continues to create hesitation among market participants for longer-term contracts.
positive_highlights: Record net income of $53 million ($0.86 EPS) surpassing the previous record set just one quarter ago.
TCE rate hit an all-time high of approximately $34,000/day, up significantly from Q1 and over 20% YoY.
Completed sale of eight Unigas Pool vessels for a combined $183 million with expected net book gain of $65-$70 million.
summary: Navigator Gas reported an exceptional Q2 FY2026 with record net income of $53 million ($0.86 EPS), all-time high EBITDA of $101.6 million, and a TCE rate near $34,000/day driven by the Strait of Hormuz disruption. The company sold eight Unigas Pool vessels for $183 million with an expected net gain of $65-$70 million and completed financing for six new-builds at competitive terms. Management raised the fixed quarterly dividend to $0.08 per share starting Q3 while maintaining a 35% total capital return policy, though they expect TCE rates and terminal volumes to normalize in Q3.

negative_highlights: Adjusted net income was modestly lower than expected due to a decline of $9.4 million in other income driven by lower cash balances and weaker investment performance
Capital expenditure estimate for the Great Basin expansion increased to approximately $2.3 billion following the decision on pipeline design
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS increased to $0.45 driven by HoldCo earnings improvement and utility operating margin expansion of $12.7 million versus last year
Great Basin secured binding precedent agreements bringing total contracted demand to approximately one Bcf per day for the 2028 project
California rate case decision provided approximately $40 million in incremental annual revenue
summary: Southwest Gas reported adjusted EPS of $0.45 in Q2 FY26, up from $0.37 a year ago and slightly lower than the prior quarter due to regulatory timing adjustments at HoldCo. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance despite an expanded Great Basin project scope requiring additional capital investment. The company highlighted strong commercial momentum with contracted demand reaching approximately one Bcf per day for the 2028 expansion.

negative_highlights: Steel demand in the industrial market did not grow at the same pace as other sectors due to Section 232 tariffs affecting customers.
Cash from operations declined year-over-year primarily driven by higher working capital needs and increased raw material costs.
USMCA discussions have advanced but have not yet produced concrete results, creating lingering uncertainty for trade frameworks.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA rose significantly in Q2 due to higher volumes and better margins (expansion from 12.2% to 16.5%).
Mexico shipments increased supported by strengthening commercial market fundamentals and effective trade defense measures.
Net debt position improved to $112 million, reflecting a strong balance sheet despite working capital build-up.
summary: Ternium reported a significant increase in Q2 FY2026 results with Adjusted EBITDA rising 50% sequentially and margins expanding to 16.5%. Net income reached $465 million driven by strong operating performance, while the balance sheet remains robust with net debt of only $112 million following a dividend payment of $255 million.

negative_highlights: Affiliate channel volume dropped more than 70% YoY, with full-year expectations down greater than 60%.
Full-year cash generation guidance was cut significantly from a prior range of $250M-$450M to $200M-$375M.
Direct business volume ramp took longer than expected due to the transition and onboarding time for new sales talent.
positive_highlights: Storage Attachment Rate reached a record high of 74% with over 15,500 battery systems installed in Q2.
Direct business monthly sales growth exceeded 10% YoY starting in June/July after inflection from negative growth.
Distributed power plant assets are on track to generate approximately $40 million in GAAP gross revenue and over $10 million in operating margin for the year.
summary: Sunrun reported Q2 FY2026 results with Aggregate Subscriber Value of $1.1 billion and positive cash generation of $45 million excluding safe harbor investments. Management revised full-year guidance for Aggregate Subscriber Value to a lower range of $4.6B-$4.9B (from prior $4.8B-$5.2B) and reduced the full-year cash generation outlook to $200M-$375M due to significant volume contractions in affiliate channels, slower direct business ramp-up, and higher capital costs.

negative_highlights: Outback traffic declined 190 basis points and Carrabba's traffic was down 250 basis points.
Q3 adjusted diluted EPS guidance is negative, ranging between -$0.27 and -$0.22 due to a full-year tax rate expected to be negative.
Brazil equity method investment recognized an approximate $900,000 loss in Q2.
positive_highlights: Full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance raised from $0.75-$0.90 to $0.90-$1.00.
Outback guest metric scores improved for the fourth consecutive quarter with gains in Service (+7 pts), Atmosphere (+7 pts), and Value (+6 pts).
Q2 U.S. comparable restaurant sales were positive 230 basis points, driven by a +420 bps increase in average check.
summary: Q2 FY26 revenue was $1.02 billion (up 1% YoY) with adjusted EPS of $0.39 beating the prior year's $0.32 and missing Q3 guidance due to a negative earnings outlook for that quarter. Management raised full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance from $0.75-$0.90 to $0.90-$1.00 driven by improved mix trends, while maintaining U.S. comparable restaurant sales guidance of 1%-2% and acknowledging Q3 comp sales will be flat (1%-2%).

negative_highlights: Northwest Natural Gas EPS declined to $0.09 in the quarter compared to $0.12 in the prior year period
Water utility financial results were modestly below plan due to higher O&M expenses supporting platform integration and centralization efforts
SiEnergy earnings of $0.05 per share represented a decrease from $0.03 in Q2 2025, though this was partially offset by the full quarter contribution from the Pines acquisition
positive_highlights: SiEnergy achieved organic customer growth exceeding 15% in the second quarter
Northwest Natural received a Washington regulatory order granting over 80% of requested revenue requirement increase with new rates effective August 1st, 2026
MX3 storage expansion project secured unanimous approval from Columbia County Board of Commissioners for its conditional use permit
summary: Northwest Natural reported Q2 FY26 EPS of $0.01 for the consolidated company and segment-specific results including Northwest Natural Gas at $0.09 (vs prior year $0.12) and SiEnergy at $0.05 (vs prior year $0.03). Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance in the range of $2.95-$3.15 per share, stating they now expect to finish in the top half of that range driven by strong first-half performance and regulatory settlements. The quarter was impacted seasonally for gas utilities (winter heating months) while water utility results were modestly below plan due to integration costs.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they remain 'measured' on expectations due to soft housing conditions expected to persist through Q3 and beyond.
Structural gross margins are projected to decline from current levels (8.5%-9.5% guidance) as elevated pricing normalizes in the back half of 2026.
SG&A expenses rose $12M YoY due to Disdero acquisition, fuel costs (+50%), and freight rates.
positive_highlights: Net sales increased >4% YoY driven by Disdero acquisition ($25M contribution) and volume growth in multi-family channels (up 11%).
Specialty gross margin expanded to 20.0%, excluding a $7.2 million duty-related benefit.
Announced new partnership with Trex for distribution rights in 11 markets, validating the channel strategy.
summary: BlueLinx reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $814 million (up >4% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $35.6 million ($9.1M adj net income), beating expectations despite a challenging housing market. Management noted that structural gross margins were elevated at 10.9% due to pricing but expects them to normalize in the back half, while specialty volumes are projected to be flat sequentially. The company announced new distribution rights for Trex and Georgia-Pacific, with full impact expected starting in Q3/Q4.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened significantly from $15.7 million in Q2 FY2025 to approximately $23.8 million in Q2 FY2026.
Average Revenue Per Member (ARPM) declined by $0.06 quarter-over-quarter due to the heavy weighting of discounted annual memberships and theatrical revenue mix shifts.
Gross margin contracted from 69% in Q2 FY2025 to 54% in Q2 FY2026, primarily driven by a shift away from high-margin distribution/theatrical titles toward lower-margin core Guild subscriptions.
positive_highlights: Guild membership grew by nearly 400,000 in Q2 (approx +17% sequentially), significantly outpacing the prior year's pace of 230,000 additions.
Sales and marketing expense decreased to $61.1 million from $81.7 million in comparable periods last year as a percentage of revenue improved substantially due to scale.
Deferred revenue increased by $16 million quarter-over-quarter to $83 million following the successful launch of annual memberships.
summary: Angel reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $111 million (up 28% YoY) and Guild membership growth to 2.85 million members, driven by the 'America 250' campaign which boosted annual sign-ups but lowered Average Revenue Per Member (ARPM). While operating leverage improved with sales/marketing spend dropping as a percentage of revenue, GAAP net loss widened to $23.8 million and adjusted EBITDA loss was approximately $7.7 million for the first half of 2026. Management reaffirmed its commitment to limit full-year adjusted EBITDA losses to no more than $25 million.

negative_highlights: Organic e.l.f. brand (excluding Rhode) was largely in line with the previously outlined high single-digit decline.
Unit volumes were down approximately three percentage points, though pricing and mix added roughly 39 percentage points to growth.
Marketing spend for Q1 was below expectations due to timing of investment.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 36% year-over-year, marking the company's 30th consecutive quarter of growth.
Rhode contributed approximately $160 million in net sales driven by record-breaking summer innovation launches.
Management raised full fiscal 2027 guidance for organic net sales to 6%-7%, up from a prior outlook of 4%-5%.
summary: e.l.f. Beauty reported Q1 FY2027 net sales growth of 36% year-over-year and adjusted EPS of $1.75 per diluted share, significantly beating expectations driven by Rhode's record performance and a one-time tariff refund benefit. Management raised its full fiscal 2027 guidance for net sales growth to an 18%-20% range from the prior 12%-14%, along with corresponding increases in adjusted EBITDA and EPS outlooks.

negative_highlights: GAAP operating loss remains at $43.3 million despite significant improvement over the prior year period.
Full-year guidance does not yet include revenue contribution from the pending LivePerson acquisition, which is expected to close in H2 FY2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue reached an all-time high of $61.9M, up 45% YoY and 40% QoQ.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by 33% year-over-year to a loss of $9.6 million due to disciplined cost management and synergies from acquisitions.
OASYS platform is driving rapid conversion, including an eight-figure commitment signed in less than 90 days.
summary: SoundHound reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $61.9 million, a 45% year-over-year increase and its largest all-time quarter driven by the OASYS platform launch. Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly with a loss narrowing to $9.6 million (a 33% improvement), while GAAP gross margin expanded six percentage points sequentially to 58%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations based on this strong first-half performance.

positive_highlights: Total revenue of $233 million exceeded expectations and the high end of the prior quarter's guidance range.
summary: Oportun reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $233 million and adjusted EBITDA of $49 million, both exceeding the high end of prior guidance ranges. The company delivered its seventh consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability with EPS growing year-over-year while improving credit performance to a 12% annualized net charge-off rate. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $10 million at the midpoint and lowered the projected annualized net charge-off rate, citing balance sheet optimization and disciplined growth.

positive_highlights: Signed a key joint development agreement with a leading provider for optical connectivity integration targeting millions of units annually starting in 2027.
summary: Aeva reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $6.1 million and non-GAAP operating loss of $26 million, with liquidity strengthened to over $300 million following an equity raise. Management highlighted a major joint development agreement for optical connectivity targeting initial volumes in H2 2027 and ramping in 2028, alongside progress on automotive programs like Bendix and Daimler Truck. The company emphasized financial discipline while expanding into new markets without significant reconfiguration of core technology.

negative_highlights: Core Gas Utility segment reported an adjusted loss of $3 million, up from a $10 million loss in the prior year due to higher bad debt expense and O&M costs.
Missed revenue recovery expectations as lower usage net of weather mitigation in Missouri partially offset gains in Alabama.
Regulatory settlements in Missouri regarding accounting authority did not immediately resolve lost margin issues, requiring future rate cases for durable solutions.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS improved by $0.03 per share compared to the prior year quarter due to non-recurring preferred dividend expense in FY25 and a gain on sale of divested businesses totaling $254.6 million after-tax.
Completed divestitures of Spire Marketing and Spire Storage, simplifying the business model into a fully regulated utility profile with enhanced earnings visibility.
summary: Spire reported an adjusted loss of $15 million ($0.26 per share) for Q3 FY2026, a slight improvement from the prior year's loss but still below expectations given recent divestitures and transition costs. Management reaffirmed fiscal 2026 guidance of $3.90-$4.10 EPS (excluding discontinued operations) and maintained long-term growth targets despite ongoing regulatory settlements in Missouri and Alabama. The company highlighted a gain on sale of $254.6 million from divested businesses which significantly impacted the bottom line, while noting that core utility earnings remain under pressure.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue declined by 10% YoY to $14 million, reflecting changes in product mix and lower unit prices.
Total bookings were weighted towards IoT solutions which had a lower ARPU compared to other segments.
Professional services gross margin was volatile at 21%, recovering from -44% the prior year due to specific project mixes.
positive_highlights: Core revenue accelerated to a double-digit growth rate of 14% YoY, marking the highest quarterly growth in over two years.
Gross margins expanded by 760 bps to 41%, reflecting structural cost reductions and higher SaaS mix.
The company achieved positive adjusted EBITDA for the third consecutive quarter with $93 million in cash on hand.
summary: SmartRent reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $40 million (up 4% YoY) and core revenue of $38 million (up 14%), driven by a 13% increase in SaaS revenues to $16 million. Gross margins expanded significantly by 760 basis points to 41%, while the company achieved its third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA at $700,000 and deployed share buybacks totaling approximately $3 million.

negative_highlights: EV charging gross margin contracted to 26.9% from 33.8%
Maintenance revenue nearly flat at $4.1M vs $4.0M
Data center revenue upside expected only in next fiscal year
positive_highlights: Revenue up 32% YoY to $25.7M
Gross margin expanded to 34.6% from 30.1%
Seventh consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA
summary: Orion Energy Systems reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $25.7 million, up 32% year-over-year, with net income of $2 million versus a loss of $1.2 million in the prior year. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.5 million, up from $200,000. The company reiterated its fiscal 2027 guidance of $95-$97 million revenue and positive adjusted EBITDA, and highlighted strength in automotive, retail, public sector, and EV charging, plus initial data center entry.

negative_highlights: Hawaii conventional throughput is expected between 59,000 and 65,000 barrels per day in Q3 due to the refinery turnaround.
Q3 Hawaii capture is projected to be below typical normalized guidance of 100%-110% due to inventory monetization timing and higher freight costs.
Working capital outflows totaled $312 million, driven by building refined product inventories ahead of the Hawaii turnaround.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income reached $499 million, or $10.10 per share, reflecting exceptional operational execution in volatile markets.
Hawaii crude differential guidance was raised to between $11.50 and $13.50 per barrel for the third quarter following the turnaround completion.
Total liquidity strengthened to approximately $1.4 billion after reducing term debt by over 20% via a new senior unsecured notes issuance.
summary: Par Pacific reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with adjusted net income of $499 million ($10.10 per share) and adjusted EBITDA of $571 million, driven by a combined refining index averaging approximately $33 per barrel. Management raised full-year guidance for Hawaii crude differentials to between $11.50 and $13.50 per barrel following the completion of the refinery turnaround in July. The company strengthened its balance sheet with total liquidity of approximately $1.4 billion after reducing term debt by over 20% via a new senior unsecured notes issuance.

negative_highlights: Capital markets revenue declined 1% globally due to industry softness in office and midsize multifamily transactions
EMEA leasing trends were mixed with a decline of 6%, attributed primarily to quarterly deal timing variances and macroeconomic uncertainty
positive_highlights: Set company records for highest second quarter total revenue and lowest gross debt balance
Adjusted EPS grew 17% to $0.35, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
Leasing business rose 27% globally with Americas leasing up 35%, driven by strength in legal, accounting, insurance, and tech sectors
summary: Cushman & Wakefield reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $2.8 billion (up 11% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.35 (up 17%), setting records for total revenue and leasing/services volume while achieving the lowest gross debt balance in company history. Management raised its full-year 2026 guidance, projecting mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth and increasing the annualized adjusted EPS target to a range of 18%-23%. The strong performance was driven by double-digit growth across all geographies (Americas, APAC, EMEA) with leasing up 27% globally and services expanding 7%, despite a softness in capital markets.

negative_highlights: Consumer revenue growth was modest (5% sequentially) due to seasonal weakness in major appliances offsetting AC strength.
The new 2,200 volt PowiGaN technology is currently a demonstration only and not expected to generate meaningful revenue for several years.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin expanded by 160 bps sequentially to 55.1%, driven by better mix with industrial rising to 43% of sales.
Industrial revenue grew 16% year-to-date, led by home and building automation, power tools, and broad-based applications.
Company successfully reduced channel inventory weeks on hand from above nine at the start of the year down to a healthy range of 7.3 weeks.
summary: Power Integrations reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $119 million (up 3% YoY and 10% sequentially) with Non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 17.1%. Management raised the full-year guidance for non-GAAP OpEx, projecting a low single-digit decrease despite continued investment in strategic growth markets like data center and automotive.

negative_highlights: Effective tax rate remains elevated at 33.7%, driven by U.S. taxation of foreign earnings and repatriation taxes
No share buybacks were executed in the quarter despite a stock offering, with cash used for capacity expansion instead
positive_highlights: Adjusted revenue of $919 million exceeded the top end of guidance range
Book-to-bill ratio reached 1.32 for Q2 with strong demand in AI, industrial power, and aerospace defense segments
Total backlog grew 18% to $1.9 billion (6.1 months) reflecting improved delivery performance
summary: Vishay reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted revenue of $919 million, exceeding the top end of guidance and growing 9.5% sequentially driven by volume growth and price increases. Adjusted gross margin expanded to 22.6%, surpassing expectations as higher volumes offset cost pressures. Management raised full-year outlooks for Q3 with a midpoint representing a 4.5% sequential increase, while reaffirming the path toward exiting at 24% quarterly gross margin.

negative_highlights: Pharma R&D services revenue was $11.4 million, reflecting timing of deliverables and a strategic shift away from one-time smaller deals.
Operating expenses increased by approximately $21 million year-over-year due to commercial expansion and product pipeline investments.
positive_highlights: Total revenue increased 45% year-over-year to $263.7 million driven by volume growth and ASP increases.
GAAP gross margins expanded significantly from 63% last year to 68% in the current quarter.
Caris Detect launched with strong interest, while Caris Assure blood cases grew 50% year-over-year.
summary: Caris Life Sciences reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $263.7 million, a 45% year-over-year increase driven by molecular profiling services growth of 55%. GAAP gross margins expanded to 68%, and the company achieved its fifth consecutive quarter of positive Adjusted EBITDA ($55.7M) and free cash flow ($6.4M). Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.03-$1.04 billion from a prior range of $1.0-$1.02 billion, citing strong H1 performance.

negative_highlights: CMS has filed notice of intent to appeal the District Court's decision regarding the four and a half star rating, creating litigation uncertainty for future payments.
Outpatient cost trends remain elevated compared to prior years despite moderating in Q2
Second-half outlook anticipates seasonal EBITDA loss in Q4 due to AEP-related investments
positive_highlights: GAAP net income increased by $67 million year-over-year in the first half of 2026
Operating leverage expanded by more than 200 basis points, with SG&A improving approximately 220 bps YoY
Cohort progression is delivering stronger economics as members move from year one to two
summary: Clover Health reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.5 billion (up >$550M YoY) and GAAP net income of $28 million for the quarter ($55M H1), beating expectations with membership growth of 48% in Medicare Advantage. Management increased full-year guidance across all metrics, including total revenue to $2.92B-$3B and adjusted EBITDA to $70M-$85M, citing favorable cost trends and cohort maturation under Clover Assistant as key drivers.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth was muted at only +2% sequentially as stronger bookings have not yet fully translated into shipments.
Tariff-related headwinds persisted, including $10 million in higher gross tariff expenses offsetting a $35 million refund.
Production rates are expected to lag booking growth through the second half of 2026 due to sourcing transitions and hiring needs.
positive_highlights: Bookings increased for the fourth consecutive quarter at $680M (+17% sequentially).
Operating cash flow turned positive ($17 million) and improved by approximately $50 million from Q1.
Bolzoni returned to profitability due to favorable product mix and lower freight costs.
summary: Hyster-Yale reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $813 million (up 2% sequentially) and bookings of $680 million (up 17% sequentially), marking the fourth consecutive quarter of booking growth. Consolidated operating loss narrowed to $18 million from a prior period, driven by lift truck improvements and tariff refunds offsetting higher material costs and tariffs; however, profitability remains under pressure with shipments lagging bookings due to production ramp-up constraints.

negative_highlights: Second quarter adjusted EPS missed expectations at $0.16 versus $0.22 year-over-year, reflecting higher O&M costs from severe weather events.
Management is still evaluating a recent Indiana TDSIC order regarding gas modernization investments which may impact recovery mechanisms and requires demonstrating specific project benefits.
positive_highlights: Management confirmed the data center strategy remains on track with Amazon and Alphabet agreements approved, expected to provide approximately $1.4 billion in bill reductions for existing customers over contract terms.
Demand from large load customers is robust with 3 GW of active strategic negotiations and line of sight to an additional 2 GW of potential customers beyond the current pipeline.
summary: NiSource reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated adjusted EPS of $0.16 compared to $0.22 in the prior year period, driven by increased revenue from new rates offset by higher O&M expenses due to storm activity and union negotiations. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for 2026 at a range of $2.02-$2.07 per share despite an Indiana regulatory order regarding gas modernization investments that requires better demonstration of project benefits before recovery.

negative_highlights: Net debt leverage ratio increased to two times due to $100 million Calabrian financing, up from 1.2x
Management remains cautious about potential demand destruction in industrial applications if sulfur prices moderate
Capital expenditures expected to rise to $85-$95 million for Gulf Coast expansion and integration
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $53 million was solidly within guidance range and up 27% YoY
Raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $195-$207 million, excluding new Calabrian acquisition contribution
Calabrian acquisition is accretive from day one with expected second-half EBITDA of $10-$12 million
summary: Ecovyst reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $250 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $53 million, which beat consensus expectations by solidly meeting the upper end of its guidance range ($48-$59m). Management raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $195-$207 million following the closing of the Calabrian acquisition and favorable first-half results. The company ended with net debt leverage at two times, funded by new term loan proceeds for the acquisition.

negative_highlights: Reported revenue declined 10.9% due to strategic exits and structural declines in the diaper category, which now represents less than 25% of total consumption.
The company expects a timing benefit regarding inventory levels that will partially reverse working capital improvements in H2.
positive_highlights: Underlying adjusted gross margins hit an all-time high of 43.8%, driven by favorable mix and supply chain savings.
Flushable wipes grew more than 200% YoY, making Honest the fastest-growing branded player in that segment.
Household penetration improved to 8.1%, with nearly two-thirds of growth coming from no-kid households.
summary: The Honest Company reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $83.3 million (down 10.9% YoY due to strategic exits and diaper declines) but achieved organic growth of 6.7%. Underlying adjusted gross margins expanded to 43.8%, marking an all-time high, while the company raised its full-year outlook for both revenue ($319M-$325M) and Adjusted EBITDA ($23M-$25M). Management highlighted strong momentum in Wipes (consumption up 26%) and Personal Care (+19%), which now comprise over 70% of consumption, offsetting structural headwinds in the diaper category.

negative_highlights: Silicon metal average note price declined 6% sequentially to $2,592 per ton due to low-price imports.
Company explicitly stated it will not resume the share buyback program at this time despite positive cash flow generation.
European ferrosilicon index prices fell 6%, with safeguards noted as ineffective against substitution of silicon metal.
positive_highlights: Total shipments increased 7% quarter-over-quarter to 188,000 tons driven by a 34% surge in silicon metal volumes.
Free cash flow turned positive at $20 million after improving from -$16 million in the prior quarter.
Manganese-based alloys adjusted EBITDA margins expanded significantly to 12%, up from 9% in Q1.
summary: Ferroglobe reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $379 million (up 9% sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA of $13 million (up $10m), driven by a 7% volume increase in silicon metal. Free cash flow improved to +$20 million, supported by a $28 million working capital release, though the company explicitly declined to resume share buybacks due to market conditions. Management expressed cautious optimism about demand stabilization but highlighted persistent pricing pressure from Chinese and Angolan imports.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to a $2 million loss (-3% margin) due to stock-based compensation costs.
Branded performance marketing spend saw a 9% pullback in the quarter, though management notes this is not expected to be a significant driver of growth for the rest of the year.
positive_highlights: Revenue exceeded the high end of guidance at $75M, driven by a self-serve channel growing 32% YoY to comprise roughly 67% of total revenue.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $10 million (13% margin), representing a $12 million improvement over last year and beating the prior guide range significantly.
Platform WAU grew sequentially for the second consecutive quarter, reaching an all-time high of 22.9M users.
summary: Nextdoor reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $75 million (up 15% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $10 million, beating the high end of its prior guidance range ($71M-$73M). Management raised full-year outlooks for both revenue growth to low teens and adjusted EBITDA margin to approximately 10%. Platform WAU reached an all-time high of 22.9 million with two consecutive quarters of sequential growth.

negative_highlights: Total gross profit decreased by 6.4% (from $39.8M to $37.3M) driven primarily by the lower margin profile of Pioneer Power.
ODR organic revenue declined 3.4%, and GCR margins contracted significantly due to project timing issues rather than execution failures.
positive_highlights: Total bookings reached $616 million over the past three consecutive quarters, demonstrating underlying demand health despite near-term margin pressure.
The company completed its acquisition of CYMCOR for $30 million to expand geographic reach in data centers and enhance program management capabilities.
summary: Limbach Holdings reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $173.5 million and adjusted EPS of $0.64, both missing expectations due to project timing and softness in healthcare/institutional markets which pressured gross margins down to 21.5%. Management lowered its Adjusted EBITDA guidance range for the full year while raising the revenue outlook to reflect acquisition contributions and execution adjustments.

negative_highlights: Production fell 9% sequentially and 12% year-over-year due to Canadian dispositions and unplanned lift failures
Oil sales volume decreased despite higher prices, with lower Colombia differentials offsetting price gains
Announced definitive agreement to note all oil businesses in Colombia and Ecuador
positive_highlights: Net income of $25 million compared to a net loss of $13 million in Q2 2025
Adjusted EBITDA increased to $85 million from $74 million in the prior quarter
Completed $123 million capital carry commitment on Sur Oriente block improving future economics
summary: Gran Tierra Energy reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $25 million and adjusted EBITDA of $85 million, driven by stronger commodity prices (M-1 benchmark at $101.89/bbl) and lower operating costs ($52m). However, production declined 9% sequentially due to Canadian asset dispositions and operational issues in Ecuador, while the company announced a definitive agreement to watch its Colombia and Ecuador businesses.

negative_highlights: Government services segment Adjusted operating income decreased $2.3 million due to elevated transition costs, overtime ($3.3M), fuel price pass-through delays ($1.5M impact), and supply chain penalties.
Supply chain challenges regarding Leonardo AW189 deliveries delayed aircraft modifications, adversely impacting 2026 adjusted operating income by approximately $8 million.
OES revenue guidance range was tightened despite higher Q2 performance due to increased certainty around future revenues.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased $20.5 million sequentially driven by higher revenues across segments and lower repairs/maintenance costs.
Berry Aviation acquisition closed successfully with a presence now on six continents, expected to be immediately accretive to earnings and free cash flow.
OES business performance improved due to higher rates in Europe/Americas and consistent activity in Africa.
summary: Bristow Group reported Q2 FY2026 results with revenues of $23.1 million higher than the prior quarter and Adjusted EBITDA up by $20.5 million compared to Q1. Management affirmed full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue ($1.6 billion-$1.7 billion) but tightened OES revenue guidance while updating government services segment guidance due to transition costs and supply chain delays impacting profitability. The company closed the acquisition of Berry Aviation, which is expected to be accretive, and continues pursuing the sale of its Norway Offshore Energy Services business.

negative_highlights: Revenue missed expectations primarily due to Google's policy change deprecating Explore More (impacting over $20 million of ex-TAC in H2) and removal of low-quality publishers.
Average revenue per scaled advertiser remained relatively flat despite a 2% growth in the number of scaled advertisers YoY.
Foreign exchange represented roughly a $7.5 million headwind to adjusted EBITDA, with FX expected to remain a drag for the remainder of 2026.
positive_highlights: xTAC gross profit increased 12% year-over-year to $192.4 million driven by higher ad rates and mix shifts towards premium publishers.
Adjusted EBITDA of $55.5 million came in above the high end of guidance with a margin of 29%.
Strategic win secured with Fox News, expanding partnership across the Fox ecosystem including local news, sports, and weather.
summary: Taboola reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $476.8 million (up 2% YoY), which missed the high end of its guidance due to a Google policy change deprecating Explore More and an aggressive cleanup of low-quality international publishers. Despite these headwinds, xTAC gross profit grew 12% YoY to $192.4 million driven by higher ad rates and mix shifts, while adjusted EBITDA came in at the high end of guidance ($55.5m). Management raised full-year ex-TAC guidance to a midpoint range reflecting these impacts but noted that revenue would have exceeded expectations absent the specific headwinds.

negative_highlights: Blended acquisition cap rate was lower than the prior quarter, though management attributed this to design choices within their Core Plus Fund.
New client rent recapture rates were materially below portfolio averages due to a small number of new tenant deals involving strategic haircuts.
positive_highlights: AFFO per share grew 3.8% to $1.09 in Q2 with YTD growth accelerating to 5.2%.
Full-year investment volume guidance raised from $9.5 billion to $10 billion due to robust pipeline strength.
Global investments totaled approximately $2.6 billion at a weighted average cash yield of 7.3%, including new data center JV activity.
summary: Realty Income reported strong Q2 FY26 results with AFFO per share growing 3.8% to $1.09 and YTD growth accelerating to 5.2%. Management raised full-year guidance for both AFFO (midpoint up $0.02) and investment volume ($10B vs prior $9.5B), citing a robust pipeline, disciplined capital allocation, and successful execution of new funding channels including the Cloud Capital data center JV.

negative_highlights: Reported interactive margin was depressed by the doubling of U.K. tax rates from ~21% to 40%
Sequential revenue growth in interactive decelerated due to the full impact of new taxes
First-half free cash flow conversion is lower than pro forma estimates due to a $7 million restructuring outflow
positive_highlights: Interactive revenue grew 15% and EBITDA grew 13% year-over-year despite the tax hike
U.K. gross gaming revenue increased 40% year-over-year, demonstrating strong underlying demand
Retail solutions achieved adjusted EBITDA margins above 50%, a first for the segment
summary: Second quarter revenue and EBITDA of $61 million and $27 million were in line with expectations but impacted by a near doubling of the U.K. Remote Gaming Duty which negated underlying gross gaming growth. Management raised full-year free cash flow conversion guidance to over 25% from prior guidance, citing pro forma adjustments for one-time working capital outflows rather than operational improvement.

negative_highlights: Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA fell note weakness in of the midpoint of guidance ranges due to lighter model improvement pace in Q2.
Higher compute costs associated with training existing models and new development reduced sequential flow-through to Adjusted EBITDA to 70%.
positive_highlights: Consumer vertical advertiser spend set another record, finishing 28% above Q4 2025 levels despite being a seasonally slow period.
MAX publisher earnings grew double digits quarter-over-quarter with consistent share of waterfalls.
SEC inquiry concluded with no recommended action.
summary: AppLovin reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.92 billion (up 53% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $1.61 billion (up 58% YoY), both falling slightly below the midpoint of guidance ranges due to lighter-than-normal model improvement timing rather than demand weakness or competitive issues. Management noted that Q3 is off to a strong start with new model improvements now live, leading them to raise their full-year outlook and guide for Q3 revenue between $2.055 billion and $2.085 billion (46%-48% YoY growth). The company repurchased approximately 1.14 million shares ($551 million) during the quarter while maintaining a net leverage of roughly 0.1x.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 16% year-over-year due to a $19 million drop in eXtend and AV ancillary revenues.
Daily throughput per stall was 2% lower year-over-year, softer than expected as the network enters 2026.
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $10.6M widened compared to prior periods due to non-charging headwinds.
positive_highlights: Core charging business delivered its 18th consecutive quarter of double-digit year-over-year revenue growth (up 19%).
EVgo announced a strategic agreement to deploy EVgo-branded Superchargers with Tesla, effectively doubling the addressable market.
Mature 350 kW stalls are already operating at mid-2028 levels of daily throughput per stall.
summary: EVgo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $83 million, a 16% year-over-year decrease driven entirely by lower non-charging business (eXtend and AV), while core charging network revenue grew 19%. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $10.6 million in the quarter, aligning with prior guidance but missing market expectations for profitability given the top-line miss.

negative_highlights: Adjusted combined ratio increased to 76.7% from 73.1% YoY, primarily driven by higher attritional losses in the rapidly growing crop book.
Commercial earthquake rates declined more than 20%, and large commercial new business pricing faced pressure below technical levels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 34% driven by opportunistic buybacks and strong underwriting performance across a diversified portfolio.
Crop gross written premium surged 96% YoY, with full-year outlook raised to over $400 million from an initial expectation of ~$280-$350 million (implied).
Company initiated a quarterly dividend of $0.45 per share and repurchased approximately 369k shares at attractive prices.
summary: Palomar Holdings reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with adjusted net income of $63.8 million (up 31% YoY) and gross written premium increasing 27%. Management raised full-year adjusted net income guidance to the range of $270-$280 million, citing record crop growth exceeding initial expectations despite higher attritional losses in that segment.

negative_highlights: Total net product revenue decreased by approximately 34% year-over-year, primarily due to lower demand for ELEVIDYS.
Management explicitly expects total net product revenue in the second half of 2026 to be modestly lower than the first half as new patient cohorts progress through the treatment journey.
Q3 ELEVIDYS revenue is expected to trend lower than Q2 due to variability inherent in one-time gene therapy sales cycles.
positive_highlights: Company delivered GAAP and non-GAAP operating profitability for the quarter with combined R&D and SG&A expenses decreasing significantly year-over-year on a non-GAAP basis.
Cash and investments increased by approximately $197 million during the quarter, strengthening liquidity to fund pipeline initiatives independently.
PMO franchise remains stable with adherence rates exceeding 90% despite competitive pressures expected later in 2027.
summary: Sarepta reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $329 million and total revenues of $401 million, representing a significant year-over-year decline driven by lower demand for ELEVIDYS which performed in line with expectations. Management narrowed its full-year 2026 guidance to the range of $1.2 billion-$1.3 billion (lower than prior) while raising collaboration revenue guidance due to higher contract manufacturing from Roche, and tightened operating expense guidance to reflect disciplined cost management.

negative_highlights: Gross written premium declined 2% year-over-year to $340 million in a challenging direct market environment.
Management expects PIF growth to be relatively flat on a year-over-year basis by end of 2026 if the competitive environment persists.
Average premiums came down somewhat nationally, with management indicating rates are currently overpriced by approximately 3%.
positive_highlights: Net income increased 15% year-over-year to $25 million, generating a 31% annualized return on equity.
Policies in force grew 6% year-over-year to 484,000 despite sequential runoff and competitive pressure.
Partnership and independent agent channels represented approximately 51% of new writings during the quarter.
summary: Root reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $389 million (up 2% YoY) and net income of $25 million (up 15% YoY), though gross written premium declined 2%. Management guided for relatively flat year-over-year Policies in Force growth by the end of 2026 due to a competitive direct market environment, while noting that PIF is currently flat with Q2 levels. The net combined ratio improved to 92%, driven by an expense ratio decline partly attributable to lower performance-based equity compensation.

negative_highlights: Software gross margin contracted from 76% to 71%, reflecting revenue recognition timing on accelerated transition to hosted licensing.
Contribution ACV declined year-over-year due to the completion of initial Gates Foundation funding for Predictive Toxicology.
positive_highlights: ACV grew 27% year-over-year driven by broad-based demand and new product launches including Predictive Toxicology.
Hosted revenue percentage accelerated significantly, rising to 47% of software total in Q2 compared to 31% last year.
Net income turned positive at $6 million following a net loss of $43 million in the prior-year quarter.
summary: Second quarter revenue was $58.9 million with ACV growth of 27% year-over-year to $29.6 million, driven by new products like Predictive Toxicology and the launch of Bunsen. Management raised full-year drug discovery guidance from a prior range of $55M-$65M to $65M-$75M due to a specific $10M milestone payment received from Ajax Therapeutics.

negative_highlights: Issued 11.8 million partnership units for Stellus acquisition, increasing diluted shares outstanding to ~130 million
Leverage ratio elevated pro forma to approximately 2.8x EBITDA following the June acquisition
positive_highlights: Fee-related earnings increased 10% year-over-year to $39 million
Core fee rate expanded three basis points sequentially to 100 bps in Q2
AUM surpassed the milestone of $50 billion at period end
summary: Ridgepost Capital reported Q2 FY2026 results with fee-related earnings of $39 million (up 10% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.24 per share (vs $0.23 in prior year). Fee revenue grew 11% to $81 million, driven by a core fee rate increase to 100 bps and strong AUM growth where fee-paying AUM rose 19% YoY to nearly $35 billion. Management reiterated full-year FRE margin guidance for the mid-40s despite Stellus integration costs.

negative_highlights: Softness among smaller U.S. spine distributors (representing ~20% of revenue) continues with performance below expectations.
Non-GAAP adjusted gross margin was 71.7%, reflecting an unfavorable geography mix during the quarter.
European MDR strategy creates a discrete timing headwind, expected to reduce net sales by approximately $22 million in 2027.
positive_highlights: Global limb reconstruction net sales grew 11% on a constant currency basis led by TrueLok Elevate and Fitbone adoption.
Biologics business moved from double-digit declines to approximately flat year-over-year growth for the second consecutive quarter, indicating stabilization.
CMS restored Medicare reimbursement for bone growth stimulators retroactive to May 18th, removing a meaningful headwind for Therapeutic Solutions.
summary: Orthofix reported Q2 FY2026 net sales growth of approximately 5% on a pro forma constant currency basis and raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $95-$98 million from the prior May outlook. The beat was driven by double-digit growth in global limb reconstruction, stabilization in biologics following declines, and the restoration of Medicare reimbursement for bone growth stimulators which removed a headwind. However, management explicitly noted that profitability trends were impacted by unfavorable geographic mix, credit losses in international markets, and ongoing softness among smaller U.S. spine distributors where performance remains below expectations.

negative_highlights: Beef inflation accelerated throughout the quarter, peaking in June at record-high levels that exceeded original expectations.
Restaurant-level margins declined 90 basis points year-over-year to 23% due to higher food costs and operating expenses.
Management announced a strategic shift away from quarterly guidance citing volatility, leaving investors without near-term visibility on EBITDA targets.
positive_highlights: Same-store sales growth extended to a streak of 22 consecutive quarters with positive comp sales excluding World Cup impact.
Digital ecosystem delivered strong traffic, with comparable app channel sales growing nearly 30% year-over-year.
Company opened 16 new company-operated Shacks in the quarter, exceeding last year's pace and staying on track for a total of 60-65 openings.
summary: Shake Shack reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $417.6 million (up 17.2% YoY) and same-store sales growth of 3.5%, driven by new openings and digital channel strength despite a challenging cost environment. Management delivered results within the revised guidance range but explicitly moved away from providing quarterly outlooks, retaining only full-year annual guidance which remains at the low end due to elevated beef inflation persisting into the second half. While CEO Rob Lynch expressed confidence in long-term resilience and traffic momentum, CFO Michelle Hook noted that restaurant-level margins declined 90 bps YoY as record-high beef costs outweighed operational efficiencies.

negative_highlights: Q4 exabyte growth of 22% was below the prior quarter's pace, though management attributes this to product mix variations rather than a demand slowdown.
Sequential incremental gross margin guidance for Q1 FY27 is lower (80-81%) compared to Q4 actuals (84-85%), reflecting expected quarterly fluctuations.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat high end of guidance driven by a 44% YoY increase in exabyte shipments to 231 EB.
Gross margin expanded significantly year-over-year to 54.4%, aided by favorable pricing and mix shift to higher capacity drives.
Management confirmed strong LTA visibility extending through calendar years 2029-2031 with customers.
summary: Western Digital reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $3.75 billion (up 44% YoY) and EPS of $3.56 (up 109% YoY), beating the high end of guidance with gross margins expanding to 54.4%. Management raised visibility on AI-driven demand, citing strong LTA extensions through 2031, while guiding Q1 FY27 revenue at midpoint growth and EPS between $3.85-$4.15.

negative_highlights: EBIT margin compressed year-over-year by 550 basis points due to deliberate strategic investments over note weakness in-term profitability.
Acquiring margins in Mexico faced compression from device restocking losses and memory chip cost inflation.
positive_highlights: Net revenue surpassed $10 billion for the first time with a robust 50% year-over-year growth rate.
Credit portfolio reached $16.4 billion growing 75% YoY, supported by NPLs at historical lows (7.0% total) and normalized provisions in Brazil.
Brazil commerce conversion improved significantly (+1.1 percentage points YoY) following the free shipping threshold change.
summary: MercadoLibre reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue surpassing $10 billion for the first time with a year-over-year growth of 50%, while income from operations was $683 million representing an EBIT margin of 6.7%. Sequentially, margins were broadly stable but down 550 basis points year-on-year due to strategic investments in Brazil commerce (lower take rates), device restocking costs in Mexico, and energy cost absorption. Management emphasized strong cash generation ($214M adjusted free cash flow) despite high capital expenditures of $441 million.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin remained flat at 6.4% compared to the prior year quarter.
Revenue growth was impacted by timing differences in new contract startups and exits.
No specific quantitative guidance provided for AI/automation (GXO IQ) impact on margins or site count beyond qualitative targets.
positive_highlights: Strongest commercial quarter in three years with new business wins up more than 30% YoY to $410 million, driven by strategic verticals like data centers and aerospace/defense.
Record level of incremental revenue secured for the full year at over $1 billion ($353 million specifically for 2027).
Balance sheet strengthened with net leverage down to 2.6x from 3x, positive free cash flow generation, and resumption of share buybacks.
summary: GXO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.4 billion (up 4% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.59, with an EBITDA margin of 6.4% consistent with the prior year quarter. Management reiterated full-year guidance for organic growth at 4%-5%, adjusted EBITDA between $945 million-$965 million, and diluted EPS between $2.95-$3.15, citing strong commercial momentum in strategic verticals like data centers and aerospace/defense. The company highlighted a record of over $1 billion in incremental revenue secured for 2026 and resumed share repurchases.

negative_highlights: RVO costs remain elevated due to the absence of Small Refinery Exemptions for qualifying refineries in 2025.
Wholesale marketing contribution was partially offset by a $3 million reduction in asphalt results amid price volatility.
Refining margins face headwinds as crude differentials and backwardation curves have flattened compared to Q2 levels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS beat expectations at $5.48 per share driven by stronger refining margins and higher throughput following the Big Spring turnaround completion.
Logistics segment delivered record quarterly adjusted EBITDA of approximately $144 million across all Permian Basin offerings.
Delek Logistics (DKL) reached 80% third-party income on a pro forma basis, reinforcing economic separation strategy.
summary: Delek US reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $170 million ($2.71/share) and adjusted EPS of $5.48 per share. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance range of $520-$560 million, citing strong execution despite Middle East volatility. Management highlighted a successful turnaround at Big Spring refinery with improved reliability and yields.

negative_highlights: Total revenue was below expectations, with the first half described as one of the most consequential periods that did not meet investor hopes for faster acceleration.
Nebulized TYVASO sales remained pressured by increasing competitive dynamics within the inhaled prostacyclin category.
Management explicitly declined to reaffirm or update 2026 revenue growth expectations, noting that while a path exists, it has 'certainly narrowed'.
positive_highlights: Total revenue of $453 million from the core TYVASO franchise, driven by record levels of starts, referrals, total patients, and commercial patients exiting the quarter.
Significant expansion of the sales force to roughly double its size, with representatives deployed in early July to increase engagement frequency across PAH and PH-ILD indications.
Submission of two major new drug applications (sNDA for nebulized TYVASO in IPF and NDA for ralinepag in PAH) representing potential multi-billion dollar growth catalysts.
summary: United Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $783 million, which was essentially flat with the prior quarter and below management's expectations due to competitive dynamics in the nebulized TYVASO category. Management explicitly stated they are not reaffirming or updating any prior 2026 growth guidance despite expecting a stronger second half driven by sales force expansion and record patient metrics. The company highlighted significant clinical progress with sNDA filings for ralinepag (PAH) and nebulized TYVASO (IPF), targeting potential approvals in 2027.

negative_highlights: SG&A expenses increased by 19% year-over-year to $82.1 million, primarily driven by personnel costs from sales force expansion.
R&D expenses were relatively flat at $20.4 million despite ongoing clinical investments in new indications like vitiligo and hidradenitis suppurativa.
positive_highlights: Net product revenues reached $129.9 million with a robust 59% year-over-year growth rate.
Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to the range of $525-$540 million, reflecting strong momentum in H1.
Received FDA approval for ZORYVE cream 0.3% for plaque psoriasis in children down to age two.
summary: Arcutis Biotherapeutics reported Q2 FY26 net product revenues of $129.9 million, a 59% year-over-year increase and a 23% quarter-over-quarter rise driven by strong demand for ZORYVE in plaque psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and seborrheic dermatitis. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance from $480-$495 million to $525-$540 million following the launch of new commercial initiatives including a virtual health platform and expanded sales forces in primary care/pediatrics. Management highlighted FDA approval for ZORYVE cream 0.3% in children as young as two years old, marking significant expansion into pediatric indications.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue growth was minimal at only 0.5% year-over-year.

Significant capital commitment required for SK Hyper (KRW 750 billion) with further investment needed to reach the 15 GW target, raising concerns about direct financial burden despite plans for external financing.
positive_highlights: AIDC revenue surged 92.5% year-over-year driven by the Pangyo Data Center and new Seoul construction.
Operating income expanded significantly due to base effects from prior cybersecurity incident expenses, masking underlying operational strength.
Management confirmed stable shareholder returns with a Q2 dividend of KRW 830 per share.
summary: Consolidated revenue was KRW 4,359 billion (up 0.5% YoY) and operating income reached KRW 566 billion (up 67.3% YoY), driven by the data center business which grew 92.5%. Management established a new subsidiary, SK Hyper, with an initial capital commitment of KRW 750 billion to expand AI infrastructure capacity toward a target of 15 GW.

negative_highlights: HETLIOZ net product sales plummeted 65% year-over-year to $5.6 million due to generic competition and destocking at specialty pharmacies.
NEREUS revenue was constrained to only $1 million in Q2 despite a wholesaler stocking of $15.2 million, reflecting significant uncertainty regarding patient demand and potential returns.
Operating expenses increased 23% year-over-year to $114.3 million due to commercialization spending for new launches and R&D ramp-up.
positive_highlights: Fanapt net product sales increased 23% year-over-year to $36 million, driven by a 31% increase in total prescriptions (TRx) and new-to-brand starts up 32%. Weekly TRx reached an 11-year high of over 2,700.
BYSANTI received FDA approval for bipolar I disorder and schizophrenia with launch expected in the second half of 2026. The company now has six approved products by end-of-2026.
summary: Vanda Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $50.5 million, a decrease of approximately 4% year-over-year and 2% sequentially compared to the prior quarter. The decline was primarily driven by a significant drop in HETLIOZ revenue due to generic competition and shipment timing issues, partially offset by growth from Fanapt bipolar I disorder launch ($36M) and PONVORY ($7.9M). Net loss widened to $62.5 million compared to Q2 2025.

negative_highlights: Water Services revenues grew only approximately 4% sequentially, outpacing a guided decline but remaining below the top-line momentum of other segments.
Management noted that full-year free cash flow potential remains limited in 2026 due to ongoing capital investment needs for infrastructure build-out.
positive_highlights: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $93 million significantly beat the high end of prior guidance range ($77M-$80M).
Water Infrastructure segment delivered record quarterly revenue of $102 million with gross margins expanding to 58% before D&A.
Chemical Technologies segment achieved record-setting revenue of $96 million and sequential gross profit growth of 35%.
summary: Select Water Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $396 million and adjusted EBITDA of $93 million, significantly beating the high end of guidance ($77M-$80M). The company delivered record revenues in its Water Infrastructure segment ($102M) and Chemical Technologies segment ($96M), while outperforming expectations in Water Services. Management raised full-year growth guidance for the Water Infrastructure segment to 25%-30% YoY, citing strong execution across all three operating segments.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance ($373M-$375M) represents a sequential deceleration compared to Q2's growth trajectory.
Gross margin is expected to vary quarter-to-quarter in the near term due to inference costs for beta products not yet monetized.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 48% YoY to $370M, marking the third consecutive quarter of accelerated growth.
Non-GAAP gross profit dollars grew 40% YoY as AI credit monetization contributed for the first full quarter.
Net dollar retention rate remained strong at 136%, with two-thirds of large customers adding full seats at renewal.
summary: Figma reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $370 million (up 48% YoY) and Non-GAAP gross profit growth accelerating to 40%, marking its first full quarter of AI credit monetization. negative_highlights: Caremark membership declined approximately 700,000 year-over-quarter due to the exit from the individual exchange business.
340B program experienced pressure and is expected to be a headwind in 2027 as manufacturers impose restrictions on Covered Entities.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income increased over 35% year-over-year to approximately $5.2 billion.
Health Services segment revenues grew nearly 11%, primarily driven by pharmacy drug mix, brand inflation, and contributions from the Rite Aid transaction.
Management raised full-year EPS guidance by $0.60 (8%) while reiterating a floor for enterprise adjusted operating income in Health Benefits of over $5 billion.
summary: CVS Health reported Q2 FY26 adjusted operating income of $5.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.58, representing increases of over 7% and 40% respectively from the prior year quarter. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for adjusted EPS by $0.60 to a range of $7.90-$8.10 and updated cash flow expectations to at least $11.5 billion, citing strong core performance across all segments including Health Services revenue growth driven by pharmacy drug mix and brand inflation.

negative_highlights: Residential revenue within For Sale was impacted by a shift to the Preferred model (approx. 600 bps) and macro slowdown in mortgage demand.
Restructuring costs of $36 million were incurred related to cost management actions announced during the quarter.
Cash and investments declined from $783M at end-Q1 to $682M at end-Q2 due to buybacks.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 18% YoY, outperforming industry transaction volumes which were flat or declining.
Rentals revenue surged 31% YoY driven by a 42% increase in multifamily properties to an all-time high of 79,000 listings.
For Sale mortgages revenue accelerated significantly with 75% growth and purchase loan origination volume up 95%.
summary: Zillow Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $772 million (up 18% YoY) and adjusted net income of $118 million ($0.52 diluted EPS), both exceeding the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year goals, citing strong execution in Rentals (+31%) and For Sale segments despite a macro headwind on purchase mortgage volume. The company accelerated its transition to the Preferred monetization model (61% adoption) while executing restructuring actions.

negative_highlights: NAV per share decreased $0.88 due to net investment loss driven by unrealized depreciation in the portfolio.
$20 million of accelerated non-recurring expenses were incurred specifically related to the externalization transition process.
Convertible notes conversion reduced principal balance from $35 million to approximately $27 million, diluting share count.
positive_highlights: Received $20 million in gross proceeds from a redeemable promissory note issued to a Magnetar-affiliated entity, mandatorily redeemable via common stock issuance upon future equity financing.
Realized gains of approximately $5.6 million were generated through distributions from CoreWeave and sales of GrabAGun Digital Holdings positions.
Portfolio remains heavily weighted toward high-growth AI infrastructure themes including OpenAI, WHOOP, VAST Data, TensorWave, and ClickHouse.
summary: Neostellar Capital reported a decrease in NAV per share from $14.24 to $13.44 due primarily to net investment losses of approximately $0.88 and accelerated externalization expenses of roughly $20 million, offset by realized gains of about $5.6 million. The company completed its transition to an externally managed structure with Magnetar Advisors effective July 15th and received a $20 million redeemable promissory note from a Magnetar affiliate subsequent to quarter-end.

negative_highlights: No formal revenue guidance provided for the remainder of 2026 or full-year ZUSDURI due to early-stage launch variability.
Management explicitly stated no 'reverse halo' effect on JELMYTO uptake despite strong ZUSDURI growth, citing competitor trials capturing some patients.
Full-year operating expense guidance increased by approximately $15M-$20M reflecting accelerated commercial and pipeline investments.
positive_highlights: ZUSDURI net product revenue reached $50.4M representing a 73% sequential increase and expanding adoption across community practices (now ~55% utilization).
Repeat prescribers nearly doubled to 204, now comprising approximately 45% of writers, indicating strong physician confidence.
Patent extension secured for ZUSDURI/UGN-103 providing protection through July 2044.
summary: UroGen Pharma reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $72.5 million, a significant increase from the prior year driven by ZUSDURI net product revenue of $50.4 million (up 73% sequentially) and JELMYTO revenue of $22 million. Management raised full-year operating expense guidance to $260-$270 million due to accelerated commercial investment while maintaining confidence in reaching profitability with existing capital resources, though no specific ZUSDURI revenue guidance was issued for the remainder of 2026.

negative_highlights: Smart mobile device revenue declined 6% YoY due to reduced handset forecasts driven by memory pricing shortages.
Automotive revenue decreased 13% sequentially and 10% YoY, primarily attributed to customer-led shipment timing shifts rather than demand weakness.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 9% sequentially and 6% year-over-year, exceeding the high-end of guidance ranges for both metrics.
Gross margin expanded nearly 500 bps YoY to approximately 30%, driven by a richer mix in data center technologies like silicon photonics and SiGe.
Silicon photonics revenue is expected to more than double in 2026 compared with the prior year, supported by new design wins and capacity ramping.
summary: GlobalFoundries reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.786 billion (up 6% YoY) and gross margin expansion of nearly 500 bps to ~30%, driven by a mix shift toward high-growth data center applications like silicon photonics which grew 62% YoY. Management raised full-year guidance for the communications infrastructure and data center end-market from high-30s growth to an expected range of 50%-60%. The company also announced its first-ever quarterly cash dividend of $0.12 per share.

negative_highlights: Gross margin on subscription business contracted slightly from 71.1% in the prior year period to 70.2%, reflecting higher veterinary invoice costs.
Average monthly revenue per pet grew only modestly by 9% YoY despite overall volume growth, indicating pricing pressure or mix shifts.
positive_highlights: Subscription adjusted operating margin expanded to 15% from 13.8% in the prior year period.
Net subscription pet growth accelerated significantly with approximately 68,100 new pets acquired via capital deployment compared to historical averages.
Lifetime value of an enrolled pet increased by 25% during the quarter due to disciplined pricing and product enhancements.
summary: Trupanion reported Q2 FY2026 subscription revenue of $276.7 million (up 14% YoY) and total adjusted operating income of $43.3 million (up 24% YoY), beating expectations with a net pet growth of approximately 18,800 pets in the quarter. Management raised full-year guidance for subscription revenue to between $1.124 billion-$1.133 billion and adjusted operating income to between $176 million-$184 million, citing improved unit economics from new product offerings like expanded deductibles and co-insurance options.

negative_highlights: Semiconductor Fabrication Solutions segment revenue declined ~13% YoY due to structural decline in silicon carbide demand with no expected recovery
R&D expenses more than doubled from prior year, though flat vs Q2, indicating potential future cost pressure as new platforms are built out
positive_highlights: Revenue beat top-end of guidance driven by AI-related demand up ~120% YoY in Thermal Processing Solutions segment
Gross margins expanded nearly 400 bps to 50%, supported by operating leverage and parts/services growth (+30%)
Book-to-bill ratio approached 1.4 for the third consecutive quarter with backlog building into FY27
summary: Amtech Systems reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $22.4 million (up 14% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $0.10, beating guidance with gross margins expanding to 50%. Management raised the Q4 revenue outlook range slightly while maintaining Adjusted EBITDA margin expectations in the low-to-mid teens despite a shift from CEO Bob Daigle to Guy Shechter.

negative_highlights: Agentic traffic remains low despite testing, as consumers prioritize end-to-end experience over specific AI sourcing methods.
Take rate expected to flatten or decline slightly in Q3 and lower again in Q4 due to seasonal increases in Dasher costs.
International markets are described as 'minimum viable scale' businesses where market position does not always correlate directly with economic profile.
positive_highlights: Accelerating restaurant growth driven by increased DashPass adoption and improved selection/quality in mature cohorts.
Record paid subscriber growth internationally, with Deliveroo showing the highest year-over-year volume growth seen in recent years.
New verticals (grocery) business is on track to be gross profit positive in the second half of the fiscal year.
summary: DoorDash reported strong underlying growth in Q2 FY26 with accelerating restaurant orders and record paid subscriber additions for DashPass across both domestic and international markets. Management highlighted significant improvements in unit economics driven by higher basket sizes from new verticals (grocery/retail) and improved retention, while noting that the quarter was impacted seasonally lower Dasher costs compared to Q1. The company reaffirmed its strategy of reinvesting efficiency gains into product development like autonomous delivery ('Dot') and AI tools rather than managing for specific take-rate targets.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased significantly year-over-year due to a $48 million milestone payment to Sanofi and qualification manufacturing costs.
SG&A expense rose primarily due to one-time advisory and legal fees associated with closing the Astellas agreement in Q2.
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment in ECLIPSE 2 switch cohort, providing unique data on patients transitioning from bulevirtide with no comparable competitor expected at launch.
SOLSTICE trial week-96 results showed 88% target not detected (TND) and 53% ALT normalization rates for the combination regimen versus monotherapy alone.
Received $240 million upfront payment from Astellas, strengthening cash position to approximately $1.01 billion in equivalents.
summary: Vir Biotechnology reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $238.9 million driven by a $240 million upfront payment from Astellas for the VIR-5500 collaboration and recognized net income of $80.1 million compared to a loss last year, while R&D expenses rose 40% YoY due to milestone payments and manufacturing costs. Management completed enrollment in ECLIPSE 2 (switch cohort) with top-line data expected from ECLIPSE 1 later this year, citing robust week-96 SOLSTICE trial results showing 88% target not detected rates. The company maintains a cash runway into the second half of 2028 following significant capital raises.

negative_highlights: High-volatile (high vol) metallurgical coal market remains weak due to oversupply, forcing the company to idle one of three Stonecoal sections at Elk Creek.
Diesel fuel costs increased quarterly by roughly 33% in Q2 and averaged $4.64/gallon, adding approximately $3/ton to produced coal costs compared to start-of-year levels.
Brook Mine project timeline pushed out with initial production now estimated for late 2027 or later due to supply chain constraints on large power transformers.
positive_highlights: Operational safety improved significantly with a 54% reduction in total reportable incident rate year-to-date compared to Q2 FY2025.
Company repurchased more than $66 million of Class A shares, representing over 8% of outstanding equity, utilizing record liquidity levels above $400 million.
Low-vol coal production portfolio is expanding with new underground sections at Maben and Berwind expected to add roughly 1.5 million tons annually by late 2027.
summary: Ramaco Resources reported Q2 FY2026 results where the company maintained full-year cost per ton guidance despite a $3/ton increase in coal costs driven by higher diesel prices averaging $4.64/gallon. Management highlighted that operational safety improved with a 58% reduction in incidents compared to the prior year and noted record liquidity of over $400 million following share buybacks exceeding 8%. Forward guidance remains intact for low-vol production growth, though high-vol output is expected to decline as the company idles sections at Elk Creek.

negative_highlights: Oil prices remain volatile with supply disruptions from the Iran conflict weighing on global inventories, though management views this as temporary rationing.
