negative_highlights: Comparable funeral revenue declined 2.4% YoY due to reduced mortality rates, with Florida cited as having significant volume decline.
Full-year revenue guidance was lowered by approximately $5 million primarily because fewer acquisitions occurred than initially anticipated in the first half of the year.
Adjusted free cash flow for H1 decreased compared to prior year ($13.8M vs $20.3M) driven by higher capital expenditures.
positive_highlights: Adjusted consolidated EBITDA grew 3.1% YoY to $33.3 million, expanding margin by 70 bps despite lower funeral volumes.
Average price per preneed interment right sold increased significantly by 17.3%, demonstrating strong pricing power and sales execution.
Funeral volume returned to positive growth in July after a declining negative trend throughout the first half of the year.
summary: Carriage Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $102.9 million (up 0.8% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.78 (up 5.4%), beating expectations despite a 3.5% decline in funeral volume due to softer mortality trends. Management updated full-year guidance, lowering the revenue midpoint by approximately $5 million primarily due to acquisition timing delays while maintaining profitability targets near historical ranges. The outlook for H2 suggests low single-digit volume growth returning after negative first-half performance.

negative_highlights: Take rate declined 200 bps due to favorable mix shift toward higher-value items
Q3 revenue growth guidance (12-14%) lags GMV growth (17-19%) due to take rate impact
Active buyer growth of 11% is below GMV growth, indicating AOV-driven sales
positive_highlights: GMV up 22% to all-time high $617 million; fourth straight quarter above 20% growth
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 290 bps to 7%, above prior guidance
Full-year guidance raised with EBITDA margin reaching 8.5% at midpoint
summary: Q2 FY2026 GMV hit an all-time high of $617 million, up 22% YoY (fourth consecutive quarter above 20%), with revenue up 17% to $193 million. Adjusted EBITDA reached $13.5 million (7% margin), expanding 290 bps YoY and beating prior guidance. Active buyers rose 11% to 1.1 million, and the company raised its full-year revenue and EBITDA outlook while guiding Q3 GMV to $610-620 million. Management highlighted Athena automation, AI pricing, and high-value item growth as key drivers.

negative_highlights: North America comparable sales declined 8.3% due to reduced order volume and lower customer acquisition.
Revised 2026 outlook: global system-wide sales decline 2%-4% and adjusted EBITDA lowered to $180-$190 million.
Transformation taking longer than expected; management acknowledged 'we must execute better and move faster'.
positive_highlights: International comps up 1.5%, seventh consecutive quarter of positive comps; U.K. up 10%, Korea up 9%.
Papa Rewards members surpassed 42 million, with loyalty customers outperforming non-loyalty by 12 percentage points.
Sandwiches almost fully offset Papadias removal, opening a new food category.
summary: Papa John's Q2 2026 North America comps declined 8.3% while international comps grew 1.5%; total performance pressured by softer consumer and heavy QSR discounting. Management revised 2026 guidance to global system-wide sales decline of 2%-4% and adjusted EBITDA of $180-$190 million, including an incremental $18 million investment. Transformation is taking longer than expected; management announced leadership changes and expects 200-250 of planned closures to occur in 2026.

negative_highlights: Consolidated order growth negative due to $364 million acquired Maritime backlog last year and $82 million non-repeat Navy orders
NRG continues weak with renewables markets soft and no recovery expected until FY2027
Utility segment adjusted EBIT margins declined 130 basis points due to NRG
positive_highlights: Record backlog of $1.54 billion with all segments book-to-bill over 100%
Adjusted EPS up 37.5% to $2.20 and full-year guidance raised to $8.30-$8.40
Test orders up 42% and Doble orders up 30% in the quarter
summary: ESCO Technologies reported Q3 FY2026 with 14% sales growth (8% organic), adjusted EPS of $2.20 (up 37.5%), and record backlog of $1.54 billion. Book-to-bill was 1.21 across all segments, with test orders up 42% and Doble orders up 30%. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $8.30-$8.40, up 38%-39% from prior year, and management remains confident in long-term demand drivers across aerospace, utility, and test markets.

negative_highlights: FY2027 subscription ARR growth guided to 18%, down from 23%
FY2026 ARR growth benefited ~1 point from DX acquisition
Management cites macro, fiscal policy, and geopolitical uncertainty as reasons for prudent guide
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 28% to $1.8 billion, cloud up 31%
RPO up 44% year-over-year to $4.8 billion
Rovo adopters grow ARR at more than 2x the rate of non-adopters
summary: Atlassian reported Q4 FY2026 total revenue of $1.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year, with cloud revenue growing 31% to $1.2 billion. RPO grew 44% to $4.8 billion, and GAAP operating margin was 12%. Management highlighted record enterprise deal activity, with $3M+ ARR customers growing over 50% and $5M+ ARR customers growing over 70%. Guidance for FY2027 subscription ARR growth is 18%, down from 23% in FY2026, reflecting prudence on macro uncertainty and the DX acquisition boost lapping.

negative_highlights: Gross margins are expected to decline in the back half as product mix returns to historical averages (mid-13% range).
Domestic retail activity and inventory levels remain flat due to geopolitical tensions, elevated fuel prices, and low consumer confidence.
EPS outlook includes approximately $0.25 of one-time transaction-related expenses from the Omars acquisition.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 12.1% year-over-year and 32.7% sequentially driven by steady production rates.
Gross profit margin expanded to 15%, aided by disciplined labor cost management and production efficiencies.
Net income reached $7.3 million with diluted EPS of $0.63, a significant increase from Q1's $0.05.
summary: Miller Industries reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $240 million (up 12% YoY) and EPS of $0.63, driven by sequential growth but impacted by product mix normalization following elevated inventory levels. Management maintained full-year guidance for revenue between $850-$900 million ($250M per quarter in H2), noting that gross margins will likely settle into the mid-13% range due to a return of chassis-to-body ratios, despite operational efficiency gains.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance midpoint implies a sequential decline from Q2 level
Gross margin benefited from one-time refund; normalized margins expected in high 30s%
Adjusted EBITDA remains negative at -$4 million
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $55M, up 56% YoY with record 17,000+ sensors shipped
Rev8 launch driving multiple million-dollar-plus orders and strong customer feedback
Capital raises provide full funding for operating plan to profitability
summary: Ouster delivered record Q2 2026 revenue of $55 million, up 56% year-over-year, with over 17,000 sensors shipped, marking the 14th consecutive quarter of product revenue growth. GAAP gross margin was 49%, aided by a one-time refund of ~1,000 basis points, while Adjusted EBITDA improved to -$4 million. Q3 revenue guidance of $54.5-57.5 million implies a slight sequential decline as Rev8 ramps to production, and full-year guidance remains unchanged. The company raised substantial capital, ending the quarter with $263 million in cash and no debt, and subsequently raised ~$191 million net, which management says fully funds its operating plan.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance lowered by ~$40M midpoint due to an estimated $25M impact from Middle East travel disruptions.
Buyback activity was intentionally conservative this quarter, with only ~650k shares repurchased despite having authorization remaining.
TFS growth remains burdened by ongoing conflict-related headwinds in Europe and Gulf countries.
positive_highlights: Gross revenue less network fees grew +51% YoY to $624 million, exceeding expectations despite macro headwinds.
Organic growth of payments-based revenue less network fees remained consistent at +11%, validating the durable business model.
International expansion accelerated with Shift4 One live in 12 countries and new POS launches in Spain and Australia.
summary: Shift4 delivered Q2 FY26 results above guidance with gross revenue of $1.29 billion (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $284 million (up 39%), though the company lowered its full-year outlook by approximately $40M midpoint due to Middle East travel disruptions impacting TFS. Management raised Q3 guidance for GRLNF ($650M), Adjusted EBITDA ($310M), and Free Cash Flow ($180M) while maintaining a conservative capital allocation stance with limited buybacks in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Higher O&M, depreciation, and interest expenses offset some earnings growth.
Missouri West residential rates expected to rise above inflation due to infrastructure investment needs in that jurisdiction.
No specific revenue or margin figures provided for the quarter beyond EPS drivers.
positive_highlights: Adjusted earnings beat prior-year expectations by $0.06 per share ($0.88 vs $0.82).
Weather-normalized demand grew 3.3% year-to-date driven by commercial and industrial usage from data center ramps.
Management reaffirmed full-year guidance with a specific Q3 EPS outlook of 50%-53%.
summary: Evergy reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted earnings of $0.88 per share versus the prior year's $0.82, driven by load growth and large customer revenues from data centers like Digital Realty and Panasonic. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance with a third-quarter EPS outlook of 50%-53% against a midpoint target of $4.24 for the year. The company highlighted strong pipeline momentum with at least one additional ESA expected in 2027, supporting long-term load growth targets.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance unchanged at JPY 530B despite strong Q1 due to Kioxia volatility
Infrastructure segment profit down JPY 25.1B YoY, mainly due to absence of prior-year gains
Renewable energy profit down due to regulatory restrictions
positive_highlights: Q1 net income record high at JPY 280.8B, up JPY 173.5B YoY
Core earnings power improved; ORIX Europe AUM at record highs, all transportation lines up YoY
Interim dividend raised to JPY 107.27 per share
summary: ORIX reported record first-quarter net income of JPY 280.8 billion, up JPY 173.5 billion year-over-year, driven by Kioxia-related gains and strong core earnings. Full-year net income guidance remains at JPY 530 billion, but first-half profit is forecast at JPY 840 billion, including JPY 540 billion of Kioxia gains. The dividend policy was revised to exclude Kioxia gains from adjusted profit, resulting in an interim DPS of JPY 107.27. Management expressed confidence in growing adjusted profits in the second half.

negative_highlights: Net income $14.6M, though up from $9.5M, remains modest
Speedway Phase I ramp intentionally cautious to avoid operational issues
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $217.8M, up 8% sequentially
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 53%, up from ~50% in Q1
Second straight guidance raise; CapEx guidance raised $100M
summary: WaterBridge reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $217.8 million (up 8% sequentially) and Adjusted EBITDA of $115.8 million (up ~12% sequentially), with Adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 53%. Management raised full-year 2026 volume and Adjusted EBITDA guidance for the second consecutive quarter and raised CapEx guidance by $100 million to $530-$590 million. The quarter included the closing of the Ranger acquisition, announcement of the NDB Landfill acquisition, and acceleration of the New Devon project. Speedway Phase I launched on schedule in July with volumes expected to ramp toward ~100,000 barrels per day and exit the year above that.

negative_highlights: Constant currency revenue declined 6.3%, with adjusted decline of 3.6% excluding Byte and dealer inventory reductions.
OIS segment revenue fell 13.2% as reported; SureSmile declined double digits.
EDS volumes declined in Americas and EMEA, with continued distributor inventory reductions.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS flat at $0.52 despite revenue decline, aided by $0.17 tariff refund benefit.
Operating cash flow more than doubled to $99 million from $48 million.
Wellspect revenue grew 7.1% as reported on new product strength.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 4.1% as reported (6.3% constant currency), with adjusted EPS flat at $0.52, supported by $44 million in tariff refunds. The company maintained its 2026 outlook of $3.5-$3.6 billion net sales and adjusted EPS of $1.40-$1.50, excluding tariff refunds. Management expects Q3 earnings to be below Q2, with improvement weighted to Q4 as investments ramp.

negative_highlights: Hedging limited participation in higher oil prices during the quarter.
Natural gas differentials remain highly negative at -$8.14 per Mcf due to takeaway constraints.
Capital spending guidance raised for 2026 to $158-$178 million, above previous plan.
positive_highlights: Sequential production increased 3% to 19,990 BOE/d, within guidance.
Realized oil price increased 38% to $95.45 per barrel.
Leverage improved to 1.7x and liquidity increased to $226 million after equity offering.
summary: Ring Energy reported Q2 2026 production of 19,990 BOE/d, up 3% sequentially, with realized oil prices up 38% to $95.45/barrel, but hedges limited upside. The company completed an equity offering, reducing debt to about $360 million and leverage to 1.7 times. Management raised second-half 2026 oil sales guidance midpoint by about 2% and lowered LOE midpoint guidance slightly, while increasing full-year 2026 capital spending to $158-$178 million. Initial 2027 guidance shows BOE volume growth of about 10% and a ~10% midpoint reduction in capital spending.

negative_highlights: Full-year guidance of $330-$415 million remains wide and unchanged.
R&D expenses increased from $72M to $79M due to ATTC investments.
Recent quarter's FRUZAQLA U.S. growth not highlighted; previous Medicare impact noted.
positive_highlights: ELUNATE and SULANDA grew over 40% in China, driving strong product sales.
FRUZAQLA ex-U.S. in-market sales grew 70% on rapid geographic expansion.
Company remains profitable with $16 million net income and $1.4 billion cash reserve.
summary: HUTCHMED reported strong H1 2026 results with oncology revenue of $162 million, up 23% year-over-year, and China product sales growth led by ELUNATE and SULANDA at over 40%. FRUZAQLA ex-U.S. in-market sales grew 70%, and the company remained profitable with net income of $16 million. Full-year guidance was reiterated at $330-$415 million, with management confident of at least beating the lower end and potentially exceeding the high end with business development and milestones. The company advanced its ATTC pipeline with two assets in Phase I and a third IND cleared, and expects key data readouts from SAFFRON and SANOVO in H2.

negative_highlights: Three properties previously generated $181,000 in quarterly rent have expired; most replacement rents will not commence until Q1-Q2 FY27.
Acquisitions this quarter included assets with shorter remaining lease terms (e.g., a vet clinic at 8.75% cap rate) which pulled the weighted average acquisition term below historical averages.
Slippage is expected to approximate 2% of adjusted cash revenue for H1 FY26, an improvement from prior forecasts but still present.
positive_highlights: Raised full-year AFFO per share guidance range from $1.29-$1.33 to $1.32-$1.34 driven by improved NOI margins and rent recaptures north of 115% on renewals.
Successfully re-tenanted a former Walgreens property to Amazon, generating significant value with zero tenant improvement allowance despite similar rent levels.
Portfolio optimization continues with disciplined dispositions of tertiary assets (e.g., Dollar Trees) improving overall real estate quality and diversification.
summary: FrontView reported Q2 FY26 adjusted cash revenue of $16.4 million and adjusted cash NOI run rate of $16.6 million following the commencement of rent from a former Walgreens property converted to Amazon. Management raised its full-year 2026 AFFO per share guidance range to $1.32-$1.34 (from $1.29-$1.33) and increased net investment guidance to $120 million, citing strong portfolio performance and accretive capital deployment.

negative_highlights: Gross premiums earned declined year-over-year due to competitive pricing pressure in Florida commercial residential
Policy count decreased by 1.4% quarter-over-quarter as the business transitions back toward growth
Commercial premium volume fell despite policy count increases, indicating rate compression
positive_highlights: Record net income of $61.7 million with diluted EPS of $2.05
Combined ratio improved significantly to 64.9% from 72.9%
Operating cash flow reached a record $166.5 million
summary: Heritage Insurance Holdings reported record Q2 FY2026 net income of $61.7 million and diluted EPS of $2.05, driven by a significant improvement in the combined ratio to 64.9% from 72.9%. Gross premiums earned declined slightly year-over-year due to competitive pricing pressure on Florida commercial residential business, while personal residential premiums grew modestly. Management highlighted substantial operating cash flow of $166.5 million and record book value per share growth.

negative_highlights: Ironton production of 4.5 million pounds was down from the prior quarter
Compounding asset runs only five days a week, with 24/7 expected in Q4
Breakeven target remains second-half, indicating still not achieved
positive_highlights: Revenue grew for the sixth consecutive quarter, up substantially from a year ago
New Jersey approved PureFive as recycled content, accelerating brand qualifications
Turnaround completed ahead of schedule and below budget; new daily throughput record in June
summary: PureCycle reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $4.5 million, up substantially year-over-year, with production of 4.5 million pounds of PureFive and about 5 million pounds of feedstock processed. The company completed a major turnaround ahead of schedule and below budget, set a new daily throughput record in June, and brought compounding in-house. Management reiterated the second-half Ironton breakeven target, citing accelerated customer qualifications following New Jersey's approval of PureFive as recycled content and commercial production of Procter & Gamble's Downy caps, with Tide caps and Vicks ZzzQuil lids scheduled for Q3 and Q4.

negative_highlights: Second half revenue may not fully reflect underlying demand due to NRDL-related commercial dynamics
XACDURO growth constrained by supply constraints
positive_highlights: Net product revenue grew 11% sequentially to $105.8 million, with business commercially profitable
zoci potential best-in-class ADC, with confirmed ORR 38.2% in extrapulmonary NEC vs ~18% for current regimens
Cash at $717.5 million, providing flexibility for investments
summary: Q2 2026 net product revenue grew 11% sequentially to $105.8 million, with the commercial business remaining profitable. Management emphasized pipeline progress, including zoci moving toward global pivotal trials and expected U.S. accelerated approval in 2028, plus ZL-1503 first-in-human data later this year. They guided for stable operating expenses and expect a return to meaningful growth in 2027, with potential first U.S. product launch in 2028. The tone is confident but acknowledges near-term revenue impact from NRDL dynamics and supply constraints.

negative_highlights: Gold price fell by 13% (nearly $600/oz) in Q2 FY2026 due to risk-off sentiment related to the Iran war, directly impacting revenue.
Management explicitly stated they kept full-year guidance wide and would not guarantee narrowing it for Q3, citing uncertainty around asset ramp-ups like Pedra Branca.
positive_highlights: Total revenue and adjusted EBITDA more than doubled year-over-year to $17.3 million (H1) and $5.6 million (Q2), respectively, driven by record land agreement proceeds.
First-half production of 3,677 GEOs exceeded the expected weighting for a low-price environment, indicating strong underlying volume growth from assets like Vareš and County Line ramping up.
summary: Gold Royalty Corp reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $5.6 million, representing a more than doubling from the prior year quarter but missing its own H1 guidance midpoint due to gold prices falling 13% in the second quarter. Management maintained full-year production guidance at 7,500-9,300 GEOs despite the lower price environment and noted that first-half results were better than expected for a low-price scenario.

negative_highlights: North American retail crop nutrient volumes declined notably in Q2 for phosphate (down ~10%) and nitrogen (down ~7%).
Nitrogen sales volumes were impacted by no production from Trinidad/New Madrid, planned maintenance at Carseland, and deferred customer purchases.
Phosphate margins faced pressure from elevated sulfur costs described as unsustainable.
positive_highlights: First-half adjusted EBITDA increased 6% YoY driven by strong potash execution and retail proprietary product growth.
Potash sales volumes raised at bottom end to 14.2-14.8 million tons due to strength in the order book and summer fill program response.
Retail proprietary products gross margin expanded significantly, offsetting declines in commodity fertilizer volumes.
summary: Nutrien reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $2.4 billion and first-half adjusted EBITDA of $3.5 billion (up 6% YoY). Management raised the bottom end of potash sales volume guidance to a range of 14.2-14.8 million tons while maintaining nitrogen and phosphate volume guidance, citing strong demand in major markets despite softer retail commodity volumes. Capital expenditure guidance was lowered by $50 million to $1.95-$2.05 billion as the company accelerates share repurchases.

negative_highlights: Global LNG exports declined by approximately 3 million tons year-over-year due to the Strait of Hormuz conflict and constraints on Middle East supply.
LNG tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz remained under 10% of pre-conflict levels, creating significant geopolitical risk premiums in global benchmarks (TTF/JKM).
China's LNG imports declined by approximately 3 million tons year-over-year during the first half as it utilized fuel-switching and storage withdrawals to manage supply shocks.
positive_highlights: Production increased by approximately 20% year-over-year to 672 TBtu driven by Stage 3 ramp-up, early train completions, and reliability improvements.
Management raised full-year EBITDA guidance midpoint by $650 million and DCF guidance by $550 million due to production outperformance and higher margins.
summary: Cheniere Energy reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 billion and distributable cash flow (DCF) of $1.2 billion, driven by a production increase to 672 TBtu (+20% YoY), higher marketing margins, and optimization activities. Management raised full-year guidance for consolidated adjusted EBITDA to $7.9-$8.4 billion and DCF to $5.3-$5.8 billion, with the new low end exceeding the prior high end due to production outperformance (approx 0.5M tons) and sustained elevated margins.

negative_highlights: Mattress Firm adjusted gross margin down 240 bps to 33.3%
International operating margin down 120 bps to 12.4%
July 4th holiday described as a 'dud' and industry demand down mid-to-high single digits
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 9% to $0.58, a record second quarter
North American operating margin up 400 bps to 26.7% on synergies
Leverage back to 2.99x, record operating cash flow of $236M
summary: Somnigroup (formerly Tempur Sealy) reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $1.8 billion, adjusted EPS of $0.58 (up 9% YoY), and adjusted EBITDA of $297 million. North America margins expanded sharply (gross +680 bps, operating +400 bps) on synergies, but Mattress Firm margins fell on financing and investments. Full-year EPS guidance was $2.85-$3.15, implying mid-single-digit industry decline and low-single-digit like-for-like growth for most segments; management noted a weak July 4th period and ongoing ERP challenges at Dreams, but reaffirmed confidence and highlighted the Leggett & Platt deal on track to close in Q3.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 35.9%, down 485 basis points year-over-year due to trade spend from national club programs and product mix shifts.
SG&A expenses increased as a percentage of sales, rising 179 basis points primarily due to higher marketing costs for the back-to-school program.
Baby pouch sales decelerated sequentially in Q2 compared to Q1 attributed to timing impacts during cooler resets.
positive_highlights: Net sales surged 42.3% year-over-year driven by volume-led growth across baby (73%) and kid segments.
Household penetration grew significantly to 6.2%, up from 5% a year ago, with repeat rates increasing among households with kids.
New meat and legume protein pouches were highly incremental at certain retailers, contributing over 85,000 new distribution points in the baby segment.
summary: Once Upon a Farm reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $85.4 million, representing a 42.3% year-over-year increase driven by volume and distribution gains. Management raised full-year guidance for net sales to $327-$335 million (up from $313-$323 million) and adjusted EBITDA to a loss of $3-$4.5 million, while acknowledging that gross margin is expected to be around 40% due to mix shifts toward lower-margin snacks and trade spend timing.

negative_highlights: Hardware gross margin declined 110 basis points due to pricing pressure and client mix shifts.
Management paused M&A activity for the remainder of FY26 to focus on organic execution under the 'One Insight' plan.
Q4 outlook remains prudent with potential headwinds from memory price increases, supply chain disruptions, and tough year-over-year comparisons.
positive_highlights: Adjusted diluted earnings per share rose 44% YoY to $3.86.
Infrastructure hardware revenue grew over 20%, reflecting strong client investment in servers and networking for AI workloads.
Cloud gross profit surged 39% driven by SaaS, IaaS growth, and contributions from the Securo acquisition.
summary: Insight Enterprises reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of $2.4 billion (up 15% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.86 (up 44%). The company raised its full-year guidance for gross profit growth to an 8%-10% range and adjusted EPS midpoint to approximately $12.45, citing strong first-half momentum driven by AI infrastructure demand.

negative_highlights: Supply constraints and capacity challenges spreading broadly
Lead times stretching, causing expedite requests to go unsupported
positive_highlights: Net sales beat high end of guidance, up 38% YoY to $1.485B
June quarter book-to-bill well above 1, strongest bookings quarter in ~4 years
September quarter EPS guidance up 165.7% YoY and 22.4% sequentially at midpoint
summary: Microchip reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $1.485 billion, up 13.2% sequentially and 38% year-over-year, beating the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.76, $0.07 above the midpoint, with gross margin at 63.8%, operating margin at 35.1%, and strong free cash flow. Data center sales soared 97.8% year-over-year, with full-year 2026 data center sales expected to reach ~$1 billion, up 69%. September quarter guidance is for net sales up 8% sequentially and non-GAAP EPS of $0.91-$0.95, with gross margin forecast at 66%-67%, above the long-term target of 65%. Bookings were the strongest in about four years, and distribution inventory correction is complete, with lead times stretching due to capacity constraints.

negative_highlights: Tobacco segment operating income fell from $35.7 million to $3.5 million year-over-year
Consolidated net loss of $5 million versus net income of $8.5 million in prior year
Ingredients segment operating loss of $700,000 with persistent consumer headwinds and high fixed costs
positive_highlights: Full-year customer demand expectations consistent with fiscal year sales plan
Net debt decreased ~$52 million year-over-year to slightly over $1 billion
No expectation of large inventory write-downs in tobacco due to management initiatives
summary: In Q1 FY2027, Universal Corp reported consolidated revenue of $524 million, down 12% year-over-year, and an operating income of $2.3 million versus $33.8 million in the prior year, driven by a steep decline in tobacco segment operating income from $35.7 million to $3.5 million due to oversupply and delayed customer watching. The ingredients segment posted a $700,000 operating loss as consumer headwinds and high fixed costs persisted. Management maintains full-year customer demand is consistent with plan, with second-half-weighted shipments expected, and sees less risk of large inventory write-downs. The company noted a net loss of $5 million versus a net income of $8.5 million last year, but highlighted net debt reduction of $52 million and a $1.1 billion liquidity position.

negative_highlights: Atera launch is expected to moderate Xenium and Visium sales, with some customers delaying orders
Q3 consumables expected to step down sequentially due to Atera order timing
No quantification of Atera consumables revenue yet
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue $151M, up 3% YoY excluding settlement revenue; consumables up 7%
Atera order flow exceeds initial expectations, with 40+ instruments planned for H2
Xenium and Visium consumables grew sequentially after Atera launch
summary: Revenue for Q2 FY2026 was $151 million, or $149.4 million excluding non-recurring settlement revenue, up 3% YoY. Total consumables revenue grew 7%, with strong growth in Chromium and Xenium utilization. The company launched Atera, a new spatial platform, and reported very strong early order flow exceeding initial expectations, with 40+ instruments expected to ship in the second half, mostly in Q4. Management raised guidance, expecting a sequential step-up in Q3 to Q4 revenue driven by Atera instrument sales and consumables, while noting some near-term cannibalization of Xenium and Visium orders.

negative_highlights: Management booked a $23 million reserve build on the remaining private legacy portfolio because the pace of improvement in Q2 was 'shy' of expectations.
Net income for the consumer lending segment declined slightly to $27 million from $26 million year-over-year due to higher marketing and origination costs associated with volume growth.
Share repurchases were lower than expected this quarter as management paused note under a 10b5-1 plan while growing at current rates.
positive_highlights: Combined originations grew by more than 60% year-over-year to $815 million driven by refinance and private loan demand.
Private charge-off rates decreased from 1.9% in Q1 to 1.8% in Q2, with delinquency improvements across the portfolio.
FFELP segment saw significant credit normalization with 91-plus delinquencies dropping more than 200 basis points year-over-year.
summary: Navient reported Q2 FY26 core earnings of $0.29 per share and total originations up over 60% year-over-year to $815 million. Management noted that while credit metrics improved, the pace of improvement in private delinquency rates moderated during the quarter leading to a specific reserve build on legacy loans. The company adopted fair value accounting for new in-school loans starting Q3 and classified nearly 10% of its legacy portfolio as held for sale.

negative_highlights: Restaurant margin decreased 66 basis points to 16.4%
EPS declined 0.7% to $1.85
Fourth quarter same-store sales expected to be negatively impacted by 75 bps due to holiday shifts
positive_highlights: Comparable sales up 6.2% with 3% traffic growth
Average weekly sales exceeded $175,000 for the first time
Full-year commodity inflation guidance reduced to ~5%
summary: Q2 revenue approached $1.7 billion, up 11.1%, with comparable sales up 6.2% and traffic up 3%. Restaurant margin dollars rose 6.9% though margin as a percentage of sales declined 66 bps. Diluted EPS decreased 0.7% to $1.85. Commodity inflation guidance was lowered to approximately 5% for the full year, and the company plans a 1% menu price increase in Q4. Development remains on track with 35 company openings planned for 2026.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses totaled $41.9 million, well above gross profit
Still early stages; no formal guidance for new acquisitions
Margin expansion depends on volume and mix, particularly Blue Ops
positive_highlights: Revenue up 520% YoY to $20.2 million
Gross margin improved to 16.1%, up from 11.6% YoY
Expect strong sequential revenue ramp in Q3 and Q4
summary: Red Cat reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $20.2 million, up 520% year-over-year, with gross margin improving to 16.1% from 11.6% a year ago and 12.7% sequentially. Management highlighted continued scaling, new product introductions (Hellcat, Blue Ops Variant 7), and strong demand, expecting a 'dramatic' revenue ramp in Q3 and Q4. Cash stood at $325.6 million, and they reaffirmed a focus on profitability in 2027.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue growth expected to decelerate to ~1% YoY due to tough comps
Gross margin declined to 88% from 91% due to higher AI compute spend
AI Search revenue not recognized in Q1 and only modest in Q2
positive_highlights: Q1 results beat guidance: revenue beat by 3% and EBITDA by 8% vs high end
Full-year revenue guidance raised by $6M
AI adoption: active AI users nearly half of prescribers, prompt volume up 25% QoQ, Scribe users up 10x in July
summary: Doximity reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $157M, up 7% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $75M (48% margin), both exceeding the high end of guidance. The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $6M to $671-$681M, while maintaining EBITDA guidance at $309-$329M as it accelerates AI investments. AI Search launched late April, with first cohort onboarded and majority of contracted revenue expected to be recognized in Q3. Q2 guidance implies 1% YoY growth due to tough comparison, with stronger growth expected in Q3.

negative_highlights: North America organic sales declined 8.4%, tequila fell ~21%
Organic net sales down 2% with U.S. spirits and Chinese white spirits weak
Impairment charges of $1.5 billion and restructuring charges of $0.9 billion
positive_highlights: Organic operating profit increased 2% despite a 2% organic sales decline
Free cash flow rose 16% to $3.2 billion, reducing net debt by $1.4 billion
Europe, LAC, and Africa delivered strong growth, with India up 7%
summary: Diageo reported a mixed fiscal 2026: organic net sales declined 2% (down ~0.5% ex-Chinese white spirits), but organic operating profit grew 2% and EPS pre-exceptionals rose 0.7% to $1.653. Free cash flow rose $463 million to $3.2 billion, net debt fell to $20.5 billion, and leverage improved to 3.1x from 3.4x. North America suffered an 8.4% organic sales decline with tequila down 21%, while Europe, LAC, and Africa grew. Management announced a $1.2 billion restructuring plan (over two years) with around $1 billion in savings, and will provide fiscal 2027 guidance at the Capital Markets Day.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million missed original guidance, pressured by ~12% quarter-over-quarter cost inflation in coiled tubing.
Two large-diameter coiled tubing units (17% of fleet) were out of service in Q2; one remains down and is not expected back until near year-end.
Q3 revenue guidance midpoint ($138 million) implies a decline from Q2, with EBITDA expected flat to modestly down.
positive_highlights: Completion Tools revenue increased 44% quarter-over-quarter to $37.1 million, with international revenue up 17% in the first half.
Q2 revenue of $141.8 million was within original guidance and rig count rose from 543 to 573 during the quarter.
Cementing jobs increased 13% sequentially to 1,155, and full-year CapEx was trimmed to the middle-to-low end of the $20-$30 million range.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $141.8 million, within guidance, but adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million missed guidance due to margin compression and two large-diameter coiled tubing units (17% of the fleet) out of service. Coiled tubing revenue fell 2% to $26.4 million, while Completion Tools revenue surged 44% to $37.1 million on strong international sales. Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $133-$143 million and flat-to-modestly-down EBITDA as the second CT unit stays down near year-end and cost inflation outpaces pricing.

negative_highlights: Metallurgical guidance lowered by $2.50 at the midpoint due to ongoing weak global steel demand from Middle East hostilities.
PRB segment volumes declined qoq (10.2M vs 11.9M tons) attributed to low natural gas prices and spring shoulder season weakness.
DTA outage impact remains uncertain with capacity constraints at the terminal, though management deems it manageable.
positive_highlights: High CV Thermal and Metallurgical segments delivered solid operational performance with significant cost reductions (Metallurgical cash costs down ~$7/ton qoq).
Leer South insurance claim settled for full limits loss ($155M total, $88M recognized in Q2 free cash flow), removing a major overhang.
High CV Thermal segment added 2 million tons to its sold position and is now nearly fully contracted with ~31 million tons.
summary: Core Natural Resources reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $126 million ($2.51 diluted EPS) and Adjusted EBITDA of $324 million, driven by strong operational performance in High CV Thermal and Metallurgical segments alongside a one-time insurance settlement of $155 million for the Leer South claim. Management adjusted full-year guidance upward on cash costs for High CV Thermal ($39-$40.50/ton) due to inflationary pressures but lowered guidance for the Metallurgical segment's SEC cash cost by $2.50 (midpoint range now $86-$91/ton). The company returned $68 million in capital via share repurchases, exceeding its Q1 return of $47 million.

negative_highlights: Expect Q3 consumables revenue to be down sequentially due to Atera transitions
Atera instrument placements concentrated in Q4, creating back-half weighted uncertainty
Xenium and Visium consumables growth likely to moderate as customers await Atera

Total consumables revenue up 7%, with double-digit growth in Chromium consumable reaction volumes
Atera order flow exceeding expectations; ordering above 40 instruments

Total consumables revenue grew 7%, with double-digit growth in Chromium consumable reaction volumes. The company highlighted exceptionally strong early order flow for the new Atera spatial platform, exceeding the prior 40-instrument guidance, and announced the acquisition of Proteintech Genomics to enhance proteomics capabilities. Management guided to sequential consumables revenue step-down in Q3 due to Atera transition, then a step-up in Q4 largely driven by Atera instrument shipments.

Second half GEOs expected to be modestly lighter than H1 due to delays at CSA and lower deliveries from Mantos Blancos
positive_highlights: Revenues of $97.8 million up 62% YoY on cash margin expansion to 96.8%
Canadian Malartic Odyssey set a quarterly production record of 28,800 ounces
Board raised quarterly dividend by 18.2% to $0.065 per share
summary: Revenues of $97.8 million and net earnings of $61.4 million ($0.33/share) beat expectations driven by a 62% YoY increase in cash flow despite lower gold equivalent ounces (GEOs). Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of 80,000-90,000 GEOs but noted the second half will be modestly lighter than the first due to production interruptions at Canadian Malartic and other assets. The company raised its quarterly dividend by 18.2% to $0.065 per share while maintaining a strong balance sheet with no contingent capital.

negative_highlights: North America delivered only 0.5% YoY revenue growth due to client budget shifts away from tax-based services and manual testing.
Software & High Tech vertical declined 1.3% YoY driven by project ramp-downs in non-AI areas outweighing AI growth.
Free cash flow turned negative at -$18 million, impacted by higher variable compensation payments related to prior-year performance.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew at the high end of guidance with organic constant currency expansion of 3.4%.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 32%, exceeding expectations and demonstrating improved profitability.
AI-native revenues accelerated, reaching $160 million in Q2 for a sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth.
summary: EPAM reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.415 billion (up 4.5% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS growth of 22%, beating the high end of guidance on profitability while missing top-line expectations for North America. Management lowered full-year 2026 organic constant currency revenue guidance to a range of 2%-3% due to idiosyncratic slowdowns in Software & High Tech and Business Information & Media verticals, specifically driven by project ramp-downs and client budget shifts away from non-AI services. The company reaffirmed its goal to reach $600 million in AI-native revenues for the year despite a projected flat-to-slow growth trajectory for H2.

negative_highlights: Management expects full-year results to be closer to the lower end of guidance ranges due to softness among lower-income consumers and Middle East conflict volatility.
Auto Glass Now Adjusted EBITDA decreased $6.6 million in Q2, primarily driven by a one-time out-of-period expense of approximately $4 million related to balance sheet cleanup.
Franchise Brands collision segment faced ongoing industry-wide softness, with Maaco specifically noted as remaining under pressure.
positive_highlights: Take Five delivered its 24th consecutive quarter of same-store sales growth, up 3.6% with systemwide sales growing 13%.
Franchise Brands segment maintained strong adjusted EBITDA margins at 59%, serving as a reliable cash generator despite industry pressure in collision repair.
Net leverage improved to 3.1x during the quarter, demonstrating continued progress toward the target of 3x.
summary: Driven Brands reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $507 million (up 7% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $107 million, though the latter was impacted by approximately $3.9 million in restatement costs not included in adjusted metrics for guidance comparisons. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance with no changes to ranges ($1.95B-$2.05B revenue; same-store sales flat to +2%; Adjusted EBITDA $430M-$460M), but explicitly stated they expect performance to trend toward the lower end of these ranges due to macroeconomic headwinds and one-time costs.

One-time hedge loss from Two Harbors-related hedging, causing equity drain

positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA over $180 million in Q2, with about $40 billion of business

Oaktree partnership seen as strategic, with shared vision on housing and MSR expertise
summary: UWM reported Q2 Adjusted EBITDA over $180 million on about $40 billion of business, with management emphasizing consistent profitability despite a tough mortgage market. The company announced a $2 billion-plus capital raise with Oaktree (including $550 million from Mat Ishbia) and decided to suspend its dividend to retain equity and strengthen the balance sheet. Management acknowledged a one-time hedge loss and a failed Two Harbors MSR acquisition, but positioned the Oaktree partnership as a strategic long-term win. Guidance outlook is forward-looking, with expectations for a significantly better mortgage market in the next few years.

negative_highlights: NII net of provisions is expected to be slightly below the midpoint of guidance due to cost of risk and provisioning pressures.

Loan portfolio expanded by 11.6% YoY, reaching BRL 1.137 trillion, supported by high penetration commercial traction and secured lines (FGI/FGO grew 64.5%).
Insurance group delivered strong resilience with total income up 8.3% YoY to BRL 2.9 billion net income.
summary: BBD reported Q2 FY2026 net income of BRL 7.1 billion (up 16.2% YoY) and total revenue of BRL 37.6 billion (up 10.3% YoY), driven by loan portfolio growth of 11.6%. The bank raised its full-year guidance for the insurance group to a range of 6%-8%, citing strong H1 performance, while noting that NII net of provisions is expected to be slightly below the midpoint due to provisioning dynamics.

Reduced net debt by $1.1 billion and redeemed 2027 notes

The company raised its second half production outlook, lowered G&A guidance by $50 million, and reduced net debt by $1.1 billion, with 95% of merger synergies actioned. Management emphasized integration progress, buybacks, and a strong balance sheet, positioning 2027 for full earnings power.

Master Planned Communities earnings increased 32% year-over-year to $134.7M driven by strong land demand and pricing power.
Vantage's underlying accident year combined ratio improved materially to 91.4%, excluding catastrophes, indicating solid underwriting discipline.

The real estate business delivered strong capital generation with MPC earnings up 32%, significant condo closings generating ~$227M net proceeds, and healthy land sales driven by pricing power. Management emphasized a strategic pivot to become an insurance holding company while recycling lower-return real estate assets.

Transaction timelines remain extended and market conditions are described as 'choppy' despite the recovery momentum.
Adjusted EBITDA at $12 million is still materially below peak levels seen in FY2024, indicating profitability has not yet fully normalized.

Larger transaction segment surged 43% to $33 million, marking its strongest performance since Q4 FY2025 as institutional investors returned and price adjustments recalibrated values.
Financing business revenue rose 15% with a notable increase in refinancings accounting for 47% of the quarter's financing revenue.

Net income turned positive at $4 million compared to a loss last year, while adjusted EBITDA improved significantly to $12 million from $1.5 million. Management highlighted broad-based growth across all segments as the company continues its recovery trajectory.

International sales headwinds from distributor buybacks and destocking (~$3 million)

FDA submission for Mobi Tubeless completed; launch expected in second half

Gross margin improved to 57%, up 5 points YoY, and the company reiterated full-year guidance despite infusion set supply constraints. Pharmacy channel adoption reached 10% of U.S. sales in the first full quarter of PayGo, and management expects continued momentum into 2027 with the Mobi Tubeless launch.

Net income surged 85% to $10.4 million ($0.61 EPS), driven by strong demand in industrial automation, data center infrastructure (+$16.3M quarter sales vs prior year), aerospace/defense (up 16%), and medical applications despite a decline in the vehicle market (-7%). Management raised full-year guidance expectations citing record bookings of $201.3 million ($1.31 book-to-bill) and structural margin improvements from their 'STAN' initiative.

LPP study enrolling extremely well with high enthusiasm

The company is on track for a brepocitinib launch in dermatomyositis by end of September, with patient enrollment completed in the phase III cutaneous sarcoidosis study. Management expects a busy second half with multiple data readouts and remains committed to a slow and steady launch approach. Share repurchases accelerated, with ~$200 million in the quarter at an average price in the high $20s.

Enrollment in OPAL is robust, and commercial readiness is advanced.

The company highlighted significant operational leverage from AI coding adoption ('AI terraforming') which increased engineering output 2.5x without additional headcount.

Nelson Labs 2026 revenue growth expected only low single digits

Q4 retail GMV and revenue expected to decline sequentially

Guidance for Q4 projects GMV of $450-$455 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $22-$25 million, positioning FY2026 for the highest annual Adjusted EBITDA in 13 years.

negative_highlights: U.S. product revenue grew only 17% YoY amid continued softness in the broader furniture market.

New Classic integration stabilized with an 8% decline in Q2 compared to a steeper drop in Q1.

The company delivered strong organic growth in the U.S. marketplace despite broader industry softness, while Europe expanded GMV by 66%. Management raised Q3 guidance to a range of $375-$400 million and authorized an additional $120 million share buyback plan.

negative_highlights: Latin America organic sales down 3% in Q4
Agriculture vertical remains soft in FY2027 guidance
Oil and gas vertical expected flat in FY2027

Management raised the long-term margin target to 30% by FY2031 and initiated FY2027 guidance of 7% organic sales growth at the midpoint, with all market verticals guiding positive for the first time. Order rates accelerated across segments, with total orders up 19% on a 3-month basis and Aerospace backlog up 15% to a record $8.5 billion.

Cerro Lindo saw a step down in silver contribution in April

Fifth consecutive annual dividend increase

The company announced a settlement with Steppe Gold, closed the Ravenswood acquisition, raised 2026 guidance to 100,000-110,000 GEOs, and increased its dividend for the fifth consecutive year. Management expressed confidence in continued growth, citing multiple development projects and a strong balance sheet with over $1.1 billion in liquidity.

Inflationary pressures from global diesel costs and service fees partially offset realized cost savings in the lower 48 states

Free cash flow generation of $738 million in Q2 exceeds production levels seen over each of the past three years

Management raised full-year oil production guidance to 123,000 barrels per day from the original estimate of 120,000 bpd by reducing rig count expectations to four for the remainder of the year despite inflationary pressures on diesel and service costs. The company reaffirmed its commitment to returning at least 60% of free cash flow to shareholders via dividends and buybacks while accelerating progress toward a $3 billion net debt target.

Adjusted EBITDA turned negative at -$360.9 million for the quarter, dominated by unrealized mark-to-market losses on digital assets totaling roughly $343 million.

positive_highlights: Power portfolio expanding significantly with Matagorda County site adding potential for approximately 2 GW of future capacity, nearly doubling current holdings.
Daily cost per petahash improved 4% year-over-year to $27.7 due to fleet optimization despite rising network difficulty.

Management highlighted significant progress on its digital infrastructure platform, including an expected expansion of total power capacity to ~4.8 GW and a pending Long Ridge acquisition anticipated to contribute roughly $144 million in annualized EBITDA upon closing.

negative_highlights: Total deposits declined on a year-over-year basis, though this was attributed to a deliberate strategy to exit high-cost single-thread relationships.

Commercial and industrial loans grew at an impressive annualized rate of 18.2%, serving as the primary driver of originated loan growth.
Non-interest-bearing deposits increased at an annualized rate of 8.1% due to treasury management business strength.
summary: Second quarter FY2026 earnings per share on a fully diluted basis reached $0.91, representing a 43% year-over-year increase in operating revenues from over $87 million compared to Q2 2025 and an improvement of the efficiency ratio to approximately 56%. The company reported strong credit quality with net charge-offs at 9 bps and maintained robust liquidity at 4.8x adjusted uninsured deposits, while commercial loan growth accelerated to an annualized rate of 18.2%.

Crude oil and NGLs throughput expected to decline low double digits for 2026

The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint by $250 million to $2.85 billion, and increased DCF and FCF guidance midpoints by $200 million. Management highlighted new Powder River Basin G&P agreements adding 270,000 dedicated acres with MVCs, and expects increased throughput from customers accelerating activity into H2 2026. Q2 distribution held at $0.93 per unit.

No financial performance metrics (revenue, EPS) were disclosed in the transcript.

EU feasibility data showed 96% freedom from AF at one year and 1.7% serious adverse event rate.
summary: Pulse Biosciences reported Q2 FY2026 results, highlighting significant progress in its nPulse cardiac catheter pivotal study, which surpassed halfway enrollment ahead of schedule and is expected to complete in early October, three months earlier than originally planned. The company raised $57.5 million in net proceeds through an ATM program, ending the quarter with over $100 million cash on hand, and amended its study protocol to increase enrollment target to 164 patients. Vybrance disposable sales rose sequentially to $434,000 from $400,000. Management expressed confidence in the technology's differentiated efficacy and workflow advantages, and announced a partnership with the Clayman Thyroid Center.

A one-time U.S. union contract signing bonus of approximately $20 million is expected in Q3, impacting free cash flow guidance.
Modest commodity headwind of roughly $10-12 million due to recovery timing mechanisms.

Management raised full-year guidance for sales, adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow following strong first-half execution.

Management raised full-year guidance for sales ($7.75B midpoint), adjusted EBITDA ($825M midpoint), and free cash flow ($325M midpoint) driven by stronger commercial vehicle demand and cost synergies from the Eaton Mobility transaction preparation.

Full-year AI growth guidance raised but total revenue and EPS guidance remained unchanged despite strong quarter

Subscription dollar-based retention rate remained steady at 107%
Secured a Fortune 100 financial services deal with ~$25M expected ARR upon full deployment
summary: Five9 reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $312 million (up 10% YoY), beating the high end of prior guidance driven by a 78% YoY acceleration in AI revenue and stable CCaaS growth. Management raised its full-year 2026 AI growth outlook from >40% to at least 60%, while keeping total FY26 revenue guidance unchanged despite pulling forward some backlog deployments into Q2. Adjusted gross margin was 61% (down sequentially due to a one-time vendor discount in Q1), and the company highlighted a new $100M Fortune 100 financial services win ramping through 2027.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 58% year-over-year due to significant contraction in the skin substitute market
Advanced Wound Care net product revenue fell 61% compared to last year
Full-year 2026 guidance lowered significantly, now expecting a decline of 64%-74% YoY for H2

Advanced Wound Care unit volume grew 30% sequentially as market share gains offset price/volume headwinds
FDA accepted the biologic license application for Amnuvx with a PDUFA target date of April 24, 2027

Management updated its full-year 2026 guidance downward from an expected decline of 45%-52% YoY to a range of 62%-68%, citing a more measured recovery pace than previously anticipated. The company executed two restructurings in Q1/Q2 reducing annual operating expenses by over $32 million, though GAAP net loss widened significantly due to valuation allowance charges.

negative_highlights: Cash usage from operations plus capex was $19.5 million, an increase of $4.5 million sequentially due to restructuring and acquisition integration costs.
Full-year revenue guidance remains capped at a maximum of $16M despite strong sequential growth in Q2.
MOVIA S launch is scheduled for October 2026 with no significant revenue contribution expected until late in the year or into 2027.

Gross margin expanded significantly to 44% QoQ after a loss last year due to favorable product mix and supply chain efficiencies.
Commercial pipeline increased to over $750M in booking opportunities across more than 130 customer engagements.
summary: MicroVision reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.5 million (up from prior year) and gross margins expanding to 44%. Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance at $10M-$16M but raised the gross margin guide from 35%-40% to 40%-45%, while maintaining cash burn guidance of ~$60M. The company highlighted commercial traction in industrial, defense, and security sectors following Luminar integration.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue growth rate expected to moderate from H1 levels due to typical seasonality where Q1 is the strongest enrollment period.
Management noted that back-half guidance assumes a more normalized cadence following an exceptionally strong first half, implying lower sequential growth rates compared to recent quarters.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $88 million representing a 43% year-over-year increase.
GAAP gross margin expanded significantly to 73%, up from 66% in the same period last year.
Company achieved GAAP net income profitability for Q2, marking its second consecutive quarter of profit after turning loss-making in Q4 FY2025.
summary: Omada Health reported its strongest quarter ever with record revenue of $88 million (up 43% YoY) and GAAP gross margin expanding to 73%. The company achieved GAAP net income profitability for the second consecutive quarter, generating $5M in net income. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance on both revenue ($334-340M vs prior $322-330M) and adjusted EBITDA ($21-27M vs prior $14-20M).

negative_highlights: Revenue growth impacted by large former client transition agreement (ended June 30, 2025)
Progyny Select not expected to be meaningful contributor in 2027
Investment spending continues, with CapEx up $1 million year-over-year
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue, gross profit, and adjusted EBITDA
Gross margin expanded 180 basis points year-over-year
Early commitments pacing meaningfully ahead of last year; confident in 1M+ lives target
summary: Progyny reported record Q2 2026 revenue, gross profit, and adjusted EBITDA, with revenue up 5.3% reported and 11% excluding a former client's transition agreement. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points year-over-year. Management highlighted strong watching season momentum with early commitments ahead of last year and retention de-risked for 2027, reiterating the target of adding 1 million or more lives. The company announced a new $200 million share repurchase program and continued to generate strong cash flow, with over $50 million in operating cash flow for the fourth time in five quarters.

negative_highlights: Americas devices growth slower in back half
Astral field safety corrective action ongoing
Supply constraints from field action
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 8% constant currency, EPS up 16%
FY2027 guidance above consensus, dividend +10%
Oura partnership driving 13,000 users, 75% undiagnosed
summary: ResMed reported Q4 FY2026 revenue growth of 8% constant currency, non-GAAP EPS up 16%, and gross margin expansion. For FY2026, they achieved 10% headline revenue growth, 180bps operating margin expansion, and over $1.6 billion in free cash flow. They announced a 10% dividend increase, accelerated buybacks, and raised FY2027 guidance that beats consensus. The company also closed the Noctrix acquisition, plans to divest MatrixCare, and reaffirmed tariff relief for their products.

Other apheresis revenue declined 3% organic on portfolio optimization and order timing
Gross margin down 40 basis points year-over-year, partly due to software benefit

Persona PLUS rollout ahead of schedule with yield improvements exceeding 5%
Free cash flow increased nearly 15-fold year-over-year
summary: Haemonetics reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $339 million, up 6% reported and organic, and adjusted EPS of $1.14, up 4% year-over-year. The company raised full-year guidance for revenue growth to 5%-8% reported and 4%-7% organic, while reaffirming operating margin expansion of 50-100 basis points. MedSurg grew 6%, apheresis grew 6% organic, and interventional technologies returned to 3% organic growth. Free cash flow conversion was 75% for the quarter, with $50 million debt repaid during the quarter and another $50 million after quarter end.

Oil cut temporarily lower due to gas-rich development and accounting noise
No buybacks recently as company builds cash for other opportunities
positive_highlights: Record quarterly total revenue of ~$246M, up 31% YoY

Adjusted EBITDA margin of 88% with record free cash flow
summary: TPL reported record quarterly total revenue of ~$246M, up 31% YoY, with record net income and free cash flow of $156M. Oil and gas royalty production averaged ~39,700 BOE/d, up 20% YoY, and produced water royalty volumes rose 15% YoY. The company reaffirmed FY CapEx guidance of $65-75M and highlighted progress on data center/power initiatives, including a $100M land acquisition in Shackelford/Jones County and completion of a desalination facility. Management expressed confidence in near-term deal announcements despite a sequential decline in water sales volumes due to weak gas prices.

Q2 revenue guidance implies continued YoY decline

Life sciences trailing 12-month book-to-bill ~1.1x excluding GLP-1, driven by radiopharma
Service-related revenues grew 11% YoY

Management initiated an 18-month Fixed-Cost Transformation Program targeting ~CAD 20M annualized savings in the first phase (Europe), about 30% of total opportunity, and reiterated the 15% operating margin target. Q2 revenue guidance is CAD 660M-CAD 700M, with margins expected to strengthen in H2.

negative_highlights: HPMC sales growth was muted at only 5% YoY due to qualification timing delays shifting shipments from the current quarter into future periods.
Specialty energy revenue declined 6% as production capacity was prioritized for higher-value defense orders, though this is expected to rebalance in H2.

AA&S segment achieved an all-time high adjusted EBITDA margin of 23.7% (up 930 bps YoY) driven by pricing and mix shifts toward aerospace/defense.
summary: ATI reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.3 billion (up 11% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $284 million ($29M above the high end of prior guidance). Management raised full-year outlooks for adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow across all metrics driven by strong AA&S performance and HPMC ramp timing. The company highlighted a record backlog of $4.4 billion and significant margin expansion in both segments.

$60 million cash outflow used for share repurchases, partially offsetting $24 million positive operating cash flow.
Pending CanAdelaar acquisition closing delayed relative to expectations due to the ordinary course of Dutch regulatory review.

Gross profit expanded to $28.5 million, up 96% YoY, with gross margins demonstrating strong operational efficiency across all regions.
Spinach brand maintained number one position in Canada edibles for the eighth consecutive quarter with market share steady at 20.8%.
summary: Cronos reported Q2 FY26 consolidated net revenue of $53 million (up 58% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of a record $13.1 million. Gross profit surged 96% YoY to $28.5 million, driven by higher average sales prices from geographic mix shifts to tax-free markets like Israel and strong vape portfolio growth in Canada. Management raised the tone on forward guidance for the pending CanAdelaar acquisition closing in H2 FY26.

summary: Following the completion of its business combination with Orla Mining on July 31st, Equinox Gold reported Q2 FY26 results where management provided updated full-year guidance rather than specific quarterly financials in this transcript. The company raised its consolidated production forecast to 870k-920k ounces for the year and increased annual dividend by 50% to $0.09/share, citing strong second-half performance at Greenstone and Valentine alongside Musselwhite contributions. However, management noted that Q2 grades were lower than anticipated due to ramp-up selectivity issues and recovery overhangs from arsenopyrite content, requiring a conservative view on the balance of the year.

summary: LifeStance Health reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $435 million (up 26% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $66 million (up 94%), both exceeding expectations with Center Margin expanding to 15.2%. No specific numerical guidance was provided for full-year 2026 or share repurchase plans, leaving investors without updated targets.

summary: Green Plains reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $93.3 million and net income attributable to Green Plains of $67.1 million ($0.83 per diluted share), representing a significant beat against the prior year's performance where second quarter earnings were only $16.4 million. The company highlighted strong execution with nearly 161 million gallons of ethanol produced despite spring maintenance, and carbon platform EBITDA reached approximately $59 million. Management maintained an upbeat outlook for the back half of the year citing healthy demand fundamentals but did not provide specific numerical guidance updates or raise prior forecasts.

Difficult prior-year comparison in Alaris and continued China vaccine pressure
Full-year guidance only toward high-end of low-single-digit growth, implying Q4 deceleration
positive_highlights: Revenue of $5 billion, up 4.4%, ahead of expectations
Adjusted EPS of $3.23, up 4.9%, ahead of expectations
Year-to-date free cash flow up 45% versus prior year
summary: BD reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5 billion, up 4.4% FX-neutral, with adjusted EPS of $3.23, up 4.9%, both ahead of expectations. The quarter saw double-digit growth across key platforms like biologic drug delivery, APM, PureWick, and advanced tissue regeneration, partially offset by Alaris and China vaccines headwinds. Management raised the midpoint of full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $12.62-$12.72 and now expects revenue growth toward the high end of the low-single-digit range. Margins contracted due to tariffs but productivity gains continued, and free cash flow rose 45% year-to-date.

negative_highlights: Labor cost inflation identified as the largest factor impacting AISC, particularly at Haile due to lack of currency protection.
Lower silver by-product credits reduced margins compared to expectations due to a lower realized silver price than anticipated.
Unhedged diesel exposure remains a risk for operations in Waihi and Didipio if oil prices remain elevated.

Strong free cash flow generation of $130 million for the quarter, bringing year-to-date total to $385 million while maintaining a debt-free balance sheet with $655 million in cash.
Significant operational milestones including record mill throughput rates at Haile and Waihi, and progress on growth projects like Waihi North reaching 200 meters into decline development.
summary: OceanaGold reported Q2 FY2026 gold production of approximately 139,000 ounces and copper of 2,700 tons, which were in line with full-year guidance despite a pullback from record-high first-quarter gold prices. The company achieved a record quarterly adjusted EBITDA margin of 61% driven by lower cost of sales and government share reductions at Didipio, while generating $130 million in free cash flow to date. Management remains on track for full-year guidance with expectations for higher production and lower all-in sustaining costs (AISC) in the second half due to grade improvements.

summary: Savers Value Village reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $448 million, up 7.4% with U.S. comps up 6.6%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 8% to $75 million with margins at 16.6%. The company is rolling out ThriftIQ, which has shown 100 basis points higher gross profit growth in pilot stores. Guidance was updated to net sales of $1.77-$1.79 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $265-$275 million for FY2026.

Management raised full-year guidance for new business wins from a previous range to $80-$100 million after securing over $80 million in immediate ramp-up awards through July.

Management raised full-year guidance for sales to $460-$480 million, EBITDA to $55-$65 million, and new business wins to $80-$100 million following a strong first half where they secured over $80 million of immediate ramp-up awards in data center, defense, and medical. The company highlighted significant margin expansion driven by mix shifts and cost-out initiatives while noting that second-half guidance remains conservative due to upcoming large-scale ramps.

negative_highlights: International revenues softened by roughly 2% YoY due to macro headwinds and fuel price impacts specifically affecting India.
Q4 growth rates are projected to moderate as the business begins comping against exceptionally strong Q4 FY25 results from large go-lives.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded sequentially by 130 bps to 28.6% driven by operating leverage and synergy realization from Sterling acquisition ($63M run rate actioned).
Full-year 2026 guidance raised across all metrics, with revenue now expected in the $1.67B-$1.71B range.
summary: First Advantage reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $449 million (up 15% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 28.6%, significantly outperforming expectations with a full-year guidance raise across all metrics including EPS growth targets. Full-year 2026 guidance raised from flat growth expectation to mid-single-digit year-over-year revenue growth.
Book-to-bill ratio neared 1.0 over the past three quarters indicating stabilizing order activity.
summary: Axcelis reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $215 million and diluted EPS of $1.06, both beating expectations as system revenue grew sequentially in power and general mature markets despite memory timing headwinds. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to mid-single-digit growth from a prior flat outlook and increased H2 2026 revenue estimates above initial expectations due to stronger-than-anticipated demand trends.

EBITDA flow-through was impacted by higher Incentive Management Fees (IMF) triggered on outperforming assets and elevated travel agent commissions related to the World Cup.
Management expects comparable hotel RevPAR growth in the mid-single digits for H2, implying a normalization of rates after an exceptionally strong first half.

summary: Host Hotels & Resorts reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDAre of $525 million (up 5.8% YoY) and comparable hotel RevPAR growth of 7%, driven by World Cup events, rate strength, and strong leisure demand in markets like Maui. Management raised full-year 2026 Total RevPAR guidance to a range of 4.75%-5.25% (midpoint +125 bps vs prior) citing first-half outperformance and an optimistic second half outlook.

negative_highlights: Jefferson crude volumes were impacted by Middle East volatility and a temporary reduction in inbound ship volumes during Q2.
summary: FTAI Infrastructure reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $76.1 million (up from $45.9M prior year), driven by record rail revenue and terminal growth despite a temporary Middle East supply disruption at Jefferson that is expected to recover in Q3. The company announced the sale of Long Ridge, which will eliminate approximately $1.4 billion of debt upon closing later this quarter. Management raised full-year expectations for adjusted EBITDA from its core rail and terminal segments due to strong momentum.

negative_highlights: Total revenues declined by $3.6 million (1.5%) as the acquired Sprint Wireline base contracted significantly.
Off-Net revenue fell $4.5 million sequentially due to grooming and termination of low-margin contracts from the Sprint acquisition.
Average price per megabit for new customer contracts decreased slightly, reflecting ongoing pricing pressure in a competitive environment.

Gross margins expanded by 260 basis points year-over-year and 90 basis points sequentially to 47% driven by the rotation to profitable On-Net services (now 63.8% of total).
Wavelength business grew revenue $1.2 million sequentially with customers upgrading existing connections from 100G to 400G, indicating strong demand confidence.

Adjusted EBITDA increased by approximately $900,000 sequentially despite revenue misses, driven primarily by cost reductions including workforce optimization that reduced headcount by 6% in the quarter. Management provided no specific quarterly guidance but reiterated multi-year targets of 6%-8% revenue growth and margin expansion.

negative_highlights: Pulpwood markets remained challenging with subdued demand and dry weather adding supply
Wildfire casualties of ~$2 million recorded, leading to salvage harvests
Southern Timber pricing expected lower on geographic mix
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $124 million well above prior year period
Wood Products delivered strongest quarterly EBITDA since Q3 2022 with lumber prices up 18% sequentially
Real Estate EBITDA up $20 million year-over-year to $38 million
summary: Rayonier reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.10 and adjusted EBITDA of $124 million, driven by PotlatchDeltic contributions and strong segment performance. Southern and Northwest Timber EBITDA rose significantly year-over-year, while Wood Products posted its best quarter since 2022. The company completed a tax-efficient land exchange with RMS, repurchased $72 million of shares, and affirmed full-year guidance with stable to higher lumber pricing trends.

negative_highlights: Flow Technologies total margin was diluted by the full quarter contribution of SPX FLOW integration costs.
Organic orders in Flow Technologies declined 3% due to deferred Middle East orders impacting regional growth visibility for near-term quarters.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 51% YoY, fueled by organic growth across all segments including Flow Technologies (up 21%) and CCT (up 17%).
Adjusted EPS reached $2.08, an 18% increase year-over-year.
Management raised full-year guidance for revenue, margin expansion to ~20.5%, and free cash flow to $565 million.
summary: ITT reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.5 billion (up 51% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $2.08 (up 18%), driven by strong organic growth across all segments including a record quarter for Flow Technologies. Management raised full-year guidance, increasing the midpoint for organic revenue to 5%-8%, adjusted operating margin expansion to approximately 20.5%, and free cash flow to $565 million. The company accelerated debt repayment with leverage at 2.5x ahead of schedule.

negative_highlights: Underlying gross margin excluding tariff refunds was only 37.7%, significantly lower than the reported 56.6%.
Retail channel sales declined sharply by 23.4% year-over-year.
Operating expenses increased to $39.6 million due to higher shipping costs ($1.4M sequential increase) and fuel prices.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly net sales of $136.3 million representing a 9.9% year-over-year increase.
Online business growth accelerated to 24% year-over-year with Amazon specifically up 49% in July.
New distribution center lease finalized for Orlando, Florida, expected operational by Q3.
summary: Karat Packaging reported record quarterly net sales of $136.3 million (up 9.9% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.48, driven by a massive one-time benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds which inflated gross margin to 56.6%. Management explicitly stated that underlying gross margins excluding the refund were approximately 37.7%, noting this was lower than expected due to higher product costs and shipping expenses in Q2. While online sales grew strongly at 24% YoY, retail channel revenue declined significantly by 23.4%.

negative_highlights: VA MDE incentive suspension reduces diluted EPS guidance by $0.35
Full-year EPS guidance midpoint lowered from $8.40 to $8.05
Outside U.S. segment revenue declined versus prior year due to volume variances
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $2.22 beat prior year's $2.16
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 15.0% from 14.7%
Collected $245 million from a major federal customer since June 30
summary: Maximus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.28 billion, in line with expectations; adjusted EPS of $2.22 beat prior year's $2.16, with adjusted EBITDA margin up to 15.0% from 14.7%. However, a customer-directed pause on the VA MDE performance incentives reduces Q4 EPS by ~$0.35, cutting full-year EPS guidance midpoint from $8.40 to $8.05. Revenue guidance is reiterated at $5.2-5.35 billion with a bias to lower end. Cash collections accelerated with $245 million received since June 30, supporting free cash flow guidance of $425-475 million.

negative_highlights: SMB revenue declined 11% year-over-year due to organic search headwinds in non-loan products.
Consumer credit card revenue fell, attributed specifically to continued organic search headwinds from LLM traffic shifts.
Revenue from the largest auto insurance carrier relationship has stabilized but remains below levels seen earlier in the year.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 6% year-over-year to $197 million, driven by an 8% increase in consumer revenue ($175M).
Non-GAAP operating income of $12 million exceeded the midpoint of guidance range.
Trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow doubled year-over-year to a record $141 million.
summary: NerdWallet reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $197 million (up 6% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $12 million, which beat the midpoint of guidance ($6M-$14M). Management raised full-year profitability expectations by narrowing the range to $90M-$105M while maintaining the previous midpoint. Q3 revenue is guided at $244M-$260M (up 17% YoY), reflecting seasonality and tailwinds from student loan regulatory changes.

negative_highlights: Revenue was flat year-over-year at $30.5 million due to a lack of non-recurring return-to-service work on Spanish Scoopers compared to Q2 FY2025.
European contract commitments with Avincis came later than expected, causing an internal estimate miss for that specific lease component.
positive_highlights: Awarded two 160-day guaranteed task orders covering four Super Scoopers, representing the longest in Bridger's history.
summary: Bridger Aerospace reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $30.5 million and a net loss of $0.5 million ($7.6M attributable to common stockholders), which was in line with expectations but missed the prior year's adjusted growth due to non-recurring return-to-service work on Spanish Scoopers recognized last quarter. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for revenue between $135-$145 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $55-$60 million, noting that recent European contract delays were partially offset by strong U.S. demand. The company highlighted new long-term task orders with the Forest Service and Department of Interior extending into Q4 as a positive structural shift.

negative_highlights: Per capita spending declined modestly by less than 1% on a same-park basis due to mix shifts toward higher-volume season pass holders rather than weaker pricing.
July performance was impacted by an unfavorable calendar shift for the Fourth of July holiday and wildfire-related air quality disruptions causing some park closures.
positive_highlights: Same-park adjusted EBITDA increased approximately 7% to $249 million despite fewer operating days due to fixed cost structure mechanics.
Active season pass base grew by 6%, with single-day and combined products yielding higher average prices indicating strong pricing power.
