Ride uptime improved in the quarter, reducing downtime at certain parks while maintaining safety standards.
summary: On a same-park basis excluding sold assets and closed parks, Q2 net revenue increased approximately 2% to $864 million while adjusted EBITDA rose roughly 7% to $249 million despite operating days declining by 3%. Management raised the trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA figure for the current portfolio to $801 million compared with prior year full-year results and reiterated expectations for growth in the second half of the year. The company highlighted a 6% expansion in its active pass base, higher average prices across admission products, and improved ride uptime as key drivers.

positive_highlights: Adjusted recurring net investment income grew 27% YoY to $208 million driven by portfolio revenue growth.
New investments exceeded $1 billion in Q2, bringing total H1 closed transactions to over $1.7 billion with returns greater than 11%.
Cost of debt was effectively managed via hedging and refinancing, resulting in a June issuance cost that was 70 bps lower than base rates would suggest.
summary: HASI reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EPS of $0.75 (up 25% YoY) and managed assets grew to $17.6 billion (+20% YoY). Management raised its full-year 2028 adjusted EPS guidance range from $3.50-$3.60 to $3.55-$3.65, citing strong investment activity exceeding $1.7 billion year-to-date and improved capital efficiency with zero ATM issuance.

negative_highlights: Mount Holly plant experienced some instability following the restart, with impact included in Q3 outlook but not expected beyond that quarter.
Jamalco refinery faces a modest cost headwind from lower quality bauxite until revised mining plans are fully implemented over the next couple of quarters.
Grundartangi Line 2 is running at slightly reduced amperage due to new replacement transformers arriving in Q4.
positive_highlights: Completed Mount Holly expansion restart at full capacity and restarted Potline 2 at Grundartangi roughly six months ahead of schedule.
Cash balance exceeded total debt ($98M) as of end-July, with cash on hand standing at $388 million after tax credit receipts.
Global aluminum deficit expected to persist through 2027 due to Middle Eastern smelter curtailments and low inventory levels.
summary: Century Aluminum reported Q2 FY26 shipments of approximately 131,000 tons and net sales of $752 million, driven by a sequential volume increase from the Mount Holly expansion and restart at Grundartangi. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $327 million due to higher realized LME prices ($3,250/ton) and regional premiums, though operating expenses increased reflecting full capacity run rates. Management raised Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $325-$345 million based on expected price increases in the second half.

negative_highlights: Expense growth per occupied room up 3.6%, causing 100 bps margin headwind
San Diego RevPAR declined 8.4% in Q2
Management retains caution due to macro uncertainty
positive_highlights: Q2 RevPAR grew 9.3%, ahead of expectations
Adjusted FFO per share up 14% year-over-year
Full-year guidance raised for RevPAR and earnings
summary: Sunstone Hotel Investors reported Q2 RevPAR growth of 9.3% (4.3% excluding Andaz Miami Beach), with adjusted EBITDAre of $77 million, up 6% year-over-year, and adjusted FFO per share of $0.32, up 14%. The company raised full-year guidance, now expecting RevPAR growth of 7%-9% for the 13-hotel portfolio, and completed the sale of Hyatt Regency San Francisco, deploying proceeds into stock repurchases. Management remains cautious on macro headwinds but notes strong group and transient pace into 2027.

negative_highlights: Net income fell 28% YoY and Adjusted EBITDA declined 9% YoY, with core ad revenue weak: services flat and RR&O down 10%.
Ad clicks declined 5% YoY and paying advertising locations fell 1% YoY amid a challenging local business environment.
Management guided Q3 EBITDA down sequentially to $70-75 million and narrowed the full-year revenue range with the top end reduced by $5 million.
positive_highlights: Net revenue of $376 million came in $8 million above the high end of the outlook range, with other revenue up 98% YoY to a record $33 million.
Yelp Host reached an annual call run rate of 2.4 million in July, more than tripling from January, and Hatch annual run-rate revenue grew 59% YoY to $35 million.
Paying advertising locations improved sequentially to down only 1% YoY, with restaurants posting the best performance in several years.
summary: Yelp's Q2 2026 revenue rose 1% YoY to $376 million, $8 million above the high end of guidance, but Adjusted EBITDA fell 9% to $91 million and net income dropped 28%. Services ad revenue was flat YoY, RR&O ad revenue declined 10%, and paying ad locations fell 1%. Other revenue surged 98% YoY to $33 million, driven by Hatch, data licensing, and food orders, with Hatch annual run-rate revenue up 59% to $35 million. Management guided Q3 revenue to $365-370 million and full-year revenue to $1.460-1.470 billion (narrowed lower at the top end), with Q3 Adjusted EBITDA expected at $70-75 million and full-year at $315-325 million, reflecting continued investments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue down to $2.49M from $3.53M year ago
Hardware revenue fell to $1.06M from $2.21M
Net income declined to $294K from $720K
positive_highlights: Monitoring revenue rose 8% to $1.43 million
Gross margin improved to 82.4%, up 750 bps
New Champion partnership and OMNI360 launch to drive growth
summary: Acorn Energy reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.49 million, down from $3.53 million a year ago due to lower hardware revenue from the cell phone contract, but monitoring revenue grew 8% to $1.43 million. Gross margin expanded 750 bps to 82.4% driven by higher-margin monitoring revenue, and net income was $294,000 ($0.12 diluted) versus $720,000 ($0.28) last year. Management announced a partnership with Champion Power Equipment for residential generator monitoring and the launch of OMNI360 for cell tower security, with expectations of returning to year-over-year revenue growth in H2 2026.

negative_highlights: Acquisition-adjusted expenses grew 150 bps more than anticipated due to variable costs tied to revenue growth, though management views this positively.
Local and regional sales were slightly weaker in specific categories like real estate and amusements compared to service and political.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 6.1% acquisition-adjusted YoY with EBITDA margin expanding to a record 49.2%.
Digital revenue increased 15.4% YoY, now comprising one-third of total billboard revenues.
Political spend exceeded $5 million in Q2 and is running ahead of the prior cycle.
summary: Lamar reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 6.1% on an acquisition-adjusted basis and EBITDA margin expansion to a record 49.2%. Management raised full-year AFFO guidance by $0.22 per share (midpoint increase) citing strong momentum carried into Q3, particularly in digital and national segments.

negative_highlights: Liberty Puerto Rico Adjusted FCF was negative -$48M in Q2 and -$91M for H1 due to single-digit declines in residential mobile and fixed revenue.
Consolidated Free Cash Flow before distributions is expected to be less robust than last year's second half as the company comps against $81 million received from weather derivatives in Q4 2025.
Liberty Caribbean results were impacted by Hurricane Melissa, resulting in roughly a $6M net decline across revenue and Adjusted OIBDA.
positive_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA grew 3% year-over-year on a rebased basis with consolidated margins expanding approximately 130 bps to 40%.
Liberty Networks delivered the best YoY revenue growth at +14%, driven by El Salvador milestones and Venezuela expansion plans.
Cost reduction initiatives are flowing through, including an AI-driven IT services deal with Amdocs estimated worth north of $250 million NPV.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $1.1 billion (up 1% reported) and Adjusted OIBDA grew 3%, though consolidated Adjusted FCF before distributions ($83M in Q2) remains significantly weighted to the fourth quarter due to weather derivative receipts from last year being comped against this period. Management highlighted strong operational progress, including postpaid mobile growth across segments and cost savings initiatives like an AI-driven IT deal with Amdocs valued at over $250 million NPV. However, Liberty Puerto Rico reported a negative Adjusted FCF of -$48M in Q2 due to single-digit declines in residential revenue despite margin expansion.

negative_highlights: Total revenues declined year-over-year due to a one-time $64.4M milestone hit by Bayer in the prior quarter which is not expected to recur
R&D expenses increased sequentially from $110.1M to $97.8M (note: text says decrease primarily due to higher activity in 2025, but QoQ comparison shows a drop; however, SG&A rose significantly)
European revenue contribution is expected to be modest (~15% of total) with staggered launches
positive_highlights: MYQORZO dispensed prescriptions nearly tripled quarter-over-quarter to approximately 1,500 patients
Unaided awareness among HCPs increased significantly from 52% in Q1 to 68% in Q2
Positive top-line results from ACACIA-HCM met both dual primary endpoints for nHCM
summary: Cytokinetics reported Q2 FY26 net product revenues of $25.3 million (up from $18.4M in the prior period), driven by accelerating MYQORZO dispensing to 1,500 patients and a successful launch in Germany. The company updated its full-year R&D/SG&A guidance upward due to commercial readiness investments for an expanded nHCM label following positive ACACIA-HCM results. Management expressed confidence in the differentiated profile of aficamten while noting that European revenue growth will be slower than U.S. velocity.

negative_highlights: Inventory finance sales declined by approximately $10.1 billion (74%) as dealers worked through existing inventory.
The company wrote off roughly $560,000 in minority investment losses related to an affiliated entity.
A note receivable of ~$48.6 million from mobile home park borrowers matured and was not repaid in full.
positive_highlights: Net income hit a company record of $23.5 million, representing nearly 60% growth year-over-year.
Diluted EPS increased to $0.99 from $0.60 in the prior year quarter.
Operating cash flow for H1 reached $24.4 million, up significantly from $11 million a year ago.
summary: Legacy Housing reported a record quarter with net revenue of $66.3 million (up 32% YoY) and diluted EPS of $0.99 (up from $0.60). The beat was driven by the commencement of deliveries under a large workforce housing order, which contributed significantly to volume growth despite lower inventory finance sales. Management highlighted strong cash flow generation ($24.4M in H1), an excellent balance sheet with no debt, and raised expectations for future orders following new federal legislation.

negative_highlights: Same-store cash NOI growth was only 0.8%, which management noted was adversely impacted by a one-time non-recurring revenue recovery recognized in the prior year.
G&A costs increased slightly from Q1 due to new leadership additions, with no immediate offsetting cost reductions mentioned.
Management acknowledged that transitioning away from outpatient medical assets will take more time than immediately anticipated.
positive_highlights: Completed sale of seven inpatient rehab facilities generating approximately $200 million gross proceeds at an exit cap rate of 7.3%.
Placed Beaumont, Texas surgical hospital under contract for a price of $49 million representing an exit cap rate of 5.9%.
Issued $100 million of Series C convertible perpetual preferred stock to raise fresh equity capital.
summary: Chiron Real Estate reported Q2 FY26 results with GAAP-redefined FFO of $0.88 and Core FFO of $1.4 per share/unit; same-store cash NOI increased only 0.8% YoY, though excluding a one-time prior-year recovery it grew 1.7%. The company executed significant capital recycling by watching seven inpatient rehab facilities for approximately $200 million gross proceeds (totaling $217M) and placing an asset under contract to watch Beaumont Surgical Hospital for $49 million. Management indicated that G&A costs will be higher short-term due to new leadership additions but expects them to normalize as the portfolio repositions toward seniors housing.

negative_highlights: $10-15 million of government orders pulled forward
Cybersecurity revenue up only 0.6% amid tough comparison
Supply chain constraints and rising equipment prices
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 12.7% to $210.4 million
Operating margin expanded 660 bps to 20.8%
Full-year outlook reaffirmed
summary: NetScout's Q1 FY2027 revenue rose 12.7% to $210.4 million, with EPS up to $0.52 from $0.34. Growth was driven by service assurance (up 19.7%) and government orders pulled forward by $10-15 million; normalized growth was mid-single digits. The company reaffirmed its full-year outlook and highlighted strong margin expansion (operating margin up 660 bps to 20.8%). Cybersecurity grew only 0.6% due to a tough comparison, but management remains optimistic on long-term opportunities.

negative_highlights: Loungefly segment sales declined by 2%, though management noted an improving trend from Q1 following SKU reductions.
Management remains cautious regarding potential upside risks from tariffs (factored in at 10-12%) and freight costs.
positive_highlights: Sales grew 7% in Q2 with broad-based momentum across regions (Europe +19%) and product lines (Core Collectibles +9%).
Gross margin expanded significantly to a record high of 56.6%, normalizing to 44.4% after removing the $25 million tariff credit.
Adjusted EBITDA delivered at $40.9M, substantially beating guidance and reversing last year's negative adjusted EBITDA.
summary: Funko reported Q2 FY26 sales growth of 7% and a gross margin of 56.6%, which normalized to 44.4% excluding a one-time $25 million tariff credit benefit. Management reiterated net sales guidance for flat-to-up-3% but raised adjusted EBITDA guidance by citing the tariff windfall and improved profitability, delivering actuals well above the prior range of $100-$110 million.

negative_highlights: Expense ratio increased by one point compared to the prior period, partially offsetting underwriting improvements.
Auto premium per policy decreased slightly quarter over quarter as Allstate prioritizes affordability for customers despite strong margins.
Prior year reserve re-estimates contributed two points of combined ratio improvement, indicating a favorable but non-recurring accounting adjustment.
positive_highlights: Property-liability combined ratio improved significantly by 4.5 points to 86.6, with underlying loss ratios improving in both auto and homeowners segments.
Net premiums written increased 2.6% supported by a 9.9% increase in issued applications across all channels.
Investment income surged 33.8% year-over-year to $1 billion due to duration lengthening, portfolio growth, and performance-based gains.
summary: Allstate reported Q2 FY26 total revenues of $18.6 billion (up 11.8% YoY) and adjusted net income of $2.3 billion ($8.99/share), driven by an improved property-liability combined ratio of 86.6%. Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EPS to a range of $40-$45 per share, citing operational excellence in auto (combined ratio 83.3) and homeowners insurance (combined ratio 94.6). The company returned $1.3 billion to shareholders via dividends and buybacks.

negative_highlights: Americas unit volume decreased by 9% driven principally by lower U.S. consumer replacement volumes and soft note-in conditions in EMEA.

Gross margin contracted due to lower tire unit volumes, unfavorable fixed cost absorption from the Fayetteville closure transition costs ($40M in 2026), inflation headwinds of $53 million, and tariff impacts of $32 million.
Full-year segment operating income is expected to be reduced by approximately $350 million due to volume declines affecting fixed cost absorption.
positive_highlights: Asia Pacific delivered revenue growth and margin expansion with a 5.3% increase in unit volumes driven by improved consumer demand across OE and replacement channels.
OE market share gains were achieved globally, particularly strong performance in the Americas where Goodyear gained share despite softness in the broader consumer backdrop.
Goodyear Forward savings program is on track to deliver benefits of roughly $70 million for Q3.
summary: Q2 sales were $4.3 billion down ~5% YoY (excluding divestitures: flat), with gross margin contracting by one percentage point to a loss of non-GAAP EPS ($0.61). Management reiterated Q3 guidance for roughly flat global unit volumes and explicitly stated the full-year outlook remains unchanged from prior expectations, citing persistent headwinds in Americas consumer replacement volume and elevated raw material costs.

negative_highlights: Net investment income of $174 million ($0.75/share) fell note weakness in of the regular dividend of $0.77 per share, ending a streak of meeting or exceeding dividends for 28 consecutive quarters.
NAV declined approximately 2.8% quarter-over-quarter to $25.53 due to unrealized net losses and realized losses from two restructurings.
positive_highlights: Repayment activity accelerated significantly with over $700 million in repayments this quarter versus expectations discussed on the last call.
summary: BXSL reported Q2 FY26 net investment income of $174 million ($0.75 per share), which missed the regular dividend of $0.77 per share for the first time in 28 consecutive quarters, resulting in a NAV decline to $25.53 due to unrealized losses and realized restructuring impacts. While repayment activity accelerated with over $700 million returned (annualized rate of 21%), management noted that new deal flow remains constructive but slower than prior periods, particularly after the start of the year. The portfolio mark declined to 95.2% driven by broader spread widening.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue shortfall of ~$90M vs expectations due to production delays
FY2026 revenue guidance midpoint cut to $3B, EBITDA midpoint to -$10M
Recorded $15M loss on battery supply agreement and ~$15M costs from product rollout delays
positive_highlights: Record order intake of $1.44B in Q3, nearly triple prior-year $509M
Record backlog of $6.4B, up 14% QoQ and >30% YoY
First data center orders and awards totaling $850M, with data center pipeline up 35% QoQ to 16 GWh
summary: Fluence Energy reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $650M, up 8% YoY but about $90M below prior expectations due to production startup delays at two new contract manufacturing facilities. Record order intake of $1.44B and record backlog of $6.4B (up 14% QoQ) were highlights, with first data center orders and awards totaling $850M. However, guidance was lowered: FY2026 revenue midpoint cut to $3.0B (from ~$3.4B) and adjusted EBITDA midpoint cut to -$10M (from +$50M), primarily due to ~$400M of revenue pushed into 2027 and $15M battery supply loss. Management expressed confidence in long-term demand but acknowledged execution risks during the ramp-up.

negative_highlights: Karnes area production was relatively flat year-over-year at just over 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.
The company is restricted on share repurchases until after closing the WildFire acquisition in late Q3.
positive_highlights: Production volumes grew by 8% year-over-year, establishing new quarterly records at both total and oil levels.
Adjusted operating income margins averaged a robust 51%, supported by higher prices and solid execution.
Management raised full-year production growth guidance to 6% from the prior expectation of 5%.
summary: Magnolia Oil & Gas reported Q2 FY26 adjusted net income of $184 million ($0.99 per share) and production growth of 8% year-over-year to 106.1 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, exceeding earlier guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 standalone production growth guidance from 5% to 6%. The company also announced a definitive agreement to acquire WildFire Energy for approximately $4.06 billion.

negative_highlights: Vormatrigine POWER1 missed primary endpoint
Relutrigine PDUFA extended to December 27, 2026 due to major amendment
Operating expenses increased to $96.9M in Q2 from $76M year-over-year
positive_highlights: FDA mid-cycle meetings for both NDAs: no advisory committee planned
BIMO inspections concluded with no Form 483 findings
Cash position $1.4B, sufficient to fund runway into 2028
summary: Praxis reported Q2 FY2026 with two NDAs in late-stage FDA review for ulixacaltamide and relutrigine. Mid-cycle meetings showed no advisory committee plans and no findings from BIMO inspections. Operating expenses rose to $96.9M and cash ended at $1.4B. The vormatrigine POWER1 study missed primary endpoints but met a key secondary endpoint, with plans to amend POWER2/POWER3.

negative_highlights: The company lost approximately 17,000 residential broadband customers during the quarter amid elevated churn rates.
Adjusted EBITDA declined to $173.5 million from $203.2 million in Q2 of the prior year.
Business services revenues decreased by $3.8 million year-over-year following the sale of fiber-to-the-tower assets.
positive_highlights: Digital channel momentum increased significantly, rising from less than 10% share last year to roughly 35% of sales in Q2.
Residential broadband ARPU increased sequentially due to promotional roll-offs and AutoPay Plus program changes.
Mobile service officially launched across the footprint with early adoption trends described as encouraging.
summary: Cable One reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $348.9 million, a decrease from the prior year quarter driven by a 7.3% drop in residential data subscribers and declines in business services following asset divestitures. The company lost approximately 17,000 broadband customers due to elevated churn while acknowledging that acquisition initiatives are gaining traction with digital channels now accounting for roughly 25-35% of sales. Management reaffirmed full-year CapEx guidance but noted a sequential decline in Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow compared to the prior year.

negative_highlights: Etsy announced a workforce reduction of roughly 12% (approx. 220 employees) concentrated in product and engineering groups.
Active buyers remained stable year-over-year rather than growing, though sequential growth was noted for the first time since 2023.
positive_highlights: Gross buyer additions accelerated with habitual and repeat cohorts showing sequential growth, ending a multi-year decline in these metrics.
Mobile app GMS grew 12.5% year-over-year to become ~47% of total GMS, driven by improved discovery and fresher content.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook tightened upward to 29%-30%, incorporating expected benefits from the restructuring plan.
summary: Etsy reported Q2 FY2026 marketplace GMS of $2.6 billion (up 7.5% YoY) and revenue of $668 million with a take rate expanding to 25.9%. Management raised full-year guidance, projecting mid-single-digit GMS growth for the year and an adjusted EBITDA margin range of 29%-30%, while announcing a new $2 billion share repurchase program following the sale of Depop.

negative_highlights: Core FFO per share guidance unchanged at $2.76-$2.78 despite higher acquisition volume due to delayed timing
Occupancy expectations moderated for standalone memory care units, leaving the portfolio ~90 bps behind internal projections year-to-date
positive_highlights: Raised FY26 SHOP acquisition midpoint by $300 million to $900M and disposition proceeds by $465 million to $730M
Core SHOP portfolio growth guidance increased to a 14% midpoint with RevPAR up 50 bps driven by pricing strength
SHOP strategy transformation is ahead of schedule, targeting 40% pro forma NOI contribution from SHOP by end of Q3
summary: LTC Properties raised its SHOP acquisition guidance for FY26 by $300 million to a midpoint of $900 million and increased expected proceeds from dispositions/loan payoffs by $465 million to $730 million. Core FFO per share remained flat at $0.68 due to the timing of acquisitions offsetting incremental NOI, while core SHOP portfolio growth guidance was raised to 14% despite a slight moderation in occupancy expectations for standalone memory care units.

negative_highlights: Gross margin of 34.7% was slightly below target due to rapid growth.
Operating expenses increased to $13.6 million, including $5.7 million non-cash stock comp and $1.8 million non-recurring costs.
Company had supply chain and quality issues during the quarter, and management admits infrastructure is not yet ready for massive revenue.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 687% year-over-year and 107% quarter-over-quarter to $16.7 million.
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $400,000 from $1.6 million in Q1.
Raised $60 million at $30 per share; cash and working capital stand at $229 million and $367 million respectively.
summary: Unusual Machines reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $16.7 million, up 687% year-over-year and 107% quarter-over-quarter, with enterprise sales accounting for about 95% of revenue. GAAP net loss narrowed to $0.16 per share from $0.32 a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $400,000 from $1.6 million in Q1. Gross margin was 34.7%, slightly below target due to scaling. The company raised $60 million at $30 per share in May, ending the quarter with $229 million cash and over $367 million in working capital. Management reiterates strong demand and supply constraints through 2027, citing the Drone Dominance Gauntlet and other government programs, but acknowledges infrastructure buildout is needed and that Q3 will not show top-line impact from these investments.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell to 25% from 26.5% on sales mix
Energy and process revenue only up 5% due to capital project pushouts
positive_highlights: Record Q1 revenue of $71.3M, up 29% YoY
Defense revenue up 40% and space up 86% YoY
Backlog at record $557M; aftermarket up 20%
summary: Graham Corporation delivered record first-quarter revenue of $71.3 million, up 29% YoY (17% organic), with defense revenue up 40%, space up 86%, and energy/process up 5%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 28% to $8.8 million, but gross margin declined to 25% from 26.5% on sales mix. Backlog reached a record $557 million, and the company reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 guidance of 18% revenue growth and 44% adjusted EBITDA growth, alongside a three-year framework for 8-10% organic growth and 14-16% EBITDA margins by FY2029.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss widened to -$20.5M from -$15.6M YoY
Wavelo adjusted EBITDA fell to $2.8M from $5.4M YoY
Corporate adjusted EBITDA dropped to -$3.9M vs -$1.7M last year due to higher professional fees and mobile losses
positive_highlights: Second consecutive quarter of positive operating cash flow ($1.9M in Q2, $5.5M YTD)
Ting achieved first-ever positive adjusted EBITDA (+$1.5M) with 32% revenue growth
Retired ~$150M Ting preferred equity and extended credit facility to July 2029
summary: Tucows Q2 FY2026 revenue increased 2% YoY to $100.6M with gross profit up 17% to $25.8M, but adjusted EBITDA declined 2% YoY to $12.3M and GAAP net loss widened to -$20.5M. Ting posted its first positive adjusted EBITDA quarter (+$1.5M) with revenue up 32% YoY, while Domains revenue declined 4% but gross profit was stable. Wavelo revenue and profitability declined, and corporate headwinds from mobile and higher professional fees persisted. Management completed a credit facility extension and retired Ting preferred equity, but guided that corporate results face continued headwinds and mobile resolution is actively being sought.

negative_highlights: Management expects to finish year at lower end of guidance due to spend timing and consumer softening
Bingo Blitz revenue declined 9.5% YoY due to intentional shift away from low-quality users
Consumer sentiment softened mid-quarter; inflation pressuring discretionary spending
positive_highlights: Disney Solitaire revenue grew 15.5% sequentially with lower marketing spend
Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 28.2% from 16.8% sequentially
D2C penetration reached 39.3% of revenue, up 63.1% YoY
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $731.1 million, up 5% YoY but down 1.8% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA was $206.1 million with a 28.2% margin, up from 16.8% in Q1. D2C revenue grew 63.1% YoY to reach 39.3% of revenue. Management maintained full-year guidance but expects to land near the lower end, citing deliberate front-loaded marketing spend reduction and softening consumer demand. Disney Solitaire revenue grew 15.5% sequentially despite lower marketing spend, but management expects sequential revenue declines in the second half due to spend timing.

negative_highlights: Sequential net income down 27% from record Q2
FX and CFD revenues down 19% YoY
Self-directed retail segment net operating revenues down 17%
positive_highlights: Net operating revenues up 47% YoY to $719.7 million
Net income up 102% YoY to $127.9 million
Record securities volumes, with ADV up 33% YoY
summary: StoneX reported Q3 FY2026 net operating revenues of $719.7 million, up 47% YoY, and net income of $127.9 million, up 102% YoY, with diluted EPS of $1.00, up 85%. Strong growth was driven by Commercial and Institutional segments, with net operating revenues up 90% and 56% respectively, and record volumes in securities. RJO integration is on track, contributing $78.8 million in net operating revenues for the quarter, and Benchmark contributed $29.5 million, its best performance to date. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but management expressed confidence in the diversified business model and continued momentum.

negative_highlights: Fraud and identity revenue growth of 14% was near the low end of the targeted mid-to-high teens
Check verification revenue growth was driven by renewal timing, not underlying growth
Free cash flow conversion fell to 70% from 99% a year ago
positive_highlights: Total revenue up 18% YoY, above the high end of guidance
Check Fraud Defender ACV grew 73% YoY to over $22 million
Top-five U.S. bank completed pilot and entered consortium
summary: Mitek reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $54 million, up 18% year-over-year and above guidance, with Adjusted EBITDA margin around 38%. Fraud and identity revenue grew 14% to $29 million, while check verification revenue grew 24% on renewal timing. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $195-200 million, fraud and identity revenue to $105-109 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin to 32-34%. Key highlights include a top-five U.S. bank joining the Check Fraud Defender consortium, Fiserv live as a reseller, and a 73% year-over-year increase in CFD ACV to over $22 million, alongside an unexpected surge in age verification demand.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income was flat YoY due to higher interest expense and non-cash amortization from recent acquisitions (LMB and Harper).
Defense sales growth slowed to mid-single digits as customers returned to habitual ordering patterns following a strong prior year.
Management noted the need for additional capital investment in fans, motors, and restraints to keep up with stronger-than-expected demand.
positive_highlights: Commercial OEM sales surged 28% YoY driven by improved supply chain unlocking demand for Boeing/Airbus platforms.
Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 220 bps to 40.5%, with organic gross margin excluding amortization up 100 bps.
New business pipeline conversion accelerated, moving $750 million of potential revenue into the base business.
summary: Loar Holdings reported record Q2 FY2026 sales of $172 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 40.5%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for net sales ($665M-$675M), adjusted EBITDA ($265M-$270M), and GAAP net income ($56M-$60M). The company highlighted strong growth in commercial OEM (up 28%) and defense markets, with a new business pipeline converting to approximately $200 million of visibility over the next five years.

negative_highlights: Traffic remains softer than management would like
E-commerce revenue flat YoY due to Home Try-On headwind of ~2.8 points
Unexpected softness in last two weeks of June brought revenue to low end of range
positive_highlights: Revenue $236M, up ~10% YoY, at low end of guidance with July rebound
Eye exams grew over 30% YoY, now ~7% of revenue
Out-of-network insurance penetration now exceeds in-network; AOV nearly matches in-network
summary: Warby Parker reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $236 million (up ~10% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of ~$33 million (14% margin), including an $11.8 million tariff refund benefit. Eye exams grew over 30% YoY to ~7% of revenue, and e-commerce glasses/contacts order volume grew low double digits excluding the Home Try-On sunset. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, excluding any Intelligent Eyewear revenue benefit, while investing ahead of the fall launch. Traffic remained soft, with late-June weakness followed by a July rebound, but the company sees e-commerce, exams, and insurance momentum and expects Home Try-On headwinds to fade through 2026.

negative_highlights: Product gross margin remained negative at -1% (pro forma -11.6%) due to promotional spending for Prime Day, though management expects this to stabilize in the mid-to-high teens of negative going forward.
Inventory balance increased significantly to $48.4 million as the company builds stock ahead of holiday season and manages potential memory cost increases.
positive_highlights: Total revenue hit a record of $156 million with service revenue reaching an all-time high of $93 million.
Non-GAAP EPS beat consensus at $0.28, including the impact of ~$8M in tariff refunds which management plans to reinvest rather than pass through fully next quarter.
Full-year guidance was significantly raised on both top-line and bottom-line metrics following a strong first half.
summary: Arlo reported record Q2 FY26 results with total revenue of $156 million (up >20% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.28, driven by a new record in subscriptions/services revenue ($93M). Management significantly raised full-year guidance for both total revenue to the range of $580-$600 million and non-GAAP net income per share to $0.90-$1.00. The company highlighted strong subscriber growth (298k new paid accounts), improved retention, and a strategic shift in capital allocation using tariff refunds for reinvestment.

negative_highlights: Direct-to-consumer revenue declined 2% due to promotional pricing strategy.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA outlook faces a weather headwind reversing the Q2 benefit, estimated at ~$5M impact.
Existing home sales remain sluggish with inventory up to 4.5 months of supply.
positive_highlights: Total ending member count grew 1% for the first time since 2021, with real estate channel growth of 7%.
Gross margin expanded 100 bps to 59%, driven by dynamic pricing and favorable weather ($5M benefit).
summary: Frontdoor reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $645 million (up 5% YoY) and net income of $125 million (up 13%), driven by member growth in the real estate channel (+7%) and margin expansion to 59%. Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA ($585M-$600M, midpoint +$20M vs prior) and revenue ($2.19B-$2.21B), citing dynamic pricing optimization and operational leverage despite a weather headwind in Q3.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income declined year-over-year to $8.1 million due to an earnout provision related to the DataPath acquisition recorded in G&A expenses.
Non-GAAP gross margin contracted slightly to 32% from Q1 levels, attributed to a less favorable deal mix in defense and Peru segments.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 17% year-over-year driven by broad-based growth across defense (12%), commercial (20%), and Peru segments.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps sequentially from Q1 to approximately 12.6%, demonstrating strong operating leverage.
Defense business received $11 million in orders for the U.S. Department of War and multi-million dollar awards from a European ministry.
summary: Gilat reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $122.7 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $15.4 million (up 31% YoY). Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for revenues between $500-$520 million and adjusted EBITDA between $61-$66 million, despite noting unfavorable Israeli shekel movements expected to increase H2 operating expenses.

negative_highlights: Amgen's KYPROLIS net sales decreased 17% year-over-year due to lower volume, though this remains within royalty revenue guidance.
R&D expenses included a $12 million one-time charge related to the Orchestra BioMed investment which was expensed under GAAP rules.
positive_highlights: Royalty revenue increased 32% year-over-year to $48 million driven by strong sales of Filspari ($141M net sales) and OJEMDA ($204M net sales).
Adjusted EPS grew 48% to $2.37, reflecting operating leverage and the scalability of the royalty model.
Successfully completed a $700 million zero-coupon convertible note offering with no dilution up to approximately $524 per share.
summary: Ligand reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $64 million (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $2.37 (up 48%), driven by royalty growth from Filspari, Ohtuvayre, and ZELSUVMI. Management raised the low end of full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $9 per share while maintaining the upper end at $9.50, citing contributions from a recent convertible offering and XOMA acquisition synergies starting in Q3. The company closed its largest-ever transaction with XOMA Royalty shortly after quarter-end, adding over 120 assets and nearly doubling the late-stage clinical pipeline.

negative_highlights: Marketing spend deliberately stepped up to $19.4M but expected lower in Q3
Revenue yield expected to be flat for the full year with Q3/Q4 deceleration
Provision guidance remains 2.5-3% with potential step-up in Q3/Q4
positive_highlights: GMV growth 37.9% YoY to record $1.3B; May GMV surpassed December holiday GMV
Active subscribers up 76.4% YoY to 854,000; record 7.2x purchase frequency
Guidance raised: revenue growth now 35%, adjusted net income up to $185M
summary: Sezzle reported record Q2 2026 results with GMV up 37.9% YoY to $1.3 billion and revenue up 51.7% to $149.7 million. Net income reached $40.8 million (27.2% margin) and adjusted EBITDA was $58 million (38.8% margin), both ahead of prior trends. Active subscribers surged 76.4% YoY to 854,000, with record purchase frequency of 7.2x. Guidance was raised: revenue growth now targets 35% (upper end of prior 30-35% range), adjusted net income raised to $185 million, and EPS to $5.25, while new products SezzleCash and Sezzle Send are conservatively modeled.

negative_highlights: Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance was lowered from $453.8M-$461.8M to $440.5M-$445.5M due to the one-time gain on facility sales and anticipated contract modifications.

Operating margins in the Residential segment contracted to 22.4% (from 26.1%) primarily because of lower ICE populations during a temporary downturn, excluding special items like ERCs from the prior year comparison.
Management noted that negotiations for modified management contracts on sold facilities are not yet complete and could impact future earnings run rates.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS beat estimates by $0.04 and Adjusted EBITDA exceeded expectations by approximately $2 million despite lower enforcement activity.

Completed sale of four facilities (California City, Otay Mesa, Midwest Regional Reception Center, Prairie Correctional Facility) for gross proceeds totaling $1.5 billion + $734 million to fortify the balance sheet and reduce debt.
ICE populations in CoreCivic's care increased 17.7% since early April as enforcement activity resumed following temporary declines.
summary: CoreCivic reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $0.38 (up from prior year's $0.36) and Adjusted EBITDA of $109.4 million, beating analyst estimates despite a decline in ICE populations driven by temporary government shutdowns and leadership changes at DHS. Management updated full-year 2026 guidance to reflect the financial impact of four recent facility sales (net proceeds ~$1.6 billion) used for debt repayment, resulting in lower adjusted EBITDA ($440.5M-$445.5M vs prior $453.8M-$461.8M), though normalized FFO per share was raised to a range of $2.61-$2.70.

negative_highlights: Energy storage volume expected to be flat or down ~4% YoY due to a fire at Greenbushes' CGP3 plant which delayed ramp-up.
Third quarter net sales and EBITDA are expected to decrease sequentially as spodumene inventory impacts roll through margins in a rising price environment.
Supply constraints persist with low inventories (under 1 month for hydroxide) due to disruptions from the Middle East situation.
positive_highlights: Specialties segment raised full-year outlook for net sales to $1.4B-$1.6B and adjusted EBITDA to $275M-$325M driven by higher pricing and volumes.
Global lithium consumption up 45% YoY through May, with stationary storage demand accelerating significantly.
Cost and productivity improvements on track for the high end of the $100M-$150M full-year target.
summary: Albemarle reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $1.7 billion (up 31% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $858 million (more than doubling to a 49% margin). Management raised its full-year outlook for the specialties segment, increasing guidance ranges for both net sales ($1.4B-$1.6B) and adjusted EBITDA ($275M-$325M), while maintaining total company ranges due to strong year-to-date performance offsetting lower energy storage volume expectations from a plant fire.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP gross margin decreased approximately 90 basis points year-over-year, while adjusted EBITDA margin compressed roughly 200 bps.
Operating expenses increased 16% year-over-year to $154 million reflecting higher sales and marketing spend and investment in AI product development.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 13% year-over-year, driven by adoption of add-on products which was the largest driver for three consecutive quarters.
International business delivered a robust quarter with revenue up 28% year-over-year.
New AI product VinMax drove promoted listings to note 23% faster and generate 34% more leads per day than non-promoted listings.
summary: CarGurus reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $251 million (up 13% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $85 million (up 7% YoY), beating the midpoint of guidance. Management raised full-year profitability outlook, expecting non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA margins to compress by approximately 50-150 basis points in 2026 relative to 2025 due to disciplined investment and AI-driven efficiency gains. Full-year revenue growth guidance remains unchanged at 10%-13% YoY.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP operating loss widened due to unexpected French employer payroll taxes ($1.7M)
Royalty growth trajectory slowed slightly sequentially compared to prior quarters
GAAP gross margin compressed to 85% from historical levels due to subcontractor costs on government contracts
positive_highlights: Revenue beat at $24.1M and ACV plus royalties hit record high of $99.5M
Full-year revenue guidance raised by $3.5 million to $95-$98M range
No single customer exceeded 10% of licensed revenue in H1, confirming diversification
summary: Arteris reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $24.1 million (up 46% YoY) and ACV plus royalties of $99.5 million (up 44% YoY), both beating the top end of guidance. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $95-$98 million, citing continued strength in semiconductors despite higher payroll taxes impacting operating loss.

negative_highlights: Power CapEx increased by $128M at the midpoint of guidance, primarily due to accelerating equipment orders for Jack County.
BKV maintains a conservative stance on monetizing its Northeast Pennsylvania asset until gas prices rebound substantively.
positive_highlights: Record adjusted EBITDAX of $142M and record adjusted net income of $51M, more than doubling Q1 results despite lower natural gas prices.
Upstream production delivered at the high end of guidance with capital spending at the low end due to operational excellence.
Total cash costs decreased 10% compared to Q1 2026 as advanced completions and efficiencies drove performance.
summary: BKV reported its strongest financial quarter since going public with record adjusted EBITDAX of $142 million and record adjusted net income of $51 million. Upstream production came in at the high end of guidance while capital expenditures were executed at the low end, driven by operational efficiencies that lowered total cash costs 10% versus Q1. Management raised full-year upstream production guidance to a midpoint of 950 MMcfe/d and increased strategic power CapEx guidance to $400-$475 million.

negative_highlights: Gain on sale margin (ex-correspondent) declined to 311 bps from 322 bps in Q1
Adjusted revenue near midpoint, not above
Industry demand softened due to higher rates and affordability
positive_highlights: Record market share: purchase 6.2% (up 13% from Q4), refinance 14.3% (up 17%)
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 28% from 26% in Q1
Redfin mortgage leads more than doubled YoY in June
summary: In Q2 FY2026, Rocket Companies delivered adjusted revenue of $2.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $766 million (28% margin, up from 26% in Q1), and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.16, its most profitable quarter in four years despite a challenging spring market. The company achieved record market share in both purchase (6.2%) and refinance (14.3%), and is executing ahead of plan on the Redfin and Mr. Cooper integrations. Management emphasized a diversified revenue base, with over 70% of revenue recurring or less rate-sensitive, and expressed confidence in long-term earnings power.

negative_highlights: Pipeline segment earnings declined to $14.4 million from $15.4 million in Q2 2025 due to lower other income and higher depreciation/amortization expenses.
Bakken East Pipeline Project FERC filing delayed to the fourth quarter of 2026, pushing potential Final Investment Decision into late 2026 or early 2027.
positive_highlights: Electric utility earnings increased $14.7 million vs prior year due to higher retail sales revenue and recovery mechanisms from renewable investments like the Badger Wind Farm ($3.3M contribution).
Natural gas distribution segment loss narrowed significantly to a seasonal loss of $3.9 million compared to $7.4 million in Q2 2025, aided by new rates and customer growth.
Secured precedent agreements for the Bakken East Pipeline Project with customers totaling nearly 1.2 billion cubic feet per day.
summary: MDU Resources reported Q2 FY2026 earnings of $21.3 million ($0.10/share), beating the prior year's $13.7 million driven by higher retail sales volumes and new rates in Montana, Wyoming, Idaho, and Washington. The company reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guidance range of $0.93-$1.00 despite a shift to filing the Bakken East Pipeline Project application in Q4 rather than Q3 due to recent precedent agreements. Management highlighted continued customer growth across natural gas distribution (up 6.7% YoY) and secured data center load, though specific financial impacts of new projects remain pending regulatory approval.

negative_highlights: Real-time payments revenue declined YoY due to lower renewal opportunities and difficult comparisons against unusually strong prior-year volumes.
Biller segment adjusted EBITDA decreased YoY primarily due to mix shifts and one-time charges related to a terminated partnership, though underlying demand remains healthy.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 7% YoY with Payment Software up 9%, driven by issuing/acquiring growth of 37% in constant currency.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 34% from 32% last year, reflecting disciplined expense management and operating leverage.
Management raised full-year revenue guidance range (now $1.895B-$1.925B) and adjusted EBITDA guidance ($545M-$560M).
summary: ACI Worldwide reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $430 million (up 7% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.54 (up 54%), significantly beating expectations driven by strong Payment Software growth in issuing/acquiring (+37%) and healthy Biller performance despite prior-year headwinds. Management raised full year guidance for revenue to the range of $1.895-$1.925 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $545-$560 million, citing strong first-half execution and a robust pipeline including new U.S.-based ACI Connetic wins.

negative_highlights: Franchise revenue decreased 3.8%, driven by a $1.1 million reduction in IT pass-through fees related to the new point-of-sale rollout.
Food and paper costs as a percentage of company restaurant sales increased approximately 90 basis points year-over-year due to commodity inflation.
positive_highlights: System-wide same-store sales growth of 3.9%, with Q3 YTD comps accelerating to 5.8% driven by Loaded Quesadillas and World Cup marketing momentum.
Restaurant-level margin expanded to 19.5% despite a 4.1% headwind in commodity inflation, primarily from produce costs.
Digital sales grew 13% year-over-year representing approximately 28% of systemwide sales.
summary: El Pollo Loco reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $129.6 million with system-wide same-store sales growth of 3.9% and a restaurant-level margin of 19.5%. Management raised full-year guidance for comparable store sales to the 3.5%-4.5% range (from an implied lower prior) and increased Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $68-$70 million, while reducing expected capital spending due to remodel timing adjustments.

negative_highlights: Supply chain disruption from the U.S. Customs Withhold Release Order on Jordan imports requires air freight expediting, which may impact gross margin in Q3/Q4.
Non-scrub wear expansion carries lower margins than core scrub products, potentially pressuring blended profitability as mix shifts.
positive_highlights: Net revenues per active customer hit an all-time high of $229, surpassing COVID-era peaks.
Non-scrub wear category surged 40%, representing nearly 20% of total net revenue.
International segment delivered record growth at 67%, with new store contributions and strong comp performance.
summary: FIGS reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of $197 million (up 29% YoY), beating the prior guidance range and marking a third consecutive quarter with growth above 25%. Adjusted EBITDA margin surged to 18.6%, driven by pricing power, lower returns, and tariff refunds, while active customers grew 13% to 3.1 million. Management raised full-year revenue guidance from the prior 14%-16% range to approximately 20% growth.

negative_highlights: Enabling Technologies sales declined 26% due to a strategic shift toward flexible capital acquisition models rather than pure unit volume.
Nevro revenue was flat sequentially after a $1.7 million decline from Q1, with management noting trial volumes remain below historical levels until late in the year.
Management explicitly stated they would not raise full-year revenue guidance despite the strong quarter due to cautious expectations for Enabling Tech and Nevro recovery.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS beat significantly at $1.34 versus implied consensus, representing a 56% year-over-year increase.
Adjusted gross profit margin expanded to 69.4%, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of sequential expansion and nearing the mid-70s target.
International spine revenue grew 14% as reported (12% constant currency), led by double-digit gains in EMEA, Latin America, and APAC.
summary: Globus Medical reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $789.6 million (up 6% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.34 (up 56%), driven by strong spine growth in the U.S. (+7%) and international markets (+14%). The company reaffirmed full-year FY2026 revenue guidance at $3.18-$3.22 billion but raised its non-GAAP EPS guidance to a range of $4.95-$5.05 from the prior $4.70-$4.80, citing margin expansion and operating leverage.

positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS up 41% year-over-year
summary: Victory Capital reported record Q2 2026 results with revenue of $435 million, up 12% sequentially and 24% year-over-year, and adjusted EPS of $2.21, up 21% quarter-over-quarter and 41% year-over-year. Total client assets reached $346 billion, up 11% from Q1, with record net long-term inflows of $4.2 billion. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 55.8%, and long-term margin guidance was raised to at least 50%. The Pioneer integration is complete, with all $110 million in net synergies realized, and management is actively pursuing M&A, citing a deep pipeline.

negative_highlights: Revenue guidance was maintained at the prior range of $205-$215M rather than raised to match the strong Q2 performance.
CDMO revenue declined year-over-year, though management noted this is consistent with program timing variability.
GMP ModTail launch will not see orders until 2027 despite GMP product availability later in FY26.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded more than 1,600 bps YoY to 58.9% driven by favorable product mix and restructuring benefits.
TriLink revenue grew 12%, with GMP consumables surging 55% YoY due to large CleanCap clinical orders.
Adjusted EBITDA improved $19.1 million YoY, exceeding expectations despite a lumpy CDMO segment.
summary: Maravai LifeSciences reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $51.4 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $8.7 million (a beat vs expectations). Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $33-$35 million while maintaining the revenue outlook, citing improved profitability from TriLink's GMP mix shift rather than changes in top-line assumptions.

negative_highlights: Memory segment revenues declined approximately 14% sequentially due to muted demand in the DRAM cycle.
Supply chain remains stretched, leading to lead times extending between four and twelve months depending on product line.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $255 million, surpassing the top end of prior guidance.
Non-GAAP EPS of $2.51 exceeded the high end of second quarter guidance range ($2.70-$2.85).
Advanced packaging contributed nearly 25% of product revenue with record sales driven by dimensional metrology.
summary: Nova Ltd reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $255 million (up 16% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.51, both at the high end or exceeding guidance. The company delivered operating margins in line with its upper-target model while maintaining strong cash reserves above $1.7 billion. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance to a range of $277-$287 million (midpoint ~$282M) and reiterated long-term growth drivers including advanced packaging adoption.

negative_highlights: Occupancy growth lagged internal expectations specifically within the AL segment due to strategic operator-led leadership upgrades and transitions.
OMF same-store cash NOI decreased 0.4% year-over-year impacted by a one-time increase in utility expenses during the quarter.
Third-quarter guidance does not yet include potential upside from five pipeline properties currently subject to an auction process.
positive_highlights: Same-store cash NOI margin expanded 230 bps year-over-year to 22.4% driven by rate growth and operating leverage.
Raised full-year SHOP same-store cash NOI guidance range to 15%-18%, reflecting strong Q2 outperformance relative to expectations.
Successfully closed or placed under contract approximately $400 million in senior housing acquisitions since the start of Q2.
summary: NHP reported Q2 FY26 same-store cash NOI growth of 20.1% driven by occupancy and margin expansion to 22.4%, though OMF segment NOI declined slightly due to one-time utility costs. Management raised full-year SHOP same-store cash NOI guidance range from the prior low-mid teens to 15%-18%. The company executed significant external growth with $30 million in new acquisitions, a hard deal on an $528 million outpatient medical facility portfolio disposition, and recast its credit facility up to $1.2 billion.

negative_highlights: Total CapEx increased by CAD 317 million YoY due to accelerated Ziply Fiber build-out and AI Fabric investments.
Wireless product revenue declined 6.6% YoY as the company disciplined hardware discounting in favor of higher margins.
positive_highlights: Bell Media delivered an exceptional quarter with revenue up 8.9% and Adjusted EBITDA up 3.8%, driven by FIFA World Cup performance (+5.3% advertising) and Crave subscriber growth (23% YoY to 5.1M).
Ziply Fiber achieved its highest quarterly residential net adds since acquisition with 45,271 additions in Canada and 99,600 total for the segment.
Wireless postpaid churn improved four basis points year-over-year to a three-year low of 1.02%.
summary: BCE reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue growth of 1.5% and Adjusted EBITDA growth of 1%, driven by strong performance in Ziply Fiber (45k residential net adds) and Bell Media (+8.9%). Management reconfirmed full-year 2026 financial guidance targets, citing disciplined execution despite higher CapEx for AI Fabric investments which pushed leverage to approximately 3.7x.

negative_highlights: Management lowered full-year IBSRELA guidance due to significant payer hurdles including step edits and prior authorizations slowing new patient starts.
R&D expenses surged 66% YoY to $26.1 million due to ACCEL trial enrollment costs.
positive_highlights: Combined revenue reached a record high of $118 million with robust growth across both products.
IBSRELA demand remains strong evidenced by the highest quarterly prescriptions and refills to date despite access friction.
Net loss narrowed significantly from $38M in Q1 2026 to $16.7M, narrowing losses on the path toward profitability.
summary: Ardelyx reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $118 million (31% YoY growth), driven by IBSRELA ($86.2M) and XPHOZAH ($31.9M). Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance for IBSRELA to a range of $350-$370 million due to significant payer hurdles impacting new patient starts, while maintaining the XPHOZAH forecast at $110-$120 million and revising OpEx guidance below $500 million. Despite acknowledging that performance fell short of internal expectations regarding access challenges, management expressed confidence in their mitigation strategies for H2 2026.

negative_highlights: SG&A expenses increased significantly to $20.1M due to commercial headcount expansion and public company costs.
R&D spending rose sharply to $3.4M as the company invests heavily in robotics platform development and new product lines.
positive_highlights: Net revenue surged 56% YoY to $17.2M driven by new surgeon onboarding and core category volume expansion.
Gross margin expanded sequentially and year-over-year to 78.3%, supported by ASP uplifts from new product launches (I135 RFX, N22 Glenosphere).
Full-year guidance raised with high conviction despite typical seasonality in Q3.
summary: Shoulder Innovations reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of $17.2 million, a 56% year-over-year increase driven by new surgeon adoption and increased utilization in the core category where volume grew approximately 50%. Gross margin expanded to 78.3%, up from 76.2% last year due to ASP improvements and cost reductions. Management raised full-year 2026 net revenue guidance to $67-$69 million (42%-46% growth) from the prior range of $65-$68 million, citing robust customer activity and a deepening pipeline.

negative_highlights: New residential same-branch sales declined 6%, dragging down overall installation segment performance amid affordability concerns.
Adjusted gross margin decreased from 34.2% to 33.3%, pressured by a 50 bps fuel cost headwind and mix shifts toward lower-margin distribution/manufacturing businesses.
Single-family starts fell 4% YoY, with public builder revenue down mid-single digits for the back half of the year.
positive_highlights: Heavy commercial same-branch sales growth exceeded 15%, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth in that segment.
Other segment revenue grew 50% net of eliminations (28% on a same-branch basis), driven by strong cellulose insulation demand and industrial fibers.
Multifamily contract backlog continues to grow, with sales inflecting positively in June and July despite broader single-family headwinds.
summary: Consolidated revenue grew 2% YoY to $778 million in Q2 FY26, driven by strong commercial growth (heavy commercial up >15%) and acquisitions, while same-branch installation sales declined less than 1%. Adjusted gross margin contracted slightly to 33.3%, impacted by a 40 bps headwind from the lower-margin 'other' segment growing 50% net of eliminations and increased fuel costs reducing installation margins by 50 bps. Management provided no financial guidance, citing recent acquisitions as an outlier factor.

negative_highlights: Lead times stretching due to foundry/OSAT constraints; some orders inside lead time go unsupported.
Data center revenue still small fraction of potential; many design wins have not yet shipped in volume.
Gross margin guidance not expected to continue rising above this level.
positive_highlights: Revenue and non-GAAP metrics all beat high end of guidance; EPS $0.76 beat by $0.07.
Data center sales up 97.8% YoY in June quarter; calendar 2026 data center expected ~$1 billion (plus 69% YoY).
summary: Q1 FY2027 revenue was $1.485 billion, up 13.2% sequentially and 38% year-over-year, beating the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.76 beat guidance by $0.07; gross margin expanded to 63.8% (up 222 bps sequentially) and operating margin to 35.1% (up 452 bps sequentially). Guidance for September quarter is strong: revenue up 8% sequentially, gross margin 66-67%, EPS $0.91-$0.95 (up 165.7% YoY at midpoint). Data center sales are booming, up 97.8% YoY in the June quarter, with calendar 2026 expected to reach ~$1 billion (up 69% YoY).

negative_highlights: Vital Care segment declined organically by 4% and reported revenue fell significantly due to the deconsolidation of IV Solutions.
OEM wind-down in international geographies continues to drag growth rates, with management noting a point or two headwind for the remainder of the year.
Currency translation impacts remain painful, specifically from the Costa Rican colón and Mexican peso, creating volatility that offsets some operational gains.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS beat at $2.37, representing a 13% year-over-year increase driven by core business earnings growth offsetting discrete items like JV deconsolidation and tariffs.
Consumables sales hit record levels with balanced organic growth across all four product families despite macro headwinds in international geographies.
Management raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance range to $415-$435M, narrowing the previous band while maintaining a positive outlook on gross margin expansion.
summary: ICU Medical reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $548 million (1% reported growth vs 6% organic), with adjusted EPS of $2.37 and Adjusted EBITDA of $110 million, beating expectations as the company raised its full-year guidance for both metrics. Management highlighted record revenues in consumables ($+6%) and infusion systems ($+12%), offset by a decline in Vital Care due to deconsolidation. The company repaid $50M in debt using strong free cash flow of $62 million (including tariff refunds) and raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance from the previous range of $400-$430M to $415-$435M.

negative_highlights: Drydock costs expected to increase in Q3 and Q4 2026
Supply growth of 3.3% over last 12 months
No explicit full-year guidance provided
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $1.21 and EBITDA of $184.2 million
Cash balance increased to $532 million despite shareholder returns
Mark-to-market gain of ~$56 million on Kamsarmax newbuildings
summary: Star Bulk reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $1.21 and adjusted EBITDA of $184.2 million, with a daily cash margin of $17,944. The company declared a $0.09 per share dividend and continues to return 100% of operating cash flow. Management highlighted strong cash generation, low leverage (net debt at 50% of demolition value), and ongoing fleet rejuvenation with new Kamsarmax deliveries, while noting expectations for Simandou volumes to ramp from 15-20 million tons in 2026 to 120 million by 2029.

negative_highlights: Q2 net income was impacted by a one-time inventory step-up amortization of $2 million and contingent consideration expense of $5.9 million.
FX headwinds reduced bottom-line earnings by approximately $6.6 million in the quarter.
Management noted that Q3 revenue is expected to be lower than Q2 as mix reverts from high-margin Zircaloy robotic arms, with European margins potentially softening.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 32% year-over-year to $207.1 million, significantly exceeding typical expectations given recent M&A integration headwinds.
Adjusted EBITDA surged 56% YoY with gross margins expanding 120 bps to 42.6%, aided by favorable mix and volume leverage in the Zircaloy segment.
Backlog increased $13 million sequentially, driven particularly by Environmental Operations Division (EOD) demand for sensors and robots.
summary: Cadre reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $207.1 million (up 32% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 56%, driven by strong performance in armor, duty gear, nuclear, and distribution segments including recent acquisitions Alien Gear and TYR Tactical. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue between $749M-$769M (midpoint ~$759M) and adjusted EBITDA of $139M-$144M (implied margin 18.6%), citing a record backlog increase of $13 million sequentially. The company expects Q3 revenue around $190M with margins normalizing, while maintaining an organic growth outlook in the high single digits to low double digits for nuclear and mid-single digits for distribution.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue growth guidance of 25.5%-26% implies deceleration from Q2's 27%
Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance remains negative, reflecting seasonal patterns and investment
Gross margin expected to revert lower in Q3 as non-subscription revenue normalizes
positive_highlights: Revenue up 27% YoY to $136 million, above the high end of guidance
Pipeline doubled YoY for the second consecutive quarter, surpassing $700 million in growth ACV
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$3.4 million, a record low margin of -2.5%
summary: Via reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $136 million, up 27% year-over-year, with 847 customers (up 23% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to -$3.4 million from -$8.1 million in the prior year. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $550-$553 million (26.6%-27.3% growth) while maintaining adjusted EBITDA guidance, and noted pipeline doubled for the second consecutive quarter. Gross margin expanded to 41% due to favorable mix, and adjusted net loss per share improved to -$0.01. Growth is driven by strong U.S. performance (up 35% YoY), network deals, and new AI Labs initiatives.

negative_highlights: Cable segment EBITDA declined 3% in Q4 due to higher sports rights costs
Free cash flow impacted by World Cup working capital timing, with collections expected in fiscal 2027
positive_highlights: Record full-year revenue of over $17 billion and EBITDA of $3.9 billion
Q4 advertising revenue up 78%, with Tubi revenue growth accelerating to 35%
Management calls fiscal 2027 off to an excellent start with strong political and upfront momentum
summary: Fox delivered record fiscal 2026 results with revenue up 5% to over $17 billion and EBITDA up 8% to a record $3.9 billion. Q4 revenue grew 28% to $4.2 billion and EBITDA grew 27% to $1.2 billion, driven by a 78% advertising revenue increase from the FIFA World Cup and Tubi's 35% revenue growth. Management raised the semi-annual dividend to $0.29 and expects continued momentum in fiscal 2027 with World Cup knockout stages and midterm elections. The pending Roku acquisition is on track for closing in first half calendar 2027.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $159 million from $42.7 million year-over-year, primarily due to an $86.2 million non-cash warrant fair value adjustment.
R&D expenses increased substantially to $48.7 million (from $29.8M) and G&A rose to $26.4 million (from $11.1M), reflecting heavy investment in clinical trials and commercial build-out.
positive_highlights: Phase III study EMERGE met all primary endpoints, demonstrating an 8.1 point placebo-adjusted improvement on MADRS at week six and the largest treatment effect ever reported in a Phase III MDD study.
summary: Definium Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 results with R&D expenses of $48.7 million and G&A expenses of $26.4 million, driven by clinical program expansion and commercial readiness investments for DT120 ODT. The company recorded a net loss of $159 million in the quarter compared to $42.7 million last year, largely due to an $86.2 million non-cash expense from warrant fair value adjustments as share prices rose. Management highlighted positive Phase III EMERGE data for MDD and upcoming VOYAGE results for GAD while noting a strengthened balance sheet with approximately $1.1 billion in cash sufficient through 2030.

negative_highlights: Management noted potential operational inefficiencies and higher auction fees for Panama Canal transits due to a high probability of El Niño weather events.
Other operating expenses included financial advisory costs related to inadequate tender offers from Diana Shipping, totaling $13.1 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of nearly $57 million exceeded expectations as dry bulk market fundamentals strengthened.
Q2 dividend increased by over 400% year-over-year, marking a record level since the strategy's inception in 2021.
Fleet acquisitions have generated an IRR exceeding 30%, with new vessels contributing approximately $0.15 per share to Q2 dividends.
summary: Genco Shipping reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $56.7 million and declared a dividend of $0.80 per share, which was more than double the prior quarter's payout. The company generated strong cash flow driven by a time charter equivalent rate (TCE) averaging over $24,200 per day, its highest quarterly level since 2022. Management projects Q3 and Q4 dividends to exceed $1 per share each based on current fixtures and the forward freight curve.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA guidance moved to lower end of previous range
Rest of world EBITDA declined slightly due to inflation outpacing pricing
Macroeconomic uncertainty and demand softness in Europe
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 9% to $99 million, strongest quarter as Magnera
Americas adjusted EBITDA up 16% to $71 million
Free cash flow guidance reaffirmed at $90-$110 million
summary: Magnera reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $857 million with adjusted EBITDA of $99 million, a 9% increase and 70 basis point margin improvement year-over-year. The company reaffirmed free cash flow guidance of $90-$110 million but moved adjusted EBITDA to the lower end of prior guidance due to persistent inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty. Americas EBITDA rose 16% to $71 million, while Rest of World declined slightly. New product Universa launched and Project CORE synergies are at full run rate.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP EPS fell to $0.17 from $0.30 YoY due to one-time items
Gross margin at 26.3%, impacted by ~160 bps from Comtrafo purchase accounting and unfavorable mix
Q2 revenue guidance of >$85M implies sequential decline due to accelerated deliveries into Q1
positive_highlights: Q1 revenue of $94.1M, up 30% YoY, surpassing expectations
Orders over $130M, including record $25M utility mining order; backlog above $300M
Generated $16M operating cash flow; cash at $153.1M
summary: AMSC reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $94.1 million, up 30% year-over-year, with Grid up 27% and Wind up 45%. GAAP net income was $9.5 million ($0.21 per share), while non-GAAP net income was $7.6 million ($0.17 per share), down from $0.30 a year ago due to purchase accounting and tax timing. Orders reached over $130 million, including a record $25 million mining utility order, and 12-month backlog exceeded $300 million. Q2 guidance calls for revenue above $85 million and non-GAAP EPS above $0.17, with fiscal 2026 expected to be better than fiscal 2025.

negative_highlights: Natural gas Waha prices averaged negative $3.14/Mcf, forcing curtailments
Inflationary pressures from rising diesel costs partially offset by efficiency gains
Management expressed uncertainty about hitting $675M CapEx target if oil prices stay high, affecting fuel costs
positive_highlights: Record FCF of $751M, up ~50% QoQ, and record FCF/share of $0.88
Full-year oil production guidance raised to 199 MBbl/d, 10% above 2025, with CapEx down ~1%
Year-to-date added ~55,000 net acres for ~$1.05B at attractive valuations
summary: Permian Resources reported record Q2 free cash flow of $751 million, up nearly 50% quarter-over-quarter, and record FCF per share of $0.88. Oil production increased 3% sequentially to about 198,000 bbl/day, helped by a 50% increase in workover rigs and higher working interest (82% vs original 75% expectations). Full-year oil production guidance was raised to 199,000 bbl/day (10% above 2025), while CapEx midpoint is $1.95 billion, about 1% lower than last year. Management highlighted aggressive year-to-date acquisitions of about 55,000 net acres for ~$1.05 billion, with leverage at 0.5x.

negative_highlights: CRS segment-adjusted EBITDA margin declined 270 bps to 26.3%
Military and helicopter revenue declined 3% due to input delays
Free cash flow guidance maintained despite strong Q2 due to supply chain fluidity
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to a record 14.4%
LEAP and CFM56 DFW programs reached profitability in the quarter
Raising full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS
summary: StandardAero's Q2 2026 showed revenue up 4.6% to $1.6B, adjusted EBITDA up 12.3% to $230M with record 14.4% margin, and adjusted EPS up 24% to $0.40. Both LEAP and CFM56 DFW programs reached profitability, and the company raised full-year guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS. CRS segment margin declined 270bps on timing issues but is expected to recover in H2. A new $180M license expansion is expected to add ~$25M annual EBITDA over the next few years.

negative_highlights: Salt Adjusted EBITDA down 15% due to higher production costs and lower highway volumes
Production costs at Goderich higher than planned, with no efficiency gains yet
Tariff exposure on Canadian salt a fluid risk despite mitigation efforts
positive_highlights: Plant Nutrition Adjusted EBITDA up 32% to $15 million, full-year guidance raised to $49-$57 million
Highway de-icing pricing up 8%, C&I pricing up 6%, with substantial double-digit bid season price gains
summary: Compass Minerals reported Q3 FY2026 total Adjusted EBITDA of $39.9 million, slightly down from $41 million a year ago, with a net loss of $5.7 million improved from a $17 million loss. Salt revenue rose 5% to $173.9 million on 9% pricing gains, but salt Adjusted EBITDA fell 15% due to higher costs and lower volumes. Plant Nutrition Adjusted EBITDA jumped 32% to $15 million, prompting a full-year segment guidance raise to $49-$57 million. Management raised consolidated EBITDA guidance midpoint to $230 million (range $218-$242 million) but narrowed salt guidance, citing cost pressures and operational delays; bid season pricing is strong with double-digit increases, but tariffs remain a risk.

negative_highlights: Husky adjusted net sales fell ~9% YoY to $339.6 million due to macro uncertainty, elevated resin prices, shipping disruptions from the Middle East conflict, and tariff impacts.
Pro forma adjusted EBITDA margins contracted by approximately 230 bps on a consolidated basis as Husky's weakness offset CompoSecure's strength.
Management explicitly stated that full-year guidance does not assume material improvements in macro conditions or resin prices beyond marginal stabilization.
positive_highlights: CompoSecure delivered record sales of $133.6 million, up ~12% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 70 bps to 41.3% driven by ROS deployment and new program wins like Samsung and American Express.
Husky expanded margin sequentially by approximately 590 basis points through better labor/fixed cost absorption despite lower volume.
Pipeline growth at Husky accelerated with double-digit increases in systems and aftermarket tooling, indicating demand is being deferred rather than canceled.
summary: GPGI reported Q2 FY26 pro forma adjusted net sales of $473.2 million (down ~4% YoY) and pro forma adjusted EBITDA of $113.9 million (down ~13% YoY), driven by a strong beat at CompoSecure but significant weakness at Husky due to macro headwinds, volatile resin prices, shipping disruptions, and tariffs. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue ($1.95B-$2.1B) and adjusted EBITDA margins (27%-29%), noting that the maintained ranges do not assume material further improvement in market conditions despite some stabilization.

negative_highlights: Q4 net churn rose 37 bps YoY to 2.2%, with 17 bps from one-time factors
Q4 free cash flow fell 21% YoY to $89M due to working capital timing
FY2027 churn expected roughly flat YoY
positive_highlights: Revenue of $608M beat the high end of implied guidance by $6M
Adjusted EBITDA ex-items of $166M was $12M above the high end of guidance
Exceeded $100M cost savings goal; first full year of positive net income and operating income
summary: Peloton delivered Q4 FY2026 revenue of $608M, slightly above guidance, with gross margin up 260bps to 56.7%. Adjusted EBITDA was $142M (or $166M excluding one-time legal contingencies), above guidance, and FY2026 marked the first full year of positive net income ($63M) and operating income ($161M). Management projects record gross margin, EBITDA, and net income in FY2027, while expecting churn to be roughly flat year-over-year. The company is also executing a balance-sheet refinancing and plans new consumer product launches in fall 2027.

negative_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA decreased year-over-year by approximately 10% to $96 million, primarily due to the video business shutdown and higher distribution costs.
Consumer revenue declined 2%, with organic broadband subscriber count dropping by 500 lines before acquisition offset.
Business gross margin contracted to 75.5% as a result of roughly $12 million in increased distribution costs related to Quintillion network restoration.
positive_highlights: Consumer gross margin expanded to 71.8% driven by declines in video programming costs following business exit.
Wireless subscriber base grew by 2,100 lines during the quarter despite organic broadband churn.
GCI net leverage stands at 2.1x with $447 million of undrawn capacity on its credit facility.
summary: Liberty Capital reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $261 million (flat YoY) and Adjusted OIBDA of $96 million (down 11% YoY). The quarter was impacted by the shutdown of the video business, a small organic decline in consumer broadband subscribers offset by an acquisition, and increased distribution costs from restoring service on the Quintillion network. Management announced plans to initiate a quarterly dividend starting December with an initial aggregate amount of $60 million per year.

negative_highlights: GAAP net income dropped sharply to $0.07 per share due to a one-time charge of approximately $0.34 per share.
