Gross originations declined significantly from Q1 levels as the company managed leverage and waited for deal closings in July.
Non-accruals increased slightly, representing 2.7% of cost basis or 1.5% of fair value at quarter end.
positive_highlights: Net investment income fully covered the declared third quarter distribution of $0.38 per share ($0.36 regular + $0.02 supplemental).
Weighted average internal risk rating remained stable at 4.3, consistent with the prior quarter.
Interest coverage ratio improved to 2.5x from 2.3x in Q1 despite adding four new non-accrual names.
summary: NCDL reported Q2 FY26 net investment income of $0.41 per share and GAAP EPS of $0.07, which was significantly below the prior quarter's $0.18 due to realized/unrealized losses totaling $0.34 per share driven by amendments on two underperforming investments. Net asset value declined 1.8% quarter-over-quarter from $17.50 to $17.19, while gross originations fell materially to approximately $12 million compared to $83 million in Q1 due to leverage management and deal timing. Management maintained a defensive posture with non-accruals rising slightly to 1.5% of fair value but emphasized strong credit metrics including an interest coverage ratio of 2.5x.

negative_highlights: Total consolidated revenue declined 1.2% YoY due to a 9.4% drop in the Consumer segment.
Q3 guidance anticipates combined gross margin headwinds of approximately 200 bps driven by elevated memory costs and supply constraints.
APAC Enterprise growth was down 16% YoY as management addresses ongoing go-to-market transformation challenges.
positive_highlights: Enterprise revenue grew 7.7% YoY to $89M driven by double-digit growth in Pro AV Managed Switches.
Non-GAAP gross margin hit an all-time high of 54.1%, up 660 bps YoY, with contribution margin at its highest level since Q1 2019 (25.9%).
Consumer ARR grew 15% YoY to $41.6M and direct-to-consumer channel revenue increased over 20%.
summary: NETGEAR reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $168.6 million (down 1.2% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.16, beating the high end of guidance due to strong Enterprise growth offsetting Consumer declines. Management raised full-year outlooks for both revenue and operating margin based on this performance but issued a cautious Q3 guide expecting combined gross margins to face approximately 200 bps headwinds from memory costs, with non-GAAP operating margins projected between -3% and 0%. The company repurchased $12.9 million in shares during the quarter.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 150 basis points due to revenue mix shift toward equipment-heavy commercial projects
Management conservatively guided, noting Q2 included some revenue acceleration that will impact second-half performance
Interest expense was lower, but operating cash flow not fully detailed in this excerpt
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 51% to a record $33 million, with a record 28.2% margin on net revenue
Contract revenue up 33% to $231 million; organic net revenue growth was 18% year-over-year
Full-year financial targets raised; strong contract wins including $110 million LADWP solar streetlight expansion
summary: Willdan reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with contract revenue up 33% year-over-year to $231 million, net revenue up 23% to $117 million, and record adjusted EBITDA of $33 million, a 51% increase. Adjusted EPS rose 38% to $2.07, and GAAP EPS increased 53% to $1.58. Management raised full-year financial targets, citing robust demand, especially from commercial data center projects, and margin expansion driven by mix and AI-enabled productivity. They guided to a 25% adjusted EBITDA margin for 2026, up from 21.8% in 2025, though noted Q2's 28.2% margin was aided by revenue acceleration and may not persist.

negative_highlights: Core Celsius brand net sales declined approximately 12% YoY due to SKU rationalization and shipment timing gaps.
Q3 outlook for Celsius is expected to be similar to Q2 before exiting the year into growth, indicating continued pressure.
Alani Nu faces a tougher comp in Q4 compared to Q3 as it rolls over inventory builds from last year.
positive_highlights: Alani Nu net sales grew approximately 21% YoY with retail and track channel growth of ~56%.
Gross margins remained consistent at ~48%, offsetting commodity inflation through integration efficiencies.
Completed Rockstar Energy integration on the nine-month timeline, stabilizing that portfolio segment.
summary: Celsius Holdings reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $818 million (up ~11% YoY), driven by Alani Nu's strong growth but offset by a decline in the core Celsius brand due to SKU rationalization and shipment timing. Gross margins remained flat at approximately 48%, while SG&A was held steady despite lower volume, resulting in adjusted EBITDA of $184 million (down from prior year). Management reaffirmed that Q3 results will mirror Q2 for the Celsius brand before a recovery is expected to begin in late 2026/early 2027.

negative_highlights: One-time non-cash charge of ~$31 million related to convertible note remeasurement
SG&A guidance increased by an additional $5 million to ~$50 million increase for the year
Gvoke's weak start to the year, though it rebounded sequentially
positive_highlights: Total revenue $92.1 million, up 29% YoY; net product revenue up 34%
RECORLEV up 81% YoY to $56.8 million with records in referrals, new starts, and prescribers
Full retirement of convertible notes eliminates ~$3 million annual interest and simplifies capital structure
summary: Xeris reported record Q2 2026 total revenue of $92.1 million, up 29% year-over-year, and net product revenue of $91 million, up 34%. RECORLEV grew 81% to $56.8 million, Gvoke rebounded sequentially to $22.5 million, and KEVEYIS delivered $11.7 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose over 50% to $19.3 million. The company raised the bottom end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $385-390 million, reflecting 33% growth at the midpoint. It also fully retired its convertible notes with a one-time non-cash charge of $31 million, and advanced its XP-8121 pipeline toward a planned phase III start by year-end.

negative_highlights: Phase III readout timing for petosemtamab colorectal cancer trials delayed to Q1 FY27 from earlier expectations.
Interim analysis for EPKINLY frontline DLBCL study expected in Q4, later than analyst models anticipated.
positive_highlights: EPKINLY sales grew 48% YoY to DKK 312 million with accelerated growth and new site activations in the US community setting.
Positive top-line results from Phase III EPCORE DLBCL-2 trial showing statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival for EPKINLY plus lenalidomide/rituximab.
European approval of EPKINLY plus R-squared for second-line follicular lymphoma, making it the first and only bispecific-based therapy approved in Europe for this indication.
summary: Genmab reported strong first-half FY26 results with total revenue growing 25% YoY to DKK 396 million for its proprietary portfolio (EPKINLY and TIVDAK), driven by a 48% increase in EPKINLY sales. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting revenue of DKK 4.3-4.5 billion (+19% YoY) and operating profit of DKK 1.1-1.4 billion, reflecting the strength of their late-stage pipeline progress including positive Phase III interim data for EPKINLY in DLBCL.

negative_highlights: Life Sciences revenue fell 31.3% YoY due to liquidity constraints impacting R2 unit sales
Spectrum segment revenue decreased by $54 million (from implied prior period) and Adjusted EBITDA dropped ~$600k-$400k due to network terminations
Cash position declined from $108.2M at year-end 2025 to $87.8M as of June 30, 2026
positive_highlights: Infrastructure achieved a record quarter with Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7M and gross margin expansion of ~60 bps YoY
Broadcasting completed refinancing to retire debt, repurchase equity interests, and fund transaction costs ahead of CONX acquisition
DBMG adjusted backlog increased to $2.7 billion with strong demand visibility into 2027-2028
summary: INNOVATE reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $421.6 million (up 74.2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $46.3 million (up from $15.7m), driven primarily by a record Infrastructure segment ($414M). However, Life Sciences revenue declined 31.3% to $2.2 million due to liquidity constraints at R2, while the Spectrum segment saw slight declines following network terminations.

negative_highlights: Sales down 21% year-over-year to $152.5 million
Oil and gas end market remains soft with no sign of significant improvement
Capacity ramp-up costs at Wisconsin are expected to persist, pressuring gross margin
positive_highlights: Q2 sales of $152.5 million up 18.6% sequentially, exceeding prior expectation of roughly flat revenue
Gross margin improved 420 basis points sequentially to 27.1% from 22.9%
Operating cash flow of $56.6 million enabled debt reduction of ~$30.8 million
summary: In Q2 FY2026, Power Solutions International reported net sales of $152.5 million, up 18.6% sequentially from Q1, exceeding expectations, but down 21% year-over-year due to softer oil and gas demand and shipment timing. Gross margin improved sequentially by 420 basis points to 27.1%, driven by operational improvements at Wisconsin, though year-over-year it declined from 28.2%. Operating cash flow was strong at $56.6 million, enabling $30.8 million debt reduction. Management expects H2 2026 sales to exceed H1, roughly in line with H2 2025, but provided no formal guidance due to order timing variability and continued oil and gas softness.

negative_highlights: Two Florida managed-only contracts valued at $100 million combined annual revenue were delayed until July 1, 2027 due to unresolved budgetary issues.
No revenues were recognized from the new skip tracing contract in Q2 due to a lapse in ICE appropriations funding during the government shutdown.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 15% YoY and net income surged 63% YoY driven by new contracts entered in 2025 totaling up to $520 million annually.
ISAP V contract revenue remained resilient despite reduced pricing due to a technology shift toward higher-priced ankle monitors, with participant counts rising from ~17k to ~54k on GPS devices.
Management raised full-year net income guidance range and adjusted EBITDA guidance following strong first-half performance.
summary: GEO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $732 million (up 15% YoY) and net income of $47.5 million (up 63% YoY), driven by new ICE contracts and a technology mix shift in the ISAP program. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for GAAP net income to $168-$175 million on revenues of $2.95-$3.05 billion, excluding earnings from two Florida facilities delayed until July 1, 2027 due to budgetary issues.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined to $18 million from $27 million year-over-year
Adjusted net loss widened to $17.7 million from $10.8 million
Operating and G&A expenses up 3.8% due to higher payroll and fuel costs
positive_highlights: May and June volumes exceeded prior year levels due to counter-seasonal customer growth
RNG credit prices up: California LCFS +31% YoY, D3 RIN +8% YoY
New RNG facilities to add ~300,000 MMBtus annually, reaching full operational platform
summary: Suburban Propane reported an adjusted net loss of $17.7 million ($0.27 per unit) for Q3 FY2026, wider than the prior year's loss of $10.8 million ($0.17). Adjusted EBITDA fell to $18 million from $27 million. Retail propane volumes declined 1.8% to 70.6 million gallons, mainly due to warm April weather, partially offset by customer base growth. The company highlighted RNG project progress, with new facilities expected to boost annual injection to 750,000-800,000 MMBtus for FY2027, and noted improving environmental credit prices.

negative_highlights: Wheels volume declined 8% YoY (though up sequentially), with aluminum pass-through diluting margins by ~360 bps
Engineered Structures revenue fell 13% due to the divestiture of the Savannah Disc facility
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24% YoY with organic growth of 21%, excluding M&A impacts
EBITDA margin expanded 340 bps to 32.1%; EBITDA outpaced revenue by 59%
Free cash flow in Q2 was $479 million, enabling a dividend increase and share repurchases
summary: Howmet reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $3.4 billion (up 24% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.33 (up 46%), both beating the high end of guidance with EBITDA margin expanding to 32.1%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue, EBITDA, and EPS across the board while maintaining a strong balance sheet following an $840 million free cash flow generation in H1.

negative_highlights: Gross-to-Net (GTN) for BRINSUPRI came in at the lower end of the previous guidance range due to better-than-expected contracting dynamics.
Combined R&D and SG&A expenses increased by 38% year-over-year as investments scale up.
positive_highlights: BRINSUPRI revenue reached $309.2M in Q2 with new patient starts accelerating to approximately 7,000 per quarter (vs prior expectation of 6,300).
Management raised peak sales estimates for BRINSUPRI from >$5B to >$7B and TPIP from >$2B to >$6B.
TPIP open-label extension data showed patients catching up on efficacy metrics after switching from placebo, with 80% achieving functional Class 1 or 2.
summary: Insmed reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $425.5 million ($309.2M from BRINSUPRI and $116.3M from ARIKAYCE), representing strong sequential growth driven by organic new patient starts exceeding expectations for the blockbuster launch. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for BRINSUPRI to a range of $1.25 billion-$1.4 billion (from >$1B) and increased peak sales estimates significantly, projecting combined lead asset peaks over $14 billion versus previous projections of ~$8 billion.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined sequentially from Q1 primarily due to lower natural gas prices and reduced trading volatility consistent with normal seasonal patterns.
RNG upstream business saw results close to breakeven EBITDA in the quarter, requiring continued ramp-up for profitability.
Uncertainty surrounding final 2027 emission standards led to a large pre-note of legacy diesel trucks by fleets.
positive_highlights: RNG fuel volumes increased 3% YoY to 63.2 million gallons, with upstream dairy projects producing 2.1 million gallons in Q2.
Fuel and customer mix variations modestly reduced margins during the quarter, which is normal seasonal behavior factored into outlooks.
Completed two additional stations including a critical node in British Columbia to complete the Western Canadian natural gas fueling network.
summary: Clean Energy reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $106 million and adjusted EBITDA of $16 million, which management described as in-line with expectations but missing the upper end of its annual guidance range. The company maintained full-year financial outlooks assuming improved performance in H2 2026, though it noted that RNG upstream results were close to breakeven despite sequential improvement over Q1. Management highlighted uncertainty regarding the timing and value of the Section 45Z production tax credit rules expected later this year.

negative_highlights: Midstream constraints in April-May reduced oil production by ~2,000 bbl/d
Q2 free cash flow fell to $6 million due to 153% CapEx increase
Turn-in-lines missed guidance due to third-party infrastructure delays
positive_highlights: Raised full-year oil production guidance to ~30% year-over-year growth
Drilling costs per lateral foot down 7.5% in Texas and 32% in New Mexico
Silverback production approximately double note-side case projection
summary: Riley Exploration Permian reported Q2 FY2026 with oil production near the high end of guidance, 5% sequential growth, and a June exit rate of 24.4 thousand barrels per day. The company raised full-year oil production guidance to ~30% year-over-year growth, with Q3 expected to be up >20% sequentially. Midstream constraints in April-May reduced oil production by ~2,000 barrels per day, but new Targa pipeline is expected in early Q4 2026. Full-year CapEx guidance was increased by 12% at the midpoint, and free cash flow declined to $6 million in Q2 due to higher capital spend.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating margin was impacted by a 60-basis point headwind from Argentina anticipation and lower hardware sales compared to the prior year.
Financial Solutions organic revenue declined 10%, driven primarily by higher non-recurring revenue in the comparable period last year rather than volume deterioration.
Full-year guidance for adjusted operating margin was lowered due to incremental technology infrastructure investments exceeding $100 million and slower execution of growth initiatives.
positive_highlights: Free cash flow generation exceeded $1 billion for the quarter with an FCF conversion rate of 112%.
Clover GPV grew at 9% in the quarter, while Clover revenues increased by 13% adjusted for anticipation and non-recurring revenue.
Recurring revenue represented approximately 84-85% of total adjusted revenue with underlying growth remaining stable.
summary: Fiserv reported Q2 FY26 adjusted revenue of $4.96 billion, a decrease of 4% YoY and 5% organically, with EPS of $1.84. Management updated full-year guidance to organic revenue growth of -1% to flat (down from prior expectations) due to Argentina macro headwinds, slower client ramps, hardware attrition, and divestitures. Adjusted operating margin was lowered to a range of 31%-31.5%, reflecting incremental technology investments and the aforementioned impacts.

negative_highlights: Revenue flat at $56.4M, below prior-year $56.8M
Net loss widened to $7.3M from $2.9M
Channel inventory remained below historical norms through much of Q2
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.3M from -$3.0M
Gross margin up 660 bps to 38.8% (with tariff refunds)
Early Q3 weekly year-over-year note-through growth since GTA VI pre-orders
summary: Turtle Beach reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $56.4 million, essentially flat year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 38.8% including tariff refunds (excluding one-time items, about 31.2%). Adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.3 million from -$3.0 million, but net loss widened to $7.3 million due to increased marketing and higher interest. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance of $335-$355 million revenue and $44-$48 million adjusted EBITDA, citing strong second-half catalysts like GTA VI and Call of Duty. They highlighted early Q3 weekly year-over-year watch-through growth and repurchased $25 million of stock in the quarter.

negative_highlights: Total loan growth slowed to +2.3% YoY, significantly below the prior ~7% guidance and industry average.
Management explicitly revised full-year nominal loan growth forecast down from around 7% to around 6% due to subdued GDP activity in H1.
Cost of risk increased quarter-over-quarter as management established an additional CLP 50 billion in provisions reflecting a cautious stance on macro uncertainty.
positive_highlights: Operating revenues surged 20.9% year-over-year to CLP 922 billion supported by a 5.8% net interest margin expansion from higher inflation.
Fee income grew 10.7% YoY, with transactional services rising 20.4%, driven by increased card activity and new acquiring partnerships (Banchile Pagos).
The bank maintained its leading market share in local currency demand deposits at 19.7% among private banks.
summary: Banco de Chile reported Q2 FY26 operating revenues of CLP 922 billion (up 20.9% YoY) and net income of CLP 391 billion driven by higher inflation and fee growth, though loan growth was muted at +2.3% due to a one-time accounting migration effect masking underlying pro forma growth of +2.9%. Management revised its full-year nominal loan growth guidance down from ~7% to ~6% citing weaker-than-expected macroeconomic performance in the first half, while maintaining NIM expectations around 4.6% and raising cost-of-risk provisions by CLP 50 billion.

negative_highlights: No change in cash runway guidance; no updates on enrollment percentages
FDA meeting for non-IPF ILD program still not granted; timeline subject to approval
RCC market strategy remains narrow until phase II dose data available
positive_highlights: Cash runway extends into 2030, fully funding development programs
Competitive failure in RCC leaves Trevi essentially alone in all three cough indications
ATS presentations and JAMA highlight reinforce drug's efficacy profile
summary: Trevi's Q2 2026 call highlights continued pipeline execution: OCEAN-1 phase III and LAKE-2b phase IIb trials initiated, with OCEAN-2 expected in Q3. Cash of ~$319M extends runway into 2030, funding IPF and non-IPF ILD programs. The highly anticipated FDA meeting for non-IPF ILD is a near-term catalyst, and the competitive RCC program termination is viewed positively, reinforcing Trevi's potential first-in-class position. Guidance unchanged.

negative_highlights: Transportation demand remains soft reflecting lower vehicle production rates, with no expectation of improvement in Q3 or the second half.
Healthcare business is experiencing a rebalancing of inventory levels by customers which weighed on first-half results despite intact underlying trends.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS beat by $0.09 driven by better-than-expected volume growth (+1% vs projected negative) and pricing execution (3/4 of organic growth).
Asia segment delivered double-digit organic sales growth, with the region growing sequentially +20%. Both business segments showed strong momentum in Asia.
Adjusted EBITDA margins hit a record 18.3%, expanding 110 bps year-over-year due to operating leverage and productivity initiatives.
summary: Avient reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EPS of $0.96, beating expectations by $0.09 driven by volume growth and pricing actions that pushed organic sales up 4.3%. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to a record 18.3%, an increase of 110 bps year-over-year. Management raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow while updating capital expenditure expectations downward.

Manufacturing disruptions at Nashik facility following Q1 fire
Europe brands declined slightly year-over-year due to competition on Dymista
positive_highlights: Total revenues of $3.8 billion, up 3.5% operationally, exceeded expectations
Greater China net sales increased 16% year-over-year, ahead of expectations
Raised midpoint of 2026 financial guidance across all key metrics
summary: Viatris delivered Q2 2026 revenue of $3.8 billion, up 3.5% operationally year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.69, exceeding expectations. The company raised its full-year guidance across all key financial metrics. Growth was led by Greater China (up 16% year-over-year) and strong complex generics in North America, while emerging markets declined 2% due to supply constraints. Management also highlighted strategic progress including FDA approval for Gwyn Lo, the planned sale of Tyrvaya, and continued capital returns of $550 million to shareholders.

negative_highlights: Q3 energy prices are expected to be lower than last year despite having fewer resources due to the dry season.
El Niño scenario brings pressure on note weakness in-term prices in July, August, and September with recovery only expected starting October.
Financial results were partially offset by worsening interest rates (SELIC at 14%) and slightly higher leverage.
positive_highlights: EBITDA reached BRL 6.7 billion, representing a 21.5% year-over-year increase driven by generation segment contribution.
Generation unit margin improved from BRL 80 to BRL 100 quarter-on-quarter due to favorable price mix in the Northeast and Southeast sub-markets.
Company successfully migrated to Novo Mercado (highest governance level) at B3 and received Pro-Ethics seal for 2025-2026.
summary: AXIA Energia reported Q2 FY2026 EBITDA of BRL 6.7 billion (up 21.5% YoY), driven by improved generation margins and stable transmission results. Management raised full-year investment targets to approximately BRL 5-5.5 billion, citing the need for asset resilience against climate risks like El Niño. While capital allocation remains robust with a declared shareholder return program of BRL 7.7 billion (including new PNC redemptions), management issued cautious guidance on Q3 energy prices and availability due to seasonal dry season pressures.

negative_highlights: Illinois ZEC revenue recognition was $85 million in Q2 compared to $200 million last year due to timing differences.
Nuclear capacity factor reduced by 1.8% quarter-over-quarter primarily due to additional planned refueling outage days.
positive_highlights: Raised full-year operational earnings guidance range to $11.50-$12.50 EPS (midpoint up $0.50).
Nuclear fleet achieved a capacity factor above 99% during the Mid-Atlantic heat wave ahead of July.
summary: Constellation Energy reported Q2 FY26 GAAP EPS of $1.42 and adjusted operating earnings per share (EPS) of $2.55, beating expectations driven by Calpine accretion and higher PJM capacity prices despite a lower-than-expected Illinois ZEC revenue recognition ($85 million vs $200 million prior year). Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted operating EPS guidance to an expanded range of $11.50-$12.50 per share, increasing the midpoint by $0.50 from the previous outlook.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 5.8% year-over-year, with video and news/advertising driving approximately 75% of the decline.
Broadband net subscriber losses remained elevated at 40,000 in a highly competitive environment.
Residential ARPU declined 1.1% year-over-year due to product mix shifts away from lower-margin video.
positive_highlights: Gross margin reached an all-time high of 71%, expanding 180 bps year-over-year despite lower revenues.
Mobile net additions accelerated significantly with 50,000 lines added (up ~33% YoY), marking the best quarter to date.
Convergence ARPU grew 2.4% year-over-year to $79.80 driven by multi-product relationships.
summary: Optimum reported Q2 FY26 revenue of approximately $2 billion (down 5.8% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $786 million (down 2.2% YoY). Broadband net losses were 40,000 while mobile added 50,000 lines; gross margin expanded to an all-time high of 71%. Management reiterated a full-year revenue decline expectation and noted that ARPU is expected to face tougher comparisons in the second half.

negative_highlights: Rubber segment adjusted EBITDA fell 61% year-over-year primarily due to lower annual pricing agreements and unfavorable customer mix.
Tire production rates in key regions remain below historical norms, limiting near-term volume recovery potential for the Rubber business.
Management noted limited order visibility into the second half of the year despite reaffirming guidance.
positive_highlights: Specialty segment delivered its best quarterly performance since early 2022 with adjusted EBITDA increasing 96% year-over-year driven by volume growth and pricing actions.
Working capital initiatives generated a $4 million cash source in the quarter, offsetting roughly $60 million of headwind from higher oil-derived feedstock costs.
Management reaffirmed full-year guidance while lifting free cash flow expectations to slightly positive levels at the midpoint.
summary: Orion reported Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $58 million (up 26% sequentially) and generated positive free cash flow of $2 million despite a year-over-year decline in the Rubber segment driven by lower contractual pricing. Management reaffirmed full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $170-$210 million while lifting the midpoint for annualized free cash flow to $5 million, citing working capital improvements and favorable trade flows.

negative_highlights: Large display driver IC sales declined 21.0% sequentially as panel makers pulled forward inventory purchases in prior quarters.
Supply constraints from AI demand are rippling across the semiconductor supply chain, causing higher manufacturing costs and extended lead times for mature process nodes.
Q3 guidance anticipates a sequential decline in large display driver IC sales due to continued customer inventory pull-forward.
positive_highlights: Automotive driver IC sales increased double-digits sequentially due to broad-based customer replenishment following the Lunar New Year slowdown.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 33.1% from 30.4% in Q1, exceeding guidance of around 32%.
Himax is well-positioned for automotive growth with LTDI and TCON solutions becoming standard platforms for ultra-large displays.
summary: Himax reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $227.4 million (up 14.2% sequentially and 5.9% YoY) with gross margins expanding to 33.1%, both significantly exceeding the company's guidance range. Diluted EPS was $0.114, beating the upper end of the guided range ($0.086-$0.103), driven by strong automotive IC sales and a favorable product mix despite supply constraints in non-AI applications.

negative_highlights: Hardware delivery and data center readiness remain primary execution risks to revenue ramp
Contracted capacity only 120 MW of 212 MW, leaving 92 MW yet to be sold
positive_highlights: Secured capacity increased to 212 MW, up 80 MW from prior guidance, and capacities quadrupled year-to-date
Executed $8.8 billion of total contract value year-to-date, including $4.9 billion NVIDIA partnership
Raised approximately $2.2 billion of capital since December 2025 with a $1.6 billion oversubscribed financing
summary: In Q2 FY2026, SharonAI reported a major expansion in secured AI factory capacity to 212 MW from 132 MW prior, and contracted capacity grew to 120 MW with total contract value reaching approximately $8.8 billion year-to-date. Key wins include a six-year $4.9 billion NVIDIA partnership, a $1.32 billion take-or-pay with a global AI lab, and a $373 million agreement at a record price over $4 per GPU hour. The company raised about $2.2 billion in capital since December 2025, including a $1.6 billion oversubscribed round. Management expressed confidence in demand outpacing supply and guides for material revenue ramp from Q3 through 2027.

negative_highlights: Patient Services gross profit declined 57% YoY due to increased clinical labor costs and conservative fee-for-service approach.
Medical Loss Ratio (MLR) for capitated members rose to 85.5% from 71%, reflecting the ramp-up of new delegated lives.
One major Florida contract launch was delayed by two months, pushing effective date from Q3 to Q4.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 34.6% YoY driven by Specialty Pharmacy growth of 57.6% and new capitated contracts in Nevada, Oregon, and California exclusivity.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.2 million, marking the second profitable quarter as a public company within guidance range.
Strategic refinancing replaced an expiring convertible note with a 5-year term loan ($75M), improving liquidity without dilution.
summary: Starling Oncology reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $161 million (up 34.6% YoY) and achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.2 million, beating the prior loss guidance range. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue and gross profit ranges while narrowing the adjusted EBITDA outlook to reflect a delayed contract launch in Q3. The company successfully completed a strategic refinancing extending debt maturities to 2031 without equity dilution.

negative_highlights: Net loss included roughly $33 million in pre-tax costs related to reverse asset sales and legacy subservicing transfers.
Servicing adjusted pre-tax income decreased over 60% year-over-year due to an almost 80% increase in MSR runoff driven by lower interest rates.
Unfavorable fair value adjustments on the reverse mortgage book totaled approximately $12 million, creating significant volatility.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 24% year-over-year with record origination volume and servicing additions exceeding first-half expectations.
Originations pre-tax income increased over three times versus last year, while margins improved to 26 basis points from the prior quarter.
Servicing UPB ended the quarter up 10% year-over-year against an industry growth of only 3%, driven by organic expansion.
summary: Onity reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 24% year-over-year driven by record origination volume and servicing additions exceeding guidance. However, the quarter included a net loss due to roughly $33 million in pre-tax transaction costs related to asset sales/transfers and approximately $24 million in unfavorable fair value adjustments on reverse MSRs. Management lowered its full-year 2026 adjusted ROE outlook to the low end of the previously guided range (10%-15%) citing persistent market volatility.

negative_highlights: Progress toward new U.S. contract slower than in the past
Q1 had minimal product revenues, reflecting variability
Meridian promotion agreement expired and was not renewed
positive_highlights: Q2 product revenues of $38M, with $24M IV TPOXX delivered to SNS and $13M international orders
Net income of $12M, EPS of $0.17
Targeting new international contract and order delivery by March of next year
summary: In Q2 FY2026, SIGA reported product-related revenues of $38 million, including $24 million of IV TPOXX delivered to the U.S. Strategic National Stockpile and $13 million of oral TPOXX to international customers. Net income was $12 million, with fully diluted EPS of $0.17. The U.S. contract process is slower than expected, but management remains confident in TPOXX's role, and they are targeting a new international contract with delivery by March 2027.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they will not add incremental fleets speculatively despite tight market conditions.
Pricing pressure persists specifically in the sand and proppant markets within West Texas.
Free cash flow remains negative due to capital expenditures of $32 million.
positive_highlights: Revenues increased sequentially by $48 million driven by stimulation services ($430M) and Flotek ($102M).
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 14% from 12% in the prior quarter.
Free cash flow improved significantly to a negative $8 million, up from negative $25 million in Q1.
summary: ProFrac reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $498 million (up from $450M in Q1) and adjusted EBITDA of $69 million with a margin expansion to 14%. Management raised the full-year capital expenditure guidance range slightly higher than previously stated, citing an acceleration of engine upgrade programs. The company reiterated its disciplined approach to not adding incremental fleets speculatively while noting that pricing benefits are layering in for Q3 and Q4.

negative_highlights: Cyber Safety segment growth remained mid-single digits
Operating profit growth of 9% lagged revenue growth
Agentic AI revenue expected to be modest in FY2027
positive_highlights: Bookings and revenue both up 11% year-over-year, above guidance
Trust-Based Solutions bookings grew 25%
Engine passed half a billion dollars in annual revenue run rate
summary: Gen delivered Q1 FY2027 with bookings and revenue both up 11% year-over-year, above the high end of guidance, and non-GAAP EPS grew 19%. The company raised full-year FY2027 guidance to 9%-11% revenue growth and 14%-18% EPS growth. Cyber Safety grew mid-single digits, while Trust-Based Solutions grew 25%, with Engine crossing a $500 million annual revenue run rate. Management highlighted record paid customers of over 80 million and continued margin stability at 50%.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses are expected to increase in H2 due to the ramp-up of the STARS-2 trial.
SG&A expense is anticipated to see a modest increase during the remainder of the year.
positive_highlights: LINZESS delivered a second consecutive quarter of strong performance with U.S. sales up 14% YoY to $282.3 million driven by mid-single-digit demand growth and improved net price.
Full-year LINZESS guidance raised significantly, projecting annualized sales between $1.15 billion and $1.20 billion representing a greater than 30% increase year-over-year.
FDA approval of LINZESS for functional constipation in pediatric patients two years and older established it as the only prescription therapy approved for this age group.
summary: Ironwood reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $113 million with LINZESS U.S. net sales reaching $282.3 million (up 14% YoY). Management raised full-year guidance for LINZESS to a range of $1.15 billion-$1.20 billion and adjusted EBITDA to greater than $310 million, citing mid-single-digit demand growth and improved net price. The company repaid its convertible notes at maturity with cash on hand.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS midpoint reduced by roughly $0.12 due to financing costs, price/cost neutrality drag of ~$15M, and Eddyfi integration dilution
Gross margins declined 90 bps YoY driven by transitory logistics cost spikes in the Middle East (up triple) and commodity inflation
Middle East volumes down double digits due to geopolitical conflict, though management views this as temporary
positive_highlights: Total core sales reached record levels with double-digit organic growth in equipment segments
Eddyfi acquisition closed ahead of schedule, contributing approximately $35 million to full-year EBITDA guidance increase
Americas segment delivered strong performance with North America showing particularly robust demand for automation and gas control
summary: ESAB reported Q2 FY26 total sales of $766 million (up 13% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $150 million (up 8%), driven by record core sales and the integration of Eddyfi. Management raised its full-year 2026 outlook for both Total Core Sales ($3B-$3.1B) and Adjusted EBITDA ($615M-$625M), incorporating seven months of Eddyfi results while acknowledging $15 million in transitory price/cost headwinds from logistics and commodities. The company noted a 90-basis-point margin decline due to these costs, though it expects sequential pricing improvement and volume growth in the second half.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $77 million due to one-time transaction costs, financing fees ($41M), and non-cash intangible asset amortization from the Legend acquisition.
Cash balance at quarter-end was $155 million, below the prior range guidance but attributed to seasonal lows and significant debt financing costs associated with closing the deal.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat guidance by $10M ($196M vs implied ~$185-190M) driven by a massive 193% growth in the media segment (including Legend).
Adjusted EBITDA of $53 million exceeded the guided range, resulting in an operating margin roughly 270 bps above guidance.
Legend acquisition synergies are realizing faster than expected with cross-note underway and prediction market deals signed immediately post-close.
summary: Genius Sports reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $196 million (up 65% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $53 million, beating guidance on all metrics including a significant margin expansion to roughly 27%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.005-$1.025 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $285-$295 million (approx. 29% margin), citing strong organic growth, Legend integration synergies ahead of schedule, and new prediction market partnerships with Kalshi and Polymarket.

negative_highlights: Product revenue fell 66% YoY and service repair activities were slower than planned due to geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East.
Total orders declined sequentially by 6%, reflecting timing delays rather than demand destruction.
$10 million of discrete revenue headwind recognized specifically from installation/commissioning delays.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded year-over-year to 20% driven by disciplined cost execution and favorable mix.
Spares revenue increased 70% YoY as customers prepare for upcoming contracts.
summary: HMH reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $171 million (flat sequentially) and adjusted EBITDA of $34 million with margins expanding to 20% YoY despite a discrete $10M headwind from Middle East delays. Management maintained full-year guidance for adjusted EBITDA between $157-$177 million, citing strong digital technology order intake offsetting slower repair activity and geopolitical timing shifts.

negative_highlights: Q3 production guidance assumes a ramp-up from Ras Laffan, which was largely shut-in due to conflict impacts.
Willow project remains on track for early 2029 first oil but peak CapEx has not yet been passed.
positive_highlights: Production beat high-end guidance driven by record Permian output exceeding 900k bbls/day and strong Lower 48 performance.
$5 billion disposition target achieved ahead of schedule with $1.7 billion in non-core asset sales completed in July.
LNG portfolio expanded to 12 million tons per annum via new agreements in Indonesia and the U.S. Gulf Coast.
summary: ConocoPhillips reported Q2 FY26 production of 2.248 million boe/d and adjusted EPS of $3.24, both exceeding the high end of guidance. The company generated $7.2 billion in cash flow from operations and delivered $4.2 billion in free cash flow after $3 billion CapEx. Full-year distribution targets remain unchanged at 45% of CFO, with production guidance for Q3 raised to a range of 2.29-2.32 million boe/d.

negative_highlights: Gross margin dropped to 37.3% from 44.7% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA margin down to 17.5% from 31.2%
Section 232 tariff expenses added ~$17M in the quarter; net leverage low but cash flow pressured
Q3 revenue expected to step down sequentially due to pull-forward of $15-20M residential orders
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $295.3M, up 15.6% YoY with double-digit growth in both segments
Backlog grew 15.6% to record $1.4B; book-to-bill 1.1 for 23 consecutive quarters
Strong demand commentary: quoting activity 'crazy high' across the U.S., and New York coming back strong
summary: Tecnoglass reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $295.3 million, up 15.6% YoY, with record backlog of $1.4 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $51.7 million (17.5% margin). Margins fell sharply due to higher aluminum costs (+77% YoY), peso appreciation, and Section 232 tariffs ($17M expense). Management narrowed FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.08-1.12B and adjusted EBITDA to $220-230M, expecting Q3 EBITDA roughly flat sequentially. Demand remains strong, pricing actions are flowing through starting Q3, and automation is on track, but margin headwinds persist.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased to $27.7 million from $17.5 million prior year due to Hypercon investment.
note, general, and administrative (SG&A) expenses rose to $57 million compared to $41.6 million in the prior period.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 48% year-over-year to $481 million, exceeding consensus estimates.
Royalty revenues surged 50% YoY to CHF $307.7 million due to strong performance from DARZALEX SC and VYVGART Hytrulo.
Signed five new collaboration agreements in the quarter (four announced Q2, one in July), including firsts for ADCs and nucleic acids.
summary: Halozyme reported a record second quarter with total revenue of $481 million (up 48% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of CHF 329 million, driven by robust royalty growth of 50%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue to the range of $1.835 billion-$1.91 billion and increased projected royalties significantly above prior expectations.

negative_highlights: Product segment gross margin contracted to 9.7% from the prior year due to increased European construction costs
Net income decreased slightly on a GAAP basis (EPS $0.43 vs $0.46) reflecting a one-time $6.6 million write-off of a storage project not pursued
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 10.6% to $258.8 million with gross profit up 20.8% to $68.7 million
Energy storage revenue surged 195.1% year-over-year to $42.8 million due to new capacity and high asset availability in PJM
Full-year guidance raised significantly for both total revenues ($1.15B-$1.2B) and adjusted EBITDA ($630M-$650M)
summary: Second quarter revenue increased 10.6% to $258.8 million driven by strong energy storage performance and electricity segment growth, while gross profit expanded 20.8%. Management raised full-year guidance for both total revenues (now expecting $1.15B-$1.2B) and adjusted EBITDA ($630M-$650M), citing accelerating momentum across all three business segments.

negative_highlights: Q2 growth was capped below expectations due to a customer's inability to source sufficient switches caused by memory shortages, leading to an estimated $20-$25M revenue reduction in Q3 for the 100G segment.
Production capacity remains significantly constrained through mid-2027; current output is bounded almost entirely by production limits and key component availability (specifically DSPs/TIAs).
Q4 guidance implies a slower ramp than anticipated due to material constraints, with management expecting only $50M-$80M of 1.6T revenue in Q4 despite high demand.
positive_highlights: Returned to non-GAAP profitability with income per share of $0.06, beating the expected range of a loss of $0.03 to earnings of $0.03.
800G revenue increased more than tenfold year-over-year and doubled sequentially; 1.6T volume orders received from major hyperscale customers are beginning shipment in Q2/Q3.
CATV business delivered record revenue of $84.6 million (including the specific figure mentioned for total CATV), up 43.8% YoY, driven by Mediacom selection and amplifier shipments.
summary: Applied Optoelectronics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $191.9 million (up 86% YoY), which was in line with guidance but missed the upper end due to a specific customer shortage affecting 100G products that reduced expected growth by an estimated $20-$25M for Q3. The company returned to non-GAAP profitability with income of $0.06 per share, beating expectations and marking its fifth consecutive quarter of record revenue. Management reiterated full-year guidance around $1.1B but noted near-term capacity constraints on 800G/1.6T products remain the primary limiter despite robust demand.

negative_highlights: Order book remains low at 14.4% of existing fleet compared to historical highs like 66% in 2008.
Global trade volume growth projected to slow from 5% in 2025 to 3.5% in 2026 due to tariff impacts and unwinding front-loading effects.
positive_highlights: Net income swung from a loss of $3.1M in Q2 FY25 to $6.6M in Q2 FY26, driven by rates more than doubling year-over-year.
Operational utilization remained at 100% with no idle periods for the quarter.
Refinanced MV Ekaterini loan facility increased balance by approximately $8 million, boosting liquidity.
summary: EuroDry reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of $17.7 million and adjusted EPS of $2.44, representing a significant recovery from the prior year's loss driven by time charter rates more than doubling to an average of $20,398 per day. Management highlighted strong liquidity with cash assets at $37.5 million and announced a refinancing agreement for MV Ekaterini that increased its loan facility balance by nearly $8 million. The company reiterated disciplined capital allocation through newbuild orders while maintaining operational flexibility on index-linked charters.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to be slightly down compared to Q3 2025 due to the timing of investments in sales and marketing.
Implied take rate for full year 2026 is projected to remain relatively flat versus 2025, impacted by new business incentives.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 17% year-over-year to $3.6 billion, exceeding the high end of management's outlook.
Growth among first-time bookers accelerated to 11%, marking the highest growth seen in four years.
Customer support costs per booking declined approximately 16% year-over-year driven by AI assistant adoption.
summary: Airbnb reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.6 billion (up 17% YoY) and gross booking value growth of 16%, exceeding the high end of its outlook across every key metric including nights booked, ADR, and first-time bookers. Management raised full-year guidance for both top-line growth to at least mid-teens and adjusted EBITDA margin to a minimum of 35.5%. The company highlighted accelerated momentum in core markets like the U.S., France, UK, and Australia alongside strong expansion market performance.

negative_highlights: Organic volume down 1.6% on total revenue, impacted by prior-year landfill event volumes
Residential volume declined 4.3% due to known contract losses
Large container volumes declined 2.2% due to soft construction activity
positive_highlights: Raised full-year 2026 guidance across all metrics
Core price on related revenue of 6.4% exceeded cost inflation
Underlying business margin expanded 90 basis points
summary: Republic Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue growth of 4.6% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 4.5%, with adjusted EPS of $1.85. The company maintained adjusted EBITDA margin at 32.1% despite headwinds from prior-year landfill event volumes. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue, adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow, citing higher fuel recovery fee revenue, increased recycling commodity prices, and acquisitions. Volume declined 1.6% on total revenue due to tough comps, but underlying pricing exceeded cost inflation and management expects sequential volume improvement.

negative_highlights: Operating income included a one-time gain from the U.S. tower portfolio sale, masking underlying organic operating performance.
International revenue growth was dampened by an expected loss of government support in the U.S. Virgin Islands which expired at end of 2025.
Capital expenditures decreased $3.8 million year-over-year due to variable timing of reimbursable spending under government programs.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded by approximately 170 basis points year-over-year to reflect operating discipline.
Net leverage ratio improved significantly from 2.36 times at end of 2025 to 0.91 times following the $268 million tower sale proceeds.
Board authorized an expansion of share repurchase authorization to $30 million and increased quarterly cash dividend by 5.5%.
summary: ATN International reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $184.5 million (up 2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA growth of nearly 9%, driven by a one-time gain from the U.S. tower portfolio sale which improved operating income to $240 million. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance range of $183-$193 million, maintaining expectations despite excluding recurring impacts like lost rents and expired subsidies in specific regions.

negative_highlights: note, general, and administrative expenses increased significantly by $6.3 million (from $15.6M to $21.9M) driven primarily by a one-time legal charge.
Research and development spending decreased slightly due to reduced AMX0035 activity for progressive supranuclear palsy, offset by higher avexitide spend.
positive_highlights: Ended Q2 with $250.8 million cash and marketable securities, securing runway into 2028 for milestones including LUCIDITY readout and potential launch.
LUCIDITY trial last patient visit completed; database expected to lock in late August or early September following a successful double-blind period.
CMS/CDC published new ICD-10 code specific to PBH effective October 2026, enhancing recognition of the condition for diagnosis and epidemiology.
summary: Amylyx reported Q2 FY2026 operating expenses of $45.7 million (up 7% YoY) and ended the quarter with $250.8 million in cash, providing a runway into 2028 to fund operations through the anticipated LUCIDITY top-line readout in late August or early September. Management reiterated its strategic priorities of advancing NDA readiness for avexitide and strengthening commercial launch preparations targeting a potential 2027 launch if approved by the FDA. The company remains blinded to the pivotal Phase III data but expressed strong confidence in execution as they await results from the study evaluating their first-in-class GLP-1 receptor antagonist.

negative_highlights: Outpatient utilization elevated through first six months
Expect increasing membership churn in back half due to CMS program integrity
Market morbidity data only four months, not fully credited in guidance
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 70% year-over-year to $4.9 billion
Earnings from operations increased $619 million year-over-year to $389 million
Full-year earnings from operations guidance raised by $250 million
summary: Oscar Health reported Q2 2026 revenue of $4.9 billion, up 70% year-over-year, with MLR improving to 79.2% and SG&A expense ratio at a record low of 14.2%. Earnings from operations surged to $389 million, and net income was $362 million, both up sharply year-over-year. The company raised full-year 2026 earnings from operations guidance to $500-700 million, up $250 million, and improved MLR guidance to 81.5%-82.5%. Management highlighted favorable risk adjustment and utilization trends but remained cautious on CMS program integrity-driven member churn in the second half.

negative_highlights: Revenue down 7.8% YoY, at low end of guidance
Delivery Systems revenue down 18.4% with 770 systems placed vs 957
Lowered full-year revenue outlook to $280-290 million
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $17 million, up from $13.9 million YoY and above guidance
Adjusted gross margin expanded 590 basis points to 71.8%
SkinStylus revenue grew nearly 50% YoY in Q2
summary: Q2 revenue of $72.1 million fell 7.8% YoY and came in at the low end of guidance, with equipment sales down 18.4% and consumables down 3.5%. Adjusted EBITDA of $17 million beat guidance of $11-13 million, driven by gross margin expansion and cost discipline. Management lowered the full-year revenue outlook to $280-290 million while raising adjusted EBITDA guidance to $39-46 million. They introduced a new device rental program, received FDA clearance for SkinStylus periorbital wrinkles, and plan to repay the October 2026 convertible maturity with cash.

negative_highlights: Core earnings declined 10% year-over-year in Canada due to unfavorable claims and expense experience within group insurance.
Corporate segment loss widened by approximately CAD 45 million compared to the prior year, driven by P&C retro business cycle softening and increased central AI spending.
Retail outflows persisted in Global WAM despite improved sequential trends.
positive_highlights: Asia core earnings grew 21% year-over-year to record levels driven by double-digit sales growth in Hong Kong, Singapore, and Japan.
Global WAM generated net inflows of CAD 4 billion supported by record gross flows and strength in institutional business (CQS/Comvest).
summary: Manulife reported Q2 FY26 results with APE sales growing 21% year-over-year and core EPS increasing 16%. Core ROE rose to 16.3%, driven by strong performance in Asia (core earnings +21%) and Global WAM, partially offset by unfavorable claims experience in Canada's group insurance segment. The company announced a new long-term care reinsurance transaction transferring biometric risk on CAD 3.2 billion of reserves while retaining asset management.

negative_highlights: Logistics revenue down 10% sequentially on lower last-mile transportation activity
Grid interconnection delays persist (e.g., 7-8 year wait for one energy customer)
Guidance excludes potential ancillary services, which are hard to predict
positive_highlights: Record quarter with revenue up 12% sequentially and adjusted EBITDA up 30% sequentially
Raised Q3 guidance and introduced Q4 guidance with strong ramp expectations
Expanded contracts with three investment-grade technology companies, including new scope and longer terms
summary: Solaris reported record Q2 2026 with revenue of ~$219M, up 12% sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA of ~$108M, up 30% sequentially, with adjusted pro forma EPS of $0.39. The company raised Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90M-$105M and introduced Q4 guidance of $100M-$120M, reflecting GESA acquisition and new contract ramps. Management highlighted multiple contract expansions with three investment-grade tech customers, a new nuclear SMR investment, and strong demand with multiple gigawatts in active negotiations.

negative_highlights: Net revenue declined 10.1% to $166 million, with adjusted EBITDA loss of $26.6 million
