positive_highlights: Net investment income increased sequentially by $14.2M ($0.29/share) driven by mark-to-market gains in the equity portfolio.
Portfolio credit quality improved with non-accrual rates declining to 1.44% (fair value) and 4.41% (amortized cost).
Management successfully validated asset marks via $64M+ of third-party sales at ~99% of par, countering market skepticism.
summary: CION reported Q2 FY2026 net investment income of $14.2 million ($0.29/share), beating the prior quarter's $12.9 million and meeting its monthly base distribution target of $0.30/share via subsequent capital actions. Management validated portfolio marks with over $64 million in asset sales at 99% of par, while deleveraging reduced net debt-to-equity to 1.52x from 1.62x. The company plans further leverage reduction to a target of ~1.35x and authorized an additional $50 million share repurchase program.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined significantly year-over-year primarily driven by higher material costs, duties, tariffs, and wage inflation totaling over $36 million
F-150 volume ramp in the back half has not yet shown an uptick as hoped for Q4 releases
Global auto production outlook remains flat or uncertain due to Middle East conflict impacts on oil prices
positive_highlights: $16 million free cash flow delivered, representing a $40 million improvement over last year
97% of new program launches had green customer scorecards for quality and service
Fluid Handling segment won nearly $40 million in annual sales from conquest business due to competitor issues
summary: Second quarter sales were $721.3 million (up 2.2% YoY), but Adjusted EBITDA fell to $53.9 million from $62.8 million due to material costs and tariffs, resulting in an adjusted net loss of $0.13 per share versus a profit last year. Management maintained full-year guidance at the midpoint despite tightening the range for better visibility, citing that Q2 headwinds are expected to resolve or mitigate in H2 as price recoveries take effect.

negative_highlights: Cash at quarter end was $106 million, requiring subsequent financing to extend runway
No specific updates on RGX-202 data until BLA filing complete in Q1 2027
Commercial plans for subretinal wet AMD just beginning with AbbVie, early stage
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment in RGX-202 confirmatory study ahead of schedule, with over 60 patients treated across pivotal and confirmatory trials
Received $100 million milestone payment from AbbVie and raised $108 million in net proceeds, extending cash runway into Q4 2027
FDA confirmed RGX-121 data sufficient for accelerated approval review, with no additional RCT required
summary: REGENXBIO reported Q2 2026 cash of $106 million, strengthened by a $100 million AbbVie milestone and a $108 million follow-on offering, pro forma cash over $310 million with runway into Q4 2027. Key milestones completed: enrollment in RGX-202 confirmatory study ahead of schedule, FDA alignment on accelerated approval for RGX-121 BLA resubmission, and first patient dosed in NAAVIGATE trial for diabetic retinopathy. BLA submission for RGX-202 initiated in Q3 2026, with top-line wet AMD data from ATMOSPHERE and ASCENT expected in Q4 2026. Management expressed confidence in upcoming data and financial position.

negative_highlights: Same club sales growth of 1.7% was entirely driven by rate, not member growth
Membership flat sequentially at 21.5 million; net member growth slowdown acknowledged
Marketing initiatives will take time to implement and gain traction
positive_highlights: Revenue up 7% to $365 million, with growth across all segments
Black Card penetration up 210 bps year-over-year to approximately 68%
Opened 23 new clubs, consistent with prior year
summary: Planet Fitness reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $365 million, up 7% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA up 3.5%. System-wide same club sales increased 1.7%, entirely driven by rate, with Black Card penetration up 210 bps to ~68%. Membership reached 21.5 million, up 3.6% year-over-year but flat sequentially; attrition at 3.5%. The company reiterated its guidance with no negative comp quarters expected in Q3 or Q4, but noted the marketing initiatives will take time to gain traction.

negative_highlights: Gross margin of 47.6% included ~100 bps of discrete tariff refunds; underlying mix was unfavorable due to equipment ramp investments.
Operating expenses grew in line with guidance, but CapEx is expected to increase through the remainder of the year to support capacity ramps.
positive_highlights: Semiconductor revenue grew 28% YoY to $554M with strong momentum in NAND upgrades, logic, and DRAM.
Electronics & Packaging revenue surged 44% YoY to $381M driven by chemistry equipment demand for AI servers.
Specialty Industrial market delivered a rare high growth quarter (up 14% YoY) led by datacom testing and defense.
summary: MKS reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.25 billion (up 28% YoY) and EPS of $3.30, both beating the high end of guidance with raised expectations for Q3. Management highlighted strong sequential growth across all segments driven by AI demand in semiconductors and electronics packaging, while gross margin remained healthy at 47.6%. The company reaffirmed its deleveraging strategy via term loan prepayments and maintained a dividend increase.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance held at prior range despite Q2 beat and strong H1 results
Life Sciences Products business was flat year-over-year due to a strong comparison quarter last year
Management cited geopolitical situation as reason for prudence in holding guidance
positive_highlights: Life Sciences Services revenue grew 15% year-over-year driven by BioStorage growth
Achieved milestone of positive Adjusted EBITDA ($400,000) for the quarter
Generated $5 million in net cash from operating activities in H1 FY26
summary: Cryoport reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $49 million from continuing operations, with Life Sciences Services growing 15% year-over-year and positive Adjusted EBITDA of $400,000. Management affirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance at the prior range of $192-$196 million despite a strong first-half performance ($97M), citing geopolitical uncertainties as the reason for not raising targets. The company highlighted operational milestones including positive cash flow generation and new facility launches.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss of $116 million driven by fair value change on note-in of private wealth profits interests
Anticipated expiration of a managed account of roughly $1.5 billion next quarter
G&A expenses up $10 million YoY, partly due to platform distribution fees
positive_highlights: Fee-related earnings up 30% YoY, with core FRE up 33% excluding retroactive fees
Gross inflows of $10 billion, with record private wealth subscriptions of $2.8 billion
Dividend raised 18% to $0.33 per share, with additional share repurchases
summary: StepStone reported strong Q1 FY2027 results: fee-related earnings of $106 million, up 30% YoY, with a 39% FRE margin; adjusted EPS of $0.48, up from $0.40. Gross inflows were $10 billion, with record private wealth subscriptions of $2.8 billion and SPRING inflows of $1.7 billion. Management raised the quarterly dividend by 18% to $0.33 per share, and repurchased shares. They see no limiting factor to sustaining multi-billion dollar inflows, with expansion into defined contribution and data/tech partnerships as long-term growth levers.

negative_highlights: Prepaid Solutions remains choppy with uneven customer ordering patterns expected through late 2026
Gross margin expansion of ~160 bps was partially offset by unfavorable segment mix and lower-margin prepaid revenue
SG&A expenses increased to $37 million due to Arroweye integration costs
positive_highlights: Record first-half free cash flow of $36 million compared to just $1 million prior year
Secure Card Solutions organic revenue grew 12% excluding Arroweye acquisition impact
Raised Integrated Paytech segment full-year growth guidance from 15% to approximately 20%
summary: CPI reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $149 million (up 15% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $24 million (up 7%), driven by Secure Card Solutions growth and a one-time tariff refund benefit. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue growth to high single-to-low double digits and free cash flow to $45-$50M, while reaffirming the adjusted EBITDA outlook despite ongoing softness in Prepaid Solutions.

negative_highlights: PCR and nucleic acid amplification sales declined 8% CER
QIAstat-Dx sales declined 7% on respiratory comparison
China sales down low teens, though sequential improvement
positive_highlights: Sales and EPS exceeded outlook in Q2
Growth pillars delivered 5% CER growth, above market
Dividend increased 40% to $0.35 per share
summary: Qiagen reported Q2 2026 net sales of $535 million, flat at CER, beating guidance for a ~2% decline, and adjusted EPS of $0.62, above the outlook of at least $0.60. Growth pillars grew 5% CER, with Sample Technologies up 9% and QIAcuity double-digit, but PCR was down 8% and QIAstat-Dx fell 7% on respiratory comparison. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance of 1-2% CER growth and EPS of at least $2.43, expecting second-half growth to improve to 3-4% CER. Operating income margin contracted to 29.4% from 29.9%, and the dividend was raised 40% to $0.35.

negative_highlights: Full-year LOE expense raised to $10.30 per BOE due to production enhancement initiatives and higher workover costs
Net premium on Bakken crude expected to fade over the course of the year as differentials normalize below WTI
positive_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow of $414 million exceeded expectations
Oil production came in at the high end of guidance driven by four-mile program execution (26 wells executed)
Balance sheet grew to $612 million with normalized leverage declining below one-half turn
summary: Chord Energy reported Q2 FY26 results with oil production at the high end of guidance and adjusted free cash flow of $414 million exceeding expectations. Management raised full-year volume guidance by 2,000 bpd due to investments in low-cost base production initiatives while maintaining capital spending outlooks essentially unchanged despite dropping a frac crew later in the year.

negative_highlights: Pressure restrictions from Milepost 171 incident to be lifted through 2026 into 2027
Growth capital outlook increased for development activities
Permit durability remains a key requirement, not yet finalized
positive_highlights: Record throughput on U.S. Gulf Coast segment; strong demand for connectivity
Increased full-year normalized EBITDA guidance to CAD 1.04 billion
Open season secured 465,000 bpd of 20-year customer commitments
summary: South Bow reported strong Q2 2026 results, with record throughput on the U.S. Gulf Coast segment and raised full-year normalized EBITDA guidance to CAD 1.04 billion (within a 2% range) and distributable cash flow guidance to CAD 665 million (within 2%). Leverage improved to 4.4x net debt to EBITDA, and the board approved a CAD 0.50 quarterly dividend. Management highlighted the successful open season securing 465,000 bpd of 20-year commitments, advancing Prairie Connector and Liberty Bridge projects toward a mid-2027 FID, and noted pressure restrictions on Keystone are expected to be lifted in phases through 2026 and 2027.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin contracted slightly to 7.3% from 7.5%, driven by scaled payments to publishers for Carrot Ads.
Q2 GAAP net income declined 4% YoY primarily due to a timing shift in stock-based compensation vesting dates, not operational weakness.
positive_highlights: GTV grew 14% YoY with orders up 9%, outpacing order growth via deepening customer engagement and AOV increase of 4% to $115.
Advertising and other revenue accelerated to +16% YoY, significantly outperforming GTV growth at a rate of 2.9% investment.
Operating cash flow surged 143% YoY to $493 million, supported by strong collections and efficiency gains.
summary: Instacart reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.04 billion (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $313 million (up 19% YoY), driven by GTV growth of 14%. Management raised the midpoint for both GTV ($10.425B, +14%) and adjusted EBITDA ($330M, +19%) guidance for Q3 FY26 while widening the ranges to reflect increased scale.

negative_highlights: Total revenue growth only 0.9% constant currency; customer support revenue down 4.6% YoY
ARR up only 0.2% YoY
FY2027 guidance (core revenue +2%-3%) implies modest growth, with no acceleration expected
positive_highlights: Cloud bookings up 24.1% YoY, above the 16%-20% target range
Core cloud revenue up 8.9% constant currency, with 64 cloud deals >$1M, up 49% YoY
Non-GAAP diluted EPS up 26.8% and gross margin up 220 basis points
summary: OpenText reported Q4 FY2026 total revenue of $1.35 billion, up 2.9% YoY (0.9% constant currency), with core portfolio revenue up 5.3% (3.1% cc) and cloud revenue up 6.0% (4.3% cc). Core cloud revenue grew 8.9% cc, and enterprise cloud bookings rose 24.1% YoY, above the 16%-20% target. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 37.1%, non-GAAP EPS was $1.23 (up 26.8%), and operating cash flow was $186 million (up 17.5%). Management guided FY2027 core revenue growth of 2%-3% and cloud revenue growth of 8%-10%, calling FY2027 a 'foundation year' with investments in sales capacity and ecosystem partnerships.

negative_highlights: NAV declined sequentially from $11.02 to $10.94 driven primarily by net unrealized depreciation on select investments.
Net realized losses were recorded during the quarter, associated with restructuring activity and legacy portfolio investments.
Management noted heightened investor scrutiny around redemption activity in non-traded perpetual BDCs and AI-related disruption concerns.
positive_highlights: Net investment income of $0.28 per share exceeded the quarterly dividend of $0.26 by roughly $0.02.
Termination of legacy Sierra Credit Support Agreement freed approximately $67 million for redeployment into new assets.
Credit quality improved quarter-over-quarter with non-accruals not covered by CSA at only 0.2%.
summary: Barings BDC reported Q2 FY2026 net investment income of $0.28 per share and NAV of $10.94, which declined sequentially from the prior quarter due to unrealized depreciation on select investments despite earnings exceeding the dividend. The company successfully terminated a legacy credit support agreement freeing approximately $67 million for redeployment while maintaining leverage at 1.18x within its target range. Management noted that private credit behavior is becoming more rational with reduced capital chasing, though they remain selective and cautious regarding sectors like software due to AI-related market noise.

negative_highlights: Subscription revenue grew only 1.3% FX neutral, below internal expectations
Full-year FX-neutral subscription revenue guidance reduced to low single-digit growth
Remainder of subscription revenue (ex-growth drivers) declined modestly FX neutral due to weak consumption and mix
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating income grew 62% and free cash flow grew 79% in Q2
Four growth drivers (global expansion, B2B, ads, AI) grew 20% FX neutral and now represent 18% of subscription revenue
CX Platform saw average sales cycles decline more than 50% and implementation time cut from 30 days to one week
summary: VTEX reported Q2 2026 subscription revenue of $63.8 million, up 11% in USD and 1.3% FX neutral, coming in just above the bottom of guidance. GMV grew 18% in USD and 7% FX neutral. Profitability was strong with non-GAAP operating income up 62% and free cash flow up 79%. Management lowered full-year FX-neutral subscription revenue guidance to low single-digit growth, citing macro headwinds in Brazil and Argentina and a mix shift to larger accounts.

negative_highlights: Reported GAAP results were significantly impacted by a $460 million goodwill impairment triggered by sustained share price decline (down ~50% YoY).
Commercial Auto reported prior year reserve development of $17.7 million, marking successive quarters of adverse development in bodily injury coverage.
Personal Auto profitability is constrained by high concentration in California requiring double-digit rate increases and slowing new business growth.
positive_highlights: Underlying P&C normalized combined ratio improved sequentially from 102.8% to 102%, driven by expense discipline and stronger underwriting performance.
Commercial Auto delivered an underlying combined ratio of 93.7% with a 9.2% year-over-year increase in policies in force, despite prior year reserve strengthening.
Life business generated $18 million of net operating income supported by growth in earned premiums and favorable mortality experience.
summary: Kemper reported a net loss of $464.8 million ($7.90 per share) driven by a non-cash goodwill impairment of $460 million and an allowance for credit losses on surplus notes; adjusted consolidated net operating income was $26.3 million, reflecting sequential improvement in underlying P&C underwriting performance but being offset by prior year reserve development in Commercial Auto ($17.7M). Management emphasized that restoring profitability is the top priority over growth, citing a need to tighten underwriting and take additional rate actions despite strong underlying combined ratios.

negative_highlights: Q3 revenue guidance lowered due to supply chain delays on optics from Chinese suppliers affecting commercial products
Products gross margin declined sequentially to 41.2% as higher manufacturing spend offset sales mix benefits
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 expected in a wide range of $1M-$7M, down significantly from the prior quarter's $13.8M
positive_highlights: Record quarter with total revenue of $83M and products revenue growing 45% YoY
Awarded Joint Laser Weapon System contract with a ceiling exceeding $600 million
Defense segment grew 72% year-over-year driven by HELSI-2 and munitions programs
summary: nLIGHT reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $83 million (up 34% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $11 million, beating expectations with strong growth in defense products (+72% YoY). Management raised the ceiling on a new Joint Laser Weapon System contract to over $600 million while maintaining progress on HELSI-2. However, Q3 revenue guidance was lowered due to supply chain constraints affecting commercial optics from Chinese suppliers.

negative_highlights: Transaction activity remained muted as refinancing and M&A slowed significantly due to asset price volatility and wider spreads.
A specific credit markdown on Loparex drove a modest NAV decline after the company's transformative M&A transaction fell apart.
Management remains cautious regarding software exposure (18% of portfolio) citing rapid market changes, despite it being their best-performing sector.
positive_highlights: Adjusted NII grew quarter-over-quarter to $0.34 driven by elevated non-recurring fee income from the Mavis Tire repayment ($66M accrued PIK) and higher LSI dividends.
NAV decline was isolated to a single credit (Loparex), contrasting with Q1 where three-quarters of declines were due to broad portfolio spread widening.
Net leverage decreased to 1.11 times, the lowest level in over two years, providing substantial flexibility for future deployment.
summary: Blue Owl Capital reported adjusted NII of $0.34 per share and NAV of $14.26 in Q2 FY2026; the quarter-over-quarter NAV decline was driven by a specific credit markdown on Loparex rather than broad spread widening, while fee income spiked due to the repayment of Mavis Tire preferred equity ($274M cash). Management maintained its base dividend at $0.31 and declared an additional supplemental dividend of $0.02 per share, supported by strong spillover income.

negative_highlights: Full-year FY2026 revenue growth (18%) is below Q4's 43% YoY, indicating some slowdown later in the year
Balance sheet shows net debt of $22 million despite $128 million cash
No specific quantitative update on AI-related revenue or cost savings beyond qualitative commentary
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 43% YoY; adjusted EBITDA up 87% YoY with 270 bps margin expansion
Home services revenue up 88% YoY, with HomeBuddy integration going well
Initial FY2027 guidance implies 16% revenue growth and 38% adjusted EBITDA growth with margin expansion
summary: QuinStreet reported record Q4 FY2026 with revenue up 43% YoY to $373.9M and adjusted EBITDA up 87% to $41.4M, driving margin expansion. Full-year revenue grew 18% to $1.3B with adjusted EBITDA up 38%, and the company guided to continued strong growth in FY2027, expecting 16% revenue growth and 38% EBITDA growth at the midpoint, with opportunities for upside. The home services vertical, boosted by HomeBuddy, grew 88% YoY, while financial services grew 24% with auto insurance up 37%.

negative_highlights: NII net provisions were flat at 3.5%, reflecting higher cost of risk from government lines (FGI/FGO) and legacy cohorts.
Fee and commission income growth slowed to just 1.7% year-over-year compared to double-digit revenue growth in other segments.
positive_highlights: Net income grew 16.2% year-over-year to BRL 7.1 billion with ROAE of 16.2%, exceeding market expectations.
Loan portfolio expanded by 30% over the last 30 months, reaching BRL 1.137 trillion in Q2 FY2026.
Insurance group operating result grew 8.3% year-over-year to reach a net income of BRL 2.9 billion.
summary: BBDO reported Q2 FY2026 net income of BRL 7.1 billion (up 16.2% YoY) and total revenue of BRL 37.6 billion (up 10.3% YoY), driven by loan portfolio growth of 11.6%. The bank raised its full-year guidance for the insurance group to a range of 6%-8%, citing strong H1 performance, while noting that NII net provisions are expected to be slightly below the midpoint due to higher baselines in government lines.

negative_highlights: International volumes were lower due to Middle East disruptions
Sulfur sales could see delays or disruption due to Middle East freight volatility
Waha to Gulf Coast spread normalization may reduce midstream gas marketing income
positive_highlights: Production exceeded the high end of guidance by 23,000 BOE/d
Free cash flow of ~$3 billion, highest since Q3 2022
Midstream and marketing adjusted earnings of ~$960 million, a new quarterly record
summary: Occidental reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.40, with production of 1.43 million BOE/d, exceeding the midpoint of guidance by 23,000 BOE/d. Free cash flow was approximately $3 billion, the highest since Q3 2022, and midstream and marketing set a new record with adjusted earnings of about $960 million. The company reduced principal debt to $11.8 billion, raised the dividend by 8%, and reaffirmed a plan to add over $4 billion of annual sustainable cash flow by 2030, with approximately 85% achievable at lower prices. Guidance reflects expectations for normalized Waha/Gulf Coast spreads partially offset by upstream price improvements, while Middle East disruptions could impact sulfur sales and freight costs.

negative_highlights: Q3 LOE expected to rise to $73-$81M from $72M
Full-year capital guidance could hit high end due to accelerated projects
Surety lawsuit outcomes uncertain; potential damages not assured
positive_highlights: Q2 free cash flow up 50% sequentially to $31 million
Production up 3% YoY, at midpoint of guidance
LOE below low end of guidance; net debt/EBITDA down to 1.2x
summary: W&T Offshore reported Q2 2026 net income of $12.6 million ($0.08 per share) and adjusted EBITDA of $54 million, in line with Q1. Free cash flow rose 50% sequentially to $31 million, and net debt fell to $200 million with leverage at 1.2x. Production was 34.7 MBOE/d at the midpoint of guidance and up 3% year-over-year, while LOE was below the low end of guidance. The company reiterated full-year guidance and guided Q3 production above 35 MBOE/d midpoint, with management expressing confidence in the balance sheet and litigation upside.

negative_highlights: Shop occupancy declined 70 bps sequentially to 91.7%, partly due to tenant recaptures.
Same-property leased occupancy down 40 bps year-over-year to 96.3%.
Unexpected Wren Kitchens bankruptcy impacted occupancy, though settlement income was received.
positive_highlights: FFO as adjusted up 10% to $0.40 per share, exceeding internal expectations.
Raised full-year FFO guidance by $0.02 at midpoint to $1.50-$1.54.
New lease cash spreads year-to-date nearly 30% and expected to exceed 20% for the year.
summary: Urban Edge Properties reported a strong Q2 2026 with FFO as adjusted of $0.40 per share, up 10% year-over-year, and same-property NOI growth of 3.2%. The company raised its full-year FFO guidance by $0.02 to $1.50-$1.54 per share and increased the low end of same-property NOI guidance to 3.25%. Leasing activity remains robust with new lease cash spreads of 13% in the quarter and nearly 30% year-to-date, though shop occupancy dipped to 91.7% due to strategic recaptures and the Wren Kitchens bankruptcy. Capital recycling continued with acquisitions in Virginia and Massachusetts funded by asset sales, and management expressed confidence in continued rent growth driven by limited supply and strong demand.

negative_highlights: Sustaining capital at Gibraltar elevated at CAD 48 million in H1 2026
Gibraltar cathode production lower due to SX/EW electrical issues
Florence C1 cost of $4.72/lb not indicative of future; fixed costs high during ramp-up
positive_highlights: Revenue of CAD 331 million was the highest ever for Trekor
Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 125 million and operating cash flow of CAD 183 million
Florence generating positive operating margins and ~CAD 10 million EBITDA in Q2
summary: Trekor reported record revenue of CAD 331 million in Q2 FY2026, with adjusted EBITDA of CAD 125 million and operating cash flow of CAD 183 million. Florence produced over 5 million lbs of cathode in its first full production quarter, while Gibraltar produced 30 million lbs; the company maintained annual guidance. Management expressed confidence in ramp-up progress and highlighted strong copper prices and a contracted negative TC of -CAD 140/t for 2027, while noting cost pressures and higher sustaining capital.

negative_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow was -$42 million due to working capital usage
Brokerage gross margin declined 70 bps sequentially due to fuel price headwinds
Last mile expected to weaken in Q3
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $40 million exceeded the high end of outlook
Truckload gross profit per load up 11% sequentially, highest growth in four years
Managed Transportation awarded ~$100 million in freight under management in Q2 and another $100 million in July
summary: RXO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $40 million (above the high end of guidance), and adjusted EPS of $0.06. Brokerage volume grew 2% YoY, with truckload spot mix up 900 bps sequentially to 42% and truckload gross profit per load up 11% sequentially, the largest gain in four years. Last mile stops grew 3%, and managed transportation won ~$100 million in freight under management. Management guided to continued brokerage volume and gross profit per load growth in Q3, but expects weakening in last mile. Free cash flow was -$42 million due to working capital, expected to convert strongly in Q3.

negative_highlights: Quarter described as 'quiet' with no major business updates
Launch pace for brepocitinib expected to be 'slow and steady'
Continued litigation uncertainty with Pfizer and BioNTech
positive_highlights: Phase III cutaneous sarcoidosis study enrollment initiated ahead of schedule
Received $950M upfront payment from Moderna settlement, with $770M to Genevant
Cash position strong at ~$4B before receiving settlement funds
summary: Roivant reported a quiet Q1 FY2027 with $200M R&D expense, ~$100M non-GAAP G&A, and cash just under $4B before receiving $772M from Moderna's settlement. The company initiated Phase III for cutaneous sarcoidosis ahead of schedule, with top-line data expected in 2028. Management reiterated readiness for brepocitinib launch in dermatomyositis by end of September and expects a busy second half with multiple readouts. They continue share repurchases, having bought back ~$200M in the quarter at average high-$20s per share.

negative_highlights: $176 million one-time non-cash impairment charge recognized for capitalized development expenses on discontinued ATJ-60 project in South Dakota.
GAAP net loss of $177 million ($0.75/share) due to the significant impairment and severance charges.
Gross margin contracted slightly from 44% YoY despite revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA outlook for FY2026 doubled to >$60M driven by Canada CFR pathway approval and increased 45Z tax credit monetization expectations ($70M vs $52M prior).
Revenue grew 7% YoY despite planned maintenance downtime at the North Dakota facility.
Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR) pathway approved retroactively, unlocking access to a >1 billion gallon compliance market starting Q3.
summary: Gevo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $47 million (up 7% YoY) and gross profit of $20 million on a margin of 43%. The company recognized a one-time non-cash impairment charge of $176 million related to discontinued South Dakota projects, resulting in an adjusted net loss of $1 million ($0.01/share). Management raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from the prior estimate of ~$30 million to more than $60 million.

negative_highlights: Full-year EBITDA margin guidance implies a slight step-down to ~29.7%, driven by normalizing contract mix from cost-plus acquisitions rather than operational weakness.
Cash used in operations was $4 million due to working capital requirements associated with rapid revenue growth.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat consensus with sequential growth of 20.4% and year-over-year organic growth of 24.4%.
Backlog reached a record $1.3 billion, up 65% from the prior fiscal year end.
Bookings in Q2 totaled nearly $500 million across all end markets.
summary: Karman Space & Defense reported record Q2 FY26 results with revenue of $182 million (up 58% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $55 million (up 55% YoY). The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance to a range of $730-$745 million in revenue, citing strong visibility from a record backlog. Management reaffirmed expectations for 25% or higher organic growth and highlighted the conversion of contingent supply agreements into firm contracts.

negative_highlights: The software practice within investment banking continued to face headwinds due to AI-related disruption concerns in that specific sector.
positive_highlights: Record second quarter revenue of $226 million representing a 51% year-over-year increase and 43% sequential growth.
Investment banking revenues surged 56% to $178 million, driven by double-digit growth across M&A, capital advisory, Private Funds Advisory, portfolio valuations, and transaction opinions.
Non-compensation expense grew only high single digits for the full year despite significant revenue expansion, demonstrating strong operating leverage.
summary: Lincoln International reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $226 million (up 51% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.26 following its IPO. Adjusted operating margin was 20%, with investment banking revenues up 56% and valuation/opinions revenues up 35%. Management raised the full-year guidance for non-compensation expense to high single-digit growth, citing strong leverage from top-line expansion.

negative_highlights: Customer environment remains challenging, with persistent pressure on industry foot traffic.
Higher sales force costs are expected to continue for the next couple of quarters, creating a headwind.
Healthcare case volumes eased from Q1 in both one- and two-year stack basis.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA grew 10% to a record $604 million and margin expanded 29 bps to a record 5.7%.
Independent restaurant case growth of 5.1% was the strongest since Q4 2023, with 21st consecutive quarter of share gains.
Pronto sales outlook raised to $1.3 billion for 2026 and $1.7 billion for 2027, up from prior estimates.
summary: US Foods delivered record adjusted EBITDA of $604 million, up 10%, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 29 basis points to a record 5.7%. Adjusted EPS grew 21%. Independent restaurant case growth reached 5.1%, the strongest since Q4 2023, with 21st consecutive quarter of share gains. The company raised Pronto sales guidance to $1.3 billion for 2026 and $1.7 billion for 2027, up from prior estimates. Management remains confident in achieving over $300 million in cost savings by 2027, with $50 million already realized in H1 2026.

negative_highlights: Net sales growth of 4.1% was driven by pricing, with volumes slightly lower
Elevated tariff costs (Section 232) and inflation persist, partially offset by refunds
Softer new residential construction activity expected in Q4
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 440 bps to a record 27.1%
Raised annual adjusted EBITDA guidance for the third consecutive quarter
WMS adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 650 bps to a record 28.1%
summary: Q3 FY2026 was a record quarter: net sales grew 4.1% to $395.9M, adjusted EBITDA rose 24.3% to a record $107.4M with margin expansion of 440 bps to 27.1%, and adjusted EPS increased 47.1% to $0.50, partly helped by a one-time tax benefit. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $367M-$372M and narrowed net sales growth to 2.8%-3.5%, while lowering SG&A and tax rate guidance. WMS led growth with sales up 10.3% and EBITDA margin up 650 bps to 28.1%, and specialty valves are seeing traction in industrial water/data centers.

negative_highlights: Automotive revenue declined in high single digits due to weakness in Europe, though nearly flat YTD
Europe region saw a decline of 15% YoY (low single digits excluding procurement entity changes)
Memory price headwinds expected to impact gross margins by approximately 75 basis points in Q3
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue reached a new high for the company
Adjusted EPS grew 80% year-over-year to $0.45 driven by operating leverage
Semiconductor segment delivered exceptional double-digit growth across all geographies
summary: Cognex reported record Q2 revenue of $314 million (up 17% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 80%, driven by strong performance in semiconductor, electronics, and logistics segments. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for nearly all end markets to double-digit or high single-digit growth ranges, citing favorable demand environments and successful execution of cost reduction initiatives which delivered approximately $35 million in annualized net reductions. The company highlighted record quarterly revenue, margin expansion with adjusted EBITDA margins reaching 32.2%, and robust free cash flow conversion.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EPS growth in Q4 was only 6.1% due to a lower tax provision in the prior year.
FY2026 EPS was negatively impacted by $120M in additional interest and tax expense.
Revenue guidance includes $500M acquired growth, implying organic growth lower than total.
positive_highlights: Record performance with revenue growth of 17.6% in Q4 and 10.9% for FY2026, exceeding expectations.
EBITDA margin expansion of 110 bps to 12.3% and free cash flow per share up 68%.
Raised fiscal 2027 guidance with revenue growth over 11%, EBITDA margin in high 12% range, and at least $900M free cash flow.
summary: CACI reported Q4 and FY2026 with record revenue, EBITDA margin, and free cash flow. Q4 revenue was $2.7B (+17.6% YoY, 11.6% organic), EBITDA margin 13% (up 150 bps), adjusted EPS $8.91 (+6.1%), and free cash flow $233M. Full-year revenue grew 10.9%, EBITDA margin 12.3%, free cash flow $735M (up 68% per share), and contract awards exceeded $10B. Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue growth of 11.3%-13.4%, high-12% EBITDA margin, adjusted EPS of $32.96-$33.86, and free cash flow of at least $900M. Executives highlighted strength in electronic warfare, space, and counter-UAS, with the $500M Domestic Shield award and a classified counterspace win. Leverage reduced to 3.7x and expected to reach low-3s by June 2027.

negative_highlights: Supply Chain Services sales were flat (+0.6%) due to decreased activity with certain existing customers.
SG&A expenses increased by $15.7 million YoY, though operating leverage helped offset this in the margin calculation.
Management declined to provide specific Q3 guidance or confirm if 12% margins are sustainable beyond mix effects.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 12.2%, a new high watermark up from 11.5% last year.
Innovative Pumping Solutions sales surged 52.6% YoY driven by water and wastewater activity, reaching $142.7 million.
Free cash flow turned positive at $29.8 million for the quarter after negative FCF in H1 FY2025.
summary: DXP reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $576.5 million (up 15.6% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to a new high watermark of 12.2%. The company generated strong free cash flow of $29.8 million for the quarter, reversing prior year negative trends through reduced CapEx and improved profitability.

negative_highlights: NAV declined 10.4% due to the portfolio sale at a 5% discount plus transaction costs
Quarterly NAV fell 2.1% due to markdowns at Pluralsight, PVHC, and Zilliant
Net investment income per share of $0.22 was modest relative to dividend of $0.17
positive_highlights: Net leverage reduced to ~0.4x pro forma, significantly improving financial flexibility
Non-accruals declined to 1.6% at fair value from 2.8% in Q1
Strong repayment activity totaling $111.6 million in Q2
summary: Q2 FY2026 results showed adjusted NII of $0.21 per share, NAV declined 2.1% to $6.58 due to portfolio markdowns, and non-accruals improved to 1.6% at fair value. Management announced a major portfolio sale to a continuation vehicle at a 5% discount, reducing NAV by 10.4% but cutting net leverage to ~0.4x, and initiated a strategic review with KBW. Repayment activity was strong, and the Domo sale is expected to repay $69 million in Q4.

negative_highlights: NUCYNTA franchise net revenue was lower than expected, down 24% year-over-year due to pricing for authorized generic products.
Total product revenue guidance lowered from prior expectations of approximately $850-$925 million (implied) to a new range of $825-$855 million.
positive_highlights: JORNAY prescriptions grew by 13.1% year-over-year with prescribers reaching an all-time high of over 30,000 healthcare providers.
AZSTARYS acquisition integration is complete and revenues beat consensus expectations for a partial quarter at $12.9 million.
BELBUCA revenue increased 10% year-over-year to $57.7 million.
summary: Collegium reported Q2 FY26 net product revenues of $199.9 million (up 6% YoY), driven by a 41% increase in JORNAY revenue to $46.1M and initial AZSTARYS sales, partially offset by lower NUCYNTA franchise revenue due to authorized generic pricing dynamics. Management raised full-year guidance for the ADHD portfolio while lowering total product revenue expectations from prior levels of approximately $850-925 million (implied) to a new range of $825-$855 million, citing specifically lower pain portfolio net revenue.

negative_highlights: Heavy capital spending does not commence until February/March 2027, meaning Q3 FY26 cash flow will remain driven by exploration rather than production.
Resource statement for Patterson Corridor East is delayed pending further drilling results to define the high-grade subdomains and overall footprint.
positive_highlights: Completed all planned key construction milestones on schedule and within budget, validating conservative cost estimates despite industry inflation pressures.

Executed a new term sheet to note an additional 1.3 million pounds of uranium at spot price exposure, bringing total contracted volume under negotiation for up to 20 million pounds with global utilities.
Confirmed strong market demand with the five-year forward uranium price sitting at $105/lb and spot prices stabilizing around a new floor of $85.
summary: NexGen Energy provided a construction update for Q2 FY2026 rather than financial earnings results, reporting that all planned key milestones were completed to scope and budget within the CAD 2.2 billion project guidance established in August 2024. The company executed a term sheet to watch an additional 1.3 million pounds of uranium at spot price exposure during the quarter while maintaining strong liquidity with over CAD 970 million available for construction financing options including prepayments.

negative_highlights: Reported diluted EPS only $0.09 due to $23 million in charges from fraudulent loan repurchases
Net income down 10% in capital markets segment due to mix shift to brokered lending
Additional $12-16 million expected in Q3 for Fannie Mae review completion
positive_highlights: Transaction volumes up 3% YoY to $14.4 billion, debt financing up 8% to $12.5 billion
Adjusted core EPS increased 3% to $1.19, excluding repurchase-related charges
GSE market share up 350 basis points to nearly 15% year to date
summary: Walker & Dunlop's Q2 FY2026 core business grew modestly with transaction volumes up 3% to $14.4 billion and adjusted core EPS up 3% to $1.19, but reported diluted EPS was $0.09 due to $23 million in charges related to fraudulent loan repurchases. Management confirmed Freddie Mac's investigation is complete and expects $12-16 million additional charges in Q3 for Fannie Mae, with no further repurchases expected. Guidance for the year was not formally revised but management expressed confidence in core earnings excluding these charges, with GSE market share up to 15% and $114 billion in remaining GSE capacity.

negative_highlights: Natural gas prices fell significantly due to widening regional differentials
Adjusted G&A increased to $2.7M, though low among peers
Uncertainty around new Cherokee test well and potential stacked pay opportunity
positive_highlights: Revenue up 48% YoY and adjusted EBITDA up 49% YoY
Net income nearly doubled to $27M, driven by 22% oil production growth
Continued shareholder returns with $5.05 per share in dividends since 2023
summary: SandRidge reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue up 48% YoY to $51M, adjusted EBITDA up 49% to $34M, and net income of $27M ($0.72/share). Production grew 11% YoY (22% oil growth), driven by higher oil prices and the Cherokee drilling program. The company announced a bolt-on acquisition in the Cherokee Play, continues to pay dividends, and maintains a strong balance sheet with no debt. Guidance for 2026 remains intact with $76-97M capex and 10 wells planned.

negative_highlights: Management expects modest compression in Title margins for H2 due to front-loaded recruiting expenses and tuck-in acquisitions.
Residential purchase volumes remain at historically low levels (~4M annual pace) driven by elevated mortgage rates, limiting near-term growth potential.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net earnings beat prior year by $52M, with Title segment earnings up 33% YoY to $448 million.
Commercial revenue reached a record pace for H1 at $778 million (up 24%), driven by strong order volumes across industrial and multifamily sectors.
Title adjusted pre-tax margin expanded significantly to an industry-leading 17.8% from 15.5% in the prior year.
summary: FNF reported Q2 FY26 adjusted net earnings of $370 million ($1.39/share), beating the prior year's $318 million driven by a 33% increase in Title segment pre-tax earnings to $448 million and strong commercial revenue growth up 24%. The company returned approximately $195 million to shareholders via dividends and buybacks while maintaining an adjusted pre-tax title margin of 17.8%, though management noted modest compression is expected in the second half due to recruiting costs.

negative_highlights: Europe delivered only mid-single-digit growth, with traffic pressured by macro and tourism slowdown
Full-year outlook remains prudent on Europe due to macroeconomic uncertainty
Tariff and higher labor/material costs partially offset margin expansion
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 13%, ahead of mid to high single-digit outlook
Gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 73.6%
Full-year outlook raised after Q1 over-delivery
summary: Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 13% in constant currency, exceeding the mid-to-high single-digit outlook, with Asia up 25%, North America up 13%, and Europe up 5%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 73.6%, and AUR increased 15%. The company raised its full-year outlook while maintaining caution on Europe due to macro uncertainty. New customer acquisition was 1.5 million in DTC, and core product sales grew mid-teens.

negative_highlights: Red Sea hostilities forced ships to reroute via the Suez Canal and exit high-risk zones, reducing fleet efficiency
Spot supply remains tightly constrained following major consolidation by a private aggregator earlier in the year
Second-hand asset values are currently at premium levels making it challenging for DHT to acquire additional tonnage
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue reached $255 million on TCE basis with adjusted EBITDA of $231 million
Net income hit a record high of $198.3 million ($1.23 per share), exceeding the previous full-year record set in 2020
Fleet secured two additional one-year time charter contracts at an average rate of $109,000 per day for older vessels
summary: DHT Holdings reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $255 million and adjusted EBITDA of $231 million, marking the company's strongest quarter in history with net income reaching a record $198.3 million ($1.23 per share). Management raised full-year guidance expectations by citing strong market conditions driven by geopolitical disruptions that expanded ton-mile demand while maintaining conservative leverage and robust liquidity. The board approved a quarterly cash dividend of $1.22 per share, continuing its streak of 66 consecutive payouts.

negative_highlights: Management confirmed that full-year earnings guidance is being reevaluated and will likely be lower due to reduced gain-on-sale revenue.
Net Interest Margin (NIM) contracted significantly at the holding company level as operations moved into the bank, where interest income replaces securitization gains.
positive_highlights: Net interest income surged to $25 million for Q2 FY2026 compared to $16.2 million a year ago, driven by holding more SBA loans and CNILA business on the bank books.
Tangible book value per share has grown 75.3% over the last 12 quarters since converting to a financial holding company structure.
summary: NewtekOne reported Q2 FY2026 results where net interest income grew significantly to $25 million from the prior year period due to a shift of operations into Newtek Bank and increased SBA loan holdings. However, management explicitly stated that guidance for full-year earnings is being reevaluated as they transition away from gain-on-sale revenue toward stable net interest income. Consequently, forward-looking EPS targets previously cited ($0.79-$0.89) are no longer supported in the current quarter's outlook.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $18 million from $8 million year-over-year due to higher clinical trial costs and personnel expenses
R&D expenses increased significantly to $16 million compared to $7.9 million in the prior period
No financial guidance provided for revenue or cash burn rate
positive_highlights: Phase III PTCL trial enrollment is on track with an interim futility analysis projected for early Q1 2027
Atopic dermatitis Phase I data showed strong efficacy, with 75% of patients achieving EASI-75 in Cohort 4 versus 20% placebo
No significant safety issues or disease rebound observed after treatment cessation
summary: Corvus Pharmaceuticals reported a net loss of $18 million for Q2 FY2026 compared to an $8 million loss in the prior year period, driven by increased R&D expenses and stock compensation. The company maintains cash reserves sufficient to fund operations into Q2 2028 following a recent capital raise. Management provided clinical updates on soquelitinib but did not offer any financial guidance or revenue projections.

negative_highlights: Total revenue missed expectations due to a decline in equipment sales and legacy ATG service pressure
Full-year guidance was lowered on both top-line EBITDA and free cash flow metrics
Galileo FDX STC approvals for mid-to-large airframes are coming online slower than anticipated
positive_highlights: Military and government service revenue surged +40% YoY driven by geopolitical demand
Galileo LEO aircraft online grew to 184 units (+66% QoQ) with strong adoption of HDX/FDX models
5G unit shipments accelerated significantly to 138 units in the quarter
summary: Gogo reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $222.8 million (down 1% YoY) and a net loss of -$2 million compared to prior year profit, driven by lower equipment sales ($31.5M vs expectations). Management revised full-year guidance downward for total revenue ($870-895M), adjusted EBITDA ($175-185M), and free cash flow ($65-85M) primarily due to slower-than-anticipated Galileo STC approvals, equipment mix headwinds, and a $3.2 million litigation expense included in the outlook.

negative_highlights: Content licensing revenue experienced lumpiness and was a drag in Q2
Traditional search-driven traffic continues to decline, impacting digital ad revenue
Digital revenue mix slightly ticked down to 47.4% in Q2
positive_highlights: Digital-only ARPU reached another record high, increasing 34% year-over-year
Free cash flow increased 11% year-over-year to approximately $20 million
Second consecutive quarter of positive net income and digital-only subscription revenue growth
summary: USA TODAY Co. reported Q2 2026 with positive net income for a second consecutive quarter, $20 million free cash flow (up 11% year-over-year), and record digital-only ARPU (up 34% year-over-year). Digital-only subscription revenue grew for the second consecutive quarter and digital other revenue also grew, but content licensing was lumpy and search-driven traffic declined. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, expecting improved revenue trends, EBITDA and margin expansion, and fourth consecutive year of free cash flow growth, with a goal of becoming majority digital in the back half of 2026.

negative_highlights: Operating margin decreased by 30 basis points year-over-year due to higher network costs associated with non-human traffic growth, though this is expected to stabilize.
Restructuring charges of $151 million impacted the quarter's net income and GAAP profitability.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 36% year-over-year to $696.1 million with gross margin expanding sequentially for the first time in eight quarters.
Record large customer additions of 986 net new customers over 12 months, representing a 27% increase from last year.
Free cash flow surged 69% year-over-year to $56.4 million as operating leverage improved.
summary: Cloudflare reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $696.1 million, a 36% year-over-year increase driven by record large customer additions and accelerating growth in the Workers developer platform. Operating income rose to $96.1 million (non-GAAP margin 13.8%) with gross margins expanding sequentially for the first time in eight quarters to 73.1%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance expectations, citing strong momentum across all product lines and customer cohorts.

negative_highlights: Marketing optimization expected to be a headwind in Q3 vs Q2
G&P results slightly offset by commodity price sensitivity
Still some price-related shut-ins returning in Q3
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA up 38% year-over-year, record quarter
Permian volumes up 450 MMcf/d sequentially, tracking ahead of expectations
Guidance raised to top end of range; dividend up 25%
summary: Targa Resources reported record Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.603 billion, up 14% sequentially and 38% year-over-year, driven by record Permian volumes of 7.2 Bcf/d, record NGL transportation and fractionation volumes, and record LPG exports. Management raised expectations to the top end of the $5.7-$5.9 billion full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range, suggesting near $1 billion growth over 2025. Marketing optimization outperformed by ~$250 million in H1, though some of that is expected to moderate in H2. Dividend increased 25% to $1.25 per share, with $80 million of buybacks in Q2.

negative_highlights: Xavantina gold production started slower than anticipated due to development ramp-up, resulting in mined gold at the low end of guidance.
TCRC savings realized in Q2 will be spread over the remainder of the year rather than fully recognized immediately.
positive_highlights: Gold sales surged 65% quarter-over-quarter due to end of rainy season, filter press commissioning, and industrial dryer operation at Xavantina.
Copper operations produced a combined 17,315 tons with consolidated shipping cash costs declining sequentially to $2.42/lb.
Net debt leverage ratio improved significantly to 0.8x from a peak of 2.6x in early 2025.
summary: Ero Copper reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $284 million and adjusted EBITDA of $144 million, driven by a 65% quarter-over-quarter increase in gold sales from Xavantina. Management maintained full-year guidance for consolidated copper C1 cash costs ($1,100-$1,350/oz) while raising capital expenditure guidance to include a new power line at Xavantina. The company continues its deleveraging strategy with net debt leverage reduced to 0.8x and expects stronger production in the second half.

negative_highlights: U.S.-based revenue remained flat or slightly down, primarily attributed to the company assuming last year's run rate for EOCL contracts.
Mission Solutions backlog is not broken out by segment and remains subject to lumpy delivery schedules from sovereign programs.
positive_highlights: Total revenues grew 50% year-over-year to $33.3 million driven by record space-based intelligence revenue of $24.5 million.
International subscription revenues surged 150% compared to the prior period, now comprising over 80% of total funded backlog.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 14.2%, demonstrating strong operating leverage as high-margin Gen-3 services scale.
summary: BlackSky reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $33.3 million, representing a 50% year-over-year increase and a 60% sequential gain driven by record space-based intelligence services revenue of $24.5 million. Adjusted EBITDA reached $4.7 million with an expanded margin of 14.2%, supported by international subscription revenues growing 150%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue between $130M-$150M and adjusted EBITDA between $12M-$24M, citing strong momentum from Gen-3 scaling.

negative_highlights: F&G Life Re resale reduced incremental earnings by $8 million in Q2 compared to Q1, and MYGA sales were de-emphasized due to returns falling below thresholds.
Buyback capacity is limited with only approximately $12-$15 million remaining under current authorization after a large quarter of repurchases.
positive_highlights: Core retail sales reached $1.8 billion for the quarter, described as one of the strongest quarters on record despite industry contraction in FIA sales.
Retained AUM grew by 8% year-over-year to $74.7 billion driven by positive asset flows and disciplined capital allocation.
Operating expense ratio decreased to 47 basis points at quarter-end, continuing a multi-year trend of scale benefits.
summary: F&G reported Q2 FY2026 results largely in line with expectations, posting adjusted net earnings of $85 million ($0.65/share) and retained AUM growth of 8% to $74.7 billion despite a challenging industry environment for Fixed-Indexed Annuities. Management highlighted strong core retail sales momentum but noted that alternative investment returns were below the long-term target, with Q2 annualized returns at approximately 5.9%. The company executed significant capital return activities including share repurchases of 4.5 million shares and dividends paid from self-funded capital.

negative_highlights: Management declined to provide specific full-year revenue guidance despite strong Q2 performance, citing a desire to assess the entire year before updating.
Proleukin revenue was slightly down from $11M in Q1 due to wholesaler inventory stocking timing.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $99.3M driven by robust demand exceeding Q2 guidance.
Gross margin reached an all-time high of 56% due to volume, in-house manufacturing efficiencies, and Proleukin normalization.
FDA granted Fast Track designation for lifileucel in undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma and dedifferentiated liposarcoma.
summary: Iovance reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $99.3 million (up 66% YoY), driven by record Amtagvi sales of approximately $91 million which exceeded the guidance range of $79M-$81M. Gross margin expanded to an all-time high of 56%, up from 41% in Q1, while R&D expenses decreased for a fourth consecutive quarter. Management declined to provide specific full-year revenue guidance but confirmed they are reviewing their previously issued range and expect to announce updated figures during the third quarter.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue of $57 million was significantly lower than the prior year's $239 million, primarily because the comparison quarter included a one-time $202 million BLA approval and Takeda amendment benefit.
Management explicitly stated they do not provide guidance for Sanofi beyond 2026 due to commercial support ending that year.
Oncology progress remains preclinical or early-stage with no specific licensing timelines provided, relying on partner experimentation.
positive_highlights: Adjusted total revenue guidance raised at midpoint due to increased supply sales from Matrix-M demand ($5M increase) and expected royalties/milestones from Takeda/Serum Institute ($10M increase).
Combined GAAP R&D/SG&A expense guidance improved by $10 million, with a target of achieving non-GAAP P&L profitability as early as 2028.
Sanofi partnership confirmed intent to be among first movers in combination vaccine market; Phase III study initiation could trigger a $125M milestone payment.
summary: Novavax reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $57 million (down from $239M prior year due to a one-time milestone in the comparison period) and an adjusted net loss driven by R&D expenses. Management raised its full-year 2026 guidance for non-GAAP total revenues ($235-$275M midpoint increase of $5M) and combined GAAP R&D/SG&A expenses (midpoint reduction to $390M). The company reiterated a three-year expense framework targeting profitability by 2028, citing cost reductions and strong partner momentum as key drivers.

negative_highlights: Revenue dropped sharply from $28.9M in Q2 FY25 due to absence of licensing revenue this quarter
Net loss widened significantly compared to net income reported in the prior year period
ZYNQUISTA NDA resubmission delayed slightly, now anticipated for Q4 2026
positive_highlights: SONATA-HCM trial completed enrollment and was significantly over-enrolled
ZYNQUISTA DKA rates observed are similar to standard of care and below previous trials
Steno-1 study expected to achieve adequate exposure levels by end of August
summary: Lexicon reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $0.7 million compared to $28.9 million in the prior year period due to a lack of commercial sales for sotagliflozin and licensing revenue from Novo Nordisk being absent this quarter versus last year's $27.5M milestone payment. The company recorded a net loss of $31.8 million ($0.07/share) driven by R&D expenses rising to $17.4 million primarily due to the SONATA-HCM trial and an early debt extinguishment charge of $4.3 million. Management reiterated 2026 operating expense guidance but noted a slight delay in ZYNQUISTA's NDA resubmission timeline, now targeting Q4 2026.

negative_highlights: Net reopening and ramp-up costs increased to $6.9 million from Q2 2025, raising year-to-date total to $10.9 million.
Management noted diminishing returns on reducing premium labor utilization as contract FTEs stabilized at approximately 1.1% of total FTEs.
Medicare Advantage pre-authorization denials remain a challenge with substantial disparity compared to Medicare fee-for-service patients.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased 9.2% to $348 million despite absorbing an $11.5M year-over-year decrease in net provider tax impact due to Florida Medicaid adjustments.
Net revenue per discharge grew 3.9%, driven by higher patient acuity, particularly in stroke and brain injury categories.
Nursing turnover improved significantly with annualized rates around 19% (lowest in over a decade) as career ladder participation reached 43% of eligible RNs.
summary: Encompass Health reported Q2 FY2026 revenue growth of 9.6% and adjusted EBITDA increase of 9.2%, driven by discharge volume growth and higher net revenue per discharge due to increased patient acuity. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both operating revenue ($6.41B-$6.49B) and adjusted EPS ($6.02-$6.25), citing strong capacity additions, favorable ePOB trends, and a successful admit-and-appeal strategy with an 89% success rate on Medicare Advantage denials.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased slightly due to timing differences and lower external spending on small molecule programs (offset by launch investments)
note, general, and administrative expenses rose $4M YoY primarily reflecting commercial launch support costs
Clinical data for Alzheimer's pipeline delayed from end of 2026 to first half of 2027
positive_highlights: $3.6M net product revenue in first full commercial quarter
Q3 guidance raised to $10-$12 million range based on strong adoption trajectory
>50% of covered lives secured for AVLAYAH with high physician awareness
summary: Denali Therapeutics reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $3.6 million from its first full commercial quarter for AVLAYAH in Hunter syndrome. Management raised guidance for the following quarter (Q3) to a range of $10-$12 million, citing strong physician engagement and payer access exceeding 50% coverage. Operating expenses were flat compared to the prior year period despite launch investments.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined significantly year-over-year from $107.4 million due to no flight equipment sales.
Overall gross margin contracted sharply to 22.9% compared to 32.9% last year, exacerbated by startup costs at new facilities.
MRO facility utilization remains low (Goodyear under 20%, Millington ramping up), delaying the realization of operating leverage.
positive_highlights: Leasing revenue grew approximately 50% year-over-year to $12.4 million driven by an expanded engine and freighter portfolio.
Tech Ops revenue increased nearly 9% to $33.8 million due to the ramp-up of CRJ multi-line maintenance at Millington.
Secured a $35 million sale contract for a 737 aircraft to the U.S. Marshals Service, expected to close in Q4.
summary: Second quarter revenue of $70.9 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $2.2 million missed expectations due to the absence of flight equipment sales ($33.4M in Q1) and lower USM feedstock acquisitions, resulting in a net loss of $5.6 million compared to prior year income. Management maintains that these results reflect timing rather than trajectory, with guidance for the second half remaining unchanged but dependent on ramping up MRO capacity at Goodyear and Millington. The company expects meaningful improvement as stored Spirit aircraft are returned to service and new lease deliveries occur.

negative_highlights: OEM and national revenue declined 18% year-over-year, signaling a trough that is expected to reverse only in Q3.
Website units (Dealer Inspire) continued to decline compared to the prior year as management shifts focus from volume expansion to product innovation.
Lower uptake of add-on dealer media products remained a near-term headwind partially offsetting core marketplace gains.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 29.4%, outperforming the high end of guidance for a second consecutive quarter due to operating leverage.
Marketplace revenue grew over 7% year-over-year, driven by dealer count growth and new Premium Plus package adoption.
Dealer Verified Listings launched successfully in June as an integrated trust signal connecting AccuTrade assets with consumer marketplace listings.
summary: Cars.com reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $179.9 million (up 1% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 29.4%, beating the high end of guidance for a second consecutive quarter. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance with flat-to-2% revenue growth and margins between 29%-30%. While OEM/national revenue declined, strong marketplace performance (up 7%) and cost discipline drove profitability.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin decreased approximately 90 basis points to 21% due to increased R&D investments and Endospan integration costs.
Free cash flow turned negative at -$12 million compared to +$11.7M in the prior year, impacted by $10.2M transaction bonuses for Endospan acquisition.
BioGlue revenue declined 2% YoY due to normal quarter-to-quarter variability from stock-in-distribution business.
positive_highlights: Stent graft revenue accelerated to +12% YoY against a much tougher comparison, up from Q1's +10% growth.
On-X revenues grew +18% YoY on constant currency basis driven by global market share gains and the newer U.S. opportunity for younger patients.
Successfully received FDA PMA approval for AMDS Hybrid Prosthesis in late June, removing IRB review barriers.
summary: Artivion reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $125.8 million (up 9% constant currency) and adjusted EBITDA growth of approximately 7%, driven by stent graft acceleration (+12%) and On-X gains (+18%). Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for adjusted revenue between $480M-$496M and adjusted EBITDA between $92M-$99M, declining from prior expectations despite the strong quarter. The company cited a prudent decision to maintain conservatism in guidance due to timing shifts in preservation services (Q3) and ongoing integration costs associated with the Endospan acquisition.

negative_highlights: SCO pricing outlook is described as dependent on diesel draw and volatile forward curves, with management noting difficulty in predicting end-of-year levels.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net earnings hit all-time high of CAD $4.6 billion with adjusted funds flow reaching record levels at CAD $6.9 billion.
Total corporate production set a new company record averaging approximately 1,677,000 BOEs per day in Q2 FY26.
Oil sands mining and upgrading achieved the highest quarterly net back ever recorded at approximately CAD $78 per barrel.
summary: Canadian Natural reported record Q2 FY26 results with adjusted net earnings of CAD $4.6 billion (CAD $2.20/share) and funds flow of CAD $6.9 billion, driven by a historic production run rate averaging approximately 1.677 million BOEs per day. Management raised its full-year annual production guidance range to between 1.637 million and 1.682 million BOE/d (a 20k increase at the midpoint) while maintaining an unchanged capital program of CAD $6 billion before acquisitions. The company returned approximately CAD $4 billion in cash, including a quarterly dividend of CAD $0.525 per share.

negative_highlights: $298.8 million non-cash impairment charge recorded in the second quarter related to Lancaster and Plainville facilities classified as held for sale

Guidance for Q3 was lowered, reflecting recovery assumptions, and the company emphasized disciplined investment and menu innovation like wraps, which lifted transactions but created a check drag.

FY2026 comp sales guidance lowered to 1.5%-2% from 1.5%-2.5%

Npower penetration increased 200 basis points to 84% of net sales

EPS was $0.48, down from $0.50, and guidance for FY2026 comp sales and EPS was narrowed/lowered. The company opened three stores in Q3, including its first in Wisconsin, and launched a DoorDash partnership.

Targus consumer products segment reported a $6 million loss in Q2
positive_highlights: Operating adjusted EBITDA of $66 million, best core operating quarter in nearly three years
Debt reduced by $497 million since December 2024, net debt down to $285 million
Added five senior producers and reactivated key institutional accounts

Total revenues were $239 million, up $14 million year-over-year, driven by a $30 million increase in management fees from carried interest in SpaceX funds. The company reduced total debt by $497 million since December 2024 to $1.277 billion, with net debt down $87 million to $285 million. Management highlighted reactivated institutional accounts, a strong capital markets pipeline, and expects to comfortably cover $306 million in upcoming senior note maturities with cash and investments.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $33.6 million in Q2.
Results weighed by $10.7 million acquisition-related costs.
ASM acquisition closing subject to final procedures.

Conditional $725 million loan from Office of Strategic Capital announced.

Management highlighted conditional $725 million government loan, progress on ASM acquisition closing late August, and announced VAC acquisition expected to close early 2027. Continued investment in rare earth expansion and maintained strong balance sheet with ~$1 billion liquidity.

Total capital return guidance increased by $50 million due to strong business performance.

Management raised full-year 2026 capital return guidance from $500 million to a range of $550-$600 million driven by strong first-half performance, while noting that base premium rates remain relatively flat versus the prior year despite modest sequential pressure.

Stormwater storage products grew 18% in the quarter

Management maintained full-year guidance of $3.35-3.55 billion sales and $1.0-1.05 billion EBITDA, citing dynamic inflation and a tepid demand environment. Non-residential end markets beat expectations, while residential demand was modestly worse.

negative_highlights: SoHo revenue declined by 4.7% year-over-year, with guidance indicating continued declines of 5%-7% for the next two quarters.

The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance range without raising it, citing that first-half performance suggests they will finish above the midpoint but not enough to warrant an expansion. Management highlighted record corporate channel revenue ($60.5M) and noted SoHo decline narrowed to 4.7% YoY.

negative_highlights: Issued policies declined 12% YoY, full-year expected down mid-single digits

summary: Primerica reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted operating revenues up 8% YoY and adjusted net operating income up 11%, with adjusted operating EPS up 17% to $6.41 including a $0.15 tax benefit. The ISP segment grew revenues 21% and pre-tax income 31%, with record AUM of $140 billion and $397 million in net inflows. Term Life premiums grew 3.4% but issued policies declined 12%, and the company guided full-year issued policies down mid-single digits. Management raised ISP sales guidance to 10%-15% growth for 2026, while maintaining full-year expense growth of 7%-8%.

Manning & Napier integration showing early success with live referral channels established between firms.
summary: Abacus Global Management reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $73 million (up 30% YoY) and adjusted net income of $27.1 million ($0.28 EPS), beating the high end of its prior guidance range of $24-$26 million. The company raised full-year adjusted net income guidance to $100-$106 million from a previous expectation, while reiterating Q3 expectations of $26-$28 million. Capital deployed reached approximately $200 million in the quarter with strong inflows into longevity funds totaling $544.2 million year-to-date.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are not baking a pronounced decline in prices into the forecast due to macro uncertainty.

Merchandise contribution dollars grew while holding or gaining share across major categories, driven by strength in energy drinks and core center-of-store items.
New customer sign-ups exceeded 600,000 per month with approximately 46% being new or lapsed customers.
summary: Murphy USA reported strong Q2 FY26 results with same-store fuel volumes up 0.5% and merchandise contribution dollars growing despite category pressures like lottery and beer declines. Management provided conservative guidance for the second half of the year, citing macro uncertainty and potential consumer budget pressure as reasons to guide toward the low end of ranges rather than baking in a prolonged price decline scenario.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA down 22% YoY
Net loss $171 million including $103 million deferred tax allowance

summary: Tronox reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $868 million, up 19% YoY, driven by strong TiO2 and zircon volumes, with TiO2 volumes at the high end of guidance and zircon exceeding expectations. Adjusted EBITDA was $73 million, down 22% YoY due to exchange headwinds, pricing, and costs, but within guided range. Pricing improved sequentially for both TiO2 and zircon, and the company expects further sequential price increases and EBITDA of $95-$115 million in Q3, with positive full-year free cash flow. Management highlighted anti-dumping progress, including India and a context reinstatement of duties on Chinese TiO2, and noted cost headwinds from Middle East conflict and input costs.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 75%, down from 78% in the prior quarter.
Cloud subscription Net Revenue Retention (NRR) declined sequentially to 111% as legacy downsells work through backward-looking metrics.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $8.1M, significantly beating the prior guidance range of -$5M to -$2M driven by greater-than-expected revenue and expense timing shifts.
Full-year 2025 guidance was raised for both cloud subscription revenue (to $429-$433M) and total revenue ($695-$703M).
AI is driving tangible value with a reported 25% upcharge on licenses, new deals in previously untapped industries, and strong pipeline generation.
summary: Appian reported Q2 FY2026 (Q2 CY2025) revenue of $170.6 million (+17% YoY), with cloud subscriptions growing 21% to $106.9M and adjusted EBITDA turning positive at $8.1M, beating the prior guidance range of -$5M to -$2M. Management raised full-year 2025 guidance for total revenue ($695-703M) and cloud subscriptions ($429-433M), citing strong AI-driven demand and a shift in federal government spending patterns post-DOGE. The company highlighted an upmarket strategy yielding larger deals, though gross margin contracted slightly to 75% due to timing of expenses.

International Nurse growth for FY2027 is expected to be lower than anticipated due to embassy appointment backlogs slowing visa processing.
Locum Tenens volume increased only ~1%, falling below typical seasonal uplift patterns.

Nurse and Allied volume growth accelerated, with travel nurse orders up ~40% YoY as of early August.
Search business in Physician segment showed strong momentum with new searches rising 37% sequentially.
summary: Second quarter consolidated revenue was $673 million (up 2% YoY), beating the high end of guidance by 6%, driven primarily by a surprise labor disruption revenue of $25M versus expected $10M. Adjusted EPS reached $0.77, significantly exceeding expectations due to non-recurring reserve reversals and billing true-ups that added roughly $27 million to earnings metrics. Management raised the Q3 outlook for Nurse and Allied segment volume growth (expecting 9%-11% YoY) but maintained a conservative revenue guidance range of $640M-$655M, anticipating lower margins in Technology and Workforce Solutions due to pricing pressure.

negative_highlights: Pipeline Transportation segment Adjusted EBITDA declined year-over-year due to the divestiture of EPIC Crude equity interest.
Waha pricing remains below original guidance assumptions, though offset by Gulf Coast marketing gains and returning curtailed volumes in H2.

Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance raised by $70M to the midpoint, reflecting mid-to-high single-digit volume growth expectations and improved Waha pricing recovery.
Kings Landing 2 processing capacity expansion accelerated to an expected in-service date of mid-2028.
summary: Kinetik reported record Q2 FY26 results with Adjusted EBITDA of $281 million and Distributable Cash Flow of $195 million, driven by operational execution and favorable commodity prices despite curtailments. Management raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $1.04 billion-$1.1 billion (a 7% increase at the midpoint) and increased capital expenditure guidance to approximately $560 million, citing strong customer activity pull-forwards in New Mexico and Delaware South.

negative_highlights: Gross bookings growth lagged rides growth by approximately 11 percentage points, attributed to seasonal impacts in the Bikes business which carries lower average gross bookings per ride.
Freenow integration is still early-stage with only two months of data compared to three last year, and full global app integration is not expected until 2027.
positive_highlights: Gross bookings accelerated 23% year-over-year to $5.5 billion driven by strong North America rideshare growth in low-scale markets like Canada.
Adjusted EBITDA expanded 37% year-over-year, reflecting continued cost leverage and margin expansion trajectory toward the 4% target for next year.
Driver supply remains robust with driver earnings at an all-time high (up ~8% per ride YoY) and a strong preference gap favoring Lyft among multi-platform drivers.
summary: Lyft reported Q2 FY2026 results with gross bookings up 23% year-over-year to $5.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA growing 37%. The company achieved record metrics including over 30 million active riders, 262 million rides in the quarter, and a new all-time high where approximately 30% of North American rides are linked to partners. Management maintained an upbeat tone regarding operational excellence, driver supply strength (driver earnings at all-time highs), and progress on autonomous vehicle partnerships.

negative_highlights: Moody's negative outlook persists, though management expects improvement
Batch Zero timeline is uncertain and may extend beyond February 2027
positive_highlights: Q2 adjusted EPS rose 30% YoY to $1.16

summary: Sempra reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.16, up from $0.89 in Q2 2025, with GAAP EPS of $1.21. The company affirmed its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.80-$5.30 and 2027 guidance of $5.10-$5.70, along with long-term EPS growth of 7%-9%. Management highlighted strong Texas demand, with 44 GW of Batch Zero load requests (140% increase over current peak), and Oncor's incremental capital opportunities totaling $10 billion. The pending sale of a 45% stake in SI Partners is expected to close later this quarter, deconsolidating ~$9 billion of debt, and the company expressed rising confidence in Oncor's capital plan roll-forward.

The company raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, though expects Q3 and Q4 EBITDA to decline YoY due to higher sports rights costs. Platforms grew 9% ex-divestiture, and advertising improved to -0.6% YoY. Management announced a $100 million accelerated share repurchase, and highlighted strategic deals including Bundesliga and Full Swing acquisition.

Gross margin improved significantly to breakeven status from a gross loss of $0.2M in Q2 FY2025.
