The company achieved breakeven gross loss compared to a previous loss, while total operating expenses decreased by approximately 15% due to cost reduction measures including lower share-based compensation and headcount reductions. Management reaffirmed full-year FY2026 revenue guidance in the range of $4 million-$6 million and adjusted EBITDA between a $28 million and $31 million loss.

Mobility Tech core sales declined due to prior-year compare
positive_highlights: Core sales flat, ahead of guide, with EFS up ~5%
Adjusted operating margin expanded 190 bps
Raised full-year EPS guidance

Adjusted operating margin expanded 190 bps, with underlying expansion of 70 bps. The company raised its full-year EPS guidance, citing cost savings and a solid pipeline. Repair Solutions remains a drag with margins down 180 bps, but management is addressing it with leadership changes and operational focus.

Subscription revenue grew 13.6%, while ARR accelerated to 12% sequential growth driven by resources and public works/utilities sectors. The company delivered adjusted operating income less stock-based compensation of $116 million (28.3% margin) for the quarter, which was in line with expectations despite early-year investments.

Adjusted EBITDA of $69 million was near the high end of guidance, reflecting controlled medical cost trends (YTD trend slightly better than the 5.2% assumption) and G&A improvement of approximately 210 bps YoY.
Net leverage declined to 2.26x on a trailing twelve-month basis after retiring $92 million in debt during the quarter.
summary: Astrana Health reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $973 million (up 49% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $69 million (up 43% YoY), finishing near the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $255-$280 million while reaffirming revenue guidance at $3.8 billion - $4.1 billion, citing broad-based outperformance and reinvestment into growth opportunities.

Guidance was not detailed in the provided excerpt, but management noted improved retention rates and positive early demand for Essentials, while expecting sub-$30,000 revenue to decelerate and go slightly negative this year.

The company highlighted nearly 100% multi-product attachment on new deals, six PAR Ordering wins, and PAR Intelligence reaching roughly 20,000 restaurant sites, with 17,000 retail sites. Management raised the full-year outlook, citing strong pipeline and deployment momentum, and remains confident in accelerating ARR growth in the second half.

negative_highlights: Incremental FX headwinds are expected to offset a significant portion of the Q2 beat in full-year revenue guidance.

GAAP operating margins expanded nearly 130 bps YoY to 8.2%, with non-GAAP operating margin at 16.3% above the high end of guidance.
AgentPulse standalone launch received strong demand, doubling Control package counts and increasing average deal size by 2x-3x.
summary: Q2 FY26 revenue was $124.5 million (up 22% YoY), exceeding the high end of guidance with a specific beat of $3.7M on top-line and non-GAAP operating income beating by $1.2M. Management raised full-year ARR guidance to a midpoint range of $522.1-$528.1 million (a raise of ~$1M) while acknowledging incremental FX headwinds that offset some of the Q2 outperformance.

Expanded distribution partnerships with Boise Cascade and six regional distributors

Fiber cement organic growth was 20%, driven by strategic initiatives and a destocking comp. Management raised the full-year guide, maintains cost pressures of $80-100M, and confirmed synergy targets. They also announced expanded distribution agreements and redeemed $400M of notes, reducing leverage to 2.7x.

Annual net income fell to $1.7 billion from $2.3 billion due to prior-year gains
Quarterly free cash flow impacted by World Cup working capital timing
positive_highlights: Record annual revenue and EBITDA, with Q4 revenue up 28% and EBITDA up 27%

FOX One subscriber acquisition and retention exceeded expectations, with minimal cannibalization

Q4 revenue grew 28% to $4.2 billion and EBITDA grew 27% to $1.2 billion, driven by a 78% advertising revenue increase from the World Cup and strong Tubi growth. Adjusted EPS rose 41% in Q4 to $1.79. Management raised the dividend to $0.29 per share and expects continued momentum into fiscal 2027 with World Cup and midterm advertising tailwinds.

negative_highlights: The company completed its current share buyback authorization, leaving no active program for further capital return in the near term unless a new one is approved.
Average premium per policy remained flat despite revenue growth, indicating pricing pressure or volume-driven expansion rather than rate hikes.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew by 11% driven by premium growth while average premium per policy remained flat.
Pre-tax income was $18 higher than the same quarter last year despite challenging market conditions and rate softening.
Retention rates consistently remain above 90%, demonstrating strong customer stickiness.
summary: HCI Group reported Q2 FY2026 results with revenue growing by 11% and diluted EPS of $5.60 (up from $5.18 YoY), driven by a 6% increase in gross premiums earned despite flat average premium per policy. Pre-tax income exceeded $110 million, representing an 18% year-over-year increase compared to the record prior period. Management highlighted strong retention rates above 90%, successful pivots of CORE into residential markets generating ~$6M/month new business, and a completed share buyback program utilizing over half of its authorization.

Company remains at 4x net debt to EBITDA, expecting upper threes by year-end
Average owner down payment including equity unchanged at mid-to-high twenties
positive_highlights: Contract sales increased 22% over prior year, exceeding high end of guidance

summary: Marriott Vacations Worldwide reported Q2 2026 contract sales up 22% year-over-year, with VPG up 23% to $4,477, and adjusted EBITDA of $215 million, exceeding the high end of guidance. Adjusted free cash flow for the first half was $201 million versus $22 million a year ago. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $805-$830 million, a $50 million increase, and highlighted record sales months and ongoing owner engagement initiatives.

negative_highlights: Offshore Pipeline Transportation segment performed slightly below expectations due to unplanned downtimes at key fields
Non-recurring margin opportunities from SPR releases and market dislocations are not expected to continue into Q3
Q2 results were broadly in line with internal estimates rather than a clear beat
positive_highlights: Retired approximately $83 million of high-cost preferred securities in the quarter
Reduced all-in annual run rate cost of capital by an estimated $25 million year-to-date
Marine Transportation segment returned to full capacity after dry docking
summary: Genesis Energy reported Q2 FY2026 results broadly in line with internal expectations but slightly below external guidance for the Offshore Pipeline segment due to operator challenges and unplanned downtimes at key fields. Management highlighted significant balance sheet optimization, including $95M asset sales, a new securitization facility, and the retirement of approximately $83 million in high-cost preferred securities, reducing total outstanding Series A by roughly 40% year-to-date. While non-recurring margin opportunities from market dislocations boosted Q2 earnings, management explicitly warned that these specific benefits are not expected to continue into Q3.

negative_highlights: Adjusted attributable net income missed Q1 levels due to lower realized gold prices ($4,447/oz vs $4,884 in Q1) and an elevated effective tax rate of 46%.

Consolidated AISC increased sequentially by $50/oz to $2,157 driven by one-time crusher costs at Lindero (~$115/oz impact), contractor mobilization at Séguéla, and external factors like Argentina macroeconomics adding ~$49/oz.
Cash balance decreased from Q1 levels due to the concentration of income tax payments ($79.3 million) in the second quarter.

Executed significant shareholder returns via share buybacks totaling $82 million in Q2 (approx. 41% of FCF).
Séguéla plant expansion and Diamba Sud feasibility study milestones confirmed, anchoring the path to exceed half a million ounces annually by mid-2028.
summary: Fortuna Mining reported Q2 FY2026 results with revenue of $380 million and adjusted attributable net income of $75 million ($0.25/share), which was sequentially lower than the record Q1 due to lower realized gold prices, higher taxes, and increased costs. Consolidated AISC rose to $2,157/oz from a peak in Q2 before expected declines in H2 as one-time items like crusher refurbishment at Lindero and contractor mobilization at Séguéla normalize. Management reaffirmed annual production guidance of approximately 60% growth by mid-2028 driven by the Diamba Sud project and the approved 30% expansion at Séguéla.

negative_highlights: Later-line patient accrual is naturally diminishing as the company successfully captures the TKI-pretreated population.
Gross-to-net deductions remain stable at around 30% due to payer mix maturation, limiting immediate margin expansion from pricing power.
positive_highlights: IBTROZI net revenue grew 25% to $23.2 million, driven by a shift toward first-line patients which now account for approximately 85% of new starts.
The company is the number one choice for newly diagnosed advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive lung cancer patients based on IQVIA claims data from January to May 2026.
Completed an opportunistic convertible debt financing that was approximately 5x oversubscribed, allowing the retirement of higher-cost term loan debt and strengthening the balance sheet.
summary: Nuvation Bio reported Q2 FY26 net revenue of $31.7 million, a beat on the median estimate driven by IBTROZI U.S. product revenue growth of 25% to $23.2 million and collaboration/license revenue of $8.5 million. The company raised its capital position significantly via an oversubscribed convertible note offering that allowed it to retire higher-cost debt, while maintaining a cash balance of $661 million. Management highlighted strong commercial momentum with first-line new patient starts growing 30% quarter-over-quarter and IBTROZI establishing itself as the market leader in both first-line and overall settings.

negative_highlights: Q3 guidance implies pre-tax income slightly below Q2 actual
Q3 and Q4 revenue expected to be more modest with a Q4 step-down

negative_highlights: Gross margin expansion was modest at ~50 bps sequentially, partially offset by COGS increases from ramping new products like Fetal Focus and Latitude.
Management noted that Q2 sequential volume growth for Signatera was exaggerated by weather-related suppression in Q1 2026.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly test processing of approximately 1,044,000 units with Oncology MRD growing ~56% YoY to 283,000 units.
Signatera received FDA approval as a companion diagnostic for muscle-invasive bladder cancer and Japanese PMDA approval for colorectal cancer.
NCCN issued its highest Category 1 recommendation for Signatera in adjuvant treatment of muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
summary: Natera reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $753 million (up ~38% YoY) and processed a record 1,044,000 tests with Oncology MRD volumes surging 56% year-over-year. Management raised the full-year revenue guidance range to $2.85-$2.91 billion at the midpoint, implying roughly 31% growth ex true-ups while holding OpEx steady. The quarter was driven by strong sequential volume acceleration in Signatera and ASP improvements across Women's Health and Organ Health.

negative_highlights: Q3 segment EBIT fell to $58M from $72M, driven by warmer weather and AmeriGas weakness
AmeriGas Q3 EBIT down $25M on lower retail volumes and customer attrition
Year-to-date adjusted EPS declined to $3.17 from $3.55 due to lost tax credits and higher interest
positive_highlights: Year-to-date segment EBIT up to $1.187B, modestly ahead of prior year
Utilities segment EBIT increased by $10M in Q3 on higher gas base rates
AmeriGas leverage at 4.3x, lowest in 10 years, with expected distributions to parent in 2027
summary: In Q3 FY2026, UGI's reportable segment EBIT fell to $58M from $72M a year ago, driven by warmer weather and continued customer attrition at AmeriGas, partially offset by utility growth. Year-to-date, segment EBIT rose modestly to $1.187B, but adjusted diluted EPS declined from $3.55 to $3.17 due to lost investment tax credits and higher interest. Management reaffirmed FY2026 EPS guidance of $2.75-$2.90, despite a noted guidance cut for midstream growth investments. AmeriGas is expected to resume distributions to the parent in 2027.

negative_highlights: Management noted that some large potential engagements in the pipeline are not yet factored into guidance until they reach 100% certainty.
Gross margin may face downward pressure on a weighted basis if the company wins lower-margin projects, though strategic mix is expected to trend upward over time.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 58% YoY with adjusted gross margin expanding two points sequentially to 49%, nine points above the public target.
Adjusted EBITDA surged 92% YoY, exceeding consensus by $8.5 million or 50%. Fully diluted EPS of $0.41 nearly doubled analyst estimates.
Customer diversification accelerated as the largest customer's share fell to 37% while a new big tech partner scaled from 17% to 34%.
summary: Innodata reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $92.1 million (up 58% YoY) and adjusted gross margin expansion to 49%, significantly beating analyst consensus on all key metrics including EPS ($0.41 vs $0.21). Management reiterated guidance for over 40% year-over-year revenue growth, citing a broadening customer base where the largest client dropped to 37% of revenue while new frontier lab partnerships scaled. The company highlighted strong cash generation and announced an ATM program alongside leadership transitions.

negative_highlights: Three multifamily loans downgraded to 4-rated during the quarter
Recorded $30 million increase in reserves due to macroeconomic conditions
Realized loss of $47 million expected on Q3 asset sales
positive_highlights: No new non-accrual or 5-rated loans in the quarter or year
Deployed $6.7 billion year-to-date, near-record pace
Expecting to resolve $800 million or 40% of non-accrual/REO by year-end
summary: STWD reported Q2 2026 distributable earnings of $152 million or $0.40 per share, with no new non-accrual or 5-rated loans. The company deployed $2.5 billion in the quarter and another $1.7 billion in July, bringing year-to-date investments to $6.7 billion. Management expects to resolve approximately $800 million of non-accrual and REO assets by year-end, and anticipates the strongest origination quarter in Q3. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but management signaled continued recovery and growth.

negative_highlights: OUS revenue grew only 12% due to European tender timing delays
Revenue shift to Q3/Q4 from Europe could impact quarterly phasing
R&D expenses up $3.9M YoY to $11.6M
positive_highlights: Revenue up ~120% YoY; U.S. revenue up >150%
Gross margin 59%, second consecutive quarter at/near high end of guidance
Raised full-year revenue and gross margin guidance
summary: Senseonics reported Q2 2026 revenue of $14.5 million, up ~120% YoY, with U.S. revenue up >150% to $12.6 million. Gross margin was 59%, above guidance and the highest organic performance in company history, leading to raised full-year revenue guidance to $62-66 million and gross margin guidance to 58-61%. The Eon Care Network added 28 providers, surpassing 90 total and on track to exceed the 100-provider goal by year-end. European transition caused some revenue timing delays but full-year outlook unchanged.

negative_highlights: Incremental U.S. carrier pass-through fees of $71M pressured gross margin
Q3 organic revenue guidance decelerates to 11%-12% growth
GAAP operating income impacted by $33M prepaid asset impairment
positive_highlights: Record revenue of $1.5B, up 22% reported and 17% organic YoY
Raised full-year organic revenue growth guidance to 13%-13.5%
Record Q2 free cash flow of $353M
summary: Twilio delivered record Q2 revenue of $1.5 billion, up 22% reported and 17% organic year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross profit growth accelerating to 18%. The company raised its full-year organic revenue growth guidance to 13%-13.5% from 9.5%-10.5% and raised full-year non-GAAP operating income and free cash flow guidance. Management highlighted strong growth in messaging, voice, and software add-ons, plus early customer wins for the new Conversations Layer.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 73% in Q2, down from Q1
CapEx expected to be incrementally higher in Q3 and Q4
eProbe customer eval conversion uncertain; could take close to a year
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue up 19% YoY; H1 revenue up 22% YoY
Backlog grew to $271 million, up 10% QoQ and 16% YoY
Reaffirmed 20% full-year revenue growth guidance
summary: PDF Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $61.5 million, up 19% year-over-year, with first-half revenues up 22%. Backlog grew to $271 million, up 10% sequentially and 16% year-over-year, driven by multiple eight-figure contracts (secureWISE and DirectScan) and record Cimetrix bookings. Gross margin was 73%, down sequentially due to higher perpetual licenses in Q1, but management expects expansion toward the 77% target. The company reaffirmed 20% full-year revenue growth guidance, despite increased CapEx for eProbe tools.

negative_highlights: Gold Bar production missed targets due to carbonaceous material absorbing dissolved gold during leaching
AISC rose significantly in Q2 primarily driven by the shortfall in production ounces at Gold Bar
No dividend expected from San José JV for the remainder of FY2026
positive_highlights: Los Azules FID work program on track to conclude in Q4 with major process packages awarded
Geotechnical campaign allows consolidation of pit design, increasing mineable ore and reducing stripping by roughly 22%
Enhanced financing proposal from Finland's Export Credit Agency (Finnvera) advancing alongside other ECA engagements
summary: The company reported a disappointing quarter with production falling short of expectations at the Gold Bar mine due to unexpected carbonaceous material reducing recoveries and higher costs driven by lower volume. Management explicitly stated this was not a quarter they wanted and admitted execution fell short, though they raised Los Azules progress as a long-term offset. Guidance for San José dividends is paused until next year.

negative_highlights: Lower-than-planned grades at Kensington, Rochester, and Palmarejo operations are expected to rebound in H2 but impacted Q2 production.
New Afton's partial year guidance was refined downward as the ramp-up to target throughput of 16,000 tonnes per day is now pushed from end-Q2 to early Q4.
$140 million non-cash fair value uplift expense related to Rainy River stockpile inventory reduced reported EPS and EBITDA.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $1.1 billion and record free cash flow of $388 million despite lower realized metal prices.
Ending cash balance exceeded $1 billion for the first time in company history, doubling year-end 2025 liquidity to over $2 billion by Q4 expectations.
Rochester achieved a new quarterly crushing record of 6.8 million tonnes with Phase 2A Leach Pad expansion progressing ahead of schedule.
summary: Coeur reported record quarterly revenue of $1.1 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $478 million in Q2 FY26, driven by the first full quarter contributions from acquired New Afton and Rainy River assets despite lower-than-planned grades at three operations. Management recalibrated guidance for 2026 to reflect a slower ramp-up timeline for underground production at both Canadian mines compared to original assumptions, while maintaining confidence in strong second-half cash flow generation once non-cash acquisition accounting impacts ($140M) are removed.

negative_highlights: Consolidated Adjusted FCF before distributions for H1 was only $19M, significantly lower than the prior year's H1 due to a one-time $81M weather derivative receipt.
Liberty Costa Rica revenue declined sequentially compared to Q1 despite top-line improvement over last year.
Hurricane Melissa headwinds in Jamaica impacted Liberty Caribbean results by roughly $6 million net across both revenue and Adjusted OIBDA.
positive_highlights: Adjusted OIBDA grew 3% year-over-year to $436 million, driven by strong postpaid mobile trends across the group.
Liberty Puerto Rico Adjusted OIBDA margin expanded significantly to 32%, up from 29% last year, with churn stabilizing at healthy levels.
Announced an AI-driven IT services deal with Amdocs valued at north of $250 million NPV expected to drive OpEx reductions starting in Q4.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $1.1 billion (up 1% reported) and Adjusted OIBDA grew 3%, though consolidated Adjusted FCF before distributions ($83M in Q2) remains significantly weighted to the fourth quarter due to weather derivative receipts from last year's hurricane season. Management highlighted strong operational progress in Puerto Rico with margin expansion, but noted that H2 free cash flow momentum will likely be less robust than 2025 as they lap a large $81 million insurance payout and face higher P&E spending.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined year-over-year despite strong New Expensify growth
Classic customer base is shrinking as the company migrates users to New Expensify
Management noted uncertainty regarding which business strategy (New growth vs Classic churn mitigation) will win out first
positive_highlights: Free cash flow reached $6.4 million, up 162% sequentially from Q1
New Expensify net new revenue grew over 250% year-over-year to exceed $10M in ARR
Raised full-year free cash flow guidance by approximately $3-5M
summary: Q2 revenue declined year-over-year to $33.9 million as the company navigates a transition between its cash-generating Classic product and rapidly growing New Expensify cohort. Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance from $6-9M to $12-14M, citing improved profitability despite top-line pressure and resolved legal settlements. The business executed significant capital allocation with approximately 7% share repurchases while investing in AI features that drove a Platform of the Year award.

negative_highlights: The holding unit recorded a loss of BRL 46.2 million, representing an deterioration of BRL 8.7 million compared to the prior year.
Curtailed energy impact rose from 15.7% to 23.7%, resulting in a negative revenue impact of approximately BRL 34.8 million.
positive_highlights: EBITDA reached BRL 1.6 billion, representing a 21% increase compared to the same period last year.
Recurring net income grew significantly by 42.6%, reaching BRL 645 million driven by operational improvements and tax benefits.
Copel Distribuição's billed market expanded by 7.2%, contributing directly to boosting second quarter results.
summary: Copel reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with consolidated recovery EBITDA of BRL 1.6 billion (up 21% YoY) and recurring net income of BRL 645 million (up 42.6%). The quarter was highlighted by the completion of the tariff review for Copel Distribuição, which recognized investments exceeding double the 2021 base level. Management maintained its dividend policy with a minimum payout ratio of 75% and declared interest on equity totaling BRL 706 million.

negative_highlights: Q2 sales were partially inflated by a one-time inventory stocking event of approximately $6 million, which will create a headwind for Q3.
Management described growth trajectory as 'moderating' due to high market penetration (over 70% in major markets) and the natural lifecycle dynamics of an established product.
R&D expenses increased year-over-year from $69M to $74M primarily driven by advancement of three phase III trials.
positive_highlights: KIMMTRAK demonstrated a landmark doubling of the likelihood of being alive at five years (16% OS rate vs. 8%) in metastatic uveal melanoma patients treated with KIMMTRAK as their only therapy.
Q2 net sales reached $116 million, representing an 18% increase over Q2 FY25 and a sequential growth of approximately 3% when normalized for the stocking event.
The company holds a strong balance sheet with $880 million in cash and marketable securities as of June 30th.
summary: Immunocore reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $116 million (up 18% YoY) and H1 revenue of $223 million (up 16% YoY), driven by strong U.S. growth despite a one-time $6M inventory stocking headwind in the quarter. Management reiterated that top-line data for the TEBE-AM trial is expected as early as year-end, though enrollment remains ongoing with minimal impact from remaining patients. The company highlighted exceptional five-year overall survival data for KIMMTRAK and maintained its strategic focus on advancing three phase III melanoma trials.

negative_highlights: Delivery and other cloud applications revenue declined 6% YoY to $396 million, dragging overall top-line.
Q2 CapEx of $347 million was below guidance due to delayed GPU shipments arriving in Q3.
Full-year EPS guidance lowered by approximately $0.15-$0.20 compared to prior expectations.
positive_highlights: Announced total volume of multi-year commitments for cloud infrastructure services exceeds $2.8 billion this year.
Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS) revenue grew 39% YoY, driven by strong demand and a new robotics customer win.
Security revenue maintained momentum with growth of 10% YoY ($604M), led by WAF upgrades from major enterprises.
summary: Akamai reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.1 billion (up 5% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.59, missing the implied consensus due to a decline in delivery services (-6%) and lower-than-expected CapEx ($347M vs guidance). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance slightly but lowered Q3 specific guidance by approximately $8 million YoY due to foreign exchange headwinds. The company announced significant multi-year cloud infrastructure commitments totaling over $2.8 billion, with a new robotics deal worth more than $600 million expected to ramp in 2027.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed ~500 bps YoY
Headwinds in transactional product lines and portable storage units on rent
World Cup benefit creates sequential step-down into Q3
positive_highlights: Revenue up 4% YoY and adjusted EBITDA exceeded outlook
Modular activations up 16% YoY, pending orders up 13%
Enterprise account revenue up 21% YoY
summary: WSC reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $612M, up 4% YoY and above the ~$585M expectation, with leasing and services revenue up 6% and D&I revenue up 25%. Adjusted EBITDA was $228M, exceeding the $223M outlook, though margins compressed ~500 bps YoY to 37.2% due to upfront activation costs and mix. Management modestly raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, citing strong modular activations (up 16% YoY), order book growth (up 13% YoY), and enterprise account revenue up 21%, while noting headwinds in transactional product lines and a step-down from World Cup activity in Q3.

negative_highlights: I&M revenue down 5.5% YoY due to site losses and outage timing
Adjusted SG&A up to 22.1% of revenue from 21.2%
positive_highlights: C&E revenue up 16.8%, record segment revenue of $207 million
Combined C&E & Geo backlog up 20% YoY to $1.18 billion
Consolidated adjusted gross margin up 135 bps to 38.2%
summary: TIC Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $584 million, up 3.3% year-over-year (organic growth 2.5%). Adjusted gross margin expanded 135 basis points to 38.2%. C&E grew 16.8% to $207 million, Geo grew 7.9% to $81 million, but I&M declined 5.5% to $297 million due to site losses and outage timing. Combined backlog rose 20% to a record $1.18 billion, and the company expects improved growth in the second half.

negative_highlights: Oil and gas royalties contributed only approximately 5% of total Q2 revenues.
Management noted that converting the digital infrastructure opportunities into firm revenue depends on diligence timelines and power availability ramp-up, which may take time to finalize.
positive_highlights: Revenue hit an all-time high of $66.8 million driven by strong sequential growth in surface use royalties and produced water handling volumes.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to a robust 89% with free cash flow reaching $40.2 million (60% margin).
Digital infrastructure pipeline advanced significantly, moving from initial discussions to late-stage negotiations or signed LOIs.
summary: LandBridge reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $66.8 million (up 41% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $59.8 million with an 89% margin. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for Adjusted EBITDA between $210M-$230M, which was previously raised last quarter. The company highlighted a robust digital infrastructure pipeline involving seven counterparties representing over 10 gigawatts of potential.

negative_highlights: Total quarterly investment income decreased by $14 million quarter-over-quarter driven by portfolio size reduction and non-accruals
New deal activity remained light due to geopolitical uncertainty, specifically tensions in the Middle East/Iran situation
NAV per share declined 2.8% from Q1 levels
positive_highlights: $4 million in share repurchases completed during the quarter under a $300M program
KKR waived its portion of subordinated income incentive fee, providing an $11 million positive impact on Q2 net investment income
Portfolio rotation continued with sales of approximately $500 million to third parties and capital return from legacy asset Global Jet
summary: FSK reported Q2 FY2026 net investment income of $0.44 per share and adjusted net investment income of $0.43 per share, resulting in a NAV decline to $18.30 due to portfolio value decreases exceeding earnings. Management reiterated guidance for annualized yield between 8%-9% but noted that loan sales were muted by geopolitical tensions (specifically Iran) which impacted repayment activity and new deal origination volumes.

negative_highlights: China revenue declined 23% as IVD pricing guideline uncertainty impacted note
Respiratory season forecast revised down; assuming below-average season for 2026-2027
Free cash flow guidance withdrawn; Q2 operating cash flow was negative $111 million
positive_highlights: Ex-China revenue grew 6%, with Labs ex-China up 9% and TRIAGE up 9%
Adjusted EBITDA increased 21% to $129 million, margin up 310 bps to 20%
North America grew 6% and JPAC grew 10%
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 2% constant currency, with ex-China growth of 6%; adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $129 million with margin up 310 bps to 20%. China revenue declined 23% and respiratory season is expected to be soft, leading to guidance cuts for FY2026 revenue ($2.52B-$2.60B), adjusted EBITDA ($540M-$560M), and adjusted EPS ($0.65-$0.90). Free cash flow guidance was withdrawn, and operating cash flow was negative $111 million for the quarter.

negative_highlights: Specialty market conditions more competitive; rates continuing to soften
Established $30 million reserve for Middle East developments
GAAP net income per share only $0.87 due to one-time costs
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 93% year-over-year to $575 million
Adjusted net operating EPS grew to $1.14, with ROE of 13%
Share repurchase guidance tracking to upper end of $200-250 million range
summary: Radian reported Q2 2026 with total revenues of $575 million, up 93% year-over-year, driven by the Inigo acquisition, and net earned premiums up 116% to $504 million. Adjusted net operating EPS grew to $1.14, with adjusted net operating ROE of 13%. Mortgage segment new insurance written rose 14% to $16.3 billion, and persistency improved to 82%. Specialty net premiums earned increased 9% to $267 million, with plans for second-half earned premiums to be about 20% higher than first-half. Guidance for full-year share repurchases was raised to the upper end of the $200-250 million range, and expected Radian Guaranty dividends increased to $650 million or more. Market conditions in specialty insurance are more competitive, and a $30 million Middle East reserve was established.

negative_highlights: F1 revenue declined 15% YoY due to a calendar variance reducing the race count from nine to five races in Q2 and eight vs eleven YTD
Adjusted OIBDA for F1 decreased year-to-date because of lower event counts, with team payments as % of Adjusted OIBDA at 61.7%
F3 revenue declined due to the sale of cars at the beginning of the new cycle last year
positive_highlights: F1 viewership up 13% year-over-year, with Apple TV attracting a younger and more female audience
MotoGP attendance increased +4% through Mugello with record numbers in Thailand and Germany
Las Vegas Grand Prix ticket sales trending well ahead of last year's levels as of July
summary: Liberty Media reported Q2 FY26 results where F1 revenue declined 15% YoY and Adjusted OIBDA fell 30%, primarily driven by a calendar variance that reduced the race count to eight events compared to eleven last year. MotoGP showed growth in constant currency due to event mix changes, but overall consolidated performance was weighed down significantly by the absence of Saudi Arabia and Bahrain races held earlier in the quarter. Management noted that F1 revenue recognition is based on season-based accruals tied to the specific race count staged.

negative_highlights: Southwest Steel Processing expected to generate a net loss of $0.50 per diluted share in 2026
SG&A expenses increased to 12.1% of sales versus 11.7% a year ago
Interest expense rose $1.1 million year-over-year due to higher rates on senior notes
positive_highlights: Record consolidated revenues of $440 million, up 10% year-over-year
Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $3.10-$3.30
Engineered Products operating income up 50% year-over-year
summary: Park-Ohio reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $440 million, up 10% year-over-year, with record revenues in Supply Technologies and Engineered Products. Adjusted EPS rose 24% to $0.93, and operating income increased 22% year-over-year. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for net sales to $1.7-1.73 billion and adjusted EPS to $3.10-3.30, citing strong demand across multiple end markets. Management also noted strong backlogs and continued operational improvements, while reviewing strategic alternatives for Southwest Steel Processing, which is expected to be a drag this year.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross margins faced pressure, with Payables segment margins contracting significantly due to a mix shift toward lower-margin buyer-funded revenues and higher interchange costs.
Treasury Solutions saw margin compression as high-growth segments like Passport (125% growth) and Priority Tech Ventures expanded at lower margins than the core CFTPay platform.
Merchant Solutions revenue included 3.6% of volume from acquisitions, with organic merchant growth slowing to mid-single digits amid macro headwinds in construction and restaurants.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 9% YoY driven by strong organic growth (7.2%) across segments, particularly a 21.6% increase in Payables and 14.9% in Treasury Solutions.
Adjusted EPS increased 12% year-over-year to $0.29 despite margin headwinds.
Total customer accounts on the platform grew nearly 13% YoY to reach 1.8 million.
summary: Priority Commerce reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $262.3 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.29 (up 12% YoY). Management maintained full-year guidance for revenue ($1.01B-$1.04B), gross profit, and adjusted EBITDA but expects results to be at the lower end of their respective ranges due to margin pressures from business mix shifts and higher interchange costs. The company ended with $120.3 million in cash on hand.

negative_highlights: Company remains in a net loss position with cash burn of approximately $15 million annually
positive_highlights: Revenue beat expectations with a significant year-over-year increase to $13.4 million
Net loss improved materially from the prior period's $15.9 million to $5.9 million
Raised full-year revenue guidance range and narrowed ranges for operating expense
summary: OmniAb reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $13.4 million (up from $3.9M in the prior year) and a net loss narrowing to $5.9 million ($0.05/share). Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both total revenue and cash balance, citing strong momentum driven by milestone payments and two xPloration instrument sales.

negative_highlights: Total revenue and adjusted net income declined 1% and 2% organically, missing expectations.
U.S. revenue declined 7%, with companion animal portfolio down 6%.
Management lowered full-year guidance due to intensified competitive pressure and softer clinic visits.
positive_highlights: Livestock revenue grew 11% in the quarter, led by strong U.S. performance.
Companion animal diagnostics revenue grew 12%, with sustained demand in urgent and emergency care.
International revenue grew 6% organically, supported by broad-based emerging market growth.
summary: Zoetis reported Q2 FY2026 organic revenue and adjusted net income declines of 1% and 2% respectively, with U.S. revenue down 7% and companion animal portfolio down 6%, while international grew 6% and livestock grew 11%. The company cited intensified competitive pressure and softer clinic visits, leading to increased promotional spending and a revised full-year outlook reflecting continued near-term headwinds. Management highlighted strength in diagnostics (revenue up 12%) and livestock, but acknowledged price realization could be flat to -2% for the year due to gross-to-net adjustments.

negative_highlights: Cortrophin guidance modestly revised down to $520-540M from prior (not stated)
ILUVIEN revenue down 16% YoY on international shipment timing
Gout sales force expansion adds costs, limiting near-term operating leverage
positive_highlights: Record Q2 revenues of $266M and record adjusted EBITDA of $71.6M
Cortrophin up 43% YoY with July record new cases and gout expansion off to strong start
Total revenue guidance of $1.1B and EBITDA growth of 27% reiterated
summary: ANI Pharmaceuticals reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $266M (up 26% YoY) and record adjusted EBITDA of $71.6M (up 32% YoY). Cortrophin Gel revenue was $117.1M, up 43% YoY and 56% QoQ; management revised full-year Cortrophin guidance modestly to $520-540M, still representing 50-55% growth. The gout sales force expansion is fully operational with strong leading indicators, and generics revenue grew 10% YoY. The company reiterated total revenue guidance of $1.1B and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $285-300M.

negative_highlights: Fuel hedges offset ~$20 million in the quarter, trading upside for certainty
Over $40 million of foregone margin at Montana Renewables due to turnaround
Working capital built $70 million, including $30 million crude inventory and $30 million receivables
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes of $175 million despite turnarounds
Restricted group leverage below 4x, expected to surpass 3x next quarter
MaxSAF catalyst test met or exceeded expectations; SAF run rate to ramp to 120-150 million gallons by spring 2027
summary: Calumet reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $175 million, with strong performance in both Specialties and Montana Renewables despite planned turnarounds. The company deleveraged below 4x restricted group leverage, repurchased $115 million of notes and terminated a sale-leaseback. Management guided to accelerated deleveraging, announced a novel MaxSAF 150 second-phase expansion to reach 120-150 million gallons of SAF by spring 2027, and identified ~$50 million of low-risk specialty growth capital for 2027-2028.

negative_highlights: System revenue declined 34% year-over-year due to used-device cannibalization
Operating loss of $0.3M vs. operating income of $1.4M in prior year
Withdrew FY2026 revenue guidance due to proposed CMS reimbursement cuts
positive_highlights: Applicator unit volume up 27% year-over-year, a new all-time record
Applicator revenue up 13% year-over-year, partially offsetting system sales weakness
Finalized VDAs at amounts below accrued balances, yielding a $0.9M favorable swing
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue fell 3% YoY to $9.7M, with system sales down 34% to $2.3M due to used-device cannibalization and industry distress, while applicator revenue grew 13% YoY and unit volume rose 27% YoY. Gross margin contracted to 76.2% and the company swung to an operating loss of $0.3M, with net loss of $0.7M. Management withdrew FY2026 guidance due to proposed CMS reimbursement cuts for UltraMIST under the PFS rule, though HOPPS proposed rule includes a 14% increase. The company intends to challenge the PFS proposal during the comment period.

negative_highlights: Book value per share declined to negative $45.58, down $1.31 from year-end 2025
Holding company cash and liquid assets decreased to $337 million from $357 million at year-end 2025
Oversight board settlement offer of ~$3 billion was dismissed by bondholders as inadequate
positive_highlights: Consolidated GAAP net loss improved to $46 million from $56 million in the prior year quarter
Adjusted net loss improved to $7 million from $8 million in the prior year quarter
National's leverage ratio improved to 21:1 from 24:1 at year-end 2025
summary: MBIA reported a narrower adjusted net loss of $7 million in Q2 2026, compared to $8 million a year earlier, driven by lower loss expenses at National. National's PREPA exposure decreased by $35 million to $390 million, and the oversight board increased its settlement offer to about $3 billion, but bondholders dismissed it as inadequate. Holding company liquidity declined to $337 million, and book value per share fell to negative $45.58. Management is cautiously monitoring PREPA litigation and potential sale options, with no new guidance provided.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow was negative $258 million in Q2 due to cash taxes, prepaid deliveries, and elevated production costs
Goose production impacted by April crusher fire; remediation and phase 1 crusher upgrades expected by end of Q3
Adjusted EPS of $0.03 was hit by ~$71 million realized losses on gold collar contracts
positive_highlights: Menankoto Exploitation Permit granted, allowing Fekola Regional pre-stripping to commence
Fekola, Masbate, and Otjikoto exceeded expectations; production guidance raised for those operations
AISC guidance lowered to $2,370-$2,550/oz, with full year expected at or below low end
summary: Consolidated Q2 production of ~204,000 oz in line with expectations; adjusted net income was $41M ($0.03/sh) with ~$71M realized losses from gold collar contracts. Fekola, Masbate, and Otjikoto outperformed, while Goose was impacted by the April crusher fire. The Menankoto Exploitation Permit was granted, clearing the way for Fekola Regional pre-stripping. 2026 production guidance narrowed to 820-920k oz, cash cost guidance unchanged, AISC guidance lowered; management expects meaningful free cash flow improvement in H2 and into 2027 as prepaid contracts are complete.

negative_highlights: Ebouri-5-8 water cut increased faster than expected, implying more reservoir connectivity
Exploration well at West Etame encountered water-bearing zone and was not commercial
Production uplift from Baobab drilling not significant until 2027
positive_highlights: Net income of $42.4 million and adjusted EBITDAX of $54.8 million in Q2
Baobab production resumed and is slightly above pre-startup forecast
Egypt drilling program expanded to 10-15 wells with no increase in CapEx guidance
summary: VAALCO reported Q2 2026 net income of $42.4 million and adjusted EBITDAX of $54.8 million. Management noted sequential improvement in revenue and profitability, but cited persistent U.S. headwinds and macro factors such as ACA/Medicaid enrollment and GLP-1 adoption.

The company maintained a balanced business mix across residential and commercial segments while returning capital via dividends and share repurchases.

HSA saw mixed results due to MEDITECH EMR conversion causing lower cash collections
U.K. revenue impacted by funding pressures at the NHS as administration rebalances budget
positive_highlights: Post-acute portfolio delivered strongest growth with EBITDARM increasing more than $70 million year-over-year
MEDIAN revenue increased 24% and Ernest Health increased 13%
Refinancing transaction extends debt maturities to 2032, clearing runway until late 2028
summary: MPT reported normalized FFO of $0.15 per share in Q2 FY2026, which was in line with expectations despite mixed results from HSA due to EMR conversion disruptions and delayed supplemental funding. Management announced a comprehensive refinancing extending debt maturities until late 2028, eliminating near-term obligations through secured notes issuance and asset sales. While post-acute operators showed strong growth led by MEDIAN and Ernest Health, behavioral health coverage declined slightly in the U.S. and U.K., with specific liquidity pressures noted for HSA.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined to 16%, down from the prior period due to product mix shift and inventory write-offs

Net loss widened to RMB 102 million compared to net income of RMB 5.9 million in Q2 last year

Same-store sales surged by 24% year-over-year driven by operational efficiency gains
summary: NIU reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 1.44 billion (up 14.7% YoY) and sales volume of 434,000 units (up 24%), driven by a structural shift in China towards electric motorcycles which offset declines in the premium e-bicycle segment. Gross margin contracted to 16%, down from last year's levels due to product mix changes toward lower-margin models, inventory write-offs for international micromobility, and elevated raw material costs. Management provided Q3 revenue guidance of RMB 1.86-2.03 billion (up 10%-20% YoY), maintaining a disciplined stance amidst domestic regulatory headwinds.

negative_highlights: Q2 TVision integration caused a 150 basis point drag on EBITDA margins
Q3 guidance expects approximately 200 basis points margin drag from TVision costs
Political spending contribution is described as 'de minimis' at about 200 basis points
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 34% year-over-year
CTV spend surged by nearly 50%
TVision pilot campaigns achieved an average lift of 1.4x conversion rates
summary: Viant reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with revenue up 34% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of $14.2 million, both exceeding the high end of guidance. CTV spend surged nearly 50%, accounting for over half of total ad spend, driven by new customer acquisition via ViantAI and TVision integration pilots showing significant conversion lifts. Management raised Q3 guidance expectations implicitly through strong commentary on durable growth pipelines despite acknowledging a temporary margin drag from TVision.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined 2.8% year-over-year despite growth in all streams
Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 1.6% from 2.8% due to higher marketing spend and tax expense
Japan revenue fell 6.7% YoY with MAU declining 3.3%
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA of $5.5M exceeded the high end of Q3 guidance range
Korea revenue grew 20% YoY on a constant currency basis driven by paid content and advertising
English platform webcomic app MAU increased 3.7% year over year
summary: WBTN reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $338.5 million (down 2.8% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $5.5 million, which beat the high end of guidance but was below prior year levels due to increased marketing investments in Korea. Management highlighted strong growth in Korean paid content (+4.3%) and advertising (+11.5%), alongside a new strategic direction involving AI initiatives and an investment in RI Games Holdings for IP adaptations. Q3 2026 revenue guidance remains flat-to-low single-digit (0.7%-3.3% CC), with adjusted EBITDA expected between $0-$5 million.

expecting slightly free cash flow negative at year-end due to mortgage and revolver carryover
conversion rate from enrollment to start was lower in Q2 than historical levels
positive_highlights: revenue growth of 22.4% YoY
adjusted EBITDA growth of 42.4%
reiterating full-year guidance while increasing CapEx outlook
summary: Lincoln Educational Services reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with revenue growth of 22.4% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 42.4%, significantly beating expectations. Management reiterated full-year guidance while increasing the capital expenditure outlook to support new campus developments in Suitland, Maryland; Tempe, Arizona; and Hicksville/Rowlett. The company highlighted a robust August start projection driven by high school recruiting improvements and noted that student conversion rates are recovering from Q2 pressures.

negative_highlights: First-half revenue was lighter than expected due to partial quarter impact from April business rule changes and channel inventory normalization for IHEEZO.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$1.2 million, reflecting continued commercial investments in the sales organization.
positive_highlights: VEVYE delivered quarterly revenue of $29.4 million, up nearly 58% YoY, with prescriptions growing 21% sequentially despite new co-pay rules.
IHEEZO achieved record unit demand (65,477 units) and a trailing 12-month reorder rate of approximately 85.5%, validating the in-office market strategy.
Harrow secured access to millions of previously blocked commercial lives via a new top-three PBM win for VEVYE.
summary: Harrow reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $70.7 million (up 11% YoY and ~60% sequentially) with GAAP gross margins at 71%. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue between $350M-$365M, implying a second-half run rate of approximately $235M-$250M. The quarter was driven by record demand in IHEEZO and VEVYE following business rule changes and PBM coverage wins.

negative_highlights: Portfolio generated a net loss of $50.3 million concentrated in five names, including ChyronHego which contributed a $21.5 million loss.
NAV per share declined 3.2% quarter-over-quarter to $13.37 due to the portfolio loss and buyback activity.
Weighted average spread on the direct origination portfolio narrowed slightly to 539 bps from 540 bps in the prior quarter.
positive_highlights: Net investment income ($0.40) exceeded the quarterly dividend ($0.31), providing $0.09 of accretion per share.
Stock repurchases of $31.9 million were executed at an average price of $11.58, fully utilizing authorization to support NAV.
Undrawn capacity under the revolving credit facility remains robust at $925 million ($800 million adjusted for recent maturities).
summary: MFIC reported a net loss of $50.3 million ($0.61 per share) driven by credit pressure in a limited number of positions, resulting in NAV per share declining 3.2% to $13.37. Net investment income was $0.40 per share, which exceeded the declared dividend of $0.31 per share. The company prioritized deleveraging over new stock repurchases, reducing leverage modestly to 1.54x while maintaining a sound liquidity position.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $46.6 million from $26.9 million due to higher R&D and G&A expenses including BLA-enabling PPQ initiatives.
One patient in the REVEAL pivotal trial experienced a Grade 2 SAE of peripheral sensory neuropathy requiring overnight hospitalization, though classified as non-severe with rapid recovery.
No top-line revenue reported for this pre-revenue clinical-stage company.
positive_highlights: Longer-term REVEAL Part A data showed 100% response rate at 12 months, far exceeding the FDA-aligned 33% threshold with no evidence of plateau effect.
Total cash and cash equivalents reached $455.4 million following a successful follow-on financing in June 2026.
Expanded partnership with Catalent secured for future commercial manufacturing support at an established AAV facility.
summary: Taysha reported a net loss of $46.6 million ($0.13 per share) for Q2 FY2026 compared to a prior quarter's loss of $26.9 million, driven by increased R&D and G&A expenses related to BLA-enabling manufacturing initiatives and clinical trial expansion. The company completed dosing in the REVEAL pivotal (17 patients) and ASPIRE trials but disclosed one Grade 2 SAE involving peripheral sensory neuropathy requiring hospitalization for management, though recovery was rapid. Management maintains confidence in TSHA-102's efficacy data exceeding FDA thresholds while emphasizing a strengthened balance sheet with $455.4 million in cash to support operations through late 2028.

negative_highlights: China Q2 RevPAR softened slightly compared to the strong first quarter, attributed to forward-shifting travel demand from Chinese New Year holidays.
Key money revenue was down slightly year-over-year, though management views this as stable within a $200M-$250M range.
positive_highlights: Global RevPAR grew 4.1% with growth across all three regions (Americas, EMEA, Greater China).
Net system size growth accelerated to 5%, driven by record development activity and a high-quality estate strategy.
Fee margin expanded significantly by 120 basis points due to scale efficiencies and cost reductions in owner programs.
summary: IHG reported strong first-half performance with global RevPAR growth of 4.1%, gross system growth of 6.5%, and net system growth of 5%. Adjusted earnings per share grew 13% supported by a record development pipeline where openings and signings were up 8% year-on-year, while fee margins expanded by 120 basis points.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margins were below expectations at 12.4%, down 540 bps YoY due to one-time labor/subcontractor costs and weather impacts.
Intense weather events in Georgia slowed deployment of crews for A.L. Grading Contractors.
General administrative expenses increased as the company matures its corporate infrastructure post-IPO.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 114% year-over-year driven by strength across commercial/industrial and residential end markets.
Total backlog reached a record $866 million, up 35% from the prior year period.
Successfully closed acquisition of Allied Paving in Atlanta with team-sourced execution.
summary: Cardinal Infrastructure Group reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $227 million (up 114% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $28.1 million, though margins were below expectations due to one-time costs, weather impacts in Georgia, and deployment shifts for a diversified project mix. Management raised full-year revenue guidance from the prior range of $680-$890 million to $880-$900 million (midpoint ~$890M) while updating adjusted EBITDA margin expectations to 16%-18% due to transitional costs and SG&A investments. The company also announced the acquisition of Allied Paving, adding $28 million in revenue for Q3.

negative_highlights: Total margin headwind of nearly 100 basis points driven by accelerated inflationary costs (ocean freight, steel) exceeding the benefit from a $5 million tariff refund.
Ice and beverage platform margins were approximately 400 bps lower than established cooking platforms due to initial investment phases in new product launches.
Expectation of incremental inflationary margin pressures of $10-$15 million for the remainder of the year.
positive_highlights: Delivered over 8% organic revenue growth for the second consecutive quarter despite challenging macro conditions.
Raised full-year organic revenue guidance to 6%-8%, beating prior expectations of 4%-6%.
Adjusted EPS expansion achieved primarily through volume-driven sales and $200 million in share repurchases.
summary: Middleby reported Q2 FY26 commercial foodservice revenue of $631 million with organic growth of 8.3%, driven by strength in ice and beverage platforms despite a total margin headwind of nearly 100 basis points from inflationary costs exceeding tariff refunds. Management raised full-year organic revenue guidance for the core business to 6%-8% (from prior expectations) while maintaining adjusted EPS guidance at $6.73-$6.89, citing momentum in QSR new product adoption and a pent-up replacement cycle.

negative_highlights: G&A expenses increased by $0.4 million due to the consolidation of Peak Maritime Management AS

summary: Himalaya Shipping reported a net profit of $24.6 million and EBITDA of $44 million for Q2 FY2026, representing significant year-over-year growth driven by time charter equivalent earnings rising from $28,400 to approximately $50,600 per day. The company declared total cash distributions of $0.59 per share and entered into new index-linked charters at premiums above the Baltic Capesize Index while converting several vessels to fixed rates. Management expressed strong confidence in a robust second half driven by structural ton-mile increases from iron ore and bauxite, noting that Q1 2027 coverage is premature given current curve spreads.

negative_highlights: Computing segment revenue decreased 23.7% compared to Q1 due to inventory adjustments

summary: IMOS reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with revenue of NT$7,383 million (up 28.7% YoY) and gross margin expanding to 18.0%, driven by record demand exceeding capacity in memory products which grew over 46% year-over-year. Net earnings per ADS reached a new high of $0.80 compared to a loss last year, with management raising CapEx guidance for the full year above 25% of revenue and planning further expansion into AI ASIC testing.

Net realized and unrealized change resulted in an aggregate loss of $18.3 million for the quarter, impacting GAAP earnings significantly below core income levels.

Portfolio remains highly diversified with only four non-accrual investments, representing just 0.4% of market value and 1% at cost.
New originations in the core middle market maintain attractive credit metrics including median debt-to-EBITDA of 2.3x for new platform companies.

NAV declined approximately 2% from the prior quarter primarily attributable to this specific provision for losses rather than portfolio-wide deterioration, with PIK income remaining low at 2.4%. Management maintained a cautious tone regarding macro headwinds like tariffs affecting consumer names while highlighting resilience in government services.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they have not provided further guidance on future milestones or timelines for construction initiation.

NRC approved the Safety Evaluation Report on Postulated Initiating Events methodology, advancing licensing readiness for Project TETRA and TEFLA.
Signed ground lease agreements with Texas A&M University to secure a 77-acre site at RELLIS campus.

summary: GrowGeneration reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $43.2 million (up 5.5% YoY) and achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.3 million after returning to profitability in the quarter. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from breakeven to a range of $2-$3 million while reaffirming revenue guidance at $162-$168 million, driven by proprietary brand penetration reaching 40% and cost reductions.

negative_highlights: Manufacturing revenue decreased 49% quarter-over-quarter due to lower new purchase orders.
Services O&M revenue declined following the expiration of two contracts in Q1 2026.
Full-year 2026 manufacturing revenue is projected to be less than full-year 2025 results.

summary: Consolidated Water reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $32.9 million, a decrease from the prior quarter and year-over-year decline in manufacturing offset by growth in retail, bulk, and services segments. Net income attributable to stockholders was $4.0 million ($0.25 per diluted share), down from $5.2 million in the prior period due primarily to lower manufacturing gross profit and a change in revenue mix. Management noted that full-year 2026 manufacturing results are expected to remain below last year's record level, though they expressed cautious optimism regarding future quarters supported by new orders.

negative_highlights: Total Non-GAAP gross margin declined 120 bps YoY to 18.6%.
Public Cloud revenue fell 2% YoY reflecting lower infrastructure and services demand.
Free cash flow was negative $48 million in Q2, with full-year FCF expected between -$50M and +$70M.

Public Cloud revenue was modestly ahead of the lower end of the guided range due to higher-than-anticipated hyperscaler consumption.
Strategic partnerships with AMD and Palantir are advancing, targeting 15 MW cumulative AI capacity by end of 2027.
summary: Rackspace reported Q2 FY26 GAAP revenue of $670 million (up 1% YoY), beating Private Cloud guidance but missing Public Cloud targets due to lower infrastructure/services demand; total company Non-GAAP gross margin contracted by 120 bps to 18.6%. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance at a decline, citing a strategic pivot away from low-margin Public Cloud toward higher-value AI and regulated enterprise services.

negative_highlights: Aerospace revenues decreased by 8% due to unfavorable project mix.
Effective tax rate increased significantly from 5.6% to 16.4% driven by OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax rules implementation.
positive_highlights: Record backlog of $32 billion achieved with a sequential increase driven predominantly by international orders.
GAAP gross margin expanded to 25.3% (up from 24%) and non-GAAP operating income increased significantly year-over-year.
Elbit Systems secured major new awards including a sole prime supplier status for the U.S. Army ENVG-B system ($212M) and a $1.4B European modernization contract.
summary: Elbit Systems reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $2.287 billion (up 15.9% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $3.61 (up 34%), driven by double-digit growth across all segments including a record backlog expansion to $32 billion. Gross margins expanded sequentially, with non-GAAP gross margin reaching 25.6%, while operating income grew significantly due to favorable project mix in the U.S. and Israel inventory replenishments. Management highlighted strong demand visibility from Europe and North America, noting that customers are increasingly willing to fund capacity expansion directly.

note, general, and administrative expenses rose to $9.2 million due to stock-based compensation
Durability data not expected until after the safety follow-up period following the 13-week or 26-week readouts
positive_highlights: Positive interim data suggests ABS-201 was well-tolerated with favorable safety and tolerability profile

$40 million strategic investment from Eli Lilly completed alongside a $100 million financing round
summary: Absci reported positive interim Phase I data for ABS-201 in the HEADLINE trial, demonstrating a favorable safety profile and an estimated half-life of at least 65 days supporting potential dosing two to three times over six months. The company announced a $40 million strategic investment from Eli Lilly alongside a completed $100 million financing round, bringing total cash reserves to approximately $201 million as of June 30, 2026. Management anticipates an interim proof-of-concept readout later in the year and plans to initiate a Phase II endometriosis trial in Q4.

negative_highlights: Implantable sales grew only 1% as PowerVision programs were discontinued following unresolved clinical data issues.
U.S. cataract procedure volumes remained flat, moderating overall growth compared to international markets.
Surgical glaucoma segment faced continued headwinds from reimbursement changes affecting Hydrus performance.
positive_highlights: Sales grew 7% year-over-year with equipment sales surging 25% driven by UNITY adoption.
Core operating margin expanded significantly to 64.7%, up 250 basis points from the prior year.
PanOptix Pro achieved approximately 90% conversion of PanOptix accounts in the U.S., exceeding expectations.
summary: Alcon reported Q2 FY26 sales of $2.8 billion, up 7% year-over-year on constant currency, driven by strong performance in surgical equipment (up 25%) and ocular health (up 12%). Management raised its full-year core diluted EPS guidance to a range of 12%-15%, citing the benefit from share repurchases and a $60 million tariff refund. While implantable growth was modest at 1% due to discontinued PowerVision programs, leadership expressed confidence in PanOptix Pro adoption and a robust pipeline including Vivity Pro.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they do not provide formal revenue guidance for the current year or potentially 2027, citing rapid growth as a reason to avoid misguidance.
Cash and cash equivalents decreased by $1 million quarter-over-quarter due to collection cycles with customers, though Q4 generation is expected to be positive.
positive_highlights: Net product sales increased 78% year-over-year to $17.1 million, driven by a 280% increase in field sales calls and record patient enrollments via Fennec HEARS.
July recorded an all-time high for completed PEDMARK infusions, new patient enrollments, active patients on therapy, and new customers simultaneously.
Medical affairs expanded unique HCP reach by 63% and affiliated sites by 72%, with discussions shifting from general awareness to implementation of CIO prevention.
summary: Fennec Pharmaceuticals reported Q2 FY2026 net product sales of $17.1 million, a 78% year-over-year increase from $9.7 million in the prior period. The company achieved its seventh consecutive quarter of growth with record demand and an all-time high for completed infusions in July. Management stated they do not provide formal revenue guidance but expressed confidence that trends seen early in Q3 will sustain momentum through the remainder of 2026.

negative_highlights: Base business net sales declined by $10.2 million (2.9%) driven primarily by a volume decrease of $15.5 million.
GAAP EPS was negative at -$0.05 due to approximately $9.7 million in acquisition, divestiture-related expenses and restructuring costs.
Management noted softness in College Inn consumption and the need to improve performance across retail branded channels.

Base business net sales are on track with plan for YTD FY26 at approximately flat compared to prior year ($711.4M vs $711.2M).
Spices & Flavor Solutions segment Adjusted EBITDA increased 29% due to improved cost environment and tariff refunds.
summary: B&G Foods reported Q2 FY26 net sales of $383.3 million (down 9.7% YoY) and a GAAP loss of $4 million ($0.05/share), though adjusted metrics beat prior year with Adjusted EBITDA rising to $60.4 million on the back of divestitures, acquisitions, and tariff refunds. Management reaffirmed full-year FY26 guidance for net sales between $1.735 billion-$1.775 billion and Adjusted EBITDA between $275 million-$290 million despite a challenging industry backdrop involving inflationary pressures in vegetable oil and spices.

negative_highlights: High-powered laser shipments remain significantly behind customer demand despite increased signals, creating a supply constraint relative to the fastest-growing segment.
Convertible note equity conversion resulted in a $7.8 billion non-cash GAAP charge, turning reported net income into a loss of $7.2 billion for Q4.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 109% year-over-year to $1.01 billion, marking eight consecutive quarters of top-line growth with three straight quarters above 20% sequential expansion.
Non-GAAP gross margin crossed the 50% threshold in Q4 at a revenue level well below the original target run rate, driven by mix and pricing power.
Q1 FY2027 guidance raised to $1.225-$1.275 billion with operating margins of 39.5%-40.5%, achieved more than one quarter ahead of schedule.
summary: Fourth quarter revenue surged 109% year-over-year to $1.01 billion and non-GAAP EPS was $3.23, significantly beating the high end of guidance due to strong components ($649M) and systems ($357M) performance driven by AI demand. Management raised Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance to a range of $1.225-$1.275 billion (midpoint $1.25B), noting they are hitting this target more than one quarter ahead of schedule, and projected non-GAAP operating margins between 39.5% and 40.5%. Gross margin expanded to 50.4%, crossing the previously targeted threshold at a much lower revenue run rate.

negative_highlights: Net asset value per share declined $0.23 to $16 due to realized and unrealized losses totaling $0.26 per share.
Realized loss of $9.4 million recognized on the liquidation of investment in Sundance, alongside other rotation-related losses.
Non-accrual rate increased 20 basis points to 2.7% driven by additions for 4over and Diverzify.
positive_highlights: New floating-rate loan originations averaged 566 basis points over SOFR, reflecting a wider pricing environment than the prior quarter.
Debt-to-equity ratio remained within target range at 1.17x despite leverage increases from delayed realizations rather than deliberate moves.
Watch list held steady at approximately 5.5% of fair market value with no material deterioration in credit quality overall.
summary: KBDC reported net investment income of $0.42 per share and EPS of $0.16 for Q2 FY2026, slightly below the prior quarter's NII but in line with expectations given a lower dividend coverage ratio relative to NAV decline. The company maintained its target debt-to-equity range at 1.17x while rotating out of broadly syndicated loans into higher-yielding private credit assets averaging 566 bps over SOFR. Management noted modest deal flow pickup and stable watch list levels, though realized losses from Sundance and unrealized marks on specific positions weighed on NAV.

negative_highlights: Calendar shift reduced reported organic revenue by approximately 2%, masking underlying growth that would have been higher.
Nexus contribution in Q3 was described as a 'small amount' with full ramp-up expected to occur primarily in the fourth quarter and fiscal 2027.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue grew 9% to $5B with underlying growth excluding calendar shift estimated at +2%; AOI margins expanded nearly 20 bps driven by supply chain efficiencies.
Client retention reached record levels of approximately 98%, reflecting strong service execution and client relationships across the portfolio.
Aramark Nexus contributed late-quarter revenue from a top global hyperscaler, with scope increasing 40% to an estimated $140M-$160M annually per site.
summary: Aramark reported Q3 FY26 organic revenue growth of 9% to $5 billion and adjusted operating income (AOI) expansion of nearly 20 basis points to a margin that drove AOI up 18%. Management raised the fiscal 2026 organic revenue guidance range from prior levels to an increase of 9%-10%, while reaffirming AOI growth expectations of 12%-17% and adjusted EPS growth of 20%-25%. The quarter was driven by record client retention at approximately 98%, strong new business wins totaling $1.6 billion year-to-date, and the initial ramp-up of Aramark Nexus operations.

negative_highlights: Negative revenue adjustment of $136 million related to exiting Deutsche Bahn and Network Rail contracts
Adjusted loss per share was $0.63 due to one-time charges including a non-cash impairment of $75 million
Volume headwinds in Northern Europe, China, and Middle East affecting Harsco Environmental
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA increased by over 20% compared to last year
Harsco Environmental revenues grew on a like-for-like basis with improved pricing and volumes
Rail aftermarket revenue growth offset lower original equipment sales

Adjusted EBITDA increased by over 20% to $34 million driven by Harsco Environmental and aftermarket volumes at Rail, though adjusted loss per share was $0.63 due to one-time exit charges of roughly $190 million in accrued liabilities. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged despite better-than-anticipated first-half performance, citing uncertainty from Middle East geopolitical pressures.

negative_highlights: Live streaming revenue declined YoY to CNY 1.1 billion amid softer user spending and industry-wide competition.
Sales and marketing expenses increased sharply by 58% YoY (to RMB 91M) primarily due to promotional efforts for Goose Goose Duck Mobile.
Interest income dropped significantly from RMB 59 million to RMB 26 million, reflecting lower cash balances.
positive_highlights: Game-related services revenue surged 54% YoY to CNY 638 million due to publishing success (Goose Goose Duck) and advertising growth.
Gross margin expanded 120 bps sequentially to 14.7%, driven by the shift toward higher-margin game publishing and in-game item sales.
Non-GAAP operating income turned positive at RMB 16 million, a significant improvement from RMB 0.4 million last year.
summary: HUYA reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of CNY 1.74 billion (up 11% YoY), driven by a 54% surge in game-related services and advertising to CNY 638 million, while live streaming revenue declined slightly year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 14.7%, narrowing the operating loss to RMB 7 million as higher-margin publishing contributions offset slower core streamer performance. Management raised its share repurchase authorization from $50M-$100M and highlighted strong monetization in their new title, Goose Goose Duck Mobile.

negative_highlights: IDI real estate vertical declined modestly due to industry headwinds including limited inventory and elevated interest rates.
Gross revenue retention decreased slightly by two percentage points to 95% compared to the prior year period.
positive_highlights: Revenue reached a record $26.7 million, up 23% year-over-year with four of five verticals hitting all-time highs.
Adjusted gross margin expanded two percentage points to a new high of 86%, driven by operating leverage and scale.
Added a record 447 IDI customers in Q2, surpassing the previous quarterly record of 400.
summary: Red Violet reported a record Q2 FY2026 with revenue of $26.7 million (up 23% YoY), adjusted gross margin expanding to a new high of 86%, and cash flow from operations reaching $10.6 million. The company added a record 447 IDI customers in the quarter, including significant growth across four verticals while FOREWARN expanded into home healthcare with over 25,000 new users. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 'high 30s' following this exceptional performance.

negative_highlights: SG&A expenses increased to $41.2M due to employment costs and one-time restructuring charges related to the April efficiency initiative
Net loss widened slightly to $39.1M compared to $37.8M in Q1, though still better than prior year
positive_highlights: Q2 net revenue of $45.7M, representing substantial growth over the prior quarter and year-ago period
Gross margin expanded significantly to 55% from Q1's 6%, driven by volume increases at Nucleus facility
Full-year guidance raised to $140-$150 million based on strong H2 momentum
summary: Autolus reported Q2 FY26 net product revenue of $45.7 million, a significant increase from the prior quarter and year-ago period, driven by strong adoption in over 80 U.S. centers and early launch momentum in the UK. Management raised full-year guidance for AUCATZYL to $140-$150 million (from an original range of $120-$135 million) citing improved gross margins that expanded to 55% from Q1's 6%. The company also announced a new strategic financing with Perceptive Advisors providing up to $250 million in notes.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year due to the absence of robotic system deliveries in Q2.
Operating loss increased quarter-over-quarter despite sequential revenue growth, indicating high fixed cost burn during a transition period.
Catheter supply remains constrained by contract manufacturer output (Osypka AG), limiting ability to capture full demand and impacting near-term margins.
positive_highlights: Recurring revenue grew significantly to $6.2 million (up 70% sequentially), driven by the launch of MAGiC and a new portfolio of robotically navigated catheters.
Management expects recurring revenue gross margins to expand from current levels in Q2/Q3 toward mid-70s as manufacturing volumes ramp up.
GenesisX received its first U.S. purchase order from an academic medical center, demonstrating progress on compatibility with non-modified X-rays.
summary: Stereotaxis reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.7 million, a year-over-year decline due to the lack of robotic system deliveries but an increase sequentially from Q1 driven by catheter sales. Gross margin was 58%, with operating loss widening slightly to $4.6 million compared to $4.0 million in the prior year quarter. Management provided specific guidance for recurring revenue growth ($7M in Q3, $8M in Q4) and system revenue stabilization at approximately $3M per quarter in H2, while explicitly stating that full-year visibility is limited by supply constraints on catheters.

negative_highlights: Year-over-year revenue declined significantly from $4.1 million due to lower product and service sales.

Gross margin contracted sequentially by 130 bps (from implied higher levels) driven by the shift in mix toward services/consumables which have different margins, though absolute gross profit improved slightly or held steady relative to prior year context of instrument-heavy quarters; specifically noted as a decline from Q2 2025.
Management explicitly stated that caution among academic customers regarding grant funding delays is not expected to end by the balance of 2026.
positive_highlights: Revenue showed sequential growth from Q1 to Q2 ($3.1M vs $2.8M) indicating early recovery momentum.
New Chief Commercial Officer Tony Bazarko has already engaged with ~20% of North American customers and is refocusing the organization on large accounts.
SECURE-SG100K study completed 10,000 samples in May; preliminary data expected to drive future buyback commitments.
summary: Seer reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.1 million, a decrease from the prior year's $4.1 million and an increase sequentially from Q1's $2.8 million due to macroeconomic headwinds in academic funding and elongated sales cycles. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance range of $16-$18 million despite the challenging environment, citing positive trends in customer interest for H2 driven by new commercial leadership and upcoming data releases.

negative_highlights: June advertising yield was reduced by a shift in film slate composition toward R-rated titles and budget shifts for the FIFA World Cup.
Unlevered free cash flow turned negative at -$2.1 million due to one-time operational transformation costs.
Management paused dividend payments and share repurchase programs following the announcement of the acquisition.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 12.7% year-over-year to $58.4 million driven by a 19.3% increase in attendance.
Adjusted OIBDA improved significantly, reaching $2.1 million compared to the prior period.
Local advertising revenue surged 48.4% YoY to $9.5 million due to sales force rebuilding and premium inventory expansion.
summary: NCMI reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $58.4 million (up 12.7% YoY) and adjusted OIBDA of $2.1 million (a three-fold increase), with results falling within the company's guidance range despite June headwinds from film mix shifts and FIFA World Cup budget reallocation.
