Adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially from a Q1 loss of negative $0.4 million to positive $5.3 million, driven largely by the completion of a debt restructuring that generated a gain on debt of approximately $91.8 million and reduced interest expense.

negative_highlights: Inorganic revenue contribution is likely to be lower than the original $55M plan due to slower deal closing timelines in regulatory-heavy markets like Canada.
GAAP net loss widened slightly compared to Q2 FY25, though this was expected and driven by non-cash equity-based compensation of ~$48.2M.
Attrition rates increased modestly, with 70% occurring at lower performance ratings (1-3), which management views as a positive filter but indicates ongoing headcount challenges.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat guidance by approximately $12M-$17M with a total increase of 23.7% versus the prior period.
Organic revenue growth accelerated to 20.5%, significantly outpacing initial expectations and demonstrating strong underlying demand.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded materially, reflecting favorable operating leverage and reduced cost of services.
summary: The company reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $217.7 million, beating the prior guidance range of $190M-$205M by approximately 10% and exceeding expectations with a 23.7% year-over-year increase driven primarily by organic growth of 20.5%. Adjusted EBITDA came in at roughly $46 million (up ~55%), while management reaffirmed full-year FY26 revenue guidance of $980M-$1B despite acknowledging that the pace of M&A deal closures is slower than anticipated, resulting in lower-than-planned inorganic contribution. Management expressed strong confidence in organic momentum and pricing power but noted ongoing investments in Global Mobility and consulting which currently suppress margins.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $8.5 million due to a down pistachio crop (yields affected by heat/pollination issues) and higher property operating expenses.
Demand for fresh produce decreased following the Cyclospora outbreak, causing markets to soften across berries and leafy greens.
positive_highlights: Adjusted FFO improved to -$1.6 million from -$3.5 million year-over-year driven by higher cash rents and lower interest costs.
Almond prices reached $2.70/lb for the split in shell, significantly above projections, with initial 2026 pricing at $2.50/lb (two-thirds higher than last year).
Water allocation increased by 3% recently, which is expected to lower water deal pricing and reduce operating expenses heading into winter.
summary: The company reported a net loss of $8.5 million and an adjusted FFO loss of $1.6 million for the second quarter, representing significant improvement over last year's losses but still missing expectations for profitability. Management highlighted strong almond prices ($2.70/lb final pricing expected) which will drive revenue recognition in Q4 2026 following a down pistachio crop and disappointing water allocations that increased operating expenses.

negative_highlights: Free cash flow turned negative at -$7 million due to increased memory inventory buildup.
Days Inventory on Hand rose significantly from 80 days in Q1 to 95 days as the company front-runs supply for growth.
Gross margin guidance was lowered slightly (implied) or held steady at 51%-52% to account for elevated memory costs not expected to be passed through.
positive_highlights: Broadband revenue grew 54% year-over-year to $133.5 million, exceeding guidance by approximately $20M-$18.5M.
Rest-of-market bookings represented ~60% of total bookings in the quarter with a book-to-bill well over 1.5.
Full-year revenue guidance was raised from a midpoint of roughly $485 million to a new range of $505 million-$525 million.
summary: Harmonic reported Q2 FY26 broadband revenue of $133.5 million (up 54% YoY), significantly beating the high end of guidance ($115M-$125M) and EPS of $0.21, which beat the range of $0.15-$0.19. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a new range of $505 million to $525 million (up from prior $475M-$495M), citing record backlog and strong rest-of-market growth. The company completed its transformation into a pure-play broadband entity following the sale of its video business.

negative_highlights: Contribution ex-TAC declined in desktop (-13%) and non-programmatic business lines.
Softness observed within the travel vertical during Q2.
positive_highlights: Programmatic revenue hit a Q2 record at $95.2M, representing an 11-12% year-over-year increase driven by CTV ($37.8M) and mobile in-app (up 23%).
Full-year guidance was raised for the third time this year on contribution ex-TAC and programmatic revenue.
Enterprise spend increased over 25% YoY, with the number of advertisers activated growing from under 400 to over 750.
summary: Nexxen reported record Q2 results with programmatic revenue of $95.2 million (up 12% YoY) and contribution ex-TAC of $97.8 million (up 11% YoY). The company raised its full-year guidance for both contribution ex-TAC ($388M-$402M, up from prior midpoint) and programmatic revenue ($380M-$393M, up from prior midpoint), marking the first top-line guide raise of the year. Management highlighted record CTV revenue growth of 33% YoY to $37.8 million and strong enterprise spend increases.

negative_highlights: CEO explicitly stated they are not adjusting expectations for data availability, maintaining guidance despite accelerated site activation
Solid tumor program ALLO-316 faced real safety challenges and the team had to develop a management algorithm after toxicity emerged
ALPHA3 primary analysis requires overwhelming efficacy to achieve statistical significance at the interim EFS point

Enrollment accelerated to meet the goal of activating over 80 sites by year-end, now expecting approximately 100 active sites with a majority in the U.S.
ALPHA3 trial achieved rapid MRD clearance in a majority of patients with no treatment-related hospitalizations
summary: Allogene provided a business update for Q2 FY2026 focusing on clinical progress rather than financial results, highlighting the receipt of RMAT and Fast Track designations for cema-cel in first-line consolidation based on interim MRD data. The company reported accelerating enrollment to reach its goal of 100 active sites by year-end but maintained guidance that the primary EFS analysis will occur mid-2027 without raising expectations despite faster site activation.

negative_highlights: SG&A expenses were $10.9 million with no specific guidance raised despite strong top-line growth.
Qbrexza revenue was down slightly due to patient mix and payer deductible resets.
Eurax Cream is a new niche product launched late in the quarter with no established sales trajectory yet.
positive_highlights: Emrosi net product revenues reached $8.1 million in Q2, up significantly year-over-year.
Total prescriptions for Emrosi grew by approximately 20% sequentially to ~36,000 units.
The unique prescriber base expanded from 3,700 at end of Q1 to over 4,500 in Q2.
summary: Journey Medical reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $18.5 million, a 23% year-over-year increase driven by Emrosi net product revenues of $8.1 million and improved ASPs. The company achieved positive GAAP EBITDA ($1.4M) and adjusted EBITDA ($2.9M), narrowing its loss to $0.01 per share compared to a prior period loss of $3.8M. Management highlighted accelerating prescription growth for Emrosi (up 20% sequentially) but noted that SG&A expenses remained elevated due to launch-related spending and upcoming marketing programs, with no specific guidance raised.

negative_highlights: Q2 GAAP gross margin declined to 14.4% due to product mix shifts in South Korea operations rather than execution issues.
Smart eyewear revenue remains nominal with Q3 expected to be negative on margins as overheads are absorbed before scale is reached.
Revenue of $9 million was at the high end of guidance but did not explicitly beat consensus estimates mentioned by management.
positive_highlights: Smart eyewear entered commercial production with first product revenue and delivery orders for ~19,000 packs in Q3 (nine-fold increase from Q2).
Defense drone pipeline grew by 41% to $183 million, exceeding $100 million specifically on drones.
Smartphone qualification passed critical milestone with lead customer confirming >1,000 cycles under the new hybrid protocol.
summary: Enovix reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $9 million (up 21% YoY), which landed at the high end of guidance but missed analyst consensus expectations due to a lack of specific beat confirmation in the text. The company recorded its first smart eyewear product revenue and advanced smartphone qualification milestones, though gross margins were pressured by South Korea mix shifts resulting in GAAP margins of 14.4%. Management maintained Q3 revenue guidance between $9-10 million but did not raise it despite strong pipeline growth.

negative_highlights: Customer traffic declined 4.9% due to deferrals among value-seeking consumers following an e-commerce re-platform that impacted sales by approximately 150 basis points.
Full-year comparable store sales guidance was narrowed at the top end (by about 1%) reflecting a more measured view on when lower-value customers will return.
Inventory increased approximately 37% year-over-date to support segmentation strategy, creating potential working capital pressure if note-through slows.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 6.3% driven by higher value customer mix and product attachment.
Average ticket increased 7.1%, offsetting a 4.9% decline in traffic, with strong performance from premium lenses like Nikon Eyes.
Management raised the full-year adjusted operating income outlook despite narrowing top-line revenue expectations.
summary: Net revenue grew 2.5% to $499 million while adjusted comparable store sales increased 2.2%, driven by a 7.1% average ticket expansion that offset a 4.9% decline in traffic. Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 6.3% and adjusted EPS rose to $0.25 per share, though management narrowed the full-year top-line guidance range due to persistent deferrals from lower-value transactions following an e-commerce re-platform.

negative_highlights: Net sales declined 4% YoY, including approximately 220 bps of impact from the store closure program.
EMEA region faced headwinds due to geopolitical climate in the Middle East impacting travel retail.
Full-year guidance still anticipates a top-line decline rather than growth.
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating income doubled year-over-year, reaching $9 million ($8.6m constant currency).
Traditional watch business delivered impressive global wholesale growth of 12%.
Americas region stabilized with mid-single digit U.S. growth and Asia grew 4% led by double-digit India performance.

The company highlighted an increase in annual recurring revenue (ARR) by $7 million and noted that roughly 80% of total revenue is now recurring or highly recurring.

Cost of risk normalized to 2.1%, remaining well below the company's risk appetite despite portfolio growth.

summary: Coherent reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $2.05 billion (up 34% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 (up 74% YoY), driven by exceptional demand in data center transceivers, OCS, and CPO ramping ahead of schedule. Net income rose 23.4% year-over-year to $162.3 million driven by strong gross profit and mix
summary: PFG reported Q4 FY26 net sales growth of 6.4% and adjusted EBITDA increasing 7.4%, with full-year revenue up nearly 9%. Hyperscaler revenue projected to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027, up from less than 2% of total revenue in FY25.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $62.4 million (a margin of ~21%), representing a more than 300 bps expansion compared to Q2 FY25.

Alcohol category faces macro pressure despite the success of specific promotions like Margarita of the Month.

While Chili's delivered strong same-store sales growth driven by traffic and price, Maggiano's reported comp sales declines of -5.3% with flat profit assumptions built into next year.

Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance ($42M-$46M) despite a negative EBITDA quarter due to ongoing construction costs.

Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at approximately -$0.9 million for the quarter but is expected to turn positive upon opening of Bradley and Addison Phase II later this year. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance with an annualized revenue run rate between $42M-$46M and adjusted EBITDA between $4M-$6M.

Management raised full-year guidance expectations for sequential revenue growth in both Q3 (guidance $8.3M-$9.0M) and Q4 (guidance $8.75M-$9.25M).

summary: Hyperion DeFi reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted gross profit of $1.2 million (up 20% q/q) and net income of $31.0 million driven by a $54.8M unrealized gain on HYPE treasury, though this masks an operating decline in the 'DeFi monetization' segment which fell 36% to $158k due to USDH stablecoin wind-downs. Management highlighted the successful launch and adoption of EVO+ in China as well as back-to-back record quarters in the U.S., though they declined to provide specific numerical guidance for Q3 or full-year targets.

summary: Anterix reported Q1 FY2027 GAAP revenue of $2 million and operating expenses of $9.5 million, including an approximately $11 million gain from broadband license exchanges that significantly improved the income statement. Management highlighted a strong balance sheet with no debt and cash reserves exceeding $116 million while noting active engagement on nearly a dozen utility spectrum opportunities. The company reiterated it does not provide formal financial guidance but expects single-digit million gains in subsequent quarters.

negative_highlights: Field Systems ARR growth guidance lowered to high single digits due to a discrete decision to replace a low-margin white-label product with an internal solution.
Management confirmed they are undertaking a strategic review of the Transportation and Logistics business following credible inbound interest from multiple parties.

Trimble Connect added over one million projects in Q2 alone with nearly 30 billion API calls.

The company announced a new $1 billion share repurchase authorization while undertaking a strategic review of its Transportation business amid inbound interest.

Management raised full-year GMS guidance to $10.1-$10.3 billion (representing 10-12% growth) from the prior outlook of 8-10%, maintaining EBITDA guidance at $400-$420 million.

negative_highlights: Core gross margin declined sequentially from Q1's 46.5% to 40.6% due to higher costs associated with renting systems for private cloud demand.

summary: Cerebras Systems reported Q2 FY26 core revenue of $209.9 million (up 103% YoY) and record gross margins at 40.6%, beating guidance on all metrics despite a sequential margin dip due to temporary rented capacity costs for OpenAI ramp-up. Management raised full-year 2026 core revenue guidance to the range of $880-$890 million, along with adjusted gross and operating margin targets. The company highlighted significant progress in securing over 600 MW of data center capacity by end-2027 and expanding manufacturing capabilities.

negative_highlights: Unfavorable win rate at City of Dreams Macau negatively impacted property EBITDA by approximately $9 million.
VIP win rate declined significantly from a prior year norm, dropping to 2.7% in Q2 FY26 compared to 3.4%-3.7% previously.

positive_highlights: H1 GAAP gross margin reached a historic high of 31% driven by favorable product mix toward higher-margin Hubs and powertrains.
Non-GAAP operating loss for the first half narrowed to $8.8 million from $14.9 million in the prior year period, demonstrating operational leverage.
Cash position strengthened with cash on hand rising 35% quarter-over-quarter following capital raises.
summary: Xos reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.7 million on 30 units delivered, a decline from the prior year quarter due to order deferrals and customer acceptance delays. GAAP gross margin was 12.1% for the quarter but improved significantly in H1 with a record 31%, while operating loss narrowed sequentially despite lower volumes. Management revised full-year guidance downward, projecting revenue between $35 million and $43 million.

negative_highlights: Take rate came in at 3.6% (low end of guidance) due to higher interest rates reducing gain on sale and faster-than-anticipated migration of large partners directly to lower-take-rate Figure Connect.
First lien volume grew 3x year-over-year, which typically carries a lower take rate than HELOCs, creating a modest structural headwind for the metric.
positive_highlights: Consumer loan marketplace volume surged to $4.3 billion, up 132% year-over-year, beating the top end of prior guidance by 4%.
Figure Connect adoption accelerated significantly, growing from 56% share last quarter to 65% this quarter as partners migrate directly to the capital-light platform.
Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 55%, reflecting strong operating leverage and a shift toward fee-based economics with ecosystem fees now being the largest revenue contributor.
summary: Figure reported Q2 FY26 consumer loan marketplace volume of $4.3 billion (up 132% YoY), beating the top end of guidance by 4%. Adjusted net revenue reached $218 million with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 55%, driven largely by Figure Connect now representing 65% of total volume and ecosystem fees becoming the largest P&L line item. Management raised Q3 volume guidance expectations, citing strong July performance ($1.7B) and a confident outlook for August/September.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $4.1 million, though improved YoY
No repurchases made under the authorized share buyback program due to blackout period
EMJX figures are hypothetical model results and do not represent actual trading returns yet
positive_highlights: Net sales increased 27% year-over-year to $3.4 million
Supply chain fill rate recovery reached 98%
New-to-brand consumers for Halo increased 13% year-over-year
summary: Net sales for the fiscal third quarter totaled $3.4 million, representing a 27% year-over-year increase driven by Halo's operational improvements and supply chain recovery reaching 98%. GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $4.1 million, an improvement of 40% year-over-year to a smaller absolute loss compared to the prior period. Management highlighted a debt-free balance sheet with no repurchases made under the newly authorized program due to blackout periods.

negative_highlights: Revenue was not recognized for two treatments due to one low-yield batch and one out-of-specification batch.
Two scheduled biopsies were cancelled last-minute in Q2 due to patient health deterioration.
Manufacturing yields remain variable with a rare event of an out-of-spec test failure requiring FDA specification review.
positive_highlights: Net revenue increased 31% QoQ to $11.4 million driven by five treated patients.
Expanded qualified treatment center (QTC) network now includes seven activated centers nationwide with CHOP completing its first treatment shortly after activation in May.
Achieved CMS New Technology Add-on Payment (NTAP) status effective October 2026, providing supplemental reimbursement for Medicare beneficiaries.
summary: Abeona Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue of $11.4 million, a 31% quarter-over-quarter increase driven by five patient treatments, though one low-yield batch and one out-of-specification batch resulted in no revenue recognition for those specific cases despite patients receiving treatment. R&D expenses decreased to $5 million from Q1's $9.6 million due to the exclusion of a one-time licensing cost incurred earlier in the year. Management highlighted operational bottlenecks including scheduling disruptions, patient health deterioration leading to cancellations, and manufacturing yield variability as key headwinds.

negative_highlights: Total revenues declined 2.9% YoY, with electronics and home appliances revenue moderated by a high trading base and upstream price increases.
General merchandise growth was impacted by the same high comparison base effects seen in other categories during Q2.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP net income surged 20.8% YoY to RMB 8.9 billion driven by robust profitability and loss reduction in new businesses.
JD Retail gross margin expanded 130 bps YoY to a record high of 18.5%, marking the 17th consecutive quarter of expansion.
JD Food Delivery narrowed total losses by over 50% YoY while maintaining healthy order volume momentum.
summary: JD.com reported Q2 FY26 total revenues of RMB 346 billion, a slight year-on-year decline of 2.9% due to high comparison bases in electronics and home appliances. Non-GAAP net income surged by 20.8% YoY to RMB 8.9 billion as JD Retail gross margin expanded to 18.5% and JD Food Delivery losses narrowed significantly. Management raised the outlook for H2, expecting top-line growth re-acceleration in electronics/home appliances once base effects normalize.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened from income in prior year due to structural margin compression and legal provisions.
Net other loss of $230.8 million caused fair value volatility on Arashi Vision Inc., wiping out core business profitability.
No specific full-year guidance provided despite strong top-line growth.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 38.9% YoY to $102.7M driven by strong overseas audio live streaming growth of 54.8%.
summary: Xunlei reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $102.7 million, up 38.9% year-over-year, driven by a 22.6% increase in subscription services and a 54.8% surge in overseas audio live streaming. However, the company posted an operating loss of $4.8 million due to higher costs associated with revenue mix shifts (lower-margin live streaming) and legal provisions, resulting in a net other loss of $230.8 million primarily from fair value volatility on investments. Management announced a new $20 million share repurchase program initiated July 1st but provided no specific guidance for the full year.

negative_highlights: Proteus launch delayed by approximately six months from late 2026 to Q2 FY2027 due to manufacturing repeatability concerns.
Revenue declined significantly year-over-year, dropping $591k in the prior period to just $344k this quarter.
Company is executing a reduction in force representing approximately 20% of total headcount.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed significantly to $23.5 million compared to a net loss of $28.8 million in the prior year quarter.
Adjusted operating expenses decreased sequentially and YoY, with GAAP OpEx falling from $30.5M to $25.8M due to cost actions.
Management confirmed sufficient capital runway extending into Q4 2028 following the reduction in force.
summary: QSI reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $344,000 (down from $591,000 in the prior year) and a net loss of $23.5 million, while maintaining full-year guidance for approximately $1M revenue despite announcing significant cost-cutting measures including a 20% reduction in force. Management delayed the Proteus launch timeline to Q2 FY2027 from late 2026 following internal testing that revealed manufacturing repeatability risks requiring an additional design cycle before production.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide formal financial guidance for the upcoming quarter citing macro uncertainty.
Total operating expenses increased year-over-year by approximately 26% due to stock-based compensation and commissions, despite sequential improvement.
The proposed merger with TYTL Corp remains non-binding and subject to shareholder approval, a fairness opinion, and valuation analysis.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 57% year-over-year driven by a strategic shift toward higher-margin non-QM products like bank statement loans.
July operating margins reached the highest level in company history, reflecting improved product mix and cost discipline.
Sequential cash burn decreased to $1.7 million from Q1 levels as working capital timing normalized.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue increased 57% year-over-year to $2.6 million while net loss declined by 24% from the prior quarter and cash burn decreased to $1.7 million. Management highlighted a shift toward higher-margin non-QM products, resulting in July margins reaching company records and sequential improvements across operating expenses and adjusted EBITDA. However, management explicitly stated they are not providing formal financial guidance for Q3 due to market uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Engineering and design revenues declined 4%, primarily due to soft demand in sustainability consulting for mixed-use clients.
Consolidated gross margin was impacted by a revenue mix shift toward lower-margin installation services following the Bowers acquisition.
Sustainability consulting business experienced softer market conditions reflecting broader commercial real estate challenges.
positive_highlights: Organic revenue growth was nearly 60%, with total revenue more than doubling when including acquisitions.
Full-year 2026 guidance raised significantly on both top-line ($4.7B-$4.8B) and bottom-line (~$565M-$585M).
Backlog reached a record $5.7 billion, up 105% year-over-year.
summary: Legence reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.3 billion (up 111% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA growth of 114%, driven by organic expansion in data centers/technology and the Bowers acquisition. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for both revenue ($4.7B-$4.8B, up ~13%) and adjusted EBITDA (~$565M-$585M, up ~20%), citing strong backlog growth of $5.7 billion (up 105% YoY) and accelerating project execution speeds.

negative_highlights: Consolidated revenue declined year-over-year, with the GEO segment down 26% due to non-renewals and lower capacity renewals.
Two legacy satellites (Anik F4 and Telstar 14R) were retired during the quarter, creating a headwind for cash flow visibility.
Net loss widened significantly to CAD 559 million compared to prior periods.
positive_highlights: Secured the first contract in the ESCP-P program, adding significant backlog and funding for Lightspeed acceleration.
GEO segment backlog increased to CAD 900 million due to a five-year extension of a broadcast video contract.
FCC report confirmed eligibility for $189 million in incentive payments related to C-band spectrum repurposing.
summary: Telesat reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of CAD 79 million and a net loss of CAD 559 million, driven by lower GEO segment revenue (down 26% YoY) due to contract expirations and satellite retirements. Management reiterated its guidance for the legacy GEO business but raised full-year investment guidance for Lightspeed from CAD 1-1.2 billion to CAD 1.3-1.5 billion following a decision to accelerate constellation expansion to 225 satellites funded by new government contracts.

negative_highlights: Inflation proved more persistent than anticipated at over 32%, impacting macroeconomic conditions and FX dynamics.
Net income was impacted by increased depreciation associated with the commercial launch of 5G assets.
Paycell margins faced volatility due to erosive POS transaction profitability, though total revenue grew 22%.
positive_highlights: Group revenue achieved genuine real growth of 2.5% YoY in an environment where inflation exceeded 30%.
Digital Business Services delivered outstanding performance with revenue up 33% to TRY 8.7 billion, supported by a system integration backlog of TRY 16 billion.
Turkcell crossed the historic milestone of 40 million mobile subscribers for the first time in company history.
summary: Turkcell reported Q2 FY2026 group revenue of TRY 71.8 billion (up 2.5% YoY) and net income of TRY 5.2 billion, driven by real growth despite inflation exceeding 30%. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged after revising year-end inflation expectations to around 28%, citing disciplined pricing and strong momentum in Digital Business Services (+33%) and FWA (+64k subscribers). The company crossed the 40 million mobile subscriber milestone with a postpaid base of 32.5 million, while EBITDA margin remained steady at 41.8%.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide quantitative guidance on YUVIWEL patient starts or sales ranges, citing insufficient time in market for analytical trends.
SG&A expenses increased significantly from EUR 145 million in Q1 to EUR 173 million in Q2 due to investments accelerating global launches.
positive_highlights: Total product revenue more than doubled year-over-year, with YORVIPATH reaching blockbuster status on a run-rate basis in its second launch year.
YUVIWEL enrollment accelerated rapidly to over 220 unique patients by end of July, capturing >65% reimbursement approval rate and demonstrating strong market expansion beyond switches.
COACH trial data showed unprecedented arm span improvements (+9.4 cm) with combination therapy compared to limb lengthening surgery.
summary: Ascendis Pharma reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of EUR 339 million (up from EUR 145m in the prior quarter), driven by YORVIPATH sales of EUR 252 million and SKYTROFA at EUR 55 million. The company achieved a significant non-product milestone gain of EUR 17 million related to TransCon CNP, resulting in net profit of EUR 207 million. Management raised full-year cash flow guidance expectations from greater than EUR 300m (implied prior) to greater than EUR 500 million for the remainder of 2026.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses rose sequentially to $806 million as timing effects reversed from Q1 and international expansion investments accelerated.
Overall NPLs deteriorated slightly by 40 basis points due to portfolio mix shifts rather than fundamental credit quality issues in core segments.
positive_highlights: Net income reached a milestone $1.1 billion, up 49% year-over-year and marking the first time exceeding $1B.
Risk-adjusted net interest margin expanded to a record 12.4%, driven by lending growth and disciplined risk expansion rather than portfolio deterioration.
Mexico banking license approved with deposits at $5.7 billion, demonstrating successful transformation into a full-scale digital bank.
summary: Nu Holdings reported a historic quarter with net income exceeding $1 billion for the first time ($1.1B), driven by gross revenue of nearly $5.9 billion and record risk-adjusted NIM expanding to 12.4%. The company achieved this while maintaining an efficiency ratio near its long-term target of 20% despite sequential operating expense increases due to international expansion investments.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined year-over-year due to the end of Menarini's reimbursement ($6.5M impact)
Phase III XPORT-EC-042 study failed to achieve statistical significance in endometrial cancer, leading to a strategic pivot away from that program
Cash runway extends only to September 2026 without additional financing or lender waivers
positive_highlights: U.S. XPOVIO net product revenue of $30.8M showed consistent underlying demand despite competition
Strong clinical momentum for selinexor in myelofibrosis with FDA feedback supporting SVR35 as a surrogate endpoint
Planned sNDA submission remains on track for August 2026
summary: Karyopharm reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $33.4 million (down from $37.9M prior year) and a net loss of $67 million due to the conclusion of Menarini's reimbursement, though underlying operating performance improved with disciplined expense reductions. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for total revenue between $130-$150 million but highlighted an urgent liquidity constraint requiring financing or strategic alternatives by September 10th to avoid a default on their term loan.

negative_highlights: Total Q2 revenue declined 5% year-over-year as a $10M drop in SEO revenue offset data growth.
Marketing revenue fell 10% to $26.5 million due to declines in both international markets and organic search channels.
Full-year guidance implies only low-single-digit growth, suggesting the business has not yet recovered its prior high-growth trajectory.
positive_highlights: Data services revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $11.2M driven by enterprise subs and B2B OpticOdds solutions.
Adjusted free cash flow of $9.6 million was generated, with a strong conversion rate of 81% in the quarter.
Non-SEO marketing revenue now accounts for 67% of total marketing business, diversifying away from organic search.
summary: Grandstand reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $37.8 million and adjusted EBITDA of $7.7 million, both in line with expectations but representing a 5% year-over-year decline due to lower marketing revenue offsetting strong data growth ($11.2M). The company reiterated full-year guidance for revenue between $165-$170 million and adjusted EBITDA between $45-$50 million, noting that the current run rate implies modest flat-to-low-single-digit annual growth rather than a significant beat or raise.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin contracted 130 bps year-over-year due to a combined 280 bps drag from FX and U.S. tariffs.
Net leverage increased to 1.8x following the accelerated share repurchase (ASR) and debt refinancing activities.
Middle East conflicts continue to impact demand in key markets like the UAE, though mitigated by strength elsewhere.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 15% in constant currency, hitting the high end of guidance with double-digit growth across Americas (14%), EMEA (15%), and APAC (23%).
D2C channel accelerated to 16% growth while retail revenue surged 50%, driven by new store openings.
Full price realization remained strong at 93% in Europe, demonstrating brand resilience against promotional pressure.
summary: Birkenstock reported Q3 FY26 revenue of EUR 720 million (up 15% in constant currency) and adjusted EBITDA of EUR 242 million. Management raised full-year guidance for revenue growth to the high end of its range at 15% and increased the minimum adjusted EBITDA target to at least EUR 710 million, citing strong momentum across all regions despite FX headwinds and tariffs.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses increased by $0.9 million YoY due to investments in clinical development for PTSD and alcohol use disorder research.
G&A expenses rose approximately $0.7 million driven by higher professional fees and administrative costs.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 35% YoY to $17.1 million driven by a 42% increase in system shipments (125 units).
Operating income surged over 300% year-over-year, marking the 12th consecutive quarter of profitability.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded significantly from 11% to 20%, reflecting strong operating leverage.
summary: BrainsWay reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $17.1 million (up 35% YoY) and operating income increasing over 300% to $2.4 million. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance from a range of $66M-$68M to $68M-$70M, citing strong demand for the SWIFT protocol and growing remaining performance obligations of $80.4 million.

negative_highlights: NAND growth is expected to be slower next year as the market focuses primarily on upgrades rather than wafer capacity additions.
Q1 FY27 will be a 14-week quarter, which may result in higher-than-average step-up in operating expenses compared to standard quarters.
positive_highlights: Record Q3 revenue of $9.1 billion driven by double-digit sequential growth across all segments.
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to a record 50.4% (up 40 bps sequentially) and operating margin hit a record 34%.
DRAM revenue grew 52% YoY, while Applied Global Services delivered record $1.8 billion in revenue.
summary: Applied Materials reported record Q3 FY26 revenue of $9.1 billion (up 15% sequentially and 25% YoY) with non-GAAP EPS of $3.50 (up 41% YoY). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance, citing strengthened demand visibility from customers providing eight-quarter rolling forecasts through to 2030. The company expects particularly strong growth in DRAM and leading-edge foundry logic for the second half of calendar 2027.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of approximately $51 million as the company front-loaded investments in operating expenses.
Cash operating expenses were elevated at ~$93 million due to integration costs and growth investments, though management expects moderation later in the year.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $83.8 million representing more than 13-fold growth versus the prior year period.
Pro forma organic revenue grew approximately 85% year-over-year, validating underlying business execution beyond acquisition impacts.
Backlog increased approximately 33% sequentially to roughly $757 million with a two-year strategic pipeline exceeding $1.4 billion.
summary: Ondas reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $83.8 million (up >13x YoY) and adjusted gross margin stable at 50.4%. Management raised the full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $525-$550 million, citing strong organic growth drivers including Sentrycs (+298% pro forma), Airobotics (+112%), and 4M (+258%). The company ended with approximately $1.4 billion in cash equivalents after deploying capital for new acquisitions.

negative_highlights: Public sector revenue declined YoY due to temporary budgetary shifts in late Q2 driven by conflict spending priorities.
VDR deal timing remains uncertain, causing some large hyperscaler transactions to be under active review rather than fully processed.
Fiscal 2026 guidance was lowered from prior expectations with a new range of $100-$150 million.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew sequentially by 20% to $24.3M driven by VDR and licensing services which were up 40% QoQ.
Executed approximately $11.3 million in annualized cost reductions, with a target of reaching $15-$20 million total savings by end of FY26.
Secured major public sector wins including multi-year renewals with the Pac-12 Conference and CHP for document redaction.
summary: Veritone reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $24.3 million (up 20% sequentially and 5% YoY), but missed expectations due to delayed public sector budget shifts related to the conflict in Iran and timing issues with hyperscaler VDR deals. Management lowered fiscal 2026 full-year guidance to a range of $100-$150 million, citing reduced visibility on government contracts and specific VDR deal closures. The company executed significant cost reductions totaling approximately $11.3 million annually as of June 30, positioning for potential breakeven in the first half of fiscal 2027.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue growth implies ~28% in H2 against an exceptionally strong prior year of ~36%, indicating a conservative outlook.
Rental segment margins faced an approximate 50 basis point headwind from increased fuel costs, though partially offset by pricing power.
positive_highlights: Rental segment revenue surged >39% YoY driven by fleet absorption ahead of plan on large-scale mega projects.
Adjusted core EBITDA reached $531 million, reflecting a robust margin mix between rental and sales segments.
Management raised OWN program contribution guidance for the full year by approximately $11M due to strong institutional demand.
summary: EquipmentShare reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.4 billion (up 26% YoY) and rental segment revenue of $908 million (up >39% YoY). Adjusted core EBITDA grew to $531 million, representing a beat on the prior period's implied growth trajectory despite management noting that full-year guidance remains conservative for the back half. Management raised specific OWN program contribution guidance by approximately $11M and highlighted strong demand visibility in mega projects.

negative_highlights: Telco core income declined 2% YoY to PHP 16.6 billion, primarily due to a 6% increase in depreciation and amortization.
Home revenues dropped 1% to PHP 30 billion as the business continues to lag from Q1 installation constraints carried into H1.
Maya's contribution to core income was lower than expected for the quarter due to one-time accounting adjustments, though underlying growth remains strong.
positive_highlights: Enterprise revenues grew 5% to PHP 24.8 billion, driven by ICT revenue expansion of 22%.
Wireless top-ups turned positive in June (+1%) and improved further in July (+3%), indicating a recovery trend after Q1 constraints.
Home fiber net adds accelerated significantly in the second quarter with postpaid churn improving to 1.4%.
summary: PLDT reported first-half FY26 service revenues of PHP 108.7 billion (up 2% YoY) and EBITDA of PHP 56.1 billion at a stable 52% margin, though Telco core income declined 2% to PHP 16.6 billion due to higher depreciation. Wireless revenue was broadly flat while Home revenues fell 1% following Q1 installation constraints that are now recovering in the second quarter with positive net adds starting in May. Enterprise remained a strong growth driver up 5%, and management reiterated full-year CapEx guidance of mid-PHP 50 billion despite elevated depreciation from network upgrades.

negative_highlights: Consolidated net loss widened year-over-year from $3.9M to $4.3M driven by increased costs for Coosa permitting, stock-based compensation, and product development.
Graphite flake input prices remain at historic lows ($500-$600/ton), which management notes is suboptimal compared to the higher price environment desired when Coosa comes online in 2028-2029.
positive_highlights: Received formal EXIM approval for a $25 million loan to support Kellyton Phase I development, representing non-dilutive capital with single-digit cost of capital expectations versus mid-teens private market rates.
summary: Westwater Resources reported a Q2 FY2026 consolidated net loss of $4.3 million ($0.03/share), an increase from the prior year's loss of $3.9 million due to higher permitting costs, stock-based compensation, and product development expenses. The company received a significant non-dilutive milestone in the form of a formal EXIM approval for a $25 million loan dedicated exclusively to advancing Phase I construction at the Kellyton Graphite Plant. Management maintains a target timeline for commercial production starting as soon as next year (late 2026/early 2027), contingent on securing remaining capital and closing documentation.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased significantly by 46% YoY due to higher court costs and stock-based compensation from the IPO.
Management explicitly stated they do not provide guidance on deployments or earnings, limiting forward visibility.
Cash efficiency ratio excluding Bluestem/Conn's portfolios was lower at 67.8%, reflecting one-time portfolio impacts.
positive_highlights: Record deployments in July of $185 million across the spectrum including new auto finance portfolios.
Strong growth in legal channel collections, up 54% YoY to $64 million.
Forward flow commitments reached a record $480.7 million as of June 30th.
summary: Jefferson Capital reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $178 million (up 16% YoY) and collections of $301 million (up 18% YoY), driven by strong deployments including a record July figure. Adjusted EPS was $0.77, with cash efficiency at 72.2%. The company raised its estimated remaining collections to $3.4 billion (+18%) but did not provide specific forward guidance for revenue or earnings.

negative_highlights: Revenue from Remini declined, attributed partly to market saturation rather than AI disruption.
Splice revenue also contributed negatively to the overall portfolio growth rate.
Organic growth of 3% was lower than Q1's 6%, reflecting a blended impact from low single-digit growth in newer acquisitions like AOL and Vimeo.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 126% YoY with organic revenue growth of 3%, exceeding internal expectations.
AOL Advertising performance was better than anticipated following price experiments and infrastructure upgrades.
Management successfully closed the acquisition of Tractive ($759M EV) and reached an agreement to acquire Airtable for $1.29 billion.
summary: Bending Spoons reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $704 million (up 126% YoY) and adjusted operating income of $381 million (up 150%), driven by strong performance in AOL Advertising, WeTransfer, and Tractive. Management provided full-year guidance for revenue between $2.78 billion-$2.82 billion and adjusted operating income between $1.46 billion-$1.51 billion, which excludes the pending Airtable acquisition expected to close later this year.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened significantly to $78.9 million compared to a prior year loss of $45.3 million.
SG&A expenses surged by $27.4 million quarter-over-quarter, primarily due to hiring for the commercial function and pre-launch activities.
No revenue reported in Q2 as product shipments are not expected until late third quarter 2026.
positive_highlights: FDA approved REVTORPYK for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without PIK3CA mutation following progression on endocrine therapy.
NCCN updated guidelines recommending gedatolisib regimens as preferred Category 1 options in the second-line setting.
Positive efficacy data from VIKTORIA-1 showed median PFS of 11.1 months for the triplet regimen versus 5.6 months with alpelisib.
summary: Celcuity reported a Q2 FY2026 net loss of $78.9 million ($1.44/share) and an adjusted net loss of $58.7 million ($1.07/share), representing significant year-over-year deterioration in profitability driven by a $35 million increase in SG&A expenses to support commercial launch preparations. While the company achieved major regulatory milestones including FDA approval for REVTORPYK (gedatolisib) and positive Phase III data, it has not yet generated any revenue from product sales as shipments are expected only late in Q3 2026.

negative_highlights: Total revenue fell 20% due to a significant pullback in procurement services, which dropped 45% compared to the prior-year quarter.
Net income per diluted share decreased from $0.06 to $0.05 primarily because of higher tax expenses following the full release of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets.
Systems integration revenue was slightly below recent quarterly averages, with management noting a downturn in mainstream business demand.
positive_highlights: Systems integration revenue increased 46% year-over-year to $13.9 million as the business mix shifts toward higher-margin offerings.
Facilities management revenue surged 84% to $2.7 million, offsetting declines in maintenance agreements with discrete project work.
Blended gross margin expanded significantly from 16.4% last year to 22.8%, reflecting the structural improvement in earnings quality.
summary: Total revenue declined 20% year-over-year to $35.1 million due to a sharp drop in procurement services ($18.2M vs $33M prior year), though higher-margin systems integration grew 46%. Gross profit increased 11% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 12%, driven by the shift toward high-margin segments, but net income fell slightly to $0.05 per share due to a one-time tax valuation allowance release in Q4 FY2025 affecting comparability.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated they are not reaffirming prior revenue guidance and declined to provide specific numbers due to deployment timing uncertainty.
Operating loss widened significantly in Q2 compared to the same period last year as expenses rose sharply ahead of commercialization.
Sequential gross margin contracted from 48% in Q1 to approximately 28% in Q2, attributed to product mix and pre-revenue engineering investments.
positive_highlights: Sequential revenue growth accelerated by approximately 51%, reaching $8.1 million.
Gross margin expanded significantly year-over-year from roughly 7.8% to 27.9% due to a shift away from lower-margin acquired product sales.
Series A rights exercise generated net proceeds of approximately $20.12 million, strengthening the balance sheet for larger customer engagements.
summary: AmpliTech Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $8.1 million (up 51% sequentially but down year-over-year) and a net loss of roughly $3.09 million driven by elevated investments in R&D, marketing, supply chain readiness, and cybersecurity to support larger customers. Gross margin improved significantly from the prior year period due to product mix changes following an asset acquisition, rising from 7.8% YoY but declining sequentially from Q1's 48%. Management explicitly declined to reaffirm or provide specific revenue guidance for the remainder of FY2026, citing timing uncertainties in large telecom deployments.

negative_highlights: Retail revenue declined approximately 2% year-over-year due to consumer sentiment issues
Automotive scanning volumes are trending lower, though a reversal is anticipated
Full-year FY2026 total revenue expected to be slightly lower than FY2025 if the customer's vendor review plan proceeds
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 7% sequentially to $5.9 million despite macro headwinds
Adjusted EBITDA remained positive for the fifth consecutive quarter at $1.1 million
Major customer volume reduction fears have not materialized as expected; new purchase order signed
summary: Q2 FY26 revenue was $5.9 million (up 16% YoY), with gross margin at 91%, adjusted EBITDA of $1.1M, and net income of $633k. Management noted that a major customer's vendor review is not yet causing the volume reductions previously feared, though full-year revenue for FY2026 may be slightly lower than FY2025 if plans proceed as communicated. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with $11.8M in cash and no debt.

negative_highlights: Pulp sales volumes were lower compared to Q2 FY25 due to concentrated maintenance downtimes at Pine Bluff and Três Lagoas mills.
EBITDA from Brazilian operations declined 20% year-over-year driven by lower prices, export volume contraction, and unfavorable FX effects.
positive_highlights: Free cash flow remained strong despite volatile geopolitical conditions.
summary: Suzano reported Q2 FY26 results with solid free cash flow and the successful closing of the Arbex acquisition on July 1st, though paperboard volumes were impacted by customer inventory build-up ahead of price increases. Pulp sales reached 2.9 million tons driven by higher export prices to $601/ton despite constrained production from maintenance downtimes in Pine Bluff and Três Lagoas. Management reiterated a focus on deleveraging the business following Arbex consolidation, with cash costs expected to decline below BRL 800/ton in H2 due to reduced downtime and wood consumption.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened due to an incremental operating loss of $1.4M and unfavorable FX impact of $400k, alongside non-cash warrant charges
Discontinued operations revenue declined 34% year-over-year as the company winds down ESWL and distribution businesses
positive_highlights: HIFU capital system sales reached an all-time high of 13 units globally with U.S. volumes growing 47% year-over-year
Gross margin expanded significantly to 55.6%, up from 51.1% in the prior period, driven by pricing and cost reductions
Management secured a $40 million equity offering to fortify balance sheet for growth initiatives
summary: FocalTherics reported Q2 FY26 HIFU revenue of $13.2 million, a 39% year-over-year increase driven by 13 capital system sales and strong procedure volume growth in the U.S. Gross margin expanded to 55.6%, while operating expenses rose due to strategic investments and non-cash warrant charges.
