summary: Lucid Diagnostics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.5 million (up ~17% sequentially) on a test volume of 2,770 units that remained within the targeted range but did not beat prior quarter levels due to pending Medicare reimbursement status. Management highlighted significant progress in commercial coverage with Concert and VA contracting milestones while noting cash burn remains elevated at $11.3 million per quarter as they build infrastructure ahead of expected Medicare approval.

negative_highlights: Management stated they are being patient on pension pricing in the U.K. because current bid values drive returns below their comfort level.
The Just Group business is still undergoing integration, with a focus on reducing costs and exiting early-stage initiatives to improve its cost structure.
positive_highlights: Distributable earnings per share increased 15% year-over-year driven by a record $77 billion of fundraising and strong organic inflows.
Net rents on new leases were significantly higher than expiring levels, with U.S. signings at 25% above expiration and Canadian signings over 70% above expiration.
Completed the acquisition of Oaktree to create one of the most comprehensive credit businesses globally.
summary: Distributable earnings before realizations increased 15% year-over-year to $1.4 billion in the quarter ($0.61 per share), while total distributable earnings including realizations reached $1.5 billion or $0.66 per share. The company reported record fundraising of $77 billion and completed strategic initiatives including the acquisitions of Oaktree and Just Group, alongside a simplification transaction approved by shareholders. Management highlighted strong leasing momentum with net rents 25% above expiring levels in the U.S., though they noted patience on pension pricing due to current market rates.

negative_highlights: ARR missed bottom-end guidance due to four large transactions slipping beyond anticipated timelines related to foreign entity status procurement requirements
Insysets conversion ARR uplift was lower than expected, particularly in U.S. state and local government where growth dropped below the mid-20% range seen last year
Full-year revenue outlook lowered from $561M-$573M (implied prior) to a new range of $555 million-$561 million
positive_highlights: Defense and intelligence ARR grew 25% driven by strong platform adoption
Genesis launched late in Q2 generated over $400k in new ARR with early signs of product-market fit across international policing, state AGs, and enterprise sectors
Gross revenue retention rate continued to climb in the first half as customers convert to Inseyets
summary: Cellebrite reported Q2 FY26 ARR of $508 million (up 21%) and revenue of $131 million (up 16%), but missed the bottom end of guidance due to delayed large transactions involving cloud/AI procurement requirements. Management lowered full-year ARR guidance by approximately $15 million at the midpoint, citing moderation in Insights conversions and elongated sales cycles for federal deals requiring new permits like FEPs. Conversely, adjusted EBITDA targets were raised to reflect continued cost discipline despite lower revenue expectations.

negative_highlights: Same center occupancy declined significantly by 240 basis points to 68.6%, primarily due to lower enrollment and consolidation impacts
Full-year revenue guidance was lowered with tuition contribution reduced from an expected ~3% to approximately 2.5%
Free cash flow outlook is weak, projected at less than $10 million for the year due to elevated costs associated with footprint optimization
positive_highlights: Champions revenue grew double-digits for four consecutive quarters driven by new site openings and higher average revenue per site
Crème de la Crème summer camp enrollment increased approximately 26% compared to last year, signaling repositioning traction
Marketing initiatives successfully drove a week-over-week increase in inquiries across the portfolio
summary: KinderCare reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $698 million, down slightly from the prior year's $700 million and missing expectations due to a 4% decline in total enrollment driven by footprint optimization. Adjusted EPS was $0.08 compared to $0.22 last year, while adjusted EBITDA fell to $63 million as management updated full-year guidance downward to reflect the impact of closing approximately 80-85 centers and a reduced tuition contribution assumption from state subsidies.

negative_highlights: Ipiranga expects margins in Q3 to decline from current levels as they normalize toward first-quarter figures due to Middle East conflict impacts.
Ultragaz volume decreased by 3% YoY, with a specific drop of 4% in the bottled segment and 2% in bulk segments.
Hidrovias adjusted EBITDA fell 8% compared to Q2 FY2025 primarily due to the sale of its coastal navigation operation.
positive_highlights: Net income reached a historic high of BRL 1,677 million, representing a 46% increase compared to Q2 FY2025.
Operating cash flow generation hit an all-time record of BRL 4.8 billion due to strong operations and working capital release at Ipiranga.
Leverage ratio improved significantly to 0.9x, the lowest level since 2008.
summary: Ultrapar reported record net income of BRL 1,677 million (up 46% YoY) and recurring adjusted EBITDA of BRL 3,657 million for Q2 FY2026. The company achieved a significant working capital release at Ipiranga driven by diesel imports amid Middle East volatility, resulting in record operating cash flow generation of BRL 4.8 billion. Management anticipates margins will normalize to first-quarter levels due to the offsetting effects of fighting illegal practices and ongoing supply disruptions.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue/EBITDA growth is capped at a modest implied rate of 6.5% due to pro-forma adjustments.
Same-Quarter Revenue (MSR) forecasted to decline by approximately 3% in Q4 FY26 compared to the prior year quarter.
positive_highlights: Achieved a record first-half booking total of 470 MW, with Q2 alone contributing 260 MW.
Secured an additional 600 MW in reservations from customers for future capacity needs.
Raised full-year sales target to 1 GW and CapEx guidance to RMB 10 billion reflecting strong demand.
summary: GDS Holdings reported a record first-half of FY26 with 470 MW in new bookings and secured an additional 600 MW in reservations for future needs. Management raised its full-year sales target to 1 GW from the prior guidance, alongside raising CapEx paid guidance from RMB 9 billion to RMB 10 billion. Pro forma adjusted EBITDA growth is now implied at 6.5% for FY26 following pro-forma adjustments that deduct one-time items and restructured recurring income.

negative_highlights: Platform revenue decreased approximately 10% year-over-year to $3.7 million.
Total platform expenses increased by approximately 11% to $5.9 million, primarily due to bad debt charges on uncollectible development fees.
positive_highlights: Platform Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at approximately $0.3 million, an improvement of roughly $0.4 million from the prior year quarter's loss.
Completed first fund tokenization for PURE Pickleball & Padel and launched a second offering (Steamboat Springs Hyatt Studios) with an initial slate targeting ~$100 million in managed assets.
summary: Q2 platform revenue declined approximately 10% year-over-year to $3.7 million due to timing of project financings and lower development fees, while total expenses rose by roughly 11% to $5.9 million driven by bad debt charges. Adjusted EBITDA improved significantly from a loss in the prior period but remained below guidance targets as management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $18-$22 million without raising it.

negative_highlights: Management lowered full-year ROAE guidance expectations from ~9.5-10% to 9.25%, citing second-half margin pressures.
NIM on investments is being built conservatively at 2% for the remainder of the year due to potential rate hikes and derivative offsets.
Concerns expressed regarding a new local tax project in Bogotá that could add COP 500 billion to operational expenses.
positive_highlights: Attributed net income reached COP 577 billion, up 17% compared to the prior year quarter.
ROAE expanded significantly to 12.7%, reflecting strong profitability despite macro headwinds.
Loan growth accelerated with total loans increasing 2.1% over the quarter and deposits growing 3.8%.
summary: Grupo Aval reported Q2 FY26 attributed net income of COP 577 billion (up 17% YoY) and ROAE of 12.7%, driven by loan/deposit growth and strong investment portfolio contributions. Management maintained full-year ROAE guidance at 9.25% despite a first-half performance near 10%, citing caution regarding second-half NIM pressures from further rate hikes, earthquake impacts on asset quality, and potential local tax increases in Bogotá.

negative_highlights: Total net revenues decreased by 1.3% year-over-year to $56.5 million due to a lower average number of vessels owned and operated.
First half revenue declined slightly, indicating that recent strong market rates have not yet fully offset the impact of fleet size reduction.
positive_highlights: Charter coverage stands at 96% for 2026 with highly attractive average daily rates of approximately $30,900 per day.
Fleet utilization remains remarkably tight with idle capacity just 200,000 TEU or 6% of the global fleet as of early July.
Newbuilding prices moved higher up approximately 2% quarter-over-quarter reflecting robust demand across the sector.
summary: Euroseas reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of $56.5 million and EPS of $4.74 per diluted share, representing a slight miss against the prior year's revenue growth despite higher charter rates driven by supply tightness. Management noted that while current market conditions are strong with high utilization, they anticipate potential moderation in demand towards the end of 2026 as geopolitical disruptions may ease and new vessel deliveries increase.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$14M due to IM-4 estimated complete adjustment of $14.7M and acquisition-related costs
Gross profit margin pressure from one-off adjustments on the IM-4 mission
positive_highlights: $206 million revenue delivered, more than four times the prior year
Record $1.8 billion backlog with diversification across civil (37%), commercial (49%), and national security (14%) segments
Won three GEO communication satellites valued at over $600 million for a 30-month term
summary: Intuitive Machines reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $206 million (up from a loss in the prior year) and adjusted EBITDA of -$14 million (improving from -$25 million). The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance for revenue between $900M-$1B and positive adjusted EBITDA, citing record backlog growth to $1.8 billion driven by diversification into commercial GEO satellites ($600M award) and national security programs (SDA Tranche 3/AMDT3). Management noted that near-term cash usage remains elevated due to strategic inventory investments but expects free cash flow improvement in the second half of the year.

negative_highlights: F-16 revenue was lower than last year due to prior period pull-forward of inventory buildup costs ($5.7M vs $12.6M)
R&D expenses increased by approximately $1 million as the company accelerates investments in NextGen capabilities
positive_highlights: Revenue grew ~11% YoY to $26.7M driven by organic growth excluding F-16 timing differences
Gross margin expanded significantly to 51.7%, marking four consecutive quarters above the 50% threshold
Secured a major new OEM contract for an eVTOL aircraft program with over 400 orders in backlog
summary: Innovative Aerosystems reported Q3 FY26 revenue of $26.7 million (up ~11% YoY) and net income of $4.5 million ($0.25 diluted EPS), driven by strong organic growth in commercial/business aviation excluding a difficult F-16 comparison. Gross margin expanded to 51.7%, the fourth consecutive quarter above 50%. Management raised Q4 revenue guidance expectations (implied beat) and highlighted significant strategic wins including an eVTOL contract win, Aydin acquisition integration progress, and inclusion in the Russell 2000 Index.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $5 million driven largely by one-time leadership transition costs ($0.9M) and stock-based compensation
No revenue guidance provided as the company is still in a learning stage with initial commercial launch only just beginning
FDA pivotal trial timeline remains uncertain pending review, though management expects to start before year-end
positive_highlights: Completed enrollment of ALIGN-ACS pilot study with 134 patients ahead of schedule, results accepted at TCT conference
Initial commercial orders shipped and first patients onboarded in concierge practices across four target geographies
Operating cash outflow decreased by 7% QoQ due to cost efficiencies and pausing non-key projects
summary: HeartBeam reported a net loss of $5 million for Q2 FY2026, which included approximately $1 million in one-time items related to leadership transition and severance; excluding these, the underlying operating cash outflow decreased by roughly 7% quarter-over-quarter. Management confirmed that initial commercial orders have shipped with patients being onboarded at concierge practices across four U.S. geographies (New York, Dallas, South Florida, Southern California), though specific revenue figures were not disclosed as the business remains in a learning stage. The company submitted its pre-submission to the FDA today for heart attack detection indication via the 510(k) pathway.

negative_highlights: Exploration and evaluation expenses surged $45.6 million year-over-year, primarily due to a one-time charge of $37.5M owed to Allseas
Cash used in operating activities increased to $20.1 million from $10.7 million in the prior period (excluding tax timing differences)
Management clarified that no investment decision has been made for the Brownsville processing site and future capital commitments remain contingent on U.S. government support
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed to $60.1 million from a net loss of $74.3 million in Q2 FY2025
NOAA certification for USA-A application expected imminently, with permanent grant anticipated by October 2026 despite administrative delays
New Master Services Agreement signed with Eco Minerals to provide vessel charter and AUV equipment
summary: TMC reported a net loss of $60.1 million in Q2 FY2026 compared to $74.3 million in the prior year period, driven by exploration and evaluation expenses increasing significantly due to charges owed to Allseas ($37.5M) related to their development agreement signed in May. While management highlighted steady progress on U.S. permitting milestones for USA-A and USA-B applications and confirmed that cash reserves are sufficient for at least 12 months, they explicitly stated no investment decision has been made regarding the Brownsville processing site yet.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened by $9.7 million year-over-year due to pre-development acceleration
Cash used in operating activities increased from $7.2M (H1 '25) to $22.8M (H1 '26)
Management explicitly stated they cannot provide specific spending guidance until feasibility studies conclude
positive_highlights: Successfully completed IPO raising $310 million, bolstering liquidity significantly
Treasury cash balance increased robustly from $31M to $288.7M in six months
Completed approximately 1,200m of underground development and commissioned a replacement hoist
summary: Sunshine Silver Mining & Refining reported a net loss of $16.7 million ($0.13 per share) for Q2 FY2026, an increase from the prior year's loss due to accelerated development activities and IPO-related costs. The company raised approximately $310 million in its recent IPO, bringing cash on hand to $288.7 million at quarter-end with no long-term debt. Management provided a clear path toward production targeted for late 2028 but declined to provide specific financial guidance or updated spending forecasts beyond noting that G&A will taper off starting Q1 2027.

negative_highlights: Q2 Revenue declined from Q1 due to the elimination of $1.8 million in staking revenue following the sale of Ethereum holdings.
General and administrative expenses increased to $10.3M, including a one-time cash charge of $1.8M for an early termination fee on an asset manager agreement.
Management explicitly stated that AI compute deployment is contingent on closing specific deals in Q4 rather than being fully operational.
positive_highlights: Net loss narrowed significantly from $77.5 million in Q1 to $12.4 million in Q2 as the business transitioned away from digital asset volatility.
Acquired two additional commercial aircraft engines already generating contracted lease revenue with targeted double-digit annual returns.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance remains intact at $18-$22M despite capital deployment into buybacks and new assets.
summary: Forum Markets reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $1.4 million and a net loss narrowing to $12.4 million from the prior quarter's $77.5 million loss due to asset sales and buybacks rather than operational growth. Management reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $18-$22 million, driven by aircraft lease income ($5-6M in H2) and a pending AI compute deal expected to contribute ~$8-12M in Q4. The company executed significant share repurchases (7.1M shares), reducing outstanding equity by 35%.

negative_highlights: Q2 combined ratio spiked to 99.5%, significantly above H1 average of 93.1%, due to $162 million in catastrophe and large losses.
Management explicitly stated they do not expect Q3 growth to match the quarter's pace, citing seasonality where more premium is earned in Q4 for wind perils.
Reinsurance acquisition expense ratio was higher than anticipated as new partner business earns through without Fidelis Partnership commissions.
positive_highlights: Gross premiums written grew by over 6% in both the quarter and year-to-date, driven by new underwriting partners.
Book value per diluted common share increased 23% YoY to $26.56 due to strong capital returns including a $73 million return (buybacks + dividends).
War-related lines have run at a sub-20% loss ratio since the Russia-Ukraine conflict, demonstrating profitable deployment in geopolitical risk.
summary: Pelagos Insurance Capital reported Q2 FY26 gross premiums written of $1.3 billion (up 6% YoY) and operating net income of $29 million ($0.34 diluted EPS). The quarter's combined ratio was elevated at 99.5%, driven by large loss events totaling $162 million, including specific losses from the Middle East conflict and a gas plant explosion in Qatar; however, management views this as random timing variability rather than an underlying trend deterioration. Management maintained its full-year guidance for mid-single-digit growth and ROAE targets of 13%-15%, citing that H1 results are broadly on plan with Q3/Q4 expected to normalize the combined ratio.

negative_highlights: The company remains at an operating loss, reporting a non-GAAP net loss of $5.8 million ($0.07 per share) compared to a larger loss last year.
Management noted that autonomous processing and Plaque Tracker are expected to drive further margin expansion in 2027 rather than the current fiscal year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 48% year-over-year to $64.1 million, marking the fastest growth rate in eight quarters.
Plaque revenue reached $7.8 million, beating expectations by approximately $3-4 million and driving significant gross margin expansion of 770 bps quarter-over-quarter.
New account additions hit a record cohort of 340 accounts added during the prior year (2025), ramping in line with or ahead of expectations.
summary: HeartFlow reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $64.1 million, up 48% year-over-year and ahead of expectations, driven by accelerating plaque adoption and durable FF-CT utilization. Management raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to a range of $246-$250 million (representing 40%-42% growth) and increased the non-GAAP gross margin outlook to approximately 82%. The company highlighted record new account additions in Q2, with plaque activations ahead of plan and coverage reaching roughly 78%.

negative_highlights: Research and development expenses increased by 9.8% due to AI investment
AI BOX was integrated into existing suites rather than growing as a separate line item
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased by 6% year-over-year to CNY 162.1 million
Gross margin expanded five percentage points to reach 70.1%
Net loss narrowed significantly from CNY 73.9 million to CNY 14.4 million
summary: In the first half of FY2026, YXT reported total revenues of CNY 162.1 million, a 6% year-over-year increase driven by AI product adoption and large enterprise focus. Gross margin expanded significantly to 70.1%, up five percentage points from the prior period, while net loss narrowed substantially to CNY 14.4 million. Management expressed confidence in further gross margin expansion for H2 due to continued operational efficiencies.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined from 24.5% to 23% driven by $7 million incremental marketing/IT investment in Q2.
Digital Wallet segment adjusted EBITDA fell 9% YoY and revenue per active user decreased 5% due to regional mix shifts including weaker rest-of-world markets.
Merchant Solutions volume growth of only 5% reflects a slowdown in same-store sales for existing customers despite strong iGaming volumes.
positive_highlights: Resolution of major inherited SPAC-era legal overhang via settlement in principle with Farzad litigation removes significant restructuring expense drain on cash flow and P&L.
Completion of debt refinancing extending maturity profile to 2030, upsizing the revolver, and reducing net leverage ratio from 5.5x at Q4 end to a projected year-end range of 5.1-5.2x.
Strong double-digit user growth in Latin America for digital wallets and successful launch of PaysafeWallet in Poland expanding consumer reach.
summary: Paysafe reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $447.4 million (up 4% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $102.8 million (down 2%), resulting in an EPS miss due to increased marketing/IT investments and interest expenses despite the resolution of legacy litigation matters. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for revenue and adjusted EBITDA while updating adjusted EPS expectations, citing a strong first-half growth rate of 7% that met prior outlooks.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased approximately 87% year-over-year to $34.2 million due to Melinta integration and new personnel.
note and marketing expense surged 95% to $12.4 million reflecting a larger product portfolio rather than organic growth efficiency gains.
New LDO pilot is not included in current guidance, with visibility into its impact expected only by late year or early next year.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA beat prior year by more than doubling from $22.4M to $58.7M driven by Melinta portfolio contribution and DefenCath growth.
Signed a multi-year commercial supply agreement with an additional large dialysis organization (LDO), securing agreements with all five top U.S. dialysis providers.
Positive Phase III ReSPECT data for REZZAYO met primary endpoint of fungal-free survival at day 90, positioning the product for sNDA submission in Q3.
summary: CorMedix reported Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue of $101.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $58.7 million, significantly beating the prior year period which included no Melinta contribution. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance at $325-$345 million while raising full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a new range of $125-$140 million following a multi-year commercial supply agreement with an additional large dialysis organization.

negative_highlights: Low unit volume sales (9 consoles) failed to match revenue growth despite margin expansion.
Operating expenses increased YoY by $800k due to investments in commercial and product development initiatives.
Net loss widened from $12.6M prior year quarter, though this included a one-time warrant valuation charge of ~$1.7M.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 14% YoY to $1.97M driven by a 5% increase in circuit ASP and favorable product mix.
Gross margin expanded significantly from 56% to 76% due to pricing power and transition to contract manufacturing.
Installed base growth accelerated with nine consoles sold in Q2, bringing the first-half total to 24 units.
summary: Nuwellis reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.97 million (up 14% YoY) and gross margins expanding to 76%, driven by pricing adjustments and product mix shifts rather than volume growth, which remained low with only nine consoles sold in the quarter compared to three last year. The company reported a net loss of approximately $4.8 million, including roughly $1.7 million in warrant valuation expense from recent financing activities that strengthened cash reserves but did not provide formal financial guidance for future periods.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 20 basis points due to a significant LIFO expense of $6.4 million compared to $2.9 million in the prior-year quarter.
Flow control operations experienced muted sales growth, partially offsetting gains from other segments within Engineered Solutions.
Fiscal 2027 guidance assumes more difficult comparisons and potentially lower market growth rates in the second half of the year.
positive_highlights: Organic sales growth accelerated to 10%, driven by double-digit volume increases in automation (over 20%) and fluid power operations.
EBITDA margin expanded more than 60 basis points year-over-year, leveraging strong top-line momentum into higher returns.
Free cash flow increased 16% YoY to $461 million for the full fiscal year, supported by working capital optimization.
summary: Applied Industrial Technologies reported a solid finish to fiscal Q4 FY26 with record sales of $1.3 billion (up 10% YoY) and EPS of $3.17 (up 13%). EBITDA margins expanded by over 60 bps to 13%, driven by volume growth in automation and fluid power, though gross margin was slightly down due to LIFO expense. Management raised intermediate financial targets for fiscal 2028-2029, increasing the sales objective to $7 billion from $5.5 billion and EBITDA margins to 14%.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses spiked sharply to ~$7.5 million due to public company costs, legal fees, and one-time equipment purchases.
Net loss widened materially to approximately $7.2 million compared to a prior year net loss of roughly $1.6 million.
Management declined to provide specific visibility on converting the MOU with Powers into a full contract.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew YoY to approximately $216,000 despite accounting deferrals on the SkyKnight program.
Gross profit increased significantly to roughly $184,000 compared to $82,000 in Q2 FY25.
Cash position strengthened with total cash and equivalents at June 30 reaching approximately $25.3 million.
summary: Swarmer reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $216,000 compared to $138,000 in the prior year period, driven by a commercial deal where only ~$200k was recognized due to accounting treatment. Gross profit rose to roughly $184,000 from $82,000 primarily reflecting this revenue recognition mechanics rather than margin expansion on scale. Operating expenses surged to approximately $7.5 million (up from $855,000) driven by public company costs and one-time equipment purchases, resulting in a net loss of ~$7.2 million versus a prior year loss of ~$1.6 million.

negative_highlights: Gross margin fell sharply to 19.5% due to elevated milk prices, resin costs, and oil-related transportation expenses.
Management expects input cost pressures to persist into the third quarter before conditions normalize.
Net income was minimal at $0.1 million ($0.01 per share) despite record sales volume.
positive_highlights: Net sales reached $66.9 million, marking the highest quarterly figure in company history and up 24.1% year-over-year.
The quarter extended a streak of growth to 27 consecutive quarters with nearly seven years of uninterrupted performance.
Distribution expanded significantly for Muscle Mates (nearly 800 Walmart locations) and Farmer Cheese (nationwide at Walmart, coming soon to Target).
summary: Lifeway Foods reported record quarterly net sales of $66.9 million in Q2 FY2026, representing a 24.1% year-over-year increase and extending its streak to 27 consecutive quarters of growth. However, gross margin contracted significantly to 19.5%, primarily due to elevated milk prices, packaging resin costs, and transportation pressures related to the Middle East conflict. Management noted that while SG&A decreased as a percentage of sales (operating leverage), near-term profitability remains under pressure from these input cost headwinds.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted to 19.1%, with total operating expenses rising 19.4% primarily driven by $129.6 million of stock compensation from the IPO.
Revenue was negatively impacted by a payer mix shift due to ACA exchange subsidy expiration, resulting in approximately $16 million lower revenue compared to expectations.
Net loss widened to $28.3 million as reported earnings were significantly offset by one-time IPO-related expenses and No Surprises Act comparability issues.
positive_highlights: Same-market revenue increased by $53.1 million (3.8% YoY) driven by emergent transport growth and new market starts totaling over $43 million in incremental annualized revenue.
911 Nurse Navigation calls grew significantly to nearly 29,000, representing a 50% year-over-year increase as the company expands this non-emergent solution.
Air medical volumes increased 6.9% YoY due to strong demand and improved capture rates in weather-constrained markets.
summary: GMR Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.49 billion (3.3% YoY growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $285 million, which was down 11.8% YoY due to a lack of favorable No Surprises Act estimate adjustments compared to the prior year. Management reiterated full-year guidance for revenue between $5.89B-$6.18B and adjusted EBITDA between $1.135B-$1.195B, noting that underlying performance remains strong despite headwinds from ACA subsidy expiration impacts of approximately $16 million per quarter.

negative_highlights: Management declined to provide specific numerical guidance for fiscal 2027, noting that results will reflect higher team compensation and luxury tax expenses.
SG&A expenses increased by $2.9 million related to the proposed spin-off transaction costs.
NHL revenue sharing expense is expected to increase in FY27 due to changes under the new collective bargaining agreement.
positive_highlights: Total revenues increased 36% year-over-year driven by a Knicks championship run that generated $182 million in playoff-related revenues versus $115.2 million the prior year.
Adjusted operating income swung from an adjusted loss of $16.8 million to a profit of $39.6 million, reflecting robust demand and record per-game gate revenues during the postseason.
Sponsorship revenues more than doubled year-over-year during the championship run due to heightened partner activation opportunities.
summary: For fiscal Q4 FY26, MSG Sports reported total revenues of $278.7 million and adjusted operating income (AOI) of $39.6 million, representing a significant beat against the prior year's revenue of $204 million and AOI loss of -$16.8 million driven by Knicks championship playoffs. Management raised full-year FY26 guidance to approximately $59 million in AOI from an implied lower range based on Q4 results but declined to provide specific numerical guidance for fiscal 2027, citing higher team compensation and revenue sharing expenses as headwinds.

negative_highlights: Sweaty Betty revenue declined 3% in the quarter due to an ongoing strategic reset of its U.S. business.
Work Group revenue fell 2%, though this was noted as modestly ahead of expectations amidst varying progress across brands.
Gross margin decreased 70 basis points YoY, primarily pressured by a ~310 bps unmitigated tariff headwind and elevated oil prices.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $0.40 beat the high end of prior guidance ($0.35-$0.38) driven by strong revenue growth and disciplined cost management.
Merrell delivered double-digit revenue growth (10%) with triple-digit basis point market share gains in the U.S. hike category.
Saucony achieved 9% quarterly growth on top of a massive 40% YoY increase last year, raising its full-year outlook to mid-teens.
summary: Wolverine World Wide reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $506 million (up 7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $0.40 (up 14%), both exceeding expectations with the latter beating the upper end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $1.98B-$2.0B from $1.965B-$1.985B and adjusted EPS guidance to $1.55-$1.65 from $1.43-$1.58, citing strong H1 execution by Merrell (up 10%) and Saucony (up 9%). The company also raised its full-year gross margin outlook to approximately 46.9%.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance was lowered from $2,508M midpoint to $2,462M due to new market deterioration and travel volatility.
Adjusted operating margin of 13.2% missed the guided range driven by dollar weakness in Colombia and utilization below targets.
North America region experienced a 2.4% revenue contraction while new markets saw an 17.7% decrease.
positive_highlights: AI Pods adoption accelerated with revenue growing roughly 60% quarter-over-quarter, now comprising ~45 of top client projects.
Top 20 clients grew by 6.6% year-over-year while new market segment dragged growth down significantly.
Free cash flow for the first half reached a record $48.7 million.
summary: Globant reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $614.4 million, which was within the prior guided range but represented a slight year-over-year decline and sequential growth of only 1.2%. Management revised full-year 2026 revenue guidance downward to a range of $2.43B-$2.46B from the previous $2.46B-$2.51B, citing geopolitical pressures in new markets (specifically Middle East) and travel sector slowdowns due to oil prices. Adjusted operating margin slipped below expectations to 13.2% as FX headwinds impacted Colombia and utilization targets were missed.

negative_highlights: Market share recovery is expected to take more time than anticipated due to prior retail disruptions.
Share buybacks have been suspended to prioritize debt paydown, indicating a shift away from aggressive capital return.
Management declined to provide specific leverage ratio targets or timelines for deleveraging.
positive_highlights: Category remains robust with value up ~3.4% and volume up ~1.6% in the frozen segment year-to-date.
summary: Management stated that retail disruptions in Germany and France are largely resolved but warned it will take time to return market share to neutral levels despite strong category growth of roughly 3% year-to-date. The company suspended share buybacks to focus on deleveraging while maintaining dividends, with a EUR 200 million productivity program remaining on track.

negative_highlights: Revenue of $113 million represents a significant decline from $215.4 million in Q2 FY2025 due to legacy adjustments
Gross loss widened significantly to $71 million compared to gross profit of $13 million last year, primarily driven by non-cash catch-up adjustments
Net loss attributable to stockholders was $84.3 million ($1.55 per diluted share) versus a net loss of only $10.3 million in the prior period

positive_highlights: Operating expenses reduced by 32% year-over-year following a cost program that cut headcount by 27%.
summary: Second quarter revenue was approximately $0.4 million, flat year-over-year compared to Q1's growth but lower than the prior period due to timing in services and deferred recognition from a vet agreement. Operating expenses decreased by 32% YoY following headcount reductions, yet net loss widened slightly to $7.3 million driven by non-cash charges on convertible notes. Management explicitly declined to provide revenue guidance for FY2026 citing the lumpy nature of project delivery and deferred revenue recognition.

negative_highlights: Exchange revenue fell 38% YoY and transaction revenue dropped 15% due to a 66% decline in spot trading volumes
Credit card receivables remained flat while provision for expected credit losses spiked from $3.6m to $20.1m driven by fraud-related delinquency maturation
Assets on platform declined significantly to $8.4 billion from $18.2 billion in Q2 2025 due to crypto price declines and net outflows
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 37% YoY to $45.5 million despite a weak crypto trading environment
Services revenue and interest income surged 117% YoY to $26 million, now representing 59% of net revenue
Prediction markets volume reached new monthly highs in July with strong engagement in Bitcoin contracts
summary: Total revenue grew 37% year-over-year to $45.5 million driven by services and OTC growth, while exchange revenue declined 38% due to soft crypto volumes. Net loss narrowed slightly to $107.7 million from a prior quarter's adjusted EBITDA deterioration of roughly $26M compared to Q1, primarily reflecting non-cash mark-to-market losses on Bitcoin holdings following the May strategic investment. Management provided no formal revenue guidance for 2H but expects technology and G&A expenses between $155m-$170m full year.

negative_highlights: Second-quarter net revenues moderated sequentially due to trade inventory normalization following first-quarter shipment adjustments.
Management expects Mainland China sales for the full year to be broadly flat year-over-year amid tightening domestic regulations and conservative approval timelines.
Gross margin expansion is partially attributed to temporary product mix shifts, with expectations that margins will settle back to a healthy range as flows normalize.
positive_highlights: Top-line grew 14.8% year-over-year driven by international expansion and an acquired entity completed in May 2025.
Gross margin expanded sequentially to 35.4%, up 790 basis points year-over-year due to supply chain optimization and mix shifts.
Non-GAAP operating profit reached RMB 149.6 million, marking the 11th consecutive quarter of positive non-GAAP income from operations.
summary: RLX Technology reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 1.01 billion (up 14.8% YoY) and gross profit of RMB 357.8 million with a margin expansion to 35.4%. Management noted that sequential revenue moderation was due to trade inventory normalization following Q1 regulatory-driven shipments rather than demand softening, while highlighting the upcoming consolidation of a Western European acquisition in Q3 which will boost reported growth.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $5 million from a prior year adjusted loss, though this reflects one-time settlement costs.
Galena Q2 production was suppressed by phase 2 shaft upgrades and waste development activities designed for H2 ramp-up.
A minor fire at Galena displaced some high-grade ore in the specific scope mined during Q2.
positive_highlights: Consolidated revenue increased 71% YoY to $46.3 million driven by higher realized silver prices ($67/oz vs $34/oz).
Cosalá production rose 26% YoY to ~337k oz supported by improved recoveries and entering the high-grade EC120 zone.
Settlement of Sprott and Royal Gold obligations removed >$76M in variable debt service with only 3.3% dilution.
summary: Americas Gold and Silver reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $46.3 million (up 71% YoY) driven by a silver price increase to $67/oz, while consolidated production reached ~800k silver equivalent ounces with Cosalá output up 26%. The company settled remaining variable delivery obligations for Sprott and Royal Gold, removing over $76 million in future debt service. Management reiterated full-year guidance of 3.2-3.6M oz despite Q2 being a trough quarter due to infrastructure spending at Galena.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined sequentially and YoY to 63.7% due to product mix shift as Conversational AI products remain at a subscale stage.
Operating cash flow turned negative at -$2.1 million compared to -$0.4M in the prior year quarter, primarily driven by annual bonus payments and share repurchases.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat high end of guidance at $40.4 million, marking third consecutive quarter of accelerating top-line growth.
GAAP net profit surged to $2.2 million (up 50% YoY) driven by improved operating leverage and disciplined cost management in G&A.
Dollar-based net retention rate improved significantly to 104%, moving back above the 100% threshold from 94% last year.
summary: Total revenue for Q2 FY26 reached $40.4 million, beating the high end of guidance and growing 18% year-over-year to a third consecutive quarter of accelerating growth. GAAP net profit was $2.2 million (up 50%), though gross margin contracted slightly to 63.7% due to product mix changes as Conversational AI usage grew at a subscale stage. Management raised Q3 revenue guidance expectations, projecting between $41M and $42M with growth of 15.8%-18.6%, while reaffirming the goal of achieving GAAP operating profitability by year-end.

negative_highlights: Skillz revenue declined sequentially by ~3% excluding one-time items, driven by an 8% drop in paying monthly active users
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $13.6 million from a normalized loss of $2.7 million due to elevated litigation costs near the Papaya trial conclusion
Skillz user acquisition spend decreased significantly as management paused spending to repair operational funnels
positive_highlights: RZR exceeded $10 million in quarterly revenue for the first time, growing 6% QoQ and 75% YoY
RZR delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of profitability with sequential growth each period
Company secured a unanimous jury verdict awarding approximately $730 million against Papaya Gaming
summary: Firy reported Q2 FY26 GAAP revenue of $31 million (up 23% YoY), but the company posted a net loss of $24.5 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $13.6 million, including approximately $11 million in litigation expenses. While RZR achieved its fourth consecutive quarter of profitability with strong growth, Skillz revenue declined sequentially due to operational headwinds and reduced user acquisition spend aimed at fixing funnel issues. Management highlighted a recent court victory awarding ~$730 million against Papaya Gaming but noted that proceeds are not yet realized in financial statements.

negative_highlights: Sales of resins and major chemicals decreased in the Brazilian market by 2% and 4%, respectively.
Polyethylene sales fell 11% in Mexico due to lower availability from reduced utilization rates at Braskem Idesa.
Management warned that global petrochemical fundamentals remain under pressure with overcapacity, suggesting Q2 results were a tactical capture of value rather than structural improvement.
positive_highlights: Consolidated recurring EBITDA reached $1.043 billion, representing an increase compared to the previous quarter.
International spreads for resins and main chemicals expanded significantly in Brazil (82%) and Mexico (73%).
Green polyethylene sales increased by 49% due to commercial opportunities in Europe.
summary: Braskem reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated recurring EBITDA of $1.043 billion with a margin of 24%, driven by significant international spread increases (up to 73% in Mexico) and PIS/COFINS credits, partially offset by lower Brazilian sales volumes and currency appreciation. Management noted that the strong quarter was largely tactical due to Middle East conflict-induced supply shocks rather than structural demand growth, with spreads expected to normalize toward pre-conflict levels in Q3. The company emphasized a focus on capital structure restructuring and operational discipline as it navigates global overcapacity.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss was $75 million due to one-time non-cash items totaling $64.4M (tax charge and stock-based comp).
Operating costs were high at $44 million with depreciation rising to $18.1 million during the rapid deployment phase.
No specific guidance on future profitability or margin expansion was provided for this transitional quarter.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew ~270% YoY driven by lease revenue from GPU rental fleet deployment and bespoke assets for customers.
Total Contract Value (TCV) stands at $1.9 billion with an average duration of approximately three years.
Management secured a strategic procurement agreement worth $4B-$5B in compute hardware with multiple OEMs, including Dell.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $31.1 million (up ~270% YoY), but the company reported a GAAP net loss of $75 million and an operating loss of $12.9 million, heavily impacted by one-time non-cash items including a $55.7M tax charge from transitioning to C-Corp status and $64.4M in other transaction-related adjustments. Management reaffirmed guidance for approximately $400 million annualized recurring revenue at year-end 2026 but provided no specific EPS or margin targets due to the one-time nature of the quarter's results.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly stated no specific revenue or EPS numbers were released, indicating an absence of financial performance data
Strategic shift away from immediate CCS deployment may disappoint investors focused on clean energy transition metrics
Project financing remains uncertain and dependent on securing partner capital or additional equity
positive_highlights: Company possesses sufficient capital ($310M) to support operations and development without rushing deals
Strategic pivot aligns with market demand for speed-to-power in a supply-constrained grid environment (ERCOT)
Project Permian site design preserves optionality to add carbon capture later via partnership with Oxy
summary: NET Power reported Q2 FY2026 results with no specific revenue or EPS figures disclosed in the transcript; management highlighted a strategic recalibration to prioritize unabated natural gas power generation over carbon capture due to immediate grid constraints and market demand for speed. The company redirected capital focus toward behind-the-meter solutions while preserving long-term optionality for CCS, citing $310 million cash on hand but noting that project financing remains required.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 27% year-over-year as one-time non-recurring revenue from CreateStudio in Q1 trails off
Adjusted EBITDA loss widened slightly to $1.7 million despite lower operating expenses due to the revenue miss
Gross profit decreased compared to the prior year quarter
positive_highlights: Net dollar retention rate reached an all-time high of 91% for the core customer segment
Stockholders' equity hit a new record of $12.2 million following debt paydowns
Cost reduction actions reduced operating expenses by $1.7M compared to Q1
summary: Parabolic reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.3 million, a decrease of approximately 16% from the prior quarter and 27% year-over-year due to non-recurring revenue trailing off in legacy products. Net loss narrowed by 41% compared to Q1 driven by cost reductions totaling $1.7M versus Q1, while adjusted EBITDA remained at a loss of $1.7 million. Management raised full-year guidance expectations citing significant second-half growth from ConnectAndSell ($6.5M contribution) and legacy product improvements.

negative_highlights: Gross revenue remained essentially flat both year-over-year and sequentially in a challenging macro environment
Adjusted EBITDA remains negative at approximately $1.7 million, missing the profitability target for H1
Revenue stability attributed to external headwinds including World Cup spending shifts, tariff uncertainty, geopolitical events, and evolving Roblox policies
positive_highlights: Gross margin improved to 41% sequentially, up from 36% in Q1
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed approximately $0.4M YoY to ~$1.7 million despite flat revenue
Weighted pipeline per seller increased significantly to ~$2.8 million driven by new leadership and acquired assets
summary: Super League reported Q2 FY26 gross revenue of approximately $3 million (flat YoY and sequentially) with net revenue increasing to ~$1.24M (+16% seq). Gross margin expanded to 41%, while Adjusted EBITDA remained a loss of ~$1.7M, improving from the prior year quarter but missing profitability targets for H1. Management reaffirmed guidance for adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q4 and highlighted pipeline growth driven by new sales leadership and Misfits integration.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly declined to provide full-year guidance for 2026, citing parabolic volatility in fuel prices that makes forward-looking statements unreliable.
CASK increased significantly year-over-year due to a 61.8% rise in fuel costs and temporary deleveraging of fixed costs over reduced capacity.
Recurring free cash flow was nearly breakeven (negative BRL 80 million) hindered by non-recurring restructuring payments totaling approximately BRL 794 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to a record 10.2%, recapturing approximately BRL 448 million of the fuel headwind through disciplined capacity management and pricing actions.
Operating revenue reached a quarterly record, supported by RASK growth of 12.7% YoY despite significant volume reductions.
NPS increased 26 points since December 2025 as operational reliability improved to make Azul the most on-time airline in Latin America.
summary: Azul reported Q2 FY2026 operating revenue of BRL 5 billion (up 0.7% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of BRL 510 million in a seasonally weak quarter impacted by fuel prices up 61%. Management declined to provide full-year guidance due to extreme volatility in the fuel curve, noting that capacity was reduced proactively by 10.6% to protect liquidity while maintaining record RASK.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss was $12.8M for the quarter and Adjusted EBITDA was -$3.2M due to merger-related stock-based compensation charges ($9.4M) and legacy business wind-down costs.
Material weaknesses in internal controls remain unremediated with a multi-step remediation plan underway involving an external accounting firm.
positive_highlights: Contracted annualized recurring revenue on live compute reached $22 million as of August 4th, inclusive of new Blackwell cluster deliveries announced last week.
summary: Corvex reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.8 million entirely from its newly integrated AI platform business following a March merger with Corvex Legacy Holdings; the legacy healthcare segment was fully wound down and transferred to lenders, resulting in no meaningful year-over-year comparisons. Management highlighted that contracted annualized recurring revenue on live compute reached approximately $22 million as of August 4th, driven by new cluster deliveries including Blackwell expansion funded via debt financing and customer prepayments. The quarter included significant non-cash stock-based compensation charges ($9.4M) related to merger equity awards and disclosed unremediated material weaknesses in internal controls.

negative_highlights: Revenue was constrained by a temporary suspension of mining and processing operations due to TAC negotiations in Brazil.
Not all produced material (low-grade fines) could be sold within Q2, resulting in lower revenue than production volume might suggest for the period.
Operational timeline pushed forward by three months regarding full capacity ramp-up.
positive_highlights: Production volume increased significantly by 52% quarter-over-quarter to deliver 35,400 tons of lithium oxide concentrate.
Company maintained high gross margins at 60% and achieved record EBITDA margin of 47%. All-in sustaining costs decreased over 30% year-over-year to $668/ton.
Deleveraged balance sheet significantly, repaying 43% of total debt over the last two years.
summary: Sigma Lithium reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of $55 million and generated approximately $30-32 million in cash flow from operations for the quarter. While production volumes increased by 52% to 35,400 tons due to a ramp-up that surpassed guidance, revenue was impacted by lower sales volume compared to total production as low-grade material produced but not sold during the quarter is being monetized later. Management adjusted its full-year cost guidance downward based on executed costs of $668/ton and pushed forward certain operational timelines by three months due to a temporary suspension related to TAC negotiations.

negative_highlights: Average note price for Zgounder was $68.29/oz, which is below the quarter's average due to a precipitous drop in June prices.
positive_highlights: Production of 1.7 million ounces (silver equivalent), representing a 61% year-over-year increase driven by record mining rates at Zgounder.
Cash flow generation reached $48 million, up 522% from the prior year quarter, with total H1 operating cash flow hitting $119 million.
Discovery of a new high-grade zone parallel to the main structure at Boumadine (intercept of 51m @ 890 g/t silver equivalent) and completion of Phase 2 tailings facility.
summary: Aya reported Q2 FY2026 production of 1.7 million ounces (silver equivalent), a 61% year-over-year increase and 12% quarter-over-quarter rise, driven by record performance at the Zgounder mine where mining rates reached 4,900 tonnes per day against a plant nameplate capacity of 2,700 tonnes. Revenue surged to $97 million (up 151% YoY) and net income hit $35 million due to strong cash costs ($17.69/oz at Zgounder) despite silver prices averaging below the quarter's low-water mark. Management confirmed full alignment with H1 guidance for production, cash cost, and CapEx while highlighting a successful Nasdaq listing as a major catalyst.

negative_highlights: Hardware revenue decreased 19% YoY due to a specific large order delay that prevented meeting proposed expectations for the quarter.
Service revenue declined 28% YoY as non-recurring customization revenues and recurring service renewals lagged timing assumptions.
positive_highlights: Gross margin expanded sharply to 87% from 73%, driven by high-margin license revenue mix and inventory liquidation.
Net loss improved 51% YoY to $0.56 per share, with cash position strengthened to over $4.5 million following warrant exercises.
Significant pipeline growth identified in EMEA (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Portugal) and new opportunities in AI agent governance.
summary: Q2 FY26 revenue grew 13% YoY to $1.92 million driven by a 53% increase in license fees, but the quarter missed proposed expectations due to a delayed hardware shipment shifting into H2. Gross margin expanded significantly to 87%, while net loss improved 51% to $0.56 per share on an adjusted basis of shares post-reverse split. Management targets profitability for the second half of 2026, citing strong pipeline growth in EMEA and new AI governance opportunities.

negative_highlights: Full-year cash spend guidance increased slightly to $27-$28 million reflecting accelerated commercialization activities.
Net loss of $8.5 million includes significant non-cash charges related to earn-out shares and vesting liabilities.
Modest pay deployment revenue expected for the JV in 2026, with more meaningful commercial revenue anticipated only beginning in 2027.
positive_highlights: Signed an exclusive sales agreement with Kubota Corporation to deploy AirJoule systems in water-constrained regions of Texas and California.
First full-scale Prime system commissioned in Newark is operating outdoors at high uptime and tracking toward the expectation of 2,000 liters per day.
Awarded one of the UAE's first Expo City green licenses, providing access to business missions and a seat in the Green Majlis Leadership Forum.
summary: AirJoule Technologies reported a net loss of $8.5 million for Q2 FY26, driven by non-cash losses on earn-out shares and an increase in full-year cash spend guidance to approximately $27-$28 million from the prior expectation. Management highlighted significant commercial milestones including an exclusive partnership with Kubota Corporation for residential development in Texas and California, a deployment at GE Vernova's Frontier Campus, and regulatory validation via UAE green licenses.

negative_highlights: Net loss widened to $17.2 million due to a $13.1M unrealized fair value change on digital asset holdings (primarily Ether).
All Q2 revenue came from the 'Access' model; no revenue was recognized yet from the primary 'Build' clusters.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$4.9 million for the quarter.
positive_highlights: Signed over $3 billion in total contract value (TCV) with more than half added incrementally since April, significantly exceeding initial projections.
Generated positive operating cash flow of $17.4 million driven by customer prepayments totaling $60.8 million at quarter end.
Active qualified pipeline reached $5.9 billion in August, nearly double the current signed book.
summary: Axe Compute reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.2 million (up from $35k in Q1) and a net loss of $17.2 million driven by $13.1M in unrealized digital asset losses, though adjusted EBITDA was -$4.9M excluding those non-cash items. Management highlighted the signing of over $3 billion in total contract value (TCV), including an incremental $2.9B in H1 Q3, with a projected annualized run rate exceeding $696 million upon full deployment by early 2027. The company announced its first customer prepayment of $317M and signed a new agreement for additional power capacity.

negative_highlights: Operating expenses increased by two percent due to deliberate investments in growth hiring and public company costs ahead of the second half ramp.
Revenue recognition for hosting is just beginning, while related party services revenues are winding down as APR agreements conclude.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance remains conservative at $8M-$10M for Q4 2026 due to assumptions regarding no acceleration in GPU energization.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 30% YoY to $6.18M driven by Technology Solutions ($3.23M) as the legacy rail business was divested.
Net income from continuing operations surged to $48.7M, compared to a loss of $1.6M in Q2 2025.
Signed new agreements adding up to 55 megawatts with Axe Compute Inc., valued at over $500 million in contracted revenue.
summary: Duos Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $6.18 million (up 30% YoY) and net income from continuing operations of $48.7 million following the divestiture of its rail business and a gain on investment sales. The company reconfirmed full-year 2026 guidance to exceed $50M in revenue, citing approximately $17-18M annualized recurring revenue expected by Q4 exit run rate. Management highlighted significant progress in AI infrastructure deployment with new multi-megawatt contracts and a strengthened balance sheet of $112.3 million cash.

negative_highlights: Solutions revenue declined 4% YoY due to execution gaps and pricing pressure on renewals
Full-year revenue guidance narrowed slightly despite the Q2 beat, reflecting weaker solutions outlook for H2
Middle East conflict continues to weigh on booking volumes in affected corridors
positive_highlights: Record revenues of $7.7 million achieved ahead of expectations
Platform revenue grew 19% YoY to $2.9 million, driven by Clearit refund claims and Korean Air addition
Adjusted EBITDA loss improved significantly to a record low -$2 million
summary: Freightos reported record Q2 revenue of $7.7 million (up 3% YoY), driven by a strong platform beat but offset by a solutions decline of 4%. Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to -$2 million due to cost discipline, with cash ending the quarter at $21.4 million. Management raised full-year transaction growth guidance slightly while narrowing revenue expectations and maintaining an adjusted EBITDA breakeven target for Q4.

negative_highlights: One surface waiver signature remains pending from a single leasehold operator, though management expects it soon.
Phase Three expansion potential is capped at the standard air permit limit of roughly 757 MW; further growth requires switching to an PSD permit process which typically takes 18 months.
positive_highlights: Secured two key development permits from Ector County and received approval of Notice of Intent to commence grading for Phase One.
Successfully closed the acquisition of the flagged 54-acre corridor, securing all necessary land for planned development.
Expanded total gross capacity across Phases One and Two to roughly 757 MW by finalizing a PPA in New Era's own name.
summary: New Era delivered significant de-risking progress in Q2 FY2026 by securing construction permits and closing the acquisition of a critical land corridor at its flagship TCDC site. The company expanded Phase Two power capacity from 450 MW to approximately 550 MW, bringing total gross capacity for Phases One and Two to roughly 757 MW against previously contemplated levels. Management reaffirmed the target timeline for Phase One delivery in Q4 FY2026 (late 2027 calendar), citing that power availability is now secured via a finalized PPA structure.

negative_highlights: Net loss of $143 million was driven by non-cash items including a $54M depreciation charge and an $85M provision for Swedish VAT tax liability which management intends to contest.
Bitcoin mining revenue grew only modestly (7% q/q) as the business navigates rising difficulty, though this is offset by strong HPC growth.
positive_highlights: Announced a new five-year GPU cloud deal adding $70M in annualized recurring revenue (ARR) alongside an existing Cohere contract, reaching $180M total contracted HPC ARR ahead of schedule.
HPC business grew significantly with quarterly revenue rising from roughly $5 million to $7.1 million driven by the May B200 cluster go-live and new GB300 contracts.
Management confirmed strong demand for GPU clusters, noting willingness to rent additional capacity at higher prices per token than previously forecast.
summary: HIVE reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $79 million (up 10% q/q and 74% y/y) with earnings from operations growing to $15.2 million despite a net loss driven by non-cash depreciation ($54M) and a Swedish tax provision ($85M). Management highlighted the closing of two major GPU cloud deals adding $95 million in annualized recurring revenue, pushing total contracted HPC ARR past $180 million ahead of their year-end target. The company emphasized strong demand for its compute power and plans to deploy additional capacity via partnerships with Bell Canada.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined 30 bps YoY to 12.2%, though improved sequentially by 10 bps due to mix and efficiencies
Free cash flow was an outflow of $37 million in Q4 due to increased CapEx for capacity expansion
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue of $1.316B beat the top end of guidance range
Non-GAAP EPS of $4.10 exceeded expectations, driven by operating leverage with expenses at just 1.3% of revenue
DCI business reached a near-$1 billion annualized run rate in Q4
summary: Fabrinet reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $1.316 billion (up 45% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.10, both exceeding the top end of guidance. The company raised its full-year fiscal 2026 revenue to a record $4.6 billion (+36%) and is entering FY27 with strong momentum across data center, communications infrastructure, and automotive segments. Management highlighted significant capacity expansions in Thailand and Santa Clara to support accelerating demand.

negative_highlights: Net income was negative BRL 320 million due to an impairment charge of BRL 233 million related to the TDUP São Luís port.
Debt service coverage ratio remained low at 0.2x LTM, negatively impacted by seasonality and not yet fully reflecting debt reduction benefits.
Radar's performance was impaired by lower ATR prices reducing lease contributions.
positive_highlights: Expanded net debt reduced significantly to BRL 9.2 billion via IPO proceeds (BRL 2.3b) and prepayments, a 20% drop from Q1.
Rumo EBITDA reached BRL 2.3 billion with volume up 9%, while Compass delivered higher margins in residential/commercial segments despite lower industrial consumption.
Raízen's out-of-court reorganization plan approved by 81.6% of financial creditors, marking a key turnaround step.
summary: Cosan reported a negative net income of BRL 320 million for Q2 FY2026, showing significant improvement over the prior year but missing profitability expectations due to an impairment charge and seasonality in investee dividends. The company highlighted strategic progress including Compass' IPO proceeds (BRL 2.3 billion), debt prepayments totaling nearly BRL 9 billion reducing expanded net debt by 20% to BRL 9.2 billion, and a projected Debt Service Coverage Ratio range of 0.8x-1.2x for year-end 2026.

negative_highlights: Pathology business growth was modest at only about $100,000 sequential increase to ~$6.1 million
positive_highlights: Quarterly revenues surpassed $7 million for the first time in company history
Adjusted EBITDA swung to positive approximately $400,000 from a loss of -$200,000 in Q1
Product revenue reached an all-time quarterly record of approximately $900,000
summary: Precipio reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $7 million, a sequential increase from $6.7 million in Q1 and a year-over-year growth of roughly 22% to $5.7 million. The company returned to positive adjusted EBITDA with approximately $400,000 (up from -$200,000 in Q1) and generated about $700,000 in operating cash flow while ending the quarter with over $3 million in cash on hand without raising capital. Management highlighted record product revenue of roughly $900,000 driven by a new commercial team and distributor partnerships.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss exceeded CAD 1.1 million for the nine-month period due to non-cash expenses and asset revaluation losses
Digital asset treasury value of approximately CAD 48 million is subject to significant volatility in crypto markets
Management explicitly stated that current market conditions have not rewarded their efforts yet
positive_highlights: Houdini Swap contributed CAD 1.2 million revenue and CAD 685,000 operating income with a 60% margin in its first month of inclusion
All validators maintained 100% uptime during Q3 FY2026
Company successfully financed Houdini acquisition using balance sheet rather than note treasury SOL
summary: For the nine months ended June 30th, 2026, Sol Strategies reported an EBITDA loss of CAD 1.1 million after adjusting for significant non-cash items including over CAD 6 million in impairment and revaluation losses on its digital asset treasury valued at approximately CAD 48 million. The company acquired Houdini Swap which contributed one month of revenue (CAD 1.2M) but the overall financials reflect a challenging macro environment with volatile crypto markets impacting the balance sheet. Management expressed confidence in long-term growth and team execution despite acknowledging that current market conditions have not yet rewarded their efforts.

negative_highlights: Fatal incident occurred at BMA's Peak Downs mine in Queensland within CEO Brandon Craig's first month
CEO stated ambition to work through tenure without a fatality was not met, requiring immediate learnings and response
Fuel prices elevated impacted financials by approximately AUD 200 million
positive_highlights: Record production numbers achieved in iron ore business in Western Australia
Escondida performed incredibly well with copper contributing over 50% of EBITDA
Net debt ended the year below target range at less than $9 billion
summary: BHP reported strong financial results for FY26 driven by record production in iron ore and Escondida copper amidst resilient prices. The company ended the year with less than $9 billion of net debt and paid a highest-in-four-years dividend of $8.7 billion, though management immediately pivoted to address a fatal incident at Peak Downs mine which halted momentum on safety goals.

negative_highlights: Fixed income primary market offerings were significantly reduced in Q2, with management noting they did less in the quarter than in an average month.
Mark-to-market losses on investment banking books and secondary trading flows impacted top-line growth by approximately BRL 400-420 million for the half-year.
Equities revenue declined sequentially by 2% due to lower ADTV, while fixed income fees were pressured by a shift in client mix toward low-yield daily liquidity products.
positive_highlights: Corporate segment revenues surged 117% year-over-year to BRL 8 billion driven by cross-note derivatives, FX, and credits despite lower fixed income offerings volume.
Retail revenue grew 8% YoY with equities up 11%, funds platform growing 23% YoY on performance fees, and retail net new money meeting the soft target of BRL 20 billion.
Adjusted EBT margin expanded to 32% sequentially due to operating leverage from controlled expenses against a resilient underlying business.
summary: XP reported Q2 FY26 gross revenue of BRL 5.1 billion (up 8% YoY) and adjusted EPS growth of 9%, driven by strong corporate segment performance (+32%) despite a challenging fixed income primary market environment that suppressed underlying retail momentum. Management noted the quarter was impacted by mark-to-market losses on investment banking books, estimating roughly BRL 400-420 million in negative impacts compared to prior periods where such effects were lower or absent. While meeting soft guidance targets for net new money and maintaining a robust capital ratio of 20.3%, management adopted a cautious tone regarding future credit growth, emphasizing collateralized lending strategies and conservative risk approaches as they navigate geopolitical volatility.

negative_highlights: Net loss remained significant at $14.6 million despite expense reductions, indicating high cash burn relative to current revenue.
GLDY assets under management were broadly unchanged (3,111 ounces) in Q2 compared to the prior quarter.
Material weaknesses regarding internal controls and disclosure procedures remain unremediated as of June 30.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased by $20.4 million (57.1%) driven principally by lower stock-based compensation charges.
Completed five key institutional partnerships in Q2, including custody with Inspira Financial and brokerage access via Siebert/tZERO to remove accreditation barriers.
Recognized first income from the tokenized gold platform ($134k earned in Q2) proving the yield mechanism is repeatable.
summary: Streamex reported Q2 FY2026 net loss of $14.6 million (down from $46.7M in Q1) and operating expenses reduced by $20.4M due to lower stock-based compensation, while recognizing its first income stream of approximately $134k in gold lease revenue. Management provided no specific financial guidance but indicated that institutional adoption is expected as a catalyst in the third quarter following recent partnership integrations with Siebert Financial and Inspira Financial. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with $41.8M total liquidity, zero debt, and an operating cash burn run rate of approximately $1.1M/month excluding one-time items.

negative_highlights: International revenue decreased 5.8% YoY due to lease closures in the Middle East region
HWI blended RevPAR declined 3.8% YoY impacted by geopolitical conflict and Southeast Asia ramp-up challenges
First-half operational results were below expectation in some regions affected by severe weather
positive_highlights: China revenue grew 14.9% YoY driven by steady network expansion and RevPAR recovery
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 38.3%, with asset-light business delivering robust growth
Hanting Inn new version achieved meaningful RevPAR improvement and strong franchisee recognition
summary: In Q2 FY2026, H World Group reported revenue of RMB 7.1 billion (up 10.8% YoY) and adjusted net income of RMB 1.7 billion (up 26.9% YoY). Management maintained full-year guidance for hotel openings despite a slower first half due to supply chain issues, while keeping the full-year RevPAR outlook unchanged amidst macro uncertainties like extreme weather and geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East.

negative_highlights: Consolidated gross margin compressed to 26.7% due to inventory sold below cost for liquidity and portfolio rationalization.
One-time direct listing costs of approximately $1.4 million in deal fees plus non-cash accounting charges from convertible note conversion.
Wine and spirits revenue declined 3% YoY as the company deprioritizes legacy brands.
positive_highlights: Non-alcoholic and functional segment revenue increased 132% YoY to approximately $409,000 in Q2.
Core brands grew 12% YoY with product margins of 43.7%, significantly higher than legacy lines.
DTC and e-commerce revenue expanded more than fourfold (480%) year-over-year.
summary: Q2 FY26 net revenue was approximately $5.6 million (up 2% YoY), while core brands grew 12% and the non-alcoholic/functional segment surged 132%. The company reported a GAAP loss of $7.5M driven by one-time direct listing costs ($4.3M) and intentional inventory write-downs below cost to simplify the portfolio, resulting in compressed gross margins (26.7%). Management provided full-year guidance with net revenues at no less than $18.5 million.

negative_highlights: Total revenue decreased 4% year-over-year, missing expectations for broad-based AI-led expansion.
General business revenue fell 3% quarter-over-quarter and 4% year-over-year.
Management explicitly stated advertising businesses will remain under pressure in the second half due to deliberate monetization hold-back.
positive_highlights: AI Cloud Infra revenue increased 50% year-over-year, outpacing industry averages.
GPU cloud revenue accelerated sharply with +283% YoY growth and improved margins due to mix shift.
Apollo Go achieved a major milestone in Hong Kong as the first fully driverless testing provider in that market.
summary: Baidu reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of CNY 31.3 billion, a decrease of 4% year-over-year and 2% quarter-over-quarter, driven by declines in general business (CNY 25.2b) and iQIYI (down 5%). While AI Cloud Infra grew strongly at +50% YoY with GPU cloud revenue surging 283%, the overall miss on top-line growth resulted from pressure in advertising-related segments, leading to a net decline in total earnings.

negative_highlights: Q4 GAAP EPS declined from $0.27 to $0.01 due to lower net income
International sales down approximately 15% attributed to temporary contract manufacturer ramp-up issues
positive_highlights: Record Q4 bookings of $660 million, up 93% year-over-year
Full-year FY26 organic revenue growth accelerated to 7.9%
FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 217 bps YoY to 15.3%
summary: Mercury Systems reported record Q4 FY26 revenue of $290 million and full-year organic growth of 7.9%, driven by a massive 93% year-over-year increase in bookings to a new quarterly record of $660 million. Management raised its outlook for FY27, targeting low double-digit organic revenue growth while maintaining an adjusted EBITDA margin profile in the high teens and full-year FCF conversion near 35%. The company highlighted strong domestic demand (up 13%) and expanded backlog visibility to over $1.9 billion.

negative_highlights: Supply chain remains a governor on near-term revenue conversion due to incoming parts constraints
One-time tariff impact artificially inflated FY26 profitability which will not repeat in future periods
positive_highlights: Revenue of $1.846B beat expectations with 36% YoY growth; EPS of $3.70 up 79%
Wireline revenue in Communications Solutions Group hit a record billion-dollar quarter, surpassing wireless for the first time
summary: Keysight reported record Q3 FY26 results with revenue of $1.846 billion (up 36% YoY) and EPS of $3.70 (up 79%), both exceeding the high end of guidance. Operating margin expanded to 33.2%, up 820 bps, driven by strong core growth in Communications Solutions Group where wireline revenue hit a record billion-dollar quarter for the first time. Management raised full-year and Q4 outlooks citing robust demand across AI infrastructure, defense modernization, and semiconductor markets.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA declined 4.5%, primarily driven by a 21% drop in Argentina due to lower domestic passenger volumes and normalized cargo storage revenues.
Uruguay adjusted EBITDA fell 16% as non-recurring costs for the new ILS system implementation weighed on results before revenue recognition began in August.
Domestic traffic in Argentina declined approximately 8-12%, constrained by Flybondi's significantly reduced operating fleet and higher fuel prices.
positive_highlights: Total revenues grew 8% year-over-year outpacing traffic figures with revenue per passenger rising nearly 9% to $22.9.
Four of six segments delivered double-digit EBITDA growth led by Armenia (up 21%), Brazil, Italy, and Ecuador.
International demand remained healthy across the portfolio including a 6% increase in Argentina's international traffic.
summary: Total revenues excluding IFRIC 12 grew 8% year-over-year to outpace traffic figures, driven by double-digit growth in Armenia and Brazil despite a decline in Argentina's cargo business due to an exceptionally bad prior-year comparison base. Adjusted EBITDA fell 4.5%, with the majority of the miss concentrated in Argentina (down 21%) and Uruguay (down 16%), while four other segments delivered strong double-digit growth. The board approved a $150 million cash dividend for 2026, marking an important milestone in capital allocation.

negative_highlights: Total revenues decreased from $84.6 million in the prior period due to a decrease in paying users attributable to geopolitical events
Operating income declined significantly to $19.4 million compared with $30.6 million last year, driven by higher marketing spend and lower core business revenue
Management expects overall revenues for 2026 to remain broadly in line with last year despite the strong Q2 beat
positive_highlights: Revenues of $82.6 million exceeded the upper end of management's prior guidance
Non-GAAP net margin remained healthy at 41.7% despite a 106% increase in note and marketing expenses YoY
Game services revenue grew by 11.6% year-over-year to $34.2 million
summary: Yalla reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $82.6 million, which beat the upper end of guidance but represented a decline from last year due to geopolitical impacts on paying users. Non-GAAP net margin remained healthy at 41.7% despite doubling watching and marketing expenses YoY. Management maintained full-year revenue guidance broadly in line with expectations while noting potential for updates if new games perform strongly.

negative_highlights: Ball and Racket segment guidance was lowered for full-year sales growth from 12%-14% to approximately 14%, with management noting Q2's 24% pace is not sustainable.

Adjusted net finance costs of $21 million exceeded the prior guidance range due to higher hedging costs and currency losses, impacting bottom-line EPS by roughly $0.08 per share from tariff refunds only.
Corporate expenses increased significantly to $68 million versus $45 million last year due to higher IT investments and deferred compensation.
