positive_highlights: Revenue grew 32% on a reported basis and 30% ex-currency across all segments with double-digit growth in every region including Asia Pacific (+60%) and China (+36%).
Adjusted gross margin expanded to 65.8%, driven by underlying mix benefits of over 300 bps excluding the one-time tariff refund.
Salomon Softgoods led Outdoor Performance with strong footwear momentum, while Wilson Tennis 360 saw racket growth exceed 50% due to the Blade v10 launch.
summary: Amer Sports reported Q2 FY26 revenue growth of 32% (ex-currency) and adjusted EPS of $0.22 vs prior year's $0.06, driven by strong performance across Arc'teryx, Salomon Softgoods, and Wilson Tennis 360 segments with double-digit growth in all regions. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately 24% from the previous 20%-22%, along with increases in adjusted operating margin guidance to 14.2%-14.5%. The quarter featured significant one-time net tariff refund benefits of $64.3 million, which inflated reported margins but management clarified that underlying organic expansion remains robust.

negative_highlights: Total revenue declined 5.9% to $18.2 million, driven by a 13.1% drop in the MeowGo business
Gross margins contracted from 52.8% to 50.2%, with service gross margins falling sharply from 56.6% to 39.1%
Full-year revenue guidance was lowered by $10M-$15M due to macroeconomic headwinds and geopolitical tensions
positive_highlights: GlocalMe IoT revenue surged 392.4% year-over-year, growing from $0.2 million to $0.8 million
GlocalMe SIM business grew by 78%, increasing revenue contribution significantly
New product lines including PetPhone and CPE R50/R55 demonstrated strong momentum with positive market feedback
summary: Total revenue decreased by 5.9% to $18.2 million in Q2 FY26 due to macroeconomic headwinds and a significant surge in chip costs affecting the uCloudlink 1.0 business line, while new growth engines like GlocalMe IoT showed strong YoY expansion of 392.4%. Management revised full-year guidance downward from $85M-$100M to $75M-$85M citing persistent macroeconomic challenges and global trade headwinds.

negative_highlights: Gross margin expansion was largely offset by incremental cost pressures related to fuel, energy, and product inputs (approx. 60 bps).
Larger discretionary projects remain under pressure due to consumer uncertainty and housing affordability issues.
Inventory turns declined from 4.6x to 4.5x as merchandise inventories rose by approximately $2 billion.
positive_highlights: Sales increased $2.6 billion or 5.7% YoY to $47.9B driven by broad-based demand across the business.
Adjusted EPS of $4.92 beat expectations, aided by a one-time tariff refund benefit that reduced COGS by $685 million.
International performance was strong with Canada and Mexico out-competing the company average.
summary: Home Depot reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $47.9 billion (up 5.7% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $4.92 (up 5.1%), exceeding expectations driven by a one-time IEEPA tariff refund benefit that boosted gross margin to 33.7%. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, projecting comp sales growth between flat to 2%, with the Q2 tariff windfall expected to be fully offset in Q3 and Q4 by incremental fuel, energy, and commodity cost pressures. While international (Canada/Mexico) and Pro segments showed strength, management noted continued pressure on larger discretionary projects and a frozen housing market.

negative_highlights: SGI segment recorded an operating loss of RMB 64 million as the company continues heavy investment in product development for actuation modules and Kosmo.
Kosmo revenue contribution is expected to be small (low eight digits) this year, with significant ramp-up anticipated only starting Q3.
positive_highlights: SGI segment recorded first-ever revenue contribution of RMB 45 million driven by robotic actuation module sales to Sharpa.
Management raised full-year 2026 SGI guidance from RMB 100M to a range of RMB 200-300M due to demand exceeding expectations.
Robotics LiDAR shipments surged approximately 193% YoY, while total ADAS and robotics combined growth was nearly 80%.
summary: Hesai Group reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of RMB 861 million (up ~22% YoY), driven by a core LiDAR business generating RMB 816 million and the debut of Strategic Growth Initiatives (SGI) at RMB 45 million. Management raised full-year 2026 SGI revenue guidance from RMB 100 million to RMB 200-300 million, citing faster-than-expected commercialization of robotic actuation modules and Kosmo spatial intelligence platform revenues expected in Q3.

negative_highlights: Intelligent solutions revenue growth moderated to just 4% due to delivery fluctuations from domain controllers.
Net cash used in operating activities increased slightly year-over-year, though attributed to normal working capital and strategic inventory investment for fleet expansion.
positive_highlights: Robotaxi revenue surged 691% year-over-year to a record $12.1 million.
Fare charging revenue jumped nearly 8x compared to the prior year period.
Operating loss narrowed by over 30% YoY as non-GAAP operating expenses grew at only 9.6%, significantly outpaced by top-line growth.
summary: Pony.ai reported Q2 FY26 total revenue of $36.2 million, a 69% year-over-year increase driven by robotaxi revenues reaching a record high of $12.1 million (up 691%) and fare charging revenues surging nearly 8x to over 40%. Operating loss narrowed significantly from -$75M in Q2 FY25 to -$45.4M, with non-GAAP operating expenses growing at only 9.6% while revenue grew by 69%, demonstrating strong operating leverage.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue decreased by approximately $0.2 million (40% YoY) primarily due to the conclusion of AgPlenus' agreement with Bayer in May.
First-half revenues declined significantly from $2.9 million in H1 2025 to $0.7 million, largely attributable to lower Casterra sales following significant seed revenue last year.
APH1 herbicide program was discontinued by partner Bayer because the target protein proved non-essential for weed survival.
positive_highlights: Net loss improved by approximately $2.9 million (nearly 62%) compared to Q2 2025 due to lower operating expenses.
Successfully completed hit-to-lead milestones on two of six active drug development collaborations with results exceeding partner expectations.
Reduced consolidated cash usage in the quarter to approximately $2.1 million, aligning with a full-year burn expectation range of ILS 8.5M-$9.5M.
summary: Evogene reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $0.3 million compared to $0.5 million in the prior year period, a decrease driven by the conclusion of an agreement with Bayer and lower sales from Casterra. The company's net loss narrowed significantly to approximately $1.8 million from $4.7 million in Q2 2025 due to reduced operating expenses and discontinued operations losses. Management highlighted strategic progress including six active drug development agreements, successful hit-to-lead milestones on two programs, and a reduction in cash burn expectations for the full year.

negative_highlights: Full-year GMV guidance was lowered to $149-151 billion (from above $155 billion) due to a measured view of German volumes where retail sales grew less than 1% in real terms.
U.S. revenue growth slowed sequentially compared to Q2 as the company completed back book receivable sales that were not repeated, causing reported take rates to dip slightly.
German consumer discretionary spending remains soft with no immediate recovery expected for H2.
positive_highlights: Transaction margin dollars grew at 42%, significantly outpacing revenue growth of 27% and volume growth of 18%.
Fair Financing (big-ticket spend) GMV surged 82% year-over-year to $4.7 billion, now representing 13% of total volume.
Klarna membership reached 2 million paying subscribers with subscription revenue growing over 600%, decoupling growth from pure transaction volume.
summary: Klarna delivered a strong quarter with revenue of $1.04 billion (up 27%) and transaction margin dollars rising 42% to $446 million, beating the high end of guidance on every line item for two consecutive quarters. Management raised its full-year adjusted operating income outlook by approximately $35-40 million due to stronger unit economics, despite a downward revision to the GMV forecast driven primarily by softer-than-expected consumer sentiment in Germany.

negative_highlights: Membership services revenue declined sequentially by 4% to RMB 4.0 billion due to seasonality and lack of blockbuster content.
Online advertising revenue remained flat at RMB 1.2 billion sequentially with no year-over-year growth mentioned for the quarter.
Other revenues fell 17% sequentially, indicating weakness in non-core business segments.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed by 8% sequentially to RMB 130.3 million due to disciplined marketing spend and improved content efficiency.
Overseas membership revenue surged with Brazil up 215%, Mexico up 150%, and Thailand showing steady growth on a profitable basis.
Brand advertising delivered double-digit year-over-year growth, particularly in beauty, personal care, healthcare, and AI application sectors.
summary: Total revenues were RMB 6.3 billion, up 1% sequentially but down year-over-year due to a 4% decline in membership services revenue driven by seasonality and the absence of major hits like 'The Legend'. Non-GAAP operating loss narrowed substantially from Q1 (RMB 148.6 million) to RMB 130.3 million, approaching breakeven as AI-driven cost efficiencies began materializing.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at -$19 million for the quarter due to high marketing investment.
Net loss per share was $0.52, down from a prior year loss of $0.94 but still representing an operating deficit.
positive_highlights: Revenue beat guidance of $46M-$48M with total revenue at $45 million for IM8 and $46.5 million consolidated.
Gross margin expanded significantly to 65% in Q2, up from prior periods.
Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) improved by roughly 21% sequentially despite doubling acquisition spend.
summary: The company reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $46.5 million (up 3.9x YoY), with IM8 contributing $45 million at a gross margin expansion to 65%. Management raised full-year total revenue guidance to $220-$230 million and initiated 2027 projections, citing record July performance where CAC fell 21% despite doubled acquisition spend. The business crossed into positive adjusted free cash flow in Q2 due to a new funding facility.

negative_highlights: Cash on hand of $1.8 million is explicitly stated as insufficient to fund operations for the next 12 months without additional financing.
The company faces substantial doubt regarding its ability to continue as a going concern due to liquidity constraints and accumulated deficit of $138 million.
Vivos is not in compliance with Nasdaq minimum stockholders' equity requirements ($2.5 million) and faces potential delisting proceedings.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 35% year-over-year to $5.2 million, driven by a $1.9 million increase in service revenue from SCN diagnostic services and treatment.
Gross margin expanded to 57% for the quarter as revenue growth outpaced cost increases associated with new staff and facilities.
Referral volume from SCN physicians to SAMC centers has increased three to four times since the end of Q2, indicating strong operational synergy.
summary: Vivos Therapeutics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.2 million, a 35% year-over-year increase driven by service revenue growth from the Sleep Center of Nevada (SCN) acquisition, while product revenue declined due to a strategic pivot away from VIPs. The company incurred a net loss of $5.5 million and ended the quarter with only $1.8 million in cash, explicitly stating that existing funds are insufficient to fund operations for the next 12 months without additional financing. Management highlighted significant headwinds including non-compliance with Nasdaq minimum equity requirements and substantial doubt regarding the company's ability to continue as a going concern.

negative_highlights: Solar PLF declined due to a mix of curtailment (approx. half) and adverse weather patterns, impacting capacity utilization
Manufacturing margins contracted from last year's Q1 level of 40% down to the current quarter's 34%
Grid connectivity issues in Rajasthan continue to cause temporary curtailments for certain projects
positive_highlights: Operating portfolio grew 26% YoY to 13.5 GW with over 1 GW commissioned in Q1 FY27
Profit after tax increased by 16% year-over-year to INR 6 billion, aided by a significant one-time cash inflow of INR 57 billion from Andhra Pradesh DISCOM post-quarter end
Manufacturing business delivered strong external sales with adjusted EBITDA margin at 34%
summary: ReNew reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of INR 44.6 billion (up 14% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR 30.4 billion (up 12% YoY), driven by a 26% growth in its operating portfolio to 13.5 GW. Management reiterated full-year FY2027 consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance of INR 103-109 billion, maintaining the range despite acknowledging margin contraction in manufacturing and curtailment impacts on solar PLF.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA loss widened significantly from negative $21 million to negative $34.6 million due to heavy R&D and corporate infrastructure spending.
R&D expenditure rose sharply to SEK equivalent of roughly $20.4 million in H1, up from $13 million the prior year.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew 26% YoY on a constant currency basis driven by expansion within existing customers and new deployments.
Signed partnership to deploy 500 Tesla Semi trucks which will triple the fleet size upon completion in late 2027.
Sales pipeline increased three-fold following concerted sales team investments.
summary: Einride reported H1 FY26 revenue of EUR 27 million (up 26% YoY), but Adjusted EBITDA widened to a loss of $34.6 million from negative $21 million in the prior year due to increased R&D and IPO preparation costs. Management guided for constant currency revenue growth to double in H2, expecting EUR 39-42 million (driven by Amazon and Tesla Semi ramp), which would result in an annualized run rate of EUR 85-95 million by December. The company reiterated a path to cash flow breakeven in late 2028 with a deployed fleet of 1,500-2,000 vehicles.

negative_highlights: Cash gross margin decreased slightly to 41.8% from 43.6% YoY, primarily due to higher utility costs passed through to customers.
Wholesale revenue growth (29.3%) was lower than the total net revenue growth rate of 14.2%, indicating retail and non-IDC segments contributed less aggressively.
positive_highlights: Wholesale capacity in service rose by 49.4% year-over-year to surpass the 1 GW milestone at 1,007 MW with a utilization rate of 73.9%.
Secured 345 MW in new order wins during Q2 from leading cloud providers and AI-native companies, bringing total H1 orders to 862 MW.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 33.0%, reflecting ongoing operational efficiency enhancements.
summary: VNET reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 2.78 billion (up 14.2% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of RMB 918.3 million (up 25.4% YoY), driven by a robust wholesale IDC business that surpassed the 1 GW capacity milestone in service. Management reiterated full-year guidance for net revenues between RMB 11.5 billion-RMB 11.8 billion and adjusted EBITDA of RMB 3.55 billion-RMB 3.75 billion, maintaining unchanged estimates despite a slight sequential decline in cash gross margin attributed to higher utility pass-through costs.

negative_highlights: Adjusted operating margin contracted significantly due to the exit of Homestyles ($1.8M sales decline) and lack of prior year foreign currency gains.
Q4 guidance for Q1 FY27 (6.5%-7% margins) is lower than current performance, citing rising energy prices and supply chain inflation pressures.
Demand environment weakened significantly following geopolitical events, with consumer confidence remaining subdued.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 4% over FY26 and delivered record adjusted EPS of $4.94 despite a challenging macro environment.
Free cash flow generation exceeded $47 million, enabling a 25% dividend increase and share repurchases.
Health and wellness category continued to deliver positive year-over-year growth.
summary: Flexsteel reported Q4 FY26 net sales of $115.4 million (up 0.7% YoY) and adjusted operating margins of 7.1%, down from the prior year's 9.0%. The quarter included a one-time benefit of tariff refunds but also reflected costs associated with exiting the Homestyles ready-to-assemble category, which contributed roughly $12 million in sales for the fiscal year.

negative_highlights: Management explicitly warned that the annualized revenue figure of $414 million is a mathematical equivalent only and should not be treated as a full-year forecast.
The Q&A session focused heavily on explaining why market capitalization remains low despite high revenues, citing a lack of retail support from investment banks following their direct listing.
No specific guidance was provided for the second half of FY26 or FY27; management only stated they are pursuing a previously announced $430M objective without confirming if it is achievable.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew approximately 59% year-over-year to $207 million for the first half of FY26.
Adjusted EBITDA run rate increased significantly from ~$190k in Q1 to over $700k in Q2 due to gross margin expansion and integration efficiencies.
Gross profit expanded by approximately 26% year-over-year, improving the company's profitability profile.
summary: For the first half of FY26 (Q1+Q2), iQSTEL reported $207 million in revenue versus approximately $130 million year-ago, representing a 59% increase. The company highlighted that its annualized run rate is now roughly $414 million but explicitly stated this figure should not be considered a forecast for the full fiscal year. Management noted significant margin expansion with gross profit growing from $3.8M to $4.8M and adjusted EBITDA rising from ~$0.2M in Q1 to over $0.7M in Q2, driven by integration synergies.

negative_highlights: Global Solutions segment revenue decreased 5% year-over-year to $27.6 million due to the non-repetition of a specific aircraft sale.
Backlog coverage ratio declined from 86% in Q1 to 71% in Q2 as note weakness in-cycle orders were delivered, reducing funded visibility.
positive_highlights: Revenue surged 100% year-over-year to $201.8 million driven by the Deep Strike program execution.
Net income swung from a loss of $11.8 million in Q2 FY2025 to a profit of $6.7 million in Q2 FY2026.
Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded significantly year-over-year, with the tactical systems segment reaching 17% margin.
summary: AEVEX reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $201.8 million, representing a 100% year-over-year increase driven by the tactical systems segment and the Deep Strike program. Net income turned positive at $6.7 million compared to a loss in the prior year, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding significantly. The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire BlackSea Technologies for up to $650 million and raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a midpoint of $710 million.

negative_highlights: Equity notional volume showed softness compared to June, attributed to the SpaceX event rather than a structural trend.
Crypto revenue remains low at approximately $2.25 million (just over 1% of total Q2 revenue), though prediction markets are growing rapidly.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly revenue of $198.8 million and record adjusted operating profit of $62.6 million driven by the PDT Rule elimination tailwind.
Customer assets surged to a record $28.5 billion, representing 79% year-over-year growth with average account size doubling to over $5,500.
Options volume reached 213 million contracts (up 68% YoY) and Webull secured its first-ever top-five position among retail brokers in options.
summary: Webull reported record Q2 FY26 revenue of $198.8 million (up 51% YoY) and adjusted operating profit of $62.6 million (up 169% YoY), driven by the successful navigation of the SEC's elimination of the Pattern Day Trader Rule which boosted options volume to a top-five industry position. Adjusted operating margin expanded significantly to 31.5%, while customer assets grew 79% year-over-year to $28.5 billion, with net deposits reaching $1.6 billion.

negative_highlights: Comparable average transactions declined 2.1%, primarily due to pressure in weather-sensitive outdoor categories during Memorial Day weekend.
Gross margin contracted 80 bps YoY, with elevated fuel and transportation costs largely offsetting the $30 bps tariff refund benefit.
Full-year outlook revised down as residential construction pressures impact acquisitions FBM (45% exposed) and ADG.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS exceeded expectations even excluding $0.11 benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds ($96M pre-tax charges).
Delivered five consecutive quarters of positive comparable sales, demonstrating strategy resilience across changing economic conditions.
Online sales grew 15.7% driven by digital experience investments and the Mylow AI agent which triples conversion rates for users.
summary: Lowe's reported Q2 sales of $26 billion (up 8.3% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $4.40, beating expectations despite a soft comparable sales increase of only 0.2%. Management updated full-year guidance to the low end of the previous range ($92B sales, ~11.6% operating margin), citing elevated fuel/transportation costs offsetting tariff benefits and persistent pressure on DIY demand from weather and macro uncertainty.

negative_highlights: Enterprise cloud services declined slightly by 1% year-over-year to RMB 740 million due to upstream supply pricing hikes affecting SOE/government customers.
Capital expenditures were high at RMB 3.3 billion in the quarter, with full-year CapEx remaining fixed at RMB 15 billion despite volatile monthly purchasing patterns.
positive_highlights: Total revenue reached a record RMB 3.07 billion, up 31% year-over-year and 40% quarter-over-quarter.
AI cloud gross billings surged to RMB 1.33 billion (+82%), accounting for over half of public cloud revenue.
Adjusted operating profit turned positive at RMB 124 million, marking a turnaround from an adjusted loss in the prior year.
summary: Kingsoft Cloud reported Q2 FY26 revenue of RMB 3.07 billion (up 31% YoY), driven by a record AI cloud gross billing of RMB 1.33 billion (+82% YoY). Adjusted operating profit turned positive for the first time with an adjusted margin of 4%, while full-year CapEx guidance remains unchanged at RMB 15 billion despite high quarterly spend.

negative_highlights: Management expects Q3 lithium gross margins to be similar to Q2, implying no immediate expansion despite volume strength.
Supply constraints in certain markets are expected to gradually normalize toward the end of the year, potentially dampening price premiums.
BESS inventory builds and project implementation delays may lead to a slowdown in battery storage demand growth over the next 12-18 months.
positive_highlights: Record quarterly lithium sales volumes of more than 84,000 metric tons achieved from operations in Chile and Australia.
Lithium prices increased during the second quarter supported by stronger-than-expected market demand.
Iodine business delivered good results with robust market demand and favorable pricing.
summary: SQM reported a strong second quarter of FY26 with record quarterly lithium sales volumes exceeding 84,000 metric tons and robust iodine results supported by favorable pricing. Management raised full-year global demand expectations to over 2.1 million metric tons and updated capital expenditure guidance to approximately $3 billion for the 2026-2028 period to support growth initiatives like Salar Futuro. While Q3 lithium prices are expected to be flat, volumes remain strong with a potential upside in Q4.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue declined sequentially from Q1 due to lower solar cell sales volume despite strong module growth.
Shipment timing was affected by CBP reviews and detentions of Ethiopian facility products during the quarter.
Management explicitly stated that previously issued full-year guidance is no longer relevant until clarity emerges on regulatory issues.
positive_highlights: First-half revenue surged 87.6% year-over-year to $261 million driven by higher solar cell, module sales, and OEM services.
Gross margin nearly doubled in the first half from 16.6% to 32.5%, reflecting improved production consistency and mix shifts.
Management confirmed that Section 232 policy is viewed as a positive risk development supporting U.S. manufacturing strategy.
summary: TOYO reported strong first-half revenue of $261 million (up 87.6% YoY) and Q2 revenue of $118.2 million (up 35% YoY), driven by module sales, though Q2 saw a sequential decline due to lower cell mix. Gross margins expanded significantly in the first half to 32.5%, but management explicitly declined to reaffirm full-year guidance citing near-term uncertainties regarding CBP detentions and Section 232 tariff negotiations.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted to 34% from 55% in Q2 2025 due to a higher reduce exposure note mix and elevated costs.
Revenue missed the original full guidance of $55 million-$60 million because retail revenue was deconsolidated.
Adjusted EBITDA fell sharply to $5.7 million from $18.1 million in Q2 2025.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $47 million beat the adjusted guidance range excluding retail revenue.
Cost of production improved significantly to $122 per pound from $175 in Q1 and $129 last year.
Wholesale note price increased to $211 per pound, exceeding the original guidance of $185-$190.
summary: Second quarter revenue was $47 million, missing the prior guidance of $55 million-$60 million due to a deconsolidation of retail operations and unfavorable product mix. Gross margin declined from 55% in Q2 2025 to 34% in Q2 2026 driven by a higher proportion of low-value trim in the production mix and elevated costs of $122 per pound. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.7 million, significantly below last year's $18.1 million but an improvement from the first quarter loss.

negative_highlights: Adjusted non-GAAP gross margin remained negative at -19.9%
Operating cash flow was -$54 million with significant outflows for R&D
Automotive results were softer, offsetting gains in data centers and materials
positive_highlights: AI data center revenue more than doubled from fiscal 2025 versus fiscal 2026
Power segment grew approximately 20% sequentially in Q4 driven by AI demand
Debt conversion of $46 million reduced net debt to ~$600M and saved annual interest
summary: Wolfspeed reported Q4 FY26 revenue of $150 million, meeting the midpoint of guidance and showing a 6% sequential increase driven by AI data center growth which more than doubled from fiscal 2025. Adjusted non-GAAP gross margin was -19.9%, reflecting continued underutilization despite product mix improvements, while operating cash flow remained negative at -$54 million due to debt service and R&D investments.

negative_highlights: Q4 net new customer additions of ~1,800 were below recent trends due to deliberate prioritization of higher-quality customers and organizational restructuring.
S&E revenue faces a specific headwind from card acceptance challenges with large ad providers (Meta/Google) impacting volume growth by approximately 2 points YoY in Q4 FY2027 guidance.
TPV mix contraction compressed the AP/AR take rate to 16.0 bps, down 0.5 bps sequentially.
positive_highlights: Core revenue grew 16% year-over-year to $400.5 million with non-GAAP operating margin expanding 370 bps sequentially to 23%.
Customer spend on AI increased over 50% year-over-year, and TPV from AI-first customers nearly doubled quarter-over-quarter.
Invoice financing volume and revenue grew approximately 30% YoY with expected loss rates improving by more than 50%.
summary: BILL reported Q4 FY2026 core revenue of $400.5 million (up 16% YoY) and non-GAAP operating margin expanding to 23%. Management raised full-year FY2027 guidance for total revenue ($1.807B-$1.857B, +9%-12%) and EPS ($3.56-$3.79), while explicitly noting headwinds from S&E card acceptance dynamics and go-to-market restructuring that will impact Q1 FY2027.

negative_highlights: Haircare did not return to organic sales growth yet, though evidence of Aveda's turnaround in the U.S. is emerging.
Middle East conflict disruptions reduced EUKEM (Europe, UK, Middle East) growth by approximately 2%.
positive_highlights: Organic sales grew 3% with broad-based performance across categories; makeup trend improved by 500 bps to stabilize.
Gross margin expanded 150 basis points while operating margins rose significantly, funding additional consumer-facing investments.
Fiscal 2027 guidance was raised on profitability (operating margin) and sales growth acceleration is expected in North America.
summary: The company reported a strong beat with organic sales rising 3% and diluted EPS growing 66%, significantly exceeding the initial outlook from August. Operating margins expanded by 320 basis points to reach an annualized run-rate that prompted management to raise their fiscal 2027 operating margin guidance range to 12.7%-13.5%. Management expressed high confidence in accelerating growth for fiscal 2027, citing a diversified portfolio of billion-dollar brands and successful execution across all regions.

negative_highlights: Consolidated delivered sales were down 1% excluding divestitures due to lower wholesale performance
Joybird business experienced a significant decline with written sales decreasing 17%
Adjusted operating margin contracted to 3.9% from 4.8% last year driven by fixed cost deleverage and friction costs
positive_highlights: Retail written sales increased 16% driven by new/acquired stores and positive same-store growth
Company returned $35 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, a 62% increase versus the prior year
Wholesale backlog remains solid entering Q2 despite choppy order patterns
summary: Fiscal Q1 FY27 consolidated delivered sales declined 3% reported (down 1% excluding case goods divestitures) while retail same-store sales slipped slightly despite a strong 16% growth in written sales. Adjusted operating income was $19 million, down from the prior year due to deleverage on lower wholesale and Joybird volume alongside friction costs from strategic investments like plant consolidations. Management provided cautious guidance for Q2 adjusted margins of 4%-5.5%, citing uneven demand patterns and ongoing supply chain transformation expenses.

negative_highlights: Advertising revenue declined 1% YoY due to softer demand in key verticals like handsets and cosmetics.
Operating margin contracted significantly from 36% last year to 28% primarily driven by higher ad production costs and marketing expenses.
Management warned of pressure on Q3 advertising growth due to a high revenue base established during the previous food delivery price war.
positive_highlights: Value-added service revenue surged 19% YoY driven by membership services and one-off ticket purchases.
Ad revenues from Automobile (+NEV launches) and Internet Services (AI demand) delivered solid growth despite broader market softness.
Video consumption metrics showed double-digit year-over-year growth with improved high-quality content supply.
summary: Weibo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $453.8 million (up 2% YoY) and ad revenue of $381 million (down 1% YoY), while value-added services grew to $72.9 million (+19%). Operating income was $125.4 million with a margin of 28%, down from 36% last year due to higher costs, though net margins remained at 23%. Management expressed caution regarding the second half outlook, citing persistent macro headwinds in consumption and advertising budgets for sectors like handsets and e-commerce.

negative_highlights: Marmaxx comparable sales increased only 1% and were below expectations, driven by a small decrease in customer transactions.
Adjusted SG&A was unfavorable by 20 basis points versus last year due to incremental store wage and payroll costs.
Full-year adjusted gross margin guidance is down 40-50 bps for the back half primarily due to higher fuel costs.
positive_highlights: Consolidated comparable sales increased 4%, driven by higher average basket size across all banners except Marmaxx.
HomeGoods delivered an outstanding 7% comp sales increase, while TJX Canada and International divisions grew comps by 6%-7%.
Adjusted pre-tax profit margin expanded to 11.9%, up 50 basis points versus last year due to merchandise margin favorability from tariff changes.
summary: TJX reported Q2 FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS of $1.22 (up 11% YoY) and consolidated comparable sales growth of 4%, both significantly above plan despite a miss at the Marmaxx division which was attributed to self-inflicted execution issues regarding merchandise mix. Management raised full-year guidance for pre-tax profit margin, gross margin, and EPS, citing strong performance in HomeGoods (7% comp), TJX Canada (6%), and International divisions offsetting the weaker US apparel results.

negative_highlights: Management maintained full-year revenue guidance despite Q2 strength, indicating caution regarding H2 seasonality or potential Lantheus TruVu launch impacts.
R&D investment increased significantly to AUD $130 million (up from prior periods) as the company prioritizes late-stage clinical programs over maximizing near-term earnings.
positive_highlights: Precision medicine revenue grew 27% YoY with gross margins expanding 100 bps to 65% due to pricing discipline and manufacturing efficiencies.
BiPASS study enrollment is proceeding rapidly, with the Melbourne site alone enrolling a significant proportion of patients before other sites opened.
Zircaix received Breakthrough Therapy designation in the U.S. and remains on track for resubmission following an administrative FDA delay.
summary: Telix reported H1 FY26 revenue of AUD $477 million (up 22% YoY) and EBITDA of AUD $52 million (up 146% YoY), driven by a precision medicine business delivering AUD $390 million in sales. Management maintained full-year guidance for the upper end of its range, citing strong Q2 execution but noting that R&D spend increased to fund late-stage assets like BiPASS and Zircaix.

negative_highlights: Asia home base continues to phase out as the company shifts towards higher-value Western markets.
Q3 revenue guidance ($181M-$183M) implies a slight deceleration in growth rate compared to Q2's 25% pace.
positive_highlights: Revenue of $178.1M beat top-of-range guidance with YoY growth accelerating from 23% in Q1 to 25% in Q2.
Adjusted EBITDA hit a quarterly record of $42.4 million, representing a margin expansion to 24%. Marketing spend declined sequentially by 6% while revenue grew.
Total addressable audience reached beyond 700 million users via OEM white label solutions and SDKs, up from 500 million six months ago.
summary: Second quarter revenue of $178 million beat the top of guidance and grew 25% year-over-year to surpass seasonal peaks early in the year. Adjusted EBITDA reached a quarterly record of $42.4 million (24% margin), exceeding expectations with growth fueled by advertising (+27%) and carrier revenue (+21%). Management raised full-year revenue guidance by adding $2-$5 million above Q2 overperformance, citing strong momentum entering the second half.

negative_highlights: Adjusted gross margin declined 140 bps year-over-year to 60.9% due to lower volumes, excess inventory, and tariffs.
Prestige fragrance note-out remained negative (-1%) in the second half with flankers lacking differentiation.
Consumer Beauty adjusted EBITDA fell 67% year-over-year primarily from supply chain cost absorption.
positive_highlights: Q4 like-for-like sales down only 1%, beating the guidance range for a mid-single-digit decline.
Free cash flow of $348 million was well ahead of expectations, driven by strong working capital management and reduced CapEx.
Consumer Beauty adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially in Q4 supported by tighter cost control.
summary: Coty reported Q4 FY2026 like-for-like sales down 1%, beating the guidance of a mid-single-digit decline and exceeding expectations despite macro volatility. Adjusted EPS came in at breakeven for the quarter (excluding equity swap), while free cash flow reached $348 million, significantly ahead of guidance due to disciplined working capital management. Management provided no full-year FY2027 guidance but forecast Q1 sales declines of low-to-mid-single-digits and EBITDA declines in the low teens as they navigate a transition year involving portfolio simplification and an upcoming Gucci exit.

negative_highlights: Fuel price volatility in late Q2 temporarily dampened demand for low-value freight before easing from June onwards.
Extreme weather events including typhoons and flooding caused near-term disruptions to transportation activities across various parts of China.
positive_highlights: Transaction service revenue grew rapidly at +33.1% YoY driven by full commission network rollout and improved monetization per order.
Net cash provided by operating activities reached RMB 2.15 billion, supporting liquidity for new initiatives and shareholder dividends.
summary: Full Truck Alliance reported Q2 FY26 net revenues of RMB 3.38 billion (up 4.4% YoY) and GAAP-adjusted net income of RMB 1.43 billion (up 6% YoY). Transaction service revenue surged 33.1% to RMB 1.77 billion, driven by a commission network rollout reaching 94.7% penetration across eligible cities. Management raised the platform-wide fulfillment rate record high to 47%, up 2.9 percentage points quarter-over-quarter.

negative_highlights: Total outstanding loan balance fell 13.5% YoY reflecting weak demand in the SBO segment
Net loss continued for the quarter with credit costs remaining elevated relative to income base
Industry margins are narrowing due to regulatory fee transparency requirements and interest rate compression
positive_highlights: New loan sales increased to RMB 51.1 billion, up 4.6% YoY and 4.8% QoQ
Consumer finance new loans grew strongly at +27.6% YoY to RMB 36.9 billion as the company gains share in a contracting market
Asset quality improved sequentially with CM3 flow rate dropping from 1.2% (Q1) to 1.0% (Q2)
summary: Total income declined by 15.5% year-over-year in Q2 FY26 due to a contraction in the Rongyi loan balance and elevated credit costs amidst weak small business demand. While new loan sales grew sequentially (+4.8%) and asset quality metrics improved (CM3 flow rate down, NPL ratio stable), management explicitly stated that net loss continued for the quarter despite sequential narrowing from last year.

negative_highlights: Rising diesel costs in the second quarter added roughly CNY 0.02 to per-parcel transportation cost, weighing on margins temporarily.
Management noted that global oil price environments remain highly uncertain for the remainder of the year.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income surged 50.3% year over year to CNY 3.1 billion.
Combined unit cost of transportation and sorting declined by CNY 0.02 despite oil price pressures, aided by intelligent routing that grew route-coordinated volume by 120% YoY.
Retail parcel volume expanded significantly with reverse logistics daily average reaching approximately 9.8 million pieces.
summary: ZTO reported Q2 FY26 revenue of CNY 14.5 billion (up 23% YoY) and adjusted net income of CNY 3.1 billion (up 50.3% YoY), driven by a 6.5% increase in parcel volume to 10.49 billion pieces. Management raised full-year parcel volume guidance to a range of 40.83-42.37 billion, reflecting an updated growth expectation of 6%-10%. Despite rising oil prices adding CNY 0.02 per parcel cost in the quarter, combined unit transportation and sorting costs decreased by CNY 0.02 due to AI-driven efficiency gains.

negative_highlights: Spot rates softened significantly over the last few weeks after an early-year spike, dropping to around $30k for round trips by late Q2.
Vessel OpEx increased quarter-over-quarter due to higher crew travel costs related to disruptions in the Middle East and Strait of Hormuz closures.
Global LNG trade volumes were broadly flat year-to-date (down less than 1%), with Europe imports down compared to last year despite resilience elsewhere.
positive_highlights: Revenues reached close to $107M in Q2, marking the second-best quarter since Q4 2021 driven by high spot earnings on Flex Volunteer and Flex Artemis.
The board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.75 per share for the 20th consecutive time, bringing total dividends paid over the last 12 months to $3 per share.
Fleet average TCE ended at $86,100 per day with strong cash flow from operations of $63 million generated in the quarter.
summary: FLEX LNG reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $106.8 million (excluding EUAs) and net income of $44.9 million ($0.83 EPS), representing a significant improvement over the first quarter but missing prior full-year guidance expectations for revenue growth due to softening spot rates in late summer. Management maintained its full year 2026 guidance, expecting revenues between $345-$370 million and TCE between $73k-$78k per day, citing strong contract coverage of ~89% for remaining available days despite geopolitical disruptions from the Iran conflict reducing Middle East exports.

negative_highlights: Historically low water levels on the Danube and Rhine impacted over 50% of river capacity PCDs in Q3 with an estimated 10-12% cancellations.
Company issued future cruise vouchers to affected guests, creating a financial impact extending beyond 2026 into 2027/2028 as they are redeemed.
Adjusted gross margin for the full year is expected to be impacted by incremental expenses related to low water conditions and voucher issuances.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased 16.5% YoY to $2.2 billion, driven by a 10.9% increase in capacity PCDs and higher Net Yield of $645 (+6.2%).
Advanced bookings for the 2027 season are up 21% year-over-year at this point in time with rates equal to or above prior seasons.
India itinerary for 2027/2028 is completely sold out, and China outbound business continues to expand.
summary: Viking reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $2.2 billion (up 16.5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $748 million (up 18.2% YoY), driven by capacity expansion and higher yields despite low water levels affecting European rivers in July-August. Management noted that Q3 will likely reflect the financial impact of issuing future cruise vouchers to affected guests, with potential margin pressure extending into 2026-2027. The company remains confident in its booking curves for 2027 (53% booked) and fleet expansion strategy.

negative_highlights: GAAP gross margin declined to 17.8% due to a significant non-cash depreciation charge included in Cost of Revenues.
Net loss remains substantial at $3.1 million ($0.14/share), indicating the business has not yet achieved GAAP profitability despite revenue growth.
Management explicitly stated they cannot segment revenues by product or geography, limiting visibility into specific high-growth verticals like AI data centers.
positive_highlights: Revenue re-accelerated with a 21% YoY increase and a massive 174% QoQ jump from Q1.
Backlog conversion was strong, ending June at $5.4 million after booking over $500k in drone/robotics orders in a single week.
Operating expenses decreased to $4.5M YoY (excluding one-time stock grants), reflecting disciplined cost management and the impact of relocating manufacturing from San Diego to Yuma, Arizona.
summary: Beam Global reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $8.6 million, a 21% year-over-year increase and a sharp rebound from the first quarter, driven by backlog conversion and new orders in Europe and drone sectors. Gross margin contracted to 17.8% GAAP (down from 20.3%) due to non-cash depreciation of $700k included in cost of revenues; excluding these items, adjusted gross margin was 26.2%. The company narrowed its net loss to $3.1 million ($0.14/share) compared to a prior year loss of $4.3 million, aided by reduced operating expenses and the absence of last year's goodwill impairment.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue of $6.7 million is far below the implied run-rate needed to meet a $200M annual target given current progress.
Management explicitly stated that Q3 will be 'drastically impacted' by licensing activity, suggesting significant near-term growth has not yet materialized in reported results.
Revenue recognition remains subject to regulatory audit and SEC oversight regarding tokenomics, introducing uncertainty on timing.
positive_highlights: Reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $200 million despite a weak Q2 performance.
Signed definitive agreements for CyberCatch acquisition ($94M cash) and BankWyse bank charter conversion, expanding the platform's security and banking capabilities.
Secured over 1 billion shares outstanding through financing activities including Vivasor stock swap.
summary: Datavault reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $6.7 million, predominantly from its acoustics group, which is significantly below the reiterated full-year target of $200 million and implies a substantial miss against prior expectations for this stage of growth. Management reaffirmed the $200 million annual guidance but noted that significant revenue recognition will occur in Q4 following mid-September exchange launches rather than immediately in Q3. The company highlighted major non-revenue transactions including acquisitions (CyberCatch, BankWyse) and licensing deals with Vivasor/Scilex to strengthen its balance sheet.

negative_highlights: GAAP net loss was $35.3 million, primarily driven by a non-cash Bitcoin valuation decline of $28.2M and income tax provision.
Cash rent from the flagship Nscale lease only commenced in August ($3.3M), with full ramp expected not until 2027-2028.
ERCOT paused Batch Zero approval for the Ward County expansion, delaying revenue recognition on incremental capacity to late 2027.
positive_highlights: Revenue grew YoY due to transition from Bitcoin mining ($36% margin) to digital infrastructure leasing (99% adjusted gross margin).
Company maintains a debt-free balance sheet with nearly $600 million of liquidity and over $400M cash at quarter end.
ERCOT verification process is viewed as favorable for the company due to existing operating history since 2023.
summary: Ionic Digital reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $48.6 million (up from $37.2M prior year) and adjusted EBITDA of $37.6 million, driven by a shift to digital infrastructure leasing with straight-line non-cash recognition rather than cash rent which commenced in August. Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $190-$195 million but noted the ERCOT Batch Zero process has paused approval for their Ward County expansion pending verification, pushing expected energization to late 2027.

negative_highlights: Average ticket remained flat year-over-year despite strong traffic and sales volume increases.
Management noted that performance in home and apparel categories is not yet where it needs to be, requiring continued work into FY2027.
SG&A expenses grew 7% versus last year due to higher compensation costs and planned spending on capital projects.
positive_highlights: Net sales grew 5.3% year-over-year with comparable sales up 3.8% driven by traffic acceleration.
Digital comparable sales increased 8.7%, led by more than 25% growth in same-day delivery units.
Gross margin rate expanded to 33.7%, excluding a one-time $994 million tariff refund benefit.
summary: Target reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $26.5 billion, representing a 5.3% year-over-year increase driven by a 3.8% rise in comparable sales and traffic growth of 3.6%. Adjusted EPS was $4.11 per share compared to $2.05 last year, with gross margin expanding to 33.7% aided significantly by tariff refunds. Management raised full-year adjusted operating guidance from a range of 4.8%-5.0% to 4.9%-5.1%, citing broad-based strength across demographics and categories.

negative_highlights: Gross margin contracted sequentially by 50 basis points due to seasonal factors, though this was offset by YoY expansion.
Cash and note weakness in-term investments decreased to $2.3 billion following the closing of the Empower Semiconductor acquisition for $1.5 billion.
positive_highlights: Revenue reached first-ever quarter above $4 billion with broad-based growth across all end markets led by data center (>100% YoY) and industrial (53% YoY).
Gross margin expanded sequentially to a high-end result, supported by record inventory levels that declined in days despite volume increases.
Management raised Q4 gross margin guidance from 72.5-73.5% range implied previously to approximately 74%, indicating strong pricing power and mix shifts.
summary: ADI reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $4.02 billion (up 40% YoY), finishing above the high end of guidance with record earnings per share of $3.45 at the top of expectations. Management raised full-year gross margin outlook to approximately 74%, citing favorable mix, higher fixed cost absorption, and price adjustments driving a sequential expansion despite inflationary pressures.

negative_highlights: Cash operating costs for Ergo rose 7% year-on-year due to higher oil prices and carbon/cyanide costs.
Far West Gold Recoveries cash costs increased by 10%, reflecting the transition phase of its expansion project before full capacity ramps up in Vision 2028.
positive_highlights: Production beat guidance with roughly 5 tons (approx 1,300 oz) achieved against a lower prior year baseline due to the gold price surge.
Operating profit for Ergo more than doubled from ZAR 2 billion last year to ZAR 4.1 billion in FY26.
Free cash flow increased by 85% YoY to ZAR 2.3 billion, supporting a final dividend of ZAR 1.20 per share.
summary: DRDGOLD reported exceptional Q4 FY26 results driven by a 40% increase in the gold price and production of roughly 5 tons (approx 1,300 oz), exceeding guidance. Revenue surged to ZAR 11.2 billion (+42%) while operating profit more than doubled to ZAR 4.1 billion for Ergo alone. Management highlighted strong cost discipline despite rising input costs like diesel and carbon, resulting in robust free cash flow of ZAR 2.3 billion.

negative_highlights: Q4 deconversion revenue decreased by approximately $11 million due to M&A activity among financial institutions.
Fiscal year Q4 free cash flow declined 10% YoY primarily driven by lower deconversion revenue.
Core segment operating margin contracted 139 bps in the quarter attributed to temporary product mix including new conversion teams.
positive_highlights: Record fiscal year core wins totaling 58, surpassing the previous record of 57 set in both 2019 and 2024.
Secured Woodforest National Bank ($9.2B assets), identified as the largest new bank client in company history.
Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 92 bps for fiscal year to reach 24%.
summary: Jack Henry reported Q4 FY26 non-GAAP revenue of $633 million (up 7% YoY) and a non-GAAP operating margin of 21%, exceeding prior guidance. Full year fiscal 2026 saw record performance with GAAP EPS of $6.98 (+12%) driven by strong core wins, including the largest new bank client in company history at Woodforest National Bank ($9.2B assets). Management provided FY27 full-year non-GAAP revenue guidance of 6.3%-7.3% and margin expansion of 20-40 bps.

negative_highlights: Demand environment remained subdued with low consumer confidence and elevated mortgage rates weighing on sales pace in key markets like Atlanta, Seattle, Portland, San Francisco, and Texas.
Joint venture income was lower than the prior year at $6 million compared to $15 million.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin of 25.6% beat guidance by 35 basis points driven by mix and operational efficiency.
Luxury move-up business accounted for approximately 61% of home sales revenues, generating the highest margins among segments.
Management increased projected annual share repurchases to $700 million from a previous projection of $650 million.
summary: Toll Brothers delivered a solid beat on both revenue and EPS in Q3 FY26, generating $2.6 billion in home sales revenue (up 4% YoY) and an adjusted gross margin of 25.6%, which exceeded the midpoint of guidance by 35 basis points. Management reaffirmed full-year delivery guidance while narrowing the settlement range to reflect a higher average delivered price between $995,000 and $1 million. The company increased its projected annual share repurchases from $650 million to $700 million.

negative_highlights: H1 cash costs of $2,665/oz are significantly above the full-year guidance range of $1,900-$2,000.
Manh Choh is currently mining lower-grade material from the North Pit before transitioning to higher grades.
positive_highlights: Completed acquisition of Lucky Shot claims and royalty, removing overhang ahead of feasibility study.
Manh Choh production expected to exceed 41,000 ounces for the year as operations shift to high-grade South Pit.
Kitsault Valley drilling efficiency improved with five rigs averaging high 470-480 meters per day.
summary: Management reported Q2 production of approximately 8,900 ounces from the 30% stake in Manh Choh and reiterated full-year guidance of 40,000-45,000 ounces. The company closed on the Lucky Shot acquisition to remove royalty burdens and remains unhedged on gold, positioning it to capture upside as prices stabilize above $4,000. Cash costs for H1 were $2,665/oz, with expectations of improvement in H2 driven by higher-grade South Pit mining.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue plummeted to $42.1 million, a drop of over half compared to the prior year ($66.4M), driven largely by one significant material handling customer navigating a capital freeze.
Gross margin contracted sequentially and declined year-over-year due to unfavorable product mix, tariff impacts, and loss of operating leverage from lower volumes.
Cash position weakened with cash and equivalents falling to $0.3 million at quarter-end compared to $0.4M previously.
positive_highlights: Operating expenses decreased significantly, dropping from $6.5M (YoY) and $4.8M (QoQ), reflecting successful cost containment measures including headcount reductions.
Net loss narrowed sequentially to -$2.3 million ($0.11/share) compared to a prior quarter net loss of -$3.2 million, indicating improved profitability trajectory despite revenue misses.
Secured OEM certification from Hyster-Yale Materials Handling for Class 1-3 lift trucks and increased an existing white-label customer's yearly order commitment by 50%.
summary: Fourth quarter revenue was $8.2 million (up 25% sequentially but down year-over-year to $6.6M prior Q and significantly below the $16.7M in FY2025), while full-year revenue contracted sharply from $66.4M to $42.1M due to a major customer's capital freeze, tariffs, and higher fuel prices. Gross margin declined sequentially by 10 basis points to 27.4% (from Q3) and fell year-over-year to 30.2%, driven by product mix shifts and lower volumes absorbing fixed costs despite operating expense reductions of $2.6M in the quarter.

negative_highlights: R&D expenses surged $29 million (32% increase) and S&G expenses jumped $14.2 million (64% increase), indicating high burn.
Management explicitly stated OpEx spend is at a 'peak' as trials near completion, implying elevated costs are not yet stabilizing.
No new revenue streams or partnerships were announced to offset the heavy investment in global commercialization.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew to $44.5 million, up 29% year-over-year on a constant exchange rate basis.
Lisaftoclax and Olverembatinib have cleared FDA/EMA for global registration in multiple indications including high-risk MDS and CML-CP.
Enrollment is proceeding as planned with GLORA-4 expected to complete by the end of 2026 or early 2027.
summary: Total revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $44.5 million, representing a 29% year-over-year increase driven by product sales of $41.6 million in China. R&D expenses increased to $102.8 million and watching & distribution expenses rose significantly to $33.4 million due to heavy investment in global registration trial enrollment for the two approved products, Lisaftoclax and Olverembatinib. Management reaffirmed its cash runway through 2027 but noted that OpEx is currently at a peak as trials near completion.

negative_highlights: Reported net sales decreased 26% year-over-year due to the timing of legacy backlog fulfillment.
Net loss widened to $7.2 million from $2.3 million, primarily driven by a step-up in public company operating expenses and non-cash financing charges totaling approximately $4 million.
Defense delivery timelines for key projects like the Marine Corps trainer are uncertain due to government funding availability.
positive_highlights: New orders increased 72% year-over-year and approximately 150% since the Meta collaboration launch.
Gross margin expanded by 13 percentage points from 17% to 30%, driven by higher ASPs on new consumer units.
Secured major strategic partnerships with Tesla, NASA, U.S. Marine Corps (Infantry Fireteam Trainer), and Sirica Therapeutics.
summary: Net sales declined year-over-year to $767,000 from $1 million due to the clearance of a legacy backlog in Q4 FY2026 rather than weak demand. Gross profit increased by 29% and gross margin expanded significantly to 30%, driven by higher pricing on new consumer units (Omni One for Quest) compared to lower-priced pre-order shipments delivered previously. Management highlighted strong order growth of 72% year-over-year but noted that defense revenue recognition remains uncertain due to government funding timing, with larger awards likely in FY2028.

negative_highlights: Available days decreased by 2% YoY due to geopolitical disruptions and market dynamics.
Adjusted EBITDA was negatively impacted by a $15 million increase in time charter expenses, primarily reflecting additional insurance premiums reimbursed by charterers.
Net LTV remains elevated at 27.9%, above the target range of 20%-25%.
positive_highlights: Revenue increased by $82 million (25%) YoY driven by combined TCE rate growth of 24% despite available days declining 2% to 13,152.
EBITDA reached a record run-rate over $900 million with contracted revenue backlog hitting an all-time high of $4.4 billion extending through 2037.
Management doubled the share repurchase authorization from $100 million to $200 million, having already returned $6.30 per unit in accretion since Q2 2024.
summary: Navios Maritime Partners reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $410 million (up 25% YoY) and net income of $167.9 million on a fleet with lower available days but significantly higher TCE rates across all segments. Management raised the common unit repurchase authorization to $200 million, doubling the prior program size while maintaining liquidity for newbuilding deliveries. The company continues to de-lever its balance sheet toward a 20%-25% net LTV target amidst strong contracted revenue visibility extending through 2037.

negative_highlights: Vertical application revenue decreased 16% YoY due to weak demand for Chinese APP data in Market Intelligence (-12%) and Financial Risk Management (-17%).
Management described the stance as 'cautiously optimistic' regarding Q3/Q4, citing a need for strict cost discipline.
Value-Added Services revenue declined 15% YoY despite a quarterly spike from the 618 shopping festival.
positive_highlights: Developer Subscription Services revenue hit a historic high of RMB 70.7 million (+32% YoY).
EngageLab ARR scaled to $14.6 million with record-breaking growth and cumulative signed contracts exceeding RMB 200 million.
Gross margin improved significantly by 197 basis points year-over-year, validating operating leverage.
summary: Aurora Mobile reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 101.2 million (up 13% YoY), driven by a record Developer Subscription Services quarter of RMB 70.7 million and global flagship EngageLab ARR reaching $14.6 million (+170% YoY). The company achieved its fifth consecutive quarter of GAAP net profit with gross margin expanding 197 bps to approximately 58%, while generating positive operating cash flow of RMB 23.3 million and repurchasing 44,000 ADS.

negative_highlights: Smart devices net revenues declined 31.5% YoY to RMB 86.8 million due to reduced demand for smart learning devices.
Gross margin for the Smart Devices segment contracted to 32.8%, down from 41.5% in Q2 FY2025, driven by rising memory costs.
positive_highlights: Operating profit reached RMB 111.5 million, representing nearly fourfold year-over-year growth.
Learning services net revenues surged 20.9% YoY to RMB 795.6 million driven by AI-powered tutoring and essay grading features.
Online marketing gross margin improved significantly to 28.7%, up approximately three percentage points year-over-year.
summary: Youdao reported Q2 FY2026 net revenues of RMB 1.5 billion (up 3.5% YoY) and operating profit of RMB 111.5 million (nearly fourfold YoY). Gross margins expanded across Learning Services (+590 bps), Online Marketing Services (+290 bps), while Smart Devices margin contracted due to memory costs but is expected to recover in H2. Management raised guidance for gross margin expansion and reiterated a focus on profitable growth over rapid revenue acceleration.

negative_highlights: Gross margin declined due to an unfavorable shift in revenue mix as lower-margin supply chain business grew faster than hotel operations.
Adjusted net profit margin decreased by 1.3 percentage points year-over-year to 16.0%.
Full-year guidance for total group net profit margin was maintained at a slight decline compared to the prior period.
positive_highlights: Retail revenue surged 63.2% year-over-year to RMB 1,575 million due to strong product innovation and brand recognition.
