negative_highlights: No commercial revenue reported as the company has not yet commercialized any portfolio assets
Phase III initiation is contingent on ongoing planning and financing activities, introducing execution risk to the timeline
European strategy remains in early days with no finalized partnerships or market access agreements identified
positive_highlights: givastomig received FDA Fast Track designation and may be eligible for an Accelerated Approval Pathway in first-line HER2 negative, Claudin 18.2 positive gastroesophageal cancer
Phase Ib data showed a 75% ORR with tumor reduction in 51 of 52 evaluable patients at the 8 mg/kg dose combination with nivolumab and chemotherapy
Company maintains a debt-free balance sheet providing financial flexibility for clinical development
summary: NovaBridge Biosciences reported a debt-free balance sheet with approximately $216 million in cash and investments as of June 30, 2026, supporting operations through anticipated phase III interim data readouts for givastomig in 2028. The company highlighted significant regulatory progress for its lead oncology program givastomig, including FDA Fast Track designation and potential eligibility for an Accelerated Approval Pathway in first-line HER2 negative gastroesophageal cancer following a Type B meeting. Management outlined plans to initiate phase III studies as early as the fourth quarter of 2026 subject to planning activities.

negative_highlights: Medical contract manufacturing divestiture reduced total sales by approximately 6% compared to the prior year.
Non-cash mark-to-market charge of $15 million on minority investments impacted GAAP EPS, though adjusted metrics remain strong.
positive_highlights: Record Q3 sales of $818 million driven by organic growth across all three segments (IPS +5%, MFS +11% organic, ATS +31% organic).
Backlog increased 35% year-over-year with broad-based contribution from Advanced Technology Solutions and Medical & Fluid Solutions.
Free cash flow conversion exceeded 100% at 144% in the quarter, enabling $159M in share repurchases and continued deleveraging to a 1.7x leverage ratio.
summary: Nordson reported record Q3 FY26 sales of $818 million (up 10% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $3.25 (up 19%), both exceeding the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to a range of $3,000-$3,750M and adjusted earnings to $11.80-$12.00 per share, citing sustained order momentum and backlog growth up 35% YoY.

negative_highlights: Production & Precision Ag sales declined 6% due to lower shipment volumes in South America and Europe amid elevated input costs.
Management lowered full-year Production & Precision Ag sales guidance by approximately 10 points year-over-year.
Net tariff expense is expected to rise from ~$750 million this year to roughly $1 billion next year, creating a headwind for FY27.
positive_highlights: Construction & Forestry net sales surged 18% year-over-year to $3.6 billion driven by strong infrastructure and data center demand.
Small Ag & Turf segment delivered a solid 12% YoY revenue increase with an operating margin expansion to 18.4%.
Full-year tariff refund activity totaled $382 million, providing significant one-time earnings support.
summary: Deere reported Q3 FY26 net sales of $12.6 billion (up 5%) and EPS of $5.10, beating expectations driven by strong Construction & Forestry growth (+18% YoY) offsetting declines in Production & Precision Ag (-6%). Management raised full-year net income guidance to a range of $4.75-$5 billion but narrowed segment margin outlooks for Agriculture (to 11%-12%) and Construction (to 10.5%-11.5%), citing softening demand in South America, Europe, and tariff headwinds.

negative_highlights: Men's total sales remained essentially flat, representing only 50% of revenue compared to 52.5% last year.
Footwear volumes have declined for 50 consecutive months; men's denim sales fell approximately 3.5% YoY.
Operating margin contracted to 17.4% from 18.4%, with SG&A expenses rising significantly due to marketing and labor costs.
positive_highlights: Women's business grew 9.5% YoY, representing 50% of total sales compared to 47.5% last year.
Gross margin expanded by 40 basis points to 47.8%, with merchandise margins up 110 bps excluding tariff impacts.
Kids business delivered an outstanding quarter increasing 11% YoY on top of a strong prior period.
summary: Buckle reported Q2 FY27 net sales of $319.8 million (up 4.6% YoY) and diluted EPS of $0.87, missing the prior year's $0.89 per share despite a comparable store sales increase of 2.1%. Gross margin expanded to 47.8%, driven by tariff refunds and private label mix shifts which offset higher SG&A expenses including marketing increases. Management reiterated its policy against providing future guidance.

negative_highlights: Revenue was impacted by continued cyclical softness in outgoing demand during H1 FY2026.
Business operations were negatively affected by PRC mining machine sales restrictions announced in February.
Management expects modest revenue contribution from the new ASIC in H2 2026, with meaningful impact deferred to fiscal 2027.
positive_highlights: Successfully completed the tape-out of next-generation mining ASIC, transitioning from design to manufacturing and silicon validation phases.
Realized approximately RMB 23.1 million in annualized labor cost savings through organizational restructuring and divestiture of non-core businesses.
Board approved a $15 million share repurchase program over the next two years.
summary: Intchains reported first-half FY2026 revenue of RMB 11.1 million and a net loss per share of RMB 1.22 against the backdrop of cyclical softness in outgoing demand and PRC mining machine sales restrictions. Management provided no specific financial guidance for H2, noting continued market headwinds but expressing confidence that their new ASIC tape-out completed in July will enable commercial launch in Q4 2026 with meaningful impact expected in fiscal 2027. The company also announced a $15 million share repurchase program funded by existing cash balances.

negative_highlights: Reported net loss widened significantly to $22.7 million due to non-cash write-downs on vanadium assets and higher operating costs.
Cash operating costs excluding royalties increased to $5.10/lb from $4.63/lb YoY, driven by external input price pressures including the Iran war impact on diesel and explosives.
Management explicitly stated that not all current vanadium sales are profitable in the present market environment.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA returned to positive territory at $2.7M compared with a negligible profit ($34k) in the prior year period.
Cash provided before working capital items more than tripled to $6.6 million from $2.2 million YoY due to improved operations and pricing flow-through.
Secured a binding agreement to restructure approximately $82.2M of commercial debt, extending maturity from September 2026 to March 2030.
summary: Largo reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $44 million (up 68.5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA returning to positive at $2.7 million after a loss in the prior year period, driven by higher vanadium volumes (+53%) and improved pricing ($6.96/lb). Management maintained full-year guidance for vanadium production but introduced initial volume guidance for new copper-PGM concentrate (300-380 tons/month) following the start of commercial-scale output in August. Significant non-cash items, including a write-down on vanadium assets and deferred tax expenses, contributed to a reported net loss of $22.7 million despite operational improvements.

negative_highlights: Merchandise gross margin rate decreased approximately 20 basis points year-over-year due to price investments and inflation under a point.
Membership fee income growth is expected to moderate throughout the remainder of the year as last year's fee increase normalizes.
positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS of $1.36 beat expectations and was up 19% year-over-year.
Membership reached a new milestone of 8.5 million members, with fee income growing nearly 10% YoY.
Gas business outperformed significantly with comp gallons increasing 10.5%, driving fuel profit ahead of plan.
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $6.1 billion (up 15.9% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $1.36 (up 19%), both beating expectations driven by strong gas business performance and membership growth to a new milestone of 8.5 million members. Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.60-$4.80 while maintaining comparable club sales growth guidance at 2%-3%. The quarter highlighted durable momentum with traffic accelerating for the 18th consecutive quarter, though merchandise gross margin contracted approximately 20 basis points due to continued price investments.

negative_highlights: Overseas operations are still early-stage investments; management explicitly stated they will avoid front-loading expenses and aim for profitability only by the second half of the year.
Reliance on specific high-growth segments like SMEs (30% GMV share) and private labels suggests continued vulnerability if these niche markets face headwinds.
positive_highlights: Achieved operating profitability for the first time with non-GAAP adjusted net profit turning positive at RMB 39 million versus a loss of RMB 37 million last year.
GMV from private label products grew over 25% YoY, lifting their share to approximately 10% and contributing significantly to gross margin expansion.
International business scaled rapidly with first-half GMV exceeding RMB 95 million (more than tenfold increase), expected to turn profitable in H2.
summary: ZKH reported Q2 FY26 GMV growth of 18.9% YoY and net revenue growth of 12.8%, marking the fastest pace in recent quarters. The company achieved a significant financial milestone by turning to positive operating profit for the first time, with non-GAAP adjusted net income reaching RMB 39 million compared to a loss last year. Management raised guidance expectations for H2 GMV acceleration and reiterated confidence in achieving full-year growth targets of 15%-20%.

negative_highlights: Total reported revenue decreased 5.7% year-over-year, primarily stemming from adjustments in home renovation and furnishing business.
Home renovation revenue fell 30.1% YoY as the company proactively exited inefficient cities and acquisition channels with weak unit economics.
New home market remained under pressure with GTV growth of only 1.2% YoY, reflecting a cautious environment where demand is concentrated in high-quality projects.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP net income grew 74.9% year-over-year to RMB 3.185 billion with Non-GAAP net margin reaching 13%, a three-year high.
Existing home contribution margin expanded significantly, up 6.1 percentage points YoY to 46.1%, driven by higher platform service revenue mix and lower fixed labor costs.
Home renovation contribution margin improved substantially year-over-year despite revenue decline due to centralized procurement lowering material costs.
summary: In Q2 FY2026, total revenue declined 5.7% year-over-year to RMB 34.1 billion (implied from segment sum), while Non-GAAP net income surged 74.9% YoY to RMB 3.185 billion driven by gross margin expansion and lower operating expenses. Existing home transaction services returned to growth with GTV up 6.3%, whereas new home, renovation, and rental segments faced revenue pressure or declines due to market adjustments and strategic channel exits. Management emphasized strict financial discipline, a leaner cost structure, and resource reallocation toward high-quality projects rather than broad expansion.

negative_highlights: Net Investment Income was flat quarter-over-quarter ($0.15/share), failing to beat expectations
Payment-in-kind interest income dropped significantly from the prior year period (reduced by 53%)
Recurring revenue profile relies heavily on cash interest, which may be sensitive to rate environments
positive_highlights: Net Investment Income remained consistent at $78 million despite market volatility
Nonaccruals as a percentage of total assets declined to approximately 0.7%
Successfully exited Valley Electric Company for ~$328M consideration, achieving a 4.8x multiple on invested capital
summary: Prospect Capital reported Q4 FY26 Net Investment Income of $78 million ($0.15/share) and NAV of $2.9 billion, which were in-line with the prior quarter but missed implied expectations given a significant one-time exit gain from Valley Electric Company that was not included in recurring NII guidance comparisons. Management highlighted strong balance sheet metrics including 66% unencumbered assets and reduced nonaccruals at 0.7%, while noting that interest income is now predominantly cash-based (91%) following a reduction in payment-in-kind income to 10%. The company announced monthly distributions of $0.035 per share for September and October, maintaining its long history of shareholder returns.

negative_highlights: NPL over 90 days increased from 8.9% to 9.8% in Q2, driven by portfolio aging (318 bps impact), with management expecting further increase to low-teens by year-end.
Stage 3 coverage declined from 77% to 74.1% due to Desenrola renegotiations, though management attributes it to lower LGD from FGO guarantees.
Q3 guidance implies adjusted net income down 6% sequentially (to ~BRL 265 million) due to tax rate normalization and rising cost of risk.
positive_highlights: Adjusted net income grew 135% YoY to BRL 283 million, with adjusted ROE expanding from 15.5% to 20.2%.
Revenue growth of 67% YoY (BRL 4.1 billion) outpaced cost growth, with efficiency ratio improving 210 bps sequentially to 44.8%.
Credit portfolio grew 99% YoY to BRL 31.9 billion, driven by secured products (+158% YoY), while 71% of revenue now comes from no- or lower-credit-risk streams.
summary: PicPay reported a strong Q2 2026, with managerial revenues of BRL 3.7 billion (up 59% YoY, 17% QoQ), adjusted net income of BRL 283 million (up 135% YoY, up 67% QoQ), and adjusted ROE of 20.2%. Management beat guidance on credit portfolio, revenues, NII, gross profit, and net income, with credit portfolio at BRL 31.9 billion (3% above guidance) and gross profit 8.4% above guidance. Guidance for Q3 2026 expects continued growth with managerial revenues around BRL 4 billion, but adjusted net income is expected to decline sequentially to ~BRL 265 million due to the normalization of the Lei do Bem tax benefit and higher cost of risk. The company closed the Kovr acquisition (now KEV Seguros) in August 2026, expecting BRL 80-100 million net income contribution for August-December 2026.

negative_highlights: Gross margin was pressured by hardware-heavy revenue mix, with management expecting expansion only as GPU-as-a-service projects ramp.
Operating cash flow was negative $4.3 million in H1, though improved from negative $12.5 million a year earlier.
Guidance for 2026 upper end of $200 million and 2027 target of $450-$500 million depend on execution of delivery schedules and workload migration.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue of $50.1 million exceeded the raised guidance of $44 million by 14% and represented 138% YoY growth.
Operating loss narrowed to $2.2 million in Q2 from $41.1 million in Q1, a 95% reduction, as share-based compensation declined 78% sequentially.
Cash balance of $179.4 million at end of H1, up 82% sequentially, with $79.8 million added during the half.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue reached $50.1 million, up 138% YoY and 78% QoQ, beating raised guidance of $44 million by $6.1 million. H1 revenue was $78.4 million, up 99% YoY. Operating loss narrowed to $2.2 million in Q2 from $41.1 million in Q1, due largely to reduced share-based compensation. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to at least $200 million from $137-$200 million, and targets $450-$500 million for 2027. Cash stood at $179.4 million at end of H1, boosted by convertible debt and financing activities.

negative_highlights: Vehicle margin declined to 12.1% in Q2 from 14.3% in the year-ago quarter, due to production generation transition and industry-wide cost pressures.
July delivery ramp for MONA L03 was hampered by extreme weather and supply chain disruptions, which delayed the expected pace of delivery growth.
Net loss widened YoY to RMB 1.34 billion from RMB 0.48 billion, with R&D expenses up 32.1% YoY reflecting heavy investment in new models and AI technologies.
positive_highlights: Q3 2026 delivery guidance of 115,000-121,000 units implies QoQ growth of 11.3%-17.1%, and revenue guidance of RMB 21.7-23.4 billion implies QoQ growth of 9.9%-18.5%.
International business hit a record: overseas deliveries exceeded 20,000 units in Q2, up 81% YoY, and now account for more than 25% of total H1 revenues, with average export ASP above EUR 40,000.
Monumental L03 (MONA L03) orders set a new company record, with Q3 new uncancelable orders up 50% QoQ; two shifts of production have been started to ramp deliveries.
summary: Q2 2026 revenue was RMB 19.74 billion, up 8% YoY and 51.5% QoQ; vehicle deliveries reached 103,295 units, up 65% QoQ. Gross margin was 20.7%, above 20% for the second consecutive quarter, though vehicle margin fell YoY to 12.1% due to production generation transition. Net loss narrowed to RMB 1.34 billion from RMB 1.7 billion QoQ. Q3 2026 guidance calls for deliveries of 115,000-121,000 units and revenue of RMB 21.7-23.4 billion, implying QoQ growth of 9.9%-18.5%. XPeng Robotics raised over $900 million at a $6.2 billion post-money valuation, led by IDG, with plans to start scaled production of its IRON humanoid robot by year-end.

negative_highlights: Revenue declined 56.3% YoY and 15.5% sequentially, reflecting continued contraction in origination volumes.
Origination volume fell 70.2% YoY and 20.5% sequentially, with active borrowers down 74.8% YoY.
Provision for credit losses for deposits and other financial assets surged to RMB 95.3 million from RMB 0.7 million due to a funding partner's delayed return of guarantee money.
positive_highlights: Net income rose 23.8% sequentially to RMB 47 million, with non-GAAP adjusted net income up 104.3% sequentially to RMB 166 million.
Both 31-60 day and 91-180 day delinquency rates improved sequentially for the first time in several quarters (31-60 day: 1.73% vs 2.61% in Q1; 91-180 day: 9.09% vs 9.95%).
Operating margin expanded to 19.6% from 12% in Q1, driven by lower costs and lower credit provisions.
summary: In Q2 2026, X Financial reported net revenue of RMB 993.6 million, down 56.3% YoY and 15.5% sequentially, with net income of RMB 47 million, up 23.8% sequentially. Loan origination fell 70.2% YoY to RMB 11.63 billion, and the outstanding loan balance declined 61.5% YoY to RMB 24.97 billion. Both delinquency rates improved sequentially for the first time in several quarters, but management did not provide quantitative guidance for Q3 due to material uncertainties, while maintaining a conservative stance on credit and capital preservation.

negative_highlights: Net income fell 12% YoY to RMB 27.2 billion, with non-GAAP diluted EPS down to RMB 19.33 from RMB 22.07
Non-GAAP operating margin contracted to 26% from 27%, with total non-GAAP operating expenses up 13% YoY

EU customs duty changes on low-value cross-border consignments will cause lower fulfillment efficiency and higher costs in affected markets in the note weakness in term; first-party brand rollout slower than expected
positive_highlights: Transaction services revenue grew 13% YoY to RMB 54.7 billion
Operating cash flow increased to RMB 25.7 billion from RMB 21.6 billion
R&D expenses on non-GAAP basis up 40% YoY to RMB 4.6 billion, supporting governance and supply chain initiatives
summary: PDD reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of RMB 112.4 billion, up 8% YoY, while net income declined 12% to RMB 27.2 billion. GAAP operating profit rose 8% to RMB 27.8 billion, but non-GAAP operating margin contracted to 26% from 27%. Management noted slower-than-expected first-party brand rollout and significant near-term impact from EU customs duty changes on cross-border orders.

negative_highlights: Access control product sales declined 13.8% in Q4, partially offsetting gains in intrusion
Equipment margins face pressure from Section 122 tariffs and rising component costs due to data center supply challenges
Full-year operating income fell 1.3% to $45.6 million, impacted by a $16 million legal settlement
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 10% to a record $55.8 million, with recurring service revenue up 12.9% and equipment revenue up 7.7%
Radio unit sales grew 40% YoY and nearly 30% sequentially, driving future recurring revenue growth
Gross margin expanded to 61.3% in Q4 (from 52.8% a year ago), boosted by tariff refunds and product mix
summary: NAPCO Security Technologies reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $55.8 million, up 10% YoY, with recurring service revenue up 12.9% to $25.3 million and equipment revenue up 7.7% to $30.5 million. GAAP net income rose 52.7% to $17.8 million ($0.50 per diluted share), and adjusted EBITDA increased 44.3% to $20.6 million. Full-year revenue reached a record $202.3 million, with non-GAAP EPS up 34.5% to $1.60. Management highlighted 40% YoY growth in radio unit sales and a rising recurring revenue run rate, while noting supply chain challenges and tariff-related costs as headwinds. The company raised its quarterly dividend by 13.3% to $0.17 per share.

negative_highlights: The9bit's current revenue is still small, with the majority of games being ad-supported casual games, and management only expects meaningful revenue growth in the second half of 2026.
The CEO of The9bit was directly questioned about his reputation and track record, and management declined to address it on the call, citing it as not appropriate.
The surge in net income is driven largely by non-cash fair value recognition of 9BIT tokens, a volatile digital asset.
positive_highlights: Net income reached $32 million in Q2, up more than 39% from the previous quarter, with half-year net income of $55 million, the strongest since 2004.
The9bit surpassed 8 million registered users and 110,000 user-created games since launch.
RFAI shareholders approved NYB business combination; The9 expects to hold 15%-16% of a combined company potentially valued at ~$7.7 billion.
summary: The9 reported Q2 2026 net income of $32 million, up 39% quarter-over-quarter, driven by fair value recognition of 9BIT tokens, with half-year net income of $55 million. The9bit reached 8 million registered users and 110,000 user-created games, but revenue from the platform remains small, with management expecting stronger revenue growth in the second half after in-game purchase support launches. The pending NYB SPAC combination with RFAI, which would give The9 a 15%-16% stake in a combined company valued around $7.7 billion, was approved by RFAI shareholders, though the listing timeline remains uncertain. Management outlined a strategic repositioning around The9bit, but the platform's current revenue scale and reliance on token-based valuation raise concerns about sustainability and execution.

negative_highlights: Gearing at 20.6%, temporarily above the 10-20% target range.
Beaumont New Ammonia production constrained by third-party feedstock availability, with impacts expected through 2027.
Marketing EBIT was only about 3% of total EBIT in H1, versus a typical 10%, due to cyclone impacts and planned turnaround limiting volumes.
positive_highlights: Free cash flow rose more than 150% year-on-year to $352 million.
Interim dividend of $0.57 per share at the top end of the 50-80% payout range.
Scarborough project 98% complete, first LNG cargo on track for Q4 2026.
summary: Woodside reported H1 FY2026 production of 86.5 MMboe, free cash flow up over 150% YoY to $352 million, EBITDA of $4.6 billion, and underlying NPAT of $1.3 billion. The board declared a fully franked interim dividend of $0.57 per share. Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance for Scarborough first LNG in Q4 and announced a structural cost-out target of $350 million per year from 2028, while retiring Scope 3 targets and initiating a strategic review of Beaumont New Ammonia. Gearing of 20.6% is temporarily above the 10-20% target but expected to fall below 20% by year-end.

negative_highlights: Full-year EPS guidance of $1.54 was only raised by $0.01 excluding FX and share count changes, implying modest bottom-line leverage.
Q3 billings growth is guided to ~9%, a step-down from Q2's 17% growth, though management attributes this to seasonality and FX.
Gross margin is expected to decline to 80.5% for Q3 and 80% for Q4, reflecting investments in AI platform capacity.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue of $321M grew 9% YoY (11% cc), exceeding guidance; EPS of $0.40 beat the $0.39 guide.
Net retention rate improved to 106%, above the 105% guide and up from 103% a year ago, driven by seat expansion and Enterprise Advanced.
Q2 billings grew 17% YoY to $310M, and RPO reached $1.7B, up 15% YoY, reflecting strong bookings and demand for AI-driven workflows.
summary: Box reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $321M, up 9% YoY (11% cc), exceeding guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.40 above the $0.39 guide. Net retention rate was 106%, above guidance and up from 103% a year ago; billings grew 17% YoY to $310M and RPO reached $1.7B, up 15%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance by $10M to ~$1.29B (10% YoY growth) and EPS to ~$1.54, citing strong Enterprise Advanced adoption and AI momentum. Operating margin expanded 90 bps to 29.4%, with FX headwinds partially offsetting robust demand.

negative_highlights: Reported net sales fell 2.2% in Q4, with core volume down 3.3% excluding Bachan's, impacted by club channel reductions and prior-year pipeline build.
Cyclospora outbreak is expected to reduce FY2027 Q1 net sales by ~250 bps, with Q1 operating income expected down ~15%.
Core retail volumes were down ~7% excluding Bachan's; salad dressing category remains a drag, with Olive Garden and Marzetti Classics sales still down in August.
positive_highlights: Adjusted gross margin expanded 160 bps in Q4, the 12th consecutive quarter of gross margin improvement.
Texas Roadhouse Dinner Rolls grew 28.1% in the quarter and 76% to $58M for the year, with category-leading 61.7% share in dinner rolls.
Bachan's brand grew 8.7% in Circana data with distribution up 16.6%, and management expects stronger growth in FY2027 driven by new products and marketing.
summary: Q4 FY2026 reported net sales declined 2.2% to $465M, but adjusted net sales rose 0.4% excluding discontinued TSA sales. Adjusted operating income grew 17.5%, and adjusted EPS rose to $1.46 from $1.34. Full-year results hit records for net sales, gross profit, and operating income. For FY2027, management guides to mid-single-digit revenue growth, 100 bps gross margin expansion, and a Q1 operating income decline of ~15% due to a 250 bps Cyclospora sales headwind.

negative_highlights: Reported EPS of CAD 2.38 was impacted by a CAD 973 million goodwill charge related to divestitures.
Total deposits flat YoY and sequentially, with core deposits up but term deposits deliberately reduced.
Corporate Services net loss widened to CAD 178 million from CAD 123 million in the prior year.
positive_highlights: EPS of CAD 3.96 up 22% YoY and ROE up 200 bps to 14%, with record PPPT across all four segments.
U.S. Banking ROE improved 90 bps to 9.8% and ROTCE to 17.3%, with commercial loans up 4% sequentially.
Capital position strong: CET1 ratio at 13%, with a new NCIB for 25 million shares.
summary: BMO Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS was CAD 3.96, up 22% YoY, on record net income of CAD 2.9 billion. Revenue grew 11% YoY with positive operating leverage of 1.6%; ROE improved to 14% (up 200 bps YoY). Management reaffirmed the 15% ROE target exiting fiscal 2027 and expects Q4 impaired PCL to be in line with Q3, maintaining 2026 guidance. The bank announced a new NCIB for up to 25 million shares and expects divestitures to add 50 bps to CET1.

negative_highlights: Cost of sales increased by EUR 93 million due to operation of three additional vessels.
SG&A expenses up EUR 7 million in Q2 as the company scales its back office.
Vessel OpEx per day rose to EUR 39,871, above recent levels.
positive_highlights: Revenue more than doubled to EUR 282.8 million, with EBITDA up 106% to EUR 160.6 million.
Adjusted utilization reached 91%, up from 76% in the prior year.
Backlog at EUR 2.5 billion, up 23% YoY, and deals in the pipeline include multisite projects for 2027-2031.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue more than doubled to EUR 282.8 million (up 432% YoY), EBITDA rose 106% to EUR 160.6 million, and net profit grew 73% to EUR 95 million. Adjusted fleet utilization reached 91% for the quarter. Backlog stood at EUR 2.5 billion, up 23% YoY, with 77% at FID. Management guided revenue to EUR 854-944 million and EBITDA of EUR 420-510 million for FY2026, unchanged from prior guidance, and reported strong commercial momentum and several preferred supplier agreements.

negative_highlights: Online paying customers grew only 3% in FY2026, down two points from prior-year growth.
DIY tax lost quality customers to low-cost providers, with price cited as the top reason; management guided TurboTax revenue growth to just 2%-3% in FY2027.
FY2027 revenue guidance of 9%-10% growth marks a clear deceleration from FY2026's 14%, with Desktop revenue expected to decline in the low single digits.
positive_highlights: Q4 non-GAAP EPS grew 47% to $4.03, with total revenue up 14% to $4.4 billion.
Full-year Big Bets (Assisted Tax, Money, Mid-Market) grew 34% and represent 30% of revenue.
Mid-market customers grew 28%, with new-to-franchise mid-market customers up over 30% and Intuit Enterprise Suite revenue up 4x to $145 million in Q4.
summary: Fiscal 2026 revenue grew 14% with full-year GAAP and non-GAAP EPS up 20% each, but Q4 non-GAAP EPS beat at $4.03 (up 47%) while GAAP EPS fell slightly to $1.34. Management reset FY2027 guidance lower, expecting total revenue growth of 9%-10% (vs 14% in FY2026) due to deliberate actions in DIY tax, desktop declines, and Mailchimp stagnation. Online paying customers growth slowed to 3%, and management acknowledged losing quality DIY tax customers to low-cost providers, with a plan to rebuild the funnel at lower ARPC. The company also accelerated buybacks in Q4 and announced FY2027 non-GAAP EPS growth of 23%-24% including share-based compensation.

negative_highlights: U.S. mortgage subscription revenues declined 1% YoY, with guidance cut by ~$700K in Q3 and ~$1.2M in Q4 due to higher IMB churn from high mortgage rates.
Professional services revenues declined 3% YoY, partly due to deliberate focus on margin improvement.
FX headwinds of ~$200K each in Q3 and Q4 are assumed, impacting international revenues.
positive_highlights: Subscription revenues exceeded guidance by $1.3M, with 10% YoY growth; excluding U.S. mortgage, growth was 12% YoY.
Non-GAAP operating income of $40.8M beat by $3.3M, with 36% YoY growth and disciplined expense management.
AI momentum: 48% of ACV on platform pricing (up from 40% Q1), 230+ customers purchased AI Intelligence Units, and 12 of top 20 U.S. enterprise customers renewed early on new pricing.
summary: nCino reported Q2 FY2027 total revenues of $161M (+8% YoY) and subscription revenues of $143.5M (+10% YoY, +10% cc), beating guidance by approximately $1.3M. Non-U.S. subscription revenues grew 13% YoY to $30.9M, while U.S. mortgage subscription revenues declined 1% to $20.6M. Non-GAAP operating income was $40.8M (25% margin), up 36% YoY, and free cash flow was $34M, up 170%. The company raised full-year revenue and operating income guidance, with subscription revenue guidance raised to $573.5M-$576.5M and non-GAAP operating income to $171M-$174M, but lowered U.S. mortgage outlook due to higher IMB churn.

negative_highlights: Hospital revenue declined 29% in Q4, reflecting longer and less predictable sales cycles.
CEO retirement announcement introduces leadership transition uncertainty; succession details not yet disclosed.
R&D spend increased meaningfully year-over-year, though on a small base, with no new product pipeline details disclosed.
positive_highlights: Q4 revenue grew 12% YoY to a record $19.4 million, with home care channel up 15%.
Full-year operating margin expanded to 18.8% from 15.1%, with operating income up 43.7% to $13.9 million.
Payer coverage expanded to 87% of covered lives, with 6 million additional lives added in FY2026.
summary: Electromed reported record Q4 FY2026 revenue of $19.4 million, up 11.6% YoY, with operating income of $3.8 million, up 26% YoY, and diluted EPS of $0.39, a quarterly record. Full-year revenue grew 15.3% to $73.8 million, with operating margin expanding from 15.1% to 18.8%. Management guided to another year of double-digit top-line growth, operating leverage, and strong cash flow for FY2027, while raising the fiscal 2027 revenue-per-rep target range to $1.05M-$1.15M. CEO Jim Cunniff announced his retirement effective April 2027, with a succession planning process underway.

negative_highlights: High-end consumer end market declined 5% YoY, although it grew 2% sequentially.
Capacity constraints are emerging for FY2028, with management noting the need to secure additional fab and backend capacity.
Cellular module divestiture is expected to close in Q4; while EPS-neutral, it will reduce revenue scale.
positive_highlights: Data center revenue grew 91% YoY to $100 million, with a record quarter and 1.6T portfolio expected to exceed 50% of data center revenue in Q3.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 150 bps sequentially to 54.5%, with semiconductor products margin at 62.8%, up 210 bps sequentially.
Q3 guidance implies adjusted EPS up 119% YoY and operating margin up 1,040 bps YoY, with data center revenue up 160% YoY.
summary: Semtech reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $342 million, up 33% YoY and 17% sequentially, beating the high end of guidance. Adjusted EPS was $0.71, up 73% YoY, exceeding guidance. Data center revenue hit a record $100 million, up 91% YoY, with strong 1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge ramp. Guidance for Q3 projects revenue of $410 million (+54% YoY) and EPS of $1.05 (+119% YoY), with data center revenue up 160% YoY. The company announced the divestiture of its cellular module business, expecting an EPS-neutral deal and structural gross margin improvement.

negative_highlights: Gross profit declined 11% YoY to CNY 76.4 million, with other revenues down 17% and advertising services fees down about 70% YoY.
Outbound travel headwinds persisted; Middle East and Africa transaction volume fell over 20% YoY, and outbound tours fell to ~30% of GMV from over one-third a year ago.
Q3 guidance implies only 0% to 5% revenue growth, signaling continued uncertainty and a softer outlook.
positive_highlights: Non-GAAP profitability sustained for the sixth consecutive quarter, with non-GAAP net income of CNY 2.2 million.
Packaged tour revenue grew 7% YoY to CNY 121.1 million, driven by organized tours.
Live streaming and offline store transaction volumes both recorded double-digit YoY growth in Q2.
summary: Tuniu reported Q2 2026 net revenues of CNY 138.9 million, up 3% YoY, with packaged tours up 7% to CNY 121.1 million and other revenues down 17% to CNY 17.8 million. GAAP net income was CNY 0.7 million and non-GAAP net income was CNY 2.2 million, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of non-GAAP profitability. Gross profit fell 11% YoY to CNY 76.4 million, while operating expenses rose 5% to CNY 82.5 million. For Q3 2026, the company guides net revenues of CNY 202.1-212.2 million, implying 0% to 5% YoY growth, reflecting persistent outbound travel headwinds.

negative_highlights: AISC rose 13% to $1,893/oz due to higher royalties, stronger currencies, and inflation.
Windfall permitting delayed, with EIA expected in H2 2026, and potential project slippage to late 2029 if not received by year-end.
Tarkwa lease renewal remains uncertain, with terms and timing pending, impacting valuation and underpinning a 10% share price underperformance.
positive_highlights: Adjusted free cash flow more than doubled to $2.225 billion, with a free cash flow yield of 11%.
Production up 12% to 1.267 million ounces, with Salares Norte up 173% to 337,000 ounces at an AISC of $269/oz.
Interim dividend up 132% and additional $500 million buyback allocation, bringing total shareholder returns to $553 million delivered so far.
summary: Gold Fields reported a strong H1 FY2026 with attributable production up 12% to 1.267 million ounces and sales volumes up 18%, driven by a 51% higher average realized gold price of $4,678/oz. Adjusted free cash flow more than doubled to $2.225 billion (11% yield), and headline earnings per share more than doubled. All-in sustaining costs rose 13% to $1,893/oz due to royalties, currency, and inflation, but guidance is unchanged with production tracking to the upper end and costs to the mid/lower end of ranges. Shareholder returns were bolstered with an interim dividend up 132% and an additional $500 million allocated to buybacks, while net debt to EBITDA fell to 0.06x.

negative_highlights: Total revenue growth decelerated sequentially (Q2 at 4.9% vs. implied Q1 growth), and Q3 guidance implies 3.9% YoY growth at midpoint.
Online business expected to be flat for the full year, downgraded from slight growth, due to top-of-funnel discovery changes.
Non-GAAP gross margin declined 70 bps YoY to 79.1%, and operating margin declined 130 bps to 40%.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue of $1.28 billion beat guidance by $7 million, with enterprise revenue growing 7.8% YoY, the strongest rate in three years.
RPO grew 14% YoY to ~$4.5 billion, with non-current RPO up 25%, reflecting larger and longer-term multi-product deals.
AI momentum: licensed monthly active users of AI features in Workplace grew 125% YoY; Zoom Virtual Agent customer count grew over 250% YoY.
summary: Zoom reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $1.28 billion, up 4.9% YoY, $7 million above the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.55, $0.08 above the high end of guidance, and non-GAAP operating margin was 40%. Enterprise revenue grew 7.8% YoY, the strongest in three years, while RPO grew 14% YoY. Management raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance, now expecting $5.085-$5.095 billion (4.5% YoY growth at midpoint) and non-GAAP EPS of $6.08-$6.12, while also raising free cash flow outlook to $1.78-$1.82 billion.

negative_highlights: Full-year revenue guidance of RMB 600 million was withdrawn due to regulatory uncertainty; no replacement guidance provided.
Timeline for Chinese domestic commercial operations (Hefei project) is uncertain after a June light sport aircraft accident, despite being unrelated to EHang's tech.
Adjusted operating expenses rose 16.9% YoY, and Q2 expenses did not yet reflect cost-optimization benefits.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue rose 203% sequentially to RMB 77.9 million, driven by higher EH216 deliveries and VT35 contribution.
Gross margin held steady at 61.2% despite revenue decline and product mix changes.
Aerial media revenue surged over 270% YoY, with 22 shows and 520 GD4 drones delivered; non-passenger revenue reached 8% of total Q2 revenue.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was RMB 77.9 million, down 31% YoY from RMB 113.3 million but up 203% sequentially from RMB 25.7 million. Gross margin was 61.2%, stable. Adjusted operating loss was RMB 62 million and adjusted net loss was RMB 58.5 million. The company withdrew its FY2026 revenue guidance of RMB 600 million due to regulatory uncertainty after a June light sport aircraft accident, with no replacement guidance provided.

negative_highlights: International Banking NIM declined 7 bps sequentially due to seasonal effects.
Q4 CET1 ratio expected to be impacted by ~15 bps from migration to AIRB, absorbing impact to keep CET1 around 13%.
Chile tax rate reduction will require a one-time deferred tax asset write-down in Q4.
positive_highlights: Record EPS of CAD 2.28, up 21% YoY, and ROE of 14.2%, exceeding medium-term target of 14% ahead of schedule.
Canadian Banking ROE improved 160 bps sequentially to 19.4%.
GBM net income at record high, with revenue up 32% YoY and loans up 7% QoQ.
summary: Scotiabank reported record EPS of CAD 2.28, up 21% YoY, with ROE of 14.2%, exceeding its medium-term target ahead of schedule. Revenue grew 16% YoY with operating leverage positive for the tenth consecutive quarter and CET1 ratio at 13.1%. Canadian Banking ROE improved 160 bps sequentially to 19.4%, and GBM delivered record net income. Guidance remains positive with expectations to finish the year strong, though Q4 includes a 15 bps CET1 impact from AIRB migration.

negative_highlights: Revenue growth decelerated to 14% YoY from 20%+ in prior periods
Operating cash flow declined 10% YoY to RMB 945 million
Sales and marketing expenses surged 38% YoY due to FIFA World Cup sponsorship
positive_highlights: Adjusted operating margin expanded 1.9pp YoY to a record 43.8%
MAU exceeded 70 million, a record high
Total shareholder returns for 2026 exceeded $530 million, above 100% of last year's adjusted net income
summary: Kanzhun reported Q2 2026 revenue of RMB 2.4 billion, up 14% YoY, with adjusted operating margin expanding to 43.8% (up 1.9pp YoY). MAU hit a record 70 million, and paid enterprise customers rose 11% to 7.2 million. Management guided Q3 revenue of RMB 2.41-2.5 billion, implying 11.4%-15.6% YoY growth, and increased shareholder returns to over $530 million for 2026, exceeding 100% of prior-year adjusted net income.

negative_highlights: Full-year EPS guidance cut by $2.00-$2.50 to $11-$12, due to promotional environment and Foot Locker losses.
Foot Locker comps fell 3.6% in Q2, with expectations now -2% to flat for the year (previously 1.5%-3% growth).
Foot Locker operating loss expected to widen to $80M-$40M loss, versus prior profit of $110M-$150M.
positive_highlights: DICK'S comp sales grew 4.9% in Q2, with 9.9% two-year and 14.4% three-year comps.
DICK'S grew market share by nearly 200 basis points versus the industry.
DICK'S gross margin expanded 79 basis points, driven by DICK'S Media Network, GameChanger, and tariff refunds.
summary: DICK'S Sporting Goods reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net sales of $5.59 billion, up 53.2%, driven by the Foot Locker acquisition and a 4.9% comp at DICK'S. The company lowered full-year EPS guidance to $11-$12 from $13.50-$14.50, citing promotional pressure and Foot Locker weakness. DICK'S comp expectations were maintained at 2.5%-4%, but operating margin guidance was cut. Foot Locker comp guidance was reduced to -2% to flat, and its operating loss is now expected.

negative_highlights: Freight costs, driven by rising fuel surcharges, are pressuring gross margin and expected to continue throughout the year.
New store openings were reduced to approximately 20 from 25 due to timing, although 2027 acceleration to 40 stores remains unchanged.
Q2 gross margin expanded only 60 bps, with freight headwinds partially offsetting merchandise margin gains.
positive_highlights: Comparable sales increased 10.5% in Q2, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of comp growth, with two-year stack of 19.7%.
Adjusted EBITDA improved to $5.5 million from a loss of $1.1 million last year, and first-half EBITDA of $19.4 million exceeded full-year 2025 EBITDA.
Company raised full-year guidance: comp sales now 9%-11% (from 8%-10%) and adjusted EBITDA now $38-$42 million (from $35-$40 million).
summary: Citi Trends reported Q2 FY2026 (note the transcript says FY2026, not FY2027) total sales of $211.6 million, a 10.9% increase, with comparable sales up 10.5% (19.7% on a two-year basis). Adjusted EBITDA was $5.5 million, a $6.6 million improvement over last year's loss. The company raised its full-year comparable sales growth guidance to 9%-11% (from 8%-10%) and adjusted EBITDA to $38-$42 million (from $35-$40 million). Management noted continued momentum into Q3 with a ~25% two-year comp stack during back-to-school.

negative_highlights: Q2 revenue declined 4.3% YoY to RMB 24.7 billion, at the low end of guidance
Q3 revenue guidance implies a 5% to 0% YoY decrease, and management expects full-year revenue to be slightly negative
Non-GAAP operating margin fell 120 bps to 8.1% due to fulfillment deleverage from higher return rates
positive_highlights: SVIP members grew 8% YoY and drove 54% of online spending, with SVIP membership reaching 10 million milestone
Shan Shan Outlets grew GMV over 20% in H1, with management guiding to continued similar momentum and double-digit same-store sales growth
Announced new $1 billion share repurchase program, targeting payout of no less than 75% of 2025 non-GAAP net income
summary: Q2 FY2026 total net revenues fell 4.3% YoY to RMB 24.7 billion, at the low end of guidance, as consumers remained highly selective. Non-GAAP net income attributable to shareholders was RMB 392.2 million (down from RMB 2.1 billion), dragged by a one-time withholding tax adjustment; adjusted for that, underlying non-GAAP net profit was RMB 2.0 billion with a 7.9% net margin. Gross margin slipped 20 bps to 23.3%, and non-GAAP operating margin declined to 8.1% from 9.3%. For Q3, management guided revenue down 5% to 0% YoY and expects full-year revenue slightly negative, citing persistent macro softness.

negative_highlights: Operating loss widened to $7.7M from $2.2M YoY, largely due to increased depreciation and public company costs.
Net loss of $22.8M was driven by a $19.2M non-cash loss on convertible notes.
Management did not reaffirm the prior $300M ARR guidance, though noted demand is not the constraint.
positive_highlights: Revenue more than doubled YoY to $6.7M, with compute revenue up 328% to $5.6M.
Gross margin expanded to 66.6% from 55.1% YoY, driven by GPU activations and curtailment credits.
Signed 21 new contracts totaling $169.7M, bringing total signed contract value to $282.5M.
summary: Q2 FY2026 revenue was $6.7M, up 118% YoY from $3.1M, with gross margin expanding to 66.6% from 55.1%. GPU fleet grew 224% to 3,088, and the company signed 21 new contracts totaling $169.7M, bringing total signed contract value to $282.5M. Operating loss widened to $7.7M from $2.2M YoY due to higher D&A, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed sequentially to $0.8M. Management did not reaffirm the $300M ARR target but noted they are not demand constrained, with land/power being the primary gating factor.

negative_highlights: AI application segment revenue growth slowed to 3.9% from 17% in Q1, with B2B project work dampening growth.
Gross margin declined YoY to 46.3% due to semiconductor supply cost increases and business mix changes.
Middle East demand remains paused due to military conflict, and North America shows price sensitivity from supply-chain price increases.
positive_highlights: Total revenue growth accelerated to 16% YoY, up from 8.3% in Q1.
PaaS revenue grew 16.9% to $67.9M, with 318 premium customers contributing 89.5% of PaaS revenue.
Smart home and robot products revenue grew 23.2% to $13.5M, driven by smart security and energy demand.
summary: Tuya reported Q2 2026 revenue of $92.9M, up 16% YoY, accelerating from 8.3% in Q1. PaaS revenue grew 16.9% to $67.9M, while AI application and other segments grew only 3.9% to $11.5M. Blended gross margin was 46.3%, with PaaS margin at 46.8%, down YoY due to semiconductor cost increases. Non-GAAP operating margin held at 10.3%, and net cash from operations was $6.2M. Management expects gradual demand recovery with continued growth, but did not provide specific guidance.

negative_highlights: Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to 6-9% from prior 'more than 12%' for the full year.
Gross margin was 21.2%, lower than expected due to lower scale and a mix shift toward China, with expectations for reversal in H2.
H1 operating cash flow was an outflow of EUR 29.3 million, driven by EUR 26 million of working capital investment; working capital rose to about 14% of LTM sales.
positive_highlights: Q2 revenue rose to EUR 27.8 million from EUR 18.2 million in Q1, and equipment revenues surged to EUR 39.4 million in H1 2026 from EUR 10.7 million in H1 2025.
Order intake reached EUR 52.3 million in the last eight weeks and EUR 96.6 million year-to-date, with guidance raised to EUR 125-150 million and management expecting the upper half.
Order backlog reached a record EUR 89 million, with most 2026 orders flowing into 2027 and a strong second-half and 2027 outlook.
summary: Schmid's H1 2026 revenue rose to EUR 46.0 million from a weak prior-year half, with equipment revenues jumping to EUR 39.4 million from EUR 10.7 million. Order intake accelerated sharply to EUR 96.6 million year-to-date, including EUR 52.3 million in the last eight weeks, leading management to raise full-year order intake guidance to EUR 125-150 million and expect the upper half. However, adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was cut to 6-9% from prior >12%, reflecting lower scale and margin mix; revenue guidance of at least EUR 100 million was maintained. The balance sheet was repaired via a EUR 30.75 million debt-to-equity swap and EUR 33 million raised, with total debt reduced from EUR 53 million to about EUR 23 million.

negative_highlights: Net revenue fell 31.6% YoY to RMB 3.57 billion; non-GAAP net profit fell 75.4% YoY to RMB 455 million, partly due to a one-off tax expense of ~RMB 500 million.
C-M2 for August expected to rise ~25% sequentially; risk deterioration may take two to three quarters to resolve.
Q3 guidance of RMB 400-500 million non-GAAP net income implies a 67-73% YoY decline; management expects funding costs to rise ~25bps already seen in July-August.
positive_highlights: Risk metrics improved in Q2: C-M2 fell 17% sequentially to 0.66%, 30-day collection rate rose 2.3pp to 88.1%, and 90-day delinquency fell from 3.5% to 2.83%.
Tech solutions business grew sharply: loan volume up 515% YoY to RMB 10.5 billion, outstanding balance up 313% to RMB 16.1 billion.
Funding costs declined ~10bps sequentially, with ABS issuance up 90% to RMB 5.5 billion and issuance costs down ~20bps.
summary: Q2 2026 net revenue was RMB 3.57 billion, down from RMB 3.91 billion in Q1 and RMB 5.22 billion a year ago, with non-GAAP net profit of RMB 455 million versus RMB 946 million in Q1 and RMB 1.85 billion a year ago. The company guided Q3 non-GAAP net income between RMB 400-500 million, implying a 67-73% YoY decline. Management cited a late-June industry liquidity crisis and a nationwide collections crackdown, causing a sharp reversal in risk metrics in August with C-M2 expected to rise ~25% sequentially. They plan to maintain strict risk controls, expecting volume not to return to Q2 levels for two to three quarters.

negative_highlights: Core commissions fell 44.1% YoY and recurring management fees dropped 10.8% YoY in Q2, reflecting legacy run-off and continued revenue mix shift.
International segment net revenues declined 21.9% YoY in H1, driven by deliberate contraction of insurance and exit from legacy referral channels.
Overall client acquisition has yet to return to growth; regulatory headwinds heightened noticeably according to CFO.
positive_highlights: Operating margin expanded 9.2 percentage points YoY to 34.8% in Q2; half-year operating margin hit a record 36.3%.
Performance-based income (carry) reached RMB 238 million in H1 2026, up 364% YoY, with 63 consecutive quarters of Non-GAAP profitability.
US-dollar AUM grew 11.7% YoY to $6.5 billion while overseas RM headcount fell 36.2%, indicating early decoupling of asset growth from headcount.
summary: Q2 FY2026 net revenue was RMB 620 million, down 1.5% YoY, but operating income rose 34% YoY to RMB 216 million with an operating margin of 34.8%. Non-GAAP net income was RMB 238 million, up 25.9% YoY and 77.8% QoQ. First-half performance-based income surged 364% YoY to RMB 238 million, while US-dollar AUM grew 11.7% YoY to $6.5 billion despite overseas RM headcount declining 36.2%. Management maintained full-year operating margin guidance above 30% and emphasized the Singapore AI Wealth Management Department proof point (AUM from <$100M to >$400M, monthly profitability in July 2026) as evidence of a scalable model.

negative_highlights: Non-GAAP net income fell YoY due to a $14M FX loss from U.S. dollar weakness.
SHOPLINE gross margin pulled back sequentially due to mix shift toward lower-margin value-added services.
BIGO Ads gross margin decreased QoQ due to higher contribution from lower-margin third-party advertising.
positive_highlights: Total revenue grew 16.3% YoY to $591M, with accelerated QoQ growth of 6.3%.
BIGO Ads revenue up 53.1% YoY, with third-party BIGO Audience Network growing 74.1% YoY.
Full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance raised to ~20% YoY growth, up from previous teens level.
summary: JOYY reported Q2 2026 revenue of $591M, up 16.3% YoY and 6.3% QoQ, with non-GAAP operating profit of $49M, up 28.2% YoY. Social entertainment revenue grew 7.4% YoY, BIGO Ads grew 53.1% YoY, and SHOPLINE grew 28.6% YoY. Management raised full-year non-GAAP operating income growth guidance to around 20% (from teens), driven by better-than-expected H1 performance. Q3 revenue guidance of $602-622M implies 11.4%-15.2% YoY growth.
